docs.title: NeuralOps Recipe Format Guide (v1.0.0)
docs.text: This document provides a practical, user-facing guide to authoring, validating, and executing NeuralOps Recipe Language (NRL) v1.0.0 recipes.

docs.title: 1. Overview
docs.text: A NeuralOps Recipe is a declarative contract that defines a sequence of post-training model optimizations. Unlike arbitrary Python code that mutates model checkpoints imperatively in memory, a recipe can be: - Pre-validated before any device memory is allocated. - Audited against strict architecture and parameter schemas. - Hashed into a canonical SHA-256 fingerprint for publication and verification. - Safely rolled back on failure to preserve model integrity.

docs.title: 2. Anatomy of a Recipe
docs.text:
A recipe consists of five top-level sections:

apiVersion: "neuralops/v1"
kind: "Recipe"

metadata:
  name: "distilbert-fast-aasvd"
  version: "1.0.0"
  description: "Activation-Aware SVD compression on DistilBERT attention layers."
  author: "Taha Majlesi"
  tags: ["distilbert", "aasvd", "compression"]
  license: "MIT"
  production_ready: true

model:
  source: "distilbert-base-uncased"
  dtype: "float32"
  revision: "6cdc0aad91a5ae9d8e7c10b77e8a9fcf45db04a2"
  family: "bert"

operations:
  - id: "compress-attn"
    type: "weights.compress"
    version: "1.0.0"
    config:
      method: "aasvd"
      target_ratio: 0.5
      rank_step: 32
      whitening: true

validation:
  profile: "standard"
  policy: "fail_fast"
  thresholds:
    max_perplexity_increase: 0.05

execution:
  device: "cpu"
  seed: 42
  rollback: true

artifacts:
  output_dir: "./output/distilbert-aasvd"
  save_model: true
  save_report: true
  format: "hf"

docs.title: 3.1 Metadata (metadata)
docs.text: Stores provenance and discovery tags: - name (required): DNS-like identifier matching ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,62}$. - version (required): Strict SemVer 2.0.0 string (e.g., 1.0.0). - description (required): Human-readable explanation of transformation purpose. - author (optional): Author or team name. - tags (optional): List of search keywords. - production_ready (optional): Set to false when testing with validation.profile: "none". - references (optional): List of external URLs or DOI citations.

docs.title: 3.2 Model (model)
docs.text: Declares the base model foundation: - source (required): HuggingFace model identifier or local checkpoint path. - dtype (required): Target tensor precision (bfloat16, float16, float32, fp8). - revision (optional): 40-character Git commit hash for exact checkpoint pinning. Floating branch names like main or latest are rejected to guarantee reproducibility. - trust_remote_code (optional): Boolean flag passed to HuggingFace model loader. - device_map (optional): HuggingFace device allocation strategy (e.g., auto, cpu). - family (optional): Model architecture family (llama, bert, gpt2, generic).

docs.title: 3.3 Operations (operations)
docs.text: The ordered pipeline of transformations: - id (optional): Stable identifier for dependency tracking. - type (required): Registered operation name (e.g., weights.compress, attention.replace). - version (required): Pinned semantic version of the operation contract (e.g., 1.0.0). - config (required): Operation-specific parameter payload, strictly validated against its contract schema. - depends_on (optional): List of preceding operation IDs that must succeed before this stage runs.

docs.title: 3.4 Validation (validation)
docs.text: Configures the multi-tier safety gates: - profile (required): - none: Bypass gates (requires metadata.production_ready: false). - structural: L1 gate only (verifies shapes, dtypes, and tensor connectivity). - numerical: L1 + L2 gates (verifies forward pass execution without NaN or Inf). - behavioral: L1 + L2 + L3 gates (measures perplexity delta and output similarity). - empirical: L1 + L2 + L3 + L4 gates (evaluates on hardware benchmarks and real datasets). - production: Exhaustive certification. - policy (optional): fail_fast (halt on first gate failure), continue_on_warning, or collect_all. - gates (optional): Explicit gate override list. - thresholds (optional): Numerical criteria overrides (e.g., max_perplexity_increase: 0.05).

docs.title: 3.5 Execution (execution)
docs.text: Execution runtime parameters: - device: Device placement (auto, cuda, cpu, mps). - seed: Integer RNG seed for deterministic transformations. - rollback: Boolean indicating whether to automatically restore snapshots on failure (default: true). - memory_budget_gb: Optional peak host/device memory allocation limit.

docs.title: 3.6 Artifacts (artifacts)
docs.text: Terminal export configuration: - output_dir (required): Destination folder for transformed checkpoints. - save_model (optional): Whether to serialize model weights (default: true). - save_report (optional): Whether to emit structured verification evidence (default: true). - format: Export layout (hf, safetensors, vllm, sglang, onnx, gguf).

docs.title: 4. Canonical Hashing (recipe_hash)
docs.text:
Every recipe document can be digested into a unique SHA-256 fingerprint. The hashing engine: 1. Strips comments and surface formatting. 2. Sorts mapping keys lexicographically by UTF-8 bytes at all depths. 3. Eliminates insignificant whitespace. 4. Normalizes text to Unicode NFC format.

Two recipes differing only by indentation, comments, or key order will compute identical recipe hashes.

docs.title: 5. Well-Formedness Rules Summary
docs.text: Every recipe must conform to the 15 Well-Formedness Rules defined in NRL v1.0.0: - W1 (Root Fields): apiVersion, kind, metadata, model, operations must be present. - W2 (SemVer): Version tags must strictly follow X.Y.Z. - W3 (Registry): Every operation type must exist in the active registry. - W4 (Version Check): Pinned operation version must match available registry contracts. - W5 (Parameter Schema): Configuration objects must satisfy operation JSON schemas. - W6 (Fail-Closed): Unknown attributes are strictly forbidden at all nesting depths. - W7 (Unique IDs): Operation identifiers must not collide. - W8 (Dependency Resolution): depends_on must refer to declared preceding operation identifiers. - W9 (Acyclic Order): Dependencies cannot refer forward in the operation array. - W10 (Type Chain): Lifecycle states must unify cleanly across consecutive transformations. - W11 (Preconditions): Declared model family must satisfy all operation prerequisites. - W12 (Self-Composition): Operations declare whether multiple self-invocations are allowed. - W13 (Dataset Requirement): Profiles empirical and production require evaluation datasets. - W14 (Gate Reference): Threshold overrides must reference recognized validation gates. - W15 (Production Gate): Profile none requires metadata.production_ready: false.

docs.title: 6. Common Error Codes
docs.text: Code Meaning Remediation E_SCHEMA_MISSING_FIELD A required field is missing. Check root keys and operation configs. E_SCHEMA_UNKNOWN_FIELD An undeclared field was supplied. Remove unrecognized attributes. E_SCHEMA_INVALID_SEMVER Version string is not SemVer 2.0.0. Use X.Y.Z (e.g., 1.0.0, not 1.0). E_SCHEMA_INVALID_IDENTIFIER An identifier contains invalid characters. Use only lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens. E_VALIDATION_LEVEL_INVALID Profile none used on production recipe. Set metadata.production_ready: false. E_COMP_FORWARD_DEPENDENCY Operation references a later stage. Reorder operations or correct depends_on. E_COMP_TYPE_MISMATCH Incompatible operation state chain. Ensure operations unify state types. E_REGISTRY_UNKNOWN_OP Operation type is not registered. Check spelling and installed plugins. E_REGISTRY_UNKNOWN_VERSION Operation version does not exist. Pin a valid version (e.g. 1.0.0).

docs.title: 7. Python API Integration
docs.text:
The Python API provides direct, programmatic bindings for recipes:

from neuralops.recipe import load_recipe, recipe_hash, save_recipe

# 1. Loading a recipe
recipe = load_recipe("examples/recipes/distilbert-aasvd.yaml")
print(f"Loaded recipe: {recipe.metadata.name} v{recipe.metadata.version}")
print(f"Canonical Hash: {recipe_hash(recipe)}")

# 2. Schema verification
errors = recipe.validate_schema()
if errors:
    raise ValueError(f"Recipe validation failed: {errors}")

# 3. Modifying and saving
recipe.metadata.description = "Updated description for calibrated run."
save_recipe(recipe, "output/distilbert-updated.yaml", format="yaml")

docs.title: 8. CLI Quickstart
docs.text:
NeuralOps exposes recipe management via the nops CLI tool:

# Validate a recipe statically without loading weights:
nops surgery plan --recipe ./examples/recipes/distilbert-aasvd.yaml

# Apply the recipe and produce verifiable execution evidence:
nops surgery apply --recipe ./examples/recipes/distilbert-aasvd.yaml

docs.title: NeuralOps Recipe Language Specification v1.0.0
docs.text: Status: NORMATIVE SPECIFICATION Version: 1.0.0 API Version: neuralops/v1 Date: 2026-10-31 Authors: NeuralOps Core Architecture Team

docs.title: Section 1 — Introduction and Design Axioms
docs.text:
NeuralOps Recipe Language (NRL) is a declarative, statically typed, versioned domain-specific language for specifying post-training deep learning model transformation pipelines. Rather than relying on imperative Python scripts that mutate state in place, NRL recipes define an explicit, reproducible transformation contract that can be pre-validated, statically checked for structural compatibility, simulated without hardware allocation, safely executed with atomic transactional rollbacks, and certified with cryptographic execution provenance.

The language is governed by four immutable design axioms:

docs.title: A1 — Declarative
docs.text:
The recipe specifies WHAT transformations are to be applied, never HOW they are computed. A recipe file is purely data. It contains no imperative control flow (if, when, switch), no iterative loops (for, while), no variable assignments (let, set), no computational expressions, and no custom function invocations. If an operator requires different transformation policies depending on model architecture or hardware capacity, multiple discrete recipes must be authored, validated, and selected at the workflow orchestration layer.

Rationale: Declarative representations decouple transformation intent from execution engines. A recipe can be inspected, planned, statically analyzed for shape and rank invariants, and validated before touching memory or allocating GPU devices. Imperative logic embedded in transformation files creates opaque side effects, non-reproducible dynamic branches, and unpredictable mutation states.

Counter-Example Violation: 

# VIOLATION OF A1: Contains imperative conditional branch
operations:
  - type: attention.replace
    if: "model.num_heads > 32"  # REJECTED: Imperative control flow
    config:
      target: chunk_gla

docs.title: A2 — Typed and Versioned
docs.text:
Every operation, type transition, and recipe schema is explicitly typed and pinned to a semantic version. Each operation contract specifies strict input and output state types (e.g., NeuralOpsModel[loaded] \(\rightarrow\) NeuralOpsModel[attention_replaced]). All operation references in recipes must pin a semantic version (major.minor.patch). The language specification itself is versioned under apiVersion: neuralops/v1 and guarantees backward compatibility for all minor and patch iterations.

Rationale: Silent runtime behavior drift across library releases is the primary cause of regression in post-training optimization. Pinned operational contracts guarantee that an operation executed six months later evaluates against identical parameter schemas, numerical invariants, and validation gates.

Counter-Example Violation: 

# VIOLATION OF A2: Unversioned type and loose contract
operations:
  - type: attention.replace  # REJECTED: Missing explicit version pinning
    config:
      target: latest         # REJECTED: Floating, unpinned configuration

docs.title: A3 — Composable with Explicit Dependencies
docs.text:
Operations form a strictly ordered linear transformation chain with declarative dependency tracking. Operations execute in sequential pipeline order (\(O_1 \rightarrow O_2 \rightarrow \dots \rightarrow O_n\)). The depends_on field establishes an explicit declaration of semantic dependency and postcondition consumption, not an automated reordering mechanism. Forward references, circular dependencies, and out-of-order state mutations are statically illegal.

Rationale: Linear transformation chains enable deterministic state snapshots and clean backward rollback paths. Allowing arbitrary graph dependencies or auto-reordering introduces combinatorial validation states and makes transactional failure recovery non-deterministic.

Counter-Example Violation: 

# VIOLATION OF A3: Forward dependency and implicit reordering
operations:
  - id: op1
    type: weights.compress
    depends_on: [op2]  # REJECTED: Forward dependency; op2 has not executed
  - id: op2
    type: attention.replace

docs.title: A4 — Reproducible with Evidence
docs.text:
A recipe transformation is only certified when accompanied by structured, cryptographic execution evidence. The static recipe hash (recipe_hash computed over canonicalized bytes) is necessary but insufficient for scientific reproducibility. A complete execution evidence record binds the static recipe hash to the base model git commit SHA, exact framework versions (torch, transformers, neuralops), hardware device metadata, pseudorandom generator seed, per-stage latency/memory telemetry, and validation gate certificates.

Rationale: Model surgery modifies billions of numerical parameters. Without verifiable cryptographic evidence binding the inputs, environment, and intermediate verification gates, downstream deployment teams cannot verify whether a deployed checkpoint matches its designated transformation lineage.

Counter-Example Violation: 

# VIOLATION OF A4: Unverifiable external artifact without revision or seed
model:
  source: "meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B"
  revision: "main"  # REJECTED: Floating branch pointer violates strict reproducibility
execution:
  seed: null        # REJECTED: Unseeded non-deterministic execution

docs.title: Section 2 — Lexical Structure
docs.text:
1. Surface and Canonical Encodings: The surface representation of a Recipe is valid YAML (1.2). The canonical wire and storage representation is valid JSON (RFC 8259). Both encodings parse into an identical abstract syntax tree (AST).
  2. Value Primitives: The language admits exactly seven primitive types:
  3. string: UTF-8 encoded text, normalized to Unicode Normalization Form C (NFC) prior to canonicalization.
  4. integer: 64-bit signed decimal integer (-9223372036854775808 to 9223372036854775807).
  5. float: IEEE 754 double-precision floating-point number. Canonical output renders the shortest equivalent decimal representation (1.0 is serialized as 1).
  6. boolean: Literal true or false.
  7. null: Explicit null value (null or ~ in YAML, null in JSON).
  8. array: Ordered sequence of zero or more values.
  9. object: Unordered mapping of unique string keys to values.
  10. Identifiers: All object keys, identifiers, and recipe names must match the DNS-style identifier regular expression: ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,62}$ Keys must begin with an alphanumeric ASCII character, followed by up to 62 lowercase alphanumeric characters or hyphens.
  11. Operation Type Namespacing: Operation types must conform to dot-delimited hierarchical namespaces: ^[a-z]+(\.[a-z0-9_-]+)+$ (e.g., attention.replace, weights.compress, export.model).
  12. Version Strings: All version fields must strictly adhere to Semantic Versioning 2.0.0 (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH with optional -PRERELEASE and +BUILD metadata). Floating ranges (^1.0.0, ~1.2) are rejected.
  13. Comments: YAML comments (# ...) are permitted in surface syntax for human documentation, but are stripped during AST construction and do not survive canonicalization or hashing.

docs.title: Section 3 — Full EBNF Grammar
docs.text:
The grammar of a NeuralOps Recipe is specified in Extended Backus-Naur Form (EBNF):

Recipe                 ::= "{" WS*
                           '"apiVersion"' WS* ":" WS* ApiVersion WS* "," WS*
                           '"kind"' WS* ":" WS* '"Recipe"' WS* "," WS*
                           '"metadata"' WS* ":" WS* Metadata WS* "," WS*
                           '"model"' WS* ":" WS* ModelSpec WS* "," WS*
                           '"operations"' WS* ":" WS* OperationList WS*
                           ( "," WS* '"validation"' WS* ":" WS* ValidationSpec )?
                           ( "," WS* '"execution"' WS* ":" WS* ExecutionSpec )?
                           ( "," WS* '"artifacts"' WS* ":" WS* ArtifactsSpec )?
                           WS* "}" ;

ApiVersion             ::= '"neuralops/v1"' ;

Metadata               ::= "{" WS*
                           '"name"' WS* ":" WS* Identifier WS* "," WS*
                           '"version"' WS* ":" WS* SemVerString WS* "," WS*
                           '"description"' WS* ":" WS* JSONString
                           ( "," WS* '"author"' WS* ":" WS* JSONString )?
                           ( "," WS* '"created_at"' WS* ":" WS* ISO8601String )?
                           ( "," WS* '"tags"' WS* ":" WS* StringList )?
                           ( "," WS* '"license"' WS* ":" WS* JSONString )?
                           ( "," WS* '"production_ready"' WS* ":" WS* Boolean )?
                           ( "," WS* '"references"' WS* ":" WS* StringList )?
                           WS* "}" ;

ModelSpec              ::= "{" WS*
                           '"source"' WS* ":" WS* JSONString WS* "," WS*
                           '"dtype"' WS* ":" WS* DtypeString
                           ( "," WS* '"revision"' WS* ":" WS* GitCommitHash )?
                           ( "," WS* '"trust_remote_code"' WS* ":" WS* Boolean )?
                           ( "," WS* '"device_map"' WS* ":" WS* JSONString )?
                           ( "," WS* '"family"' WS* ":" WS* Identifier )?
                           WS* "}" ;

OperationList          ::= "[" WS* Operation ( WS* "," WS* Operation )* WS* "]" ;

Operation              ::= "{" WS*
                           ( '"id"' WS* ":" WS* Identifier WS* "," WS* )?
                           '"type"' WS* ":" WS* OperationType WS* "," WS*
                           '"version"' WS* ":" WS* SemVerString WS* "," WS*
                           '"config"' WS* ":" WS* JSONObject
                           ( "," WS* '"depends_on"' WS* ":" WS* IdentifierList )?
                           WS* "}" ;

ValidationSpec         ::= "{" WS*
                           '"profile"' WS* ":" WS* ValidationProfile
                           ( "," WS* '"policy"' WS* ":" WS* ValidationPolicy )?
                           ( "," WS* '"gates"' WS* ":" WS* GateOverrideList )?
                           ( "," WS* '"thresholds"' WS* ":" WS* JSONObject )?
                           WS* "}" ;

ValidationProfile      ::= '"none"' | '"structural"' | '"numerical"' | '"behavioral"' | '"empirical"' | '"production"' ;

ValidationPolicy       ::= '"fail_fast"' | '"continue_on_warning"' | '"collect_all"' ;

ExecutionSpec          ::= "{" WS*
                           ( '"device"' WS* ":" WS* DeviceString WS* ","? )?
                           ( '"seed"' WS* ":" WS* Integer WS* ","? )?
                           ( '"rollback"' WS* ":" WS* Boolean WS* ","? )?
                           ( '"memory_budget_gb"' WS* ":" WS* Number )?
                           WS* "}" ;

ArtifactsSpec          ::= "{" WS*
                           '"output_dir"' WS* ":" WS* JSONString
                           ( "," WS* '"save_model"' WS* ":" WS* Boolean )?
                           ( "," WS* '"save_report"' WS* ":" WS* Boolean )?
                           ( "," WS* '"format"' WS* ":" WS* ExportFormat )?
                           WS* "}" ;

ExportFormat           ::= '"hf"' | '"safetensors"' | '"vllm"' | '"sglang"' | '"onnx"' | '"gguf"' ;

OperationType          ::= '"' [a-z]+ ("." [a-z0-9_-]+)+ '"' ;
Identifier             ::= '"' [a-z0-9] [a-z0-9-]{0,62} '"' ;
SemVerString           ::= '"' [0-9]+ "." [0-9]+ "." [0-9]+ ( "-" [0-9A-Za-z.-]+ )? ( "+" [0-9A-Za-z.-]+ )? '"' ;
DtypeString            ::= '"bfloat16"' | '"float16"' | '"float32"' | '"fp8"' ;
DeviceString           ::= '"auto"' | '"cuda"' | '"cpu"' | '"mps"' ;
GitCommitHash          ::= '"' [0-9a-f]{40} '"' ;
ISO8601String          ::= '"' [0-9]{4} "-" [0-9]{2} "-" [0-9]{2} "T" [0-9]{2} ":" [0-9]{2} ":" [0-9]{2} ( "Z" | [+-] [0-9]{2} ":" [0-9]{2} ) '"' ;

docs.title: Section 4 — Type System
docs.text: The NRL type system is a static refinement type system over deep learning models and runtime artifacts.

docs.title: 4.1 Domain Types
docs.text:
1. NeuralOpsModel[state] Represents an in-memory PyTorch neural network module parameterized by its lifecycle transformation state:
  2. state = loaded: Model loaded directly from base weights; untouched.
  3. state = attention_replaced: Quadratic multi-head or grouped-query attention modules transplanted with subquadratic linear/recurrent operators.
  4. state = compressed: Weight matrices subjected to low-rank SVD, ASVD, or spectral factorizations.
  5. state = quantized: Weights converted to discrete low-bit representations (FP8, INT4 AWQ/GPTQ).
  6. state = pruned: Structural decoder layers, attention heads, or MLP intermediate widths removed.
  7. state = adapted: Post-surgery adapters attached (LoRA) or knowledge-distillation fine-tuning applied.

  8. state = *: Universal wild-card state matching any lifecycle state.

  9. ServingArtifact[engine] Represents a serialized runtime package prepared for production serving engines:

  10. engine ∈ {hf, safetensors, vllm, sglang, tensorrt_llm, tgi, onnx, gguf}

docs.title: 4.2 Operation Type Signatures
docs.text: Operation Type Input Type Signature Output Type Signature State Transition Category attention.replace NeuralOpsModel[loaded] NeuralOpsModel[attention_replaced] Structural Surgery attention.configure NeuralOpsModel[*] NeuralOpsModel[*] Hyperparameter Tuning weights.compress NeuralOpsModel[*] NeuralOpsModel[compressed] Numerical Compression weights.decompose NeuralOpsModel[*] NeuralOpsModel[compressed] Tensor Factorization weights.quantize NeuralOpsModel[*] NeuralOpsModel[quantized] Discrete Quantization weights.prune NeuralOpsModel[*] NeuralOpsModel[pruned] Structural Sparsity architecture.reduce_mlp NeuralOpsModel[*] NeuralOpsModel[pruned] Dimensionality Shrinkage architecture.drop_layer NeuralOpsModel[*] NeuralOpsModel[pruned] Depth Pruning architecture.modify NeuralOpsModel[*] NeuralOpsModel[*] Topology Modification adaptation.lora NeuralOpsModel[*] NeuralOpsModel[adapted] Parameter Efficient Fine-Tuning adaptation.distill NeuralOpsModel[*] NeuralOpsModel[adapted] Recovery Fine-Tuning adaptation.heal NeuralOpsModel[*] NeuralOpsModel[adapted] Micro-Calibration export.model NeuralOpsModel[*] ServingArtifact[engine] Terminal Export export.checkpoint NeuralOpsModel[*] ServingArtifact[hf] Intermediate Checkpoint verify.parity NeuralOpsModel[S] NeuralOpsModel[S] Identity Probe

docs.title: 4.3 Static Verification Capabilities and Preconditions
docs.text: The type system catches structural order violations at compile time before weights or memory are allocated. - Why export.model \(\rightarrow\) weights.compress is caught: export.model emits ServingArtifact[engine], which does not satisfy the input constraint NeuralOpsModel[*] required by weights.compress. The type checker raises E_COMP_TYPE_MISMATCH. - Why weights.compress \(\rightarrow\) attention.replace requires preconditions: Both operations consume and produce NeuralOpsModel. However, replacing an attention layer after compressing weight projections invalidates the low-rank projection factorizations (\(U, S, V\)). This semantic conflict is caught by static precondition checking (preconditions: [model.attention_intact == true]), producing E_COMP_PRECONDITION_UNSATISFIED.

docs.title: Section 5 — Operation Registry Protocol
docs.text: The operation registry manages the repository of executable transformation contracts.

docs.title: 5.1 Registration Contract Interface
docs.text: Every operation contract exposes the following immutable interface properties: - name: Namespaced identifier (e.g., attention.replace). - version: SemVer 2.0.0 string (e.g., 1.0.0). - input_state: Required NeuralOpsModel input state. - output_state: Resulting NeuralOpsModel or ServingArtifact output state. - params_schema: JSON Schema Draft 7 object defining all configuration parameters. - preconditions: List of static and dynamic predicates evaluated against the model architecture before execution. - postconditions: List of invariant checks evaluated after operation execution. - declares_mutations: Dotted module and parameter path prefixes touched by the operation (used for transactional snapshots). - deterministic_given_seed: Boolean indicating whether identical seeds produce bit-identical weight matrices. - estimated_time_and_memory: Analytic resource estimation function taking model dimensions and producing estimated latency and VRAM footprint.

docs.title: 5.2 Coexistence and Versioning Rules
docs.text:
1. Multiple versions of the same operation name coexist within the registry simultaneously (e.g., weights.compress@1.0.0 and weights.compress@2.0.0).
  2. Version bumps obey strict rules:
  3. MAJOR: Any change to input/output state types, removed parameters, breaking changes in numerical behavior, or added required parameters.
  4. MINOR: Backward-compatible additions of optional parameters or enhanced kernel dispatch options.
  5. PATCH: Implementation bug fixes preserving exact mathematical and interface contracts.
  6. Deprecation Policy: Deprecated operation versions emit E_OP_VERSION_DEPRECATED warnings during planning. An operation version is never deleted until a major bump of the Recipe Language itself (apiVersion: neuralops/v2).

docs.title: 6.1 attention.replace
docs.text:
• Version: 1.0.0
  • Input / Output State: NeuralOpsModel[loaded] \(\rightarrow\) NeuralOpsModel[attention_replaced]
  • Supported Families: Standard transformer decoder backbones (llama, gpt2, qwen, mistral, bert). Excludes recurrent backbones (mamba, rwkv).
  • Params Schema: 
    {
  "type": "object",
  "required": ["target"],
  "properties": {
    "target": {"type": "string", "enum": ["chunk_gla", "retnet", "cosformer", "decay_linear_attention", "hgrn2"]},
    "head_dim": {"type": "integer", "enum": [32, 64, 128]},
    "chunk_size": {"type": "integer", "default": 64},
    "gate_low_rank_dim": {"type": "integer", "default": 16}
  },
  "additionalProperties": false
}
  • Preconditions: has_standard_attention(model) == true, model.config.hidden_size % head_dim == 0.
  • Postconditions: all_attention_modules_match(model, target) == true.
  • Declares Mutations: ["*.self_attn", "*.attn"].
  • Deterministic Given Seed: true.

docs.title: 6.2 attention.configure
docs.text:
• Version: 1.0.0
  • Input / Output State: NeuralOpsModel[*] \(\rightarrow\) NeuralOpsModel[*]
  • Supported Families: All transformer families.
  • Params Schema: 
    {
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "chunk_size": {"type": "integer", "minimum": 16},
    "clamp_min": {"type": "number"},
    "clamp_max": {"type": "number"}
  },
  "additionalProperties": false
}
  • Preconditions: model.has_attention == true.
  • Postconditions: attention_parameters_configured(model) == true.
  • Declares Mutations: ["*.attn.config"].
  • Deterministic Given Seed: true.

docs.title: 6.3 weights.compress
docs.text:
• Version: 1.0.0
  • Input / Output State: NeuralOpsModel[*] \(\rightarrow\) NeuralOpsModel[compressed]
  • Supported Families: All dense and transformer architectures.
  • Params Schema: 
    {
  "type": "object",
  "required": ["method", "target_ratio"],
  "properties": {
    "method": {"type": "string", "enum": ["svd", "asvd", "fwsvd", "hnc_svd"]},
    "target_ratio": {"type": "number", "minimum": 0.05, "maximum": 0.95},
    "rank_step": {"type": "integer", "default": 32},
    "whitening": {"type": "boolean", "default": false}
  },
  "additionalProperties": false
}
  • Preconditions: uncompressed_linear_weights_exist(model) == true.
  • Postconditions: model.compression_ratio <= target_ratio.
  • Declares Mutations: ["*.mlp.*", "*.self_attn.*_proj"].
  • Deterministic Given Seed: true.

docs.title: 6.4 weights.decompose
docs.text:
• Version: 1.0.0
  • Input / Output State: NeuralOpsModel[*] \(\rightarrow\) NeuralOpsModel[compressed]
  • Supported Families: All models containing dense linear layers.
  • Params Schema: 
    {
  "type": "object",
  "required": ["rank"],
  "properties": {
    "rank": {"type": "integer", "minimum": 4},
    "targets": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}}
  },

docs.title: Section 7 — Well-Formedness Rules (W1–W15)
docs.text:
A recipe document must satisfy all fifteen static well-formedness rules:

  • W1 — Root Schema Conformance: The document must match top-level fields: apiVersion, kind, metadata, model, operations. Error: E_SCHEMA_MISSING_FIELD Violation: kind: "Recipe" omitted.
  • W2 — SemVer Validity: Version strings in metadata.version and operations[i].version must parse as valid SemVer 2.0.0. Error: E_SCHEMA_INVALID_SEMVER Violation: version: "v1.2".
  • W3 — Operation Registry Membership: Every operation type must exist in the active operation registry. Error: E_REGISTRY_UNKNOWN_OP Violation: type: "quantum.teleport".
  • W4 — Operation Version Compatibility: The pinned version in operations[i].version must exist in the registry for that operation name. Error: E_REGISTRY_UNKNOWN_VERSION Violation: type: "attention.replace", version: "99.0.0".
  • W5 — Strict Parameter Schema Conformance: The config object must validate against the operation's JSON Schema with additionalProperties: false. Error: E_SCHEMA_UNKNOWN_FIELD Violation: config: { target: "chunk_gla", bogus_option: 42 }.
  • W6 — Fail-Closed Schema Validation: Unknown fields at any level of the recipe document trigger immediate rejection. Error: E_SCHEMA_UNKNOWN_FIELD Violation: metadata: { name: "test", experimental_flag: true }.
  • W7 — Unique Operation Identifiers: Every explicit operation id must be unique across the recipe. Error: E_COMP_DUPLICATE_ID Violation: Two operations sharing id: "step-1".
  • W8 — Declared Dependency Resolution: Every element in depends_on must reference a valid preceding operation id. Error: E_COMP_FORWARD_DEPENDENCY Violation: depends_on: ["non_existent_op"].
  • W9 — Strictly Preceding Dependencies: No operation may depend on itself or an operation appearing later in the array. Error: E_COMP_FORWARD_DEPENDENCY Violation: Operation at index 0 declaring depends_on: ["op-2"].
  • W10 — Linear Type Chain Validity: The output type of operation \(i\) must unify with the input type of operation \(i+1\). Error: E_COMP_TYPE_MISMATCH Violation: export.model (ServingArtifact) followed by weights.compress (NeuralOpsModel).
  • W11 — Precondition Satisfiability on Declared Family: Declared model family must satisfy all static preconditions of each operation. Error: E_COMP_PRECONDITION_UNSATISFIED Violation: attention.replace declared on model: { family: "mamba" }.
  • W12 — Disallow Incompatible Self-Composition: Multiple applications of identical operations must be explicitly permitted by the operation contract. Error: E_COMP_SELF_COMPOSE_DISALLOWED Violation: Applying attention.replace twice in the same pipeline.
  • W13 — Empirical Profile Requires Evaluation Dataset: If validation.profile is set to empirical or production, an evaluation dataset must be provided or policy configured. Error: E_VALIDATION_NO_DATASET Violation: Profile is empirical but no dataset or calibration corpus is configured.
  • W14 — Valid Gate Threshold References: Threshold configuration overrides must reference gates registered in the validation engine. Error: E_VALIDATION_UNKNOWN_GATE Violation: thresholds: { imaginary_loss_gate: 0.1 }.
  • W15 — Production Safety Gate Contract: If validation.profile is "none", the recipe must explicitly declare metadata.production_ready: false. Error: E_VALIDATION_LEVEL_INVALID Violation: Profile "none" with production_ready: true or omitted.

docs.title: Section 8 — Operational Semantics (E1–E6)
docs.text:
The recipe executor operates as a deterministic, transactional state machine:

  • E1 — Execution Loop: The engine executes operations sequentially: For op in recipe.operations:
  • Resolve operational contract from registry.
  • Verify all depends_on operations succeeded.
  • Evaluate operation preconditions against model.
  • Capture atomic snapshot over op.declares_mutations.
  • Apply operation: (model_next, op_evidence) = op.apply(model_curr, op.config).
  • Execute run_validation_gates at configured profile.
  • If any required gate fails: invoke rollback, abort, and raise E_EXEC_VALIDATION_FAILED.

  • If gates pass: commit stage, append evidence record to chain, release snapshot.

  • E2 — Snapshot Scope: Snapshots capture only state paths listed in op.declares_mutations. The snapshot stores parameter tensors, buffers, sub-module references, model config attributes, and pseudorandom generator states. Unmutated sub-modules are never cloned.

  • E3 — Transactional Rollback: Upon gate failure or unhandled exception during operation execution, restore(model, snapshot) restores the mutated state paths bit-for-bit. If the rollback restore fails, the engine raises E_EXEC_ROLLBACK_FAILED and halts immediately.

  • E4 — Validation Shortcut Restriction: When profile == "none", validation gates are bypassed for rapid testing. This execution path is rejected unless metadata.production_ready: false is explicitly set.

  • E5 — Empirical Fallback: When profile == "empirical" and physical hardware or dataset is unavailable, empirical gates return skipped: true (never passed: true). The validation status reflects PARTIAL rather than SUCCESS.

  • E6 — Dry-Run Planning: The planning phase (plan_recipe) executes all W1–W15 checks, verifies type transitions, evaluates preconditions against model configuration metadata, and estimates VRAM and latency without loading weight tensors or creating CUDA contexts.

docs.title: Section 9 — Composition Rules (C1–C7)
docs.text:
• C1 — Linear State Threading: The output model state of stage \(i\) forms the input model state of stage \(i+1\).
  • C2 — Declarative Intent: The depends_on attribute declares logical dependency; it does not alter execution sequence.
  • C3 — Multiple Predecessors: An operation may depend on multiple preceding stages (depends_on: [op1, op2]); all named stages must complete successfully.
  • C4 — No Forward References: An operation cannot reference a stage that appears later in the document.
  • C5 — Acyclicity: Strict compliance with C4 guarantees that the dependency graph is a directed acyclic graph (DAG).
  • C6 — Cascade Skip Semantics: If an optional stage is skipped, all downstream operations that depend upon it must also be skipped, or the pipeline is invalid.
  • C7 — Verifiable Evidence Chain: Each stage appends a signed evidence record containing input_state_hash, output_state_hash, gate certificates, duration, and peak memory allocated.

docs.title: Section 10 — Versioning Policy
docs.text:
NeuralOps maintains three distinct, independent versioning streams:

  1. Language Version (apiVersion: neuralops/v1): Governs the grammar, top-level keys, well-formedness rules (W1–W15), and canonical hashing algorithm. A change to language semantics or canonical hashing requires apiVersion: neuralops/v2.
  2. Operation Contract Version (type: name, version: X.Y.Z): Governed by individual operation definitions. A breaking parameter change in weights.compress increments its major version (2.0.0) without bumping the language version.
  3. Library Package Version (neuralops.__version__): The runtime software release (e.g., 1.9.0), independent of recipe contracts. A recipe does not pin the library package version.

docs.title: Section 11 — Canonical Form and Hashing
docs.text:
To compute a deterministic cryptographic hash (recipe_hash):

  1. Stripping: Comments and YAML formatting are removed.
  2. Key Ordering: All dictionary keys are sorted lexicographically by UTF-8 byte value at all nesting depths.
  3. Whitespace Normalization: Insignificant whitespace is eliminated (colon followed by single space, comma followed by single space).
  4. Number Formatting: Numbers use the shortest equivalent representation (1 instead of 1.0 if integer).
  5. String Encoding: Strings are normalized using Unicode Normalization Form C (NFC) and UTF-8 encoded.
  6. Hash Computation: The canonical UTF-8 byte string is digested with SHA-256. The resulting string is prefixed as sha256:<64_hex_digits>.

Two recipes are semantically identical if and only if their computed recipe_hash values are equal.

docs.title: Section 12 — Error Taxonomy
docs.text: Category Error Code Description Example Trigger Recommended Remediation Parse E_PARSE_JSON_SYNTAX Invalid JSON syntax encountered. Trailing comma in JSON payload. Validate JSON with standard parser. Parse E_PARSE_YAML_SYNTAX Malformed YAML syntax. Indentation mismatch on operation list. Align indentation to 2 spaces. Parse E_PARSE_DUP_KEY Duplicate key in single mapping. Two version: keys in metadata. Remove duplicate key definition. Schema E_SCHEMA_MISSING_FIELD Required field is missing. Missing metadata.name. Provide required field in recipe. Schema E_SCHEMA_UNKNOWN_FIELD Unknown property rejected (fail-closed). metadata.extra_key: 123. Remove undeclared field. Schema E_SCHEMA_WRONG_TYPE Field value type mismatch. seed: "123" (string instead of int). Pass correct primitive type. Schema E_SCHEMA_INVALID_SEMVER Version string violates SemVer 2.0.0. version: "v1.0". Use strict X.Y.Z format. Schema E_SCHEMA_INVALID_IDENTIFIER Key or identifier violates regex. name: "My Recipe!". Use lowercase alphanumeric and hyphens. Registry E_REGISTRY_UNKNOWN_OP Operation type not registered. type: "matrix.quantum_solve". Check registered operation names. Registry E_REGISTRY_UNKNOWN_VERSION Operation version not found. type: "attention.replace", version: "9.9.9". Check supported operation versions. Registry E_REGISTRY_DUPLICATE Duplicate registration attempt. Registering same op and version twice. Increment version or use override. Composition E_COMP_DUPLICATE_ID Non-unique operation id. Two operations with id: "compress". Assign unique identifiers. Composition E_COMP_FORWARD_DEPENDENCY Dependency references future stage. Step 1 depends on Step 2. Reorder pipeline or fix depends_on. Composition E_COMP_TYPE_MISMATCH Incompatible lifecycle states. export.model before weights.compress. Place export at pipeline termination. Composition E_COMP_PRECONDITION_UNSATISFIED Precondition check failed. attention.replace on Mamba model. Ensure target model supports operation. Composition E_COMP_SELF_COMPOSE_DISALLOWED Operation applied multiple times. Running attention replace twice. Remove redundant operation. Validation E_VALIDATION_NO_DATASET Empirical profile missing corpus. Profile empirical without dataset. Supply dataset or lower profile. Validation E_VALIDATION_UNKNOWN_GATE Unknown gate referenced in config. Override on non_existent_gate. Verify gate identifier spelling. Validation E_VALIDATION_LEVEL_INVALID Profile none on production recipe. Profile none with production_ready: true. Set production_ready: false or validate. Execution E_EXEC_OPERATION_FAILED Internal error applying operation. Out-of-memory or kernel crash. Inspect operation configuration. Execution E_EXEC_VALIDATION_FAILED Required validation gate failed. Cosine similarity below threshold. Adjust thresholds or add recovery stage. Execution E_EXEC_ROLLBACK_FAILED Failed to restore pre-stage snapshot. State dict mismatch during restore. Fatal error: reload base model. Execution E_EXEC_SNAPSHOT_FAILED Memory error taking snapshot. Insufficient CPU RAM for state paths. Reduce snapshot scope or memory budget. Execution E_EXEC_BASE_MODEL_LOAD_FAILED Base model checkpoint missing/corrupted. Bad HuggingFace repo path. Verify model path and revision SHA. Version E_LANG_VERSION_TOO_NEW Recipe apiVersion unsupported. apiVersion: "neuralops/v9". Upgrade neuralops package. Version E_LANG_VERSION_TOO_OLD Deprecated apiVersion. apiVersion: "neuralops/v0". Upgrade recipe to neuralops/v1. Version E_OP_VERSION_DEPRECATED Deprecated operation version used. Operation marked for sunset. Update operation version in recipe.

docs.title: Section 13 — Extension Protocol
docs.text:
Third-party packages may register custom operations using the extension protocol:

from neuralops.operations.base import Operation, OperationContract
from neuralops.operations.registry import register_operation

class CustomAttentionSurgery(Operation):
    contract = OperationContract(
        name="custom.sparse_attention",
        version="1.0.0",
        input_state="loaded",
        output_state="attention_replaced",
        params_schema={
            "type": "object",
            "required": ["sparsity_pattern"],
            "properties": {
                "sparsity_pattern": {"type": "string"}
            },
            "additionalProperties": False,
        },
        preconditions=["has_standard_attention"],
        postconditions=["verify_sparse_pattern"],
        declares_mutations=["*.self_attn"],
        deterministic_given_seed=True,
    )

    def apply(self, model, config):
        # Implementation logic mutating declared paths
        return transformed_model, {"sparsity_applied": config["sparsity_pattern"]}

register_operation(CustomAttentionSurgery())

Namespace Rules: - Custom operations must use namespaced identifiers with at least one dot (company.operation). - Registration fails if (name, version) collides with an existing registration.

docs.title: Section 14 — Conformance Test Suite Specification
docs.text: This section defines 30+ test recipes with expected outcomes for verification:

docs.title: Category 1: Valid Recipes (5 Cases)
docs.text:
1. Case 1.1 — Minimal Valid Recipe: Single attention.replace operation with required fields. \(\rightarrow\) VALID
  2. Case 1.2 — Multi-Stage Valid Pipeline: attention.replace \(\rightarrow\) weights.compress \(\rightarrow\) export.model. \(\rightarrow\) VALID
  3. Case 1.3 — Pruning and Healing Pipeline: architecture.drop_layer \(\rightarrow\) adaptation.heal \(\rightarrow\) export.checkpoint. \(\rightarrow\) VALID
  4. Case 1.4 — Full Recipe with Explicit Metadata and Overrides: All optional metadata fields, validation thresholds, and execution seed provided. \(\rightarrow\) VALID
  5. Case 1.5 — Micro-Quantization Pipeline: weights.quantize with method fp8 and export.model. \(\rightarrow\) VALID

docs.title: Category 2: Schema Violations (5 Cases)
docs.text:
1. Case 2.1 — Missing apiVersion: \(\rightarrow\) E_SCHEMA_MISSING_FIELD
  2. Case 2.2 — Unknown Field in Metadata: \(\rightarrow\) E_SCHEMA_UNKNOWN_FIELD
  3. Case 2.3 — Non-SemVer Version String: version: "1.0" \(\rightarrow\) E_SCHEMA_INVALID_SEMVER
  4. Case 2.4 — Illegal Identifier Characters: id: "op#1" \(\rightarrow\) E_SCHEMA_INVALID_IDENTIFIER
  5. Case 2.5 — Wrong Type for Seed: seed: "123" \(\rightarrow\) E_SCHEMA_WRONG_TYPE

docs.title: Category 3: Registry Violations (5 Cases)
docs.text:
1. Case 3.1 — Unregistered Operation: type: "quantum.entropy" \(\rightarrow\) E_REGISTRY_UNKNOWN_OP
  2. Case 3.2 — Unregistered Version: type: "attention.replace", version: "9.9.9" \(\rightarrow\) E_REGISTRY_UNKNOWN_VERSION
  3. Case 3.3 — Missing Required Parameter in Config: attention.replace without target \(\rightarrow\) E_SCHEMA_MISSING_FIELD
  4. Case 3.4 — Undeclared Parameter in Config: target_ratio passed to attention.replace \(\rightarrow\) E_SCHEMA_UNKNOWN_FIELD
  5. Case 3.5 — Parameter Out of Range: target_ratio: 1.5 for weights.compress \(\rightarrow\) E_SCHEMA_WRONG_TYPE

docs.title: Category 4: Composition Violations (5 Cases)
docs.text:
1. Case 4.1 — Duplicate Operation Identifiers: Two stages with id: "stage-1" \(\rightarrow\) E_COMP_DUPLICATE_ID
  2. Case 4.2 — Forward Reference Dependency: Step 1 depends on Step 2 \(\rightarrow\) E_COMP_FORWARD_DEPENDENCY
  3. Case 4.3 — Invalid Lifecycle Type Transition: export.model followed by weights.compress \(\rightarrow\) E_COMP_TYPE_MISMATCH
  4. Case 4.4 — Architecture Incompatibility: attention.replace on Mamba \(\rightarrow\) E_COMP_PRECONDITION_UNSATISFIED
  5. Case 4.5 — Disallowed Self-Composition: Consecutive attention.replace \(\rightarrow\) E_COMP_SELF_COMPOSE_DISALLOWED

docs.title: Category 5: Validation Configuration Violations (5 Cases)
docs.text:
1. Case 5.1 — Empirical Profile Without Dataset: Profile empirical without dataset \(\rightarrow\) E_VALIDATION_NO_DATASET
  2. Case 5.2 — Unknown Gate in Thresholds: thresholds: { fake_gate: 0.5 } \(\rightarrow\) E_VALIDATION_UNKNOWN_GATE
  3. Case 5.3 — None Profile with Production Flag: Profile none with production_ready: true \(\rightarrow\) E_VALIDATION_LEVEL_INVALID
  4. Case 5.4 — Invalid Validation Profile Name: Profile "ultra" \(\rightarrow\) E_SCHEMA_WRONG_TYPE
  5. Case 5.5 — Negative Threshold Value for Absolute Metric: max_abs_diff: -0.1 \(\rightarrow\) E_SCHEMA_WRONG_TYPE

docs.title: Category 6: Canonical Form and Hashing Tests (5 Cases)
docs.text:
1. Case 6.1 — Whitespace Invariance: Space/newline variants produce identical SHA-256 hash.
  2. Case 6.2 — Key Reordering Invariance: Permuted mapping keys produce identical SHA-256 hash.
  3. Case 6.3 — Description Sensitivity: Mutating description changes SHA-256 hash.
  4. Case 6.4 — Operation Order Sensitivity: Permuting operations changes SHA-256 hash.
  5. Case 6.5 — Pinned Version Sensitivity: Changing operation version changes SHA-256 hash.

docs.title: Section 15 — Non-Goals and Explicit Exclusions
docs.text:
The following capabilities are deliberately excluded from NeuralOps Recipe Language v1.0.0:

  1. No Conditional Logic (if, when, ternary): Prevents non-deterministic execution branches and preserves static plan verification.
  2. No Iterative Loops (for, while, repeat): Transformation length must be statically bounded and unrollable.
  3. No Variables or Macros (let, const, eval): Eliminates scoping ambiguity and variable capture issues.
  4. No Custom Functions or Lambdas: Prevents execution of arbitrary code within recipe definitions.
  5. No User-Defined Types: Type system is closed and statically known to the compiler.
  6. No Recursion: All transformations are strictly finite linear sequences.
  7. No Embedded Foreign Scripts (No Python, Bash, Lua): Eliminates sandbox escape vectors and guarantees pure declarative data.
  8. No Parallel Execution Branches (DAG): v1 is strictly linear (\(O_1 \rightarrow O_2 \dots\)); DAG scheduling is reserved for v2.0.
  9. No Inline Numerical Computation: All numeric values must be explicit literals.
  10. No Side Effects Outside Model State: No network requests (except via terminal export adapters), no file system writes outside artifacts.output_dir, and no untracked telemetry.

docs.title: Reporting a Vulnerability
docs.text: We take the security of NeuralOps and its compiled kernel execution pipeline seriously. If you discover a security vulnerability, memory corruption flaw in CUDA/Triton kernels, or model deserialization exploit, please report it responsibly.

docs.title: How to Report
docs.text:
1. Do not create a public GitHub issue for undisclosed security vulnerabilities.
  2. Email your report to: security@neuralops.ai or open a private advisory on GitHub Security Advisories.
  3. Include the following details in your report:
  4. Component affected (e.g., neuralops.export.exporter, neuralops.integrations.tgi, Triton kernel memory offset).
  5. Minimal reproducible proof-of-concept (PoC) script.
  6. Operating system, PyTorch version, and CUDA / Triton driver versions.
  7. Potential impact (arbitrary code execution, host denial of service, memory out-of-bounds read/write).

docs.title: Secure Model Deserialization & Serialization Policy
docs.text:
• Pickle Security: NeuralOps enforces strict weights-only loading (weights_only=True via torch.load and native safetensors format) when loading serialized linear attention adapter weights.
  • Triton JIT Kernel Compilation: Kernel generation validates compilation block sizes, tensor bounds, and alignment to prevent buffer overruns on GPU SRAM/L1 cache.
  • Serving Adapters: The continuous batching adapters (tgi.py, sglang.py) enforce maximum request length limits and thread-safe lock isolation to guard against denial-of-service memory exhaustion attacks.

docs.title: Training Orchestration Verification Report
docs.text:
End-to-end verification of the post-surgery training loop and knowledge distillation healing pipeline.

  • Multi-Dataset Ingestion: Comma-separated tokenized datasets streaming verified.
  • Varlen Packing: Variable-length document packing with cu_seqlens boundaries verified.
  • Scheduler Parity: Warmup-Stable-Decay (wsd) learning rate trajectory verified.

docs.title: Attentions API Reference
docs.text:
NeuralOps registers exactly 131 canonical subquadratic, linear, recurrent, and low-rank attention mechanisms unified under neuralops.core.registry.ATTENTION_REGISTRY across 14 foundational architectural families.

Every attention mechanism implements the standard interface neuralops.core.base.BaseAttention and can be instantiated directly via factory constructors (neuralops.create_attention) or injected in-place into pre-trained transformer architectures via universal AST and topological surgery (neuralops.replace_attention).

docs.title: 1. Architectural Taxonomy (14 Foundational Families)
docs.text:
The 131 attention mechanisms are organized into 14 foundational architectural families, totaling exactly 131 registered modules:

# Architectural Family Count Primary Computational Regime State Complexity Representative Module Identifiers 1 Exact Softmax & IO-Aware Dense Attention 6 Compute-Bound / Quadratic Wall \(\mathcal{O}(L^2)\) full, full_attention, mqa, gqa_attention, flash_attention3, flash_attention3_fp8 2 Kernelized & Feature-Map Linear Attentions 15 Memory-Bound / Associative Scan \(\mathcal{O}(D^2)\) cosformer, cosformer_attention, performer_attention, regla_attention, eat_attention, chela_slay 3 Gated Linear Recurrences 11 Near-Knee / Chunked Scans \(\mathcal{O}(D^2)\) gated_linear_attention (GLA), decay_linear_attention, hgrn2_gated_layer, factorised_matrix_state 4 Delta-Rule Recurrences & Associative Memory 7 Near-Knee / Hardware Registers \(\mathcal{O}(D^2)\) gated_delta_net, kda_attention, hla_attention, nexus, phantom 5 Continuous-Time & Selective State-Space Models (SSMs) 6 Register-Pinned Associative Scan \(\mathcal{O}(D \cdot N)\) selective_ssm, \cdot D)\) svd_linear_attention, asvd_attention, residual_svd_attention, linformer_attention, spectraformer_attention 8 Multi-Head Latent & Key-Value Compressed Attentions 9 Memory-Bound / KV Minimization \(\mathcal{O}(d_c)\) mla_attention (DeepSeek MLA), qcqa_attention, token_compressed_attention, compressed_mha_attention 9 Hybrid Linear-Recurrent & Attention-SSM Architectures 14 Dynamic Dispatch / Mixed Dynamic jamba, samba_m3, griffin_ssd, hymba_transx, granite_hybrid, hybrid_attention, aegis_hybrid 10 Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) & Sparsely-Gated Attentions 6 Dynamic Routing / Sparse Execution \(\mathcal{O}(K \cdot D)\) bam_umoe, expert_choice_moe, reap_moe, samba_moe, moe_deltakv_paged, mixattention_moska 11 Test-Time Training (TTT) & Fast-Weight Systems 2 Online Optimization / Gradient Steps \(\mathcal{O}(D^2)\) ttt_linear_attention, template_attention 12 Memory-Augmented & External Latent Recurrences 4 External Memory Cache / Retrieval \(\mathcal{O}(M \cdot D)\) spectron_fp8, aegis_spectron_fp8, aegis_v1–aegis_v6, vig_attention, vspec

[!NOTE] Summing across all 14 families: \(6 + 15 + 11 + 7 + 6 + 13 + 19 + 9 + 14 + 6 + 2 + 4 + 5 + 14 = \mathbf{131}\) canonical attention mechanisms. All benchmark results, execution logs, and LaTeX tables are publicly mirrored at: 👉 https://huggingface.co/datasets/Hooshaai/neuralops-results

docs.title: 2.1 Exact Softmax & IO-Aware Dense Attention (6 Modules)
docs.text:
• Module IDs: full, full_attention, mqa, gqa_attention, flash_attention3, flash_attention3_fp8
  • Mathematical Operator: $\(\text{Attention}(Q, K, V) = \text{softmax}\left(\frac{Q K^\top}{\sqrt{d_k}} + M\right) V\)$
  • Hardware Profile: High arithmetic intensity, but bounded by quadratic \(\mathcal{O}(L^2)\) memory bandwidth and KV-cache footprint during autoregressive decoding.

docs.title: 2.2 Kernelized & Feature-Map Linear Attentions (15 Modules)
docs.text:
• Module IDs: cosformer, cosformer_attention, performer_attention, positive_kernel_linear_attention, galerkin_attention, regla_attention, halo_regla, eat, eat_attention, chela_slay, chela_slay_attention, triton_cosformer, rpc_attention, zeros_attention, xattention
  • Mathematical Operator: $\(O_i = \frac{\sum_{j=1}^i \phi(Q_i) \phi(K_j)^\top V_j}{\sum_{j=1}^i \phi(Q_i) \phi(K_j)^\top}\)$ Using the associative property: \(\sum_{j} (\phi(Q_i) \phi(K_j)^\top) V_j = \phi(Q_i) \left( \sum_{j} \phi(K_j)^\top V_j \right)\), reducing complexity to \(\mathcal{O}(L \cdot D^2)\) with \(\mathcal{O}(D^2)\) constant state memory.

docs.title: 2.3 Gated Linear Recurrences (11 Modules)
docs.text:
• Module IDs: gated_linear_attention (GLA), gated_linear_attn, gla_attention, decay_linear_attention, decay_linear_attn, factorised_matrix_state, hgrn2_gated_layer, hgrn2_gated_outer, hgrn2_outer, goldfinch_ahn, salt_attention
  • Mathematical Operator: $\(S_t = \alpha_t \odot S_{t-1} + K_t^\top V_t, \quad O_t = Q_t S_t\)$ where \(\alpha_t = \exp(-\text{softplus}(\beta_t))\) provides data-dependent forgetting, computed via parallel chunk-wise associative scans in Triton.

docs.title: 2.4 Delta-Rule Recurrences & Associative Memory (7 Modules)
docs.text:
• Module IDs: gated_delta_net, gated_deltanet_block, hgrn2_gated_deltanet, kda_attention (Kronecker Delta Attention), hla_attention, nexus, phantom
  • Mathematical Operator: $\(S_t = S_{t-1} + \beta_t (V_t - S_{t-1} K_t) K_t^\top\)$ Updates hidden memory via the error-driven Delta rule, preventing capacity saturation in associative recall tasks.

docs.title: 2.5 Continuous-Time & Selective State-Space Models (SSMs) (6 Modules)
docs.text:
• Module IDs: selective_ssm, simple_ssm, mamba_block (S6), upi_stuffed_mamba, mamba_svd_flash, svd_mamba
  • Mathematical Operator: $\(h_t = \bar{A}_t h_{t-1} + \bar{B}_t x_t, \quad y_t = C_t h_t + D x_t\)$ where input-dependent discretization \(\Delta_t = \text{softplus}(\text{Linear}(x_t))\) allows selective filtering across continuous sequence trajectories.

docs.title: 2.6 Block-Sparse, Dilated & Sliding-Window Attentions (13 Modules)
docs.text:
• Module IDs: adaptive_span_attention, adaptive_sparse_attention, adasplash_attention, cluster_attention, block_transformer_hiba, nsa_attention, lsh_attention, routing_attention, sink_attention, dynamic_conv_attention, hamming_attention, moba_attention, progressive_token_pruning
  • Characteristics: Enforces band-limited or block-diagonal attention masks, bounding token interactions to local context windows \(W\) with \(\mathcal{O}(L \cdot W \cdot D)\) time complexity.

docs.title: 2.7 SVD Spectral & Low-Rank Decomposed Attentions (19 Modules)
docs.text:
• Module IDs: linformer_attention, nystrom_attention, asvd_attention, svd_linear, svd_linear_attention, svd_linear_attn, svd_linear_decay, svd_linear_inject, svd_llm_v2_attention, adaptive_svd_attention, residual_svd_attention, svd_projection_attention, svd_seq, svd_compressed, naive_svd, minimal_svd, spectraformer_attention, fused_svd_kernel, triton_svd_linear_attention
  • Mathematical Operator: $\(W \approx U_r \Sigma_r V_r^\top \implies Q = X W_q \approx (X U_r) (\Sigma_r V_r^\top)\)$ Projects sequence representations through an optimal Eckart-Young-Mirsky rank-\(r\) bottleneck, reducing parameter counts and FLOPs.

docs.title: 2.8 Multi-Head Latent & Key-Value Compressed Attentions (9 Modules)
docs.text:
• Module IDs: mla_attention (DeepSeek Multi-Head Latent Attention), qcqa_attention, compressed_attention, compressed_mha_attention, token_compressed_attention, projection_factorized_attn, lola_attention, padre_attention, lora_attention
  • Characteristics: Compresses Key-Value representations into low-dimensional latent vectors \(c^{KV}_t \in \mathbb{R}^{d_c}\) (\(d_c \ll H \cdot d_h\)), reducing inference KV-cache memory consumption by up to \(6\times\).

docs.title: 2.9 Hybrid Linear-Recurrent & Attention-SSM Architectures (14 Modules)
docs.text:
• Module IDs: jamba, jamba_info, samba_m3, griffin_ssd, hymba_transx, granite_hybrid, hybrid_attention, native_hybrid_attention, optimized_hybrid_attention, split_head_hybrid, tri_branch_hybrid, hybrid_local_kernel, aegis_hybrid, minimal_nova
  • Characteristics: Seamlessly interleaves Transformer attention layers and recurrent/SSM blocks to combine exact syntactic precision with linear long-context throughput.

docs.title: 2.10 Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) & Sparsely-Gated Attentions (6 Modules)
docs.text:
• Module IDs: bam_umoe, expert_choice_moe, reap_moe, samba_moe, moe_deltakv_paged, mixattention_moska
  • Characteristics: Dynamically routes tokens across sparse sets of specialized attention heads or expert projections using warp-synchronous gating kernels.

docs.title: 2.11 Test-Time Training (TTT) & Fast-Weight Systems (2 Modules)
docs.text:
• Module IDs: ttt_linear_attention, template_attention
  • Characteristics: Treats hidden state updates as an inner-loop online self-supervised gradient step, continually adjusting weights during forward inference.

docs.title: 2.12 Memory-Augmented & External Latent Recurrences (4 Modules)
docs.text:
• Module IDs: landmark_local_attention, refined_landmark_attention, rala_attention, nasc_attention
  • Characteristics: Maintains persistent external memory slots and landmark tokens to route context across arbitrarily long sequences.

docs.title: 2.13 Modern Positional, Rotary & Geometric Attention Variants (5 Modules)
docs.text:
• Module IDs: alibi, unified_rope, wgqa_attention, cross_attention, primal_attention
  • Characteristics: Injects geometric and relative distance inductive biases into key-query inner products via linear slope penalties (ALiBi) or complex rotation angles (RoPE).

docs.title: 2.14 Hardware-Fused, Low-Precision & Spectral-Transform Attentions (14 Modules)
docs.text:
• Module IDs: spectron, spectron_fp8, aegis_spectron_fp8, aegis_v1, aegis_v2, aegis_v3, aegis_v4, aegis_v5, aegis_v6, soa_attn, fusion_attn, orion, vig_attention, vspec
  • Characteristics: Fused Fast Walsh-Hadamard Transforms (FWHT), FP8 Tensor Core quantization, and fused SRAM execution eliminating DRAM roundtrips.

docs.title: neuralops.create_attention
docs.text:
def create_attention(
    name: str,
    config: Any = None,
    dim: int | None = None,
    num_heads: int | None = None,
    embed_dim: int | None = None,
    rank: int | None = None,
    **kwargs: Any,
) -> nn.Module

Universal factory constructing any registered attention mechanism from ATTENTION_REGISTRY. Normalizes hyperparameter aliases (embed_dim, dim, d_model, num_heads, heads, rank) automatically.

Parameters: - name (str): Canonical attention mechanism identifier. - config (Any, optional): Optional architectural configuration dataclass. - embed_dim / dim (int, optional): Hidden embedding dimension (e.g., 768, 2048, 4096). - num_heads (int, optional): Number of attention heads (e.g., 12, 16, 32). - rank (int, optional): Low-rank bottleneck dimension for SVD-based variants. - **kwargs: Mechanism-specific hyperparameters forwarded to the constructor.

Example: 

import torch
import neuralops

attn = neuralops.create_attention(
    "gated_delta_net",
    embed_dim=768,
    num_heads=12,
)

x = torch.randn(2, 64, 768)
out = attn(x)
print("Output shape:", out.shape)  # torch.Size([2, 64, 768])

docs.text:
def replace_attention(
    model: nn.Module,
    attention: Optional[str] = None,
    rank: Optional[int] = None,
    copy_weights: bool = True,
    layers: Optional[List[int]] = None,
    attention_type: Optional[str] = None,
    **kwargs: Any,

Drop-in replace attention layers in any PyTorch or Hugging Face model (GPT-2, LLaMA, Mistral, BERT, RoBERTa, Qwen) in-place, preserving model configuration, topology, and parameters.

Parameters: - model (nn.Module): PyTorch or Hugging Face Transformer model to transplant. - attention (str, optional): Target attention mechanism from neuralops.list_attentions(). - rank (int, optional): Rank parameter for low-rank or SVD-based attention variants. - copy_weights (bool): Whether to transplant weights from the original attention projections. - layers (List[int], optional): Subset of layer indices to replace (default: replaces all). - **kwargs: Mechanism-specific constructor arguments forwarded to the new attention module.

docs.title: Compression Engines API Reference
docs.text:
NeuralOps registers exactly 72 canonical model compression engines unified under neuralops.core.registry.COMPRESSOR_REGISTRY across 8 foundational algorithmic paradigms.

All compression engines implement calibrated low-rank matrix decomposition, structured pruning, integer/floating-point quantization, tensor networks, or dynamic KV-cache compression to drastically reduce VRAM footprints and accelerate inference while preserving model accuracy.

docs.title: 1. Algorithmic Taxonomy (8 Foundational Paradigms)
docs.text:
The 72 compression engines span 8 foundational algorithmic paradigms, totaling exactly 72 registered engines:

# Paradigm Key Paradigm Name Count Typical Ratio Speedup Representative Engine Identifiers 1 svd Low-Rank SVD Factorization 16 2x – 6x 1.3x – 2.4x fwsvd_compressor, adasvd_compressor, direct_svd, residual_svd_compressor, swift_svd, dobi_svd, erc_svd 2 dynamic_rank Adaptive & Dynamic Rank Allocation 11 2x – 5x 1.2x – 2.0x adaptive_ranks, come_compressor, dynamic_rank, entropy_budget_allocation, grecodec_compressor, sdrm_compressor 3 pruning Structured Pruning & Sparsity 10 2x – 4x 1.2x – 1.8x admm_pruner, sparsegpt, wanda_engine, flap, mamba_shedder, proxsparse, armor_pruner, bonsai_pruner 4 subspace Subspace & Residual Projection 9 3x – 8x 1.2x – 1.6x optimal_subspace_projection, subspace_projection, drone_compressor, enlighten_compressor, liftr, oats_compressor 5 tensor_decomp Tensor Network Decompositions 8 4x – 16x 1.2x – 1.6x tt_compressor, kronecker_compressor, kronecker_tt_lora, cur_compressor, cur_moe_compressor, rpca_compressor 6 quant Integer & Floating-Point Quantization 7 4x – 8x 1.4x – 2.0x faq_quantizer, rotational_slicegpt_int4, uniql_compressor, astro_quantizer, coopq_quantizer, huffman_coder 7 kv_cache KV-Cache Optimization & Compression 6 2x – 6x 1.5x – 3.2x aatc_xkv_compressor, cachenotes_compressor, delta_kv, hybridkv_compressor, kvtc_compressor, zerokv_neo_compressor 8 rotational Rotational Invariance Transforms 5 2x – 4x 1.3x – 1.7x slicegpt, slicegpt_pca, flat_llm, hashed_net_compressor, roast_hashed_linear

[!NOTE] Summing across all 8 paradigms: \(16 + 11 + 10 + 9 + 8 + 7 + 6 + 5 = \mathbf{72}\) canonical compression engines. All empirical compression Pareto curves, WikiText-2 perplexity benchmarks, and GLUE retention matrices are available on Hugging Face: 👉 https://huggingface.co/datasets/Hooshaai/neuralops-results

docs.title: 2.1 Low-Rank SVD Factorization (svd — 16 Engines)
docs.text:
• Module IDs: a3_compressor, aa_svd_compressor, adasvd_compressor, direct_svd, dobi_svd, erc_svd, frandi_compressor, fwsvd_compressor, hybrid_svd_layer, residual_svd_compressor, saes_svd_v2, salr, svd_linear, svd_llm_compressor, swift_svd, swift_svd_act
  • Mathematical Principle: Given weight matrix \(W \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{out}} \times d_{\text{in}}}\) and activation covariance \(C_X = \mathbb{E}[X^\top X]\), whitening transforms the optimization space: $\(\tilde{W} = W C_X^{1/2} = U \Sigma V^\top\)$ Truncating to rank \(r\) minimizes empirical reconstruction error \(\|(W - \hat{W}) X\|_F^2\): $\(\hat{W} = U_r \Sigma_r V_r^\top C_X^{-1/2} = A B, \quad A \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{out}} \times r}, \; B \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times d_{\text{in}}}\)$

docs.title: 2.2 Adaptive & Dynamic Rank Allocation (dynamic_rank — 11 Engines)
docs.text:
• Module IDs: adaptive_ranks, come_compressor, dynamic_rank, entropy_budget_allocation, gfws, grecodec_compressor, mgie_budget, mlorq_compressor, modegpt_compressor, sdrm_compressor, soka_compressor
  • Mathematical Principle: Instead of uniform rank \(r\) across all layers, dynamically allocates rank budgets based on layer-wise singular value entropy \(\mathcal{H}_l = -\sum_i \bar{\sigma}_{l,i} \log \bar{\sigma}_{l,i}\) and Hessian eigenspectrum curvature, allocating higher rank to sensitive early layers.

docs.title: 2.3 Structured Pruning & Sparsity (pruning — 10 Engines)
docs.text:
• Module IDs: admm_compressor, admm_pruner, armor_pruner, ast_pruner, bonsai_pruner, flap, mamba_shedder, proxsparse, slim_compressor, sparsegpt
  • Mathematical Principle: Solves constrained \(\ell_0\) or \(\ell_{2,1}\) group-sparse minimization via Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM) or second-order Taylor approximations: $\(\min_W \mathcal{L}(W) + \frac{\rho}{2} \|W - Z + U\|_F^2 \quad \text{s.t.} \quad \|Z_{\text{cols}}\|_0 \le k\)$

docs.title: 2.4 Subspace & Residual Projection (subspace — 9 Engines)
docs.text:
• Module IDs: cr_compressor, drone_compressor, enlighten_compressor, liftr, lsc_compressor, oats_compressor, optimal_subspace_projection, subspace_projection, tomoe_compressor
  • Mathematical Principle: Projects layer activations into orthogonal principal subspaces, decomposing operations into a shared invariant basis plus small residual corrections.

docs.title: 2.5 Tensor Network Decompositions (tensor_decomp — 8 Engines)
docs.text:
• Module IDs: compot_compressor, cur_compressor, cur_moe_compressor, kronecker_compressor, kronecker_tt_lora, nmf_compressor, rpca_compressor, tt_compressor
  • Mathematical Principle: Decomposes high-order weight tensors into Tensor-Train (TT) cores (\(W = G_1 G_2 \cdots G_d\)) or Kronecker matrix products (\(W = A \otimes B\)), unlocking exponential theoretical parameter reduction.

docs.title: 2.6 Integer & Floating-Point Quantization (quant — 7 Engines)
docs.text:
• Module IDs: astro_quantizer, coopq_quantizer, faq_quantizer, huffman_coder, kmeans_quantize, rotational_slicegpt_int4, uniql_compressor
  • Mathematical Principle: Maps continuous FP16/FP32 weights to discrete low-bit grids (INT8, INT4, FP4 MX format) using optimal asymmetric scales and zero-points: $\(W_q = \text{clamp}\left(\left\lfloor \frac{W}{S} \right\rceil + Z, -2^{b-1}, 2^{b-1}-1\right)\)$

docs.title: 2.7 KV-Cache Optimization & Compression (kv_cache — 6 Engines)
docs.text:
• Module IDs: aatc_xkv_compressor, cachenotes_compressor, delta_kv, hybridkv_compressor, kvtc_compressor, zerokv_neo_compressor
  • Mathematical Principle: Reduces KV-cache memory footprints during generation via delta compression (\(K_t - K_{t-1}\)), attention sink retention, and importance-driven token shedding.

docs.title: 2.8 Rotational Invariance Transforms (rotational — 5 Engines)
docs.text:
• Module IDs: flat_llm, hashed_net_compressor, roast_hashed_linear, slicegpt, slicegpt_pca
  • Mathematical Principle: Applies orthogonal rotation matrices \(Q \in \mathbb{O}(D)\) (such as randomized Hadamard transforms) to eliminate activation outliers across channels, enabling aggressive 25%–40% column slicing without perplexity collapse.

docs.title: neuralops.create_compressor
docs.text:
def create_compressor(
    name: str,
    model: Any = None,
    rank: int | None = None,
    **kwargs: Any,
) -> Any

Instantiates any of the 72 registered compression engines from COMPRESSOR_REGISTRY.

Parameters: - name (str): Canonical compressor name (e.g., "fwsvd_compressor", "adasvd_compressor", "sparsegpt", "slicegpt"). - model (nn.Module, optional): Model instance to compress. - rank (int, optional): Target low-rank bottleneck or compression rank. - **kwargs: Hyperparameters forwarded to the compressor constructor.

Example: 

import neuralops

# Create Fisher-Weighted SVD compressor targeting rank 32
compressor = neuralops.create_compressor(
    "fwsvd_compressor",
    model=model,
    rank=32,
)
compressed_model = compressor.compress()

docs.title: Serving Integrations API Reference
docs.text: NeuralOps provides production serving adapters for high-throughput concurrent inference across Hugging Face Transformers, vLLM, Text Generation Inference (TGI), SGLang, and TensorRT-LLM.

docs.title: PagedKVCache
docs.text:
Location: neuralops.inference.paged_cache.PagedKVCache

class PagedKVCache:
    def __init__(
        self,
        num_blocks: int,
        block_size: int,
        num_heads: int,
        head_dim: int,
        dtype: torch.dtype = torch.float32,
        device: str | torch.device = "cpu",
    ) -> None

Manages non-contiguous physical blocks of Key/Value tensors per sequence (vLLM-style paging). Eliminates memory fragmentation with dynamic block allocation, virtual-to-physical block tables, zero-copy sequence forking, Copy-on-Write (CoW), and online defragmentation.

Core Methods: - allocate_sequence(seq_id: int) -> None: Registers a new sequence with an initial allocated block. - fork_sequence(parent_seq_id: int, child_seq_id: int) -> list[int]: Forks an active sequence sharing existing blocks with incremented reference counts. - copy_on_write(seq_id: int, block_idx: int) -> int: Copies a shared physical block to a private allocated block upon token modification. - append_token(seq_id: int, key: torch.Tensor, value: torch.Tensor) -> tuple[int, int]: Appends key and value vectors into the sequence's current block slot. - get_kv(seq_id: int) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]: Materializes the logical KV cache up to current sequence length. - get_fragmentation_stats() -> dict[str, Any]: Reports total blocks, free blocks, allocated blocks, and external fragmentation percentage. - defragment() -> dict[str, Any]: Compacts physical blocks in-place into contiguous memory. - free_sequence(seq_id: int) -> None: Frees all blocks belonging to the sequence, decrementing reference counts.

docs.title: PagedStateTable (Subquadratic Recurrent State Management)
docs.text:
Location: neuralops.models.paged_state.PagedStateTable

class PagedStateTable:
    def __init__(
        self,
        num_pages: int,
        num_heads: int,
        head_dim: int,
        dtype: torch.dtype = torch.float32,
        device: str | torch.device = "cpu",
    ) -> None

Virtualized recurrent state table for linear attention (GLA, Gated DeltaNet, RetNet) and SSM (Mamba, S6) models: - Maintains \(\mathcal{O}(1)\) constant state memory per token during autoregressive generation. - Zero-copy sequence branching for beam search and speculative decoding. - Dynamic page table translation with Copy-on-Write isolation.

docs.title: ContinuousBatcher
docs.text:
Location: neuralops.inference.engine.ContinuousBatcher

class ContinuousBatcher:
    def __init__(
        self,
        model: nn.Module | None = None,
        max_batch_size: int = 8,
        max_seq_len: int = 2048,
    ) -> None

Dynamic iteration-level batch scheduler admitting incoming requests on-the-fly without waiting for complete sequence generations to finish.

Core Methods: - add_request(request_id: str, input_ids: torch.Tensor, max_new_tokens: int = 16): Admits a new generation request into the pending queue. - step(model: nn.Module | None = None) -> list[dict[str, Any]]: Executes a single autoregressive decoding step across all currently active batch slots and yields emitted token dictionaries {"request_id": str, "token": int, "finished": bool}.

docs.title: Text Generation Inference (TGIServingAdapter)
docs.text:
Location: neuralops.integrations.tgi.TGIServingAdapter

docs.title: Kernels API Reference
docs.text: NeuralOps implements 26 canonical Triton JIT kernel modules (housing 62 unified JIT operators across 4 architectural tiers) and 112 Native CUDA C++ Packages (housing 114 native implementations) delivering fused subquadratic sequence modeling, paged state management, and fused training objectives.

docs.title: 1. 3-Level Fallback Hierarchy
docs.text:
Every compute operator in NeuralOps conforms to the strict 3-level fallback execution hierarchy:

┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Level 1: Native CUDA C++ Extension (Max Throughput)    │
│  - NVCC compiled intrinsics, warp shuffles, tensor core│
│  - 112 packages housing 114 native implementations     │
└───────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────┘
                            │ (Fallback if CUDA uncompiled, with logger.warning)
┌───────────────────────────▼────────────────────────────┐
│ Level 2: Triton JIT Kernel (Autotuned GPU Compilation) │
│  - Autotuned 2D/3D tiles, FP16/BF16/FP32, zero block-ptr│
│  - 26 canonical modules housing 62 unified operators   │
└───────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────┘
                            │ (Fallback if non-CUDA or MPS/CPU, with logger.warning)
┌───────────────────────────▼────────────────────────────┐
│ Level 3: Vectorized PyTorch Reference (Universal CPU)  │
│  - Pure torch.Tensor fallback, exact numerical parity  │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Backend selection uses zero-allocation dispatch tables cached via @lru_cache. Backend forcing is accessible via neuralops.core.dispatch.force_kernel_backend.

docs.title: 3. Native CUDA C++ Kernel Suite (112 Packages, 114 Implementations)
docs.text: The native CUDA C++ kernel suite is implemented in neuralops/core/cuda_kernels/ and neuralops/csrc/. Key highlights: - 112 Modular Kernel Packages: Including moe_routing, hgrn2_fused_bwd_scan, linear_attention, selective_scan, chunked_delta_gate_scan, paged_attention, sliding_window_attn, lut_codebook_dequant_gemm, flash_gqa, cosformer_linear_attention, and fused_rotary_emb. - Warp-Level Shuffles: __shfl_xor_sync and __shfl_down_sync eliminate shared memory roundtrips during reduction trees. - 128-bit Vectorized Memory Loads: float4 and int4 memory transactions maximizing DRAM bus utilization. - Shared Memory Padding: Resolves bank conflicts across parallel warp access patterns.

docs.text: All kernels are empirically benchmarked on physical hardware: - Primary Physical Testbed: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 (Ada Lovelace SM 8.9, AD104 silicon). - Physical Specifications: 5,888 CUDA cores, 46 SMs, 184 Tensor Cores (4th gen), 160.2 TFLOPS boost / 141.6 base FP16, 504.0 GB/s GDDR6X, Arithmetic Intensity Ridge Point \(I^* = 317.9\text{ FLOP/Byte}\), 12 GB VRAM. - Master Benchmark Dataset: https://huggingface.co/datasets/Hooshaai/neuralops-results.

docs.title: Experiment Results Ledger & Provenance API
docs.text:
NeuralOps features an immutable, dual-storage Experiment Results Ledger designed for scientific reproducibility, cryptographic provenance, and zero-fake verification.

Every benchmark execution, kernel profile, and downstream fine-tuning run is recorded with exact hardware telemetry, Git commit SHAs, driver versions, and physical timestamp metadata.

docs.title: 1. Dual-Storage Architecture
docs.text:
The results ledger synchronizes across two complementary storage formats:

  1. Human-Readable JSONL (.jsonl): Git-friendly line-delimited JSON enabling fine-grained diff tracking, commit review, and stream parsing.
  2. High-Performance SQLite (.sqlite): Indexed relational database supporting rapid SQL aggregation, multi-dimensional queries, and automated LaTeX table generation.
+-------------------------------------------------------------------+
|               NeuralOps Experiment Results Ledger                 |
+-------------------------------------------------------------------+
           |                                             |
           v                                             v
  Git-Friendly Stream                            Indexed Query Engine
  results_ledger.jsonl                           results_ledger.sqlite
  (Full Run Telemetry)                           (Relational Projections)
           \                                             /
            +--------------------+----------------------+
                                 |
                                 v
        Hugging Face Hub Master Benchmark Dataset:
        https://huggingface.co/datasets/Hooshaai/neuralops-results

docs.title: 2. Official Hugging Face Dataset
docs.text:
All benchmark records, raw telemetry logs, and SQLite database snapshots are mirrored and versioned in the official Hugging Face benchmark repository:

👉 https://huggingface.co/datasets/Hooshaai/neuralops-results

docs.title: Repository Contents
docs.text:
• results_master.sqlite: SQLite master ledger containing all 203 verified module runs, 131 attentions, and 72 compression sweeps.
  • benchmarks_telemetry.jsonl: Timestamped hardware telemetry logs with GPU temperature, VRAM allocation, and arithmetic intensity.
  • latex_tables/: Publication-grade .tex tables matching verified ledger figures for empirical papers.

docs.title: 3. Physical Hardware Telemetry Invariants
docs.text: All empirical data points in the results ledger are grounded in physical execution on: - Silicon: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 (Ada Lovelace SM 8.9, AD104 silicon). - Hardware Profile: 5,888 CUDA cores, 46 SMs, 184 Tensor Cores (4th gen), 160.2 TFLOPS boost / 141.6 base FP16, 504.0 GB/s GDDR6X, Arithmetic Intensity Ridge Point \(I^* = 317.9\text{ FLOP/Byte}\), 12 GB VRAM. - Institution: Department of Computer Engineering, College of Engineering, University of Tehran.

docs.title: Recording an Experiment Result
docs.text:
import neuralops
from neuralops.benchmarks.results_ledger import ResultsLedger, BenchmarkRecord

# Initialize ledger pointing to local storage
ledger = ResultsLedger(
    jsonl_path="results/results_ledger.jsonl",
    sqlite_path="results/results_ledger.sqlite",
)

# Record benchmark execution with provenance
record = BenchmarkRecord(
    module_name="gdn_scan",
    family="delta_recurrence",
    model="gpt2",
    sequence_length=2048,
    batch_size=2,
    dtype="float16",
    latency_ms=0.364,
    speedup=4.51,
    peak_vram_mb=264.0,
    arithmetic_intensity=138.5,
    achieved_tflops=36.4,
    status="PASS_FAST",
    hardware="NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 (SM 8.9)",
)
ledger.record(record)

docs.title: Querying the Ledger
docs.text:
# Query top-performing kernels by speedup
top_kernels = ledger.query_sql("""
    SELECT module_name, speedup, achieved_tflops, peak_vram_mb
    FROM benchmarks
    WHERE status = 'PASS_FAST' AND sequence_length = 2048
    ORDER BY speedup DESC
    LIMIT 10
""")

for row in top_kernels:
    print(f"{row['module_name']:<25} | {row['speedup']:.2f}x | {row['achieved_tflops']:.1f} TFLOPS")
