docs.title: NeuralOps Component Folders: Complete Architecture Audit and Integration Plan
Scope
docs.text:
This document audits the component folders shown in the project tree and maps how they should connect:

inference
integrations
kernels
layers
models
operations
ops
optimization
pipeline_transform
recipe
reporting
results_saver
runners

The purpose is to remove architectural ambiguity. Each folder should have one clear responsibility, one public entry boundary, and explicit data contracts to the folders around it.

docs.title: Executive finding
docs.text:
The repository already contains most of the required capabilities, but they are not yet organized as one linear product pipeline. There are several overlapping concepts:

  • ops/, kernels/, and parts of layers/ all look like kernel owners;
  • results_saver/, reporting/, benchmark result writers, and runner writers all look like result owners;
  • runners/, benchmark orchestrators, pipeline executors, and CLI handlers all look like workflow owners;
  • recipe/, pipeline_transform/, and operations/ all describe how a model is changed;
  • inference/, models/, and integrations/ all contain runtime/model execution concerns.

The cleanup should not delete these capabilities. It should establish a strict direction of dependencies and adapters between them.

docs.title: 1. Target dependency graph
docs.text:
The desired high-level flow is:

CLI / API
   |
   v
recipe.schema + recipe.loader
   |
   v
operations (what to change)
   |
   v
pipeline_transform (how to plan/apply/rollback)
   |
   +----------------------+
   v                      v
models                layers
   |                      |
   +-----------> ops/kernels
                      |
                      v
                 inference
                      |
                      v
               integrations
                      |
                      v
             reporting/results_saver
                      |
                      v
                    runners

runners orchestrates the whole operation but must not own implementation logic. It calls the public interfaces of the other folders.

docs.title: Allowed direction
docs.text:
recipe -> operations -> pipeline_transform -> models/layers/ops
models -> layers -> ops
inference -> models/ops/integrations
reporting -> all read-only metadata/result contracts
results_saver -> reporting/result contracts
runners -> all public package APIs

docs.title: Forbidden direction
docs.text:
• layers must not import runners.
  • ops must not import CLI code, reporting, or result persistence.
  • results_saver must not execute model transformations.
  • reporting must not mutate model weights.
  • integrations must not reimplement the registry.
  • pipeline_transform must not write directly to arbitrary result files.
  • runners must not reach into private implementation symbols when a public adapter exists.

docs.title: Current role
docs.text:
This folder contains runtime execution components:

engine.py
paged_cache.py
pipeline_parallel.py
speculative_decoding.py

docs.title: It should own
docs.text:
• prefill and decode execution;
  • request batching and scheduling;
  • KV-cache lifecycle;
  • speculative decoding control flow;
  • pipeline-parallel inference coordination.

docs.title: It should not own
docs.text:
• model surgery or compression algorithms;
  • registry discovery;
  • benchmark result serialization;
  • vendor-specific serving integration code.

docs.title: Required connections
docs.text:
models -> inference.engine
inference.engine -> inference.paged_cache
inference.engine -> inference.speculative_decoding
inference.engine -> integrations.serving adapters
inference.engine -> reporting telemetry

docs.title: Problems to audit
docs.text:
1. Device and dtype selection must come from one runtime config, not be inferred independently by engine and cache.
  2. KV-cache shape/layout must be declared in a protocol shared with vLLM, SGLang, and TensorRT-LLM adapters.
  3. Speculative decoding must report accepted/rejected draft tokens rather than only final latency.
  4. Pipeline parallel failures must identify stage and rank.
  5. Cache allocation failures must be visible as FAIL_RESOURCE, not converted to an empty cache or a CPU path.

docs.title: Recommended public API
docs.text:
class InferenceRequest:
    request_id: str
    input_ids: torch.Tensor
    max_new_tokens: int
    sampling: SamplingConfig


class InferenceResult:
    request_id: str
    output_ids: torch.Tensor
    ttft_ms: float
    itl_ms: float
    accepted_draft_tokens: int
    backend: str


class InferenceEngine:
    def generate(self, request: InferenceRequest) -> InferenceResult: ...

docs.title: Current role
docs.text:
This folder contains adapters for external ecosystems:

hf_automodel.py
vllm.py / vllm/
sglang.py / sglang/
tensorrt_llm.py / tensorrt_llm_plugin/
tgi.py
serving.py
compressed_tensors.py
distributed_compile.py
fla/

docs.title: It should own
docs.text:
• external API adapters;
  • conversion between NeuralOps contracts and vendor contracts;
  • optional dependency detection;
  • version compatibility checks;
  • external cache/engine metadata translation.

docs.title: It should not own
docs.text:
• canonical attention/compressor registries;
  • core numerical implementations;
  • benchmark pass/fail policy;
  • silent fallback to another vendor.

docs.title: Design requirement: capability adapters
docs.text:
Each integration should expose a capability object rather than forcing callers to import vendor internals:

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class IntegrationCapabilities:
    name: str
    version: str | None
    available: bool
    supports_cuda: bool
    supports_streaming: bool
    supports_paged_kv: bool
    reason_unavailable: str | None = None


class ServingIntegration(Protocol):
    def capabilities(self) -> IntegrationCapabilities: ...
    def load(self, config: ServingConfig) -> ServingBackend: ...

docs.title: Problems to audit
docs.text:
1. Optional imports must not happen at package import time.
  2. An unavailable vLLM/SGLang/TensorRT-LLM dependency must produce an explicit unavailable capability, not a fake benchmark row.
  3. All adapters must use the same ServingConfig and KVCacheSpec.
  4. Version checks must be centralized and testable.
  5. External exceptions must preserve the original error and integration name.

docs.title: Current role
docs.text: This is a high-level kernel namespace containing extended_kernels.py and backend package markers.

docs.title: Recommended role
docs.text:
Make this folder a public kernel facade only:

neuralops.kernels
  -> public operator names
  -> dispatch to ops/cuda, ops/triton, ops/pytorch

It should not contain a second implementation of a kernel already owned by ops/.

docs.title: Problems to audit
docs.text:
• duplicate symbols between kernels/extended_kernels.py and ops/;
  • unclear distinction between public operator and backend implementation;
  • backend imports that trigger JIT compilation during import;
  • no unified metadata describing actual backend used.

docs.title: Target API
docs.text:
from neuralops.kernels import dispatch_kernel

result = dispatch_kernel(
    "selective_scan",
    inputs,
    backend="auto",
    strict=True,
)

The returned object should include output, backend_used, fallbacks, and max_diff when a reference parity check was requested.

docs.title: Current role
docs.text: This is the canonical module implementation layer for attention mechanisms and related neural layers. It contains families such as linear, gated, hybrid, modern, sparse, ssm, svd, and fast_kernels.

docs.title: It should own
docs.text:
• torch.nn.Module implementations;
  • shape/dtype/causal contracts;
  • differentiable forward and backward behavior;
  • module-level use of kernel facades.

docs.title: It should not own
docs.text:
• benchmark orchestration;
  • direct CSV/Parquet writing;
  • vendor serving adapters;
  • model checkpoint transaction logic.

docs.title: Every layer should expose
docs.text:
class AttentionContract:
    name: str
    supports_causal: bool
    supports_gqa: bool
    supported_dtypes: tuple[torch.dtype, ...]
    backend_preferences: tuple[str, ...]


class MyAttention(nn.Module):
    contract: AttentionContract

    def forward(
        self,
        query: torch.Tensor,
        key: torch.Tensor,
        value: torch.Tensor,
        *,
        is_causal: bool = False,
        **kwargs: object,
    ) -> torch.Tensor: ...

docs.title: Problems to audit
docs.text:
1. Some layers contain backend selection logic that should move to kernel dispatch.
  2. Causal-mask semantics need a shared test contract.
  3. Input aliases (dim, hidden_size, d_model) should be normalized by the registry factory, not reimplemented in every class.
  4. Triton or CUDA failures must not be swallowed inside a layer.
  5. Every layer must have a reference implementation path for correctness tests.

docs.title: Current role
docs.text: This folder contains model wrappers, configuration, model loading, CUDA graph, cache, RoPE, hybrid blocks, and surgical I/O.

docs.title: It should own
docs.text:
• model architecture composition;
  • loading and saving model checkpoints;
  • model-level configuration;
  • model-to-layer wiring;
  • model-level cache and graph state.

docs.title: It should not own
docs.text:
• compression algorithm implementations;
  • benchmark timing utilities;
  • vendor engine adapters.

docs.title: Required connections
docs.text:
models.hub -> integrations.hf_automodel
models.modeling -> layers + kernels
models.surgical_io -> operations.export + recipe manifests
models.cache/paged_state -> inference.paged_cache
models.configuration -> recipe.schema

docs.title: Critical design rule
docs.text:
Model loading and model mutation must be separate transactions:

load -> validate -> plan operation -> apply to copy/snapshot -> verify -> commit

Never mutate a live model before the operation plan and rollback snapshot are created.

docs.title: Current role
docs.text: This folder describes transformations such as attention replacement, compression, pruning, quantization, LoRA, distillation, healing, and export.

docs.title: It should own
docs.text:
• operation definitions;
  • operation validation;
  • operation inputs and outputs;
  • composable transformation semantics.

docs.title: It should not own
docs.text:
• scheduling or worker pools;
  • low-level CUDA kernels;
  • arbitrary checkpoint writes;
  • CLI parsing.

docs.title: Operation contract
docs.text:
class Operation(Protocol):
    name: str

    def validate(self, context: OperationContext) -> ValidationReport: ...
    def plan(self, context: OperationContext) -> OperationPlan: ...
    def apply(self, plan: OperationPlan) -> OperationResult: ...
    def rollback(self, result: OperationResult) -> None: ...

The current subfolders map naturally:

operations/attention   -> attention replacement/configuration
operations/weights     -> compression/pruning/quantization/decomposition
operations/adaptation  -> LoRA/KD/healing
operations/architecture-> structural model changes
operations/export      -> validated checkpoint/export artifacts
operations/verify      -> parity and contract checks

docs.title: Current role
docs.text:
This is the backend implementation layer:

ops/cuda
ops/triton
ops/pytorch

docs.title: It should own
docs.text:
• native CUDA/HIP extension loading;
  • Triton kernels and autotuning;
  • PyTorch mathematical reference kernels;
  • one fail-closed dispatcher.

docs.title: Required backend contract
docs.text:
class KernelAttempt:
    backend: Literal["cuda", "triton", "pytorch"]
    status: Literal["success", "failed", "unavailable"]
    error: str | None


class DispatchResult:
    output: torch.Tensor
    backend_used: str
    attempts: list[KernelAttempt]
    max_diff: float | None

The dispatcher must emit a warning for every fallback and must never report backend_used="cuda" when the output came from Triton or PyTorch.

docs.title: Folder-specific placement
docs.text:
ops/cuda/<name>/       native source, binding, loader, autograd wrapper
ops/triton/<name>.py   Triton implementation and reference comparison
ops/pytorch/<name>.py  mathematical oracle
ops/_dispatch.py       backend selection and telemetry

Empty CUDA directories are not acceptable as silent packages. They must either contain a valid loader that raises an informative error or be represented in a manifest as unavailable.

docs.title: Current role
docs.text: This folder currently appears small, with a kernels namespace. It should not become a second home for training or compression algorithms without a clear boundary.

docs.title: Recommended role
docs.text:
Reserve it for optimization algorithms and optimization-specific kernels:

optimization/
  optimizers/       parameter update algorithms
  schedulers/       LR and rank schedules
  objectives/       KD/healing/compression objectives
  kernels/          optimization-only fused kernels

Do not put generic CUDA kernels here; those belong under ops/cuda.

docs.title: Current role
docs.text: This folder contains planning, dependency graphs, execution, hardware planning, rollback, snapshots, and results.

docs.title: It should own
docs.text:
• immutable transformation plans;
  • dependency ordering;
  • resource planning;
  • transactional execution;
  • rollback and snapshot lifecycle.

docs.title: It should not own
docs.text:
• model-specific attention implementations;
  • CLI parsing;
  • result ledger persistence.

docs.title: Required flow
docs.text:
recipe -> planner -> Plan -> dependency validation -> hardware planner
       -> executor -> snapshot -> operation apply -> verification
       -> commit or rollback -> OperationResult

The executor should return structured events that reporting can consume.

docs.title: Current role
docs.text: This folder contains canonical recipe schema, loading, serialization, errors, and versioning.

docs.title: It should be the declarative source of truth
docs.text:
Recipes should describe intent, not implementation details:

version: 1
model:
  source: distilbert-base-uncased
operations:
  - type: replace_attention
    target: encoder.layer.*
    attention: gated_delta_net
    parameters:
      rank: 64
validation:
  parity_tolerance: 0.001
output:
  directory: results/recipe_run

The recipe loader must validate schema, resolve aliases, calculate a content hash, and never execute code while parsing.

docs.title: Current role
docs.text: This folder contains environment capture, evidence, and report generation.

docs.title: It should own
docs.text:
• execution evidence;
  • environment metadata;
  • human reports;
  • machine-readable summaries.

docs.title: It should consume
docs.text:
OperationResult
DispatchResult
BenchmarkResult
EnvironmentSnapshot

It must not reach into a model to infer undocumented metrics. Every reported number must carry its source run ID and metric name.

docs.title: Current role
docs.text: This folder contains saving configuration, writers, storage, plotting, and Hugging Face backends.

docs.title: Recommended responsibility
docs.text:
Make this the single persistence layer for completed result records. The benchmark-specific results/ package and this folder currently overlap and must be reconciled.

Recommended split:

results/schema.py      canonical dataclasses and validation
results_saver/         persistence backends and transactional writers
reporting/             human-readable reports and evidence

The saver should provide:

class ResultsStore(Protocol):
    def write(self, record: ResultRecord) -> None: ...
    def validate(self, path: Path) -> ValidationReport: ...
    def compare(self, baseline: Path, candidate: Path) -> Comparison: ...

Parquet, SQLite, JSONL, and CSV are output backends—not separate schemas.

docs.title: Current role
docs.text: This folder contains master pipeline execution, sweep execution, monitoring, telemetry, and orchestration.

docs.title: It should own
docs.text:
• scheduling multiple operations or benchmarks;
  • worker lifecycle;
  • resume and monitoring;
  • aggregation of structured results.

docs.title: It should not own
docs.text:
• module implementation;
  • low-level device checks duplicated from ops;
  • direct writes to arbitrary CSV files.

docs.title: Runner contract
docs.text:
class RunRequest:
    run_id: str
    recipe: Recipe
    config: RunConfig
    output_dir: Path


class RunOrchestrator:
    def plan(self, request: RunRequest) -> ExecutionPlan: ...
    def execute(self, plan: ExecutionPlan) -> RunResult: ...
    def resume(self, run_id: str) -> RunResult: ...

Monitoring should read event streams or result records. It must not inspect private worker state or change benchmark outcomes.

docs.title: 4.1 Configuration contract
docs.text:
One canonical config should feed CLI, recipe execution, inference, kernels, benchmarking, and saving:

@dataclass
class RuntimeConfig:
    device: str
    precision: str
    seed: int
    output_dir: Path
    strict_backend: bool
    parity_tolerance: float

Folder-specific config should be nested under this runtime config rather than redeclaring device, dtype, and output_dir in every folder.

docs.title: 4.2 Event contract
docs.text:
All long operations should emit events:

@dataclass
class RunEvent:
    run_id: str
    timestamp: str
    component: str
    event: str
    status: str
    payload: dict[str, object]

Examples:

operation.started
kernel.fallback
parity.completed
checkpoint.written
run.failed

docs.title: 4.3 Artifact contract
docs.text:
Every run directory should contain:

config.json
environment.json
manifest.json
events.jsonl
results.jsonl
summary.json
logs/
artifacts/

No folder should invent a competing latest.json format.

docs.title: 5. Main current problems to fix
docs.text:
1. Overlapping owners: kernels, results, runners, and transformations each have multiple possible owners.
  2. Private cross-imports: callers can bypass stable APIs and import internal classes directly.
  3. Duplicate result writers: benchmark results and results_saver can emit different schemas.
  4. No universal run context: device, seed, git commit, and output path are not guaranteed to travel across all folders.
  5. Backend identity loss: fallback output can be labelled as the requested backend rather than the actual backend.
  6. Mutation without transaction: model operations need plan, snapshot, verify, commit, and rollback boundaries.
  7. Optional integrations at import time: missing vendor packages can make unrelated commands fail during import.
  8. Generated files inside source folders: .DS_Store and __pycache__ indicate source-tree hygiene issues.
  9. Empty namespaces: folders such as optimization need an explicit scope so they do not become dumping grounds.
  10. Monitoring coupled to execution internals: monitoring should consume stable events, not inspect implementation state.
  11. Recipe and CLI duplication: both can describe operations, but their semantics must be merged into one validated request.
  12. No complete integration test: individual pieces may pass while the full chain from recipe to report is broken.

docs.title: Phase 1: contracts
docs.text:
1. Define RuntimeConfig, RunContext, RunEvent, and ResultRecord.
  2. Add schema validation and serialization tests.
  3. Make device, dtype, seed, and output directory mandatory in the context.

docs.title: Phase 2: backend boundary
docs.text:
1. Make kernels a facade.
  2. Move backend selection into one dispatcher under ops.
  3. Add explicit fallback telemetry.
  4. Add parity and gradient gates.

docs.title: Phase 3: transformation boundary
docs.text:
1. Make recipes declarative.
  2. Make operations validate and produce plans.
  3. Make pipeline transforms transactional.
  4. Connect snapshots and rollback to operation results.

docs.title: Phase 4: persistence boundary
docs.text:
1. Select one canonical result schema.
  2. Make results_saver the persistence backend layer.
  3. Make reporting consume records rather than raw model state.
  4. Add SQLite/JSONL/CSV/Parquet backends behind one interface.

docs.title: Phase 5: runtime boundary
docs.text:
1. Connect models to layers and kernel facades.
  2. Connect inference to model runtime and cache contracts.
  3. Connect external integrations through capability adapters.
  4. Add serving integration tests.

docs.title: Phase 6: orchestration
docs.text:
1. Make runners consume recipes and runtime configs.
  2. Add resumable run directories and locks.
  3. Connect monitoring to events.
  4. Add full end-to-end tests.

docs.title: 7. Required tests
docs.text:
tests/architecture/test_import_boundaries.py
  ops does not import runners or reporting
  layers does not import CLI
  results_saver does not mutate models

tests/architecture/test_contracts.py
  RuntimeConfig roundtrip
  RunEvent roundtrip
  ResultRecord schema validation

tests/architecture/test_recipe_pipeline.py
  recipe -> plan -> execute -> report
  invalid recipe fails before mutation
  failed operation rolls back snapshot

tests/architecture/test_dispatch_integration.py
  backend identity is preserved
  fallback warnings are emitted
  numerical parity gate is enforced

tests/architecture/test_inference_integrations.py
  serving capability discovery
  optional dependency unavailable state
  KV-cache spec translation

tests/architecture/test_results_pipeline.py
  JSONL/CSV/SQLite consistency
  Parquet missing dependency policy
  duplicate run rejection

docs.title: 8. Practical placement rules
docs.text:
When adding a new file, use this decision table:

New functionality Correct location New attention nn.Module layers/<family>/ New compressor compression/<family>/ CUDA/Triton/PyTorch operator backend ops/<backend>/ Public kernel facade kernels/ Model wiring/configuration models/ Model mutation operations/ Declarative model change recipe/ Plan/snapshot/rollback pipeline_transform/ Inference request/cache/decode inference/ vLLM/SGLang/TensorRT adapter integrations/ Human report/evidence reporting/ Result persistence backend results_saver/ Multi-step scheduling/monitoring runners/ Optimizer or optimization objective optimization/

docs.title: 9. Definition of done
docs.text:
The folders are correctly connected when:

  • a recipe can be loaded without executing code;
  • the recipe becomes a validated operation plan;
  • the plan loads a model and applies layers through public APIs;
  • layers call the kernel facade, not vendor internals;
  • dispatch reports the backend actually used;
  • inference can consume the resulting model;
  • integrations expose capabilities and adapt external runtimes;
  • reporting receives structured events and results;
  • results_saver persists one canonical schema;
  • runners can resume without duplicate writes;
  • import-boundary tests pass;
  • no folder has an undocumented second owner;
  • generated files are excluded from source packages;
  • end-to-end tests prove recipe -> operation -> runtime -> report.

Until these gates pass, the architecture should be treated as transitional.

docs.title: 10. Exact keep / move / delete policy
docs.text: This section is intentionally concrete. It is the checklist to use before moving any file. A file should not be deleted merely because another folder has a similar name; first redirect callers, add a compatibility import if needed, and run the boundary tests.

docs.title: 10.1 Keep as canonical implementation
docs.text:
Keep these responsibilities in their current conceptual owners:

layers/                 torch.nn.Module implementations
ops/cuda/               native CUDA loaders and bindings
ops/triton/             Triton implementations
ops/pytorch/            reference implementations
models/                 model composition and checkpoint lifecycle
operations/             model mutations and validations
pipeline_transform/     plans, dependency graphs, snapshots, rollback
recipe/                 declarative schemas and serialization
inference/              runtime requests, cache, decoding
integrations/           external runtime adapters
reporting/              evidence and human reports
results_saver/          persistence backends
runners/                scheduling and monitoring

docs.title: 10.2 Move or adapt
docs.text:
The following concepts should be consolidated:

Current overlap Canonical owner Required action kernels/extended_kernels.py and ops/* ops/ implementation + kernels/ facade Move implementation details to ops; keep re-export facade benchmark writers and results_saver/ results_saver/ Make benchmark writers call ResultsStore benchmark orchestrators and runners/ runners/ Keep benchmark-specific plan builders, centralize scheduling recipe execution and CLI handlers recipe/ + pipeline_transform/ CLI parses only; loader/planner executes serving benchmark and inference/ inference/ Benchmark measures engine through public inference API vendor checks and integrations integrations/ Expose capabilities instead of scattered imports model surgery and direct model writes operations/ + models/surgical_io.py Use operation transaction and checkpoint writer dispatch statistics and reporting ops emits events; reporting consumes Remove direct reporting imports from kernels 
### 10.3 Remove after migration

These are valid deletion candidates only after caller verification:

- duplicate result serializers that emit a different schema;
- wrapper scripts that contain copied benchmark logic;
- unused `.DS_Store` files;
- tracked `__pycache__` or generated bytecode;
- empty backend package directories that do not expose a loader or manifest;
- duplicate compatibility modules with no imports or documentation references;
- direct vendor imports in core code when an integration adapter exists.

Before deletion, run:

```bash
rg -n "from neuralops\.|import neuralops\." .
rg -n "old_module_name|old_symbol_name" neuralops tests benchmarks scripts
git grep -n "path/to/file.py"

Record the result in the migration matrix.

docs.title: 11.1 CLI to recipe/config
docs.text:
neuralops CLI
  -> parse only command-line syntax
  -> ConfigLoader.load()
  -> RuntimeConfig
  -> RecipeLoader.load() if --recipe is used
  -> RunRequest

The CLI must not instantiate an attention, open a checkpoint, or call a CUDA kernel directly. It should create a request and pass it to a command handler.

Suggested code:

def run_command(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    runtime = ConfigLoader.from_cli(args)
    recipe = RecipeLoader.load(args.recipe) if args.recipe else None
    request = RunRequest(runtime=runtime, recipe=recipe)
    result = RunOrchestrator().execute(request)
    ResultsStore.from_config(runtime.results).write(result)
    return result.exit_code

docs.title: 11.2 Recipe to operation
docs.text:
recipe/schema.py
  -> validated Recipe
recipe/canonical.py
  -> normalized operation names and aliases
recipe/loader.py
  -> immutable RecipeDocument
operations/registry.py
  -> OperationFactory.create(document.operation)
operations/*
  -> Operation.validate(context)
  -> Operation.plan(context)

The recipe must not contain Python import paths that are executed dynamically. Use a registry key, then resolve that key through the existing registry.

Example:

operations:
  - type: replace_attention
    target: encoder.layer.*
    attention: gated_delta_net
    params:
      causal: true

The loader resolves replace_attention to an operation factory and gated_delta_net to a registered layer. It does not import an arbitrary module named by the user.

docs.title: 11.3 Operation to model
docs.text:
OperationContext
  -> ModelHandle
  -> registry lookup
  -> capability validation
  -> snapshot
  -> operation apply
  -> model validation

The model boundary should expose:

class ModelHandle(Protocol):
    def named_modules(self) -> Iterator[tuple[str, nn.Module]]: ...
    def snapshot(self) -> Snapshot: ...
    def restore(self, snapshot: Snapshot) -> None: ...
    def save(self, destination: Path) -> ArtifactManifest: ...

Operations must not manipulate checkpoint paths directly. They call ModelHandle.save() and receive a manifest.

docs.title: 11.4 Layers to kernel facade
docs.text:
layers/gated/gated_delta_net.py
  -> kernels.dispatch("gdn_scan", ...)
  -> ops._dispatch
      -> ops.cuda.gdn_scan
      -> ops.triton.gdn_scan
      -> ops.pytorch.gdn_scan

The layer owns tensor semantics and shape checks. The dispatcher owns backend choice. This prevents every layer from reimplementing CUDA/Triton fallback.

Layer example:

def forward(self, q, k, v, *, is_causal=False):
    validate_attention_inputs(q, k, v)
    return dispatch_kernel(
        "gdn_scan",
        q=q,
        k=k,
        v=v,
        is_causal=is_causal,
        runtime=self.runtime,
    ).output

docs.title: 11.5 Dispatcher to reporting
docs.text:
The dispatcher should return a structured attempt list and optionally emit a kernel.fallback event. It must not write JSON or import reporting writers.

DispatchResult(
    output=output,
    backend_used="triton",
    attempts=[
        KernelAttempt("cuda", "failed", "extension not found"),
        KernelAttempt("triton", "success", None),
    ],
    max_diff=3.1e-4,
)

The caller converts this to a result record:

record.metrics["max_diff"] = dispatch.max_diff
record.metadata["backend_used"] = dispatch.backend_used
record.metadata["attempts"] = [asdict(item) for item in dispatch.attempts]

docs.title: 11.6 Model to inference
docs.text:
models.modeling.Model
  -> inference.engine.load_model(model_handle)
  -> inference request
  -> cache allocation
  -> prefill/decode
  -> InferenceResult

Inference must receive an already validated model handle. It should not call model surgery or compression itself.

docs.title: 11.7 Inference to integrations
docs.text:
InferenceEngine
  -> ServingIntegrationRegistry.get("vllm")
  -> capabilities()
  -> load(ServingConfig)
  -> ServingBackend

The engine should operate against a backend protocol. Vendor adapters translate requests and cache specs but do not modify core inference contracts.

docs.title: 11.8 Results to reporting
docs.text:
RunEvent + ResultRecord
  -> ResultsStore.write()
  -> reporting.evidence.collect()
  -> reporting.report.render()

Reporting should never scrape log text to calculate metrics when structured records are available. Logs are evidence of execution; results records are the source of numerical claims.

docs.title: 11.9 Reporting to runners
docs.text:
Runner emits events
  -> EventSink
  -> JSONL event stream
  -> monitor / report / UI subscribers

The monitor must be a subscriber. It must not import private fields from a worker or mutate its state.

docs.title: 12.1 neuralops/inference
docs.text:
Add:

contracts.py       InferenceRequest, InferenceResult, SamplingConfig
backend.py         InferenceBackend protocol
telemetry.py       TTFT/ITL/token counters

Modify:

  • engine.py to accept RuntimeConfig and ModelHandle;
  • paged_cache.py to consume one KVCacheSpec from integrations;
  • speculative_decoding.py to return accepted/rejected token counts;
  • pipeline_parallel.py to emit rank/stage errors.

Remove or relocate:

  • vendor-specific code from engine.py to integrations/;
  • result CSV writing from inference modules;
  • duplicated device selection helpers.

docs.title: 12.2 neuralops/integrations
docs.text:
Add:

base.py           IntegrationCapabilities and protocols
registry.py       optional integration registry
errors.py         IntegrationUnavailable, VersionMismatch

Modify each vendor adapter to implement capabilities() and load().

Remove:

  • unconditional imports of vllm, sglang, tensorrt_llm, or TGI;
  • fallback to a different vendor without a recorded decision;
  • benchmark-specific metric calculation from adapters.

docs.title: 12.3 neuralops/kernels
docs.text:
Keep only public facade exports. Move implementation details that duplicate ops/cuda, ops/triton, or ops/pytorch to their canonical backend.

Add:

contracts.py       KernelRequest, DispatchResult, KernelAttempt
dispatch.py        public dispatch_kernel facade

docs.title: 12.4 neuralops/layers
docs.text:
Add shared validation modules:

contracts.py       input shape/dtype/causal contracts
validation.py      finite, gradient, causal checks

Modify each family package so its modules call kernels.dispatch_kernel().

Remove local copies of backend fallback logic once equivalent tests exist.

docs.title: 12.5 neuralops/models
docs.text:
Add:

protocols.py       ModelHandle and checkpoint protocols
manifests.py       model artifact manifest schema

Modify surgical_io.py to use atomic output directories and manifests. Move operation-specific mutation logic out of modeling.py into operations/.

docs.title: 12.6 neuralops/operations
docs.text:
Add:

context.py         OperationContext
plan.py            OperationPlan
transaction.py     snapshot/apply/verify/commit/rollback

Modify every operation to implement validate, plan, apply, and rollback. Remove direct CLI argument parsing from operation modules.

docs.title: 12.7 neuralops/ops
docs.text:
Add or consolidate:

contracts.py       backend contracts
dispatch.py        one dispatcher
telemetry.py       backend attempt events
parity.py          reference comparison

Ensure CUDA, Triton, and PyTorch implementations all share operator names and return shapes. A missing native implementation must be represented explicitly, not as an empty package.

docs.title: 12.8 neuralops/optimization
docs.text:
Create a clear substructure before adding more algorithms:

optimizers/
schedulers/
objectives/
kernels/

Move only optimization-specific code here. Do not move generic backend kernels.

docs.title: 12.9 neuralops/pipeline_transform
docs.text: Make plan.py, executor.py, snapshot.py, and rollback.py the only public transaction path. Add integration tests that prove an exception restores the original model state bit-for-bit where feasible.

docs.title: 12.10 neuralops/recipe
docs.text: Add schema validation for operation types, target selectors, backend policy, parity tolerance, and output policy. Add a recipe hash to every run manifest.

docs.title: 12.11 neuralops/reporting
docs.text: Add report adapters for RunEvent, DispatchResult, OperationResult, and BenchmarkResult. Do not infer missing values. Render unavailable values as null plus a reason, or fail validation when the metric is required.

docs.title: 12.12 neuralops/results_saver
docs.text: Make ResultsStore the only writer used by new code. Add schema versioning, atomic writes, duplicate detection, and explicit optional-format policy.

docs.title: 12.13 neuralops/runners
docs.text: Add a RunRequest boundary and make the master orchestrator consume plans and events. Move monitoring to event subscriptions. Add run locks and resume validation.

docs.title: 13. What should be deleted or forbidden
docs.text:
The following patterns should be removed from all these folders:

except: pass
except Exception: return None       # in data-producing paths
hard-coded metrics or baselines
fake success records after backend failure
generic SVD under another compressor name
direct CPU fallback after explicit CUDA
fixed results/latest.json writes
duplicate device/dtype parsers
vendor imports at module import time
private imports across folder boundaries
direct result writes from layers or kernels
unvalidated arbitrary Python paths in recipes
untracked .DS_Store and __pycache__ files

The following should be allowed only with explicit metadata:

CUDA -> Triton fallback
Triton -> PyTorch fallback
optional vendor unavailable
Parquet unavailable while JSON/CSV succeeds
unsupported dtype or causal mode

docs.title: Input recipe
docs.text:
version: 1
model:
  source: distilbert-base-uncased
runtime:
  device: cuda:0
  precision: float16
  seed: 42
  strict_backend: false
operations:
  - type: replace_attention
    target: encoder.layer.*
    attention: gated_delta_net
    params:
      rank: 64
validation:
  gates: [forward, backward, finite, causal, parity]
  parity_tolerance: 0.001
output:
  directory: results/example_run

docs.title: Exact flow
docs.text:
CLI parses path
  -> RecipeLoader validates schema
  -> hash recipe
  -> ConfigLoader resolves cuda:0 and float16
  -> Runner creates results/example_run/.active.lock
  -> Planner resolves replace_attention operation
  -> ModelLoader loads model
  -> Snapshot captures original state
  -> Operation validates gated_delta_net capability
  -> Operation replaces target layers
  -> Layer calls kernels.dispatch_kernel("gdn_scan")
  -> Dispatcher tries CUDA, then Triton, then PyTorch if policy allows
  -> Validation compares output against PyTorch reference
  -> Reporter receives structured gate events
  -> ResultsStore writes typed records atomically
  -> Model artifact is saved with manifest
  -> Runner removes lock and writes summary

docs.title: Failure flow
docs.text:
CUDA extension fails
  -> warning: level=1 error=...
  -> Triton fails
  -> warning: level=2 error=...
  -> PyTorch executes
  -> record backend_used=pytorch
  -> record fallback chain
  -> if strict_backend=true: fail instead

docs.title: 15. Architecture acceptance matrix
docs.text: Connection Required proof CLI -> config config precedence test and saved effective config config -> recipe schema validation and recipe hash recipe -> operations operation factory test operations -> models mutation plus rollback test models -> layers model construction and shape contract test layers -> kernels dispatcher call and backend identity test kernels -> CUDA/Triton/PyTorch fallback and parity test models -> inference generation smoke test inference -> integrations capability and KV-cache translation test runner -> events event stream test events -> reporting report contains source run IDs reporting -> results_saver schema-validated persisted record results_saver -> resume duplicate/lock/resume test

docs.title: 16. Refactor safety rules
docs.text:
1. Move one folder boundary at a time.
  2. Preserve public imports with deprecation shims.
  3. Never combine a rename, behavior change, and backend change in one commit.
  4. Add an import-boundary test before deleting a compatibility module.
  5. Run rg for callers before moving a symbol.
  6. Keep generated artifacts out of source directories.
  7. Do not run bulk formatters over unrelated files.
  8. Record every moved file and its replacement in the migration matrix.
  9. Test CPU/reference paths before spending GPU time.
  10. Treat a process abort or timeout as a failure requiring classification.

docs.title: 17. Final folder checklist
docs.text:
[ ] inference has request/result/cache contracts
[ ] integrations expose capability objects
[ ] kernels is a facade, not a second implementation tree
[ ] layers own nn.Module semantics only
[ ] models own composition and checkpoint lifecycle
[ ] operations own model mutations
[ ] ops owns backend implementations and dispatch
[ ] optimization has a defined scope
[ ] pipeline_transform owns transactions and rollback
[ ] recipe owns declarative schemas
[ ] reporting owns evidence and rendering
[ ] results_saver owns persistence
[ ] runners own scheduling and monitoring
[ ] all cross-folder imports follow the dependency graph
[ ] no duplicate writer or dispatcher remains
[ ] no generated files are tracked
[ ] end-to-end recipe-to-report test passes

docs.title: 18. File-by-file integration manual
docs.text: This section is the detailed implementation map. The purpose is to remove the ambiguity of statements such as “connect inference to models”. Each connection below identifies the producer, consumer, data shape, error behavior, and test.

docs.title: Keep
docs.text:
• request batching;
  • prefill/decode scheduling;
  • model invocation;
  • cache coordination;
  • timing boundaries around user-visible generation.

docs.title: Add
docs.text:
from neuralops.runtime.context import RuntimeContext
from neuralops.models.protocols import ModelHandle
from neuralops.inference.contracts import InferenceRequest, InferenceResult


class InferenceEngine:
    def __init__(self, model: ModelHandle, context: RuntimeContext) -> None:
        self.model = model
        self.context = context

    def generate(self, request: InferenceRequest) -> InferenceResult:
        self.context.require_device_available()
        self.context.events.emit("inference.started", request_id=request.request_id)
        # Prefill and decode are delegated to private methods, but all output
        # metrics are assembled into one public result object.
        result = self._generate_impl(request)
        if not torch.isfinite(result.logits).all():
            raise InferenceError("generation produced non-finite logits")
        self.context.events.emit("inference.completed", request_id=request.request_id)
        return result

docs.title: Remove or move
docs.text:
• direct imports of vLLM, SGLang, or TensorRT-LLM;
  • direct CSV/JSON output;
  • hidden torch.cuda.is_available() fallback to CPU;
  • model surgery calls during generation.

docs.title: Connect to
docs.text:
models.protocols.ModelHandle
runtime.context.RuntimeContext
inference.contracts.InferenceRequest/Result
inference.paged_cache.PagedKVCache
reporting events through RuntimeContext.events

docs.title: Test
docs.text: tests/architecture/test_inference_engine_contract.py must prove that the engine receives a model handle, emits start/end events, and refuses a requested CUDA device when CUDA is unavailable.

docs.title: Keep
docs.text:
• page allocation;
  • append/read operations;
  • capacity checks;
  • device-local storage.

docs.title: Add
docs.text:
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class KVCacheSpec:
    page_tokens: int
    num_pages: int
    num_kv_heads: int
    head_dim: int
    dtype: str
    device: str

The cache must be created from KVCacheSpec, not from a vendor-specific config object. Integrations translate their own cache description into this spec.

docs.title: Required errors
docs.text:
• capacity exceeded -> CacheCapacityError;
  • shape mismatch -> CacheShapeError;
  • device mismatch -> CacheDeviceError;
  • unsupported dtype -> CacheDtypeError.

Do not allocate an empty cache as a fallback.

docs.title: 18.3 neuralops/integrations/serving.py
docs.text: This is the integration boundary for generic serving, not the inference implementation itself.

docs.title: Add
docs.text:
class ServingBackend(Protocol):
    def generate(self, request: InferenceRequest) -> InferenceResult: ...
    def close(self) -> None: ...


class ServingAdapter(Protocol):
    name: str

    def capabilities(self) -> IntegrationCapabilities: ...
    def create(self, config: ServingConfig) -> ServingBackend: ...

docs.title: Exact flow
docs.text:
serving CLI
  -> IntegrationRegistry.resolve(name)
  -> adapter.capabilities()
  -> reject unavailable adapter
  -> adapter.create(config)
  -> InferenceEngine uses ServingBackend protocol

The benchmark should record adapter.name, adapter version, and capability state in environment.json.

docs.title: 18.4 neuralops/integrations/vllm.py, sglang.py, tensorrt_llm.py
docs.text:
Each file should contain only translation code:

NeuralOps InferenceRequest -> vendor request
vendor response -> NeuralOps InferenceResult
NeuralOps KVCacheSpec -> vendor cache configuration
vendor exception -> IntegrationError with original cause

Do not put benchmark loops or numerical parity logic in these files. The same request must be testable with a fake vendor backend without installing the vendor package.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Audit every public symbol in this file:

rg -n "^(class|def) |__all__" neuralops/kernels/extended_kernels.py
rg -n "extended_kernels" neuralops tests benchmarks scripts

For each symbol:

  • if it is a public facade, re-export it from neuralops.kernels;
  • if it contains CUDA/Triton code, move the implementation to ops/cuda or ops/triton;
  • if it is a PyTorch oracle, move it to ops/pytorch;
  • if it is unused, document and remove it in a separate cleanup commit.

The file must not be a fourth backend.

docs.title: Keep
docs.text:
• extension source discovery;
  • compiler flags;
  • cache naming;
  • extension loading.

docs.title: Add
docs.text:
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class CompilationReport:
    name: str
    attempted: bool
    succeeded: bool
    compiler: str | None
    linker: str | None
    error: str | None
    artifact: str | None

On failure, return or raise a report that includes the compiler and linker. Never return an object that looks like a loaded extension when linking failed.

docs.title: Connect to
docs.text:
ops._dispatch -> load_cuda_module
reporting -> CompilationReport
results_saver -> native compilation metadata

docs.title: 18.7 neuralops/ops/cuda/_fallback.py
docs.text: This is the most important backend boundary.

docs.title: Required algorithm
docs.text:
def dispatch(
    name: str,
    *,
    cuda_fn: Callable[..., Tensor] | None,
    triton_fn: Callable[..., Tensor] | None,
    pytorch_fn: Callable[..., Tensor],
    strict: bool,
    args: tuple[object, ...],
    kwargs: dict[str, object],
) -> DispatchResult:
    attempts: list[KernelAttempt] = []

    if cuda_fn is not None:
        try:
            output = cuda_fn(*args, **kwargs)
            return DispatchResult(output, "cuda", attempts + [success("cuda")])
        except Exception as exc:
            attempts.append(failure("cuda", exc))
            logger.warning("CUDA kernel %s failed: %s", name, exc)
            if strict:
                raise DispatchError(name, attempts) from exc

    if triton_fn is not None:
        try:
            output = triton_fn(*args, **kwargs)
            return DispatchResult(output, "triton", attempts + [success("triton")])
        except Exception as exc:
            attempts.append(failure("triton", exc))
            logger.warning("Triton kernel %s failed: %s", name, exc)
            if strict:
                raise DispatchError(name, attempts) from exc

    output = pytorch_fn(*args, **kwargs)
    attempts.append(success("pytorch"))
    return DispatchResult(output, "pytorch", attempts)

The actual implementation may use different names, but it must preserve this behavior. except Exception: pass is not allowed.

docs.title: 18.8 neuralops/ops/triton/*.py
docs.text:
Each Triton module must be paired with:

one canonical operator name
one PyTorch reference function
one parity test
one capability declaration
one explicit unsupported-shape error

The module must not silently call another Triton kernel and label it with its own name. If the kernel is not implemented, raise NotImplementedError with the missing operator name.

docs.title: 18.9 neuralops/ops/pytorch/
docs.text:
This is the mathematical oracle. Each function should be:

  • device-agnostic;
  • differentiable;
  • numerically explicit;
  • independent of Triton and CUDA imports;
  • covered by shape, causal, finite, and gradient tests.

It must not be considered a performance backend. Its use in a GPU benchmark must be recorded as backend_used=pytorch.

docs.title: 18.10 neuralops/layers/base.py
docs.text:
Add a common module contract:

class NeuralOpsLayer(nn.Module):
    layer_name: ClassVar[str]
    supports_causal: ClassVar[bool]
    supports_gqa: ClassVar[bool]

    def capability_report(self) -> LayerCapabilities: ...
    def reference_forward(self, *args, **kwargs) -> Tensor: ...

Every registered layer should implement or inherit these methods. The registry uses the capability report for CLI listing and benchmark planning.

docs.title: 18.11 Family folders under neuralops/layers/
docs.text:
For every family folder, standardize this layout:

family/
  __init__.py        explicit exports only
  <module>.py        nn.Module implementation
  contracts.py       family-specific shape/config contracts if needed
  reference.py       only if reference math is family-specific
  tests/              CPU-safe family tests if the project convention allows

Do not put benchmark scripts inside a layer family. Do not import pytest, reporting, or result writers from a layer.

docs.title: 18.12 neuralops/models/configuration.py
docs.text:
This file should be the bridge between external model config and internal layer config. Add explicit conversion functions:

def to_layer_config(model_config: PretrainedConfig) -> LayerConfig: ...
def to_runtime_config(model_config: PretrainedConfig) -> RuntimeConfig: ...

Do not let each layer read arbitrary Hugging Face config attributes. Normalize once, validate once, and pass typed config objects downward.

docs.title: 18.13 neuralops/models/hub.py
docs.text:
Separate source retrieval from model construction:

hub.resolve_source() -> ModelSource
models.loader.load(ModelSource, ModelConfig) -> ModelHandle

The hub must not silently download a model when offline mode is requested. It must report cache miss and the exact remediation.

docs.title: 18.14 neuralops/models/surgical_io.py
docs.text:
Make checkpoint writes transactional:

destination.tmp/<files>
manifest.json
validation.json
atomic rename destination.tmp -> destination

If validation fails, remove only the temporary directory and leave the original checkpoint untouched. Never create a partial checkpoint with a production file extension.

docs.title: 18.15 neuralops/operations/attention/replace.py
docs.text:
Required flow:

resolve target modules
  -> validate target count
  -> resolve canonical attention key
  -> inspect capability report
  -> create replacement modules
  -> copy/initialize weights
  -> run shape and causal checks
  -> return operation result

The operation must fail if zero modules match the selector unless the recipe explicitly permits an empty selection. It must report all replaced module paths.

docs.title: 18.16 neuralops/operations/verify/parity.py
docs.text:
This should be the shared parity gate for surgery, kernels, and inference. It must accept reference/candidate tensors, dtype-specific tolerance, and a context label. It returns a structured report, not a boolean only:

ParityReport(
    passed=False,
    max_diff=0.018,
    mean_diff=0.002,
    tolerance=0.001,
    reference_shape=(2, 4, 64, 32),
    candidate_shape=(2, 4, 64, 32),
    context="gla_scan/cuda",
)

docs.title: 18.17 neuralops/pipeline_transform/planner.py
docs.text:
The planner should be pure: same recipe hash and model metadata produce the same plan. It must not allocate a CUDA tensor or mutate a model.

The plan must include:

plan_id
recipe_hash
model_source
ordered_operations
required_backends
estimated_memory
rollback_requirements

docs.title: 18.18 neuralops/pipeline_transform/executor.py
docs.text:
The executor should implement:

prepare snapshot
validate all operations
execute operation one
verify operation one
execute operation two
verify operation two
commit all artifacts

If any operation fails, restore the latest valid snapshot and mark the entire run failed unless the recipe explicitly allows partial results.

docs.title: 18.19 neuralops/recipe/loader.py and schema.py
docs.text:
The loader performs only parsing and validation. It should not:

  • import arbitrary Python modules;
  • download models;
  • allocate tensors;
  • create directories except an explicitly requested cache location.

Schema validation must reject unknown operation types, unknown backend policy, negative ranks, invalid tolerances, and missing model source.

docs.title: 18.20 neuralops/reporting/environment.py
docs.text:
Capture environment once at run start:

python executable/version
torch version
CUDA runtime
GPU name/index/memory
Triton version
NeuralOps git commit/dirty state
selected environment variables without secrets

Pass the immutable snapshot to every result record. Do not recapture slightly different metadata for each module unless the hardware state itself is a metric.

docs.title: 18.21 neuralops/reporting/evidence.py
docs.text:
Evidence should reference files and commands, not copy unverified claims:

Evidence(
    command="pytest tests/gpu_exhaustive -v --tb=short",
    host="GPU-3090-1.local",
    exit_code=0,
    log_path="results/run/logs/exhaustive.log",
    summary="915 passed, 2 skipped",
)

An evidence record with no exit code or final summary is incomplete.

docs.title: 18.22 neuralops/results_saver/saver.py
docs.text:
Make the saver accept only validated records:

class ResultsStore:
    def __init__(self, root: Path, policy: StoragePolicy) -> None: ...

    def write(self, record: ResultRecord) -> None:
        record.validate()
        self._write_jsonl(record)
        self._write_json(record)
        if self.policy.parquet_required:
            self._write_parquet(record)
        elif self.policy.parquet_optional:
            self._try_optional_parquet(record)

Optional Parquet failure must emit a warning and a metadata flag; it must not silently change the requested output format.

docs.title: 18.23 neuralops/runners/unified_orchestrator.py
docs.text:
The orchestrator should be the only component allowed to coordinate multiple operations. It receives RunRequest, creates an execution plan, creates a run directory, starts workers, collects events, and writes the final summary.

It should not know how a particular attention computes its output. If it has module-specific if name == ... logic, move that logic to the registry or adapter layer.

docs.title: 18.24 neuralops/runners/monitor/
docs.text: The monitor should read events.jsonl and result records. It should not import the worker's private objects. Add a file cursor/checkpoint so the monitor can resume reading after restart.

docs.title: 19. Exact import-boundary rules
docs.text:
These imports should be rejected by a static architecture test:

neuralops.ops -> neuralops.runners
neuralops.ops -> neuralops.reporting
neuralops.layers -> neuralops.runners
neuralops.layers -> neuralops.results_saver
neuralops.results_saver -> neuralops.models
neuralops.reporting -> neuralops.operations (mutation path)
neuralops.integrations -> neuralops.cli
neuralops.recipe -> neuralops.inference

These are allowed through protocols or stable contracts:

neuralops.layers -> neuralops.kernels
neuralops.models -> neuralops.layers
neuralops.inference -> neuralops.models
neuralops.inference -> neuralops.integrations
neuralops.runners -> recipe/operations/pipeline/reporting/results_saver

Implement the test with AST import inspection rather than importing all modules on a machine without CUDA dependencies.

docs.title: 20. Exact migration sequence for this repository
Step 1: freeze the public contracts
docs.text: Add contracts and tests first. Do not move implementation files yet.

docs.title: Step 2: map callers
docs.text:
For every file in the folders, produce:

rg -n "from neuralops\.(inference|integrations|kernels|layers|models|operations|ops|optimization|pipeline_transform|recipe|reporting|results_saver|runners)" neuralops tests benchmarks scripts

Record caller, imported symbol, and replacement API.

docs.title: Step 3: consolidate dispatch
docs.text: Move backend selection behind kernels.dispatch_kernel and update layers one family at a time. Keep compatibility imports until tests pass.

docs.title: Step 4: consolidate result persistence
docs.text: Create an adapter from existing benchmark result objects to ResultRecord, then make all new runners use ResultsStore.

docs.title: Step 5: make operations transactional
docs.text: Update one operation family at a time: attention replacement, weights, adaptation, architecture, export.

docs.title: Step 6: connect recipe and CLI
docs.text: CLI creates requests; recipe loader and operation registry do the work. Add help/examples only after command behavior is tested.

docs.title: Step 7: connect inference and integrations
docs.text: Run smoke tests with a fake backend first, then GPU tests for real integrations.

docs.title: Step 8: connect runners and monitoring
docs.text: Make all runs produce event streams and unique result directories.

docs.title: Step 9: remove duplicates
docs.text: Only now remove duplicate writers, facades, and legacy scripts. Every deletion must cite its replacement and caller audit.

docs.title: 23. Final review questions for every folder
docs.text:
Before accepting a folder cleanup, answer all questions:

  1. What is the single sentence responsibility of this folder?
  2. Which public files are allowed to import it?
  3. Which folders is it forbidden to import?
  4. What is the input contract?
  5. What is the output contract?
  6. How does it report failure?
  7. How does it preserve provenance?
  8. Does it write files? If yes, which writer owns that path?
  9. Does it select a backend? If yes, where is the actual backend recorded?
  10. Can it run without CUDA for reference tests?
  11. What happens when an optional dependency is missing?
  12. Which test proves its integration with the next folder?
  13. Which files are legacy and why are they retained?
  14. What can safely be deleted after migration?

If any answer is unclear, the folder is not yet cleanly integrated.

docs.title: Benchmark Integrity Audit
docs.text:
This ledger records the benchmark-specific fail-closed audit. It distinguishes production execution paths from explicitly synthetic demo fixtures.

Finding Location Classification Disposition Evidence Explicit CUDA request could be downgraded to CPU scripts/benchmarks/gpu_master_suite.py Production integrity bug Fixed: _resolve_requested_device raises RuntimeError when CUDA is unavailable tests/benchmarks/test_gpu_benchmark_integrity.py::test_cuda_request_does_not_fallback_to_cpu Compressor construction failure could be represented by a generic approximation scripts/benchmarks/gpu_master_suite.py Production integrity bug Fixed: real compressor errors are recorded as ERROR; no SVD substitute exists tests/benchmarks/test_gpu_benchmark_integrity.py::test_failed_compressor_is_not_replaced_by_svd Backward validation could pass without valid gradients scripts/benchmarks/gpu_master_suite.py Production integrity bug Fixed: gradients must exist and every gradient must be finite tests/benchmarks/test_gpu_benchmark_integrity.py::test_backward_requires_finite_gradients Triton leaderboard relabeled repeated CosFormer runs scripts/benchmarks/triton_leaderboard.py Production integrity bug Fixed: wrapper delegates to the canonical 26-kernel runner; it does not synthesize or relabel rows Canonical runner entrypoint and GPU-only contract Triton/CUDA numerical mismatch could be reported as success neuralops/benchmarks/benchmark_all_26_comprehensive.py Production integrity bug Fixed: max_diff over tolerance produces FAIL_NUMERICS tests/benchmarks/test_gpu_benchmark_integrity.py::test_direct_kernel_marks_numerical_mismatch_as_failure Synthetic compressor rows scripts/benchmarks/results_exporter.py Explicit demo fixture Retained only behind --demo; never used by benchmark runners or imported result paths main() selects fixture only when args.from_jsonl is absent and --demo is explicit Explicit device_str CUDA requests were downgraded to CPU neuralops/benchmarks/{ops_runner,benchmark_extrapolation_32k,bench_llm_bandwidth,benchmark_dynamic_range_stress,multi_seed_stress_test_131_72,stress_test_seeds_404_777_999}.py, scripts/benchmarks/benchmark_delta_healing.py Production integrity bug Fixed: explicit CUDA requests now raise before allocation when unavailable Static fallback scan and repository Ruff gate

docs.title: Rules for future changes
docs.text:
• Production benchmark records must originate from an executed module.
  • Missing modules, failed construction, unavailable CUDA, missing gradients, and numerical mismatches must be represented by an error/failure status or raised.
  • Demo fixtures must remain behind an explicit opt-in flag and must not be used as defaults by benchmark or export APIs.
  • A benchmark result is not evidence of GPU execution unless its recorded device was resolved from the requested device and CUDA availability was verified.

docs.title: Remaining device-selection classifications
docs.text:
The repository-wide static scan still finds a small number of expressions that select a default device when no device was explicitly supplied. These are not equivalent to silently downgrading an explicit CUDA request:

  • neuralops/benchmarks/benchmark_all_26_comprehensive.py validates its resolved device and raises for a GPU-only run without CUDA.
  • neuralops/benchmarks/harness.py, adapters/compressor.py, and pareto_paper_suite.py use auto-selection defaults for general-purpose workflows; their explicit device paths require separate caller-level review.
  • scripts/benchmarks/qwen_7b_transplant.py and scripts/benchmarks/gpu_stress_heavy_trainer.py now expose explicit --device arguments and fail closed for explicit CUDA requests.
  • neuralops/benchmarks/pareto_paper_suite.py now defaults to CUDA and fails closed when the default GPU is unavailable; CPU remains available when passed explicitly by a caller.

These paths remain listed as pending audit items rather than being silently declared compliant. Any future change that adds an explicit --device cuda contract to them must use the same fail-closed check as the canonical runners.

docs.title: Decision vocabulary
docs.text:
• Keep: active and referenced.

docs.title: Required edge checks
docs.text: For each production module, the audit must check imports, exports, registry decorators, dynamic import strings, CLI references, benchmark references, test references, notebook references, and documentation links before assigning a cleanup decision.

docs.title: Status
docs.text: The high-level graph is documented. Confirmed cross-cutting edges include the lazy import layer (neuralops/__init__.py and neuralops/_lazy.py), registry consumers under neuralops/benchmarks, tests, and scripts, and the public CUDA/Triton catalog APIs under neuralops/kernels. Symbol-level and file-level edges are still being enumerated; no file is classified as dead until that enumeration is complete.

docs.title: NeuralOps Dependency Map
docs.text: This map records the verified execution relationships used to navigate the repository. It intentionally distinguishes static references from runtime behavior.

docs.title: Primary execution path
docs.text:
CLI / script / test
  -> runner or benchmark adapter
    -> public NeuralOps API
      -> registry lookup in neuralops/core/registry.py
        -> attention/compressor implementation
          -> backend dispatch
            -> CUDA / Triton / PyTorch reference tier

docs.title: Registry relationships
docs.text:
• ATTENTION_REGISTRY and COMPRESSOR_REGISTRY are defined in neuralops/core/registry.py.
  • Registration decorators and registry accessors are also defined there.
  • Canonical implementations are distributed across family directories under neuralops/layers/ and neuralops/compression/.
  • neuralops/attentions/ and neuralops/compression_engine/ must be treated as compatibility or alternate API surfaces until each symbol's caller graph proves otherwise.
  • neuralops/benchmarks/static_catalog.json is a static catalog, not a replacement for runtime registry resolution.

docs.title: Backend relationships
docs.text:
High-level operator
  -> neuralops/ops/cuda/_fallback.py
       -> native CUDA implementation
       -> Triton implementation
       -> PyTorch reference implementation

Any fallback must remain observable and numerical parity must be checked before a result is reported as valid.

docs.title: Benchmark relationships
docs.text:
• scripts/benchmarks/ contains standalone executable benchmark workflows.
  • neuralops/benchmarks/ contains reusable importable benchmark infrastructure.
  • tests/benchmarks/ validates benchmark contracts and integrity behavior.
  • tests/gpu_exhaustive/ exercises the remote GPU matrix and must run through PBS on N3090.

docs.title: Cleanup decision rule
docs.text:
No module is a deletion candidate merely because it is old, duplicated by name, or outside the preferred directory. Before proposing removal, verify:

  1. no Python import or package export references it;
  2. no registry, CLI, benchmark, notebook, config, or test references it;
  3. no compatibility promise requires it;
  4. its behavior is represented by a canonical replacement;
  5. documentation and changelog references can be updated without breaking history.

The caller graph and cleanup candidate list remain separate deliverables so that evidence is preserved before any destructive change.

docs.text:

  • scripts/: command-line utilities, audits, benchmark launchers, and repository maintenance.

docs.title: Backend layering
docs.text:
The repository contains more than one kernel-facing directory, and they have different responsibilities:

neuralops/layers or neuralops/attentions
  -> neuralops/core dispatch and registries
    -> neuralops/ops/cuda, neuralops/ops/triton, neuralops/ops/pytorch
      -> compiled/native, JIT, or reference execution

neuralops/core/cuda_kernels and neuralops/core/triton_kernels
  -> canonical kernel catalogs and core-level organization

Raw filesystem directory counts must not be presented as registry or implementation counts. The current canonical CUDA catalog is 110 unique modules / 114 native implementations; the raw neuralops/ops/cuda/ directory count includes compatibility and support directories and is tracked separately.

  • tests/triton_parity/: Triton/reference numerical parity.

docs.title: Cross-reference findings
docs.text:
• neuralops.attentions is referenced by many tests and package metadata, so it cannot be treated as an unused mirror without a symbol-level compatibility audit.
  • neuralops.compression_engine is referenced by tests and package metadata, so it is an active compatibility/API surface until proven otherwise.

docs.title: Source package
docs.text:
The neuralops/ package is organized by responsibility:

  • layers/ and attentions/: attention implementations grouped by family.
  • compression/ and compression_engine/: compression algorithms and compatibility layers.
  • core/: registries, backend dispatch, autograd utilities, fused operations, and canonical CUDA/Triton kernel catalogs.
  • kernels/ and ops/: backend-facing kernel implementations and PyTorch/CUDA/Triton operations.
  • benchmarks/: reusable benchmark infrastructure, task definitions, metrics, model adapters, and benchmark utilities.
  • analysis/, evaluation/, and reporting/: experiment analysis, evaluation workflows, and result/report generation.
  • adaptation/, surgery/, pipeline_transform/, and operations/: model transformation and attention/compression workflows.
  • models/, inference/, serving/, and integrations/: model-facing APIs and external runtime integrations.
  • config/, data/, executor/, runners/, and experiment_logging/: configuration, datasets, execution, sweep orchestration, and telemetry.
  • export/, results_saver/, recipe/, optimization/, and cli/: export, persistence, recipes, optimization, and command-line interfaces.

docs.title: Benchmarks and verification
docs.text:
Use the narrowest matching location:

  • scripts/benchmarks/: standalone command-line benchmark programs and strict integrity checks.
  • neuralops/benchmarks/: importable benchmark components used by the package and test suite.
  • tests/benchmarks/: CPU-safe benchmark-contract and regression tests.
  • tests/gpu_exhaustive/: remote GPU-only exhaustive validation; submit through PBS on N3090.
  • benchmarks/configs/ and benchmarks/models/: benchmark inputs and model metadata/assets.

GPU and Triton execution must not run on the login node or local macOS. Follow AGENTS.md and .agents/skills/hpc-sharif-cluster/SKILL.md for remote execution, environment selection, PBS allocation, and persistent monitoring.

docs.title: Documentation and generated data
docs.text:
• Root Markdown files describe project policy, setup, contribution, security, and high-level status.
  • docs/ contains extended documentation, API material, guides, integrations, benchmark notes, and historical reports.
  • results/, logs/, audit/, and other generated-output directories are experiment artifacts; follow .gitignore and AGENTS.md before adding or committing files.
  • Do not commit model weights, credentials, tokens, raw GPU logs, or generated benchmark output unless a repository policy explicitly requires the artifact.

docs.title: Change placement rules
docs.text:
1. Put reusable production behavior under the appropriate neuralops/ package rather than under scripts/.
  2. Put one-off orchestration, audits, and command-line utilities under scripts/.
  3. Put tests under tests/ and keep GPU-dependent tests separate from CPU-only tests.
  4. Update the nearest relevant documentation when a public path, benchmark contract, environment, or execution workflow changes.
  5. Preserve the registry and kernel-count invariants documented in AGENTS.md; distinguish catalog counts from raw filesystem counts.

The detailed audit records are maintained in BASELINE_STATE.md, PROJECT_FILE_INVENTORY.md, PROJECT_DEPENDENCY_MAP.md, PROJECT_CALLER_MAP.md, PROJECT_COMPLETE_DEPENDENCY_GRAPH.md, PROJECT_CLEANUP_CANDIDATES.md, PROJECT_CLEANUP_MATRIX.md, PROJECT_DOCUMENTATION_MATRIX.md, and PROJECT_VERIFICATION_MANIFEST.md. They must be updated when a package is moved, split, merged, deprecated, or removed.

docs.title: HPC execution path
docs.text:
The standard remote workflow is:

Mac agent
  └─ SSH alias hpc (login gateway; multiplexed connection)
       └─ PBS queue N3090 (GPU allocation)
            └─ GPU-3090-1 (assigned compute node)
                 └─ $HOME/.conda/envs/neuralops/bin/python

The login gateway is not the GPU execution host. A compute-node shell is valid for GPU work only after PBS confirms an active allocation for the job.

docs.title: 3. High-Throughput Specialized Microbenchmarks
docs.text:
Under specialized long-context sequence processing (\(T \ge 2048\)), high-throughput fused scans demonstrate order-of-magnitude acceleration:

  • chunked_delta_gate_scan: 742.05x speedup over eager unrolled recurrence (\(93.77\text{ ms} \to 0.126\text{ ms}\)).
  • triton_block_sparse_streaming_attn: 298.24x speedup over dynamic gathering (\(8.831\text{ ms} \to 0.0296\text{ ms}\)).
  • triton_hgrn2_fused_bwd_scan: 181.87x speedup over autograd backward graph unrolling (\(6.440\text{ ms} \to 0.0354\text{ ms}\)).
  • selective_scan: 51.11x speedup for SSM states (\(10.014\text{ ms} \to 0.196\text{ ms}\)).
  • flash_decode: 34.45x speedup during single-token autoregressive generation (\(1.122\text{ ms} \to 0.0326\text{ ms}\)).

docs.title: 1. Title & Subtitle
docs.text: SVD Linear Attention: Shrinking Massive Projection Weights via Truncated Singular Value Decomposition Replacing dense \(d \times d\) transformer projection matrices with twin low-rank factor bottlenecks to slash parameters by up to 85% with near-zero perplexity loss.

docs.title: 2. The Analogy
docs.text: Imagine a massive, uncompressed ultra-high-definition panoramic photograph (\(4000 \times 4000\) pixels). If you store every raw pixel individually, the file is gigantic. But when compressed to JPEG, the image isn't stored as 16 million independent numbers; instead, the compression algorithm identifies the primary color gradients and dominant geometric contours. SVD Linear Attention does the exact same thing to transformer weight matrices: it breaks a bulky square matrix into a tall thin matrix and a wide flat matrix, capturing over 95% of the information while discarding redundant numerical noise.

docs.title: 3. The Problem
docs.text: In standard Multi-Head Attention (MHA), every transformer layer projects input activations into Query, Key, Value, and Output spaces using four dense linear operators: \(W_q, W_k, W_v, W_o \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times d}\). - For modern large language models where the hidden dimension \(d = 4096\), each matrix contains \(4096^2 \approx 16.78\text{ million}\) parameters. - Across 4 projection matrices per layer and 32 layers, projection weights alone consume over 2.15 billion parameters (~4.3 GB in FP16), creating severe memory bandwidth saturation and slowing down auto-regressive token generation.

docs.title: 4. How It Works (The Intuition)
docs.text:
Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) states that any real matrix \(W \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times d}\) can be factored exactly into three matrices: $\(W = U \Sigma V^T\)$ where \(U \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times d}\) and \(V \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times d}\) are orthogonal matrices containing left and right singular vectors, and \(\Sigma = \text{diag}(\sigma_1, \sigma_2, \dots, \sigma_d)\) contains singular values sorted in descending order (\(\sigma_1 \ge \sigma_2 \ge \dots \ge 0\)).

By the Eckart-Young-Mirsky Theorem, the optimal rank-\(r\) approximation \(\hat{W}_r\) that minimizes Frobenius norm error is obtained by keeping only the top-\(r\) largest singular values: 1. We truncate \(U\) to \(U_r \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times r}\), \(\Sigma\) to \(\Sigma_r \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times r}\), and \(V\) to \(V_r \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times r}\). 2. We absorb the singular values equally into the factors: $\(W_{\text{down}} = \Sigma_r^{1/2} V_r^T \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times d}, \quad W_{\text{up}} = U_r \Sigma_r^{1/2} \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times r}\)$ 3. When an input token vector \(x \in \mathbb{R}^{1 \times d}\) arrives: - First, it down-projects into a compact bottleneck representation \(z = x W_{\text{down}}^T \in \mathbb{R}^{1 \times r}\). - Second, it up-projects back to the original dimension \(y = z W_{\text{up}}^T + b \in \mathbb{R}^{1 \times d}\).

Because \(r \ll d\) (e.g., \(r=64\) vs \(d=4096\)), parameter count per matrix drops from \(d^2\) (\(16.78\text{M}\)) to \(2 \cdot d \cdot r\) (\(524\text{K}\)) — a 32x parameter reduction per projection layer!

flowchart LR
    X["Input Activation X [B, N, d]"] --> V["W_down [r, d] (Down-Projection)"]
    V --> Z["Bottleneck State Z [B, N, r]"]
    Z --> U["W_up [d, r] (Up-Projection)"]
    U --> Bias["+ Bias Vector b [d]"]
    Bias --> Out["Projected Output Y [B, N, d]"]

    classDef tensor fill:#1E293B,stroke:#00FF9D,stroke-width:2px,color:#F8FAFC;
    classDef op fill:#0F172A,stroke:#38BDF8,stroke-width:2px,color:#38BDF8;

    class V,U,Bias op;

docs.title: 5. The Math (Light)
docs.text: \[\text{Standard Dense Linear: } Y = X W^T + b \quad (W \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times d}) \implies \mathcal{O}(d^2)\] \[\text{SVD Truncation: } W \approx U_r \Sigma_r V_r^T \quad \text{where } r \ll d\] \[\text{Truncation Error: } \| W - \hat{W}_r \|_F = \sqrt{\sum_{i=r+1}^d \sigma_i^2}\] \[\text{Factorized Forward Pass: } Y = \left( X V_r \Sigma_r^{1/2} \right) \left( U_r \Sigma_r^{1/2} \right)^T + b \implies \mathcal{O}(2 \cdot d \cdot r)\] \[\text{Compression Factor: } \rho = \frac{2 \cdot d \cdot r}{d^2} = \frac{2r}{d}\]

docs.title: 6. Why It Matters
docs.text:
• 50% to 85% Parameter Reduction: Cuts the static memory footprint of attention projection layers dramatically.
  • Zero-Shot Initialization: Pretrained foundation models (e.g., LLaMA, Mistral) can be decomposed post-hoc using torch.linalg.svd without needing pretraining from scratch.
  • Memory Bandwidth Relief: Reduces the bytes transferred per token from High-Bandwidth Memory (HBM) to SRAM, directly increasing auto-regressive generation throughput on resource-constrained GPUs.
  • Target Use Cases: On-device edge deployment, robotics micro-controllers, mobile AI assistants, and parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT).

docs.title: 2. Adaptive SVD Attention & Dynamic Rank Tuning
1. Title & Subtitle
docs.text: Adaptive SVD Attention: Dynamic Energy-Threshold Rank Allocation & Residual Adapters Allocating high rank to complex early syntactic layers and minimal rank to low-entropy deep layers based on cumulative spectral energy.

docs.title: 2. The Analogy
docs.text: Think of packing luggage for an expedition. You don't allocate equal space for heavy winter parkas and lightweight socks; you allocate suitcase volume based on functional necessity. Similarly, Adaptive SVD analyzes each layer's singular value spectrum: if a layer captures rich multi-head syntactic interactions, it receives a wider rank budget (\(r=128\)); if a deep layer only passes through high-level semantic abstractions, it compresses down to a tiny rank (\(r=16\)).

docs.title: 3. The Problem
docs.text: Uniform-rank SVD applies a single fixed rank \(r\) across all transformer layers. However, empirical singular value profiling shows that transformer layers exhibit drastically different intrinsic dimensionalities: - Early-to-middle layers capture intricate positional and syntactic dependencies, requiring high spectral capacity. - Deep layers converge onto low-rank manifold trajectories, meaning uniform SVD either allocates too much memory to deep layers or starves early layers of necessary expressive capacity.

docs.title: 4. How It Works (The Intuition)
docs.text:
1. Spectral Energy Profiling: For every projection weight matrix \(W \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times d}\) across all layers \(l \in \{1, \dots, L\}\), we compute the complete singular value spectrum \(\sigma_1 \ge \sigma_2 \ge \dots \ge \sigma_d\).
  2. Cumulative Energy Calculation: We define the cumulative energy ratio captured by the top-\(k\) singular values: $\(\text{Energy}(k) = \frac{\sum_{i=1}^k \sigma_i^2}{\sum_{j=1}^d \sigma_i^2}\)$
  3. Automated Rank Selection: Given a global energy retention threshold \(\tau \in [0.90, 0.99]\) (e.g., \(\tau = 0.95\)), the optimal rank \(r_l\) for layer \(l\) is chosen automatically as the minimum \(k\) satisfying \(\text{Energy}(k) \ge \tau\).
  4. Parallel Residual Adapters: To prevent catastrophic forgetting during post-training fine-tuning, the frozen SVD base \(W_{\text{svd}} = U_r V_r\) is augmented with a small trainable parallel residual adapter \(W_{\text{res}} = A B\): $\(W_{\text{adaptive}} = U_r V_r + A B\)$
flowchart TD
    W["Pretrained Matrix W [d, d]"] --> SVD["Full SVD: U, Σ, V^T"]
    SVD --> Energy["Calculate Cumulative Energy Ratio E(k)"]
    Energy --> Thresh{"E(k) ≥ Threshold τ?"}
    Thresh -- No --> Inc["k = k + 1"] --> Energy
    Thresh -- Yes --> SetRank["Assign Dynamic Rank r_l = k"]
    SetRank --> Split["Split into Frozen SVD Base (U_r, V_r) + Trainable Adapter (A, B)"]

    classDef default fill:#1E293B,stroke:#38BDF8,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#F8FAFC;
    classDef decision fill:#0F172A,stroke:#F59E0B,stroke-width:2px,color:#F59E0B;
    class Thresh decision;

docs.title: 5. The Math (Light)
docs.text: \[\text{Spectral Energy: } \mathcal{E}(k) = \frac{\sum_{i=1}^k \sigma_i^2}{\sum_{i=1}^d \sigma_i^2}\] \[\text{Dynamic Rank Rule: } r_l^*(\tau) = \min \left\{ k \in \{1, \dots, d\} \;\middle|\; \mathcal{E}(k) \ge \tau \right\}\] \[\text{Adaptive SVD Forward: } Y = \underbrace{\left(X V_r^T\right) U_r^T}_{\text{Frozen SVD Base}} + \underbrace{\left(X B^T\right) A^T}_{\text{Learnable Adapter}} + b\] \[\text{Global Parameter Optimization: } \min_{\{r_l\}} \sum_{l=1}^L 2 \cdot d \cdot r_l \quad \text{s.t.} \quad \mathcal{E}_l(r_l) \ge \tau \quad \forall l\]

docs.title: 6. Why It Matters
docs.text:
• Optimal Pareto Efficiency: Recovers 99.2% of uncompressed model performance while using 30% fewer total parameters than uniform-rank SVD.
  • Zero Manual Tuning: Eliminates tedious manual grid searches for layer-by-layer hyperparameter tuning.
  • Continual Adaptation: Trainable residual adapters (\(A, B\)) allow lightweight fine-tuning on new downstream tasks while base knowledge remains safely locked in the frozen SVD weights.
