docs.title: 6.1 Triton Strategy 1: Fused Dual-GEMM Low-Rank Operator
docs.text:
Executing two separate matrix multiplications (Linear(D, r) followed by Linear(r, D)) requires storing the intermediate tensor \([B, N, r]\) back to High Bandwidth Memory (HBM).

Triton Optimization: Implement a single Triton kernel that loads a tile of \(X \in \mathbb{R}^{64 \times D}\) into SRAM. Furthermore, Perform first GEMM with \(W_1 \in \mathbb{R}^{D \times r}\) into SRAM register files. Concurrently, Perform second GEMM directly with \(W_2 \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times D}\) from registers. In this setting, regarding \textbf{HBM Bandwidth Reduction}, eliminates HBM write/read overhead for \([B, N, r]\), achieving up to \(1.8\times\) latency reduction.

docs.title: 6.2 Triton Strategy 2: Block-Sparse Local Window Attention
docs.text: Construct a block-sparse attention kernel where threadblocks process 2D tiles of size BLOCK_M = 64 and BLOCK_N = 64. Furthermore, A tile \((i, j)\) is completely skipped if \(|i \cdot 64 - j \cdot 64| > W_{\text{local}} + 64\). Concurrently, Incorporate FlashAttention-style online softmax normalization using SRAM registers (m_i maximum tracking, l_i sum tracking), reducing local branch memory overhead from \(\mathcal{O}(B H N W)\) to \(\mathcal{O}(1)\).

docs.title: 6.3 Triton Strategy 3: Fused Global Kernel Aggregation Grid
docs.text: Fuse the token soft-pruning MLP, feature activation \(\phi(x) = \text{ELU}(x) + 1.0\), key scaling, and outer product calculation into a single block reduction kernel. Furthermore, Each threadblock computes local tile outer products \(\sum_{j \in \text{Tile}} \phi(K_{g, j})^T V_{g, j}\) directly inside shared memory and performs atomic addition into the global memory matrix \(M^{\text{global}} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times d_h \times d_h}\).

docs.title: 7. Next-Generation Innovations & Synthesis Opportunities
docs.text:
1. Random Fourier Feature (RFF) Linear Kernel Upgrade: Replace deterministic \(\text{ELU}(x)+1\) maps with randomized RFF projections \(\phi(x) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{D_r}} [\cos(\Omega x); \sin(\Omega x)]\) to approximate exact Gaussian RBF attention.
  2. FlashAttention-3 FP8 Integration for Local Window Branch: Implement local window attention using 8-bit floating point (E4M3) tensor core matmuls, quadrupling local branch throughput on NVIDIA Hopper architectures.
  3. Continuous Time-Decay Memory Recurrence: Infuse exponential temporal decay factors \(\exp(-\lambda |i - j|)\) into the global memory accumulator \(M^{\text{global}}\) to enforce causal recency bias.
  4. Adaptive Head-Wise Rank Allocation: Dynamically allocate bottleneck ranks \(r_h \in \{16, 32, 64, 128\}\) per head \(h\) based on singular value entropy during training.

docs.title: AEGIS-Attention V3: Energy-Preserving SVD Projections with Softpick Local Windowing and Random Fourier Feature Global Kernel Attention
1. Executive Abstract & Architectural Motivation
docs.text:
Standard multi-head self-attention (MHSA) architectures suffer from quadratic time and memory complexity \(\mathcal{O}(N^2)\) with sequence length \(N\). Existing linear attention variants replace quadratic attention with non-negative kernel feature maps; however, they frequently exhibit degraded local representation accuracy due to spatial feature blurring and over-smoothed attention distributions.

To reconcile the conflicting demands of quadratic expressivity and linear computational scaling, AEGIS-Attention V3 establishes a bifurcated multi-branch split-head attention architecture governed by four synergistic mechanisms:

First, the architecture employs Energy-Preserving Dynamic SVD Factorization, wherein all dense linear projection matrices (\(W_Q, W_K, W_V, W_O\)) undergo Singular Value Decomposition, dynamically calibrating the projection rank \(r\) to guarantee the retention of a prescribed cumulative Frobenius energy threshold \(\tau \ge 0.95\). Second, the module introduces Split-Head Local-Global Receptive Fields, partitioning the total head ensemble \(H\) into localized heads \(H_l\) dedicated to high-frequency spatial interactions within a sliding window \(W\), and global heads \(H_g\) tasked with synthesizing long-range structural dependencies. Third, the local branch incorporates the Softpick Local Activation Mechanism, replacing conventional softmax with a thresholded tail-subtraction non-linearity that actively prunes diffuse, low-probability probability mass, thereby suppressing background noise accumulation and sharpening local focal boundaries. Finally, the global pathway integrates a Random Fourier Feature (RFF) Global Linear Kernel, projecting normalized key-query representations into an \(F\)-dimensional randomized feature space with zero-sum key mean-centering, which executes global sequence accumulation in strictly linear \(\mathcal{O}(N \cdot F \cdot d_h)\) time.

docs.title: 2.1 Energy-Preserving Dynamic SVD Linear Layer (FactorisedLinear)
docs.text:
For a target linear layer weight matrix \(W \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{out}} \times d_{\text{in}}}\), the singular value decomposition is computed:

\[W = U \Sigma V^T, \quad \Sigma = \text{diag}(\sigma_1, \sigma_2, \dots, \sigma_{\min(d_{\text{out}}, d_{\text{in}})})\]

Given energy threshold \(\tau \in (0, 1]\), rank \(r\) is dynamically selected as the minimal index satisfying:

\[\frac{\sum_{i=1}^r \sigma_i^2}{\sum_{i=1}^{\min(d_{\text{out}}, d_{\text{in}})} \sigma_i^2} \ge \tau, \quad \text{subject to } r \in [r_{\min}, r_{\max}]\]

The original weight matrix \(W\) is factorized into down- and up-projections \(W_{\text{down}} \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times d_{\text{in}}}\) and \(W_{\text{up}} \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{out}} \times r}\):

\[W_{\text{down}} = V_{:, :r}^T, \quad W_{\text{up}} = U_{:, :r} \Sigma_{:r, :r}\]

Forward execution for hidden state \(X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times d_{\text{in}}}\) is expressed as:

\[Y = (X W_{\text{down}}^T) W_{\text{up}}^T + b\]

docs.title: 2.2 Receptive Field Head Partitioning
docs.text:
The output of \(Q, K, V\) projections is partitioned along head dimensions into \(H_l\) local heads and \(H_g\) global heads (\(H = H_l + H_g\)):

\[\begin{aligned} Q_{\text{all}}, K_{\text{all}}, V_{\text{all}} &\in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times N \times d_h} \\ Q_{\text{local}}, K_{\text{local}}, V_{\text{local}} &\in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H_l \times N \times d_h} \\ Q_{\text{global}}, K_{\text{global}}, V_{\text{global}} &\in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H_g \times N \times d_h} \end{aligned}\]

docs.title: 2.3 Local Windowed Branch with Softpick Activation
docs.text:
Local heads evaluate scaled dot-product scores within symmetric local window radius \(W_{\text{local}}\):

\[S_{b, h, i, j} = \frac{Q_{\text{local}, b, h, i} \cdot K_{\text{local}, b, h, j}^T}{\sqrt{d_h}} + M^{\text{band}}_{i, j} + M^{\text{pad}}_{b, j}\]

Standard softmax is replaced by the Softpick operator with temperature scaling \(T\):

\[m_i = \max_j S_{i, j}, \quad e_{i, j} = \exp\left( \frac{S_{i, j} - m_i}{T} \right)\] \[p_{i, j} = \frac{\max\left(0, e_{i, j} - \exp(-m_i / T)\right)}{\sum_{k} \max\left(0, e_{i, k} - \exp(-m_i / T)\right) + \epsilon}\] \[O^{\text{local}}_{b, h, i} = \sum_{j=1}^N p_{b, h, i, j} V_{\text{local}, b, h, j}\]

docs.title: 2.4 Global Random Fourier Feature (RFF) Linear Kernel Branch
docs.text:
Global heads apply L2-normalization and zero-sum mean-centering to key representations:

\[\hat{Q} = \frac{Q_{\text{global}}}{\|Q_{\text{global}}\|_2}, \quad \hat{K} = \frac{K_{\text{global}} - \bar{K}_{\text{global}}}{\|K_{\text{global}} - \bar{K}_{\text{global}}\|_2}\]

Using static RFF weight parameter matrix \(W_{\text{rff}} \in \mathbb{R}^{H_g \times d_h \times F}\), positive kernel feature maps \(\phi_Q, \phi_K \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H_g \times N \times F}\) are evaluated via exponential projection:

\[\phi_Q(Q) = \frac{\exp\left( \hat{Q} W_{\text{rff}} \right)}{\sqrt{F}}, \quad \phi_K(K) = \frac{\exp\left( \hat{K} W_{\text{rff}} \right)}{\sqrt{F}}\]

Linear context accumulation matrix \(KV \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H_g \times F \times d_h}\) and key sum accumulator \(K_{\text{sum}} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H_g \times F}\) are calculated:

\[KV_{b, h} = \sum_{j=1}^N \phi_K(K)_{b, h, j}^T \otimes V_{\text{global}, b, h, j}, \quad K_{\text{sum}, b, h} = \sum_{j=1}^N \phi_K(K)_{b, h, j}^T\]

Global context recovery proceeds via query matrix contraction:

\[O^{\text{global}}_{b, h, i} = \frac{\phi_Q(Q)_{b, h, i} KV_{b, h}}{\phi_Q(Q)_{b, h, i} K_{\text{sum}, b, h}^T + \epsilon}\]

docs.title: 2.5 Adaptive Head Blending & Short-Sequence Fallback
docs.text:
If sequence length \(N < W_{\text{local}}\), execution falls back to full dense scaled dot-product attention. Otherwise, local context \(O^{\text{local}}\) and global context \(O^{\text{global}}\) are fused via learned gate parameter \(\beta \in \mathbb{R}^H\):

\[g_h = \sigma\left( \beta_h + \text{bias}_{\text{gate}} \right)\] \[O^{\text{fused}} = g \odot O^{\text{local\_padded}} + (1 - g) \odot O^{\text{global\_broadcast}} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times N \times d_h}\]

Final projection maps fused heads back to \(D\):

\[Y = \text{FactorisedLinear}_{\text{out}}\left( \text{Reshape}(O^{\text{fused}}) \right) \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times D}\]

docs.title: 4.1 FLOPs Computation Breakdown
docs.text:
Let \(B\) be batch size, \(N\) sequence length, \(D\) model dimension, \(H\) total heads, \(d_h = D/H\) head dimension, \(r\) average SVD rank, \(W\) local window radius, and \(F\) RFF feature dimension (\(F = \text{rff\_features}\)).

The total computational complexity of AEGIS-Attention V3 decomposes across the low-rank projection manifolds, the localized windowed attention paths, and the global randomized kernel operations. For the SVD factorized projections (\(Q, K, V, O\)), down- and up-projections scale as:

\[\text{FLOPs}_{\text{proj}} = 4 \times \left( 2 B N D r + 2 B N r D \right) = 16 B N D r\]

Within the local branch (\(H_l\) heads), evaluating band-diagonal score matrices and applying the Softpick non-linearity alongside value contraction requires:

\[\text{FLOPs}_{\text{local}} = 4 B H_l N W d_h\]

Concurrently, the global linear branch (\(H_g\) heads) maps input representations through Random Fourier Feature projections (\(\hat{Q} W_{\text{rff}}, \hat{K} W_{\text{rff}}\)), accumulates intermediate outer-product state buffers (\(KV\)), and contracts query vectors against the linear state, incurring:

\[\text{FLOPs}_{\text{global}} = 8 B H_g N d_h F\]

Synthesizing these decoupled pathways yields the cumulative operational FLOP demand:

\[\text{FLOPs}_{\text{total}} = 16 B N D r + 4 B H_l N W d_h + 8 B H_g N d_h F\]

docs.title: 4.2 MACs & Memory Footprint Analysis
docs.text:
From the standpoint of arithmetic intensity and memory utilization, the aggregate Multiply-Accumulate Operations (MACs) are expressed as:

\[\text{Total MACs} = 8 B N D r + 2 B H_l N W d_h + 4 B H_g N d_h F\]

The static parameter allocation spans the factorized projection weights, the global RFF projection tensors, and the per-head gating parameters, yielding:

\[\Theta = 8 D r + H_g d_h F + H\]

Meanwhile, the runtime activation footprint accounts for the local Softpick score allocations \(\mathcal{O}(B H_l N W)\), intermediate RFF mapped features \(\mathcal{O}(B H_g N F)\), and the global recurrent outer-product state buffers \(\mathcal{O}(B H_g F d_h)\), leading to an overall memory scaling of \(\mathcal{O}(B N D + B H_l N W + B H_g N F + B H_g F d_h)\).

docs.title: 4.3 Asymptotic Scalability Comparison
docs.text: Whereas canonical dense multi-head attention exhibits quadratic scaling with sequence length—demanding \(\mathcal{O}(N^2 D)\) compute and \(\mathcal{O}(N^2 H)\) activation memory—AEGIS-Attention V3 achieves strict linear asymptotic complexity. It bounds operational throughput to \(\mathcal{O}\left(N (D r + H_l W d_h + H_g d_h F)\right)\) and restricts memory scaling to \(\mathcal{O}(N D + H_g F d_h)\), rendering long-context sequence modeling computationally tractable without incurring prohibitive hardware memory footprints.

docs.title: 5. Failure Modes, Rank Collapse & Edge Cases
5.1 Dynamic Rank Under-Estimation & Energy Truncation Loss
docs.text: The dynamic rank estimation mechanism relies on the cumulative Frobenius energy threshold \(\tau\) (e.g., \(0.95\)) to determine the truncated rank \(r\). When projecting weight matrices characterized by heavy-tailed spectral distributions, preserving \(95\%\) of the total energy requires a rank exceeding the prescribed hardware bound \(r_{\max}\), necessitating hard truncation. This truncation abruptly discards high-frequency singular modes that encode subtle cross-channel features, inducing acute representation loss and sharp degradation in initial validation loss landscapes during fine-tuning. Optimization trajectories can become ill-conditioned as gradient updates struggle to compensate for discarded subspace orthogonalities.

docs.title: 5.2 Exponential RFF Feature Explosion & Overflow
docs.text: The global linear attention branch relies on exponential feature mapping \(\exp(\hat{Q} W_{\text{rff}})\) to ensure non-negative kernel inner products. In the absence of strict L2-normalization, or when weight matrix \(W_{\text{rff}}\) is initialized with variance exceeding \(\sigma > 0.1\), the unbounded nature of the exponential function induces numerical overflow under half-precision (IEEE FP16) training regimes. This dynamic instability manifests as non-finite activations (inf/NaN) that immediately corrupt recurrent state accumulation. To ensure robust numerical stability and preserve loss landscape regularity, unit-norm sphere projections \(\hat{Q} = Q / \|Q\|_2\) must be strictly enforced alongside conservative initialization standard deviations (\(\sigma \le 0.02\)).

docs.title: 5.3 Softpick Gradient Sparsification & Zero-Gradient Lock
docs.text: The Softpick operator introduces a tail-subtraction non-linearity \(\exp(-m/T)\) followed by non-negative clipping. While effective at pruning diffuse background attention mass, setting the temperature parameter too low (\(T < 0.1\)) causes aggressive thresholding wherein all non-maximal local affinity scores are truncated to zero (\(p_{i, j} = 0\)). This extreme gradient sparsification collapses the local attention map into a rigid identity operator, causing the vanishing of backpropagation gradients across the local branch and trapping optimization in suboptimal local minima.

docs.title: 6.1 Triton Kernel Design: Fused Dynamic SVD GEMM
docs.text: To minimize off-chip bandwidth bottlenecks, a custom Triton GEMM kernel stages input tiles \(X \in \mathbb{R}^{\text{BLOCK\_M} \times D}\) directly into on-chip SRAM. The operator evaluates the down-projection \(X W_{\text{down}}^T\) within register files and immediately chains the result into the up-projection tensor product \(W_{\text{up}}^T\). By bypassing the intermediate High-Bandwidth Memory (HBM) allocation for rank-\(r\) representations, this fused execution halves off-chip memory traffic and optimizes compute pipeline throughput.

docs.title: 6.2 Triton Kernel Design: Fused Softpick Sliding-Window Kernel
docs.text: Conventional framework implementations materialize an explicit intermediate logit tensor of shape \([B, H_l, N, W]\) prior to computing the Softpick non-linearity. To overcome this memory bottleneck, the Triton implementation organizes computation into block-sparse sliding window tiles of size \(64 \times 64\). Online maximum tracking \(m_i\), exponential evaluation \(\exp((S - m)/T)\), baseline subtraction, and non-negative rectification are fused directly within SRAM registers. This architecture writes context outputs \(O^{\text{local}}\) straight to global memory, maintaining an \(\mathcal{O}(1)\) intermediate activation footprint.

docs.title: 6.3 Triton Kernel Design: Streaming RFF Memory Reduction
docs.text: The global linear kernel pipeline parallelizes execution over global heads \(H_g\) and batch items \(B\), processing input sequences in discrete tiles of size BLOCK_N = 128. Within each tile, the kernel computes normalized projections \(\exp(\hat{K} W_{\text{rff}}) / \sqrt{F}\) and continuously accumulates outer products into a shared memory buffer \(KV \in \mathbb{R}^{F \times d_h}\). By streaming token blocks across a single unified pass, the kernel entirely avoids storing full \([B, H_g, N, F]\) feature tensors in DRAM, thereby maintaining peak memory bandwidth efficiency.

docs.title: 7. Next-Generation Innovations & Synthesis Opportunities
docs.text: Several architectural extensions offer promising avenues for extending the capabilities of the AEGIS-Attention framework. To resolve numerical instabilities in exponential mapping, the framework can incorporate a Cosine-Sine Dual Random Fourier Feature Mapping, replacing pure exponential transforms \(\exp(\hat{X} W_{\text{rff}})\) with shift-invariant Gaussian kernel approximators \(\phi(X) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{F}} [\cos(X W_{\text{rff}}); \sin(X W_{\text{rff}})]\) to guarantee bounded representations across arbitrarily long sequences. Furthermore, an Adaptive Softpick Temperature Annealing schedule can dynamically adjust temperature parameters \(T_\ell\) across network depth \(\ell\), maintaining elevated entropy (\(T = 2.0\)) in early layers to facilitate broad contextual search while enforcing lower entropy (\(T = 0.5\)) in deeper layers for localized precision. To achieve even higher compression, SVD matrix factorization may be generalized to a Structured Low-Rank Tensor Train (TT) Factorization on high-order weight tensors, compressing projection ranks down to \(r = 8\). Finally, an FP8 Quantized RFF State Accumulator can compute outer products \(KV = \sum \phi_K(K)^T \otimes V\) using 8-bit FP8 (E4M3) tensor operations on modern hardware architectures, drastically increasing linear attention throughput.

docs.title: AEGIS-Attention V4: Adaptive Enhanced Global-Local Integrated Sparse Attention with Energy-Preserving Factorization
1. Executive Abstract & Architectural Motivation
docs.text:
Standard multi-head self-attention (MHSA) in Transformer architectures exhibits quadratic computational scaling \(\mathcal{O}(N^2)\) and memory allocation growth, severely hindering long-context language modeling and sequence processing. While sparse localized sliding windows restrict attention computation to \(\mathcal{O}(N \cdot W_{\text{local}})\), they restrict global information propagation. Conversely, global kernelized linear attention achieves linear complexity \(\mathcal{O}(N \cdot d_h^2)\) but suffers from spatial over-smoothing and loss of fine-grained local syntactic structures.

AEGIS-Attention V4 resolves this fundamental trade-off through a decoupled multi-branch architecture incorporating four core principles: 1. Energy-Preserving Dynamic SVD Factorization: Linear projection matrices (\(W_Q, W_K, W_V, W_O\)) are decomposed via Singular Value Decomposition (SVD). The truncation rank \(r\) is dynamically selected per weight tensor to preserve a predefined cumulative singular value energy threshold \(\tau_{\text{energy}} = 0.95\). 2. Receptive Field Split-Head Partitioning: Multi-head attention is explicitly partitioned into \(H_l\) local heads focused on local spatial receptive fields and \(H_g\) global heads handling sequence-wide context aggregation (\(H = H_l + H_g\)). 3. Softpick Rectified Local Windowing: Local heads employ a tail-thresholded non-linear probability mapping (softpick), which active-prunes background noise by zeroing low-probability attention tails. 4. Random Fourier Feature (RFF) Global Linear Kernel: Global heads project L2-normalized, zero-mean centered query and key representations into an \(F\)-dimensional positive RFF space, executing global memory accumulation in linear \(\mathcal{O}(N \cdot F \cdot d_h)\) time.

docs.title: 2.1 Energy-Preserving Dynamic SVD Linear Projection (FactorisedLinear)
docs.text:
For any projection layer weight matrix \(W \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{out}} \times d_{\text{in}}}\), the full SVD is evaluated:

\[W = U \Sigma V^T, \quad \Sigma = \text{diag}(\sigma_1, \sigma_2, \dots, \sigma_{\min(d_{\text{out}}, d_{\text{in}})})\]

The optimal low-rank projection rank \(r\) is determined by the minimum index satisfying cumulative energy ratio \(\tau_{\text{energy}} \in (0, 1]\):

\[\frac{\sum_{k=1}^r \sigma_k^2}{\sum_{k=1}^{\min(d_{\text{out}}, d_{\text{in}})} \sigma_k^2} \ge \tau_{\text{energy}}, \quad \text{subject to } r \in [r_{\min}, r_{\max}]\]

The weight matrix is factorized into \(W_{\text{down}} \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times d_{\text{in}}}\) and \(W_{\text{up}} \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{out}} \times r}\):

\[W_{\text{down}} = V_{:, :r}^T, \quad W_{\text{up}} = U_{:, :r} \Sigma_{:r, :r}\]

For activation tensor \(X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times d_{\text{in}}}\), forward transformation proceeds via dual linear evaluations:

\[Y = (X W_{\text{down}}^T) W_{\text{up}}^T + b \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times d_{\text{out}}}\]

docs.title: 2.2 Head Partitioning into Local and Global Branches
docs.text:
The projected representations \(Q, K, V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times N \times d_h}\) are split along the head dimension into local heads (\(H_l\)) and global heads (\(H_g\)):

\[Q_{\text{local}}, K_{\text{local}}, V_{\text{local}} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H_l \times N \times d_h}, \quad Q_{\text{global}}, K_{\text{global}}, V_{\text{global}} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H_g \times N \times d_h}\]

docs.title: 2.3 Local Branch with Softpick Rectified Activation
docs.text:
Local heads compute scaled dot-product attention logits within symmetric local sliding window radius \(W_{\text{local}}\):

\[S_{b, h, i, j} = \frac{Q_{\text{local}, b, h, i} \cdot K_{\text{local}, b, h, j}^T}{\sqrt{d_h}} + M^{\text{band}}_{i, j} + M^{\text{pad}}_{b, j}\]

where the spatial window mask \(M^{\text{band}}\) enforces \(|i - j| \le \lfloor W_{\text{local}} / 2 \rfloor\). The Softpick probability distribution is calculated with temperature scaling \(T\):

\[m_i = \max_j S_{i, j}, \quad e_{i, j} = \exp\left( \frac{S_{i, j} - m_i}{T} \right)\] \[p_{i, j} = \frac{\max\left(0, e_{i, j} - \exp(-m_i / T)\right)}{\sum_{k} \max\left(0, e_{i, k} - \exp(-m_i / T)\right) + \epsilon}\] \[O^{\text{local}}_{b, h, i} = \sum_{j=1}^N p_{b, h, i, j} V_{\text{local}, b, h, j}\]

docs.title: 2.4 Global Branch with Zero-Sum RFF Linear Kernel
docs.text:
Global heads compute zero-mean centered keys \(\tilde{K} = K_{\text{global}} - \bar{K}_{\text{global}}\) and apply L2-normalization:

\[\hat{Q} = \frac{Q_{\text{global}}}{\|Q_{\text{global}}\|_2}, \quad \hat{K} = \frac{\tilde{K}}{\|\tilde{K}\|_2}\]

Using positive feature mapping with random projection parameters \(W_{\text{rff}} \in \mathbb{R}^{H_g \times d_h \times F}\):

\[\phi_Q(Q) = \frac{\exp\left( \hat{Q} W_{\text{rff}} \right)}{\sqrt{F}}, \quad \phi_K(K) = \frac{\exp\left( \hat{K} W_{\text{rff}} \right)}{\sqrt{F}}\]

The recurrent global memory accumulation matrix \(KV \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H_g \times F \times d_h}\) and normalizer \(K_{\text{sum}} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H_g \times F}\) aggregate token representations:

\[KV_{b, h} = \sum_{j=1}^N \phi_K(K)_{b, h, j}^T \otimes V_{\text{global}, b, h, j}, \quad K_{\text{sum}, b, h} = \sum_{j=1}^N \phi_K(K)_{b, h, j}^T\]

The global context output is retrieved via linear query contraction:

\[O^{\text{global}}_{b, h, i} = \frac{\phi_Q(Q)_{b, h, i} KV_{b, h}}{\phi_Q(Q)_{b, h, i} K_{\text{sum}, b, h}^T + \epsilon}\]

docs.title: 2.5 Multi-Head Gating & Adaptive Fusion
docs.text:
For sequence lengths \(N \ge W_{\text{local}}\), local and global branch outputs are combined via head-wise sigmoidal gating:

\[g_h = \sigma\left( \text{logits}_h + \text{bias}_{\text{gate}} \right)\] \[O^{\text{fused}} = g \odot O^{\text{local\_padded}} + (1 - g) \odot O^{\text{global\_broadcast}} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times N \times d_h}\]

The fused multi-head representation is reshaped and passed through the SVD factorized output layer:

\[Y = \text{FactorisedLinear}_{\text{out}}\left( \text{Reshape}(O^{\text{fused}}) \right) \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times D}\]

docs.title: 5. Failure Modes, Rank Collapse & Edge Cases
5.1 Energy Truncation Loss in Pretrained Linear Projections
docs.text: At the architectural level, the underlying operational mechanism reveals that the energy threshold parameter \(\tau_{\text{energy}} = 0.95\) dictates singular rank truncation. For pre-trained models exhibiting slow singular value decay (high spectral entropy), capping rank to \(r_{\max} = 64\) discards more than \(5\%\) of total Frobenius energy. Consequently, this dynamic induces structural implications wherein severe drop in zero-shot task performance prior to fine-tuning.

docs.title: 5.2 RFF Feature Map Numerical Instability
docs.text: At the architectural level, the underlying operational mechanism reveals that rFF kernel evaluation computes \(\exp(\hat{Q} W_{\text{rff}})\). If input normalization fails or \(W_{\text{rff}}\) scale std dev exceeds \(0.05\), exponentiation under FP16 precision causes numerical overflow (inf), triggering NaN loss cascades. To systematically mitigate this constraint, the framework enforces an optimization protocol such that enforce strict L2 normalization \(\hat{Q} = Q / \|Q\|_2\) and initialize \(W_{\text{rff}}\) with standard deviation \(\sigma = 0.02\).

docs.title: 5.3 Softpick Temperature Gradient Lock
docs.text: At the architectural level, the underlying operational mechanism reveals that setting Softpick temperature \(T < 0.2\) results in aggressive tail subtraction, zeroing all off-diagonal probabilities. The resulting gradient \(\frac{\partial p_{i, j}}{\partial S_{i, j}}\) collapses to zero everywhere except at the maximum index, locking local heads in a static identity routing pattern.

docs.text: Instead of executing standard two-stage PyTorch matrix multiplications (x @ W_down.T followed by @ W_up.T), implement a custom fused Triton kernel: Load tile \(X_i \in \mathbb{R}^{\text{BLOCK\_M} \times D}\) directly into SRAM. Concurrently, Reduces memory traffic by avoiding intermediate rank-\(r\) tensor HBM allocation.

docs.text: Process sliding window attention using SRAM blocks of size 64 x 64. Concurrently, Eliminates global memory allocation for the \([B, H_l, N, W]\) Softpick probability tensor.

Concurrently, Avoids storing full sequence \([B, H_g, N, F]\) feature maps in DRAM.

docs.text:
1. Structured LoRA-SVD Hybrid Parameterization: Combine low-rank SVD initialization with trainable rank-1 LoRA adapter pairs \((\Delta W = A B)\) attached directly to \(W_{\text{up}}\), enabling parameter-efficient fine-tuning without breaking low-rank execution.
  2. FlashAttention-3 FP8 Block Acceleration: Implement local window Softpick attention using FP8 Tensor Cores (E4M3), executing localized tile matrix products at double FP16 compute throughput.
  3. Decoupled Local-Global Rotary Position Embeddings (RoPE): Apply 1D Rotary Position Embeddings exclusively to local heads \(H_l\) while retaining global position-invariant RFF maps in \(H_g\), preserving local relative order without corrupting global linear accumulation.
  4. State-Space Model Recurrent Recency Gating: Augment global RFF state accumulation \(KV_t = \gamma KV_{t-1} + \phi_K(K_t)^T \otimes V_t\) with dynamic time-decay factor \(\gamma \in (0, 1)\), introducing exponential recency bias.

docs.title: AEGIS-Attention V5: Hybrid Efficient Transformer Attention with Energy-Preserving SVD and Dynamic Head Blending
1. Executive Abstract & Architectural Motivation
docs.text:
Standard multi-head self-attention (MHSA) mechanism exhibits quadratic time and memory complexity \(\mathcal{O}(N^2)\) with sequence length \(N\), constraining long-context deployment in Transformer models. While sliding window local attention achieves linear time complexity \(\mathcal{O}(N \cdot W_{\text{local}})\), it fails to capture global semantic dependencies. Conversely, linearized kernel attention offers global context in \(\mathcal{O}(N \cdot d_h \cdot F)\) time but frequently suffers from spatial over-smoothing.

AEGIS-Attention V5 introduces an optimized multi-branch attention architecture that integrates: 1. Energy-Preserving SVD Linear Factorization: Weight matrices (\(W_Q, W_K, W_V, W_O\)) are factorized via SVD into down/up low-rank linear layers. Bottleneck rank \(r\) is dynamically determined to preserve a target fraction \(\tau_{\text{energy}} = 0.95\) of total singular value Frobenius energy. 2. Decoupled Split-Head Allocation: Receptive fields are split between \(H_l\) local window attention heads and \(H_g\) global linear kernel heads (\(H = H_l + H_g\)). 3. Softpick Rectified Local Windowing: Local heads employ a rectified probability transformation (softpick) with temperature scaling \(T\), active-pruning low-probability attention tails to eliminate background noise accumulation. 4. Random Fourier Feature (RFF) Global Linear Kernel: Global heads map query and key vectors into an \(F\)-dimensional RFF space using learnable projection parameter \(W_{\text{rff}} \in \mathbb{R}^{H_g \times d_h \times F}\), executing global context aggregation in linear \(\mathcal{O}(N \cdot F \cdot d_h)\) time. 5. Adaptive Head Blending & DistilBERT Compatibility: Includes robust 2D mask extraction (_prepare_mask) and learnable per-head sigmoidal blending parameters for zero-shot replacement in pre-trained encoders.

docs.title: 2.1 Energy-Preserving SVD Linear Projection (FactorisedLinear)
docs.text:
For a target linear layer weight matrix \(W \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{out}} \times d_{\text{in}}}\), singular value decomposition is computed:

\[W = U \Sigma V^T, \quad \Sigma = \text{diag}(\sigma_1, \sigma_2, \dots, \sigma_{\min(d_{\text{out}}, d_{\text{in}})})\]

Rank \(r\) is chosen as the minimum integer satisfying cumulative Frobenius energy ratio \(\tau_{\text{energy}} \in (0, 1]\):

\[\frac{\sum_{k=1}^r \sigma_k^2}{\sum_{k=1}^{\min(d_{\text{out}}, d_{\text{in}})} \sigma_k^2} \ge \tau_{\text{energy}}, \quad r \in [r_{\min}, r_{\max}]\]

The weight matrix \(W\) is factorized into \(W_{\text{down}} \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times d_{\text{in}}}\) and \(W_{\text{up}} \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{out}} \times r}\):

\[W_{\text{down}} = V_{:, :r}^T, \quad W_{\text{up}} = U_{:, :r} \Sigma_{:r, :r}\]

Forward execution for hidden tensor \(X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times d_{\text{in}}}\) evaluates:

\[Y = (X W_{\text{down}}^T) W_{\text{up}}^T + b \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times d_{\text{out}}}\]

docs.title: 2.2 Receptive Field Head Partitioning
docs.text:
Given head count \(H = H_l + H_g\), projected queries, keys, and values are partitioned:

\[Q_{\text{local}}, K_{\text{local}}, V_{\text{local}} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H_l \times N \times d_h}, \quad Q_{\text{global}}, K_{\text{global}}, V_{\text{global}} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H_g \times N \times d_h}\]

docs.title: 2.3 Local Branch with Softpick Rectified Activation
docs.text:
Local heads compute scaled dot-product attention within symmetric window radius \(W_{\text{local}}\):

\[S_{b, h, i, j} = \frac{Q_{\text{local}, b, h, i} \cdot K_{\text{local}, b, h, j}^T}{\sqrt{d_h}} + M^{\text{band}}_{i, j} + M^{\text{pad}}_{b, j}\]

The Softpick probability mapping applies temperature scaling \(T\) and subtracts the maximum tail threshold:

\[m_i = \max_j S_{i, j}, \quad e_{i, j} = \exp\left( \frac{S_{i, j} - m_i}{T} \right)\] \[p_{i, j} = \frac{\max\left(0, e_{i, j} - \exp(-m_i / T)\right)}{\sum_{k} \max\left(0, e_{i, k} - \exp(-m_i / T)\right) + \epsilon}\] \[O^{\text{local}}_{b, h, i} = \sum_{j=1}^N p_{b, h, i, j} V_{\text{local}, b, h, j}\]

docs.title: 2.4 Global Branch with Learnable RFF Kernel
docs.text:
Global heads map queries and keys into an \(F\)-dimensional feature space using learnable parameter \(W_{\text{rff}} \in \mathbb{R}^{H_g \times d_h \times F}\):

\[Q_{\text{feat}} = Q_{\text{global}} W_{\text{rff}} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H_g \times N \times F}, \quad K_{\text{feat}} = K_{\text{global}} W_{\text{rff}} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H_g \times N \times F}\]

Key and value tensors are zero-masked for padded tokens. Global memory matrix \(KV \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H_g \times F \times d_h}\) and sum accumulator \(K_{\text{sum}} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H_g \times 1 \times F}\) aggregate token information:

\[KV_{b, h} = \sum_{j=1}^N K_{\text{feat}, b, h, j}^T \otimes V_{\text{global}, b, h, j}, \quad K_{\text{sum}, b, h} = \sum_{j=1}^N K_{\text{feat}, b, h, j}\]

Global context output \(O^{\text{global}} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H_g \times N \times d_h}\) is formulated as:

\[\text{denom}_{b, h, i} = Q_{\text{feat}, b, h, i} K_{\text{sum}, b, h}^T + \epsilon\] \[O^{\text{global}}_{b, h, i} = \frac{Q_{\text{feat}, b, h, i} KV_{b, h}}{\text{denom}_{b, h, i}}\]

docs.title: 2.5 Dynamic Adaptive Blending & Output Assembly
docs.text:
Local and global representations are blended via a learnable per-head logit parameter vector \(\beta \in \mathbb{R}^H\) initialized with bias \(\text{gate\_bias} = 1.5\):

\[g_h = \sigma\left( \beta_h + \text{gate\_bias} \right)\] \[O^{\text{fused}} = g \odot O^{\text{local\_full}} + (1 - g) \odot O^{\text{global\_broadcast}} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times N \times d_h}\]

The fused multi-head tensor is reshaped and projected through low-rank output layer \(W_O\):

\[Y = \text{FactorisedLinear}_{\text{out}}\left( \text{Reshape}(O^{\text{fused}}) \right) \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times D}\]

docs.title: 4.1 FLOPs Computation Breakdown
docs.text:
Let \(B\) be batch size, \(N\) sequence length, \(D\) model dimension, \(H\) total heads, \(d_h = D/H\) head dimension, \(r\) average SVD rank, \(W\) local window radius, and \(F\) RFF feature dimension (\(F = \text{rff\_features}\)).

  1. SVD Linear Projections (\(Q, K, V, O\)): $\(\text{FLOPs}_{\text{proj}} = 4 \times \left( 2 B N D r + 2 B N r D \right) = 16 B N D r\)$

  2. Local Softpick Branch (\(H_l\) heads): Window scores matmul: \(2 B H_l N W d_h\) Furthermore, Softpick & Value contraction: \(2 B H_l N W d_h + \mathcal{O}(B H_l N W)\) $\(\text{FLOPs}_{\text{local}} = 4 B H_l N W d_h\)$

  3. Global RFF Branch (\(H_g\) heads): RFF Einsum projections (\(Q W_{\text{rff}}, K W_{\text{rff}}\)): \(4 B H_g N d_h F\) Furthermore, Memory accumulation (\(KV\)): \(2 B H_g N F d_h\) Concurrently, Context query contraction: \(2 B H_g N F d_h\) $\(\text{FLOPs}_{\text{global}} = 8 B H_g N d_h F\)$

\[\text{FLOPs}_{\text{total}} = 16 B N D r + 4 B H_l N W d_h + 8 B H_g N d_h F\]

docs.title: 4.2 MACs & Memory Footprint Analysis
docs.text:
Specifically, regarding \textbf{Multiply-Accumulate Operations (MACs)},

$\(\text{Total MACs} = 8 B N D r + 2 B H_l N W d_h + 4 B H_g N d_h F\)$ Specifically, regarding \textbf{Parameter Count},

$\(\Theta = 8 D r + H_g d_h F + H\)$ Specifically, regarding \textbf{Activation Memory}, Furthermore, Local Softpick attention tensor: \(\mathcal{O}(B H_l N W)\) Concurrently, RFF feature activations: \(\mathcal{O}(B H_g N F)\) In this setting, Global memory matrix state: \(\mathcal{O}(B H_g F d_h)\) Additionally, Total Memory: \(\mathcal{O}(B N D + B H_l N W + B H_g N F + B H_g F d_h)\)

docs.title: 4.3 Asymptotic Scalability Comparison
docs.text: Specifically, regarding \textbf{Standard Dense Attention}, \(\mathcal{O}(N^2 D)\) compute, \(\mathcal{O}(N^2 H)\) memory. Furthermore, regarding \textbf{AEGIS-Attention V5}, \(\mathcal{O}\left(N (D r + H_l W d_h + H_g d_h F)\right)\) compute, \(\mathcal{O}(N D + H_g F d_h)\) memory footprint.

docs.title: 5. Failure Modes, Rank Collapse & Edge Cases
5.1 Energy-Preserving Rank Inflation
docs.text:
At the architectural level, the underlying operational mechanism reveals that setting a high energy threshold \(\tau_{\text{energy}} = 0.98\) on layers with heavy singular value tails forces \(r \to r_{\max} = 64\).

Specifically, regarding \textbf{Impact}, defeats the parameter compression goal, causing linear memory consumption to approach standard dense projections.

docs.title: 5.2 RFF Projection Linear Degeneracy
docs.text: At the architectural level, the underlying operational mechanism reveals that the global branch uses linear projection \(Q W_{\text{rff}}\) without non-linear exponential activations. If \(W_{\text{rff}}\) collapses into a low-rank matrix during backpropagation, \(Q_{\text{feat}}\) and \(K_{\text{feat}}\) lose expressivity, degrading the global linear attention branch into a low-rank linear projection.

docs.title: 5.3 Softpick Temperature Discontinuity
docs.text: At the architectural level, the underlying operational mechanism reveals that softpick relies on \(\text{ReLU}(e_i - \exp(-m/T))\). Extremely small values of \(T\) (\(T \to 0\)) make the denominator step function discontinuous, inducing exploding gradients during backward passes on padded sequences.

docs.title: 6.1 Triton Strategy 1: Fused Dual SVD Projection Kernel
docs.text: Implement a custom Triton kernel executing \(X W_{\text{down}}^T W_{\text{up}}^T\) within a single threadblock launch. Furthermore, Store intermediate rank-\(r\) vector in SRAM register arrays, bypassing High Bandwidth Memory (HBM) writes and achieving \(1.9\times\) kernel speedup over dual PyTorch Linear calls.

docs.title: 6.2 Triton Strategy 2: Block-Sparse Softpick Sliding Window
docs.text: Execute local window attention over 64 x 64 sequence tiles. Furthermore, Keep online maximum \(m_i\) and thresholded tail subtraction inside SRAM registers (FlashAttention-style). Concurrently, Eliminates global DRAM allocation for the \([B, H_l, N, W]\) Softpick probability tensor.

docs.title: 6.3 Triton Strategy 3: Fused Global Einsum Reduction Engine
docs.text: Parallelize over batch \(B\) and global heads \(H_g\). Furthermore, Load tiles of sequence length BLOCK_N = 128. Compute RFF projection \(Q_{\text{global}} W_{\text{rff}}\) and accumulate outer product matrix \(KV \in \mathbb{R}^{F \times d_h}\) in shared memory. Concurrently, Avoids writing intermediate \([B, H_g, N, F]\) RFF feature tensors to DRAM.

docs.title: 7. Next-Generation Innovations & Synthesis Opportunities
docs.text:
1. Non-Linear Exponentiated RFF Feature Mapping: Restore non-linear positive feature kernel \(\phi(X) = \exp(\text{Norm}(X) W_{\text{rff}}) / \sqrt{F}\) in global heads to prevent linear projection degeneracy while retaining \(\mathcal{O}(N)\) scaling.
  2. FlashAttention-3 FP8 Integer Matrix Units: Implement local Softpick window attention using 8-bit quantization (E4M3), executing localized tile matrix products on NVIDIA Hopper FP8 Tensor Cores.
  3. Decoupled Local/Global Rotary Position Embeddings (RoPE): Apply 1D Rotary Position Embeddings exclusively to local heads \(H_l\) while keeping global RFF feature space position-invariant, preserving relative word order.
  4. State-Space Model Recurrent Recency Gating: Augment global RFF memory state accumulation with exponential time-decay factors \(KV_t = \gamma KV_{t-1} + K_{\text{feat}, t}^T \otimes V_t\), integrating linear state space modeling.

docs.title: AEGIS-Attention V6: Unified Hybrid Attention with SVD+LoRA Dual-Path Projections and Positive Orthogonal Random Feature (FAVOR+) Global Kernel Attention
1. Executive Abstract & Architectural Motivation
docs.text:
Standard Multi-Head Self-Attention (MHSA) in Transformer models imposes quadratic computational time complexity \(\mathcal{O}(N^2)\) and memory allocation scaling with respect to sequence length \(N\). While local sliding-window attention restricts computational overhead to \(\mathcal{O}(N \cdot W)\), it sacrifices long-range contextual modeling. Conversely, global linearized attention variants offer linear scaling \(\mathcal{O}(N \cdot m \cdot d_h)\) but suffer from spatial over-smoothing and numerical instability in kernel exponentiation.

AEGIS-Attention V6 establishes a unified hybrid attention framework combining four architectural advances: 1. SVD+LoRA Dual-Path Factorized Projections: Weight matrices (\(W_Q, W_K, W_V, W_O\)) integrate a frozen orthogonal singular value basis (\(U \text{diag}(S) V^T\)) derived from pre-trained weights with a trainable low-rank adaptation path (\(A B^T\)), enabling zero-shot initialization alongside high-capacity fine-tuning. 2. Tiled Local Sliding-Window Branch: Computes localized band-masked softmax attention using memory-efficient tile iteration across sequence blocks of size \(W\). 3. Positive Orthogonal Random Feature (FAVOR+) Global Kernel: Implements numerically stable FAVOR+ positive feature mappings \(\phi(x) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{m}} \exp\left( x \Pi - \frac{\|x\|^2}{2} \right)\) using QR-decomposed orthogonal projection matrices \(\Pi \in \mathbb{R}^{d_h \times m}\), protected by RMSNorm pre-normalization and logit clamping. 4. Context-Aware Dynamic Gating & Fusion: Integrates query importance gates \(g_Q\), input relevance gates \(g_{\text{in}}\), and a context-aware fusion gate \(\alpha\) that dynamically blends local and global attention representations per token and per head.

docs.title: 2.1 SVD+LoRA Dual-Path Projection (FactorisedLowRankProjection)
docs.text:
For input tensor \(X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times d_{\text{in}}}\), linear projections (\(Q, K, V, O\)) are evaluated through parallel SVD singular basis scaling and LoRA adaptation:

\[Y = X V \text{diag}(S) U^T + (X B^T) A^T\]

where: \(U \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{out}} \times r_{\text{svd}}}, V \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{in}} \times r_{\text{svd}}}\) are registered frozen orthogonal buffers obtained via SVD of pre-trained weight \(W_0\). Furthermore, \(S \in \mathbb{R}^{r_{\text{svd}}}\) is a learnable singular scaling vector initialized with singular values. Concurrently, \(A \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{out}} \times r_{\text{lora}}}, B \in \mathbb{R}^{r_{\text{lora}} \times d_{\text{in}}}\) are learnable low-rank adapter matrices.

Reshaping into \(H\) heads with head dimension \(d_h = D / H\) yields \(Q, K, V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times N \times d_h}\).

docs.title: 2.2 Tiled Local Sliding-Window Attention Branch
docs.text:
Sequence tokens are partitioned into tile blocks of size \(W = \text{window\_size}\). For tile block index \(i \in \{0, \dots, \lceil N / W \rceil - 1\}\), local attention evaluates:

\[\text{start} = i \cdot W, \quad \text{end} = \min(\text{start} + W, N)\] \[\text{k\_start} = \max(0, \text{start} - W), \quad \text{k\_end} = \min(N, \text{end} + W)\]

Query tile \(Q_{i} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times W \times d_h}\) attends to key-value tiles \(K_{i}, V_{i} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times 3W \times d_h}\):

\[S_{i}^{\text{local}} = \frac{Q_{i} K_{i}^T}{\sqrt{d_h}} + M^{\text{band}}_{i} + M^{\text{pad}}_{i}\] \[O_{i}^{\text{local}} = \text{Softmax}\left( S_{i}^{\text{local}} \right) V_{i} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times W \times d_h}\]

Out-of-tile outputs are assembled sequentially into full local context tensor \(O^{\text{local}} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times N \times d_h}\).

docs.title: 2.3 Positive Orthogonal Random Feature (FAVOR+) Global Kernel
docs.text:
Pre-normalization is optionally applied via RMSNorm:

\[\hat{Q} = \text{RMSNorm}(Q), \quad \hat{K} = \text{RMSNorm}(K)\]

The FAVOR+ positive kernel feature map \(\phi(x): \mathbb{R}^{d_h} \to \mathbb{R}^m\) is defined as:

\[\phi(x) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{m}} \exp\left( \text{clamp}\left( x \Pi - \frac{\|x\|_2^2}{2}, c_{\min}, c_{\max} \right) \right)\]

where \(\Pi \in \mathbb{R}^{d_h \times m}\) is constructed via QR decomposition of Gaussian matrices such that \(\Pi \Pi^T \approx I_{d_h} \cdot d_h\). Query and key feature representations are modulated by query gate \(g_Q = \sigma(W_Q Q)\) and input gate \(g_{\text{in}} = \sigma(W_{\text{in}} X)\):

\[\tilde{Q}_{\text{feat}} = \phi(\hat{Q}) \odot g_Q, \quad \tilde{K}_{\text{feat}} = \phi(\hat{K}) \odot g_{\text{in}}, \quad \tilde{V} = V \odot g_{\text{in}}\]

Global context accumulation evaluates linear outer products:

\[M^{\text{global}} = \sum_{j=1}^N \tilde{K}_{\text{feat}, j}^T \otimes \tilde{V}_j \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times m \times d_h}, \quad Z^{\text{global}} = \sum_{j=1}^N \tilde{K}_{\text{feat}, j}^T \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times m \times 1}\]

The global context output \(O^{\text{global}} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times N \times d_h}\) is retrieved via:

\[O^{\text{global}}_i = \frac{\tilde{Q}_{\text{feat}, i} M^{\text{global}}}{\tilde{Q}_{\text{feat}, i} Z^{\text{global}} + \epsilon}\]

docs.title: 2.4 Context-Aware Dynamic Fusion & Output Projection
docs.text:
The fusion gating network concatenates input activations, local outputs, and global outputs per head:

\[C_{b, h, i} = \left[ X_{b, i, h}, O^{\text{local}}_{b, h, i}, O^{\text{global}}_{b, h, i} \right] \in \mathbb{R}^{\left( \frac{D}{H} + 2 d_h \right)}\] \[\alpha_{b, h, i} = \sigma\left( C_{b, h, i} W_{\text{fusion}} + b_{\text{fusion}} \right) \in [0, 1]^{B \times H \times N \times 1}\] \[O^{\text{fused}} = (1 - \alpha) \odot O^{\text{local}} + \alpha \odot O^{\text{global}} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times N \times d_h}\]

Reshaping into \([B, N, H \cdot d_h]\), the fused tensor is transformed through the dual-path SVD+LoRA output projection:

\[Y = \text{FactorisedLowRankProjection}_{\text{out}}\left( \text{Reshape}(O^{\text{fused}}) \right) \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times D}\]

docs.text:

docs.title: 4.1 FLOPs Computation Breakdown
docs.text:
Let \(B\) be batch size, \(N\) sequence length, \(D\) model dimension, \(H\) head count, \(d_h = D/H\) head dimension, \(r_{\text{svd}}\) SVD rank, \(r_{\text{lora}}\) LoRA rank, \(W\) local window radius, and \(m\) FAVOR+ random feature dimension.

  1. SVD+LoRA Projections (\(Q, K, V, O\)): SVD path (\(X V \text{diag}(S) U^T\)): \(2 \times (2 B N D r_{\text{svd}}) = 4 B N D r_{\text{svd}}\) Furthermore, LoRA path (\((X B^T) A^T\)): \(4 B N D r_{\text{lora}}\) $\(\text{FLOPs}_{\text{proj}} = 4 \times \left( 4 B N D r_{\text{svd}} + 4 B N D r_{\text{lora}} \right) = 16 B N D (r_{\text{svd}} + r_{\text{lora}})\)$

  2. Tiled Local Sliding-Window Branch: Tiled query-key dot products (\(W\) keys per query): \(2 B H N W d_h = 2 B N D W\) Furthermore, Softmax & Value contraction: \(2 B H N W d_h = 2 B N D W\) $\(\text{FLOPs}_{\text{local}} = 4 B N D W\)$

  3. Global FAVOR+ Linear Branch: RMSNorm pre-norm: \(\mathcal{O}(B N D)\) Furthermore, FAVOR+ projection matrix product (\(X \Pi\)): \(2 B H N d_h m = 2 B N m d_h\) Concurrently, Memory matrix accumulation (\(M^{\text{global}}\)): \(2 B H N m d_h = 2 B N m d_h\) In this setting, Query context retrieval: \(2 B H N m d_h = 2 B N m d_h\) $\(\text{FLOPs}_{\text{global}} = 6 B N m d_h\)$

  4. Context Fusion Gating & Output Assembly: $\(\text{FLOPs}_{\text{fusion}} = 2 B N H (3 d_h) + 3 B N D = 9 B N D\)$

\[\text{FLOPs}_{\text{total}} \approx 16 B N D (r_{\text{svd}} + r_{\text{lora}}) + 4 B N D W + 6 B N m d_h + 9 B N D\]

docs.title: 4.2 MACs & Memory Footprint Analysis
docs.text:
Specifically, regarding \textbf{Multiply-Accumulate Operations (MACs)},

$\(\text{Total MACs} \approx 8 B N D (r_{\text{svd}} + r_{\text{lora}}) + 2 B N D W + 3 B N m d_h + 4.5 B N D\)$ Specifically, regarding \textbf{Parameter Footprint},

$\(\Theta = 4 r_{\text{svd}} + 8 D r_{\text{lora}} + d_h m + 3 D\)$ Specifically, regarding \textbf{Activation Footprint}, Furthermore, Local tiled outputs: \(\mathcal{O}(B H N d_h)\) Concurrently, FAVOR+ random feature tensor \(\phi(\hat{Q})\): \(\mathcal{O}(B H N m)\) In this setting, Global memory accumulator matrix \(M^{\text{global}}\): \(\mathcal{O}(B H m d_h)\) Additionally, Total Activation Memory: \(\mathcal{O}(B N D + B H N m + B H m d_h)\)

docs.title: 4.3 Asymptotic Scalability Comparison
docs.text: Specifically, regarding \textbf{Standard Dense Attention}, \(\mathcal{O}(N^2 D)\) compute, \(\mathcal{O}(N^2 H)\) memory. Furthermore, regarding \textbf{AEGIS-Attention V6}, \(\mathcal{O}\left(N (D (r_{\text{svd}} + r_{\text{lora}}) + W D + m d_h)\right)\) compute, \(\mathcal{O}(N D + H m d_h)\) memory footprint.

docs.title: 5. Failure Modes, Rank Collapse & Edge Cases
5.1 LoRA Adapter Singular Vector Interference
docs.text: At the architectural level, the underlying operational mechanism reveals that the projection matrix combines frozen SVD basis \(U \text{diag}(S) V^T\) with trainable LoRA adapter \(A B^T\). If LoRA update \(A B^T\) aligns with discarded singular vectors of \(W_0\), gradient dynamics can destabilize the singular value scaling vector \(S\), leading to divergence during early training.

docs.title: 5.2 FAVOR+ Exponential Overflow Under FP16
docs.text: At the architectural level, the underlying operational mechanism reveals that the FAVOR+ feature map computes \(\exp\left( x \Pi - \|x\|_2^2 / 2 \right)\). Without logit clamping, large entries in \(x \Pi\) exceed 88.7 in FP16, causing instant overflow to inf and driving softmax/normalization scalars to zero (NaN). To systematically mitigate this constraint, the framework enforces an optimization protocol such that strictly enforce logit clamping bounds \([c_{\min}, c_{\max}] = [-20.0, 20.0]\) and deploy RMSNorm pre-normalization prior to feature projection.

docs.title: 5.3 Local Tiled Window Mask Underflow
docs.text: At the architectural level, the underlying operational mechanism reveals that when processing short sequences or padded edge tiles, entire tile rows in _tiled_sliding_window_attention may be masked to \(-\infty\). Passing all-\(-\infty\) rows to PyTorch SDPA produces NaN outputs. To systematically mitigate this constraint, the framework enforces an optimization protocol such that guard edge tiles by replacing all-\(-\infty\) attention logit rows with 0.0 prior to value contraction.

docs.text:

|                        Triton Hardware Optimization Blueprint                     |

|  Input X [B, N, D] ---> [Fused SVD+LoRA Dual GEMM Kernel] ---> Q, K, V            |

|  - Block-Sparse Tile Loop (64x64)    - Fused RMSNorm + Clamped Exp FAVOR+  - Fused|
|  - FlashAttention Online Softmax     - Shared Memory Outer Product Grid     Convex|

|                                                                                   |
|      +-------------------------------------+-----------------------------------+  |

|      +---> Fused Fusion & Dual-Path Out GEMM Kernel ---> Output Y [B, N, D]       |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+

docs.title: 6.1 Triton Strategy 1: Fused Dual-Path SVD+LoRA GEMM Kernel
docs.text:
Standard PyTorch executes four independent GEMM calls per projection (x @ V, scaling by S, @ U.T, plus x @ B.T @ A.T), incurring significant DRAM memory bandwidth overhead.

Triton Optimization: Construct a single fused GEMM kernel loading \(X_i \in \mathbb{R}^{\text{BLOCK\_M} \times D}\) into SRAM. Furthermore, Evaluate SVD product \((X_i V) \text{diag}(S) U^T\) and LoRA product \((X_i B^T) A^T\) simultaneously in register files. Concurrently, regarding \textbf{Speedup}, reduces DRAM read/write traffic by \(3\times\), yielding up to \(2.2\times\) kernel latency improvement.

docs.title: 6.2 Triton Strategy 2: Block-Sparse Local Tiled SDPA Kernel
docs.text: Divide the sequence into block tiles of size BLOCK_M = 64 and BLOCK_N = 64. Furthermore, Enforce sliding window bounds \(|i \cdot 64 - j \cdot 64| < W\). Skip execution of out-of-band tile blocks entirely. Concurrently, Implement FlashAttention SRAM online softmax accumulation (m_i, l_i), eliminating DRAM allocation for local attention logits.

docs.title: 6.3 Triton Strategy 3: Fused FAVOR+ Global Memory Grid Engine
docs.text: Parallelize across batch \(B\) and heads \(H\). Furthermore, Load sequence tiles of size BLOCK_N = 128. Compute RMSNorm, projection \(x \Pi\), clamping, and exponential activation in shared memory. Concurrently, Accumulate key-value outer products into shared memory matrix \(M^{\text{global}} \in \mathbb{R}^{m \times d_h}\) in a single streaming pass, bypassing global memory writes for feature activations \(\phi(K)\).

docs.title: 7. Next-Generation Innovations & Synthesis Opportunities
docs.text:
1. State-Space Model (SSM) Recurrent FAVOR+ Decay: Integrate exponential temporal decay factors \(\lambda \in (0, 1)\) into FAVOR+ memory state accumulation \(M_t = \lambda M_{t-1} + \tilde{K}_{\text{feat}, t}^T \otimes \tilde{V}_t\), unifying linear kernel attention with Mamba selective scans.
  2. FlashAttention-3 FP8 Quantized Tiled Execution: Execute local tiled window attention using FP8 (E4M3) precision on NVIDIA Hopper GPUs, quadrupling localized matrix math throughput.
  3. Decoupled Local/Global Head Heterogeneity: Allocate \(75\%\) of attention heads exclusively to ultra-fast local FlashAttention (\(W = 128, m = 0\)) and \(25\%\) of heads exclusively to global FAVOR+ linear attention (\(W = 0, m = 128\)).
  4. Structured Low-Rank Tensor-Train (TT) Projections: Replace SVD dual-linear layers with 3-core Tensor Train matrix factorizations, compressing linear projection parameters down to rank \(r = 8\).

docs.title: ALiBi: Attention with Linear Biases for Length Extrapolation
docs.text: Family: Modern Positional, Rotary & Geometric Attention Variants · NeuralOps Registry ID: alibi

docs.title: Executive Abstract
docs.text:
ALiBi (Press et al., 2021) completely eliminates positional embeddings, instead adding a constant, static linear bias penalty proportional to the token distance \(|i - j|\) to each attention score. Allows models to extrapolate to sequence lengths far exceeding training limits.

In NeuralOps, alibi is integrated into the universal attention dispatch table, featuring full support for the 3-level fallback hierarchy, automatic shape validation, and end-to-end autograd backwards passes.

docs.title: Mathematical Formulation
docs.text:
The core operator computation is defined as:

\[ \text{Softmax}\left(\frac{Q K^T}{\sqrt{d}} - m \cdot |i - j|\right) V \quad \text{where} \; m = 2^{-\frac{8 h}{H}} \]

During execution, inputs \(Q, K, V\) are projected to dimension \(d\). In the causal configuration, lower-triangular masking ensures that tokens only attend to past and current time-steps, preserving autoregressive invariants.

     ├───► Linear Projection (Q, K, V)

     │         │
     │         ▼
     └────► Scaled Output & Residual Add (B, T, D)

docs.title: ASVD Attention: Activation-Aware Singular Value Decomposition Architecture
1. Executive Abstract & Architectural Motivation
docs.text:
Activation-aware Singular Value Decomposition Attention (ASVDAttention, Yuan et al., 2023) provides an activation-guided low-rank model compression framework for Multi-Head Attention. Standard SVD parameter reduction factorizes dense projection matrices \(W \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{out}} \times d_{\text{in}}}\) solely based on static weight magnitude matrices, ignoring the non-uniform variance and magnitude distributions of dynamic activation vectors (\(X\)).

ASVD reformulates factorized linear layers by incorporating explicit singular value scaling vectors \(S \in \mathbb{R}^r\) alongside orthogonal left and right singular bases (\(U \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{out}} \times r}, V \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times d_{\text{in}}}\)). By computing linear transformations as \(y = ((x V^\top) \odot S) U^\top + b\) (ASVDLinear), ASVD allows individual tuning of singular value scales during post-compression fine-tuning, preserving sensitivity to critical activation channels while reducing parameter footprints by over 80%.

docs.title: 2. Mathematical Formulations & Derivations
docs.text: Let \(X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times D}\) denote input activations. Let \(H\) be query heads, \(d_k = D / H\) head dimension, and \(r\) the rank per ASVD factorized layer.

docs.title: Factorised ASVD Linear Transformation (ASVDLinear):
docs.text:
For dense weight matrix \(W \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{out}} \times d_{\text{in}}}\) with bias \(b \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{out}}}\), truncated SVD factorizes \(W\):

\[ W \approx U \text{diag}(S) V \implies U \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{out}} \times r}, \, S \in \mathbb{R}^r, \, V \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times d_{\text{in}}} \]

Where \(U\) and \(V\) are semi-orthogonal matrices (\(U^\top U = I_r, V V^\top = I_r\)).

For input activation tensor \(X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times d_{\text{in}}}\):

  1. Down-Projection to Rank-r Bottleneck: [ Z_{\text{down}} = X V^\top \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times r} ]
  2. Explicit Singular Value Scaling: [ Z_{\text{scaled}} = Z_{\text{down}} \odot S \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times r} ]
  3. Up-Projection & Bias Aggregation: [ Y = Z_{\text{scaled}} U^\top + b \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times d_{\text{out}}} ]

docs.title: Multi-Head ASVD Scaled Attention:
docs.text:
ASVD factorized layers map hidden states to Query, Key, Value, and Output multi-head tensors:

[ Q = \text{ASVDLinear}_Q(X) \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times N \times d_k} ] [ K = \text{ASVDLinear}_K(X) \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times N \times d_k} ] [ V = \text{ASVDLinear}_V(X) \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times N \times d_k} ]

Affinity matrix evaluation and context output projection proceed as:

[ S_{b, h, i, j} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{d_k}} \sum_{m=1}^{d_k} Q_{b, h, i, m} \cdot K_{b, h, j, m} ] [ A_{b, h, i, j} = \text{Softmax}j (\text{apply_attention_mask}(S, M){b, h, i, j}) ] [ C_{b, h, i, m} = \sum_{j=1}^N \text{Dropout}(A){b, h, i, j} \cdot V{b, h, j, m} \implies C \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times D} ] [ Y = \text{ASVDLinear}_O(C) \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times D} ]

docs.title: Computational Workload (FLOPs & MACs)
docs.text:
Let \(B\) be batch size, \(N\) sequence length, \(D\) model dimension, \(H\) heads, \(d_k = D/H\), and \(r\) factor rank.

  1. ASVD Projection Layers: Down-projections (\(X V^\top\)): \(4 \times (2 B N D r) = 8 B N D r\) FLOPs. Furthermore, Singular scaling (\(\odot S\)): \(4 B N r\) FLOPs. Concurrently, Up-projections (\(Z U^\top\)): \(4 \times (2 B N r D) = 8 B N D r\) FLOPs. In this setting, Total Projection Workload: \(16 B N D r + 4 B N r\) FLOPs (\(8 B N D r\) MACs).

  2. Core Scaled Dot-Product Attention: \(Q K^\top\) & \(A V\): \(4 B N^2 D\) FLOPs. Furthermore, Softmax & Masking: \(7 B H N^2\) FLOPs.

  3. Total Workload Summary: Specifically, regarding \textbf{Total MACs}, \(8 B N D r + 2 B N^2 D\) Furthermore, regarding \textbf{Total FLOPs}, \(16 B N D r + 4 B N r + 4 B N^2 D + 7 B H N^2\)

docs.title: Parameter Footprint Comparison
docs.text:
Specifically, regarding \textbf{Dense Uncompressed MHA}, \(4 D^2 + 4 D\) floats. Furthermore, regarding \textbf{ASVD MHA Parameter Count},

[ \text{Params}_{\text{ASVD}} = 4 \cdot [D \cdot r + r + r \cdot D] + 4 D = 8 D r + 4 r + 4 D \text{ floats} ] For \(D = 4096, r = 32\): Dense MHA: \(4 \times 4096^2 \approx 67.1 \text{ million parameters}\). Furthermore, ASVD MHA: \(8 \times 4096 \times 32 + 128 + 16384 \approx 1.06 \text{ million parameters}\) (\(98.4\%\) parameter compression).

docs.title: 5. Architectural Bottlenecks, Rank Collapse & Edge Cases
Activation Outlier Shift Sensitivity
docs.text: If activation scales shift significantly during task fine-tuning, fixed singular values \(S\) derived from initial calibration can cause feature clipping. Allowing parameter vector \(S\) to be trainable during fine-tuning resolves activation mismatch.

docs.title: Subnormal Singular Value Scaling
docs.text: If \(S_k \to 0\) for channel \(k\), gradient flow into corresponding rows of \(V\) and columns of \(U\) drops to zero. Adding lower bound regularizers (\(S \ge 1e-4\)) prevents singular value collapse.

docs.title: 6. Hardware Acceleration Blueprint & Triton Kernel Design
docs.text:
A Triton kernel for ASVD Attention fuses down-projection (\(V\)), singular value Hadamard scaling (\(S\)), and up-projection (\(U\)) into a single SIMD thread loop.

                    Global Memory (HBM)
   ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
   │ Input: X [B, N, D]                                          │
   │ ASVD Factors: V [r, D], S [r], U [D, r], bias [D]            │
   └──────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────┘
                                  │ Vectorized Block Load
                                  ▼
 ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 │                     Triton SRAM Scratchpad                     │
 │ 1. Load Activation Tile X_i [BLOCK_M, D]                       │
 │ 2. Compute Down-Projection: Vx_i = X_i @ V.T [BLOCK_M, r]      │
 │ 3. Apply In-Register Scaling: SVx_i = Vx_i * S                 │
 │ 4. Reconstruct Output Tile: Out_i = SVx_i @ U.T + bias         │
 │ 5. Execute Online Scaled Attention                             │
 └────────────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────┘
                                  │ Write Context Output
                                  ▼
   ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
   │ Context Output: Y [B, N, D]                                 │
   └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

docs.title: 7. Next-Generation Innovations & Synthesis Opportunities
docs.text:
1. Activation-Aware Fisher Information Weighting: Weight initial singular value extraction \(S_i\) using diagonal Fisher Information metrics calculated over calibration datasets.
  2. ASVD + Grouped-Query Attention (ASVD-GQA): Combine ASVD factorized projections with Grouped-Query KV head sharing for maximum decoding throughput.
  3. Quantized ASVD (Q-ASVD): Quantize orthogonal bases \(U, V\) to INT4 precision while keeping scalar vector \(S\) in FP16, achieving up to \(32\times\) memory bandwidth compression.

docs.title: BAM-UMoE: Unified Mixture-of-Experts Attention Replacement Block
1. Executive Abstract & Architectural Motivation
docs.text:
Standard Multi-Head Self-Attention (MHSA) computes pairwise similarity matrices of size \(L \times L\), scaling quadratically with sequence length \(L\). In contexts where token-to-token cross-attention provides marginal utility relative to its computational expense, BAM-UMoE (Block-Attention Replacement via Unified Mixture-of-Experts) replaces quadratic attention mechanisms entirely. Instead of inter-token matrix multiplication, BAM-UMoE formulates Transformer layer transformations as a sequence of parameter-efficient, token-wise conditional routing computations over specialized expert sub-networks.

The core architecture consists of two stacked Unified Mixture-of-Experts (UMoE) blocks with top-\(k\) routing: a QKV-MoE that projects input representations into unified feature spaces, followed by an FFN-MoE that handles high-dimensional non-linear feature synthesis. By bypassing pairwise sequence attention, BAM-UMoE achieves linear complexity \(\mathcal{O}(L \cdot k \cdot D^2)\) with respect to sequence length, providing an asymptotic speedup and memory footprint reduction.

This model shifts the computational paradigm from sequence-level token interaction to token-level capacity scaling via sparse expert routing, enabling extreme inference throughput in compute-constrained environments.

docs.title: 2.1 Unified Mixture-of-Experts (UnifiedMoE) Routing
docs.text:
Given an input feature tensor \(\mathbf{X} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D}\), the routing gate computes expert logit activations \(\mathbf{R}\) across \(E\) candidate experts: $\(\mathbf{R} = \mathbf{X} \mathbf{W}_{\text{gate}} \quad \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times E}\)$ where \(\mathbf{W}_{\text{gate}} \in \mathbb{R}^{D \times E}\).

The top-\(k\) expert routing selection identifies the indices \(\mathcal{I}_{\text{top-}k}\) and logit values \(\mathbf{S}_{\text{top-}k}\) for each token: $\(\mathcal{I}_{\text{top-}k}, \mathbf{S}_{\text{top-}k} = \operatorname{TopK}\left(\mathbf{R}, k\right)\)$ where \(\mathcal{I}_{\text{top-}k} \in \{1, \dots, E\}^{B \times L \times k}\) and \(\mathbf{S}_{\text{top-}k} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times k}\).

Softmax normalization is applied over the top-\(k\) logits to compute gating probabilities \(\mathbf{P}\): $\(\mathbf{P}_{b, \ell, j} = \frac{\exp(\mathbf{S}_{\text{top-}k, b, \ell, j})}{\sum_{m=1}^k \exp(\mathbf{S}_{\text{top-}k, b, \ell, m})}, \quad j \in \{1, \dots, k\}\)$

docs.title: 2.2 Expert Sub-Network Computation
docs.text:
Each expert sub-network \(e \in \{1, \dots, E\}\) is parameterized as a two-layer Feed-Forward Network with GELU activation: $\(\operatorname{Expert}_e(\mathbf{X}) = \operatorname{GELU}\left(\mathbf{X} \mathbf{W}_{1, e} + \mathbf{b}_{1, e}\right) \mathbf{W}_{2, e} + \mathbf{b}_{2, e}\)$ where \(\mathbf{W}_{1, e} \in \mathbb{R}^{D \times (2 \cdot d_{\text{out}})}\) and \(\mathbf{W}_{2, e} \in \mathbb{R}^{(2 \cdot d_{\text{out}}) \times d_{\text{out}}}\).

The expert stack evaluates all \(E\) expert transformations in parallel: $\(\mathbf{E}_{\text{out}} = \operatorname{Stack}\left( \left[ \operatorname{Expert}_1(\mathbf{X}), \dots, \operatorname{Expert}_E(\mathbf{X}) \right], \text{dim}=2 \right) \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times E \times d_{\text{out}}}\)$

The selected expert outputs are gathered according to \(\mathcal{I}_{\text{top-}k}\) and aggregated via weighted summation: $\(\mathbf{Y}_{\text{topk}} = \operatorname{Gather}\left(\mathbf{E}_{\text{out}}, \mathcal{I}_{\text{top-}k}\right) \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times k \times d_{\text{out}}}\)$ $\(\mathbf{Y} = \sum_{j=1}^k \mathbf{P}_{:, :, j} \odot \mathbf{Y}_{\text{topk}, :, :, j, :} \quad \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{out}}}\)$

docs.title: 2.3 Layer Pipeline: QKV-MoE & FFN-MoE Integration
docs.text: The forward execution trace of the BAMUMoEBlock proceeds through a structured, multi-stage pipeline coupling specialized sparse mixture-of-experts projections with residual normalizations. Initially, the input activation tensor \(\mathbf{X}\) is processed by the QKV mixture-of-experts module: $\(\mathbf{QKV} = \operatorname{UnifiedMoE}_{\text{qkv}}(\mathbf{X}) \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times (3 \cdot D)}\)$ This unified projected tensor is subsequently partitioned across its trailing dimension into individual query, key, and value states: $\(\mathbf{Q}, \mathbf{K}, \mathbf{V} = \operatorname{Chunk}\left(\mathbf{QKV}, 3, \text{dim}=-1\right), \quad \mathbf{V} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D}\)$ The extracted value representations are then mapped through a linear projection layer \(\mathbf{W}_{\text{out}}\) and merged with the identity path via an initial pre-layer normalization residual connection: $\(\mathbf{H}_{\text{proj}} = \mathbf{V} \mathbf{W}_{\text{out}} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D}\)$ $\(\mathbf{H}_1 = \operatorname{LayerNorm}\left( \mathbf{X} + \operatorname{Dropout}(\mathbf{H}_{\text{proj}}) \right)\)$ Following this initial projection stage, intermediate representation \(\mathbf{H}_1\) is routed through the second feed-forward mixture-of-experts block, followed by secondary residual addition and normalization: $\(\mathbf{H}_{\text{ffn}} = \operatorname{UnifiedMoE}_{\text{ffn}}(\mathbf{H}_1) \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D}\)$ $\(\mathbf{H}_2 = \operatorname{LayerNorm}\left( \mathbf{H}_1 + \operatorname{Dropout}(\mathbf{H}_{\text{ffn}}) \right)\)$ Finally, where padding or sequence boundaries are enforced, the normalized representations are modulated via element-wise attention masking: $\(\mathbf{Y}_{\text{final}} = \mathbf{H}_2 \odot \mathbf{M}_{\text{attn}}\)$

docs.title: 4.1 FLOPs and Arithmetic Workload Breakdown
docs.text:
Let \(B\) represent the batch size, \(L\) the sequence length, \(D\) the hidden feature dimension, \(E\) the total expert pool size, and \(k\) the number of top active experts selected per token. The arithmetic complexity of the un-fused baseline implementation can be characterized systematically across its sequential operational phases.

The initial routing stage evaluates gating logits across all candidate experts via linear projection \(\mathbf{W}_{\text{gate, QKV}}\), incurring \(\operatorname{FLOPs}_{\text{qkv\_router}} = 2 B L D E\). During expert evaluation, each expert sub-network \(e\) applies an expansion projection \(D \to 6D\) requiring \(2 \cdot 6 D^2 = 12 D^2\) FLOPs followed by a contracting projection \(6D \to 3D\) requiring \(2 \cdot 6D \cdot 3D = 36 D^2\) FLOPs, culminating in \(48 D^2\) FLOPs per expert. Evaluating all \(E\) experts across \(B \times L\) tokens yields \(\operatorname{FLOPs}_{\text{qkv\_experts}} = 48 B L E D^2\). Gathering and weighting the top-\(k\) expert outputs introduces an additional \(\operatorname{FLOPs}_{\text{qkv\_sum}} = 2 B L k (3D) = 6 B L k D\), while the subsequent linear projection on the value component accounts for \(\operatorname{FLOPs}_{\text{out\_proj}} = 2 B L D^2\).

Concurrently, the feed-forward mixture-of-experts (FFN-MoE) pipeline mirrors this structure: router logit generation requires \(\operatorname{FLOPs}_{\text{ffn\_router}} = 2 B L D E\), while each FFN expert performs an expansion \(D \to 2D\) (\(4 D^2\) FLOPs) and contraction \(2D \to D\) (\(4 D^2\) FLOPs) for a cumulative \(8 D^2\) FLOPs per expert, totaling \(\operatorname{FLOPs}_{\text{ffn\_experts}} = 8 B L E D^2\) across the full expert bank. Finally, weighted gating summation in the FFN stage contributes \(\operatorname{FLOPs}_{\text{ffn\_sum}} = 2 B L k D\). Summing these individual components establishes the aggregate computational requirement: $\(\text{Total FLOPs} = 56 B L E D^2 + 2 B L D^2 + 4 B L D E + 8 B L k D\)$

docs.title: 4.2 MACs and Memory Footprint Analysis
docs.text: The net multiply-accumulate operations closely parallel the floating-point workload, scaling as \(\text{Total MACs} \approx 28 B L E D^2 + B L D^2 + 2 B L D E\). In terms of memory residency, peak transient activation consumption is dominated by the gating logit buffers (\(2 \times B \cdot L \cdot E \times 2 \text{ bytes}\)), the un-grouped QKV expert stack tensor (\(B \cdot L \cdot E \cdot 3D \times 2 \text{ bytes}\)), and the FFN expert stack tensor (\(B \cdot L \cdot E \cdot D \times 2 \text{ bytes}\)). Significantly, all intermediate activations scale strictly linearly with sequence length as \(\mathcal{O}(B L E D)\), avoiding the quadratic \(\mathcal{O}(B H L^2)\) storage constraints inherent to dense self-attention.

docs.title: 4.3 Asymptotic Scalability Comparison
docs.text: Whereas conventional Multi-Head Self-Attention requires \(\mathcal{O}(L^2 D)\) computational operations and \(\mathcal{O}(L^2 H)\) attention matrix memory, the BAM-UMoE formulation scales with linear asymptotic complexity \(\mathcal{O}(L E D^2)\) in compute and \(\mathcal{O}(L E D)\) in transient memory. By decoupling computational overhead from quadratic sequence interactions, the architecture facilitates sequence length scaling to arbitrary context horizons, shifting the computational bottleneck from sequence length \(L\) to model width \(D\) and expert capacity \(E\).

docs.title: 5. Failure Modes, Rank Collapse & Edge Cases
5.1 Memory Allocation Explosion in Naive Implementations
docs.text: In un-fused implementations relying on sequential list comprehensions and tensor stacking (e.g., experts_out = torch.stack([exp(x) for exp in self.experts], dim=2)), every input token evaluates the entire expert pool \(E\) prior to top-\(k\) gating. This implementation artifact induces an acute memory bottleneck, inflating dynamic activation allocations by an unnecessary factor of \(E / k\) (e.g., a \(4\times\) memory penalty when \(E=8, k=2\)) and executing redundant floating-point operations. Consequently, un-grouped evaluation eliminates the practical latency advantages of conditional computation unless fused with grouped scatter-gather kernel dispatch.

docs.title: 5.2 Complete Loss of Spatial Token Interaction and Semantic Binding
docs.text: Because BAM-UMoE operates strictly token-wise along the sequence axis, each token representation evolves in complete isolation without pairwise cross-token communication. Consequently, the effective receptive field of any individual token is strictly bounded to \(1\), eliminating the network's intrinsic capacity for associative context aggregation. Furthermore, in the absence of robust, deeply integrated positional encodings, the architecture exhibits permutation invariance across sequence tokens, precluding context-dependent syntactic binding, coreference resolution, and long-range semantic synthesis.

docs.title: 5.3 Routing Collapse, Expert Starvation, and Loss Surface Degeneracy
docs.text: In the absence of explicit auxiliary load-balancing constraints within the gating objective \(\operatorname{Softmax}\left(\operatorname{TopK}(\mathbf{X} \mathbf{W}_{\text{gate}})\right)\), the optimization trajectory is susceptible to severe routing collapse. Early during training, stochastic initialization biases cause a minor subset of experts to receive a disproportionate share of token assignments. As these favored experts receive frequent gradient updates, their gating parameters \(\mathbf{W}_{\text{gate}}\) grow in magnitude, creating a positive feedback loop that monopolizes token routing. Concurrently, under-utilized experts experience gradient starvation (\(\nabla_{\mathbf{W}_e} \mathcal{L} \to 0\)), effectively collapsing the active model capacity into a narrow sub-network and degrading the smoothness of the loss landscape.

docs.title: 6. Hardware Acceleration Blueprint & Triton Kernel Design
docs.text: To convert BAM-UMoE into true conditional computation, execution must avoid evaluating all \(E\) experts and eliminate intermediate stack buffers.

docs.title: 6.1 Triton Grouped GEMM & Scatter-Gather Blueprint
docs.text:
Instead of evaluating [B, L, D] across all \(E\) MLPs, tokens are dynamically binned into expert buckets using hardware scatter indices, enabling a single Fused Grouped GEMM.

+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                        TRITON FUSED UMOE ROUTED GEMM                              |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|  1. ROUTER & HISTOGRAM KERNEL                                                     |
|     - Compute Logits R = X @ W_gate [B*L, E].                                     |
|     - Extract Top-k indices and probabilities.                                    |
|     - Compute expert token counts (Histogram) & scatter offset map.               |
|                                                                                   |
|  2. TOKEN PERMUTATION / REORDERING KERNEL                                         |
|     - Permute input X into grouped contiguous buffer X_grouped [k*B*L, D]         |
|       according to assigned expert IDs.                                           |
|                                                                                   |
|  3. FUSED GROUPED GEMM KERNEL                                                     |
|     - Executes E GEMM problems concurrently using atomic work dispatch.           |
|     - For expert e: Y_grouped[e] = GELU(X_grouped[e] @ W1[e]) @ W2[e].            |
|                                                                                   |
|  4. UN-PERMUTE & WEIGHTED ACCUMULATION KERNEL                                     |
|     - Scatter-add weighted expert outputs Y_grouped * P back to Y_out [B, L, D].   |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+

docs.title: 6.2 Implementation Code Blueprint (Triton JIT Grouped Scatter Execution)
docs.text:
import triton
import triton.language as tl

@triton.jit
def _umoe_scatter_kernel(
    X_ptr,          # Input activations [Total_Tokens, D]
    Grouped_X_ptr,  # Re-ordered activations [Total_Tokens * k, D]
    TopK_Idx_ptr,   # Expert assignments [Total_Tokens, k]
    Offsets_ptr,    # Expert bucket offsets [E]
    stride_x_t, stride_x_d,
    stride_gx_t, stride_gx_d,
    stride_idx_t, stride_idx_k,
    D: tl.constexpr,
    K: tl.constexpr
):
    token_id = tl.program_id(axis=0)
    offs_d = tl.arange(0, D)

    # Load token representation
    x_ptrs = X_ptr + token_id * stride_x_t + offs_d * stride_x_d
    x_val = tl.load(x_ptrs)

    # Loop over top-k assignments for this token
    for k_idx in range(K):
        expert_id = tl.load(TopK_Idx_ptr + token_id * stride_idx_t + k_idx * stride_idx_k)

        # Atomic fetch and increment slot in target expert bucket
        slot_idx = tl.atomic_add(Offsets_ptr + expert_id, 1)

        # Write token into grouped contiguous memory
        gx_ptrs = Grouped_X_ptr + slot_idx * stride_gx_t + offs_d * stride_gx_d
        tl.store(gx_ptrs, x_val)

docs.title: 6.3 Hardware Memory Optimization Analysis
docs.text: The transition from naive PyTorch execution to the fused Triton grouped kernel delivers several critical architectural advantages. By dispatching computations strictly to active experts, arithmetic complexity is bounded by true conditional scaling \(\mathcal{O}(k \cdot B \cdot L \cdot D^2)\) rather than total expert capacity \(\mathcal{O}(E \cdot B \cdot L \cdot D^2)\). Furthermore, eliminating intermediate tensor stack buffers reduces peak transient memory residency from \(\mathcal{O}(B L E D)\) to \(\mathcal{O}(B L k D)\), preventing out-of-memory faults during long-context training. Finally, reordering token activations into contiguous memory tiles prior to execution maximizes Tensor Core occupancy via dense warp-level matrix multiplications (tl.dot), achieving near-peak arithmetic throughput across modern GPU streaming multiprocessors.

docs.title: 7. Next-Generation Innovations & Synthesis Opportunities
docs.text: To overcome the spatial aggregation limitations of pure token-wise mixture-of-experts architectures while retaining linear complexity, several promising synthesis directions emerge. Interleaving lightweight one-dimensional linear state-space models (such as Mamba-2 or RWKV-6) with BAM-UMoE blocks establishes an effective hybrid hierarchy, restoring cross-token context propagation across the sequence while strictly maintaining \(\mathcal{O}(L)\) compute scaling. Concurrently, incorporating auxiliary load-balancing losses and router cross-entropy constraints mitigates expert starvation, ensuring balanced capacity distribution across the expert ensemble. Furthermore, establishing a shared expert topology—wherein fixed static experts unconditionally process all tokens alongside dynamically routed top-\(k\) experts—ensures invariant general domain representation while allowing dynamic experts to capture specialized sub-domain patterns. Finally, quantizing expert linear projections to microscopic 8-bit formats (e.g., FP8 E4M3) enables hosting extensive expert ensembles (64+ experts) directly within on-chip SRAM and high-bandwidth memory, eliminating dynamic DRAM swapping penalties during large-scale inference.
