docs.title: Block Transformer HIBA: Hierarchical Intra-Block and Inter-Block Attention with Periodic Dense Rectification
1. Executive Abstract & Architectural Motivation
docs.text:
Dense Multi-Head Self-Attention (MHSA) computes pairwise interaction matrices of size \(L \times L\), scaling quadratically \(\mathcal{O}(L^2 d)\) in time and memory. Purely localized block-sparse attention models isolate token attention within non-overlapping contiguous windows of size \(B_{\text{size}}\), reducing compute to \(\mathcal{O}(L \cdot B_{\text{size}} \cdot d)\). However, local block isolation prevents information propagation across distant sequence segments, causing attention fragmentation and loss of global context.

Block Transformer HIBA (Hierarchical Intra-Block and Inter-Block Attention) addresses this trade-off through a tri-part architectural design: 1. Intra-Block Dense Attention: Evaluates exact causal self-attention within local sequence blocks of size \(B_{\text{size}}\), capturing high-frequency local syntax. 2. Inter-Block Top-\(k\) Sparse Attention: Dynamically routes queries in block \(b\) to non-local keys \(K_{\neg b}\) across all remaining sequence blocks, retaining only the top-\(k_{\text{inter}}\) cross-block connections. 3. Periodic Global Dense Rectification: Every \(T_{\text{rect}}\) layers, the model executes a full, un-constrained global dense attention pass over all \(L \times L\) token pairs, repairing accumulated representation fragmentation.

This hierarchical approach achieves \(\mathcal{O}\left(L \cdot (B_{\text{size}} + k_{\text{inter}}) \cdot d\right)\) sub-quadratic complexity on sparse layers, maintaining strict global coherence via periodic dense rectification.

docs.title: 2.1 Multi-Head Projection and Spatial Partitioning
docs.text:
Given input sequence activations \(\mathbf{X} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D}\), Query (\(\mathbf{Q}\)), Key (\(\mathbf{K}\)), and Value (\(\mathbf{V}\)) projections are defined as: $\(\mathbf{Q} = \mathbf{X} \mathbf{W}_q, \quad \mathbf{K} = \mathbf{X} \mathbf{W}_k, \quad \mathbf{V} = \mathbf{X} \mathbf{W}_v \quad \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times L \times d_h}\)$ where \(H\) is the number of heads and \(d_h = D / H\).

The sequence is partitioned into \(M = \lceil L / B_{\text{size}} \rceil\) contiguous blocks. For block \(b \in \{0, \dots, M-1\}\), token index range \(\mathcal{I}_b = [b \cdot B_{\text{size}}, \min((b+1) \cdot B_{\text{size}}, L))\) defines local block slices \(\mathbf{Q}_b, \mathbf{K}_b, \mathbf{V}_b \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times L_b \times d_h}\), where \(L_b = |\mathcal{I}_b| \le B_{\text{size}}\).

docs.title: 2.2 Stage 1: Local Intra-Block Causal Attention
docs.text:
Within block \(b\), exact causal dot-product attention computes local context: $\(\mathbf{S}_{b, \text{intra}} = \frac{\mathbf{Q}_b \mathbf{K}_b^\top}{\sqrt{d_h}} \quad \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times L_b \times L_b}\)$

A lower-triangular causal mask \(\mathbf{M}_{\text{causal}} \in \{0, -\infty\}^{L_b \times L_b}\) is applied: $\(\mathbf{M}_{\text{causal}, i, j} = \begin{cases} 0 & \text{if } i \ge j \\ -\infty & \text{if } i < j \end{cases}\)$ $\(\mathbf{A}_{b, \text{intra}} = \operatorname{Softmax}\left( \mathbf{S}_{b, \text{intra}} + \mathbf{M}_{\text{causal}} \right) \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times L_b \times L_b}\)$ $\(\mathbf{O}_{b, \text{intra}} = \mathbf{A}_{b, \text{intra}} \mathbf{V}_b \quad \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times L_b \times d_h}\)$

docs.title: 2.3 Stage 2: Inter-Block Top-\(k\) Sparse Attention
docs.text:
For query block \(b\), non-local key and value tokens belonging to all remaining blocks \(j eq b\) are concatenated into global neighbor matrices: $\(\mathbf{K}_{ eg b} = \operatorname{Concat}_{j eq b} \left( \mathbf{K}_j ight) \quad \in \mathbb{R}^{B imes H imes (L - L_b) imes d_h}\)$ $\(\mathbf{V}_{ eg b} = \operatorname{Concat}_{j eq b} \left( \mathbf{V}_j ight) \quad \in \mathbb{R}^{B imes H imes (L - L_b) imes d_h}\)$

The inter-block affinity score matrix \(\mathbf{S}_{b, ext{inter}} \in \mathbb{R}^{B imes H imes L_b imes (L - L_b)}\) is evaluated as: $\(\mathbf{S}_{b, ext{inter}} = rac{\mathbf{Q}_b \mathbf{K}_{ eg b}^ op}{\sqrt{d_h}}\)$

For each query token \(i \in \{1, \dots, L_b\}\), a discrete top-\(k\) routing step extracts the indices of the \(k_{ ext{inter}} = \min(k_{ ext{inter}}, L - L_b)\) most salient non-local keys: $\(\mathcal{T}_{b, i} = \operatorname{TopK}\left( \mathbf{S}_{b, ext{inter}, :, :, i, :}, k_{ ext{inter}} ight)\)$

Non-top-\(k\) scores are masked out with \(-\infty\): $\( ilde{\mathbf{S}}_{b, ext{inter}, :, :, i, j} = egin{cases} \mathbf{S}_{b, ext{inter}, :, :, i, j} & ext{if } j \in \mathcal{T}_{b, i} \ -\infty & ext{otherwise} \end{cases}\)$ $\(\mathbf{A}_{b, ext{inter}} = \operatorname{Softmax}\left( ilde{\mathbf{S}}_{b, ext{inter}} ight) \in \mathbb{R}^{B imes H imes L_b imes (L - L_b)}\)$ $\(\mathbf{O}_{b, ext{inter}} = \mathbf{A}_{b, ext{inter}} \mathbf{V}_{ eg b} \quad \in \mathbb{R}^{B imes H imes L_b imes d_h}\)$

The composite sparse output for block \(b\) sums local and non-local contexts: $\(\mathbf{O}_b = \mathbf{O}_{b, ext{intra}} + \mathbf{O}_{b, ext{inter}} \quad \in \mathbb{R}^{B imes H imes L_b imes d_h}\)$

The individual block outputs \(\mathbf{O}_b\) are concatenated along the sequence axis: $\(\mathbf{O}_{ ext{sparse}} = \operatorname{Concat}_{b=0}^{M-1} \left( \mathbf{O}_b ight) \quad \in \mathbb{R}^{B imes H imes L imes d_h}\)$

docs.title: 2.4 Stage 3: Periodic Global Dense Rectification
docs.text: Let \(\ell = \text{layer\_idx}\) denote the layer depth counter. If \(\ell \equiv 0 \pmod{T_{\text{rect}}}\) (where \(T_{\text{rect}} = \text{rectification\_interval}\)), the block-sparse steps are bypassed in favor of a full dense attention pass: $\(\mathbf{S}_{\text{dense}} = \frac{\mathbf{Q} \mathbf{K}^\top}{\sqrt{d_h}} + \mathbf{M}_{\text{attn}} \quad \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times L \times L}\)$ $\(\mathbf{O}_{\text{rectified}} = \operatorname{Softmax}\left( \mathbf{S}_{\text{dense}} \right) \mathbf{V} \quad \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times L \times d_h}\)$

docs.title: 2.5 Final Output Projection
docs.text: The selected context \(\mathbf{O} \in \{\mathbf{O}_{\text{sparse}}, \mathbf{O}_{\text{rectified}}\}\) is reshaped to \(\mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D}\) and projected: $\(\mathbf{Y} = \operatorname{Reshape}(\mathbf{O}) \mathbf{W}_O \quad \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D}\)$

docs.title: 4.1 FLOPs Computation Breakdown
docs.text:
Let \(B\) be batch size, \(L\) sequence length, \(D\) hidden dimension, \(H\) heads, \(d_h = D/H\), \(B_{\text{size}}\) block size, \(M = L / B_{\text{size}}\), \(k_{\text{inter}}\) top-\(k\) inter-block tokens, and \(T_{\text{rect}}\) rectification interval.

  1. Linear Projections (\(\mathbf{Q}, \mathbf{K}, \mathbf{V}\)): $\(\operatorname{FLOPs}_{\text{proj}} = 3 \times 2 B L D^2 = 6 B L D^2\)$

  2. Sparse HIBA Layers (Fraction \(\frac{T_{\text{rect}} - 1}{T_{\text{rect}}}\) of layers): Specifically, regarding \textbf{Intra-Block Causal Attention}, across \(M\) blocks: \(M \times (4 B H B_{\text{size}}^2 d_h) = 4 B H L B_{\text{size}} d_h = 4 B D L B_{\text{size}}\) FLOPs. Furthermore, regarding \textbf{Inter-Block Top-\(k\) Attention}, across \(M\) blocks: \(M \times (2 B H B_{\text{size}} (L - B_{\text{size}}) d_h) = 2 B D L (L - B_{\text{size}})\) FLOPs for raw scoring, plus \(2 B D L k_{\text{inter}}\) FLOPs for top-\(k\) value multiplication. $\(\operatorname{FLOPs}_{\text{sparse\_layer}} = 4 B D L B_{\text{size}} + 2 B D L^2 + 2 B D L k_{\text{inter}}\)$

  3. Dense Rectification Layers (Fraction \(\frac{1}{T_{\text{rect}}}\) of layers): $\(\operatorname{FLOPs}_{\text{dense\_layer}} = 4 B H L^2 d_h = 4 B D L^2\)$

  4. Output Projection (\(\mathbf{W}_O\)): $\(\operatorname{FLOPs}_{\text{out}} = 2 B L D^2\)$
\[\text{Average Per-Layer FLOPs} = 8 B L D^2 + 4 B D L B_{\text{size}} + 2 B D L k_{\text{inter}} + \left(2 + \frac{2}{T_{\text{rect}}}\right) B D L^2\]

docs.title: 4.2 MACs & Memory Footprint Analysis
docs.text:
Specifically, regarding \textbf{Multiply-Accumulate Operations (MACs)},

$\(\text{Average MACs} \approx 4 B L D^2 + 2 B D L B_{\text{size}} + B D L k_{\text{inter}} + \left(1 + \frac{1}{T_{\text{rect}}}\right) B D L^2\)$ Specifically, regarding \textbf{Peak Activation Memory}, Furthermore, Sparse Layer Attention Score Tensors: \(M \times B \cdot H \cdot B_{\text{size}} \cdot (L - B_{\text{size}}) \times 2 \text{ bytes}\) Concurrently, Dense Rectification Layer Score Tensor: \(B \cdot H \cdot L \cdot L \times 2 \text{ bytes}\) In this setting, Peak Memory: Bounded by global dense rectification layer \(\mathcal{O}(B H L^2)\).

docs.title: 4.3 Asymptotic Scalability Comparison
docs.text: Specifically, regarding \textbf{Standard Dense Attention}, \(\mathcal{O}(L^2 D)\) compute, \(\mathcal{O}(L^2 H)\) memory. Furthermore, regarding \textbf{HIBA Sparse Layers}, \(\mathcal{O}\left(L D (D + B_{\text{size}} + k_{\text{inter}} + L)\right)\) compute. Concurrently, Note: Because _inter_block_sparse computes raw scores \(\mathbf{Q}_b \mathbf{K}_{\neg b}^\top\) over all \((L - B_{\text{size}})\) non-local keys before extracting top-\(k\), the scoring step still scales quadratically with \(L\), but with a reduced top-\(k\) value matmul stage.

docs.title: 5. Failure Modes, Rank Collapse & Edge Cases
5.1 The Inter-Block Score Matrix Memory Leak
docs.text:
In _inter_block_sparse: 

scores = torch.matmul(q_b, k_neighbors.transpose(-2, -1)) * scale # [B, H, L_b, L - L_b]
top_k = min(self.top_k_inter, k_neighbors.size(2))
_, topk_idx = torch.topk(scores, top_k, dim=-1)
mask = torch.zeros_like(scores).scatter_(-1, topk_idx, 1.0)
scores = scores.masked_fill(mask == 0, float("-inf"))
Specifically, regarding \textbf{Quadratic Scoring Memory}, the kernel computes an explicit score tensor of size [B, H, L_b, L - L_b] and instantiates a dense zero mask mask = torch.zeros_like(scores). Furthermore, regarding \textbf{VRAM Spikes}, creating a dense floating-point mask of shape [B, H, L_b, L - L_b] per block allocates as much VRAM as full attention (\(\mathcal{O}(L^2)\)), negating memory savings during sparse layers.

docs.title: 5.2 Layer Counter Instance Desynchronization
docs.text:
In BlockTransformerHIBA.forward: 

use_rectify = self.layer_idx % self.rectification_interval == 0
self.layer_idx += 1
Specifically, regarding \textbf{Independent State Trap}, self.layer_idx is stored as an instance attribute within each individual layer module (self.layer_idx = 0). Furthermore, regarding \textbf{Schedule Failure}, every layer module maintains its own isolated counter (0, 1, 2...). Consequently, every layer in the model executes dense rectification on its very first forward call because 0 % T_rect == 0. Subsequent calls increment each layer independently, breaking synchronized global rectification schedules across Transformer depth.

docs.title: 5.3 Non-Causal Inter-Block Leakage in Autoregressive Tasks
docs.text:
In _inter_block_sparse: 

if (block_idx + 1) * self.block_size < total_len:
    k_select.append(k_all[:, :, end_b:, :]) # FEEDS FUTURE KEYS!
Specifically, regarding \textbf{Future Token Leakage}, the inter-block attention routine appends keys from future blocks (end_b:). Furthermore, regarding \textbf{Causality Violation}, if deployed in autoregressive decoder models (e.g., GPT), query block \(b\) attends to future keys \(k > b\), leaking future token information and invalidating generative inference.

docs.title: 6. Hardware Acceleration Blueprint & Triton Kernel Design
docs.text: To make HIBA truly sub-quadratic and eliminate quadratic VRAM allocations, inter-block top-\(k\) scoring must use coarse block centroids instead of per-token dense comparisons.

docs.title: 6.1 Triton Hardware Acceleration Pipeline Layout
docs.text:
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                        TRITON FUSED HIBA PIPELINE                                 |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|  1. COARSE INTER-BLOCK CENTROID ROUTING KERNEL                                    |
|     - Computes block centroids Q_mean, K_mean [M, d_h].                          |
|     - Evaluates coarse inter-block score matrix S_block [M, M].                   |
|     - Extracts top-k block indices TopK_blocks [M, k_blk].                        |
|                                                                                   |
|  2. FUSED INTRA-BLOCK FLASHATTENTION KERNEL                                       |
|     - Computes exact causal FlashAttention strictly within [B_size, B_size] tile. |
|     - Writes local context O_intra [B, L, D] without global matrix allocation.    |
|                                                                                   |
|  3. FUSED INTER-BLOCK ROUTED FLASHATTENTION KERNEL                                |
|     - Loads Q_b [B_size, d_h].                                                    |
|     - Indirect loads ONLY the selected k_blk key/value blocks into SRAM.          |
|     - Evaluates online softmax context O_inter over selected candidate blocks.    |
|     - Combines O_final = O_intra + O_inter in SRAM registers.                    |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+

docs.title: 6.2 Implementation Code Blueprint (Triton Fused Inter-Block Kernel)
docs.text:
import triton
import triton.language as tl

@triton.jit
def _hiba_fused_sparse_inter_kernel(
    Q_ptr, K_ptr, V_ptr, TopK_Block_Idx_ptr, Out_ptr,
    stride_qb, stride_qh, stride_qn, stride_qd,
    stride_kb, stride_kh, stride_kn, stride_kd,
    stride_vb, stride_vh, stride_vn, stride_vd,
    stride_ob, stride_oh, stride_on, stride_od,
    stride_idx_b, stride_idx_h, stride_idx_m, stride_idx_k,
    scale,
    B_SIZE: tl.constexpr,
    D_K: tl.constexpr,
    K_BLOCKS: tl.constexpr
):
    block_id = tl.program_id(axis=0)
    head_id = tl.program_id(axis=1)
    batch_id = tl.program_id(axis=2)

    # Calculate token index range for current block
    start_q = block_id * B_SIZE
    offs_m = start_q + tl.arange(0, B_SIZE)
    offs_d = tl.arange(0, D_K)

    # Load Query block tile [B_SIZE, D_K] into SRAM
    q_ptrs = Q_ptr + batch_id * stride_qb + head_id * stride_qh + (offs_m[:, None] * stride_qn + offs_d[None, :])
    q = tl.load(q_ptrs)

    # Online Softmax Accumulators
    m_i = tl.full([B_SIZE], float("-inf"), dtype=tl.float32)
    l_i = tl.zeros([B_SIZE], dtype=tl.float32)
    acc = tl.zeros([B_SIZE, D_K], dtype=tl.float32)

    idx_base = TopK_Block_Idx_ptr + batch_id * stride_idx_b + head_id * stride_qh + block_id * stride_idx_m

    # Loop ONLY over routed top-k inter-block indices
    for k_idx in range(K_BLOCKS):
        target_block = tl.load(idx_base + k_idx * stride_idx_k)
        start_k = target_block * B_SIZE
        offs_n = start_k + tl.arange(0, B_SIZE)

        # Indirect load selected Key block tile [B_SIZE, D_K]
        k_ptrs = K_ptr + batch_id * stride_kb + head_id * stride_kh + (offs_n[None, :] * stride_kn + offs_d[:, None] * stride_kd)
        k = tl.load(k_ptrs)

        # Matmul S = Q @ K.T -> [B_SIZE, B_SIZE]
        s = tl.dot(q, k) * scale

        # Online Softmax update
        m_ij = tl.max(s, axis=1)
        m_new = tl.maximum(m_i, m_ij)
        p = tl.exp(s - m_new[:, None])
        l_new = tl.exp(m_i - m_new) * l_i + tl.sum(p, axis=1)

        acc_scale = tl.exp(m_i - m_new)
        acc = acc * acc_scale[:, None]

        # Indirect load selected Value block tile [B_SIZE, D_K]
        v_ptrs = V_ptr + batch_id * stride_vb + head_id * stride_vh + (offs_n[:, None] * stride_vn + offs_d[None, :] * stride_vd)
        v = tl.load(v_ptrs)
        acc = tl.dot(p.to(v.dtype), v, acc)

        l_i = l_new
        m_i = m_new

    # Store normalized inter-block context
    acc = acc / l_i[:, None]
    out_ptrs = Out_ptr + batch_id * stride_ob + head_id * stride_oh + (offs_m[:, None] * stride_on + offs_d[None, :] * stride_od)
    tl.store(out_ptrs, acc.to(Out_ptr.dtype.element_ty))

docs.title: 6.3 Hardware Optimization Impact
docs.text:
1. Elimination of Dense Inter-Block Masks: Centroid block routing eliminates the allocation of \([L_b, L - L_b]\) dense score matrices and masks, dropping memory usage to \(\mathcal{O}(L \cdot B_{\text{size}})\).
  2. Synchronized Global Rectification: Explicit layer depth passing (layer_idx) ensures dense rectification passes occur concurrently across all layers at exact intervals \(T_{\text{rect}}\).

docs.title: 7. Next-Generation Innovations & Synthesis Opportunities
docs.text:
1. Adaptive Rectification Thresholding: Replace fixed layer intervals \(T_{\text{rect}}\) with dynamic entropy monitoring: trigger global dense rectification only when intra-block attention perplexity drops below critical bounds.
  2. Strict Causal Inter-Block Masking: Restrict inter-block key selection \(K_{\neg b}\) strictly to prior blocks \(j < b\) to support causal decoder LLM inference without lookahead leakage.
  3. Hierarchical Block Centroid Tree Top-\(k\): Abstract blocks into binary spatial trees (\(B_1 \subset B_2\)) to perform logarithmic \(\mathcal{O}(\log M)\) inter-block key selection.
  4. FP8 Block-Sparse Rectification: Execute dense rectification layers using FP8 (E4M3) Tensor Cores to reduce memory footprint by \(4\times\) during global context recovery.

docs.title: CHELA-SLAY: Spherical Linearized Attention with Yat-Kernel Fourier Features
1. Executive Abstract & Architectural Motivation
docs.text:
Standard Multi-Head Attention requires materializing an \(L \times L\) Softmax matrix, scaling quadratically \(\mathcal{O}(L^2)\) in time and memory. CHELA-SLAY (Spherical Linearized Attention with Yat-Kernel) reformulates query-key contextualization by combining unit-hypersphere projection with trigonometric random Fourier features (Yat-Kernel).

By normalizing Queries and Keys onto the unit sphere \(\mathbb{S}^{d-1}\) (\(\widehat{Q} = Q / \|Q\|_2, \widehat{K} = K / \|K\|_2\)), CHELA-SLAY eliminates vector magnitude distortions. It then applies a positive trigonometric random feature mapping \(\phi(x) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{m}} [\cos(W x), \sin(W x)]^\top > 0\), enabling linear associative matrix multiplication \(\phi(\widehat{Q}) (\phi(\widehat{K})^\top V)\). This reduces time and memory complexity to \(\mathcal{O}(L \cdot m \cdot d)\), guaranteeing stable linear scaling with respect to sequence length \(L\).

docs.title: 2. Mathematical Formulations & Derivations
docs.text:
Given input sequence representations \(X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D}\), query, key, and value states are projected as:

\[ Q = X W_Q \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D}, \quad K = X W_K \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D}, \quad V = X W_V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D} \]

Multi-head formatting yields \(Q, K, V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times L \times d}\) with \(d = D / H\).

docs.title: 1. Spherical Unit Normalization:
docs.text:
Query and key vectors are projected onto the unit hypersphere \(\mathbb{S}^{d-1}\):

\[ \widehat{Q} = \frac{Q}{\|Q\|_2 + \epsilon} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times L \times d}, \quad \widehat{K} = \frac{K}{\|K\|_2 + \epsilon} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times L \times d} \]

docs.title: 2. Trigonometric Yat-Kernel Random Fourier Mapping (\(\phi\)):
docs.text:
Given a non-trainable random Gaussian projection matrix \(W \in \mathbb{R}^{m \times d}\) with \(W_{i, j} \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma^2)\), the Yat-Kernel feature map \(\phi(x) \in \mathbb{R}^{2m}\) is defined as:

\[ \phi(x) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{m}} \left[ \cos(W x); \; \sin(W x) \right] \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times L \times 2m} \]

Applying \(\phi\) to spherical queries and keys yields feature matrices \(\phi(\widehat{Q}), \phi(\widehat{K}) \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times L \times 2m}\).

docs.title: 3. Associative Linear Attention Recurrence:
docs.text:
Using matrix associativity, the unnormalized context is evaluated via matrix multiplication:

[ KV = \phi(\widehat{K})^\top V = \sum_{t=1}^L \phi(\widehat{K}t) \otimes V_t \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times 2m \times d} ] [ K{\text{sum}} = \sum_{t=1}^L \phi(\widehat{K}_t) \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times 1 \times 2m} ]

The normalized context \(O \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times L \times d}\) is evaluated per sequence position:

\[ O = \frac{\phi(\widehat{Q}) KV}{\phi(\widehat{Q}) K_{\text{sum}}^\top + \epsilon} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times L \times d} \]

Final projection yields \(Y = \text{Concat}(O_1, \dots, O_H) W_O \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D}\).

docs.title: 3. Step-by-Step Tensor Execution Trace
docs.text:
Input: hidden_states [B, L, D]
  │
  ├──> Q, K, V Projections ──> [B, H, L, d]
  │
  ├──> Spherical Normalization:
  │      ├──> Q_hat = Q / ||Q||_2 ──> [B, H, L, d]
  │      └──> K_hat = K / ||K||_2 ──> [B, H, L, d]
  │
  ├──> Yat-Kernel Fourier Mapping:
  │      ├──> cos_feat = cos(Q_hat @ W.T) / sqrt(m) ──> [B, H, L, m]
  │      ├──> sin_feat = sin(Q_hat @ W.T) / sqrt(m) ──> [B, H, L, m]
  │      └──> phi(Q_hat) = Concat([cos_feat, sin_feat], dim=-1) ──> [B, H, L, 2m]
  │
  ├──> Associative Memory KV: phi(K_hat).T @ V ──────────> [B, H, 2m, d]
  ├──> Key Sum Vector K_sum: phi(K_hat).sum(dim=-2) ─────> [B, H, 1, 2m]
  │
  ├──> Numerator: phi(Q_hat) @ KV ─────────────────────────> [B, H, L, d]
  ├──> Denominator: phi(Q_hat) @ K_sum.T ──────────────────> [B, H, L, 1]
  ├──> Output Context: Numerator / Denominator ─────────> [B, H, L, d]
  │
  └──> transpose(1, 2) ──> contiguous() ──> [B, L, D]
  └──> Linear(D, D)(Context) ──> Output: [B, L, D]

docs.text: Step Operation Tensor Shape Description 1 Input \([B, L, D]\) Input sequence representation 2 Linear Projections \([B, H, L, d]\) Multi-head \(Q, K, V\) states 3 L2 Spherical Normalization \([B, H, L, d]\) Unit-sphere projection \(\widehat{Q}, \widehat{K}\) 4 Trigonometric Yat Mapping \([B, H, L, 2m]\) Trigonometric Fourier features \([\cos(W x); \sin(W x)]\) 5 Associative Matrix Product (\(KV\)) \([B, H, 2m, d]\) Outer-product aggregation over sequence length \(L\) 6 Key Sum Partition Function \([B, H, 1, 2m]\) Summed key feature normalization vector 7 Query Context Numerator \([B, H, L, d]\) Query projection against accumulated \(KV\) state 8 Output Projection \([B, L, D]\) Projection \(W_O\) to model dimension \(D\)

docs.title: FLOP and MAC Breakdown (\(B\): Batch, \(L\): Length, \(D\): Dim, \(H\): Heads, \(m\): Fourier Features):
docs.text:
Specifically, regarding \textbf{Input Projections (\(W_Q, W_K, W_V\))}, \(6 B L D^2\) FLOPs Furthermore, regarding \textbf{L2 Spherical Normalization}, \(6 B H L d = 6 B L D\) FLOPs Concurrently, regarding \textbf{Trigonometric Random Projections (\(W \widehat{Q}, W \widehat{K}\))}, \(2 \times (2 B H L d m) = 4 B L m D\) FLOPs In this setting, regarding \textbf{Sine / Cosine Evaluators}, \(4 B H L m\) FLOPs Additionally, regarding \textbf{Associative State Matrix (\(KV = \phi(\widehat{K})^\top V\))}, \(2 B H (2m) L d = 4 B L m D\) FLOPs Moreover, regarding \textbf{Context Numerator (\(\phi(\widehat{Q}) KV\))}, \(2 B H L (2m) d = 4 B L m D\) FLOPs From an analytical standpoint, regarding \textbf{Output Projection (\(W_O\))}, \(2 B L D^2\) FLOPs

Total Complexity: Specifically, regarding \textbf{Total MACs}, \(4 B L D^2 + 6 B L m D\) Furthermore, regarding \textbf{Total FLOPs}, \(8 B L D^2 + 12 B L m D\) (\(\mathcal{O}(L)\) linear complexity)

docs.title: Memory Footprint:
docs.text: Specifically, regarding \textbf{Static Weights}, \(4 D^2\) model parameters \(+ m \cdot d\) random weight matrix \(W\). Furthermore, regarding \textbf{Transient Activation Memory}, bounded by \(\mathcal{O}(B \cdot H \cdot m \cdot d + B \cdot H \cdot L \cdot m)\).

docs.title: 5. Failure Modes, Rank Collapse & Edge Cases
docs.text:
1. Trigonometric Cancellation in FP16: Under FP16 execution, small angular differences \(\Delta \theta = W (q - k)\) can cause catastrophic cancellation in \(\cos(\cdot)\) and \(\sin(\cdot)\), leading to zero inner products.
  2. Frequency Hyperparameter Sensitivity: The standard deviation \(\sigma\) of Gaussian matrix \(W\) acts as a bandwidth hyperparameter. If \(\sigma\) is miscalibrated, feature maps become either over-concentrated or uniform.
  3. Causal Scan Underflow: In causal decoding, small feature values in \(\phi(\widehat{K})\) can accumulate underflow errors across long sequence horizons (\(L > 32768\)).

docs.title: 6. Hardware Acceleration Blueprint & Triton Kernel Design
docs.text:
A Triton kernel for CHELA-SLAY fuses L2 normalization, trigonometric projection, and linear matrix state accumulation directly into SRAM.

# Triton Fused CHELA-SLAY Linear Attention Blueprint
import triton
import triton.language as tl

@triton.jit
def _chela_slay_fused_kernel(
    Q_ptr, K_ptr, V_ptr, W_ptr, Out_ptr,
    stride_qb, stride_qh, stride_ql, stride_qd,
    L, m, d,
    BLOCK_M: tl.constexpr
):
    pid_bh = tl.program_id(0)

    # Initialize persistent state memory in SRAM [2m, d]
    kv_state = tl.zeros((2 * m, d), dtype=tl.float32)
    k_sum = tl.zeros((2 * m,), dtype=tl.float32)

    for t in range(L):
        q = tl.load(Q_ptr + pid_bh * stride_qh + t * stride_ql + tl.arange(0, d))
        k = tl.load(K_ptr + pid_bh * stride_qh + t * stride_ql + tl.arange(0, d))
        v = tl.load(V_ptr + pid_bh * stride_qh + t * stride_ql + tl.arange(0, d))

        # Unit sphere normalize
        q_norm = q / (tl.sqrt(tl.sum(q * q)) + 1e-6)
        k_norm = k / (tl.sqrt(tl.sum(k * k)) + 1e-6)

        # Trigonometric projection
        angle_k = tl.dot(k_norm[None, :], W_ptr)
        phi_k = tl.cat([tl.cos(angle_k), tl.sin(angle_k)], axis=1) / tl.sqrt(m.to(tl.float32))

        kv_state += tl.dot(tl.trans(phi_k), v[None, :])
        k_sum += tl.sum(phi_k, axis=0)

docs.title: CHELA-SLAY: Spherical Linearized Attention with Yat-Kernel Fourier Features
1. Executive Abstract & Architectural Motivation
docs.text:
Standard Multi-Head Attention requires materializing an \(L \times L\) Softmax matrix, scaling quadratically \(\mathcal{O}(L^2)\) in time and memory. CHELA-SLAY (Spherical Linearized Attention with Yat-Kernel) reformulates query-key contextualization by combining unit-hypersphere projection with trigonometric random Fourier features (Yat-Kernel).

By normalizing Queries and Keys onto the unit sphere \(\mathbb{S}^{d-1}\) (\(\widehat{Q} = Q / \|Q\|_2, \widehat{K} = K / \|K\|_2\)), CHELA-SLAY eliminates vector magnitude distortions. It then applies a positive trigonometric random feature mapping \(\phi(x) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{m}} [\cos(W x), \sin(W x)]^\top > 0\), enabling linear associative matrix multiplication \(\phi(\widehat{Q}) (\phi(\widehat{K})^\top V)\). This reduces time and memory complexity to \(\mathcal{O}(L \cdot m \cdot d)\), guaranteeing stable linear scaling with respect to sequence length \(L\).

docs.title: 2. Mathematical Formulations & Derivations
docs.text:
Given input sequence representations \(X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D}\), query, key, and value states are projected as:

\[ Q = X W_Q \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D}, \quad K = X W_K \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D}, \quad V = X W_V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D} \]

Multi-head formatting yields \(Q, K, V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times L \times d}\) with \(d = D / H\).

docs.title: 1. Spherical Unit Normalization:
docs.text:
Query and key vectors are projected onto the unit hypersphere \(\mathbb{S}^{d-1}\):

\[ \widehat{Q} = \frac{Q}{\|Q\|_2 + \epsilon} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times L \times d}, \quad \widehat{K} = \frac{K}{\|K\|_2 + \epsilon} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times L \times d} \]

docs.title: 2. Trigonometric Yat-Kernel Random Fourier Mapping (\(\phi\)):
docs.text:
Given a non-trainable random Gaussian projection matrix \(W \in \mathbb{R}^{m \times d}\) with \(W_{i, j} \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma^2)\), the Yat-Kernel feature map \(\phi(x) \in \mathbb{R}^{2m}\) is defined as:

\[ \phi(x) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{m}} \left[ \cos(W x); \; \sin(W x) \right] \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times L \times 2m} \]

Applying \(\phi\) to spherical queries and keys yields feature matrices \(\phi(\widehat{Q}), \phi(\widehat{K}) \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times L \times 2m}\).

docs.title: 3. Associative Linear Attention Recurrence:
docs.text:
Using matrix associativity, the unnormalized context is evaluated via matrix multiplication:

[ KV = \phi(\widehat{K})^\top V = \sum_{t=1}^L \phi(\widehat{K}t) \otimes V_t \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times 2m \times d} ] [ K{\text{sum}} = \sum_{t=1}^L \phi(\widehat{K}_t) \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times 1 \times 2m} ]

The normalized context \(O \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times L \times d}\) is evaluated per sequence position:

\[ O = \frac{\phi(\widehat{Q}) KV}{\phi(\widehat{Q}) K_{\text{sum}}^\top + \epsilon} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times L \times d} \]

Final projection yields \(Y = \text{Concat}(O_1, \dots, O_H) W_O \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D}\).

docs.text:
Input: hidden_states [B, L, D]
  │
  ├──> Q, K, V Projections ──> [B, H, L, d]
  │
  ├──> Spherical Normalization:
  │      ├──> Q_hat = Q / ||Q||_2 ──> [B, H, L, d]
  │      └──> K_hat = K / ||K||_2 ──> [B, H, L, d]
  │
  ├──> Yat-Kernel Fourier Mapping:
  │      ├──> cos_feat = cos(Q_hat @ W.T) / sqrt(m) ──> [B, H, L, m]
  │      ├──> sin_feat = sin(Q_hat @ W.T) / sqrt(m) ──> [B, H, L, m]
  │      └──> phi(Q_hat) = Concat([cos_feat, sin_feat], dim=-1) ──> [B, H, L, 2m]

docs.title: 5. Failure Modes, Rank Collapse & Edge Cases
docs.text:
1. Trigonometric Cancellation in FP16: Under FP16 execution, small angular differences \(\Delta \theta = W (q - k)\) can cause catastrophic cancellation in \(\cos(\cdot)\) and \(\sin(\cdot)\), leading to zero inner products.
  2. Frequency Hyperparameter Sensitivity: The standard deviation \(\sigma\) of Gaussian matrix \(W\) acts as a bandwidth hyperparameter. If \(\sigma\) is miscalibrated, feature maps become either over-concentrated or uniform.
  3. Causal Scan Underflow: In causal decoding, small feature values in \(\phi(\widehat{K})\) can accumulate underflow errors across long sequence horizons (\(L > 32768\)).

docs.title: 6. Hardware Acceleration Blueprint & Triton Kernel Design
docs.text:
A Triton kernel for CHELA-SLAY fuses L2 normalization, trigonometric projection, and linear matrix state accumulation directly into SRAM.

# Triton Fused CHELA-SLAY Linear Attention Blueprint
import triton
import triton.language as tl

@triton.jit
def _chela_slay_fused_kernel(
    Q_ptr, K_ptr, V_ptr, W_ptr, Out_ptr,
    stride_qb, stride_qh, stride_ql, stride_qd,
    L, m, d,
    BLOCK_M: tl.constexpr
):
    pid_bh = tl.program_id(0)

    # Initialize persistent state memory in SRAM [2m, d]
    kv_state = tl.zeros((2 * m, d), dtype=tl.float32)
    k_sum = tl.zeros((2 * m,), dtype=tl.float32)

    for t in range(L):
        q = tl.load(Q_ptr + pid_bh * stride_qh + t * stride_ql + tl.arange(0, d))
        k = tl.load(K_ptr + pid_bh * stride_qh + t * stride_ql + tl.arange(0, d))
        v = tl.load(V_ptr + pid_bh * stride_qh + t * stride_ql + tl.arange(0, d))

        # Unit sphere normalize
        q_norm = q / (tl.sqrt(tl.sum(q * q)) + 1e-6)
        k_norm = k / (tl.sqrt(tl.sum(k * k)) + 1e-6)

        # Trigonometric projection
        angle_k = tl.dot(k_norm[None, :], W_ptr)
        phi_k = tl.cat([tl.cos(angle_k), tl.sin(angle_k)], axis=1) / tl.sqrt(m.to(tl.float32))

        kv_state += tl.dot(tl.trans(phi_k), v[None, :])
        k_sum += tl.sum(phi_k, axis=0)

docs.title: ClusterFormer: Dynamic Token-Clustering Attention via Batch Iterative K-Means
1. Executive Abstract & Architectural Motivation
docs.text:
Dense Multi-Head Self-Attention (MHSA) computes \(L \times L\) pairwise interaction matrices across all tokens in a sequence, leading to quadratic time complexity \(\mathcal{O}(L^2 d)\) and severe memory constraints for long context models. Standard sparse attention paradigms rely either on fixed positional windows or static random graphs, which fail to adapt to content-dependent semantic clustering in hidden representations.

ClusterFormer (ClusterAttention) reformulates sequence-wide self-attention as a dynamic, content-driven semantic partitioning problem. Prior to computing attention matrices, token embeddings are dynamically grouped into \(K\) spatial clusters using a batch-wise iterative \(K\)-means clustering algorithm (Lloyd's algorithm) operating in feature space. Pairwise attention is subsequently restricted strictly to tokens within the same cluster assignment \(C_k\).

By constraining attention calculations to intra-cluster token sets of average size \(N_k \approx L / K\), ClusterFormer reduces attention score evaluations from \(L^2\) to \(\sum_{k=1}^K |C_k|^2 \approx L^2 / K\). This achieves an asymptotic \(K \times\) reduction in attention matrix computations while preserving long-range semantic interactions among globally distant tokens that share geometric proximity in embedding space.

docs.title: 2.1 Batch-Wise Iterative \(K\)-Means Clustering
docs.text:
Given input hidden states \(\mathbf{X} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D}\), \(K = \min(\text{num\_clusters}, L)\) initial centroids \(\boldsymbol{\mu}^{(0)} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times K \times D}\) are initialized via uniform random permutation without replacement from token vectors \(\mathbf{X}\).

For \(t = 1, \dots, I\) iterations (where \(I = \text{n\_iters}\)):

  1. Euclidean Distance Computation: $\(\mathbf{D}_{b, i, k}^{(t)} = \|\mathbf{X}_{b, i, :} - \boldsymbol{\mu}_{b, k, :}^{(t-1)}\|_2 = \sqrt{\sum_{d=1}^D \left( \mathbf{X}_{b, i, d} - \boldsymbol{\mu}_{b, k, d}^{(t-1)} \right)^2}\)$

  2. Nearest Centroid Assignment: $\(c_{b, i}^{(t)} = \operatorname{arg\,min}_{k \in \{1, \dots, K\}} \mathbf{D}_{b, i, k}^{(t)} \quad \in \{0, \dots, K-1\}^{B \times L}\)$

  3. Centroid Coordinate Recalculation: $\(\boldsymbol{\mu}_{b, k, :}^{(t)} = \frac{\sum_{i=1}^L \mathbb{I}\left( c_{b, i}^{(t)} = k \right) \mathbf{X}_{b, i, :}}{\max\left(1, \sum_{i=1}^L \mathbb{I}\left( c_{b, i}^{(t)} = k \right)\right)}\)$

docs.title: 2.2 Intra-Cluster Masked Attention Computation
docs.text:
Input activations are mapped to Query (\(\mathbf{Q}\)), Key (\(\mathbf{K}\)), and Value (\(\mathbf{V}\)) spaces via linear projections \(\mathbf{W}_Q, \mathbf{W}_K, \mathbf{W}_V \in \mathbb{R}^{D \times D}\): $\(\mathbf{Q}, \mathbf{K}, \mathbf{V} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times L \times d_h}\)$ where \(H\) is the number of heads and \(d_h = D / H\).

For each cluster partition \(k \in \{0, \dots, K-1\}\), a binary cluster mask \(\mathbf{M}^{(k)} \in \{0, 1\}^{B \times 1 \times 1 \times L}\) isolates tokens assigned to cluster \(k\): $\(\mathbf{M}_{b, 1, 1, j}^{(k)} = \mathbb{I}\left( c_{b, j} = k \right)\)$

An additive mask \(\mathbf{G}^{(k)} \in \{0, -\infty\}^{B \times 1 \times 1 \times L}\) masks out keys outside cluster \(k\): $\(\mathbf{G}_{b, 1, 1, j}^{(k)} = \begin{cases} 0 & \text{if } c_{b, j} = k \\ -10^9 & \text{if } c_{b, j} \neq k \end{cases}\)$

The intra-cluster attention score matrix \(\mathbf{S}^{(k)} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times L \times L}\) for cluster \(k\) is evaluated as: $\(\mathbf{S}_{b, h, i, j}^{(k)} = \frac{\mathbf{Q}_{b, h, i, :} \mathbf{K}_{b, h, j, :}^\top}{\sqrt{d_h}} + \mathbf{G}_{b, 1, 1, j}^{(k)} + \mathbf{P}_{b, 1, 1, j}\)$ where \(\mathbf{P}\) incorporates any optional padding mask.

Softmax normalization computes cluster-gated attention weights \(\mathbf{A}^{(k)}\): $\(\mathbf{A}_{b, h, i, j}^{(k)} = \operatorname{Softmax}_j\left( \mathbf{S}_{b, h, i, j}^{(k)} \right) = \frac{\exp\left( \mathbf{S}_{b, h, i, j}^{(k)} \right)}{\sum_{m=1}^L \exp\left( \mathbf{S}_{b, h, i, m}^{(k)} \right)}\)$ $\(\mathbf{O}_{b, h, i, :}^{(k)} = \sum_{j=1}^L \mathbf{A}_{b, h, i, j}^{(k)} \mathbf{V}_{b, h, j, :}\)$

docs.title: 2.3 Output Aggregation & Reassembly
docs.text:
The intermediate cluster context vectors \(\mathbf{O}^{(k)}\) are zero-masked for queries outside cluster \(k\) and summed across all \(K\) clusters: $\(\mathbf{O}_{\text{final}, b, h, i, :} = \sum_{k=0}^{K-1} \mathbb{I}\left( c_{b, i} = k \right) \cdot \mathbf{O}_{b, h, i, :}^{(k)}\)$

The multi-head output \(\mathbf{O}_{\text{final}} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times L \times d_h}\) is reshaped to \(\mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D}\) and passed through the final output projection: $\(\mathbf{Y} = \operatorname{Reshape}\left( \mathbf{O}_{\text{final}} \right) \mathbf{W}_O \quad \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D}\)$

docs.title: 3. Step-by-Step Tensor Execution Trace
docs.text:
Step Operation Input Shape Output Shape Tensor Transformation Description 1 Projections [B, L, D] [B, H, L, d_h] Linear map via \(W_Q, W_K, W_V\) & split heads 2 Initial Centroids [B, L, D] [B, K, D] Random permutation selection of \(K\) token vectors 3 Distance Matrix [B, L, D], [B, K, D] [B, L, K] Batch Pairwise Euclidean Distance cdist(X, centroids) 4 Nearest Assignment [B, L, K] [B, L] argmin(dist, dim=-1) index extraction 5 Centroid Recalculation [B, L, D], [B, L] [B, K, D] Masked mean sum over assigned tokens (\(I\) iterations) 6 Cluster Loop (\(k=1..K\)) [B, L] [B, 1, 1, L] Construct binary additive mask \(-10^9 \cdot (1 - \mathbb{I}(c=k))\) 7 Masked Attention Q, K, V, Mask [B, H, L, d_h] Scaled dot-product + additive cluster mask + Softmax 8 Context Mask & Add [B, H, L, d_h], c [B, H, L, d_h] Accumulate O_k * IS_IN_CLUSTER_K into global out 9 Output Projection [B, L, D] [B, L, D] Reshape multi-head context & linear project \(W_O\)

docs.title: 4.1 FLOPs Computation Breakdown
docs.text:
Let \(B\) be batch size, \(L\) sequence length, \(D\) hidden dimension, \(H\) attention heads, \(d_h = D/H\), \(K\) total clusters, and \(I\) clustering iterations.

  1. Linear Projections (\(\mathbf{Q}, \mathbf{K}, \mathbf{V}\)): $\(\operatorname{FLOPs}_{\text{proj}} = 3 \times 2 B L D^2 = 6 B L D^2\)$

  2. Iterative \(K\)-Means Clustering: In each iteration \(t \in \{1, \dots, I\}\): Euclidean Distance (cdist): \(3 B L K D\) FLOPs (squared differences + sum + sqrt). Furthermore, Centroid mean updates: \(2 B L D\) FLOPs. Across \(I\) iterations: $\(\operatorname{FLOPs}_{\text{kmeans}} = I \cdot (3 B L K D + 2 B L D) = 3 I B L K D + 2 I B L D\)$

  3. Sequential Intra-Cluster Attention Loops: The Python loop executes \(K\) passes. In pass \(k\), full \(L \times L\) matrix multiplies \(\mathbf{Q} \mathbf{K}^\top\) are computed: Attention score matmul: \(2 B H L^2 d_h = 2 B L^2 D\) Furthermore, Softmax & context matmul: \(2 B H L^2 d_h = 2 B L^2 D\) Summing across all \(K\) loop iterations in the un-optimized implementation: $\(\operatorname{FLOPs}_{\text{attn\_naive}} = K \times (4 B L^2 D) = 4 K B L^2 D\)$ (Note: In a theoretical grouped implementation without dense \(L \times L\) masks, FLOPs scale as \(4 B L (L / K) D = \frac{4 B L^2 D}{K}\)).

  4. Output Projection (\(\mathbf{W}_O\)): $\(\operatorname{FLOPs}_{\text{out}} = 2 B L D^2\)$

\[\text{Total Naive FLOPs} = 8 B L D^2 + 3 I B L K D + 4 K B L^2 D\]

docs.title: 4.2 MACs & Memory Footprint Analysis
docs.text:
Specifically, regarding \textbf{Multiply-Accumulate Operations (MACs)},

$\(\text{Total MACs} \approx 4 B L D^2 + 1.5 I B L K D + 2 K B L^2 D\)$ Specifically, regarding \textbf{Peak Activation Memory}, Furthermore, Distance Tensor: \(B \cdot L \cdot K \times 4 \text{ bytes}\) Concurrently, Cluster Masks: \(K \times B \cdot 1 \cdot 1 \cdot L \times 4 \text{ bytes}\) In this setting, Full Attention Matrix per cluster iteration: \(B \cdot H \cdot L \cdot L \times 2 \text{ bytes}\). Additionally, Peak memory scale: \(\mathcal{O}(B H L^2 + B L K)\) due to un-fused \(L \times L\) attention matrices inside the loop.

docs.title: 4.3 Asymptotic Scalability Comparison
docs.text: Specifically, regarding \textbf{Standard Dense Attention}, \(\mathcal{O}(L^2 D)\) compute, \(\mathcal{O}(L^2 H)\) memory. Furthermore, regarding \textbf{Un-Fused PyTorch ClusterFormer}, \(\mathcal{O}(K L^2 D + I L K D)\) compute — slower than standard attention due to executing \(K\) sequential \(L \times L\) dense matrix multiplications in PyTorch! Concurrently, regarding \textbf{Optimized Grouped ClusterFormer}, \(\mathcal{O}\left(I L K D + \frac{L^2 D}{K}\right)\) compute, achieving an optimal \(K \times\) speedup.

docs.title: 5. Failure Modes, Rank Collapse & Edge Cases
5.1 The Sequential \(K \times L^2\) Execution Trap
docs.text:
In the naive PyTorch implementation: 

for k in range(num_k):
    scores_k = torch.matmul(Q_k, K_k.transpose(-2, -1)) * scale # [B, H, L, L]
    scores_k = scores_k + mask_add
    attn_k = F.softmax(scores_k, dim=-1)
    out_k = torch.matmul(attn_k, V_k) # [B, H, L, D_h]
Instead of computing attention exclusively on the subset of tokens inside cluster \(k\), the code evaluates a full \(L \times L\) matrix product \(K\) separate times, relying on \(-10^9\) additive masks to zero out non-cluster tokens. Specifically, regarding \textbf{Computational Disparity}, rather than accelerating attention by \(K \times\), this implementation runs \(K\) times slower than standard attention, scaling as \(\mathcal{O}(K L^2 D)\).

docs.title: 5.2 Empty Cluster Collapse & Non-Differentiable Assignments
docs.text:
1. Empty Cluster Deadlocks: If initial centroid sampling picks duplicate or outlier tokens, some clusters receive zero token assignments (\(\sum \mathbb{I}(c_i = k) = 0\)). count_k.clamp(min=1.0) prevents division-by-zero, but leaves dead centroids that waste computation.
  2. Hard Assignment Gradient Disconnect: The operation \(c_i = \operatorname{arg\,min}_k \mathbf{D}_{i, k}\) is non-differentiable (\(\frac{\partial c_i}{\partial \mathbf{X}} = 0\)). Gradients during backpropagation cannot flow through cluster assignments to optimize the embedding space specifically for \(K\)-means clustering.

docs.title: 5.3 Cluster Imbalance & Outlier Domination
docs.text: In natural language, semantic token distributions are highly skewed (e.g., common stop words form massive clusters, while domain-specific entity tokens form tiny clusters). Specifically, regarding \textbf{Worst-Case Scaling}, if a single cluster absorbs \(90\%\) of sequence tokens (\(|C_1| \approx 0.9 L\)), effective complexity reverts to \(\mathcal{O}(L^2 D)\), eliminating sparse speedup advantages.

docs.title: 6. Hardware Acceleration Blueprint & Triton Kernel Design
docs.text: To realize true sub-quadratic speedups, tokens must be physically re-ordered (permuted) into contiguous cluster blocks in SRAM before executing dense attention.

docs.title: 6.1 Triton Hardware Acceleration Pipeline
docs.text:
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                        TRITON FUSED CLUSTERATTN KERNEL                            |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|  1. K-MEANS CENTROID REDUCTION KERNEL                                             |
|     - Computes fused cdist(X, centroids) in SRAM registers.                       |
|     - Performs warp-level reduction to find min_dist cluster index c_i.           |
|                                                                                   |
|  2. TOKEN SORT & PERMUTATION KERNEL                                               |
|     - Sorts token indices by cluster ID: perm_idx = argsort(c).                   |
|     - Generates cluster boundary offsets: cluster_offsets = [0, N1, N1+N2, ...].   |
|     - Writes permuted tensors Q_sorted, K_sorted, V_sorted into contiguous memory.|
|                                                                                   |
|  3. BLOCK-DIAGONAL FLASHATTENTION KERNEL                                          |
|     - Grid launched over cluster tiles.                                           |
|     - For cluster k: reads contiguous Q_k, K_k, V_k of size [N_k, d_h].           |
|     - Computes dense FlashAttention ONLY on [N_k, N_k] matrix.                    |
|     - Writes results back to un-permuted output buffer Y[perm_idx].               |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+

docs.title: 6.2 Implementation Code Blueprint (Triton Permuted Grouped Kernel)
docs.text:
import triton
import triton.language as tl

@triton.jit
def _cluster_block_flash_attn_kernel(
    Q_sorted_ptr, K_sorted_ptr, V_sorted_ptr, Out_sorted_ptr,
    Cluster_Offsets_ptr,
    stride_qb, stride_qh, stride_qm, stride_qd,
    stride_kb, stride_kh, stride_kn, stride_kd,
    stride_vb, stride_vh, stride_vn, stride_vd,
    stride_ob, stride_oh, stride_om, stride_od,
    scale,
    BLOCK_M: tl.constexpr,
    BLOCK_N: tl.constexpr,
    D_K: tl.constexpr
):
    cluster_id = tl.program_id(axis=0)
    head_id = tl.program_id(axis=1)
    batch_id = tl.program_id(axis=2)

    # Read start and end sequence bounds for target cluster
    start_idx = tl.load(Cluster_Offsets_ptr + cluster_id)
    end_idx = tl.load(Cluster_Offsets_ptr + cluster_id + 1)
    cluster_len = end_idx - start_idx

    # If cluster is empty, exit early
    if cluster_len <= 0:
        return

    offs_d = tl.arange(0, D_K)

    # Loop over query tiles within this cluster's range
    for m_offset in range(0, cluster_len, BLOCK_M):
        offs_m = start_idx + m_offset + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_M)
        mask_m = offs_m < end_idx

        # Load Q tile [BLOCK_M, D_K]
        q_ptrs = Q_sorted_ptr + batch_id * stride_qb + head_id * stride_qh + (offs_m[:, None] * stride_qm + offs_d[None, :])
        q = tl.load(q_ptrs, mask=mask_m[:, None], other=0.0)

        m_i = tl.full([BLOCK_M], float("-inf"), dtype=tl.float32)
        l_i = tl.zeros([BLOCK_M], dtype=tl.float32)
        acc = tl.zeros([BLOCK_M, D_K], dtype=tl.float32)

        # Loop over key tiles ONLY within the same cluster
        for n_offset in range(0, cluster_len, BLOCK_N):
            offs_n = start_idx + n_offset + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_N)
            mask_n = offs_n < end_idx

            k_ptrs = K_sorted_ptr + batch_id * stride_kb + head_id * stride_kh + (offs_n[None, :] * stride_kn + offs_d[:, None])
            k = tl.load(k_ptrs, mask=mask_n[None, :], other=0.0)

            # Local intra-cluster dot product [BLOCK_M, BLOCK_N]
            s = tl.dot(q, k) * scale
            s = tl.where(mask_m[:, None] & mask_n[None, :], s, float("-inf"))

            # Online Softmax update
            m_ij = tl.max(s, axis=1)
            m_new = tl.maximum(m_i, m_ij)
            p = tl.exp(s - m_new[:, None])
            l_new = tl.exp(m_i - m_new) * l_i + tl.sum(p, axis=1)

            acc_scale = tl.exp(m_i - m_new)
            acc = acc * acc_scale[:, None]

            v_ptrs = V_sorted_ptr + batch_id * stride_vb + head_id * stride_vh + (offs_n[:, None] * stride_vn + offs_d[None, :])
            v = tl.load(v_ptrs, mask=mask_n[:, None], other=0.0)
            acc = tl.dot(p.to(v.dtype), v, acc)

            l_i = l_new
            m_i = m_new

        # Normalize and store back
        acc = acc / l_i[:, None]
        out_ptrs = Out_sorted_ptr + batch_id * stride_ob + head_id * stride_oh + (offs_m[:, None] * stride_om + offs_d[None, :])
        tl.store(out_ptrs, acc.to(Out_sorted_ptr.dtype.element_ty), mask=mask_m[:, None])

docs.title: 6.3 Hardware Acceleration Gains
docs.text:
1. True \(K \times\) Compute Reduction: By grouping tokens contiguously into cluster_len sub-matrices, total matmul calculations drop from \(L^2\) to \(\sum N_k^2 \approx L^2 / K\).
  2. Zero Waste on Masking: Eliminates \(K\) separate \(L \times L\) full-matrix allocations and \(-10^9\) mask additions, maximizing memory bandwidth and Tensor Core throughput.

docs.title: 7. Next-Generation Innovations & Synthesis Opportunities
docs.text:
1. Differentiable Soft \(K\)-Means Gating: Replace hard argmin distance assignments with temperature-annealed Softmax clustering probabilities to allow end-to-end backpropagation through cluster centroid projections.
  2. Hierarchical Balanced Balanced-Tree K-Means: Enforce equal-sized cluster constraints (\(|C_k| = L / K\)) using spatial median splits to eliminate cluster size imbalance.
  3. Cross-Cluster Top-\(m\) Routing: Allow queries in cluster \(k\) to attend to the top-\(m\) nearest cluster centroids, preventing information loss at cluster boundaries.
  4. FP8 Cluster Centroid Distance Kernels: Execute distance calculations \(\mathbf{D} = \|\mathbf{X} - \boldsymbol{\mu}\|_2\) in FP8 precision (E4M3), delivering \(4\times\) throughput speedup on NVIDIA H100 Tensor Cores.

docs.title: Compressed Multi-Head Attention (SVD & Energy-Thresholded Low-Rank Approximations)
1. Abstract & Theoretical Motivation
docs.text:
Standard Multi-Head Attention (MHA) modules in deep Transformer architectures rely on full-rank linear parameterizations for input (\(W_{\text{qkv}} \in \mathbb{R}^{3D \times D}\)) and output (\(W_{\text{out}} \in \mathbb{R}^{D \times D}\)) projections. Storing and evaluating these high-dimensional dense parameter matrices creates High-Bandwidth Memory (HBM) fetch latency and large activation storage during inference.

This module presents a Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) compression framework comprising two mechanisms: fixed-rank factorization (CompressedAttentionLayer) and cumulative spectral energy-preserving dynamic rank truncation (CompressedAttentionLayer2). By factorizing projection weights into orthogonal singular vector bases and splitting singular value square roots (\(\sqrt{\Sigma}\)) across left and right projections, the architecture enforces associative low-rank bottlenecks (\(r_{\text{qkv}}, r_{\text{out}} \ll D\)). This reduces parameter count and FLOP complexity while maintaining representation energy above defined variance thresholds \(\tau_{\text{energy}}\).

docs.title: 2. Mathematical Derivations & Formulations
docs.text: Let \(X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times D}\) be the input activation sequence, where \(B\) is batch size, \(N\) is sequence length, and \(D\) is model dimension. Let \(H\) be the number of attention heads and \(d_k = D / H\) the head dimension.

docs.title: 1. Truncated Singular Value Decomposition & Symmetric Square-Root Factorization:
docs.text:
For input projection matrix \(W_{\text{qkv}} = [W_Q; W_K; W_V] \in \mathbb{R}^{3D \times D}\) and output projection matrix \(W_{\text{out}} \in \mathbb{R}^{D \times D}\), full SVD yields:

\[ W_{\text{qkv}} = U_{\text{qkv}} \Sigma_{\text{qkv}} V_{\text{qkv}}^\top, \quad W_{\text{out}} = U_{\text{out}} \Sigma_{\text{out}} V_{\text{out}}^\top \]

where \(U_{\text{qkv}} \in \mathbb{R}^{3D \times 3D}\), \(\Sigma_{\text{qkv}} \in \mathbb{R}^{3D \times D}\), and \(V_{\text{qkv}}^\top \in \mathbb{R}^{D \times D}\).

Truncating to rank \(r_{\text{qkv}}\) and distributing singular values symmetrically via \(\Sigma^{1/2}\):

\[ W_{\text{qkv}} \approx \left( \widetilde{U}_{\text{qkv}} \widetilde{\Sigma}_{\text{qkv}}^{1/2} \right) \left( \widetilde{\Sigma}_{\text{qkv}}^{1/2} \widetilde{V}_{\text{qkv}}^\top \right) \]

where \(\widetilde{U}_{\text{qkv}} \in \mathbb{R}^{3D \times r_{\text{qkv}}}\), \(\widetilde{\Sigma}_{\text{qkv}}^{1/2} \in \mathbb{R}^{r_{\text{qkv}} \times r_{\text{qkv}}}\), and \(\widetilde{V}_{\text{qkv}}^\top \in \mathbb{R}^{r_{\text{qkv}} \times D}\).

Similarly for \(W_{\text{out}}\) with target rank \(r_{\text{out}}\):

\[ W_{\text{out}} \approx \left( \widetilde{U}_{\text{out}} \widetilde{\Sigma}_{\text{out}}^{1/2} \right) \left( \widetilde{\Sigma}_{\text{out}}^{1/2} \widetilde{V}_{\text{out}}^\top \right) \]

docs.title: 2. Cumulative Spectral Energy Preservation Criteria:
docs.text:
In CompressedAttentionLayer2, target rank \(r\) is dynamically determined by enforcing a cumulative singular value energy threshold \(\tau_{\text{energy}} \in (0, 1]\) (e.g., \(\tau_{\text{energy}} = 0.95\)):

[ r_{\text{qkv}} = \min \left{ r \in \mathbb{N}^+ \; \Big| \; \frac{\sum_{i=1}^r \sigma_{\text{qkv}, i}}{\sum_{j=1}^R \sigma_{\text{qkv}, j}} \ge \tau_{\text{energy}} \text{ and } r \ge r_{\min} \right} ] [ r_{\text{out}} = \min \left{ r \in \mathbb{N}^+ \; \Big| \; \frac{\sum_{i=1}^r \sigma_{\text{out}, i}}{\sum_{j=1}^R \sigma_{\text{out}, j}} \ge \tau_{\text{energy}} \text{ and } r \ge r_{\min} \right} ]

where \(R\) is full rank and \(r_{\min}\) is a minimum threshold constraint (e.g., \(r_{\min} = 16\)).

docs.title: 3. Forward Associative Factorization Execution Pass:
docs.text:
1. Low-Rank Intermediate Projection: [ Z_{\text{qkv}} = \left( X \widetilde{V}{\text{qkv}} \right) \odot \widetilde{\Sigma}{\text{qkv}}^{1/2} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times r_{\text{qkv}}} ]
  2. Up-Projection to QKV Subspace: [ QKV_{\text{comp}} = Z_{\text{qkv}} \widetilde{U}{\text{qkv}}^\top + b{\text{qkv}} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times 3D} ] Partitioning into Query, Key, and Value components: [ Q = QKV_{\text{comp}}[:, :, 0:D], \quad K = QKV_{\text{comp}}[:, :, D:2D], \quad V = QKV_{\text{comp}}[:, :, 2D:3D] ]
  3. Scaled Dot-Product Attention: [ S = \frac{1}{\sqrt{d_k}} Q K^\top + M_{\text{attn}} + M_{\text{pad}} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times N \times N} ] [ A = \text{Softmax}(S, \text{dim}=-1), \quad \widehat{A} = \text{Dropout}(A, p) ] [ C = \widehat{A} V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times D} ]
  4. Low-Rank Output Projection: [ Z_{\text{out}} = \left( C \widetilde{V}{\text{out}} \right) \odot \widetilde{\Sigma}{\text{out}}^{1/2} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times r_{\text{out}}} ] [ Y = Z_{\text{out}} \widetilde{U}{\text{out}}^\top + b{\text{out}} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times D} ]

docs.title: 3. Tensor Execution Flow & Dimensional Shape Tracing
docs.text:
Input: query (x) [B, N, D]
  │
  ├──> MatMul(Vh_qkv.T) [r_qkv, D] ──> [B, N, r_qkv]
  ├──> Multiply S_qkv_sqrt [r_qkv] ──> projected_x: [B, N, r_qkv]
  ├──> MatMul(U_qkv.T) [3D, r_qkv] ──> [B, N, 3D]
  ├──> Add bias_qkv [3D] ──> qkv_compressed: [B, N, 3D]
  │
  ├──> Split [0:D], [D:2D], [2D:3D] ──> Q, K, V: [B, N, D]
  │
  ├──> Scaled Dot-Product Attention:
  │      scores = Q @ K.T / sqrt(d_k)
  │      Add attn_mask & key_padding_mask (-1e9)
  │      Softmax(dim=-1) & Dropout ──> attn_weights: [B, N, N]
  │      context = attn_weights @ V ──> context: [B, N, D]
  │
  ├──> MatMul(Vh_out.T) [r_out, D] ──> [B, N, r_out]
  ├──> Multiply S_out_sqrt [r_out] ──> context_fused: [B, N, r_out]
  ├──> MatMul(U_out.T) [D, r_out] ──> [B, N, D]
  └──> Add bias_out [D] ──> Output: [B, N, D]

docs.title: Computational Workload & Memory Footprint
docs.text:
Let \(B\) be batch size, \(N\) sequence length, \(D\) model dimension, \(H\) heads, \(d_k = D / H\), \(r_{\text{qkv}}\) QKV rank, and \(r_{\text{out}}\) output rank.

  1. Parameter Savings: Original Uncompressed Parameters: \(3 D^2 (W_{\text{in}}) + D^2 (W_{\text{out}}) = 4 D^2\). Furthermore, SVD Parameters (U_qkv, S_qkv_sqrt, Vh_qkv, U_out, S_out_sqrt, Vh_out): Concurrently, \(W_{\text{qkv}}\) factors: \(3 D r_{\text{qkv}} + r_{\text{qkv}} + r_{\text{qkv}} D = r_{\text{qkv}} (4D + 1)\). In this setting, \(W_{\text{out}}\) factors: \(D r_{\text{out}} + r_{\text{out}} + r_{\text{out}} D = r_{\text{out}} (2D + 1)\). Additionally, Total SVD Parameters: \(r_{\text{qkv}} (4D + 1) + r_{\text{out}} (2D + 1)\). Moreover, Compression Ratio (e.g., \(D=768, r_{\text{qkv}}=64, r_{\text{out}}=64\)): From an analytical standpoint, Original: \(2,359,296\) parameters (\(9.44 \text{ MB}\)). In terms of operational dynamics, SVD Compressed: \(64(3073) + 64(1537) = 196,672 + 98,368 = 295,040\) parameters (\(1.18 \text{ MB}\)). Specifically, regarding \textbf{Parameter Footprint Savings}, \(\approx 8.0\times\) compression (\(87.5\%\) savings).

  2. Computational FLOPs & MACs: QKV Low-Rank Down-Projection: \(2 B N D r_{\text{qkv}}\) FLOPs (\(B N D r_{\text{qkv}}\) MACs). Furthermore, QKV Low-Rank Up-Projection: \(2 B N r_{\text{qkv}} (3D) = 6 B N D r_{\text{qkv}}\) FLOPs (\(3 B N D r_{\text{qkv}}\) MACs). Concurrently, Core Attention Scores & Context (\(Q K^\top\) & \(A V\)): \(4 B N^2 D\) FLOPs (\(2 B N^2 D\) MACs). In this setting, Output Low-Rank Down-Projection: \(2 B N D r_{\text{out}}\) FLOPs (\(B N D r_{\text{out}}\) MACs). Additionally, Output Low-Rank Up-Projection: \(2 B N r_{\text{out}} D\) FLOPs (\(B N D r_{\text{out}}\) MACs).

Specifically, regarding \textbf{Total MACs}, \(B N \left[ 4 D r_{\text{qkv}} + 2 D r_{\text{out}} + 2 N D \right]\) Furthermore, regarding \textbf{Total FLOPs}, \(B N \left[ 8 D r_{\text{qkv}} + 4 D r_{\text{out}} + 4 N D \right]\)

docs.title: 5. Architectural Bottlenecks, Rank Collapse & Failure Modes
Spectral Energy Tail Loss & Accuracy Drop
docs.text:
When energy threshold \(\tau_{\text{energy}}\) is set aggressively low (\(\tau_{\text{energy}} < 0.85\)), significant singular values in the tail of \(\Sigma_{\text{qkv}}\) are discarded. This causes degradation in fine-grained syntactic relationships and cross-head contextual routing.

Singular Energy Cumulative Spectrum:
Sum(σ_1..r) / Sum(σ_1..R)  ──>  [██████████████░░░░░]  (Threshold τ = 0.95)
                                  │ Preserved Rank r │ Discarded Tail │

docs.title: CPU-GPU NumPy SVD Initialization Bottleneck
docs.text: In CompressedAttentionLayer, SVD factorization is performed on CPU using NumPy (np.linalg.svd). For large Transformer models (\(D > 4096\)), computing CPU SVD during module instantiation causes long startup latency and CPU-to-GPU memory transfer overheads.

docs.title: Intermediate Activation Allocation Inefficiency
docs.text: The PyTorch forward pass calculates low-rank projections sequentially (projected_x = x @ Vh.T, qkv = projected_x @ U.T), instantiating intermediate activation tensors \([B, N, r_{\text{qkv}}]\) in GPU DRAM. This introduces memory bandwidth pressure compared to fused kernels.

docs.title: 6. Hardware Acceleration Blueprint & Triton Optimization Strategies
Fused Double-GEMM SVD Triton Kernel Architecture
docs.text:
To saturate GPU Tensor Cores and eliminate intermediate DRAM activation writes, Triton fuses the low-rank down-projection, singular scaling, and up-projection into a single memory-efficient kernel.

       Global Memory (HBM)
      ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
      │ Input x [B, N, D]                                      │
      │ Vh_qkv [r_qkv, D], S_qkv_sqrt [r_qkv], U_qkv [3D, r_qkv]│
      └───────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────┘
                                  │ Coalesced Tile Load
                                  ▼
 ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 │                   Triton SRAM Scratchpad                         │
 │ 1. Load Input Tile: x_tile [BLOCK_M, D]                          │
 │ 2. Compute Intermediate Down-GEMM: Z = x_tile @ Vh_qkv.T         │
 │ 3. Scale Singular Values: Z_scaled = Z * S_qkv_sqrt              │
 │ 4. Compute Up-GEMM: QKV_tile = Z_scaled @ U_qkv.T               │
 └────────────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────┘
                                  │ Direct Stream to Attention
                                  ▼
      ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
      │ Q, K, V Tensors [B, N, 3D]                             │
      └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

docs.title: Key Triton Implementation Guidelines:
docs.text:
1. Pre-Absorbed Weight Buffers: Absorb singular square roots \(\sqrt{\Sigma}\) directly into left singular matrices \(\widetilde{U}\) at initialization: [ \widehat{U}{\text{qkv}} = \widetilde{U}{\text{qkv}} \cdot \text{diag}\left(\sqrt{\Sigma_{\text{qkv}}}\right) \in \mathbb{R}^{3D \times r_{\text{qkv}}} ] This reduces the kernel workload to two sequential GEMM calls (\(x \widetilde{V}^\top\) and \(Z \widehat{U}^\top\)), removing elementwise multiplication overhead.
  2. SRAM Scratchpad Reuse: Retain low-rank activation vectors \(Z \in \mathbb{R}^{\text{BLOCK\_M} \times r_{\text{qkv}}}\) in Streaming Multiprocessor (SM) L1 registers, skipping intermediate DRAM writes entirely.
  3. Dynamic GPU-Native Batched SVD: Replace CPU NumPy initialization calls with GPU-accelerated PyTorch batched SVD primitives (torch.linalg.svd) to accelerate model compression during online training pipelines.

docs.title: Compressed Multi-Head Attention: Joint Truncated SVD Matrix Factorization
1. Executive Abstract & Architectural Motivation
docs.text:
Compressed Multi-Head Attention (CompressedDistilBertAttention) provides a zero-shot model compression framework that compresses dense linear projections in Transformer architectures (such as DistilBERT) via Joint Truncated Singular Value Decomposition (SVD). Standard MHA layers rely on four dense weight matrices (\(W_Q, W_K, W_V, W_O \in \mathbb{R}^{D \times D}\)), requiring \(4 D^2\) parameter storage per layer.

To eliminate parameter redundancy and lower hardware memory bandwidth demands, CompressedDistilBertAttention stacks the Query, Key, and Value projection matrices into a combined parameter matrix \(W_{\text{qkv}} = [W_Q; W_K; W_V] \in \mathbb{R}^{3D \times D}\) and factorizes both \(W_{\text{qkv}}\) and the output projection matrix \(W_{\text{out}} \in \mathbb{R}^{D \times D}\) using low-rank Truncated SVD. By retaining only the top-\(r\) singular components (\(r_{\text{qkv}}, r_{\text{out}} \ll D\)), the layer projects hidden states into low-rank bottleneck subspaces, reducing parameter counts and matrix multiplication FLOPs while preserving zero-shot task capabilities.

docs.title: 2. Mathematical Formulations & Derivations
docs.text: Let \(X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times D}\) denote input activations. Let \(H\) be the number of attention heads, \(d_h = D / H\) the dimension per head, \(r_{\text{qkv}}\) the target rank for QKV projections, and \(r_{\text{out}}\) the rank for output projections.

docs.title: Joint SVD Factorization of Stacked Projection Matrices:
docs.text:
The stacked input projection matrix \(W_{\text{qkv}} \in \mathbb{R}^{3D \times D}\) and output projection matrix \(W_{\text{out}} \in \mathbb{R}^{D \times D}\) undergo full Singular Value Decomposition:

[ W_{\text{qkv}} = U_{\text{qkv}} \Sigma_{\text{qkv}} V_{\text{qkv}}^\top, \quad U_{\text{qkv}} \in \mathbb{R}^{3D \times 3D}, \, \Sigma_{\text{qkv}} \in \mathbb{R}^{3D \times D}, \, V_{\text{qkv}} \in \mathbb{R}^{D \times D} ] [ W_{\text{out}} = U_{\text{out}} \Sigma_{\text{out}} V_{\text{out}}^\top, \quad U_{\text{out}} \in \mathbb{R}^{D \times D}, \, \Sigma_{\text{out}} \in \mathbb{R}^{D \times D}, \, V_{\text{out}} \in \mathbb{R}^{D \times D} ]

Truncating matrices to low-rank ranks \(r_{\text{qkv}}\) and \(r_{\text{out}}\):

[ \widehat{W}{\text{qkv}} = U{\text{qkv}}[:, :r_{\text{qkv}}] \cdot \text{diag}(\Sigma_{\text{qkv}}[:r_{\text{qkv}}]) \cdot V_{\text{qkv}}[:r_{\text{qkv}}, :]^\top ] [ \widehat{W}{\text{out}} = U{\text{out}}[:, :r_{\text{out}}] \cdot \text{diag}(\Sigma_{\text{out}}[:r_{\text{out}}]) \cdot V_{\text{out}}[:r_{\text{out}}, :]^\top ]

docs.title: Low-Rank QKV Transformation & De-stacking:
docs.text:
For input tensor \(X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times D}\):

[ P_{\text{proj}} = (X V_{\text{qkv}}[:r_{\text{qkv}}, :]^\top) \odot \Sigma_{\text{qkv}}[:r_{\text{qkv}}] \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times r_{\text{qkv}}} ] [ \text{QKV}{\text{comp}} = P{\text{proj}} U_{\text{qkv}}[:, :r_{\text{qkv}}]^\top \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times 3D} ]

Splitting \(\text{QKV}_{\text{comp}}\) along dimension \(D\) yields \(Q, K, V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times D}\). Adding original bias vectors \(b_Q, b_K, b_V \in \mathbb{R}^D\):

\[ Q = \text{QKV}_{\text{comp}}[:, :, :D] + b_Q, \quad K = \text{QKV}_{\text{comp}}[:, :, D:2D] + b_K, \quad V = \text{QKV}_{\text{comp}}[:, :, 2D:] + b_V \]

Reshaping into multi-head layouts: \(Q, K, V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times N \times d_h}\).

docs.title: Scaled Dot-Product & Low-Rank Output Projection:
docs.text:
Standard scaled attention affinity matrices are computed:

[ S_{b, h, i, j} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{d_h}} \sum_{m=1}^{d_h} Q_{b, h, i, m} \cdot K_{b, h, j, m} ] [ A_{b, h, i, j} = \text{Softmax}j (S{b, h, i, j} + M_{b, 1, i, j}) ] [ C_{b, h, i, m} = \sum_{j=1}^N \text{Dropout}(A){b, h, i, j} \cdot V{b, h, j, m} \implies C \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times D} ]

The context tensor \(C\) is projected through low-rank output buffers:

[ F_{\text{fused}} = (C V_{\text{out}}[:r_{\text{out}}, :]^\top) \odot \Sigma_{\text{out}}[:r_{\text{out}}] \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times r_{\text{out}}} ] [ Y = F_{\text{fused}} U_{\text{out}}[:, :r_{\text{out}}]^\top + b_{\text{out}} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times D} ]

docs.text: Execution Stage Input Shape Transformation / Operation Output Shape Input [B, N, D] Input activation batch [B, N, D] Low-Rank Bottleneck (QKV) [B, N, D] matmul(X, Vh_qkv.t()) * S_qkv [B, N, r_qkv] QKV Reconstruction [B, N, r_qkv] matmul(proj, U_qkv.t()) [B, N, 3D] Split & Add Bias [B, N, 3D] Slice into Q, K, V + biases [B, N, D] each Multi-Head Transpose [B, N, D] .view(B, N, H, d_h).transpose(1, 2) [B, H, N, d_h] each Score Matrix MatMul Q, K torch.matmul(q, k.transpose(-2, -1)) / sqrt(d_h) [B, H, N, N] Softmax & Value Agg scores, V apply_mask + softmax + matmul(attn, v) [B, H, N, d_h] Reshape Context [B, H, N, d_h] .transpose(1, 2).contiguous().view(B, N, D) [B, N, D] Low-Rank Out Bottleneck [B, N, D] matmul(context, Vh_out.t()) * S_out [B, N, r_out] Output Reconstruction [B, N, r_out] matmul(fused, U_out.t()) + bias_out [B, N, D]

docs.title: Computational Workload (FLOPs & MACs)
docs.text:
Let \(B\) be batch size, \(N\) sequence length, \(D\) model dimension, \(r_{\text{qkv}}\) QKV rank, \(r_{\text{out}}\) output rank, \(H\) heads, and \(d_h = D/H\).

  1. Compressed QKV Projections: \(X V_{\text{qkv}}^\top\): \(2 B N D r_{\text{qkv}}\) FLOPs. Furthermore, Singular value scaling: \(B N r_{\text{qkv}}\) FLOPs. Concurrently, \(P_{\text{proj}} U_{\text{qkv}}^\top\): \(2 B N r_{\text{qkv}} (3D) = 6 B N D r_{\text{qkv}}\) FLOPs. In this setting, Total QKV Projection Cost: \(8 B N D r_{\text{qkv}} + B N r_{\text{qkv}}\) FLOPs.

  2. Core Scaled Attention: \(Q K^\top\) & \(A V\): \(4 B N^2 D\) FLOPs. Furthermore, Softmax & Masking: \(7 B H N^2\) FLOPs.

  3. Compressed Output Projections: \(C V_{\text{out}}^\top\): \(2 B N D r_{\text{out}}\) FLOPs. Furthermore, Singular value scaling: \(B N r_{\text{out}}\) FLOPs. Concurrently, \(F_{\text{fused}} U_{\text{out}}^\top\): \(2 B N r_{\text{out}} D\) FLOPs. In this setting, Total Output Projection Cost: \(4 B N D r_{\text{out}} + B N r_{\text{out}}\) FLOPs.

  4. Total Workload Summary: Specifically, regarding \textbf{Total MACs}, \(4 B N D r_{\text{qkv}} + 2 B N D r_{\text{out}} + 2 B N^2 D\) Furthermore, regarding \textbf{Total FLOPs}, \(8 B N D r_{\text{qkv}} + 4 B N D r_{\text{out}} + 4 B N^2 D + 7 B H N^2 + B N (r_{\text{qkv}} + r_{\text{out}})\)

docs.title: Memory Footprint & Parameter Reduction
docs.text:
Specifically, regarding \textbf{Uncompressed MHA Parameter Count}, \(4 D^2 + 4 D\) floats. Furthermore, regarding \textbf{Compressed Parameter Count},

[ \text{Params}{\text{comp}} = (3D + D) \cdot r{\text{qkv}} + 2D \cdot r_{\text{out}} + 4D \text{ floats} ] For \(D = 768, r_{\text{qkv}} = 32, r_{\text{out}} = 32\): Uncompressed: \(4 \times 768^2 \approx 2,359,296\) parameters. Furthermore, Compressed: \(4(768)(32) + 2(768)(32) \approx 147,456\) parameters (16\(\times\) parameter reduction).

docs.title: 5. Architectural Bottlenecks, Rank Collapse & Edge Cases
Truncation Error & Singular Value Tail Loss
docs.text: If ranks \(r_{\text{qkv}}\) or \(r_{\text{out}}\) are set below the effective numerical rank of the original weights, the Frobenius norm error \(\|W - \widehat{W}\|_F = \sqrt{\sum_{i=r+1}^D \sigma_i^2}\) increases, deteriorating perplexity unless post-SVD fine-tuning is performed.

docs.title: Latency Bottleneck from Un-fused Intermediate Buffer Allocations
docs.text: In standard PyTorch, executing \(X \to r_{\text{qkv}} \to 3D \to D\) requires materializing intermediate \([B, N, 3D]\) tensors in HBM, which can consume extra DRAM memory bandwidth if \(r_{\text{qkv}}\) is close to \(D\).

docs.title: 6. Hardware Acceleration Blueprint & Triton Kernel Design
docs.text:
A Triton kernel for Compressed SVD Attention fuses the down-projection (\(V_{\text{qkv}}^\top\)), singular value scaling (\(\Sigma\)), and up-projection (\(U_{\text{qkv}}^\top\)) into a single SRAM matrix multiply pass.

                    Global Memory (HBM)
   ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
   │ Input: X [B, N, D]                                          │
   │ SVD Buffers: Vh_qkv [r_qkv, D], S_qkv [r_qkv], U_qkv [3D, r_qkv]│
   └──────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────┘
                                  │ Load Tiles into SRAM
                                  ▼
 ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 │                     Triton SRAM Scratchpad                     │
 │ 1. Load Activation Tile X_i [BLOCK_M, D]                       │
 │ 2. Compute Fused Bottleneck: P_i = X_i @ Vh_qkv.T * S_qkv      │
 │ 3. Reconstruct QKV Tile: QKV_i = P_i @ U_qkv.T                 │
 │ 4. Slice Q, K, V & Execute Online Scaled Attention             │
 └────────────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────┘
                                  │ Stream Output
                                  ▼
   ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
   │ Context Output: Y [B, N, D]                                 │
   └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

docs.title: 7. Next-Generation Innovations & Synthesis Opportunities
docs.text:
1. Non-Uniform Per-Layer Rank Allocation: Assign higher ranks (\(r_{\text{qkv}} = 64\)) to early layers capturing broad syntactic relationships and lower ranks (\(r_{\text{qkv}} = 16\)) to deeper layers.
  2. Quantized Low-Rank SVD (QLR-SVD): Quantize low-rank matrices \(U, V\) to INT4 or FP8 while keeping singular values \(\Sigma\) in FP32, maximizing compression ratio up to \(32\times\).
  3. LoRA Fine-Tuning over Compressed SVD: Attach lightweight LoRA adapters to frozen SVD projection buffers to restore full pre-compression accuracy with minimal trainable parameters.

docs.title: Cosformer: Linear Attention with Non-Negative Cosine Feature Maps
docs.text: Family: Kernelized & Feature-Map Linear Attentions · NeuralOps Registry ID: cosformer

docs.title: Executive Abstract
docs.text:
Cosformer (Qin et al., 2022) replaces the quadratic softmax attention mechanism with a kernelized feature map based on non-negative cosine transformations. Standard linear attentions suffer from dot-product decay and poor inductive bias for local dependencies. Cosformer addresses this by combining non-negative ReLU activation with cosine-based reweighting that emphasizes proximate token interactions without sacrificing \(O(N)\) linear complexity.

In NeuralOps, cosformer is integrated into the universal attention dispatch table, featuring full support for the 3-level fallback hierarchy, automatic shape validation, and end-to-end autograd backwards passes.

docs.title: Mathematical Formulation
docs.text:
The core operator computation is defined as:

\[ \phi(x) = \text{ReLU}(x) \cos\left(\frac{\pi x}{2 L}\right), \quad O = \frac{\phi(Q) (\phi(K)^T V)}{\phi(Q) (\phi(K)^T \mathbf{1})} \]

During execution, inputs \(Q, K, V\) are projected to dimension \(d\). In the causal configuration, lower-triangular masking ensures that tokens only attend to past and current time-steps, preserving autoregressive invariants.

     │         │
     │         ▼
     └────► Scaled Output & Residual Add (B, T, D)

docs.text:
Production-hardened Cosformer linear attention operator in NeuralOps. Incorporates numerically stable normalizer division, chunk-parallel associative scan execution in Triton, and seamless integration into HuggingFace transformer backbones with automatic shape adaptation.

docs.title: Decay Linear Attention: Learnable Multi-Scale Exponential Decay
docs.text: Family: Gated Linear Recurrences · NeuralOps Registry ID: decay_linear_attention

docs.title: Executive Abstract
docs.text:
Decay Linear Attention imposes a multi-scale exponential decay prior over the linear recurrent state. Heads are initialized with geometric decay rates spanning diverse temporal receptive fields from local token context (\(e^{-1.0}\)) to long-range context (\(e^{-0.001}\)).

In NeuralOps, decay_linear_attention is integrated into the universal attention dispatch table, featuring full support for the 3-level fallback hierarchy, automatic shape validation, and end-to-end autograd backwards passes.

docs.text:

\[ S_t = \exp(-\lambda) \odot S_{t-1} + K_t^T V_t, \quad O_t = Q_t S_t \quad \text{with learnable} \; \lambda \in \mathbb{R}^H \]

During execution, inputs \(Q, K, V\) are projected to dimension \(d\). In the causal configuration, lower-triangular masking ensures that tokens only attend to past and current time-steps, preserving autoregressive invariants.

docs.text: Family: Block-Sparse, Dilated & Sliding-Window Attentions · NeuralOps Registry ID: dynamic_conv_attention

docs.title: Executive Abstract
docs.text:
Dynamic Convolution Attention (Wu et al., 2019) replaces the expensive all-pairs attention matrix with dynamic, input-dependent convolution kernels whose filter weights are generated on the fly per token.

In NeuralOps, dynamic_conv_attention is integrated into the universal attention dispatch table, featuring full support for the 3-level fallback hierarchy, automatic shape validation, and end-to-end autograd backwards passes.

docs.text:

\[ k_t = \text{softmax}(W_k x_t), \quad y_t = \sum_{i=1}^K k_{t, i} \cdot x_{t - i + 1} \]

During execution, inputs \(Q, K, V\) are projected to dimension \(d\). In the causal configuration, lower-triangular masking ensures that tokens only attend to past and current time-steps, preserving autoregressive invariants.

docs.title: EAT: Efficient Attention Transformer Block with Progressive Token Pruning
1. Executive Abstract & Architectural Motivation
docs.text:
Multi-Head Self-Attention (MHSA) and Feed-Forward Networks (FFN) in standard Transformer blocks maintain a fixed sequence length \(L\) across all model layers. In deep networks, many tokens correspond to redundant syntax, background noise, or uninformative punctuation. Maintaining these non-essential tokens through deep layers wastes memory and quadratic FLOPs \(\mathcal{O}(L^2 d)\) in subsequent attention operations.

EAT (Efficient Attention Transformer Block) introduces dynamic length reduction by integrating a Progressive Token Pruning sub-network directly into the Transformer layer pipeline. EAT executes standard Multi-Head Self-Attention and Feed-Forward feature synthesis, then evaluates token-level salience scores to extract a top-\(k\) informative token subset \(\mathcal{I}_{\text{keep}}\). Non-essential tokens are dynamically dropped, reducing the active sequence length from \(L\) to \(L' = \lfloor \gamma \cdot L \rfloor\) (where \(\gamma < 1\)).

By progressively shrinking sequence length across Transformer depth (\(L_0 > L_1 > \dots > L_M\)), EAT compounds computational and memory savings down the network hierarchy, accelerating inference while preserving task accuracy.

docs.title: 2.1 Multi-Head Self-Attention Sub-Layer
docs.text:
Given input activations \(\mathbf{X} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D}\), Query (\(\mathbf{Q}\)), Key (\(\mathbf{K}\)), and Value (\(\mathbf{V}\)) projections yield: $\(\mathbf{Q} = \mathbf{X} \mathbf{W}_Q, \quad \mathbf{K} = \mathbf{X} \mathbf{W}_K, \quad \mathbf{V} = \mathbf{X} \mathbf{W}_V \quad \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times L \times d_h}\)$ where \(H\) is the head count and \(d_h = D / H\).

If key padding mask \(\mathbf{M}_{\text{pad}} \in \{0, 1\}^{B \times L}\) is provided, invalid padding key positions are masked: $\(\mathbf{S} = \frac{\mathbf{Q} \mathbf{K}^\top}{\sqrt{d_h}} + (1 - \mathbf{M}_{\text{pad}}) \cdot (-10^9)\)$ $\(\mathbf{A} = \operatorname{Softmax}(\mathbf{S}) \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times L \times L}\)$ $\(\mathbf{X}_{\text{attn}} = \mathbf{A} \mathbf{V} \mathbf{W}_O \quad \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D}\)$

The first residual addition and Layer Normalization yield intermediate representation \(\mathbf{X}^{(1)}\): $\(\mathbf{X}^{(1)} = \operatorname{LayerNorm}\left( \mathbf{X} + \mathbf{X}_{\text{attn}} \right) \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D}\)$

docs.title: 2.2 Position-wise Feed-Forward Sub-Layer
docs.text:
Intermediate activations \(\mathbf{X}^{(1)}\) pass through a 2-layer FFN with expansion factor 4 and GELU non-linearity: $\(\mathbf{F} = \operatorname{GELU}\left( \mathbf{X}^{(1)} \mathbf{W}_1 + \mathbf{b}_1 \right) \mathbf{W}_2 + \mathbf{b}_2 \quad \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D}\)$ where \(\mathbf{W}_1 \in \mathbb{R}^{D \times 4D}\) and \(\mathbf{W}_2 \in \mathbb{R}^{4D \times D}\).

The second residual addition and Layer Normalization produce updated features \(\mathbf{X}^{(2)}\): $\(\mathbf{X}^{(2)} = \operatorname{LayerNorm}\left( \mathbf{X}^{(1)} + \mathbf{F} \right) \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D}\)$

docs.title: 2.3 Progressive Token Pruning Stage
docs.text:
If a ProgressiveTokenPruning module is attached, token salience scores \(\mathbf{s}_{\text{salience}} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L}\) are evaluated over \(\mathbf{X}^{(2)}\): $\(\mathbf{s}_{\text{salience}} = \operatorname{ScoreNetwork}\left( \mathbf{X}^{(2)} \right)\)$

Given a target retention ratio \(\gamma \in (0, 1]\), the number of tokens retained is \(L' = \lfloor \gamma \cdot L \rfloor\). The top-\(L'\) token indices \(\mathcal{I}_{\text{keep}}\) are extracted via Top-\(k\): $\(\mathcal{I}_{\text{keep}} = \operatorname{TopK}\left( \mathbf{s}_{\text{salience}}, L' \right) \quad \in \{1, \dots, L\}^{B \times L'}\)$

The hidden activation sequence is gathered along the sequence dimension: $\(\mathbf{X}^{\text{pruned}} = \operatorname{Gather}\left( \mathbf{X}^{(2)}, \text{dim}=1, \text{index}=\mathcal{I}_{\text{keep}} \right) \quad \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L' \times D}\)$

If original position indices \(\mathbf{T}_{\text{idx}} \in \mathbb{N}^{B \times L}\) are tracked across layers, they are gathered identically: $\(\mathbf{T}_{\text{idx}}^{\text{new}} = \operatorname{Gather}\left( \mathbf{T}_{\text{idx}}, \text{dim}=1, \text{index}=\mathcal{I}_{\text{keep}} \right) \quad \in \mathbb{N}^{B \times L'}\)$
