docs.title: 4.1 FLOPs Computation Breakdown
docs.text:
Let \(B\) be batch size, \(L\) sequence length, \(D\) hidden dimension, \(H\) attention heads, \(d_h = D/H\), and \(\gamma\) pruning retention ratio (\(L' = \gamma L\)).

  1. Multi-Head Self-Attention (MHSA): Projections (\(\mathbf{Q}, \mathbf{K}, \mathbf{V}, \mathbf{O}\)): \(8 B L D^2\) Furthermore, Score matmul & context matmul: \(4 B H L^2 d_h = 4 B D L^2\) $\(\operatorname{FLOPs}_{\text{mhsa}} = 8 B L D^2 + 4 B D L^2\)$

  2. Position-wise Feed-Forward Network (FFN): Expansion \(D \to 4D\) and projection \(4D \to D\): \(2 \times (2 B L D (4D)) = 16 B L D^2\) $\(\operatorname{FLOPs}_{\text{ffn}} = 16 B L D^2\)$

  3. Progressive Token Pruning Stage: Salience scoring: \(2 B L D\) FLOPs. Furthermore, Top-\(k\) sorting: \(B L \log L'\) FLOPs. $\(\operatorname{FLOPs}_{\text{prune}} = 2 B L D + B L \log L'\)$

\[\text{Total Block FLOPs} = 24 B L D^2 + 4 B D L^2 + 2 B L D + B L \log L'\]

Downstream Transformer layer \(\ell+1\) operates on reduced length \(L'\), cutting its per-layer FLOPs by: $\(\Delta \text{FLOPs}_{\text{downstream}} = 4 B D (L^2 - L'^2) + 24 B (L - L') D^2 = 4 B D L^2 (1 - \gamma^2) + 24 B L D^2 (1 - \gamma)\)$

docs.title: 4.2 MACs & Memory Footprint Analysis
docs.text:
Specifically, regarding \textbf{Multiply-Accumulate Operations (MACs)},

$\(\text{Total MACs} \approx 12 B L D^2 + 2 B D L^2\)$ Specifically, regarding \textbf{Peak Activation Memory}, Furthermore, Attention Score Tensor: \(B \cdot H \cdot L \cdot L \times 2 \text{ bytes}\) Concurrently, Intermediate FFN Buffer: \(B \cdot L \cdot 4D \times 2 \text{ bytes}\) In this setting, Pruned Output Buffer: \(B \cdot L' \cdot D \times 2 \text{ bytes}\) Additionally, Memory scales as \(\mathcal{O}(B H L^2 + B L D)\).

docs.title: 4.3 Asymptotic Scalability Comparison
docs.text: Specifically, regarding \textbf{Standard Transformer Layer Stack}, \(\mathcal{O}(M \cdot L^2 D)\) compute across \(M\) layers. Furthermore, regarding \textbf{EAT Progressive Pruning Stack}, \(\mathcal{O}\left( D \sum_{\ell=1}^M L_\ell^2 \right)\) compute, where \(L_\ell = \gamma^\ell L_0\). Asymptotically bounds total attention compute to \(\mathcal{O}\left( \frac{1}{1 - \gamma^2} L_0^2 D \right)\), making deep Transformer inference up to \(3\times\) faster.

docs.title: 5. Failure Modes, Rank Collapse & Edge Cases
5.1 Ragged Tensor Memory Fragmentation
docs.text: When sequence lengths prune dynamically per sequence in a batch (\(L'_{b, 1} \neq L'_{b, 2}\)): Specifically, regarding \textbf{Batch Realignment Overhead}, standard PyTorch tensor layouts require padding all batch items to \(\max(L'_b)\), wasting VRAM and CPU cycles on padded dummy tokens. Furthermore, regarding \textbf{Memory Thrashing}, continuous reallocation of dynamic tensor shapes ([B, L', D]) causes host CUDA memory allocator fragmentation.

docs.title: 5.2 Irreversible Context Pruning & Information Erasure
docs.text: Progressive token pruning is a hard, one-way decision (\(\mathcal{I}_{\text{keep}} \subset \{1, \dots, L\}\)). Specifically, regarding \textbf{False Positive Pruning}, if a critical entity token (e.g., a rare medical term or negated verb) receives a low salience score at early layer \(\ell=2\), it is permanently dropped. Furthermore, regarding \textbf{Error Propagation}, downstream layers \(\ell > 2\) can never recover dropped tokens, causing severe semantic drift and hallucination on complex reasoning tasks.

docs.title: 5.3 Non-Differentiable Top-\(k\) Indexing
docs.text: The selection \(\operatorname{TopK}(\mathbf{s}_{\text{salience}}, L')\) is non-differentiable (\(\frac{\partial \operatorname{TopK}}{\partial \mathbf{s}} = 0\)). Gradients cannot backpropagate through token dropping choices during training without specialized Gumbel-Softmax relaxations or straight-through estimators, risking suboptimal score network training.

docs.title: 6. Hardware Acceleration Blueprint & Triton Kernel Design
docs.text: To optimize Progressive Token Pruning, EAT requires a custom Triton kernel that fuses salience scoring, Bitonic Top-\(k\) sorting, and contiguous SRAM token re-packing.

docs.title: 6.1 Triton Hardware Acceleration Pipeline Layout
docs.text:
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                           TRITON FUSED EAT PIPELINE                               |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|  1. FUSED FLASHATTENTION & LN1 + FFN + LN2 KERNEL                                 |
|     - Computes FlashAttention and LN1 + LN2 in SRAM registers.                    |
|     - Writes intermediate output X_2 [B, L, D].                                   |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|  2. TOKEN SALIENCE SCORING & BITONIC SORT KERNEL                                  |
|     - Evaluates score vector S = X_2 @ W_score [B, L].                            |
|     - Executes warp-level Bitonic Top-k sort in register file.                    |
|     - Extracts top-L' indices I_keep [B, L'].                                     |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|  3. CONTIGUOUS MEMORY RE-PACKING KERNEL                                           |
|     - Indirect load X_2[b, I_keep[b, i]] into SRAM.                               |
|     - Writes packed, contiguous output X_pruned [B, L', D] to device memory.        |
|     - Updates ragged offset array for downstream attention layers.                 |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+

docs.title: 6.2 Implementation Code Blueprint (Triton Token Packing Kernel)
docs.text:
import triton
import triton.language as tl

@triton.jit
def _eat_fused_token_prune_pack_kernel(
    X_ptr,          # Input hidden states [B, L, D]
    W_score_ptr,    # Scoring projection weights [D]
    Out_packed_ptr, # Pruned output buffer [B, L_PRUNED, D]
    Idx_out_ptr,    # Kept indices tracking buffer [B, L_PRUNED]
    stride_xb, stride_xl, stride_xd,
    stride_ob, stride_ol, stride_od,
    stride_ib, stride_il,
    L_ORIG: tl.constexpr,
    L_PRUNED: tl.constexpr,
    D: tl.constexpr
):
    batch_id = tl.program_id(axis=0)
    offs_d = tl.arange(0, D)

    # Base pointers for batch
    x_base = X_ptr + batch_id * stride_xb
    out_base = Out_packed_ptr + batch_id * stride_ob
    idx_base = Idx_out_ptr + batch_id * stride_ib

    # Evaluate Salience Score per token
    # (Simplified: in-register dot product with W_score)
    w_score = tl.load(W_score_ptr + offs_d)

    # Store scores in SRAM buffer for sorting
    # In Triton, we load token representations, dot product with w_score -> s_i
    # Perform Bitonic Top-k selection to extract L_PRUNED indices
    # Here we illustrate the indirect pack phase after top-k indices are selected

    for l_out in range(L_PRUNED):
        # Fetch target source token index from TopK selection
        source_token_idx = tl.load(idx_base + l_out * stride_il)

        # Indirect Load target token [D] from un-pruned sequence
        x_ptrs = x_base + source_token_idx * stride_xl + offs_d * stride_xd
        token_vec = tl.load(x_ptrs)

        # Store contiguous packed token vector into pruned output buffer
        out_ptrs = out_base + l_out * stride_ol + offs_d * stride_od
        tl.store(out_ptrs, token_vec)

docs.title: 6.3 Hardware Optimization Impact
docs.text:
1. Dynamic Memory Compaction: Re-packing pruned tokens into contiguous global memory arrays [B, L', D] restores full GPU SIMD vectorization for subsequent Transformer layers.
  2. Compound Downstream Speedup: Dropping sequence length from \(L_0 \to L'\) yields an immediate \(\left(\frac{L'}{L_0}\right)^2\) reduction in downstream Multi-Head Attention latency.

docs.title: 7. Next-Generation Innovations & Synthesis Opportunities
docs.text:
1. Differentiable Soft Token Merging (ToMe): Replace hard token dropping with weighted average token merging (\(X_{\text{merged}} = \mathbf{P} X\)), preserving \(100\%\) of key information while reducing token count.
  2. Feedback Memory Buffer for Dropped Tokens: Route dropped non-essential tokens into a global summary memory vector \(\mathbf{m}_{\text{summary}}\), allowing downstream layers to retrieve compressed background context.
  3. Adaptive Entropy-Guided Pruning Schedules: Dynamically select retention ratio \(\gamma_\ell\) based on attention layer entropy: preserve \(100\%\) sequence length in high-entropy layers and prune aggressively in low-entropy layers.
  4. FP8 Quantized Token Salience Scoring: Perform salience score projections \(\mathbf{s} = \mathbf{X} \mathbf{w}\) using FP8 (E4M3) operations to minimize scoring overhead.

docs.title: 4.2 MACs & Memory Footprint Analysis
docs.text:
Specifically, regarding \textbf{Multiply-Accumulate Operations (MACs)},

$\(\text{Total MACs} \approx 12 B L D^2 + 2 B D L^2\)$ Specifically, regarding \textbf{Peak Activation Memory}, Furthermore, Attention Score Tensor: \(B \cdot H \cdot L \cdot L \times 2 \text{ bytes}\) Concurrently, Intermediate FFN Buffer: \(B \cdot L \cdot 4D \times 2 \text{ bytes}\) In this setting, Pruned Output Buffer: \(B \cdot L' \cdot D \times 2 \text{ bytes}\) Additionally, Memory scales as \(\mathcal{O}(B H L^2 + B L D)\).

docs.title: 4.3 Asymptotic Scalability Comparison
docs.text: Specifically, regarding \textbf{Standard Transformer Layer Stack}, \(\mathcal{O}(M \cdot L^2 D)\) compute across \(M\) layers. Furthermore, regarding \textbf{EAT Progressive Pruning Stack}, \(\mathcal{O}\left( D \sum_{\ell=1}^M L_\ell^2 \right)\) compute, where \(L_\ell = \gamma^\ell L_0\). Asymptotically bounds total attention compute to \(\mathcal{O}\left( \frac{1}{1 - \gamma^2} L_0^2 D \right)\), making deep Transformer inference up to \(3\times\) faster.

docs.title: 5. Failure Modes, Rank Collapse & Edge Cases
5.1 Ragged Tensor Memory Fragmentation
docs.text: When sequence lengths prune dynamically per sequence in a batch (\(L'_{b, 1} \neq L'_{b, 2}\)): Specifically, regarding \textbf{Batch Realignment Overhead}, standard PyTorch tensor layouts require padding all batch items to \(\max(L'_b)\), wasting VRAM and CPU cycles on padded dummy tokens. Furthermore, regarding \textbf{Memory Thrashing}, continuous reallocation of dynamic tensor shapes ([B, L', D]) causes host CUDA memory allocator fragmentation.

docs.title: 5.2 Irreversible Context Pruning & Information Erasure
docs.text: Progressive token pruning is a hard, one-way decision (\(\mathcal{I}_{\text{keep}} \subset \{1, \dots, L\}\)). Specifically, regarding \textbf{False Positive Pruning}, if a critical entity token (e.g., a rare medical term or negated verb) receives a low salience score at early layer \(\ell=2\), it is permanently dropped. Furthermore, regarding \textbf{Error Propagation}, downstream layers \(\ell > 2\) can never recover dropped tokens, causing severe semantic drift and hallucination on complex reasoning tasks.

docs.title: 5.3 Non-Differentiable Top-\(k\) Indexing
docs.text: The selection \(\operatorname{TopK}(\mathbf{s}_{\text{salience}}, L')\) is non-differentiable (\(\frac{\partial \operatorname{TopK}}{\partial \mathbf{s}} = 0\)). Gradients cannot backpropagate through token dropping choices during training without specialized Gumbel-Softmax relaxations or straight-through estimators, risking suboptimal score network training.

docs.title: 6. Hardware Acceleration Blueprint & Triton Kernel Design
docs.text: To optimize Progressive Token Pruning, EAT requires a custom Triton kernel that fuses salience scoring, Bitonic Top-\(k\) sorting, and contiguous SRAM token re-packing.

docs.title: 6.1 Triton Hardware Acceleration Pipeline Layout
docs.text:
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                           TRITON FUSED EAT PIPELINE                               |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|  1. FUSED FLASHATTENTION & LN1 + FFN + LN2 KERNEL                                 |
|     - Computes FlashAttention and LN1 + LN2 in SRAM registers.                    |
|     - Writes intermediate output X_2 [B, L, D].                                   |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|  2. TOKEN SALIENCE SCORING & BITONIC SORT KERNEL                                  |
|     - Evaluates score vector S = X_2 @ W_score [B, L].                            |
|     - Executes warp-level Bitonic Top-k sort in register file.                    |
|     - Extracts top-L' indices I_keep [B, L'].                                     |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|  3. CONTIGUOUS MEMORY RE-PACKING KERNEL                                           |
|     - Indirect load X_2[b, I_keep[b, i]] into SRAM.                               |
|     - Writes packed, contiguous output X_pruned [B, L', D] to device memory.        |
|     - Updates ragged offset array for downstream attention layers.                 |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+

docs.title: 6.2 Implementation Code Blueprint (Triton Token Packing Kernel)
docs.text:
import triton
import triton.language as tl

@triton.jit
def _eat_fused_token_prune_pack_kernel(
    X_ptr,          # Input hidden states [B, L, D]
    W_score_ptr,    # Scoring projection weights [D]
    Out_packed_ptr, # Pruned output buffer [B, L_PRUNED, D]
    Idx_out_ptr,    # Kept indices tracking buffer [B, L_PRUNED]
    stride_xb, stride_xl, stride_xd,
    stride_ob, stride_ol, stride_od,
    stride_ib, stride_il,
    L_ORIG: tl.constexpr,
    L_PRUNED: tl.constexpr,
    D: tl.constexpr
):
    batch_id = tl.program_id(axis=0)
    offs_d = tl.arange(0, D)

    # Base pointers for batch
    x_base = X_ptr + batch_id * stride_xb
    out_base = Out_packed_ptr + batch_id * stride_ob
    idx_base = Idx_out_ptr + batch_id * stride_ib

    # Evaluate Salience Score per token
    # (Simplified: in-register dot product with W_score)
    w_score = tl.load(W_score_ptr + offs_d)

    # Store scores in SRAM buffer for sorting
    # In Triton, we load token representations, dot product with w_score -> s_i
    # Perform Bitonic Top-k selection to extract L_PRUNED indices
    # Here we illustrate the indirect pack phase after top-k indices are selected

    for l_out in range(L_PRUNED):
        # Fetch target source token index from TopK selection
        source_token_idx = tl.load(idx_base + l_out * stride_il)

        # Indirect Load target token [D] from un-pruned sequence
        x_ptrs = x_base + source_token_idx * stride_xl + offs_d * stride_xd
        token_vec = tl.load(x_ptrs)

        # Store contiguous packed token vector into pruned output buffer
        out_ptrs = out_base + l_out * stride_ol + offs_d * stride_od
        tl.store(out_ptrs, token_vec)

docs.title: 6.3 Hardware Optimization Impact
docs.text:
1. Dynamic Memory Compaction: Re-packing pruned tokens into contiguous global memory arrays [B, L', D] restores full GPU SIMD vectorization for subsequent Transformer layers.
  2. Compound Downstream Speedup: Dropping sequence length from \(L_0 \to L'\) yields an immediate \(\left(\frac{L'}{L_0}\right)^2\) reduction in downstream Multi-Head Attention latency.

docs.title: 7. Next-Generation Innovations & Synthesis Opportunities
docs.text:
1. Differentiable Soft Token Merging (ToMe): Replace hard token dropping with weighted average token merging (\(X_{\text{merged}} = \mathbf{P} X\)), preserving \(100\%\) of key information while reducing token count.
  2. Feedback Memory Buffer for Dropped Tokens: Route dropped non-essential tokens into a global summary memory vector \(\mathbf{m}_{\text{summary}}\), allowing downstream layers to retrieve compressed background context.
  3. Adaptive Entropy-Guided Pruning Schedules: Dynamically select retention ratio \(\gamma_\ell\) based on attention layer entropy: preserve \(100\%\) sequence length in high-entropy layers and prune aggressively in low-entropy layers.
  4. FP8 Quantized Token Salience Scoring: Perform salience score projections \(\mathbf{s} = \mathbf{X} \mathbf{w}\) using FP8 (E4M3) operations to minimize scoring overhead.

docs.title: Expert Choice Mixture-of-Experts (EC-MoE) Attention Block
docs.text: Family: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) & Sparsely-Gated Attentions · NeuralOps Registry ID: expert_choice_moe

docs.title: Executive Abstract
docs.text:
Expert Choice MoE (Zhou et al., 2022) inverts traditional token-choice routing: instead of tokens selecting top-k experts, each expert independently selects its top-C tokens. This guarantees perfect load balance across experts and eliminates auxiliary load-balancing losses.

In NeuralOps, expert_choice_moe is integrated into the universal attention dispatch table, featuring full support for the 3-level fallback hierarchy, automatic shape validation, and end-to-end autograd backwards passes.

docs.title: Mathematical Formulation
docs.text:
The core operator computation is defined as:

\[ \text{Top-C tokens chosen by each expert}: \; \mathcal{T}_e = \arg\text{top-C}_{t} (X W_g)_{t, e} \]

During execution, inputs \(Q, K, V\) are projected to dimension \(d\). In the causal configuration, lower-triangular masking ensures that tokens only attend to past and current time-steps, preserving autoregressive invariants.

docs.text:
Input Tokens (B, T, D)

     ├───► Linear Projection (Q, K, V)
     │         │

     │         │
     │         ▼
     └────► Scaled Output & Residual Add (B, T, D)

docs.title: Factorised Matrix State Attention: Recurrent Associative Matrix Memory with Low-Rank Bilinear Projections
1. Abstract & Theoretical Motivation
docs.text: Factorised Matrix State Attention (FactorisedMatrixState, registered as factorised_matrix_state) introduces an associative matrix memory recurrence mechanism coupled with factorized low-rank output projections (\(W = L R^\top\)). Standard Transformer Multi-Head Attention requires quadratic time and memory complexity \(\mathcal{O}(N^2)\) to store and compute pairwise attention scores. Factorised Matrix State replaces explicit token pairwise comparisons with a recurrent associative state matrix \(S_t \in \mathbb{R}^{D \times D}\) that accumulates unnormalized rank-1 token outer products \(x_t x_t^\top\) online. Contextualized token representations \(u_t = S_t x_t\) are evaluated in \(\mathcal{O}(N \cdot D^2)\) time, after which a bilinear low-rank matrix projection \((U L) R^\top\) transforms features into target dimensions. This structure offers \(\mathcal{O}(N)\) linear sequence complexity and \(\mathcal{O}(D^2)\) state memory overhead.

docs.title: 2. Mathematical Derivations & Formulations
docs.text: Let \(X = [x_1, x_2, \dots, x_N] \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times D}\) denote input token activations under valid sequence mask \(M \in \{0, 1\}^{B \times N \times 1}\): $\(\tilde{x}_t = x_t \odot M_t \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times D}\)$

docs.title: 1. Recurrent Associative Matrix State Accumulation
docs.text: The sequence state \(S_t \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times D \times D}\) is initialized to zero (\(S_0 = \mathbf{0}_{D \times D}\)). At timestep \(t \in \{1, \dots, N\}\), the state updates via rank-1 outer product accumulation: $\(S_t = S_{t-1} + \tilde{x}_t \tilde{x}_t^\top = \sum_{\tau=1}^t \tilde{x}_\tau \tilde{x}_\tau^\top \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times D \times D}\)$

docs.title: 2. Fast Weight Associative Memory Retrieval
docs.text: The unprojected contextualized token representation \(u_t \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times D}\) is retrieved by multiplying the state matrix \(S_t\) with input vector \(\tilde{x}_t\): $\(u_t = S_t \tilde{x}_t = \left( \sum_{\tau=1}^t \tilde{x}_\tau \tilde{x}_\tau^\top \right) \tilde{x}_t = \sum_{\tau=1}^t \tilde{x}_\tau (\tilde{x}_\tau^\top \tilde{x}_t) \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times D}\)$ Stacking \(u_t\) across all timesteps produces intermediate sequence activation tensor \(U = [u_1, \dots, u_N] \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times D}\).

docs.title: 3. Factorized Low-Rank Bilinear Output Projection
docs.text: Rather than multiplying \(U\) by a full-rank dense output weight \(W \in \mathbb{R}^{D \times D}\), output features are projected using low-rank factorized parameters \(L, R \in \mathbb{R}^{D \times r}\) (\(r \ll D\)): $\(O_{\text{raw}} = (U L) R^\top \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times D}\)$ $\(O = O_{\text{raw}} \odot M \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times D}\)$

docs.title: 3. Tensor Execution Flow & Dimensional Shape Tracing
docs.text:
The step-by-step tensor operations across Factorised Matrix State Attention are traced below:

  1. Input Tensor & Mask Reduction: \(X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times D}\) Furthermore, Mask resolution: \(M \in \{0, 1\}^{B \times N \times 1}\) Concurrently, Masked input: \(\tilde{X} = X \odot M \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times D}\)

  2. Recurrent Loop Execution (\(t = 1 \dots N\)): Extract slice: \(\tilde{x}_t = \tilde{X}[:, t, :] \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times D}\) Furthermore, Outer product: \(P_t = \tilde{x}_t.\text{unsqueeze}(-1) \cdot \tilde{x}_t.\text{unsqueeze}(1) \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times D \times D}\) Concurrently, State matrix update: \(S_t = S_{t-1} + P_t \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times D \times D}\) In this setting, Memory lookup: \(u_t = (S_t \cdot \tilde{x}_t.\text{unsqueeze}(-1)).\text{squeeze}(-1) \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times D}\)

  3. Sequence Stacking: \(U = \text{Stack}([u_1, \dots, u_N], \text{dim}=1) \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times D}\)

  4. Low-Rank Factorized Output Transformation: Down-projection: \(U_L = U L \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times r}\) (using \(L \in [D, r]\)) Furthermore, Up-projection: \(O_{\text{raw}} = U_L R^\top \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times D}\) (using \(R \in [D, r]\)) Concurrently, Final Masking: \(O = O_{\text{raw}} \odot M \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times D}\)

docs.title: 4. Analytical Complexity Profiling
docs.text: Specifically, regarding \textbf{FLOPs Computation}, Furthermore, Outer Product & State Update (\(x_t x_t^\top\)): \(N \times 2 B D^2 = 2 B N D^2\) FLOPs Concurrently, State Retrieval (\(S_t x_t\)): \(N \times 2 B D^2 = 2 B N D^2\) FLOPs In this setting, Low-Rank Output Down-Projection (\(U L\)): \(2 B N D r\) FLOPs Additionally, Low-Rank Output Up-Projection (\(U_L R^\top\)): \(2 B N r D\) FLOPs Moreover, Total Module FLOPs: \(4 B N D^2 + 4 B N D r\) (Strictly \(\mathcal{O}(N)\) in sequence length) From an analytical standpoint, regarding \textbf{MAC Operations}, In terms of operational dynamics, Outer Product & Retrieval: \(2 B N D^2\) MACs Specifically, Factorized Projection: \(2 B N D r\) MACs Furthermore, regarding \textbf{Memory Footprint & State Cache}, Concurrently, Model Parameters: \(2 \times D \times r = 2 r D\) (vs standard \(4 D^2\) MHA parameters). For \(D=768, r=32\), factor parameters \(= 49,152\) (\(48\times\) compression). In this setting, Recurrent Memory State: \(S_t \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times D \times D}\) (requiring \(B D^2\) float elements).

docs.title: 5. Architectural Bottlenecks, Rank Collapse & Failure Modes
docs.text:
Specifically, regarding \textbf{Sequential Recurrent Execution Bottleneck},

Iterating over sequence length \(N\) in a Python for t in range(N): loop launches \(N\) sequential GPU kernels, introducing massive PyTorch driver overhead and GPU underutilization. Specifically, regarding \textbf{Unbounded Recurrent State Accumulation},

State matrix \(S_t = \sum_{\tau=1}^t x_\tau x_\tau^\top\) accumulates unnormalized outer products. For long sequence lengths (\(N \gg 1000\)), entries in \(S_t\) grow monotonically, causing floating-point overflow or gradient explosion in FP16 training. Specifically, regarding \textbf{Identity Kernel Feature Map Bottleneck},

Using identity mapping \(\phi(x) = x\) without non-linear feature maps (like ELU or Softmax) limits associative capacity to degree-2 polynomial feature interactions.

docs.title: 6. Hardware Acceleration Blueprint & Triton Optimization Strategies
docs.text:
Specifically, regarding \textbf{Fused Chunk-Wise Parallel Recurrence Triton Kernel},

Rewrite sequential recurrence into a parallel chunk-wise scan Triton kernel. Compute intra-chunk associative states in SRAM and combine inter-chunk states via parallel prefix-sum scans. Specifically, regarding \textbf{Decayed Matrix Memory State Update},

Introduce a learnable decay parameter \(\gamma \in (0, 1)\) to bound memory state accumulation: \(S_t = \gamma S_{t-1} + x_t x_t^\top\). This prevents state norm explosion for infinite sequence lengths. Specifically, regarding \textbf{Symmetric Factor Initialization},

Initialize factors \(L, R\) symmetrically from thin SVD of pretrained projection weights: \(L \leftarrow \bar{U}_{:, :r} \Sigma_{:r}^{1/2}\), \(R \leftarrow \bar{V}_{:r, :}^\top \Sigma_{:r}^{1/2}\), enabling zero-shot initialization from standard MHA layers.

docs.title: FlashAttention-3: Fast and Memory-Efficient Exact Attention with Asynchronous Hardware Overlap
1. Executive Abstract & Architectural Motivation
docs.text:
Standard Multi-Head Self-Attention (MHSA) in Transformer architectures requires materializing the full intermediate attention matrix \(P = \text{Softmax}(Q K^T / \sqrt{d_h}) \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times L \times L}\) in High Bandwidth Memory (HBM). This results in quadratic IO bandwidth overhead \(\mathcal{O}(L^2)\), making memory bandwidth—rather than floating-point computation—the primary bottleneck on modern GPU accelerators.

FlashAttention-3 advances exact attention acceleration on NVIDIA Hopper GPUs through three architectural optimizations: 1. Asynchronous Hardware Overlap via Tensor Memory Accelerator (TMA): Uses hardware TMA units to asynchronously load \(Q, K, V\) tiles from HBM directly into shared memory (SRAM), overlapping memory transfers with Tensor Core matrix multiplications. 2. Warp Specialization & Producer-Consumer Pipelines: Partitions CUDA warps into dedicated producers (managing TMA loads) and consumers (executing GEMM and online Softmax reductions), eliminating warp synchronization stalls. 3. Low-Precision FP8 (E4M3) Acceleration: Casts \(Q, K, V\) activations to 8-bit floating point format (torch.float8_e4m3fn), doubling Tensor Core compute throughput and halving HBM memory access bandwidth.

docs.title: 2.1 Standard Attention vs. Tiled Online Softmax
docs.text:
Standard scaled dot-product attention evaluates:

\[S = \frac{Q K^T}{\sqrt{d_h}} + M \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times L \times L}, \quad P = \text{Softmax}(S), \quad O = P V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times H \cdot d_h}\]

FlashAttention-3 avoids HBM allocation for \(S\) and \(P\) by tiling \(Q, K, V\) into SRAM blocks of size \(B_r \times d_h\) and \(B_c \times d_h\). For query tile \(Q_i \in \mathbb{R}^{B_r \times d_h}\) and key-value tile \((K_j, V_j) \in \mathbb{R}^{B_c \times d_h}\), the online Softmax state is updated incrementally:

\[S_{i, j} = \frac{Q_i K_j^T}{\sqrt{d_h}} \in \mathbb{R}^{B_r \times B_c}\] \[m_i^{(j)} = \max\left( m_i^{(j-1)}, \; \text{rowmax}(S_{i, j}) \right) \in \mathbb{R}^{B_r}\] \[\tilde{P}_{i, j} = \exp\left( S_{i, j} - m_i^{(j)} \right) \in \mathbb{R}^{B_r \times B_c}\] \[l_i^{(j)} = \exp\left( m_i^{(j-1)} - m_i^{(j)} \right) \odot l_i^{(j-1)} + \text{rowsum}(\tilde{P}_{i, j}) \in \mathbb{R}^{B_r}\]

The unnormalized context output \(O_i^{(j)} \in \mathbb{R}^{B_r \times d_h}\) is accumulated into SRAM registers:

\[O_i^{(j)} = \operatorname{diag}\left( \exp\left( m_i^{(j-1)} - m_i^{(j)} \right) \right) O_i^{(j-1)} + \tilde{P}_{i, j} V_j\]

Upon completing sequence iteration over \(j \in \{1, \dots, \lceil L / B_c \rceil\}\), final normalized output \(O_i\) is computed:

\[O_i = \operatorname{diag}\left( l_i^{(\text{final})} \right)^{-1} O_i^{(\text{final})} \in \mathbb{R}^{B_r \times d_h}\]

docs.title: 2.2 Asynchronous TMA Overlap & FP8 Precision Casting
docs.text:
On Hopper GPUs, TMA hardware loads \(K_{j+1}, V_{j+1}\) from HBM to SRAM asynchronously in parallel with GEMM computation \(Q_i K_j^T\) on Tensor Cores.

When FP8 precision mode is enabled (use_fp8=True), inputs are cast to FP8 E4M3 format:

\[Q_{\text{fp8}} = \text{cast}_{\text{fp8\_e4m3}}(Q), \quad K_{\text{fp8}} = \text{cast}_{\text{fp8\_e4m3}}(K), \quad V_{\text{fp8}} = \text{cast}_{\text{fp8\_e4m3}}(V)\]

FlashAttention-3 executes exact FP8 GEMM on Hopper WGMMA (Warpgroup Matrix Multiply Accumulate) instructions:

\[O_{\text{fp8}} = \text{FlashAttn3}_{\text{Hopper}}\left( Q_{\text{fp8}}, K_{\text{fp8}}, V_{\text{fp8}} \right)\] \[\text{Output} = \text{cast}_{\text{dtype}}\left( O_{\text{fp8}} \right) W_{\text{out}} + b_{\text{out}} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D}\]

docs.title: 4.1 Floating Point Operations (FLOPs)
docs.text:
Let \(B\) be batch size, \(L\) sequence length, \(D\) model dimension, \(H\) head count, and \(d_h = D/H\) head dimension.

  1. Linear Q, K, V Projections: $\(\text{FLOPs}_{\text{proj}} = 3 \times 2 B L D^2 = 6 B L D^2\)$

  2. FlashAttention-3 Kernel Core: Query-Key score matmul: \(2 B H L^2 d_h = 2 B L^2 D\) Furthermore, Softmax online scaling & Value contraction: \(2 B H L^2 d_h = 2 B L^2 D\) $\(\text{FLOPs}_{\text{core}} = 4 B L^2 D\)$

  3. Output Projection: $\(\text{FLOPs}_{\text{out}} = 2 B L D^2\)$

\[\text{FLOPs}_{\text{total}} = 8 B L D^2 + 4 B L^2 D\]

(Note: Under FP8 mode, Tensor Core throughput for \(\text{FLOPs}_{\text{core}}\) increases by \(2\times\).)

docs.title: 4.2 MACs & Memory Footprint Analysis
docs.text:
Specifically, regarding \textbf{Multiply-Accumulate Operations (MACs)},

$\(\text{Total MACs} = 4 B L D^2 + 2 B L^2 D\)$ Specifically, regarding \textbf{Standard Softmax Attention HBM IO}, \(\mathcal{O}(B H L^2 + B L D)\) Furthermore, regarding \textbf{FlashAttention-3 HBM IO}, \(\mathcal{O}\left(B L D + \frac{B H L^2 d_h^2}{M_{\text{SRAM}}}\right)\) where \(M_{\text{SRAM}}\) is GPU shared memory capacity (\(\approx 228 \text{ KB}\) on Hopper H100). Concurrently, regarding \textbf{Parameter Footprint}, \(\Theta = 4 D^2\).

docs.title: 4.3 Asymptotic Scalability Comparison
docs.text: Specifically, regarding \textbf{Standard Dense Attention}, \(\mathcal{O}(L^2 D)\) compute, \(\mathcal{O}(L^2 H)\) DRAM IO scaling. Furthermore, regarding \textbf{FlashAttention-3 Engine}, \(\mathcal{O}(L^2 D)\) compute, \(\mathcal{O}(L D)\) IO scaling, achieving \(3\times\) speedup over FlashAttention-2 on Hopper GPUs.

docs.title: 5. Failure Modes, Rank Collapse & Edge Cases
5.1 Hardware Compatibility & Host Fallback
docs.text: At the architectural level, the underlying operational mechanism reveals that flashAttention-3 TMA and WGMMA instructions strictly require NVIDIA Hopper architecture (compute capability sm_90a). Invoking flash_attn_func on Ampere (sm_80) or Ada Lovelace (sm_89) GPUs triggers runtime errors. To systematically mitigate this constraint, the framework enforces an optimization protocol such that implement explicit hardware detection fallbacks to PyTorch SDPA (F.scaled_dot_product_attention).

docs.title: 5.2 FP8 Dynamic Range Underflow & Overflow
docs.text: At the architectural level, the underlying operational mechanism reveals that fP8 E4M3 has only 3 mantissa bits and a maximum representable value of 448. Unscaled attention logits \(Q K^T / \sqrt{d_h}\) exceeding 448 immediately saturate to NaN or infinity. To systematically mitigate this constraint, the framework enforces an optimization protocol such that deploy per-tensor dynamic scaling factors \(S_Q, S_K, S_V\) prior to FP8 quantization: \(Q_{\text{fp8}} = \text{cast}(Q \cdot S_Q)\).

docs.title: 6.1 Triton Strategy 1: TMA Asynchronous Memory Pipeline
docs.text:
Standard CUDA implementations use cp.async instructions, which still require warp register intervention.

Triton Optimization: Configure Triton TMA descriptors for 2D/3D tensor memory transfers. Furthermore, Issue non-blocking TMA load requests for key-value tiles \(K_{j+1}, V_{j+1}\) into shared memory pipelines while Tensor Cores execute GEMM on tile \(j\).

docs.title: 6.2 Triton Strategy 2: Warp-Specialized Producer-Consumer Pipeline
docs.text: Partition threadblock warps into 1 Producer warp and 3 Consumer warps. Furthermore, The Producer warp manages TMA memory arrival barriers (mbarrier). Concurrently, Consumer warps execute WGMMA matrix instructions on Tensor Cores continuously, eliminating warp synchronization latency.

docs.title: 7. Next-Generation Innovations & Synthesis Opportunities
docs.text:
1. FP4 Quantized KV-Cache Tiling: Integrate 4-bit NormalFloat (NF4) quantization into TMA load pipelines, quadrupling SRAM key-value tile capacities (\(B_c \to 256\)).
  2. Block-Sparse TMA Mask Pruning: Fuse block-sparse indexing tables into TMA hardware descriptor loads, fetching only non-zero attention blocks directly from HBM.
  3. Speculative Decoding Parallel Flash-3 Scan: Execute multi-token speculative draft verify passes in a single fused Hopper WGMMA GEMM kernel call.
  4. SVD Low-Rank Projection Fusion: Fuse input low-rank SVD projections directly into the FlashAttention-3 TMA load step, reducing global DRAM read passes by \(2\times\).

docs.title: FlashAttention-3 FP8: Low-Precision 8-Bit Float Transformer Attention for Hopper Architectures
1. Executive Abstract & Architectural Motivation
docs.text:
Standard Multi-Head Self-Attention (MHSA) in Transformer models operating under FP16 or BF16 precision consumes significant High Bandwidth Memory (HBM) activation storage and memory bandwidth. Intermediate attention score materialization requires \(\mathcal{O}(L^2)\) space, creating memory bandwidth bottlenecks on modern GPU accelerators.

FlashAttention-3 FP8 combines exact tiled attention algorithms with hardware-accelerated 8-bit floating point precision (E4M3 format) for NVIDIA Hopper GPUs: 1. FP8 Quantization Protocol: Activations \(Q, K, V\) are cast to 8-bit floating-point format (torch.float8_e4m3fn), halving memory bandwidth consumption and SRAM-HBM data transfer volume. 2. 2x Tensor Core Throughput Acceleration: Utilizes Hopper WGMMA (Warpgroup Matrix Multiply Accumulate) FP8 instructions, achieving up to \(2\times\) higher matrix multiplication TFLOPs over FP16. 3. IO-Optimal Tiled Memory Reduction: Integrates online softmax reduction to keep intermediate attention logits inside GPU shared memory (SRAM), maintaining exact attention output without HBM logit allocation.

docs.title: 2.1 FP8 E4M3 Precision Quantization
docs.text:
Input hidden activations \(X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D}\) are projected to query, key, and value tensors \(Q, K, V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times H \times d_h}\) in base precision (FP16/BF16).

Prior to attention core execution, tensors are cast to FP8 E4M3 format (torch.float8_e4m3fn), characterized by 1 sign bit, 4 exponent bits, and 3 mantissa bits:

\[Q_{\text{fp8}} = \text{cast}_{\text{fp8\_e4m3}}(Q) \in \mathbb{F}_{p8}^{B \times L \times H \times d_h}\] \[K_{\text{fp8}} = \text{cast}_{\text{fp8\_e4m3}}(K) \in \mathbb{F}_{p8}^{B \times L \times H \times d_h}\] \[V_{\text{fp8}} = \text{cast}_{\text{fp8\_e4m3}}(V) \in \mathbb{F}_{p8}^{B \times L \times H \times d_h}\]

docs.title: 2.2 Exact Tiled Memory Reduction in FP8
docs.text:
Query, key, and value tensors are partitioned into SRAM blocks \(B_r \times d_h\) and \(B_c \times d_h\). For query block \(Q_{\text{fp8}, i}\) and key-value block \((K_{\text{fp8}, j}, V_{\text{fp8}, j})\), WGMMA FP8 Tensor Core instructions evaluate dot products:

\[S_{i, j} = \frac{Q_{\text{fp8}, i} K_{\text{fp8}, j}^T}{\sqrt{d_h}} \in \mathbb{R}^{B_r \times B_c}\]

Online Softmax statistics \(m_i^{(j)}\) (maximum tracking) and \(l_i^{(j)}\) (sum tracking) update in SRAM registers:

\[m_i^{(j)} = \max\left( m_i^{(j-1)}, \; \text{rowmax}(S_{i, j}) \right)\] \[\tilde{P}_{i, j} = \exp\left( S_{i, j} - m_i^{(j)} \right)\] \[l_i^{(j)} = \exp\left( m_i^{(j-1)} - m_i^{(j)} \right) \odot l_i^{(j-1)} + \text{rowsum}(\tilde{P}_{i, j})\]

The unnormalized context output is updated:

\[O_i^{(j)} = \operatorname{diag}\left( \exp\left( m_i^{(j-1)} - m_i^{(j)} \right) \right) O_i^{(j-1)} + \tilde{P}_{i, j} V_{\text{fp8}, j}\]

Upon sequence loop completion, output \(O_i\) is normalized and cast back to base precision:

\[O_i = \text{cast}_{\text{dtype}}\left( \operatorname{diag}\left( l_i^{(\text{final})} \right)^{-1} O_i^{(\text{final})} \right) \in \mathbb{R}^{B_r \times d_h}\]

docs.title: 2.3 Output Projection
docs.text:
Assembled context representations \(O \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times H \cdot d_h}\) are projected through output linear layer \(W_{\text{out}}\):

\[Y = O W_{\text{out}} + b_{\text{out}} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D}\]

docs.title: 4.1 FLOPs Computation Breakdown
docs.text:
Let \(B\) be batch size, \(L\) sequence length, \(D\) model dimension, \(H\) head count, and \(d_h = D/H\) head dimension.

  1. Linear Projections (\(Q, K, V, O\)): $\(\text{FLOPs}_{\text{proj}} = 4 \times 2 B L D^2 = 8 B L D^2\)$
  2. FlashAttention-3 FP8 Kernel Core: Query-Key score matmul: \(2 B H L^2 d_h = 2 B L^2 D\) Furthermore, Softmax online scaling & Value contraction: \(2 B H L^2 d_h = 2 B L^2 D\) $\(\text{FLOPs}_{\text{core\_fp8}} = 4 B L^2 D \quad (\text{executed at } 2\times \text{ Tensor Core throughput})\)$

Total FLOP Count:

\[\text{FLOPs}_{\text{total}} = 8 B L D^2 + 4 B L^2 D\]

docs.title: 4.2 MACs & Memory Footprint Analysis
docs.text:
Specifically, regarding \textbf{Multiply-Accumulate Operations (MACs)},

$\(\text{Total MACs} = 4 B L D^2 + 2 B L^2 D\)$ Specifically, regarding \textbf{SRAM-HBM Memory Traffic}, 8-bit precision halves \(Q, K, V\) data movement volume from \(2 \text{ bytes/element}\) (FP16/BF16) to \(1 \text{ byte/element}\) (FP8). Furthermore, regarding \textbf{HBM Activation IO Complexity}, \(\mathcal{O}\left(B L D + \frac{B H L^2 d_h^2}{M_{\text{SRAM}}}\right)\). Concurrently, regarding \textbf{Parameter Footprint}, \(\Theta = 4 D^2\).

docs.title: 4.3 Asymptotic Scalability Comparison
docs.text: Specifically, regarding \textbf{Standard Dense FP16 Attention}, \(\mathcal{O}(L^2 D)\) compute, \(\mathcal{O}(L^2 H)\) DRAM IO scaling. Furthermore, regarding \textbf{FlashAttention-3 FP8 Engine}, \(\mathcal{O}(L^2 D)\) compute (at \(2\times\) Tensor Core speed), \(\mathcal{O}(L D)\) IO scaling (at \(50\%\) reduced byte volume), achieving \(4\times\) overall throughput gain over FP16 FlashAttention-2.

docs.title: 5. Architectural Bottlenecks, Rank Collapse & Edge Cases
5.1 Dynamic Range Clipping in E4M3 FP8 Format
docs.text: At the architectural level, the underlying operational mechanism reveals that the E4M3 format supports a maximum finite value of 448. Unscaled attention logits \(Q K^T / \sqrt{d_h}\) exceeding 448 overflow to NaN during kernel execution. To systematically mitigate this constraint, the framework enforces an optimization protocol such that apply dynamic pre-scaling factors \(S_Q, S_K\) before casting: \(Q_{\text{fp8}} = \text{cast}(Q \cdot S_Q)\).

docs.title: 5.2 Hardware Requirement Bottleneck
docs.text: At the architectural level, the underlying operational mechanism reveals that fP8 WGMMA hardware instructions are strictly supported on NVIDIA Hopper GPUs (sm_90a). Invoking FP8 kernels on older architectures causes immediate CUDA illegal instruction errors. To systematically mitigate this constraint, the framework enforces an optimization protocol such that implement automated fallback to PyTorch SDPA (F.scaled_dot_product_attention).

docs.title: 6. Hardware Acceleration Blueprint & Triton Optimization Strategies
6.1 Triton Strategy 1: Vectorized FP8 Quantization Kernel
docs.text: Implement a custom Triton kernel for FP8 quantization: load FP16/BF16 activations into SRAM, evaluate per-channel maximums, scale by \(S_Q\), and cast to torch.float8_e4m3fn using vectorized 16-byte packed writes.

docs.title: 6.2 Triton Strategy 2: Hopper WGMMA FP8 Tensor Core Pipeline
docs.text: Issue native FP8 WGMMA matrix instructions on Consumer warps, achieving up to \(2\times\) higher TFLOP execution speeds over FP16 Tensor Cores. Furthermore, Use TMA asynchronous load engines to prefetch FP8 key-value tiles into shared memory pipelines without warp blocking.

docs.title: 7. Next-Generation Innovations & Synthesis Opportunities
docs.text:
1. FP4 Quantized KV-Cache Integration: Quantize key-value matrices down to FP4 (E2M1) format while retaining FP8 for query vectors, achieving \(4\times\) memory bandwidth savings.
  2. Block-Sparse TMA Mask Pruning: Fuse block-sparse indexing tables into TMA hardware descriptor loads, fetching only non-zero attention blocks directly from HBM in FP8 format.
  3. Structured SVD Projection FP8 Fusion: Fuse input SVD low-rank down/up projections into the FP8 TMA prefetch kernel, executing low-rank projection and FP8 casting in a single SRAM sweep.
  4. Per-Head Dynamic FP8 Scale Calibration: Continuously update per-head scale factors \(S_{Q, h}, S_{K, h}\) online during training to prevent E4M3 saturation on outlier activations.

docs.title: Full Attention: Standard Multi-Head Scaled Dot-Product Attention Architecture
1. Executive Abstract & Architectural Motivation
docs.text:
Full Multi-Head Attention (MHA), introduced by Vaswani et al. (2017), forms the core mathematical foundation of modern Transformer architectures. It operates by partitioning the hidden representation space of dimension \(D\) into \(H\) parallel subspaces (heads) of dimension \(d_k = D / H\). For every head, input sequences are projected into Query (\(Q\)), Key (\(K\)), and Value (\(V\)) representations. Pairwise token interactions are computed via scaled inner products, yielding dynamic routing matrices that aggregate contextual information across all positions.

While standard MHA provides universal expressivity and unconstrained dense pairwise coupling between sequence elements, its computational and memory footprints scale quadratically with sequence length \(N\) (\(\mathcal{O}(N^2)\)). In high-throughput deployment settings, storing key and value projections for every query head during autoregressive decoding imposes extreme memory bandwidth bottlenecks (KV cache saturation). Nonetheless, Full MHA serves as the foundational gold-standard target against which all linear, low-rank, compressed, and grouped-query approximations are measured.

docs.title: 2. Mathematical Formulations & Derivations
docs.text: Let \(X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times D}\) represent the input activation batch, where \(B\) is batch size, \(N\) is sequence length, and \(D\) is model dimension. Let \(H\) be the number of attention heads and \(d_k = D / H\) the dimension per head.

docs.title: Subspace Linear Projections:
docs.text:
Input activations are mapped into head-partitioned spaces using learned parameters \(W_Q, W_K, W_V \in \mathbb{R}^{D \times D}\):

\[ Q = X W_Q \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times D}, \quad K = X W_K \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times D}, \quad V = X W_V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times D} \]

Reshaping and transposing \(Q, K, V\) into multi-head layouts:

[ Q_h = Q[:, :, h \cdot d_k : (h+1) d_k] \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times d_k}, \quad \forall h \in {1, \dots, H} ] [ Q \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times N \times d_k}, \quad K \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times N \times d_k}, \quad V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times N \times d_k} ]

docs.title: Scaled Pairwise Inner Product & Softmax Routing:
docs.text:
Raw attention affinity scores \(S \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times N \times N}\) are derived by computing scaled dot-products:

\[ S_{b, h, i, j} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{d_k}} \sum_{m=1}^{d_k} Q_{b, h, i, m} \cdot K_{b, h, j, m} \]

Additive attention mask \(M \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times 1 \times N \times N}\) (or broadcastable variant) is integrated to enforce causality or padding constraints:

\[ \widehat{S}_{b, h, i, j} = S_{b, h, i, j} + M_{b, 1, i, j} \]

Applying row-wise Softmax over key sequence dimension \(j\):

\[ A_{b, h, i, j} = \text{Softmax}_j (\widehat{S}_{b, h, i, j}) = \frac{\exp(\widehat{S}_{b, h, i, j})}{\sum_{l=1}^N \exp(\widehat{S}_{b, h, i, l})} \]

Dropout with probability \(p_{\text{drop}}\) and optional head mask \(H_{\text{mask}}\) scale the attention probabilities:

\[ \overline{A} = \text{Dropout}(A, p_{\text{drop}}) \odot H_{\text{mask}} \]

docs.title: Contextual Value Aggregation & Output Projection:
docs.text:
Values \(V\) are aggregated across sequence positions according to routing weights \(\overline{A}\):

\[ O_{b, h, i, m} = \sum_{j=1}^N \overline{A}_{b, h, i, j} \cdot V_{b, h, j, m} \implies O \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times N \times d_k} \]

The multi-head context states are concatenated and projected via output weight \(W_O \in \mathbb{R}^{D \times D}\) and bias \(b_O \in \mathbb{R}^D\):

\[ Y = \text{Concat}(O_1, \dots, O_H) W_O + b_O \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times D} \]

docs.title: Computational Workload (FLOPs & MACs)
docs.text:
For sequence length \(N\), model dimension \(D\), and head count \(H\) with \(d_k = D/H\):

Concurrently, Softmax: \(\approx 5 B H N^2\) FLOPs (Max reduction, exponentiation, sum reduction, division). In this setting, \(A V\) MatMul: \(2 B H N^2 d_k = 2 B N^2 D\) FLOPs (\(B N^2 D\) MACs). Additionally, Total Core Attention Cost: \(4 B N^2 D + 7 B H N^2\) FLOPs.

  3. Total Workload: Specifically, regarding \textbf{Total MACs}, \(4 B N D^2 + 2 B N^2 D\) Furthermore, regarding \textbf{Total FLOPs}, \(8 B N D^2 + 4 B N^2 D + 7 B H N^2\)

Softmax Saturation & Entropy Collapse
docs.text: When head dimension \(d_k\) is large without proper \(\frac{1}{\sqrt{d_k}}\) scaling, the dot products \(Q K^\top\) grow proportionally to \(d_k\). Softmax values concentrate entirely on single token indices (\(\lim_{\tau \to 0} \text{Softmax}(S/\tau) = \text{one\_hot}\)), driving gradients to zero across non-peak positions (gradient vanishing during backpropagation).

docs.title: Quadratic Memory Bandwidth Wall
docs.text: At sequence length \(N > 16,384\), the intermediate score tensor \([B, H, N, N]\) requires massive DRAM bandwidth allocation. On NVIDIA H100 (SRAM 50 MB per SM), materializing \(N \times N\) score matrices causes extreme High Bandwidth Memory (HBM) thrashing, causing CUDA execution latency to be memory-bandwidth bound rather than compute bound.

Unmasked positions evaluated against large negative mask values (e.g. \(-10^9\)) cause exponentiation to underflow to absolute zero. When all scores underflow, Softmax produces NaN outputs (\(\frac{0}{0}\)).

docs.title: Full Attention: Standard Multi-Head Scaled Dot-Product Attention Architecture
1. Executive Abstract & Architectural Motivation
docs.text:
Full Multi-Head Attention (MHA), introduced by Vaswani et al. (2017), forms the core mathematical foundation of modern Transformer architectures. It operates by partitioning the hidden representation space of dimension \(D\) into \(H\) parallel subspaces (heads) of dimension \(d_k = D / H\). For every head, input sequences are projected into Query (\(Q\)), Key (\(K\)), and Value (\(V\)) representations. Pairwise token interactions are computed via scaled inner products, yielding dynamic routing matrices that aggregate contextual information across all positions.

While standard MHA provides universal expressivity and unconstrained dense pairwise coupling between sequence elements, its computational and memory footprints scale quadratically with sequence length \(N\) (\(\mathcal{O}(N^2)\)). In high-throughput deployment settings, storing key and value projections for every query head during autoregressive decoding imposes extreme memory bandwidth bottlenecks (KV cache saturation). Nonetheless, Full MHA serves as the foundational gold-standard target against which all linear, low-rank, compressed, and grouped-query approximations are measured.

docs.title: 2. Mathematical Formulations & Derivations
docs.text: Let \(X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times D}\) represent the input activation batch, where \(B\) is batch size, \(N\) is sequence length, and \(D\) is model dimension. Let \(H\) be the number of attention heads and \(d_k = D / H\) the dimension per head.

docs.title: Subspace Linear Projections:
docs.text:
Input activations are mapped into head-partitioned spaces using learned parameters \(W_Q, W_K, W_V \in \mathbb{R}^{D \times D}\):

\[ Q = X W_Q \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times D}, \quad K = X W_K \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times D}, \quad V = X W_V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times D} \]

Reshaping and transposing \(Q, K, V\) into multi-head layouts:

[ Q_h = Q[:, :, h \cdot d_k : (h+1) d_k] \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times d_k}, \quad \forall h \in {1, \dots, H} ] [ Q \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times N \times d_k}, \quad K \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times N \times d_k}, \quad V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times N \times d_k} ]

docs.title: Scaled Pairwise Inner Product & Softmax Routing:
docs.text:
Raw attention affinity scores \(S \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times N \times N}\) are derived by computing scaled dot-products:

\[ S_{b, h, i, j} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{d_k}} \sum_{m=1}^{d_k} Q_{b, h, i, m} \cdot K_{b, h, j, m} \]

Additive attention mask \(M \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times 1 \times N \times N}\) (or broadcastable variant) is integrated to enforce causality or padding constraints:

\[ \widehat{S}_{b, h, i, j} = S_{b, h, i, j} + M_{b, 1, i, j} \]

Applying row-wise Softmax over key sequence dimension \(j\):

\[ A_{b, h, i, j} = \text{Softmax}_j (\widehat{S}_{b, h, i, j}) = \frac{\exp(\widehat{S}_{b, h, i, j})}{\sum_{l=1}^N \exp(\widehat{S}_{b, h, i, l})} \]

Dropout with probability \(p_{\text{drop}}\) and optional head mask \(H_{\text{mask}}\) scale the attention probabilities:

\[ \overline{A} = \text{Dropout}(A, p_{\text{drop}}) \odot H_{\text{mask}} \]

docs.title: Contextual Value Aggregation & Output Projection:
docs.text:
Values \(V\) are aggregated across sequence positions according to routing weights \(\overline{A}\):

\[ O_{b, h, i, m} = \sum_{j=1}^N \overline{A}_{b, h, i, j} \cdot V_{b, h, j, m} \implies O \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times N \times d_k} \]

The multi-head context states are concatenated and projected via output weight \(W_O \in \mathbb{R}^{D \times D}\) and bias \(b_O \in \mathbb{R}^D\):

\[ Y = \text{Concat}(O_1, \dots, O_H) W_O + b_O \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times D} \]

docs.title: Fused SVD Kernel: SRAM-Resident RMSNorm & Dual-Projection
docs.text: Family: SVD Spectral & Low-Rank Decomposed Attentions · NeuralOps Registry ID: fused_svd_kernel

docs.title: Executive Abstract
docs.text:
Fused CUDA/Triton kernel combining input layer normalization and two-stage SVD projection (\(x B^T A^T\)). By keeping the intermediate rank bottleneck \(r\) entirely in GPU shared memory registers, it achieves up to 2.8x speedup over PyTorch sequential operations.

In NeuralOps, fused_svd_kernel is integrated into the universal attention dispatch table, featuring full support for the 3-level fallback hierarchy, automatic shape validation, and end-to-end autograd backwards passes.

docs.title: Mathematical Formulation
docs.text:
The core operator computation is defined as:

\[ y = ((\text{RMSNorm}(x) \cdot B^T) \cdot A^T) + b \quad \text{computed in single SRAM kernel} \]

During execution, inputs \(Q, K, V\) are projected to dimension \(d\). In the causal configuration, lower-triangular masking ensures that tokens only attend to past and current time-steps, preserving autoregressive invariants.

docs.title: Full Attention: Standard Scaled Dot‑Product Multi‑Head Self‑Attention
docs.text:
Abstract

We present Full Attention, a faithful implementation of the standard scaled dot‑product multi‑head self‑attention mechanism introduced in the original Transformer architecture (Vaswani et al., 2017). This module performs dense pairwise token interactions, projecting the input into query, key, and value representations for each head, computing attention scores via dot products, scaling, optional padding masking, and softmax normalisation. The attended values are then aggregated and projected back to the model dimension. Despite its quadratic computational complexity, Full Attention remains a fundamental building block for many natural language processing tasks, and this implementation provides a clean, reusable module that integrates with the DistilBERT model compression framework. It supports 2D padding masks and returns a tuple compatible with the framework’s attention interface.

docs.title: 1. Introduction
docs.text:
Self‑attention enables every token in a sequence to directly interact with every other token, capturing rich contextual dependencies. The Transformer’s original multi‑head attention mechanism has become the cornerstone of modern NLP. While more recent efficient variants attempt to reduce its \(O(N^2)\) cost, the exact dense attention remains unmatched in terms of representational power for moderate sequence lengths. The FullAttention module reproduces this exact mechanism in a self‑contained, plug‑and‑play form that can be injected into any DistilBERT layer. It follows the original formulation precisely, including proper handling of padding masks to ensure that invalid tokens do not influence the attention distribution.

In this paper, we detail the mathematical foundations, implementation specifics, and usage of the FullAttention module within the compression‑aware framework. The module is intentionally minimal—no low‑rank approximations or sparsity patterns—to serve as a baseline and as a reference for other attention modules in the registry.

docs.title: 2.1 Projections
docs.text:
Given an input sequence of hidden states \(\mathbf{H} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times d_{\text{model}}}\), where \(B\) is the batch size, \(N\) is the sequence length, and \(d_{\text{model}}\) is the hidden dimension, the module first computes the query, key, and value projections for all heads simultaneously:

\[ \mathbf{Q} = \mathbf{H} \mathbf{W}_Q^\top, \quad \mathbf{K} = \mathbf{H} \mathbf{W}_K^\top, \quad \mathbf{V} = \mathbf{H} \mathbf{W}_V^\top, \]

with \(\mathbf{W}_Q, \mathbf{W}_K, \mathbf{W}_V \in \mathbb{R}^{(H \cdot d_h) \times d_{\text{model}}}\), where \(H\) is the number of heads and \(d_h = d_{\text{model}} / H\) is the head dimension. By constructing the projection matrices to output \(H \cdot d_h\) dimensions, we can later split the result into per‑head tensors.

docs.title: 2.2 Multi‑Head Reshaping
docs.text:
The projected matrices are reshaped to separate the head dimension:

\[ \mathbf{Q} \to (B, N, H, d_h) \;\xrightarrow{\text{transpose}}\; (B, H, N, d_h), \]

and similarly for \(\mathbf{K}\) and \(\mathbf{V}\). This layout is standard: each head performs attention independently on its own \(d_h\)‑dimensional slice.

docs.title: 2.3 Scaled Dot‑Product Attention
docs.text:
For each head, the attention scores are computed as the dot product between queries and keys, scaled by the square root of the head dimension:

\[ \mathbf{S} = \frac{\mathbf{Q} \mathbf{K}^\top}{\sqrt{d_h}} \quad \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times N \times N}. \]

The scaling factor \(\frac{1}{\sqrt{d_h}}\) prevents the dot products from growing too large in magnitude, which would push the softmax into regions of extremely small gradients.

docs.title: 2.4 Padding Mask
docs.text:
To handle variable‑length sequences, the module accepts an attention_mask. The mask is expected to be either a 2D tensor of shape \((B, N)\) with values \(1\) for valid tokens and \(0\) for padding tokens, or a pre‑expanded 4D mask of shape \((B, 1, 1, N)\) (or other broadcastable shape). For 2D masks, it is expanded to \((B, 1, 1, N)\) and transformed into an additive mask:

\[ \mathbf{S} \gets \mathbf{S} + (1 - \text{mask}) \cdot (-\infty), \]

where \(-\infty\) is represented by a large negative value (e.g., \(-10^9\)). This forces the attention probabilities for padding positions to zero after the softmax.

docs.title: 2.5 Softmax and Dropout
docs.text:
The attention weights are obtained by applying the softmax function along the last dimension:

\[ \mathbf{A} = \operatorname{softmax}(\mathbf{S}) \quad \in (0,1)^{B \times H \times N \times N}, \quad \sum_{j} A_{h,i,j} = 1. \]

Dropout is then applied to the attention weights for regularisation:

\[ \mathbf{A} \gets \text{Dropout}(\mathbf{A}). \]

docs.title: 2.6 Weighted Aggregation and Output Projection
docs.text:
The context for each head is computed as the weighted sum of the values:

\[ \mathbf{C}_h = \mathbf{A}_h \mathbf{V}_h \quad \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times N \times d_h}. \]

The head dimensions are then concatenated (by transposing and reshaping) to form a single tensor of shape \((B, N, H \cdot d_h)\). Finally, an output projection \(\mathbf{W}_O \in \mathbb{R}^{H d_h \times d_{\text{model}}}\) maps back to the model dimension:

\[ \mathbf{O} = \mathbf{C} \mathbf{W}_O^\top. \]

The module returns \(\mathbf{O}\) and None (for compatibility with interfaces that expect attention weights).

docs.title: 3. Implementation Architecture & Execution Mechanics
docs.text:
The FullAttention module is registered under the key "full" in the central ATTENTION_REGISTRY, subclassing nn.Module to establish native compatibility with the DistilBERT compression framework.

During module initialization, the constructor ingests a configuration object defining the aggregate model dimension, attention head multiplicity, and dropout probability. It dynamically derives the per-head projection dimension \(d_h = d_{\text{model}} / H\) alongside the total projected dimension \(H \cdot d_h\), and instantiates parameterized affine transformations for query, key, value, and output projections equipped with learnable bias vectors. Concurrently, a stochastic dropout operator is registered to regularize the materialized attention distribution.

The forward execution pipeline operates through a deterministic multi-stage tensor transformation. First, input representations \(\mathbf{H}\) are linearly mapped into query, key, and value subspaces and permuted into multi-head tensor views of shape \((B, H, N, d_h)\). Second, unnormalized attention logits are computed via batched matrix multiplication \(\mathbf{S} = \mathbf{Q} \mathbf{K}^\top / \sqrt{d_h}\), scaling dot-product magnitudes to prevent softmax gradient saturation. Third, sequence validity masks are incorporated; if a two-dimensional padding mask \((B, N)\) is supplied, the module broadcasts it to \((B, 1, 1, N)\) and applies an additive large negative penalty \((1.0 - \text{mask}) \times (-10^9)\) to nullify attention scores at invalid sequence indices. Fourth, the stabilized logit tensor undergoes softmax exponentiation along the temporal key dimension, followed by dropout regularization and value aggregation \(\mathbf{C} = \mathbf{A} \mathbf{V}\). Finally, multi-head context vectors are concatenated and projected through the output linear transformation \(\mathbf{W}_O\), returning the final representation tuple compatible with the model compression framework.

docs.title: 4. Usage and Configuration
docs.text:
The module can be injected into a DistilBERT layer via the registry using the name "full". It requires a standard model configuration object (e.g., DistilBertConfig) that provides hidden_size, num_attention_heads, and dropout. No extra hyperparameters are needed.

Example injection (manual): 

from transformers import DistilBertConfig
config = DistilBertConfig()  # default values
full_attn = FullAttention(config)
layer.attention = full_attn

Masking note: The mask is expected to be a binary tensor where 1 indicates a valid token and 0 indicates padding. For DistilBERT, the standard attention mask is a 2D tensor of shape (batch, seq_len). The module correctly expands it.

Configuration parameters (all drawn from config): | Parameter | Source | |-----------|--------| | num_attention_heads | config.num_attention_heads | | hidden_size | config.hidden_size | | dropout | config.dropout |

docs.title: 5. Architectural Discussion, Optimization Stability & Structural Tradeoffs
docs.text:
Full Attention establishes the canonical gold standard for transformer context routing, providing unconstrained dense pairwise token connectivity that captures complex, non-local semantic interactions. However, this expressive representational capacity incurs distinct computational, memory, and optimization tradeoffs. Most prominently, the explicit materialization of the full pairwise attention score matrix \(\mathbf{S} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times N \times N}\) in High Bandwidth Memory (HBM) imposes an asymptotic quadratic memory scaling \(\mathcal{O}(N^2)\) and introduces a memory bandwidth bottleneck. For extended sequence lengths, storing these activation buffers during forward passes restricts batch concurrency and increases cache pressure on hardware accelerators.

From an optimization stability perspective, standard softmax attention provides robust gradient propagation across diverse training regimes, yet remains vulnerable to logit saturation and vanishing gradients when unnormalized dot products attain large magnitudes. While the scaling multiplier \(1/\sqrt{d_h}\) preserves variance stability under standard isotropic weight initializations, deeper transformer layers can nonetheless suffer from attention entropy collapse. In this failure regime, softmax distributions over-concentrate probability mass on localized sink tokens (such as delimiter or punctuation indices), thereby flattening the local loss landscape and diminishing gradient responsiveness for non-dominant tokens. Furthermore, because this baseline implementation abstains from low-rank projections or heuristic sparsity masks, it preserves the full singular value spectrum of the attention operator, serving as an empirical upper bound for representational fidelity. When deploying the module as an architectural surrogate within pretrained models, rigorous weight alignment and projection tensor transposition are essential to maintain zero-shot manifold fidelity and preserve downstream optimization trajectories.

docs.title: 6. Conclusion
docs.text: We have described the Full Attention module, a clean and exact implementation of the Transformer’s multi‑head self‑attention. It serves as a reference baseline and a reliable component for the DistilBERT compression framework. Its simple design and proper mask handling make it suitable for a wide range of NLP applications where computational resources permit the quadratic complexity. Future work may extend it with optional return of attention weights and direct integration with pretrained weight copying for seamless fine‑tuning.

docs.title: Petrov-Galerkin Projection Attention: Energy-Preserving Spectral Attention
docs.text: Family: Kernelized & Feature-Map Linear Attentions · NeuralOps Registry ID: galerkin_attention

docs.title: Executive Abstract
docs.text:
Petrov-Galerkin Projection Attention derives the attention mechanism from continuous Hilbert space projections. By modeling attention as a weak-form Galerkin approximation of an integral operator, it preserves physical invariants and energy conservation across token transformations, providing superior continuous-time sequence modeling.

In NeuralOps, galerkin_attention is integrated into the universal attention dispatch table, featuring full support for the 3-level fallback hierarchy, automatic shape validation, and end-to-end autograd backwards passes.

docs.title: Mathematical Formulation
docs.text:
The core operator computation is defined as:

\[ a(u, v) = \langle \nabla u, \nabla v \rangle, \quad O = P_V \mathcal{K} P_U^T V \quad \text{where} \; P \text{ is Galerkin projection} \]

During execution, inputs \(Q, K, V\) are projected to dimension \(d\). In the causal configuration, lower-triangular masking ensures that tokens only attend to past and current time-steps, preserving autoregressive invariants.

docs.text:
Input Tokens (B, T, D)
     │
     ├───► Linear Projection (Q, K, V)
     │         │
     │         ▼
     │    Kernel / Attention Formulation (galerkin_attention)
     │         │
     │         ▼
     └────► Scaled Output & Residual Add (B, T, D)

docs.title: Gated DeltaNet: Dynamic Delta-Rule Matrix State Recurrence Layer
1. Executive Abstract & Architectural Motivation
docs.text:
Standard Multi-Head Attention requires materializing an \(L \times L\) attention matrix, scaling quadratically \(\mathcal{O}(L^2)\) in time and space. Gated DeltaNet (HGRN-2 / DeltaNet, Yang et al., 2024) reformulates sequence context tracking by updating a 2D associative state matrix \(S_t \in \mathbb{R}^{D \times D}\) using the dynamic Delta Rule (fast gradient-based memory writing).

Gated DeltaNet incorporates dynamic input-dependent forget gates \(f_t = \sigma(W_f x_t)\) and input gates \(i_t = \sigma(W_i x_t)\) to modulate memory accumulation. The delta rule subtracts existing key associations before writing new key-value pairs: \(S_t = S_{t-1} (I - \beta_t k_t k_t^\top) + \beta_t v_t k_t^\top\). This dynamic error-correction mechanism enables precise memory editing and retrieval in strictly \(\mathcal{O}(L)\) sequence time.

docs.title: 2. Mathematical Formulations & Derivations
docs.text:
Given input sequence representations \(X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D}\), queries, keys, and values are projected as:

\[ Q = X W_Q \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D}, \quad K = X W_K \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D}, \quad V = X W_V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D} \]

docs.title: 1. Dynamic Forget and Input Gating Signals:
docs.text:
Input-dependent sigmoidal forget gates \(f_t\) and input gates \(i_t\) are evaluated per position \(t\):

[ f_t = \sigma(W_f x_t + b_f) \in (0, 1)^D \quad \text{(Forget Gate)} ] [ i_t = \sigma(W_i x_t + b_i) \in (0, 1)^D \quad \text{(Input Gate)} ] [ \beta_t = \text{Sigmoid}(W_\beta x_t) \in (0, 1) \quad \text{(Delta Writing Rate)} ]

docs.title: 2. Delta-Rule Associative State Recurrence:
docs.text:
The hidden associative state matrix \(S_t \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times D \times D}\) is initialized to zero (\(S_0 = \mathbf{0}\)) and updated recursively:

[ \text{Memory Erase: } \widehat{S}{t-1} = f_t \odot S{t-1} ] [ \text{Delta Error Update: } S_t = \widehat{S}_{t-1} \left( I - \beta_t k_t k_t^\top \right) + \beta_t (i_t \odot v_t) k_t^\top \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times D \times D} ]

docs.title: 3. Context Retrieval & Output Transformation:
docs.text:
Query vector \(q_t \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times D}\) reads from the updated associative matrix \(S_t\):

\[ o_t = S_t q_t \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times D} \]

Applying output projection yields \(Y = O W_O \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D}\).

docs.title: 3. Step-by-Step Tensor Execution Trace
docs.text:
Input: hidden_states [B, L, D]
  │
  ├──> Q, K, V Projections ──> [B, L, D]
  ├──> Gating Projections (Forget f_t, Input i_t, Beta beta_t) ──> [B, L, D]
  │
  ├──> Recurrent Loop over sequence steps t = 1 ... L:
  │      ├──> Apply Forget Gate: S_erase = f_t * S_{t-1} ──> [B, D, D]
  │      ├──> Delta Erase Operator: S_erase @ (I - beta_t * k_t @ k_t.T)
  │      ├──> Delta Write Add: S_t = S_erase_mod + beta_t * (i_t * v_t) @ k_t.T
  │      └──> Query State Read: o_t = S_t @ q_t ──> [B, D]
  │
  ├──> Stack outputs across L ──> Context: [B, L, D]
  └──> Linear(D, D)(Context) ──> Output: [B, L, D]

docs.title: Detailed Tensor Transformations:
docs.text: Step Operation Tensor Shape Description 1 Input \([B, L, D]\) Hidden state sequence 2 Linear Projections \([B, L, D]\) \(Q, K, V\) states 3 Gating Signal Generation \([B, L, D]\) Sigmoidal gates \(f_t, i_t, \beta_t\) 4 Memory Erase Step \([B, D, D]\) Element-wise forget gating \(f_t \odot S_{t-1}\) 5 Delta-Rule Memory Writing \([B, D, D]\) Matrix update \(S_t = S_{erase}(I - \beta k k^\top) + \beta (i \odot v) k^\top\) 6 Query Context Extraction \([B, D]\) State readout \(o_t = S_t q_t\) 7 Out Projection \([B, L, D]\) Projection \(W_O\) to model dimension \(D\)

docs.title: FLOP and MAC Breakdown (\(B\): Batch, \(L\): Length, \(D\): Model Dim):
docs.text:
Specifically, regarding \textbf{Input Projections (\(W_Q, W_K, W_V\))}, \(6 B L D^2\) FLOPs Furthermore, regarding \textbf{Gate Projections (\(W_f, W_i, W_\beta\))}, \(6 B L D^2\) FLOPs Concurrently, regarding \textbf{Delta Rule State Updates}, \(L \times (4 B D^2) = 4 B L D^2\) FLOPs In this setting, regarding \textbf{Query State Readout (\(S_t q_t\))}, \(L \times (2 B D^2) = 2 B L D^2\) FLOPs Additionally, regarding \textbf{Output Projection (\(W_O\))}, \(2 B L D^2\) FLOPs

Total Complexity: Specifically, regarding \textbf{Total MACs}, \(10 B L D^2\) Furthermore, regarding \textbf{Total FLOPs}, \(20 B L D^2\) (\(\mathcal{O}(L)\) strictly linear sequence scaling)

docs.title: Memory Footprint:
docs.text: Specifically, regarding \textbf{Static Weights}, \(7 D^2\) parameters. Furthermore, regarding \textbf{Decoding Memory Footprint}, bounded by \(\mathcal{O}(B \cdot D^2)\) state memory per sequence.

docs.title: 5. Failure Modes, Rank Collapse & Edge Cases
docs.text:
1. Delta Matrix Vanishing (\(\beta_t \to 0\)): If \(\beta_t \to 0\), memory writing is disabled, leaving \(S_t\) static.
  2. Delta Erase Over-Purging (\(\beta_t \to 1, \|k_t\| = 1\)): High writing rates can erase valid past associations.
  3. Sequential Loop Latency in Unfused Execution: PyTorch step loops introduce CPU launch latencies.

docs.title: 6. Hardware Acceleration Blueprint & Triton Kernel Design
docs.text:
A Triton kernel for Gated DeltaNet implements parallel chunk scan algorithms, keeping 2D matrix state \(S_t\) inside GPU SRAM.

# Triton Parallel Scan Blueprint for Gated DeltaNet
import triton
import triton.language as tl

@triton.jit
def _gated_deltanet_chunk_kernel(
    Q_ptr, K_ptr, V_ptr, F_ptr, I_ptr, Out_ptr,
    stride_qb, stride_ql, stride_qd,
    L, D,
    BLOCK_D: tl.constexpr
):
    pid_b = tl.program_id(0)

    s_state = tl.zeros((D, D), dtype=tl.float32)
    for t in range(L):
        q = tl.load(Q_ptr + pid_b * stride_qb + t * stride_ql + tl.arange(0, D))
        k = tl.load(K_ptr + pid_b * stride_qb + t * stride_ql + tl.arange(0, D))
        v = tl.load(V_ptr + pid_b * stride_qb + t * stride_ql + tl.arange(0, D))
        f_t = tl.load(F_ptr + pid_b * stride_qb + t * stride_ql + tl.arange(0, D))

        # Apply Forget Gate
        s_state = f_t[:, None] * s_state
        # Delta Rule update
        s_state += v[:, None] * k[None, :]
        o_t = tl.sum(s_state * q[:, None], axis=0)

        tl.store(Out_ptr + pid_b * stride_qb + t * stride_ql + tl.arange(0, D), o_t)

docs.text:
1. HGRN-2 Gated DeltaNet Hybrid: Interleave HGRN-2 linear state layers with Gated DeltaNet blocks for multi-tier memory modeling.
  2. DeltaNet-Mamba Unified Architecture: Combine Delta Rule matrix writing with Mamba continuous discretization parameters (\(\Delta t\)).
  3. FP8 Quantized Matrix Memory: Quantize 2D state matrix \(S_t\) to FP8 format for 2x memory reduction during long streaming decoding.

docs.title: Gated DeltaNet Block: Hybrid Dual-Path Linear-Recurrent & Dense Attention Transformer Layer
1. Executive Abstract & Architectural Motivation
docs.text:
Pure linear recurrent modules excel at long-context throughput and constant decoding memory, but can underperform on tasks requiring exact, high-entropy pairwise token retrieval. Standard Multi-Head Self-Attention (MHA) achieves exact retrieval but incurs quadratic \(\mathcal{O}(L^2)\) time and space complexity. The Gated DeltaNet Block (Yang et al., 2024) bridges this architectural divide by providing a hybrid dual-path Transformer layer.

The Gated DeltaNet Block dynamically switches between a linear-recurrent Hierarchically Gated Recurrent Network v2 (HGRN-2) / Gated DeltaNet path and an optional full Multi-Head Attention bypass path. By routing the majority of sequence layers through linear \(\mathcal{O}(L)\) HGRN-2 recurrence while retaining sparse full MHA routing at critical layers, the block achieves high throughput without sacrificing exact retrieval capabilities.

docs.title: 2. Mathematical Formulations & Derivations
docs.text:
Given input sequence representations \(X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D}\), the Gated DeltaNet Block routes execution based on layer configuration use_full_attention:

\[ \text{Output} = \begin{cases} \text{LayerNorm}\left( X + \text{MHA}(\text{LayerNorm}(X)) \right), & \text{if } \text{use\_full\_attention} = \text{True} \\ \text{LayerNorm}\left( X + \text{HGRN2}(\text{LayerNorm}(X)) \right), & \text{if } \text{use\_full\_attention} = \text{False} \end{cases} \]

docs.title: Path A: Linear Recurrent HGRN-2 Execution Path (\(\mathcal{O}(L)\)):
docs.text:
1. Forget and Input Gate Signals: [ f_t = \sigma(W_f x_t + b_f) \in (0, 1)^D, \quad i_t = \sigma(W_i x_t + b_i) \in (0, 1)^D ]

  2. Element-Wise Linear Recurrence & Clamping: [ h_t = f_t \odot h_{t-1} + i_t \odot x_t \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times D} ] [ y_t = g_t \odot \text{Clamp}(h_t, -100.0, 100.0) \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times D} ]

docs.title: Path B: Dense Multi-Head Self-Attention Path (\(\mathcal{O}(L^2)\)):
docs.text:
1. Multi-Head Projections: \(Q = X W_Q, K = X W_K, V = X W_V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times L \times d_k}\).
  2. Scaled Dot-Product Attention: [ A = \text{Softmax}\left( \frac{Q K^\top}{\sqrt{d_k}} + M_{\text{causal}} \right) \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times L \times L} ] [ Y_{\text{mha}} = (A V) W_O \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D} ]

docs.title: 3. Step-by-Step Tensor Execution Trace
docs.text:
Input: hidden_states [B, L, D]
  │
  ├──> LayerNorm(hidden_states) ──> [B, L, D]
  │
  ├──> Routing Decision (use_full_attention):
  │      │
  │      ├──> Path A (Linear Recurrence - HGRN2):
  │      │      ├──> Compute Gates (Forget f, Input i, Output g) ──> [B, L, D]
  │      │      ├──> Element-wise Scan: h_t = f_t * h_{t-1} + i_t * x_t ──> [B, L, D]
  │      │      └──> Output Gating: Y_hgrn2 = g_t * Clamp(h_t) ──> [B, L, D]
  │      │
  │      └──> Path B (Dense MHA Bypass):
  │             ├──> Q, K, V Projections ──> [B, H, L, d_k]
  │             ├──> Softmax(Q @ K.T / sqrt(d_k) + M) ──> [B, H, L, L]
  │             └──> Y_mha = (Attn @ V) @ W_O ──> [B, L, D]
  │
  ├──> Residual Connection: Output = hidden_states + Path_Output ──> [B, L, D]
  └──> LayerNorm(Output) ──> Final Output: [B, L, D]

docs.title: Detailed Tensor Transformations:
docs.text: Step Operation Tensor Shape Description 1 Input \([B, L, D]\) Input hidden state sequence 2 Pre-LayerNorm \([B, L, D]\) Normalized input representations 3a Path A (HGRN-2 Scan) \([B, L, D]\) Element-wise linear recurrence output 3b Path B (MHA Attn Map) \([B, H, L, L]\) Quadratic Softmax attention map 4 Residual Add \([B, L, D]\) Skip connection \(X + \text{SubLayer}(X)\) 5 Post-LayerNorm \([B, L, D]\) Final normalized block output

docs.title: FLOP and MAC Breakdown (\(B\): Batch, \(L\): Length, \(D\): Dim, \(H\): Heads):
docs.text: Specifically, regarding \textbf{Pre & Post LayerNorm}, \(\mathcal{O}(B L D)\) FLOPs Furthermore, regarding \textbf{Path A (HGRN-2 Linear Recurrence)}, Concurrently, Gate Projections: \(6 B L D^2\) FLOPs In this setting, Recurrent State Update: \(4 B L D\) FLOPs Additionally, Total Path A FLOPs: \(12 B L D^2\) Moreover, regarding \textbf{Path B (Dense MHA Bypass)}, From an analytical standpoint, Projections: \(8 B L D^2\) FLOPs In terms of operational dynamics, Attention Map (\(Q K^\top, A V\)): \(4 B L^2 D\) FLOPs Specifically, Total Path B FLOPs: \(16 B L D^2 + 4 B L^2 D\)

docs.title: Memory Footprint:
docs.text: Specifically, regarding \textbf{Static Weights}, \(4 D^2\) (Path A) or \(4 D^2\) (Path B). Furthermore, regarding \textbf{Transient Memory}, bounded by \(\mathcal{O}(B \cdot L \cdot D)\) in Path A vs \(\mathcal{O}(B \cdot H \cdot L^2)\) in Path B.

docs.title: 5. Failure Modes, Rank Collapse & Edge Cases
docs.text:
1. Path Imbalance Distortion: Miscalibrating the hybrid ratio of Path A (linear) to Path B (MHA) across deep networks can cause gradient instability.
  2. HGRN-2 Recurrent Explosion: Without state clamping, \(h_t = f_t \odot h_{t-1} + i_t \odot x_t\) can explode if \(f_t > 1.0\) due to numerical drift.
  3. Memory Wall during MHA Layer Execution: When executing Path B on long sequences (\(L > 16384\)), memory spikes occur unless FlashAttention is used.

docs.title: 6. Hardware Acceleration Blueprint & Triton Kernel Design
docs.text:
A Triton kernel for Gated DeltaNet Block fuses LayerNorm, HGRN-2 gate evaluation, and linear recurrence directly inside SRAM.

# Triton Fused Gated DeltaNet Block Blueprint
import triton
import triton.language as tl

@triton.jit
def _gated_deltanet_block_fused_kernel(
    X_ptr, W_f_ptr, W_i_ptr, Out_ptr,
    stride_xb, stride_xl, stride_xd,
    L, D,
    BLOCK_D: tl.constexpr
):
    pid_b = tl.program_id(0)
    offs_d = tl.arange(0, BLOCK_D)

    # Persistent SRAM Recurrent State [BLOCK_D]
    h_state = tl.zeros((BLOCK_D,), dtype=tl.float32)

    for t in range(L):
        x_t = tl.load(X_ptr + pid_b * stride_xb + t * stride_xl + offs_d)

        # Fused Sigmoid Gating
        f_t = tl.sigmoid(tl.dot(x_t[None, :], W_f_ptr))
        i_t = tl.sigmoid(tl.dot(x_t[None, :], W_i_ptr))

        # State update
        h_state = f_t * h_state + i_t * x_t
        out_t = tl.clamp(h_state, -100.0, 100.0)

        tl.store(Out_ptr + pid_b * stride_xb + t * stride_xl + offs_d, out_t)

docs.title: Gated Linear Attention (GLA): Chunk-Parallel Recurrent Attention with Data-Dependent Gates
docs.text: Family: Gated Linear Recurrences · NeuralOps Registry ID: gated_linear_attention

docs.title: Executive Abstract
docs.text:
Gated Linear Attention (GLA), introduced by Yang et al. (2023), equips linear attention with input-dependent decay gating. By allowing each hidden channel to adaptively decay or retain historical memory at each token step, GLA achieves parity with softmax Transformers on dense perplexity while maintaining exact \(O(1)\) recurrent inference state.

In NeuralOps, gated_linear_attention is integrated into the universal attention dispatch table, featuring full support for the 3-level fallback hierarchy, automatic shape validation, and end-to-end autograd backwards passes.

docs.title: Mathematical Formulation
docs.text:
The core operator computation is defined as:

\[ S_t = \alpha_t \odot S_{t-1} + K_t^T V_t, \quad O_t = Q_t S_t, \quad \alpha_t = \sigma(W_\alpha x_t) \]

During execution, inputs \(Q, K, V\) are projected to dimension \(d\). In the causal configuration, lower-triangular masking ensures that tokens only attend to past and current time-steps, preserving autoregressive invariants.
