docs.title: GoldFinch-AHN: Adaptive Hybrid Network Combining Sliding Window and Gated DeltaNet Memory
1. Abstract & Theoretical Motivation
docs.text:
Standard Transformer self-attention enforces global \(N \times N\) token comparisons, incurring quadratic time and memory cost \(\mathcal{O}(N^2)\). However, sequence modeling requires capturing both short-range local correlations and long-range historical context. GoldFinch-AHN (Adaptive Hybrid Network) addresses this dual requirement by integrating a hybrid architectural design.

GoldFinch-AHN couples a local causal sliding-window attention mechanism with a long-range Gated DeltaNet recurrent memory stream. Dynamic, input-conditioned scalar gating coefficients \(g = \sigma(\mathbf{X} \mathbf{W}_{\text{gate}} + \mathbf{b}_{\text{gate}}) \in [0, 1]\) continuously blend short-term local representations with long-term recurrent memory features, providing linear computational complexity \(\mathcal{O}(N W + N D)\).

docs.title: 2. Mathematical Derivations & Formulations
docs.text:
Given an input representation sequence \(\mathbf{X} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times D}\), GoldFinch-AHN projects queries, keys, and values:

\[ \mathbf{Q} = \mathbf{X} \mathbf{W}_Q \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times D}, \quad \mathbf{K} = \mathbf{X} \mathbf{W}_K \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times D}, \quad \mathbf{V} = \mathbf{X} \mathbf{W}_V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times D} \]

docs.title: 1. Short-Term Causal Sliding-Window Attention Stream
docs.text:
Raw dot-product scores are scaled and masked using a causal sliding-window constraint matrix \(\mathbf{M}_{\text{window}} \in \{0, -\infty\}^{N \times N}\):

\[ \mathbf{S}_{i, j} = \frac{\mathbf{q}_i \mathbf{k}_j^\top}{\sqrt{D}} + (\mathbf{M}_{\text{window}})_{i, j} \]

where the valid spatial connectivity is restricted to causal positions within window radius \(W_{\text{size}}\):

\[ (\mathbf{M}_{\text{window}})_{i, j} = \begin{cases} 0 & \text{if } 0 \le i - j < W_{\text{size}} \\ -\infty & \text{otherwise} \end{cases} \]

Softmax probability mapping over the local window yields short-term context:

\[ \mathbf{A}^{\text{short}} = \operatorname{softmax}(\mathbf{S}, \text{dim}=-1) \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times N}, \quad \mathbf{O}^{\text{short}} = \mathbf{A}^{\text{short}} \mathbf{V} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times D} \]

docs.title: 2. Long-Term Gated DeltaNet Memory Stream
docs.text:
Long-term context is processed through a recurrent memory projection layer:

\[ \mathbf{O}^{\text{long}} = \operatorname{DeltaNet}(\mathbf{X}) = \mathbf{X} \mathbf{W}_{\text{mem}} + \mathbf{b}_{\text{mem}} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times D} \]

docs.title: 3. Adaptive Gated Context Blending
docs.text:
Input-conditioned dynamic gating weights \(\mathbf{g} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times 1}\) are generated via linear transformation and sigmoid activation:

\[ \mathbf{g} = \sigma(\mathbf{X} \mathbf{W}_{\text{gate}} + \mathbf{b}_{\text{gate}}) \in [0, 1]^{B \times N \times 1} \]

The final hybrid output blends short-term window attention and long-term memory representations:

\[ \mathbf{O}_{\text{hybrid}} = \mathbf{g} \odot \mathbf{O}^{\text{short}} + (1 - \mathbf{g}) \odot \mathbf{O}^{\text{long}} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times D} \]

Applying the final linear projection yields:

\[ \mathbf{Y} = \mathbf{O}_{\text{hybrid}} \mathbf{W}_O + \mathbf{b}_O \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times D} \]

docs.title: 3. Tensor Execution Flow & Dimensional Shape Tracing
docs.text:
Input Hidden States X [B, N, D]
  │
  ├──> Linear Projections (W_Q, W_K, W_V) -> Q, K, V [B, N, D]
  │
  ├──> Compute Score Matrix: S = Q @ K^T / sqrt(D) ───> [B, N, N]
  │
  ├──> Construct Causal Sliding Window Mask:
  │    Mask_val = ~( (i >= j) & (i - j < W_size) ) ───> [N, N]
  │    S_masked = S.masked_fill(Mask_val, -inf) ───────> [B, N, N]
  │
  ├──> Short-Term Context Readout:
  │    A_short = Softmax(S_masked, dim=-1) ────────────> [B, N, N]
  │    Out_short = A_short @ V ────────────────────────> [B, N, D]
  │
  ├──> Long-Term Gated DeltaNet Stream:
  │    Out_long = DeltaNet(X) = X @ W_mem + b_mem ─────> [B, N, D]
  │
  ├──> Dynamic Input-Conditioned Gate Computation:
  │    g = Sigmoid(X @ W_gate + b_gate) ───────────────> [B, N, 1]
  │
  └──> Context Blending & Output Projection:
       Out_fused = g * Out_short + (1 - g) * Out_long -> [B, N, D]
       Y = Out_fused @ W_O + b_O ──────────────────────> [B, N, D]

docs.title: Detailed Shape Progression Table
docs.text: Step Operation Input Tensor Shapes Output Tensor Shape 1 Projections (\(W_Q, W_K, W_V\)) X: [B, N, D] Q, K, V: [B, N, D] 2 Score Batch MatMul (\(\mathbf{Q} \mathbf{K}^\top\)) Q: [B, N, D], K^T: [B, D, N] S: [B, N, N] 3 Apply Window Mask S: [B, N, N], Mask_val: [N, N] S_masked: [B, N, N] 4 Softmax Probability Mapping S_masked: [B, N, N] A_short: [B, N, N] 5 Short-Term Context Matrix Product A_short: [B, N, N], V: [B, N, D] Out_short: [B, N, D] 6 Long-Term Delta Memory X: [B, N, D], W_mem: [D, D] Out_long: [B, N, D] 7 Dynamic Gate Computation X: [B, N, D], W_gate: [D, 1] g: [B, N, 1] 8 Convex Gate Combination Out_short, Out_long, g Out_fused: [B, N, D] 9 Output Linear Projection Out_fused: [B, N, D], W_O: [D, D] Y: [B, N, D]

docs.title: FLOP & MAC Counting
docs.text:
1. Linear Projections (\(W_Q, W_K, W_V, W_O, W_{\text{mem}}, W_{\text{gate}}\)): \(6 \times (2 B N D^2) = 12 B N D^2\) FLOPs.
  2. Short-Term Window Matrix Product (\(\mathbf{Q} \mathbf{K}^\top\)): \(2 B N W_{\text{size}} D\) FLOPs (evaluating only non-masked window pairs).
  3. Value Aggregation (\(\mathbf{A}^{\text{short}} \mathbf{V}\)): \(2 B N W_{\text{size}} D\) FLOPs.
  4. Dynamic Gating & Blending: \(3 B N D\) FLOPs.

Total Computational Cost: [ \text{Total FLOPs} = 12 B N D^2 + 4 B N W_{\text{size}} D + 3 B N D ]

When window radius \(W_{\text{size}} \ll N\), attention computation scales linearly with sequence length \(N\).

docs.title: Memory Footprint & Tensor Store
docs.text: Specifically, regarding \textbf{Parameters}, \(5 D^2 + D\) floats. Furthermore, regarding \textbf{Activation Memory}, Concurrently, Projections (\(\mathbf{Q}, \mathbf{K}, \mathbf{V}\)): \(3 B N D\) floats. In this setting, Window Scores Matrix (\(\mathbf{S}\)): \(B N^2\) (or \(B N W_{\text{size}}\) with block sparse storage) floats. Additionally, Gating Weights (\(\mathbf{g}\)): \(B N\) floats. Moreover, Peak Memory Footprint: \(\mathcal{O}(B N D + B N W_{\text{size}})\).

docs.title: 5. Architectural Bottlenecks, Rank Collapse & Failure Modes
docs.text:
1. Un-fused Dense Score Matrix Instantiation: Naive PyTorch allocates a full \(B \times N \times N\) score matrix prior to applying mask scores.masked_fill, consuming \(\mathcal{O}(N^2)\) DRAM memory despite window truncation.
  2. Simplified DeltaNet Abstraction: The current GatedDeltaNetLayer uses a static linear projection (nn.Linear) rather than dynamic recurrent state tracking, limiting long-term memory capacity.
  3. Absence of Head Specialization: The code operates on single 3D tensors \([B, N, D]\) without splitting into multiple heads, preventing multi-head feature subspace diversity.

docs.title: 6. Hardware Acceleration Blueprint & Triton Optimization Strategies
Memory Access & Vectorization Barriers
docs.text: Naive PyTorch instantiates full \(B \times N \times N\) attention tensors in DRAM, writing unmasked -inf values to global GPU memory.

docs.title: High-Performance Triton Kernel Fusion Strategy
docs.text:
1. Fused Sliding Window FlashAttention Kernel: Implement a Triton kernel that streams queries \(\mathbf{Q}_i\) and keys \(\mathbf{K}_j\) in SRAM tiles of size BLOCK_N = 64. Skip all key blocks outside the causal window range \(i - W_{\text{size}} \le j \le i\), avoiding memory allocation for non-causal entries.
# Triton Pseudocode for Fused Sliding Window Flash Kernel
@triton.jit
def _goldfinch_fused_window_kernel(
    Q_ptr, K_ptr, V_ptr, Out_ptr,
    N, D, W_SIZE: tl.constexpr, BLOCK_N: tl.constexpr
):
    # Load Query block [BLOCK_N, D]
    q = tl.load(Q_ptr + offsets_q)

    # Loop over key blocks within window range: max(0, i - W_SIZE) to i
    for j in range(start_j, end_j, BLOCK_N):
        k = tl.load(K_ptr + offsets_k)
        scores = tl.dot(q, tl.trans(k)) * scale

        # Apply causal & window bounds in SRAM registers
        scores = tl.where(causal_window_mask, scores, -1e9)
        p = tl.softmax(scores)
        acc += tl.dot(p, v)
  1. Fused DeltaNet & Gating Pipeline: Fuse long-term linear memory evaluation and sigmoid gating directly into the output write loop, avoiding intermediate DRAM writes for \(\mathbf{O}^{\text{long}}\) and \(\mathbf{g}\).

docs.title: Grouped-Query Attention (GQA): Memory-Efficient Shared Key-Value Subspace Architecture
1. Executive Abstract & Architectural Motivation
docs.text:
Grouped-Query Attention (GQA), proposed by Ainslie et al. (2023), establishes a theoretical and practical middle ground between standard Multi-Head Attention (MHA) and Multi-Query Attention (MQA). In standard MHA, every query head maintains its own independent key and value head (\(H_{KV} = H_Q\)). While MHA delivers unconstrained subspace expressivity, its memory footprint scales linearly with the number of heads during autoregressive decoding, causing severe memory bandwidth bottlenecks. Conversely, MQA collapses key and value projections to a single shared head (\(H_{KV} = 1\)), maximizing memory throughput at the cost of model capacity and fine-tuning adaptability.

GQA partitions \(H_Q\) query heads into \(G = H_{KV}\) distinct groups, where each group of size \(R = H_Q / H_{KV}\) shares a single Key-Value head pair. This structural factorization achieves up to an \(R\times\) reduction in Key-Value (KV) cache memory footprint while maintaining quality nearly identical to full MHA. Furthermore, GQA enables seamless conversion from pre-trained MHA checkpoints by group-averaging weight projections.

docs.title: 2. Mathematical Formulations & Derivations
docs.text: Let \(X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times D}\) denote the input activation tensor. Let \(H_Q\) be the number of query heads, \(H_{KV}\) the number of key-value heads such that \(H_{KV} \mid H_Q\), and \(d_k = D / H_Q\) the dimension per head. The head expansion factor is defined as \(R = H_Q / H_{KV}\).

docs.title: Linear Subspace Projections:
docs.text:
Query, key, and value transformations map input activations into compressed subspace configurations:

[ Q = X W_Q \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times (H_Q \cdot d_k)}, \quad W_Q \in \mathbb{R}^{D \times (H_Q \cdot d_k)} ] [ K = X W_K \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times (H_{KV} \cdot d_k)}, \quad W_K \in \mathbb{R}^{D \times (H_{KV} \cdot d_k)} ] [ V = X W_V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times (H_{KV} \cdot d_k)}, \quad W_V \in \mathbb{R}^{D \times (H_{KV} \cdot d_k)} ]

Reshaping into multi-head layouts:

\[ Q \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H_Q \times N \times d_k}, \quad K \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H_{KV} \times N \times d_k}, \quad V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H_{KV} \times N \times d_k} \]

docs.title: Group Expansion Operator (\(\text{repeat\_interleave}\)):
docs.text:
Key and value tensors are expanded across query head groups by repeating each KV head \(R\) times along the head dimension:

[ K_{\text{shared}} = \text{repeat_interleave}(K, R, \text{dim}=\text{head}) \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H_Q \times N \times d_k} ] [ V_{\text{shared}} = \text{repeat_interleave}(V, R, \text{dim}=\text{head}) \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H_Q \times N \times d_k} ]

Formally, for query head \(h \in \{1, \dots, H_Q\}\), the corresponding key head index is \(g(h) = \lfloor (h-1) / R \rfloor + 1 \in \{1, \dots, H_{KV}\}\).

docs.title: Scaled Dot-Product & Softmax Attention:
docs.text:
Pairwise score computation and softmax normalization proceed across expanded key vectors:

[ S_{b, h, i, j} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{d_k}} \sum_{m=1}^{d_k} Q_{b, h, i, m} \cdot (K_{\text{shared}}){b, h, j, m} ] [ \widehat{S} = \text{apply_attention_mask}(S, M) ] [ A{b, h, i, j} = \text{Softmax}j (\widehat{S}{b, h, i, j}) = \frac{\exp(\widehat{S}{b, h, i, j})}{\sum{l=1}^N \exp(\widehat{S}_{b, h, i, l})} ]

docs.title: Context Aggregation & Out Projection:
docs.text:
Context states are computed and projected back to the hidden dimension \(D\):

[ O_{b, h, i, m} = \sum_{j=1}^N \overline{A}{b, h, i, j} \cdot (V{\text{shared}}){b, h, j, m} \implies O \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H_Q \times N \times d_k} ] [ Y = \text{Concat}(O_1, \dots, O{H_Q}) W_O + b_O \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times D}, \quad W_O \in \mathbb{R}^{(H_Q \cdot d_k) \times D} ]

docs.title: Checkpoint Adaptation via Group-Averaging:
docs.text:
When converting a pre-trained MHA checkpoint (\(W_K^{\text{MHA}} \in \mathbb{R}^{(H_Q \cdot d_k) \times D}\)) to GQA, the weights for each KV group \(g \in \{1, \dots, H_{KV}\}\) are obtained by averaging across constituent query heads:

\[ W_{K, g}^{\text{GQA}} = \frac{1}{R} \sum_{r=1}^R W_{K, (g-1)R + r}^{\text{MHA}} \in \mathbb{R}^{d_k \times D} \]

docs.title: Computational Workload (FLOPs & MACs)
docs.text:
Let \(B\) be batch size, \(N\) sequence length, \(D\) model dimension, \(H_Q\) query heads, \(H_{KV}\) KV heads, and \(R = H_Q / H_{KV}\).

  1. Linear Projections: \(W_Q\): \(2 B N D^2\) FLOPs. Furthermore, \(W_K, W_V\): \(2 \times (2 B N D \cdot (H_{KV} d_k)) = \frac{4}{R} B N D^2\) FLOPs. Concurrently, \(W_O\): \(2 B N D^2\) FLOPs. In this setting, Total Projection Cost: \(4 \left(1 + \frac{1}{R}\right) B N D^2\) FLOPs.

  2. Core Attention Workload: \(Q K_{\text{shared}}^\top\): \(2 B H_Q N^2 d_k = 2 B N^2 D\) FLOPs. Furthermore, Softmax & Dropout: \(\approx 7 B H_Q N^2\) FLOPs. Concurrently, \(A V_{\text{shared}}\): \(2 B H_Q N^2 d_k = 2 B N^2 D\) FLOPs. In this setting, Total Core Cost: \(4 B N^2 D + 7 B H_Q N^2\) FLOPs.

  3. Total Workload Summary: Specifically, regarding \textbf{Total MACs}, \(2 \left(1 + \frac{1}{R}\right) B N D^2 + 2 B N^2 D\) Furthermore, regarding \textbf{Total FLOPs}, \(4 \left(1 + \frac{1}{R}\right) B N D^2 + 4 B N^2 D + 7 B H_Q N^2\)

docs.title: Memory Footprint & KV Cache Reduction
docs.text:
Specifically, regarding \textbf{Parameter Count}, \(D^2 \left(2 + \frac{2}{R}\right) + D (H_Q d_k + 2 H_{KV} d_k)\) floats. Furthermore, regarding \textbf{Autoregressive Decoding KV Cache Footprint},

[ \text{KV Cache Size}{\text{GQA}} = 2 \cdot B \cdot H{KV} \cdot N \cdot d_k \cdot b = \frac{2 B N D \cdot b}{R} \text{ bytes} ] For \(R = 8\) (e.g. LLaMA-3 70B: \(H_Q = 64, H_{KV} = 8\)), KV Cache memory bandwidth is reduced by 87.5%.

docs.title: 5. Architectural Bottlenecks, Rank Collapse & Edge Cases
Subspace Capacity Saturation & Over-Sharing
docs.text: When \(R = H_Q / H_{KV}\) is excessively high (\(R > 16\)), query heads within the same group are forced to attend over identical Key-Value projection subspaces. This constrains the model's ability to maintain distinct context channels across different query heads.

docs.title: Memory Layout Striding Overhead in Explicit Interleaving
docs.text: Calling repeat_interleave(R) creates explicit physical tensor memory copies. If executed prior to matrix multiplication in un-fused PyTorch code, it incurs unnecessary memory allocation and memory bandwidth overhead.

docs.title: Dynamic Range Bounds in Low-Precision Training
docs.text: Under FP16 precision, averaging weights across groups during conversion from MHA can produce small parameter norm drifts. Proper normalization scaling must be preserved to prevent subnormal values.

docs.title: 6. Hardware Acceleration Blueprint & Triton Kernel Design
docs.text:
An optimized Triton kernel avoids explicit repeat_interleave by indexing KV heads directly via pointer arithmetic in SRAM: kv_head_idx = query_head_idx // R.

   ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
   │ Q: [B, H_Q, N, d_k]                                         │
   │ K: [B, H_KV, N, d_k]  (Un-expanded in DRAM!)                 │
   │ V: [B, H_KV, N, d_k]  (Un-expanded in DRAM!)                 │
   └──────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────┘
                                  │ Direct Head Pointer Arithmetic
                                  │ (kv_head = q_head / R)
                                  ▼
 ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 │                     Triton SRAM Scratchpad                     │
 │ 1. Load Query Tile Q_i [BLOCK_M, d_k] for head q_h             │
 │ 2. Load Key Tile K_j [BLOCK_N, d_k] for head kv_h = q_h // R   │
 │ 3. Compute In-Register Score: S_ij = Q_i @ K_j.T / sqrt(d_k)   │
 │ 4. Execute Online Softmax & Accumulate V_j Tile                │
 └────────────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────┘
                                  │ Streaming Output
                                  ▼
   ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
   │ Context Output: O [B, H_Q, N, d_k]                          │
   └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

docs.text:
1. Dynamic Group Allocation (AdaGQA): Dynamically adjust \(H_{KV}\) per transformer layer—allocating more KV heads to early layers requiring high capacity and fewer KV heads to deeper layers.
  2. Quantized Shared KV Caching: Combine GQA with INT4 / FP8 KV cache quantization to achieve over \(32\times\) memory reduction during 128k sequence length inference.
  3. Spectral KV Subspace Alignment: Apply SVD projection to standard MHA keys before grouping to ensure orthogonal subspace retention across shared KV heads.

docs.title: Granite-Hybrid Attention: Interleaved Mamba-2 State Space Architecture with Multi-Head Attention and Mixture-of-Experts
1. Executive Abstract & Architectural Motivation
docs.text:
Standard Multi-Head Self-Attention (MHSA) architectures suffer from quadratic time and memory complexity \(\mathcal{O}(L^2)\) with sequence length \(L\), imposing prohibitive overhead for long-context generation. Conversely, pure State Space Models (SSMs) like Mamba-2 achieve linear scaling \(\mathcal{O}(L \cdot D \cdot d_{\text{state}})\), but lack the non-local associative recall and exact token-matching precision of dense self-attention.

Granite-Hybrid Attention presents a unified hybrid sequence backbone that addresses this trade-off by: 1. Interleaved SSM-MHA Topology: Alternates between Mamba-2 state space recurrence layers and dense Multihead Attention (MHA) layers in a structured ratio \(R:1\) (e.g., \(R = 9\) SSM layers for every 1 MHA layer), balancing linear long-context throughput with exact associative memory retrieval. 2. Mamba-2 Structured State Space Model: Employs 1D gated convolutions and continuous-time state space discretization \(\Delta t\) to update hidden state \(h_t \in \mathbb{R}^{D \times d_{\text{state}}}\) in linear \(\mathcal{O}(L)\) time. 3. Top-\(k\) Token-Choice Mixture-of-Experts (MoE): Every hybrid block replaces the conventional Feed-Forward Network (FFN) with a top-\(k\) routed MoE layer, dynamically dispatching token hidden states to \(k\) out of \(E\) specialized expert networks.

docs.title: 2.1 Mamba-2 State Space Recurrence Branch
docs.text:
For hidden input \(X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D}\), the Mamba-2 layer expands input dimensions and evaluates 1D causal convolutions:

\[[X_{\text{ssm}}, Z] = X W_{\text{in}} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times 2 D_{\text{inner}}}, \quad D_{\text{inner}} = D \cdot \text{expand}\] \[\tilde{X}_{\text{ssm}} = \text{Conv1D}(X_{\text{ssm}}) \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D_{\text{inner}}}\] \[\Delta t = \text{softplus}\left( \tilde{X}_{\text{ssm}} W_{\Delta t} + b_{\Delta t} \right) \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D}, \quad A = -\exp(A_{\log}) \in \mathbb{R}^{D \times d_{\text{state}}}\]

The discrete-time state recurrence updates state matrix \(h_t \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times D \times d_{\text{state}}}\) at sequence position \(t\):

\[h_t = h_{t-1} \odot \exp(\Delta t_t \otimes A) + \left( \tilde{X}_{\text{ssm}, t, :D} \otimes \Delta t_t \right)\] \[y_t = \sum_{s=1}^{d_{\text{state}}} (h_{t, s} \odot D_s) \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times D}\] \[Y_{\text{mamba}} = \left( Y \odot \text{SiLU}(Z) \right) W_{\text{out}} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D}\]

docs.title: 2.2 Dense Multihead Attention (MHA) Branch
docs.text:
Every \((R+1)\)-th block executes dense scaled dot-product self-attention:

\[Q = X W_Q, \quad K = X W_K, \quad V = X W_V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times H \times d_h}\] \[A_{\text{attn}} = \text{Softmax}\left( \frac{Q K^T}{\sqrt{d_h}} + M_{\text{mask}} \right), \quad Y_{\text{attn}} = A_{\text{attn}} V \cdot W_O \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D}\]

docs.title: 2.3 Layer Routing & Interleaving Schedule
docs.text:
The sequence transformation \(Y\) is selected according to block counter \(c\):

\[Y = \begin{cases} Y_{\text{mamba}} & \text{if } (c \pmod{R+1}) < R \\ Y_{\text{attn}} & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}\]

docs.title: 2.4 Top-\(k\) Token-Choice Mixture-of-Experts (MoE)
docs.text:
Routing logits \(S \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times E}\) are evaluated across \(E\) expert networks:

\[S = Y W_{\text{router}} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times E}\]

The top-\(k\) expert indices \(\mathcal{I}\) and unnormalized gating weights \(W_{\text{raw}}\) are selected:

\[\mathcal{I}, W_{\text{raw}} = \text{TopK}(S, k, \text{dim}=-1)\] \[W_{\text{gate}} = \text{Softmax}(W_{\text{raw}}, \text{dim}=-1) \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times k}\]

The final layer output aggregates activated expert projections:

\[\text{Output} = Y + \sum_{j=1}^k W_{\text{gate}, j} \odot \text{Expert}_{\mathcal{I}_j}(Y) \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D}\]

docs.title: 4.1 FLOPs Computation Breakdown
docs.text:
Let \(B\) be batch size, \(L\) sequence length, \(D\) model dimension, \(d_{\text{state}}\) state dimension, \(E\) total experts, \(k\) active experts per token, \(D_{\text{ff}}\) FFN inner dimension, and \(R\) Mamba-to-Attention ratio.

  1. Mamba-2 Recurrence Step (\(R / (R+1)\) fraction of layers): In-projection: \(2 B L D (2 D_{\text{inner}}) = 8 B L D^2\) (assuming \(\text{expand} = 2\)) Furthermore, 1D Convolution: \(2 B L D_{\text{inner}} d_{\text{conv}} = 16 B L D\) (for \(d_{\text{conv}} = 4\)) Concurrently, Recurrence update: \(2 B L D d_{\text{state}}\) In this setting, Out-projection: \(2 B L D_{\text{inner}} D = 4 B L D^2\) $\(\text{FLOPs}_{\text{mamba}} = 12 B L D^2 + 2 B L D d_{\text{state}}\)$

  2. Dense MHA Step (\(1 / (R+1)\) fraction of layers): $\(\text{FLOPs}_{\text{attn}} = 4 B L D^2 + 2 B L^2 D\)$

  3. Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) Step: Router projection: \(2 B L D E\) Furthermore, Expert FFN evaluation (\(k\) active experts): \(k \times \left( 2 B L D D_{\text{ff}} + 2 B L D_{\text{ff}} D \right) = 4 k B L D D_{\text{ff}}\) $\(\text{FLOPs}_{\text{moe}} = 2 B L D E + 4 k B L D D_{\text{ff}}\)$
\[\text{FLOPs}_{\text{avg}} = \frac{R}{R+1} \text{FLOPs}_{\text{mamba}} + \frac{1}{R+1} \text{FLOPs}_{\text{attn}} + \text{FLOPs}_{\text{moe}}\]

docs.title: 4.2 MACs & Memory Footprint Analysis
docs.text:
Specifically, regarding \textbf{Multiply-Accumulate Operations (MACs)},

$\(\text{Total MACs} \approx \frac{R}{R+1} (6 B L D^2 + B L D d_{\text{state}}) + \frac{1}{R+1} (2 B L D^2 + B L^2 D) + 2 k B L D D_{\text{ff}}\)$ Specifically, regarding \textbf{Parameter Footprint},

$\(\Theta = (6 D^2 + D d_{\text{state}}) + 4 D^2 + (D E + 2 k E D_{\text{ff}})\)$ Specifically, regarding \textbf{Activation Footprint}, Furthermore, Mamba recurrence state: \(\mathcal{O}(B D d_{\text{state}})\) Concurrently, Dense MHA attention logit matrix: \(\mathcal{O}(B L^2)\) (at MHA layers) In this setting, MoE routing activation: \(\mathcal{O}(B L E + k B L D)\)

docs.title: 4.3 Asymptotic Scalability Comparison
docs.text: Specifically, regarding \textbf{Standard Dense Transformer}, \(\mathcal{O}(L^2 D + L D_{\text{ff}})\) compute per layer. Furthermore, regarding \textbf{Granite-Hybrid Architecture}, \(\mathcal{O}\left(\frac{R}{R+1} L D d_{\text{state}} + \frac{1}{R+1} L^2 D + k L D D_{\text{ff}}\right)\) compute per layer, slashing total generation FLOPs by \(80\%\) when \(R=9\).

docs.title: 5. Failure Modes, Rank Collapse & Edge Cases
5.1 MoE Router Collapse & Load Imbalance
docs.text: At the architectural level, the underlying operational mechanism reveals that the routing linear layer \(S = Y W_{\text{router}}\) can experience routing collapse, where a small subset of experts (\(< k\)) receives all token assignments while remaining experts receive zero tokens. Consequently, this dynamic induces structural implications wherein defeats sparse computational savings and causes HBM memory bandwidth bottlenecks on over-allocated expert GPUs. To systematically mitigate this constraint, the framework enforces an optimization protocol such that add an auxiliary load-balancing loss \(\mathcal{L}_{\text{balance}} = E \sum_{e=1}^E f_e P_e\), where \(f_e\) is token fraction routed to expert \(e\) and \(P_e\) is average routing probability.

docs.title: 5.2 Mamba State Recurrence Gradient Vanishing/Explosion
docs.text: At the architectural level, the underlying operational mechanism reveals that the discrete time step update \(h_t = h_{t-1} \exp(\Delta t_t A)\) relies on exponentiating \(\Delta t_t A\). If \(\Delta t_t\) projects to large positive values, \(\exp(\Delta t_t A)\) explodes for positive \(A\) or vanishes to absolute 0 for negative \(A\). To systematically mitigate this constraint, the framework enforces an optimization protocol such that constrain \(A = -\exp(A_{\log})\) to be strictly negative and apply softplus non-linearity to \(\Delta t\) projections.

docs.title: 5.3 MHA Layer Switching Context Shock
docs.text: At the architectural level, the underlying operational mechanism reveals that interleaving Mamba layers (linear state space memory) with dense MHA layers (quadratic KV cache) forces sharp transitions in representation geometry. If \(R\) is set too large (\(R > 16\)), the single MHA layer fails to re-align global associative keys.

docs.title: 6.1 Triton Strategy 1: Fused Mamba-2 Recurrence Kernel
docs.text:
Standard PyTorch sequential loops over sequence length \(L\) incur \(L\) distinct GPU kernel launches, causing catastrophic overhead.

Triton Optimization: Implement a persistent C++/Triton kernel that loads input sequence blocks into shared memory. Furthermore, Fuse 1D convolution, softplus timescale projection \(\Delta t\), and state recurrence \(h_t = h_{t-1} \exp(\Delta t A) + x \Delta t\) into a single threadblock sweep across sequence length \(L\). Concurrently, Keep state tensor \(h_t \in \mathbb{R}^{D \times d_{\text{state}}}\) entirely within SRAM registers.

docs.title: 6.2 Triton Strategy 2: FlashAttention-2 Interleaved Integration
docs.text: For dense MHA execution steps, invoke a Triton FlashAttention-2 kernel with BLOCK_M = 128 and BLOCK_N = 128. Furthermore, Compute online Softmax normalization in SRAM registers, eliminating DRAM reads and writes for the \([B, L, L]\) attention logit matrix.

docs.title: 6.3 Triton Strategy 3: Grouped GEMM Fused MoE Execution
docs.text:
Standard MoE implementations launch separate GEMM calls for each expert module, incurring high launch latencies for small token batches.

Triton Optimization: Group tokens by assigned expert index using a fast SRAM parallel radix sort. Furthermore, Execute a single Triton Grouped GEMM kernel where each threadblock handles token batches assigned to expert \(e\). Concurrently, Perform scatter-gather accumulation directly in GPU shared memory before writing back to global DRAM.

docs.text:
1. Chunked State Space Scan Integration (Mamba-2 SSD): Upgrade sequential Mamba scans to parallel scalar-identity chunked matrix multiplications, enabling \(3\times\) higher training throughput via Tensor Core matrix hardware.
  2. FP8 Quantized Expert FFN Execution: Execute top-\(k\) Mixture-of-Experts MLP GEMMs using FP8 (E4M3) precision on NVIDIA Hopper GPUs, doubling expert processing bandwidth.
  3. Shared Base Expert + Top-\(k\) Routed Experts: Introduce a permanent shared expert \(E_0\) alongside \(k\) routed experts to guarantee baseline representation stability across all tokens.
  4. Dynamic Layer-Adaptive \(R\) Interleaving Schedules: Replace static \(9:1\) ratios with dynamic depth schedules (e.g. \(15:1\) in early layers, \(3:1\) in deep reasoning layers).

docs.title: Griffin SSD: State Space Duality Recurrent Linear Attention Kernel
1. Executive Abstract & Architectural Motivation
docs.text:
Griffin SSD (State Space Duality, De et al., 2024 / Dao & Gu, 2024) establishes the formal mathematical equivalence between State Space Models (SSMs) and Recurrent Linear Attention (RLA). Standard attention incurs \(\mathcal{O}(L^2)\) time and space complexity, while SSMs operate via 1D state recurrences. Griffin SSD unifies these two paradigms.

By framing state space updates as an associative matrix state recurrence \(H_t = H_{t-1} + k_t \otimes v_t\), Griffin SSD computes linear sequence contextualization in \(\mathcal{O}(L \cdot D^2)\) time and \(\mathcal{O}(D^2)\) space. This matrix state duality enables parallel training via matrix multiplications (attention view) and constant-memory autoregressive decoding via state recurrences (SSM view).

docs.title: 2. Mathematical Formulations & Derivations
docs.text:
Given input sequence representations \(X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D}\), queries, keys, and values are projected as:

\[ Q = X W_Q \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D}, \quad K = X W_K \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D}, \quad V = X W_V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D} \]

docs.title: 1. Recurrent Matrix State Accumulation (SSM Dual View):
docs.text:
An associative 2D memory matrix \(H_t \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times D \times D}\) is initialized to zero (\(H_0 = \mathbf{0}\)) and updated recursively at step \(t\):

\[ H_t = H_{t-1} + k_t \otimes v_t = H_{t-1} + k_t v_t^\top \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times D \times D} \]

docs.title: 2. Context Retrieval & Matrix Contraction:
docs.text:
Query vector \(q_t \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times D}\) interacts with state matrix \(H_t\) via matrix-vector multiplication:

\[ y_t = q_t H_t = \sum_{j=1}^t \left( q_t^\top k_j \right) v_j \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times D} \]

docs.title: 3. Parallel Matrix Multiplication Dual View (Attention View):
docs.text:
During parallel training over sequence length \(L\), the unnormalized causal attention matrix \(A_{\text{causal}} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times L}\) is evaluated directly:

[ A_{\text{causal}} = \text{Tril}\left( Q K^\top \right) \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times L} ] [ Y = A_{\text{causal}} V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D} ]

The mathematical duality guarantees that \(y_t\) evaluated recursively equals row \(t\) of \(A_{\text{causal}} V\).

Final output projection produces \(O = Y W_O \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D}\).

docs.title: 3. Step-by-Step Tensor Execution Trace
docs.text:
Input: hidden_states [B, L, D]
  │
  ├──> Q = Linear(D, D)(hidden_states) ──> [B, L, D]
  ├──> K = Linear(D, D)(hidden_states) ──> [B, L, D]
  └──> V = Linear(D, D)(hidden_states) ──> [B, L, D]
         │
         ├──> Recurrent Path (Autoregressive Decoding):
         │      ├──> Outer Product: k_t.unsqueeze(-1) @ v_t.unsqueeze(-2) ──> [B, D, D]
         │      ├──> State Recurrence: H_t = H_{t-1} + OuterProduct ──> [B, D, D]
         │      └──> Output Query Contraction: y_t = (q_t.unsqueeze(-2) @ H_t).squeeze(-2) ──> [B, D]
         │
         ├──> Parallel Path (Training):
         │      ├──> Causal Matrix: A = Tril(Q @ K.T) ──> [B, L, L]
         │      └──> Parallel Context: Y = A @ V ──> [B, L, D]
         │
         └──> Linear(D, D)(Y) ──> Output: [B, L, D]

docs.title: Detailed Tensor Transformations:
docs.text: Step Operation Tensor Shape Description 1 Input \([B, L, D]\) Input sequence representation 2 Linear Projections \([B, L, D]\) \(Q, K, V\) states 3 Outer Product (\(k_t \otimes v_t\)) \([B, D, D]\) Per-step rank-1 outer product matrix update 4 State Matrix Accumulation \([B, D, D]\) Cumulative memory state \(H_t = H_{t-1} + k_t v_t^\top\) 5 Query State Projection \([B, D]\) Output extraction \(y_t = q_t H_t\) 6 Parallel Training Matrix (\(Q K^\top\)) \([B, L, L]\) Causal lower-triangular score matrix 7 Out Projection \([B, L, D]\) Final projection \(W_O\) to model dimension \(D\)

docs.title: Computational Workload and Arithmetic Complexity
docs.text:
The arithmetic complexity of the Griffin SSD kernel scales strictly linearly with respect to sequence length \(L\), establishing an \(\mathcal{O}(L \cdot D^2)\) asymptotic bound parameterized by batch size \(B\), sequence length \(L\), and hidden model dimension \(D\). The linear projection stage mapping input activations to query, key, and value states requires \(6 B L D^2\) FLOPs across operators \(W_Q, W_K, W_V\). During sequential recurrence or parallel chunk evaluation, recurrent outer-product state updates of the form \(k_t v_t^\top\) contribute \(2 B L D^2\) FLOPs across \(L\) temporal steps. The corresponding context retrieval phase via matrix-vector contraction \(q_t H_t\) consumes an equivalent \(2 B L D^2\) FLOPs, while the final linear projection \(W_O\) adds \(2 B L D^2\) FLOPs.

Cumulatively, the architecture requires \(6 B L D^2\) multiply-accumulate operations (MACs), yielding a total workload of \(12 B L D^2\) FLOPs. Unlike quadratic softmax attention which scales as \(\mathcal{O}(L^2 D)\), the computational intensity of Griffin SSD remains invariant to sequence expansion, presenting pronounced efficiency advantages when processing ultra-long sequences.

docs.title: Memory Footprint and State Allocation
docs.text: The model parameter footprint is defined by \(4 D^2\) static projection parameters. From an execution perspective, autoregressive decoding eliminates the conventional unbounded Key-Value cache growth. Instead, memory consumption is strictly bounded by a constant-size persistent state matrix \(H_t \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times D \times D}\), demanding \(\mathcal{O}(B \cdot D^2)\) memory per batch element. Consequently, memory allocations remain static across infinite generation horizons, removing memory-capacity thresholds as a barrier to persistent streaming inference.

docs.title: 5. Architectural Bottlenecks, Optimization Stability & Failure Modes
docs.text:
The unconstrained linear recurrence underpinning state space duality introduces distinct numerical and optimization challenges that manifest predominantly across deep architectures and extended context regimes. A fundamental failure mode stems from unbounded state magnitude accumulation in the un-gated recurrence \(H_t = H_{t-1} + k_t v_t^\top\). In the absence of continuous or discrete forgetting mechanisms, the matrix state norms grow monotonically with sequence length \(L\). Across extended sequence contexts (\(L > 65536\)), this monotonic accumulation precipitates numerical overflow under standard half-precision (FP16/BF16) training regimes and degrades gradient signal stability.

Concurrently, the absence of input-dependent recency weighting induces an isotropic temporal memory bias. Because every historical token contributes additively to \(H_t\) without exponential decay or associative gating, early context signals compete symmetrically with immediate token transitions, dampening local syntax resolution and degrading associative recall on dense retrieval benchmarks. Furthermore, while the linear recurrence achieves \(\mathcal{O}(L)\) scaling with respect to sequence length, the quadratic dependency on hidden dimensionality (\(D \times D\) state requiring \(2 D^2\) FLOPs per step) induces substantial computational overhead for wide layer configurations (\(D \ge 4096\)). This structural tradeoff necessitates chunked associative scanning kernels to maintain high Tensor Core occupancy.

docs.title: 6. Hardware Acceleration Blueprint & Triton Kernel Design
docs.text:
A Triton kernel for Griffin SSD executes parallel chunk scan operations, partitioning sequence length \(L\) into blocks and executing intra-chunk GEMM with inter-chunk state accumulation.

# Triton Parallel Scan Blueprint for Griffin SSD
import triton
import triton.language as tl

@triton.jit
def _griffin_ssd_chunk_kernel(
    Q_ptr, K_ptr, V_ptr, Out_ptr,
    stride_qb, stride_ql, stride_qd,
    L, D,
    BLOCK_L: tl.constexpr
):
    pid_b = tl.program_id(0)

    # Persistent matrix state memory in SRAM [D, D]
    h_state = tl.zeros((D, D), dtype=tl.float32)

    for t in range(L):
        q = tl.load(Q_ptr + pid_b * stride_qb + t * stride_ql + tl.arange(0, D))
        k = tl.load(K_ptr + pid_b * stride_qb + t * stride_ql + tl.arange(0, D))
        v = tl.load(V_ptr + pid_b * stride_qb + t * stride_ql + tl.arange(0, D))

        # Outer product accumulation
        h_state += k[:, None] * v[None, :]
        y_t = tl.sum(q[:, None] * h_state, axis=0)

        tl.store(Out_ptr + pid_b * stride_qb + t * stride_ql + tl.arange(0, D), y_t)

docs.title: 7. Next-Generation Innovations & Synthesis Opportunities
docs.text:
Advancements in state space duality and recurrent linear attention present multiple avenues for architectural synthesis. A foundational trajectory involves the incorporation of input-dependent decay gating into the recurrent update:

\[ H_t = \gamma_t H_{t-1} + k_t v_t^\top, \quad \text{where } \gamma_t = \sigma(W_{\gamma} x_t) \]

This parameterization dynamically bounds the spectral radius of \(H_t\), preventing activation overflow while equipping the network with adaptive forgetting dynamics characteristic of selective state space models like Mamba-2.

Furthermore, hybrid architectures that strategically interleave Griffin SSD linear recurrence blocks with selective scan or local sliding-window attention layers yield favorable Pareto frontiers, combining linear generation efficiency with fine-grained local syntactic discrimination. Concurrently, low-precision state quantization techniques—specifically casting the 2D matrix state \(H_t\) into FP8 or block-scaled micro-tensor formats—halve memory bandwidth traffic during state loading in SRAM-limited accelerator kernels, unlocking high-throughput long-context streaming capabilities.

docs.title: HALO-ReGLA: Hardware-Aware Linear Optics & Rectified Gated Linear Attention
1. Abstract & Theoretical Motivation
docs.text:
Standard Multi-Head Scaled Dot-Product Attention scales quadratically \(\mathcal{O}(L^2)\) with respect to sequence length \(L\) due to explicit materialization of softmax attention matrices. HALO-ReGLA (Hardware-Aware Linear Optics with Rectified Gated Linear Attention) resolves this quadratic barrier by combining Rotary Position Embedding (RoPE) with non-negative kernel feature maps \(\phi(x) = \text{ReLU}(x)\).

By applying associative matrix algebra to non-negative query and key states, HALO-ReGLA reformulates attention scoring as a continuous matrix state accumulator \(KV = \sum_{t=1}^L \widetilde{K}_t^\top V_t \in \mathbb{R}^{d_k \times d_k}\). This reduces time and memory activation complexity from quadratic \(\mathcal{O}(L^2)\) to strictly linear \(\mathcal{O}(L \cdot d_k^2)\) in sequence length \(L\), enabling long-context processing while preserving relative positional awareness through RoPE.

docs.title: 2. Mathematical Derivations & Formulations
docs.text: Let \(X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D}\) denote the input activation sequence, where \(B\) is batch size, \(L\) is sequence length, and \(D\) is model hidden dimension. Let \(H\) be the number of heads and \(d_k = D / H\) the head dimension.

docs.title: Linear Subspace Projections & RoPE Encoding:
docs.text:
Queries, Keys, and Values are projected via linear transformations:

\[ Q_{\text{raw}} = X W_Q \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D}, \quad K_{\text{raw}} = X W_K \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D}, \quad V = X W_V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D} \]

where \(W_Q, W_K, W_V \in \mathbb{R}^{D \times D}\). Reshaping yields \(Q_{\text{raw}}, K_{\text{raw}}, V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times L \times d_k}\).

Rotary Position Embedding (RoPE) is applied to raw queries and keys:

[ Q = \text{RoPE}(Q_{\text{raw}}) = \left( Q_{\text{raw}} \odot \mathbf{C} \right) + \left( \mathcal{R}(Q_{\text{raw}}) \odot \mathbf{S} \right) ] [ K = \text{RoPE}(K_{\text{raw}}) = \left( K_{\text{raw}} \odot \mathbf{C} \right) + \left( \mathcal{R}(K_{\text{raw}}) \odot \mathbf{S} \right) ]

where \(\mathbf{C} = \cos(m \boldsymbol{\theta})\), \(\mathbf{S} = \sin(m \boldsymbol{\theta})\), and \(\mathcal{R}(x) = [-x_{D/2:}, x_{:D/2}]\).

docs.title: Rectified Non-Negative Kernel Feature Map:
docs.text:
Non-negative feature maps \(\phi(x) = \text{ReLU}(x) = \max(0, x)\) project vectors into the positive orthant:

[ \widetilde{Q} = \text{ReLU}(Q) \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times L \times d_k} ] [ \widetilde{K} = \text{ReLU}(K) \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times L \times d_k} ]

docs.title: Associative Matrix-Vector State Accumulation (ReGLA):
docs.text:
Using non-negative inner products \(\langle \widetilde{Q}_i, \widetilde{K}_j \rangle = \sum_{m=1}^{d_k} \widetilde{Q}_{i, m} \widetilde{K}_{j, m} \ge 0\), the unnormalized contextual numerator is factorized via matrix associativity:

\[ \text{Num}_{b, h, i, e} = \sum_{j=1}^L \widetilde{Q}_{b, h, i, d} \left( \widetilde{K}_{b, h, j, d} \cdot V_{b, h, j, e} \right) = \sum_{d=1}^{d_k} \widetilde{Q}_{b, h, i, d} \cdot (KV)_{b, h, d, e} \]

where the global key-value associative matrix buffer \((KV) \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times d_k \times d_k}\) is accumulated as:

\[ (KV)_{b, h, d, e} = \sum_{j=1}^L \widetilde{K}_{b, h, j, d} \cdot V_{b, h, j, e} \]

The normalization denominator \(Z \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times L \times 1}\) is derived from the key sum vector:

[ (Z_{\text{sum}}){b, h, d} = \sum{j=1}^L \widetilde{K}{b, h, j, d} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times d_k} ] [ \text{Den}{b, h, i} = \left( \sum_{d=1}^{d_k} \widetilde{Q}{b, h, i, d} \cdot (Z{\text{sum}})_{b, h, d} \right) + \epsilon ]

where \(\epsilon = 10^{-8}\) prevents division by zero.

docs.title: Output Normalization & Projection:
docs.text: [ O_{b, h, i, e} = \frac{\text{Num}{b, h, i, e}}{\text{Den}{b, h, i}} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times L \times d_k} ] [ Y = \text{Concat}(O_1, \dots, O_H) \cdot W_O + b_O \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D}, \quad W_O \in \mathbb{R}^{D \times D} ]

docs.title: 3. Tensor Execution Flow & Dimensional Shape Tracing
docs.text:
Input: hidden_states [B, L, D]
  │
  ├──> Linear(D, D) [q_proj] ──> Q: [B, L, D] ──> view & transpose ──> Q: [B, H, L, d_k]
  ├──> Linear(D, D) [k_proj] ──> K: [B, L, D] ──> view & transpose ──> K: [B, H, L, d_k]
  └──> Linear(D, D) [v_proj] ──> V: [B, L, D] ──> view & transpose ──> V: [B, H, L, d_k]
                                │
                                ├──> Apply RoPE: Q = rope(Q), K = rope(K) ──> [B, H, L, d_k]
                                ├──> Apply ReLU: Q = ReLU(Q), K = ReLU(K) ──> [B, H, L, d_k]
                                │
                                ├──> Einsum("b h n d, b h n e -> b h d e", K, V) ──> KV: [B, H, d_k, d_k]
                                ├──> Sum K over sequence: z = K.sum(dim=2) ──> Z_sum: [B, H, d_k]
                                │
                                ├──> Einsum("b h n d, b h d e -> b h n e", Q, KV) ──> Num: [B, H, L, d_k]
                                ├──> Einsum("b h n d, b h d -> b h n", Q, Z_sum) + 1e-8 ──> Den: [B, H, L, 1]
                                ├──> Output Context = Num / Den ──> [B, H, L, d_k]
                                │
                                └──> transpose(1, 2).contiguous().view([B, L, D])
                                └──> Linear(D, D) [out_proj] ──> Output: [B, L, D]

docs.title: Operational & Computational Workload (FLOPs & MACs)
docs.text:
Let \(B\) be batch size, \(L\) sequence length, \(D\) model dimension, \(H\) heads, and \(d_k = D / H\).

  1. Linear Projections: \(W_Q, W_K, W_V, W_O\): \(4 \times 2 B L D^2 = 8 B L D^2\) FLOPs (\(4 B L D^2\) MACs).

  2. Rotary Position Embedding (RoPE): \(Q, K\) rotations: \(2 \times 3 B H L d_k = 6 B L D\) FLOPs.

  3. ReGLA Linear Associative Computations: Key-Value Matrix Outer Product (\(KV = K^\top V\)): \([B, H, d_k, L] \times [B, H, L, d_k] \implies 2 B H L d_k^2 = 2 B L D d_k\) FLOPs (\(B L D d_k\) MACs). Furthermore, Key Sum Vector (\(Z_{\text{sum}}\)): \(B H L d_k = B L D\) FLOPs. Concurrently, Numerator Contracting Product (\(\widetilde{Q} \cdot KV\)): \([B, H, L, d_k] \times [B, H, d_k, d_k] \implies 2 B H L d_k^2 = 2 B L D d_k\) FLOPs (\(B L D d_k\) MACs). In this setting, Denominator Normalization (\(\widetilde{Q} \cdot Z_{\text{sum}}\)): \(2 B H L d_k = 2 B L D\) FLOPs. Additionally, Elementwise Division: \(B L D\) FLOPs.

docs.title: Complexity Summary:
docs.text: Specifically, regarding \textbf{Total MACs}, \(4 B L D^2 + 2 B L D d_k\) Furthermore, regarding \textbf{Total FLOPs}, \(8 B L D^2 + 4 B L D d_k + 10 B L D\) Concurrently, regarding \textbf{Theoretical Speedup}, completely eliminates sequence quadratic term \(\mathcal{O}(L^2 D)\). Time complexity scales strictly linearly \(\mathcal{O}(L)\) with sequence length. In this setting, regarding \textbf{Memory Buffer Footprint}, stores state matrix \((KV) \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times d_k \times d_k}\) (\(B H d_k^2\) floats), avoiding \(B H L^2\) attention maps.

docs.title: 5. Architectural Bottlenecks, Rank Collapse & Failure Modes
Non-Negative Sparsity & Gradient Dead-Zones
docs.text: Because \(\widetilde{Q} = \text{ReLU}(Q)\) and \(\widetilde{K} = \text{ReLU}(K)\), any feature channel where \(Q_{b, h, i, d} \le 0\) or \(K_{b, h, j, d} \le 0\) has its gradient \(\frac{\partial \text{ReLU}}{\partial x} = 0\) set to zero. If initialization pushes activations into negative regions, large portions of query and key channels enter permanent gradient dead-zones.

docs.title: Recurrent State Saturation under Causal Decoding
docs.text: In long autoregressive decoding tasks (\(L > 100,000\)), un-decayed accumulation \((KV)_t = (KV)_{t-1} + \widetilde{K}_t^\top V_t\) causes state matrix norm \(\|KV\|_F\) to grow monotonically. Numerical precision degradation occurs in floating-point representations (FP16 / BF16).

docs.title: Head State Capacity Bound
docs.text: The associative memory buffer \((KV) \in \mathbb{R}^{d_k \times d_k}\) has a maximum rank of \(d_k\). For sequence lengths \(L \gg d_k\) (e.g., \(L=16384, d_k=64\)), the state matrix becomes heavily saturated, causing loss of fine-grained token position retrieval capacity.

docs.title: 6. Hardware Acceleration Blueprint & Triton Optimization Strategies
Fused Linear State Accumulation Triton Kernel
docs.text:
To maximize hardware utilization, Triton fused kernels accumulate the matrix state \((KV) \in \mathbb{R}^{d_k \times d_k}\) in GPU shared memory without materializing sequence-length intermediate tensors in DRAM.

       Global Memory (HBM)
      ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
      │ Q [B, H, L, d_k], K [B, H, L, d_k], V [B, H, L, d_k]   │
      └───────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────┘
                                  │ Direct Stream Block Loads
                                  ▼
 ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 │                   Triton SRAM Scratchpad                         │
 │ 1. Apply RoPE & ReLU in SIMD Registers: Q_relu, K_relu           │
 │ 2. Accumulate Local Block KV Matrix:                             │
 │    KV_tile += K_relu_block.T @ V_block   [d_k, d_k]              │
 │ 3. Accumulate Local Key Sum: Z_tile += K_relu_block.sum(dim=0)   │
 │ 4. Compute Output Tile: Num = Q_relu @ KV_tile                   │
 │ 5. Compute Denominator: Den = Q_relu @ Z_tile.T + 1e-8           │
 │ 6. Output_tile = Num / Den                                       │
 └────────────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────┘
                                  │ Stream Context Output
                                  ▼
      ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
      │ Context Output O [B, L, D]                             │
      └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

docs.title: Key Triton Implementation Guidelines:
docs.text:
1. Fused In-Register RoPE + ReLU Feature Mapping: Execute RoPE rotation and ReLU clipping directly inside SIMD registers prior to matrix multiplication, avoiding DRAM read/write cycles.
  2. SRAM State Accumulation: Maintain matrix state \((KV) \in \mathbb{R}^{d_k \times d_k}\) in SRAM L1 cache registers across tile loops over sequence blocks BLOCK_N, writing only final context vectors \(O\) back to global HBM.
  3. Smooth Activation Replacement: To prevent ReLU gradient dead-zones, replace standard ReLU with a smooth positive activation: [ \phi(x) = \text{ELU}(x) + 1.0 \quad \text{or} \quad \phi(x) = \text{Softplus}(x) ] guaranteeing continuous positive gradients across all feature channels.

docs.title: Hamming Attention: Continuous Relaxed Binarization & Distance Distillation
1. Abstract & Theoretical Motivation
docs.text:
Standard dot-product self-attention requires high-precision floating-point multiplications over real-valued query and key vectors \(\mathbf{q}, \mathbf{k} \in \mathbb{R}^d\). This creates high memory consumption and memory bandwidth bottlenecks during inference. Hamming Attention Distillation (HAD) addresses this issue by replacing standard real-valued similarity with continuous differentiable relaxations of binary Hamming distances.

By projecting query and key representations onto a continuous pseudo-binary hypercube \([-1, 1]^d\) using hyperbolic tangent scaling \(\mathbf{q}_b = \tanh(5.0 \cdot \gamma_Q \odot \mathbf{q})\), Hamming Attention evaluates pairwise similarity using normalized Hamming distances \(D_H(\mathbf{q}_b, \mathbf{k}_b) = \frac{d - \mathbf{q}_b \mathbf{k}_b^\top}{2}\). Integrating top-\(k\) sparsity filtering prunes long-tail token pairs, yielding energy-efficient attention computation suitable for low-power hardware and binarized neural network architectures.

docs.title: 2. Mathematical Derivations & Formulations
docs.text:
Given input sequence representations \(\mathbf{X} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times D}\), query, key, and value vectors for head \(h \in \{1, \dots, H\}\) are generated:

\[ \mathbf{Q}_h = \mathbf{X} \mathbf{W}_Q^{(h)} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times d}, \quad \mathbf{K}_h = \mathbf{X} \mathbf{W}_K^{(h)} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times d}, \quad \mathbf{V}_h = \mathbf{X} \mathbf{W}_V^{(h)} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times d} \]

docs.title: 1. Differentiable Binarization Transformation
docs.text:
Real-valued vectors are scaled by head-wise learnable parameters \(\gamma_Q^{(h)}, \gamma_K^{(h)} > 0\) and projected onto the continuous unit hypercube \([-1, 1]^d\) using a sharp hyperbolic tangent activation:

[ \mathbf{Q}_{b, h} = \tanh\left( 5.0 \cdot \gamma_Q^{(h)} \odot \mathbf{Q}h \right) \in [-1, 1]^{B \times N \times d} ] [ \mathbf{K}{b, h} = \tanh\left( 5.0 \cdot \gamma_K^{(h)} \odot \mathbf{K}_h \right) \in [-1, 1]^{B \times N \times d} ]

As scale factors increase, \(\mathbf{Q}_{b, h}\) and \(\mathbf{K}_{b, h}\) converge to exact binary bipolar codes \(\operatorname{sgn}(\mathbf{Q}_h) \in \{-1, +1\}^d\).

docs.title: 2. Continuous Hamming Distance Evaluation
docs.text:
The continuous relaxed Hamming distance between pseudo-binary vectors \(\mathbf{q}_b, \mathbf{k}_b \in [-1, 1]^d\) is computed via inner products:

\[ D_H(\mathbf{q}_b, \mathbf{k}_b) = \frac{d - \mathbf{q}_b \mathbf{k}_b^\top}{2} \in [0, d] \]

The negative unnormalized score matrix \(\mathbf{S}_h \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times N}\) is derived by scaling the inverse Hamming distance:

\[ \mathbf{S}_h = -\frac{D_H(\mathbf{Q}_{b, h}, \mathbf{K}_{b, h})}{\sqrt{d}} = \frac{\mathbf{Q}_{b, h} \mathbf{K}_{b, h}^\top - d \mathbf{J}_{N \times N}}{2 \sqrt{d}} \]

docs.title: 3. Top-\(K\) Sparsity Masking & Softmax Activation
docs.text:
To enforce sparsity, top-\(k\) thresholding is applied along sequence dimension \(N\), retaining \(K_{\text{keep}} = \max(1, \lfloor N \cdot \text{ratio} \rfloor)\) entries per row:

[ \mathbf{M}{\text{sparse}, i, j} = \begin{cases} 1 & \text{if } \mathbf{S}{i, j} \in \operatorname{TopK}(\mathbf{S}{i, :}, K{\text{keep}}) \ 0 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases} ] [ \widetilde{\mathbf{S}}h = \mathbf{S}h \odot \mathbf{M}{\text{sparse}} + (1 - \mathbf{M}{\text{sparse}}) \cdot (-10^9) + \mathbf{M}_{\text{mask}} ]

Softmax mapping and value matrix multiplication compute the final head output:

\[ \mathbf{A}_h = \operatorname{softmax}(\widetilde{\mathbf{S}}_h, \text{dim}=-1) \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times N}, \quad \mathbf{O}_h = \mathbf{A}_h \mathbf{V}_h \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times d} \]

Multi-head outputs are concatenated and linearly projected back:

\[ \mathbf{Y} = \operatorname{Concat}(\mathbf{O}_1, \dots, \mathbf{O}_H) \mathbf{W}_O \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times D} \]

docs.title: 3. Tensor Execution Flow & Dimensional Shape Tracing
docs.text:
Input Hidden States X [B, N, D]
  │
  ├──> Linear Projections (W_Q, W_K, W_V) -> Q, K, V [B, H, N, d]
  │
  ├──> Differentiable Hyperbolic Binarization:
  │    ├──> Q_b = Tanh(5.0 * gamma_Q * Q) ──────────────> [B, H, N, d]
  │    └──> K_b = Tanh(5.0 * gamma_K * K) ──────────────> [B, H, N, d]
  │
  ├──> Pairwise Hamming Distance Score Product:
  │    Dot = Q_b @ K_b^T ───────────────────────────────> [B, H, N, N]
  │    Dist = (d - Dot) / 2 ────────────────────────────> [B, H, N, N]
  │    S = -Dist / sqrt(d) ─────────────────────────────> [B, H, N, N]
  │
  ├──> Apply Masking & Top-K Sparsification:
  │    ├──> Additive Mask: S = S + (1 - Mask) * (-1e9)
  │    ├──> TopK Selection: top_idx = TopK(S, k=K_keep)
  │    └──> Sparse Masking: S_sparse = S * Sparse_Mask + (1 - Sparse_Mask) * (-1e9)
  │
  └──> Softmax & Value Aggregation:
       A = Softmax(S_sparse, dim=-1) ───────────────────> [B, H, N, N]
       Context = A @ V ─────────────────────────────────> [B, H, N, d]
       Y = Reshape(Context) @ W_O ──────────────────────> [B, N, D]

docs.title: Detailed Shape Progression Table
docs.text: Step Operation Input Tensor Shapes Output Tensor Shape 1 Projections (\(W_Q, W_K, W_V\)) X: [B, N, D] Q, K, V: [B, N, D] 2 Multi-Head Permute Q, K, V: [B, N, D] Q, K, V: [B, H, N, d] 3 Query Binarization (\(\tanh\)) Q: [B, H, N, d], gamma_Q: [H, 1] Q_b: [B, H, N, d] 4 Key Binarization (\(\tanh\)) K: [B, H, N, d], gamma_K: [H, 1] K_b: [B, H, N, d] 5 Inner Product Matrix Q_b: [B, H, N, d], K_b^T: [B, H, d, N] Dot: [B, H, N, N] 6 Hamming Distance Matrix Dot: [B, H, N, N] Dist: [B, H, N, N] 7 Top-\(K\) Sparsification S: [B, H, N, N], sparsity_ratio S_sparse: [B, H, N, N] 8 Softmax Normalization S_sparse: [B, H, N, N] A: [B, H, N, N] 9 Context Aggregation A: [B, H, N, N], V: [B, H, N, d] Context: [B, H, N, d] 10 Output Linear Projection Context: [B, H, N, d] Y: [B, N, D]

docs.title: FLOP & MAC Counting
docs.text:
1. Linear Projections (\(W_Q, W_K, W_V, W_O\)): \(8 B N D^2\) FLOPs.
  2. Binarization Activation (\(\tanh\)): \(2 \times (2 B H N d) = 4 B N D\) FLOPs.
  3. Pseudo-Binary Score Inner Product (\(\mathbf{Q}_b \mathbf{K}_b^\top\)): \(2 B H N^2 d = 2 B N^2 D\) FLOPs.
  4. Top-\(K\) Selection: \(\mathcal{O}(B H N^2 \log K_{\text{keep}})\) comparison operations.
  5. Context Aggregation (\(\mathbf{A} \mathbf{V}\)): \(2 B H N^2 d = 2 B N^2 D\) FLOPs.

Total Computational Cost: [ \text{Total FLOPs} = 8 B N D^2 + 4 B N^2 D + 4 B N D ]

During quantized inference, floating-point multiplications for \(\mathbf{Q}_b \mathbf{K}_b^\top\) convert to bitwise XNOR and POPCOUNT logic operations.

docs.title: Memory Footprint & Tensor Store
docs.text: Specifically, regarding \textbf{Parameters}, \(4 D^2 + 2 H\) floats (where \(\gamma_Q, \gamma_K\) contribute \(2 H\) scalars). Furthermore, regarding \textbf{Activation Memory}, Concurrently, Pseudo-Binary Vectors (\(\mathbf{Q}_b, \mathbf{K}_b\)): \(2 B H N d = 2 B N D\) floats (or 1-bit quantized integers). In this setting, Score & Sparse Mask Tensors (\(\mathbf{S}, \mathbf{M}_{\text{sparse}}\)): \(2 B H N^2\) floats. Additionally, Peak Memory Footprint: \(\mathcal{O}(B N D + B H N^2)\).

docs.title: 5. Architectural Bottlenecks, Rank Collapse & Failure Modes
docs.text:
1. Top-\(K\) Non-Differentiability: Sorting via torch.topk creates zero gradients \(\frac{\partial \mathbf{M}_{\text{sparse}}}{\partial \mathbf{S}} = 0\), requiring straight-through estimators (STE) or soft thresholding to avoid vanishing gradients during backpropagation.
  2. Hypercube Saturation: Large scale factors \(\gamma > 10.0\) cause \(\tanh(5.0 \gamma \mathbf{Q})\) to saturate at \(\pm 1\), causing gradient vanishing across early training steps.
  3. Quadratic Score Footprint: Because Hamming Attention instantiates dense \(N \times N\) score matrices prior to top-\(k\) pruning, spatial complexity remains quadratic \(\mathcal{O}(N^2)\).

docs.title: 6. Hardware Acceleration Blueprint & Triton Optimization Strategies
Memory Access & Vectorization Barriers
docs.text: In standard PyTorch, executing torch.topk(scores) writes full \(B \times H \times N \times N\) score matrices back to DRAM before picking top elements.

docs.title: High-Performance Triton Kernel Fusion Strategy
docs.text:
1. Fused POPCOUNT & Top-\(K\) Flash Kernel: Implement a Triton kernel that packs 1-bit binarized query and key codes into 32-bit integers (int32). Compute Hamming distance using hardware POPCOUNT and bitwise XNOR instructions (__popc(q ^ k)) directly in SRAM registers.
# Triton Pseudocode for Fused Bitwise POPCOUNT Hamming Kernel
@triton.jit
def _hamming_fused_popcount_kernel(
    Q_bit_ptr, K_bit_ptr, V_ptr, Out_ptr,
    N, D, BLOCK_N: tl.constexpr, TOP_K: tl.constexpr
):
    # Load packed 1-bit integer query block [BLOCK_N, d_packed]
    q_packed = tl.load(Q_bit_ptr + offsets_q)
    k_packed = tl.load(K_bit_ptr + offsets_k)

    # Compute Hamming distance via hardware Bitwise XNOR & POPCOUNT in SRAM
    xor_val = q_packed ^ k_packed
    hamming_dist = tl.popc(xor_val)
    scores = -hamming_dist * scale

    # Keep top-K elements in register min-heap without full DRAM sort
    topk_scores, topk_idx = tl.topk(scores, K=TOP_K)
    p = tl.softmax(topk_scores)
    acc += tl.dot(p, v_selected)
  1. Register Min-Heap Sparsification: Maintain a local min-heap inside GPU registers to retain the top-\(K\) elements dynamically without writing non-selected entries to DRAM.

docs.title: HGRN-2 Gated DeltaNet: Interleaved Hierarchical Linear Recurrence & Dense Attention Architecture
1. Executive Abstract & Architectural Motivation
docs.text:
Pure linear recurrent networks provide \(\mathcal{O}(L)\) time and constant decoding memory, but can struggle with exact long-range pairwise token retrieval. Full Multi-Head Self-Attention achieves exact retrieval but suffers from \(\mathcal{O}(L^2)\) quadratic complexity. The HGRN-2 Gated DeltaNet Architecture solves this trade-off by arranging a sequence of \(N\) Transformer layers in a hybrid ratio \(R:1\).

In this hybrid topology, \(R\) consecutive layers execute fast linear \(\mathcal{O}(L)\) HGRN-2 / Gated DeltaNet recurrence, while every \((R+1)\)-th layer executes a dense Multi-Head Attention pass. This interleaved paradigm retains high throughput and low memory footprint while preserving exact retrieval capabilities.

docs.title: 2. Mathematical Formulations & Derivations
docs.text:
Given input sequence \(X^{(0)} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D}\), layer \(l \in \{0, \dots, N-1\}\) executes based on hybrid ratio \(R\):

\[ X^{(l+1)} = \begin{cases} \text{MHA-Block}\left( X^{(l)} \right), & \text{if } l \pmod{R+1} = R \\ \text{HGRN2-Block}\left( X^{(l)} \right), & \text{otherwise} \end{cases} \]

docs.title: Layer Type 1: HGRN-2 Linear Recurrence Layer (\(l \pmod{R+1} \ne R\)):
docs.text: [ f_t = \sigma(W_f X_t^{(l)}), \quad i_t = \sigma(W_i X_t^{(l)}) ] [ h_t = \text{Clamp}\left( f_t \odot h_{t-1} + i_t \odot X_t^{(l)}, -1.0, 1.0 \right) ] [ X^{(l+1)} = X^{(l)} + W_O h ]

docs.title: Layer Type 2: Dense Multi-Head Attention Layer (\(l \pmod{R+1} = R\)):
docs.text: [ Q = X^{(l)} W_Q, \quad K = X^{(l)} W_K, \quad V = X^{(l)} W_V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times L \times d_k} ] [ A = \text{Softmax}\left( \frac{Q K^\top}{\sqrt{d_k}} + M_{\text{causal}} \right) \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times L \times L} ] [ X^{(l+1)} = X^{(l)} + (A V) W_O ]

docs.title: 3. Step-by-Step Tensor Execution Trace
docs.text:
Input: X_0 [B, L, D]
  │
  ├──> Layer 0 (HGRN-2 Linear): X_1 = HGRN2_Block(X_0) ──> [B, L, D]
  ├──> Layer 1 (HGRN-2 Linear): X_2 = HGRN2_Block(X_1) ──> [B, L, D]
  │    ... (R linear layers)
  ├──> Layer R (Dense MHA Bypass): X_{R+1} = MHA_Block(X_R) ──> [B, L, D]
  │
  └──> Repeat hybrid stack for N layers ──> Final Output: [B, L, D]

docs.title: Detailed Tensor Transformations:
docs.text: Step Operation Tensor Shape Description 1 Input \([B, L, D]\) Input hidden state sequence 2 HGRN-2 Linear Layers \([B, L, D]\) \(R\) consecutive linear recurrence layers (\(\mathcal{O}(L)\)) 3 Dense MHA Layer \([B, L, D]\) 1 dense Multi-Head Attention layer (\(\mathcal{O}(L^2)\)) 4 Final Stack Output \([B, L, D]\) Hybrid representation sequence

docs.title: FLOP and MAC Breakdown (\(N\) Total Layers, \(R\) Hybrid Ratio):
docs.text:
Specifically, regarding \textbf{Number of HGRN-2 Layers}, \(N \cdot \frac{R}{R+1}\) layers Furthermore, regarding \textbf{Number of MHA Layers}, \(N \cdot \frac{1}{R+1}\) layers Concurrently, regarding \textbf{Total FLOPs},

\[ \text{Total FLOPs} = N \cdot \left( \frac{R}{R+1} \cdot 12 B L D^2 + \frac{1}{R+1} \cdot (16 B L D^2 + 4 B L^2 D) \right) \]

docs.title: Memory Footprint:
docs.text: Specifically, regarding \textbf{Static Weights}, \(N \times 4 D^2\) parameters. Furthermore, regarding \textbf{Decoding KV Cache Footprint}, reduced by factor of \((R+1)\), storing KV cache only for the \(\frac{N}{R+1}\) MHA layers.

docs.title: 5. Failure Modes, Rank Collapse & Edge Cases
docs.text:
1. Hybrid Ratio Miscalibration: Setting \(R\) too large (\(R > 16\)) degrades performance on complex retrieval tasks; setting \(R\) too small (\(R = 1\)) loses linear throughput benefits.
  2. Gradient Vanishing Across Linear Blocks: Long chains of linear recurrent layers require careful residual scaling to prevent gradient decay.

docs.title: HGRN2 Gated Layer: Hierarchical Gated Linear Recurrent Layer v2
docs.text: Family: Gated Linear Recurrences · NeuralOps Registry ID: hgrn2_gated_layer

docs.title: Executive Abstract
docs.text:
HGRN2 (Qin et al., 2024) expands upon linear recurrence by introducing an outer-product state representation with decoupled forgetting and input gates. Achieves outstanding compute efficiency and modeling capacity on billion-parameter LLMs.

In NeuralOps, hgrn2_gated_layer is integrated into the universal attention dispatch table, featuring full support for the 3-level fallback hierarchy, automatic shape validation, and end-to-end autograd backwards passes.

docs.title: Mathematical Formulation
docs.text:
The core operator computation is defined as:

\[ h_t = f_t \odot h_{t-1} + (1 - f_t) \odot (i_t \odot x_t), \quad y_t = o_t \odot (W_y h_t) \]

During execution, inputs \(Q, K, V\) are projected to dimension \(d\). In the causal configuration, lower-triangular masking ensures that tokens only attend to past and current time-steps, preserving autoregressive invariants.

docs.title: HGRN-2 Layer: Hierarchically Gated Recurrent Network v2 Element-Wise Recurrence
1. Executive Abstract & Architectural Motivation
docs.text:
Standard Multi-Head Attention scales quadratically \(\mathcal{O}(L^2)\) in time and memory. The Hierarchically Gated Recurrent Network v2 (HGRN-2 Layer, Qin et al., 2024) provides an element-wise linear recurrence block that operates in strictly \(\mathcal{O}(L)\) sequence time and constant \(\mathcal{O}(D)\) state memory.

HGRN-2 replaces 2D matrix recurrences with element-wise vector recurrence updates modulated by dynamic sigmoidal forget gates \(f_t = \sigma(W_f x_t)\) and input gates \(i_t = \sigma(W_i x_t)\). By incorporating residual state clipping bounds (\(\text{Clamp}(h_t, -C, C)\) with \(C = 1.0\)), HGRN-2 prevents state explosion and vanishing gradient instability, enabling fast and stable long-sequence modeling.

docs.title: 2. Mathematical Formulations & Derivations
docs.text:
Given input sequence representations \(X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D}\), gating signals are derived per step \(t\):

[ f_t = \sigma(W_f x_t + b_f) \in (0, 1)^D \quad \text{(Forget Gate)} ] [ i_t = \sigma(W_i x_t + b_i) \in (0, 1)^D \quad \text{(Input Gate)} ]

docs.title: Element-Wise Recurrent State Update & Bounded Clipping:
docs.text:
State vector \(h_t \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times D}\) is updated recursively:

[ \widetilde{h}t = f_t \odot h{t-1} + i_t \odot x_t \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times D} ] [ h_t = \text{Clamp}(\widetilde{h}_t, -C, C) \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times D} \quad \text{where } C = 1.0 ]

docs.title: Output Gating & Transformation:
docs.text:
Output representation \(y_t \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times D}\) is produced via output projection:

\[ y_t = W_O h_t \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times D} \]

Stacking outputs across steps produces \(Y = [y_1, \dots, y_L] \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D}\).

docs.title: 3. Step-by-Step Tensor Execution Trace
docs.text:
Input: hidden_states [B, L, D]
  │
  ├──> Linear(D, D)[W_f] ──> Sigmoid ──> Forget Gate f: [B, L, D]
  ├──> Linear(D, D)[W_i] ──> Sigmoid ──> Input Gate i: [B, L, D]
  │
  ├──> Recurrent Loop over sequence steps t = 1 ... L:
  │      ├──> Element-wise update: h_tilde_t = f_t * h_{t-1} + i_t * x_t ──> [B, D]
  │      └──> Bounded Clamping: h_t = Clamp(h_tilde_t, -1.0, 1.0) ──> [B, D]
  │
  ├──> Stack states across L ──> H: [B, L, D]
  └──> Linear(D, D)[W_O](H) ──> Output: [B, L, D]

docs.title: Detailed Tensor Transformations:
docs.text: Step Operation Tensor Shape Description 1 Input \([B, L, D]\) Input hidden state sequence 2 Forget Gate Generation \([B, L, D]\) Sigmoidal gate \(f_t = \sigma(W_f x_t)\) 3 Input Gate Generation \([B, L, D]\) Sigmoidal gate \(i_t = \sigma(W_i x_t)\) 4 Element-Wise Scan Update \([B, L, D]\) Recurrent state updates \(\widetilde{h}_t = f_t \odot h_{t-1} + i_t \odot x_t\) 5 Bounded State Clamping \([B, L, D]\) Clamping within \([-1.0, 1.0]\) 6 Out Projection \([B, L, D]\) Final linear transformation \(W_O\)

docs.title: FLOP and MAC Breakdown (\(B\): Batch, \(L\): Length, \(D\): Model Dim):
docs.text:
Specifically, regarding \textbf{Gate Projections (\(W_f, W_i\))}, \(4 B L D^2\) FLOPs Furthermore, regarding \textbf{Element-wise Recurrence & Clamping}, \(4 B L D\) FLOPs Concurrently, regarding \textbf{Output Projection (\(W_O\))}, \(2 B L D^2\) FLOPs

Total Complexity: Specifically, regarding \textbf{Total MACs}, \(3 B L D^2\) Furthermore, regarding \textbf{Total FLOPs}, \(6 B L D^2\) (\(\mathcal{O}(L)\) strictly linear sequence scaling)

docs.title: Memory Footprint:
docs.text: Specifically, regarding \textbf{Static Weights}, \(3 D^2\) parameters. Furthermore, regarding \textbf{Decoding Memory Footprint}, bounded by \(\mathcal{O}(B \cdot D)\) state memory per step.

docs.title: 5. Failure Modes, Rank Collapse & Edge Cases
docs.text:
1. State Saturation under Extreme Inputs: Constant clamping at \([-1.0, 1.0]\) can clip gradient magnitude if features frequently saturate the boundary.
  2. Channel Independence Bottleneck: Element-wise recurrence operates independently across hidden channels, relying entirely on linear projections for cross-channel mixing.
  3. Sequential Loop Latency in Unfused Execution: PyTorch step loops introduce CPU launch latencies.

docs.title: 6. Hardware Acceleration Blueprint & Triton Kernel Design
docs.text:
A Triton kernel for HGRN-2 Layer fuses gate calculation, element-wise recurrence, and state clamping inside GPU SRAM.

# Triton Fused HGRN-2 Scan Blueprint
import triton
import triton.language as tl

@triton.jit
def _hgrn2_layer_fused_kernel(
    X_ptr, W_f_ptr, W_i_ptr, Out_ptr,
    stride_xb, stride_xl, stride_xd,
    L, D,
    BLOCK_D: tl.constexpr
):
    pid_b = tl.program_id(0)
    offs_d = tl.arange(0, BLOCK_D)

    h_state = tl.zeros((BLOCK_D,), dtype=tl.float32)
    for t in range(L):
        x_t = tl.load(X_ptr + pid_b * stride_xb + t * stride_xl + offs_d)

        f_t = tl.sigmoid(tl.dot(x_t[None, :], W_f_ptr))
        i_t = tl.sigmoid(tl.dot(x_t[None, :], W_i_ptr))

        h_state = f_t * h_state + i_t * x_t
        h_state = tl.clamp(h_state, -1.0, 1.0)

        tl.store(Out_ptr + pid_b * stride_xb + t * stride_xl + offs_d, h_state)

docs.title: HGRN-2 Outer: Outer-Product Associative Matrix State Linear Recurrence Block
1. Executive Abstract & Architectural Motivation
docs.text:
Standard Multi-Head Attention requires materializing an \(L \times L\) attention matrix, scaling quadratically \(\mathcal{O}(L^2)\) in time and space. The HGRN-2 Outer Block (Hierarchically Gated Recurrent Network v2 Outer Product) extends element-wise HGRN-2 recurrence to 2D associative state matrices \(S_t \in \mathbb{R}^{D \times D}\).

HGRN-2 Outer updates memory state \(S_t\) via convex interpolation between past memory \(S_{t-1}\) and current key-value outer product \(k_t \otimes v_t\): \(S_t = f_t \odot S_{t-1} + (1 - f_t) \odot (k_t v_t^\top)\). Query inputs \(x_t\) interact directly with \(S_t\) via matrix-vector multiplication \(y_t = S_t x_t\). This formulation combines 2D matrix associative expressivity with linear \(\mathcal{O}(L \cdot D^2)\) execution and constant \(\mathcal{O}(D^2)\) decoding memory.

docs.title: 2. Mathematical Formulations & Derivations
docs.text:
Given input sequence representations \(X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D}\), key, value, and forget gate states are projected as:

[ k_t = W_k x_t \in \mathbb{R}^D, \quad v_t = W_v x_t \in \mathbb{R}^D ] [ f_t = \sigma(W_f x_t + b_f) \in (0, 1)^D \quad \text{(Dynamic Forget Gate)} ]

docs.title: Convex Outer-Product Associative Recurrence:
docs.text:
Memory matrix \(S_t \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times D \times D}\) is initialized to zero (\(S_0 = \mathbf{0}\)) and updated via convex combination:

\[ S_t = f_t \odot S_{t-1} + (1 - f_t) \odot \left( k_t \otimes v_t \right) = f_t \odot S_{t-1} + (1 - f_t) \odot (k_t v_t^\top) \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times D \times D} \]

docs.title: Query State Readout & Output Projection:
docs.text:
Input vector \(x_t\) queries memory state \(S_t\):

\[ y_t = S_t x_t \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times D} \]

Stacking \(y_t\) across time steps produces \(Y = \text{Concat}(y_1, \dots, y_L) W_{\text{out}} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D}\).

docs.title: 3. Step-by-Step Tensor Execution Trace
docs.text:
Input: hidden_states [B, L, D]
  │
  ├──> Linear(D, D)[W_k] ──> k_t: [B, L, D]
  ├──> Linear(D, D)[W_v] ──> v_t: [B, L, D]
  ├──> Linear(D, D)[W_f] ──> Sigmoid ──> Forget Gate f_t: [B, L, D]
  │
  ├──> Recurrent Loop over sequence steps t = 1 ... L:
  │      ├──> Outer Product: k_t.unsqueeze(-1) @ v_t.unsqueeze(-2) ──> [B, D, D]
  │      ├──> Convex Interpolation: S_t = f_t * S_{t-1} + (1 - f_t) * OuterProduct ──> [B, D, D]
  │      └──> State Readout: y_t = (S_t @ x_t.unsqueeze(-1)).squeeze(-1) ──> [B, D]
  │
  ├──> Stack states across L ──> Y_stack: [B, L, D]
  └──> Linear(D, D)[W_out](Y_stack) ──> Output: [B, L, D]

docs.text:
Specifically, regarding \textbf{Input Projections (\(W_k, W_v, W_f\))}, \(6 B L D^2\) FLOPs Furthermore, regarding \textbf{Outer Product Calculations (\(k_t v_t^\top\))}, \(L \times (2 B D^2) = 2 B L D^2\) FLOPs Concurrently, regarding \textbf{Convex State Accumulation}, \(L \times (3 B D^2) = 3 B L D^2\) FLOPs In this setting, regarding \textbf{Query Readout (\(S_t x_t\))}, \(L \times (2 B D^2) = 2 B L D^2\) FLOPs Additionally, regarding \textbf{Output Projection (\(W_{\text{out}}\))}, \(2 B L D^2\) FLOPs

Total Complexity: Specifically, regarding \textbf{Total MACs}, \(7.5 B L D^2\) Furthermore, regarding \textbf{Total FLOPs}, \(15 B L D^2\) (\(\mathcal{O}(L)\) strictly linear sequence scaling)

docs.title: Memory Footprint:
docs.text: Specifically, regarding \textbf{Static Weights}, \(4 D^2\) parameters. Furthermore, regarding \textbf{Decoding Memory Footprint}, bounded by \(\mathcal{O}(B \cdot D^2)\) state memory per sequence.

docs.title: 5. Failure Modes, Rank Collapse & Edge Cases
docs.text:
1. State Saturation under \(f_t \to 1\): If forget gate \(f_t \to 1\), new outer products are ignored, freezing state \(S_t\).
  2. Memory Erase under \(f_t \to 0\): If \(f_t \to 0\), past memory is completely wiped, reducing the model to 1-step windowing.
  3. Sequential Loop Latency in Unfused Execution: PyTorch step loops introduce CPU launch latencies.

docs.title: 6. Hardware Acceleration Blueprint & Triton Kernel Design
docs.text:
A Triton kernel for HGRN-2 Outer implements parallel chunk scan algorithms, keeping 2D matrix state \(S_t\) inside GPU SRAM.

# Triton Parallel Scan Blueprint for HGRN-2 Outer
import triton
import triton.language as tl

@triton.jit
def _hgrn2_outer_chunk_kernel(
    X_ptr, K_ptr, V_ptr, F_ptr, Out_ptr,
    stride_xb, stride_xl, stride_xd,
    L, D,
    BLOCK_D: tl.constexpr
):
    pid_b = tl.program_id(0)

    s_state = tl.zeros((D, D), dtype=tl.float32)
    for t in range(L):
        x_t = tl.load(X_ptr + pid_b * stride_xb + t * stride_xl + tl.arange(0, D))
        k_t = tl.load(K_ptr + pid_b * stride_xb + t * stride_xl + tl.arange(0, D))
        v_t = tl.load(V_ptr + pid_b * stride_xb + t * stride_xl + tl.arange(0, D))
        f_t = tl.load(F_ptr + pid_b * stride_xb + t * stride_xl + tl.arange(0, D))

        # Convex interpolation
        s_state = f_t[:, None] * s_state + (1.0 - f_t[:, None]) * (k_t[:, None] * v_t[None, :])
        y_t = tl.sum(s_state * x_t[:, None], axis=0)

        tl.store(Out_ptr + pid_b * stride_xb + t * stride_xl + tl.arange(0, D), y_t)

docs.title: HLA Attention: Hadamard Linear Attention via Outer-Product Associative Recurrence
1. Executive Abstract & Architectural Motivation
docs.text:
Standard Multi-Head Attention scales quadratically \(\mathcal{O}(L^2)\) in sequence length \(L\), creating a bottleneck for long-context execution. Hadamard Linear Attention (HLA Attention) eliminates the explicit \(L \times L\) attention matrix by maintaining a running associative 2D state matrix \(H_t \in \mathbb{R}^{d_k \times d_k}\) per head across time steps.

At each token position \(t\), HLA Attention computes the outer product of Key vectors \(K_t\) and Value vectors \(V_t\), accumulating them into the state matrix \(H_t = H_{t-1} + K_t \otimes V_t\). Query vectors \(Q_t\) interact directly with \(H_t\) via matrix-vector multiplication. By using matrix associativity, HLA reduces time complexity to \(\mathcal{O}(L \cdot d_k^2)\) and retains a constant \(\mathcal{O}(d_k^2)\) memory footprint during causal autoregressive decoding.

docs.title: 2. Mathematical Formulations & Derivations
docs.text:
Given input sequence representations \(X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D}\), queries, keys, and values are projected as:

\[ Q = X W_Q \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D}, \quad K = X W_K \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D}, \quad V = X W_V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D} \]

Multi-head formatting yields \(Q, K, V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times L \times d_k}\) with \(d_k = D / H\).

docs.title: Outer-Product State Recurrence:
docs.text:
The hidden associative state matrix \(H_t \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times d_k \times d_k}\) is initialized to zero (\(H_0 = \mathbf{0}\)) and updated recursively:

\[ H_t = H_{t-1} + K_t \otimes V_t = H_{t-1} + K_t^\top V_t \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times d_k \times d_k} \]

docs.title: Query Context Extraction:
docs.text:
The contextualized output vector \(O_t \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times d_k}\) for query \(Q_t\) is evaluated as:

\[ O_t = Q_t H_t = \sum_{j=1}^t \left( Q_t K_j^\top \right) V_j \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times d_k} \]

Stacking outputs across all sequence steps \(t = 1, \dots, L\) produces \(O \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times L \times d_k}\).

docs.title: Final Output Projection:
docs.text:
Multi-head outputs are concatenated and projected to model dimension \(D\):

\[ Y = \text{Concat}(O_1, \dots, O_H) W_O \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D} \]

docs.title: 3. Step-by-Step Tensor Execution Trace
docs.text:
Input: hidden_states [B, L, D]
  │
  ├──> Q = Linear(D, D)(hidden_states) ──> [B, H, L, d_k]
  ├──> K = Linear(D, D)(hidden_states) ──> [B, H, L, d_k]
  └──> V = Linear(D, D)(hidden_states) ──> [B, H, L, d_k]
         │
         ├──> Recurrent Loop over sequence steps t = 1 ... L:
         │      ├──> Outer Product: K_t.transpose(-2, -1) @ V_t ──> [B, H, d_k, d_k]
         │      ├──> State Recurrence: H_t = H_{t-1} + OuterProduct ──> [B, H, d_k, d_k]
         │      └──> Query Interaction: O_t = Q_t @ H_t ──> [B, H, d_k]
         │
         ├──> Stack outputs across L ──> Context: [B, H, L, d_k]
         ├──> transpose(1, 2) ──> contiguous() ──> [B, L, D]
         └──> Linear(D, D)(Context) ──> Output: [B, L, D]
