docs.text: Step Operation Tensor Shape Description 1 Input \([B, L, D]\) Input hidden state sequence 2 Linear Projections \([B, H, L, d_k]\) \(Q, K, V\) states 3 Outer Product (\(K_t \otimes V_t\)) \([B, H, d_k, d_k]\) Rank-1 outer-product memory update per step 4 State Matrix Accumulation \([B, H, d_k, d_k]\) Cumulative memory state \(H_t = H_{t-1} + K_t^\top V_t\) 5 Query State Projection \([B, H, d_k]\) Per-step context extraction \(O_t = Q_t H_t\) 6 Sequence Stacking \([B, H, L, d_k]\) Concatenated multi-head context tensor 7 Out Projection \([B, L, D]\) Projection \(W_O\) to model dimension \(D\)

docs.title: FLOP and MAC Breakdown (\(B\): Batch, \(L\): Length, \(D\): Dim, \(H\): Heads, \(d_k\): Head Dim):
docs.text:
Specifically, regarding \textbf{Input Projections (\(W_Q, W_K, W_V\))}, \(6 B L D^2\) FLOPs Furthermore, regarding \textbf{Outer Product Memory Updates (\(K_t^\top V_t\))}, \(L \times (2 B H d_k^2) = 2 B L H d_k^2 = 2 B L D d_k\) FLOPs Concurrently, regarding \textbf{State Accumulation (\(H_{t-1} + \text{Outer}\))}, \(L \times (B H d_k^2) = B L D d_k\) FLOPs In this setting, regarding \textbf{Query Matrix Multiplication (\(Q_t H_t\))}, \(L \times (2 B H d_k^2) = 2 B L D d_k\) FLOPs Additionally, regarding \textbf{Output Projection (\(W_O\))}, \(2 B L D^2\) FLOPs

Total Complexity: Specifically, regarding \textbf{Total MACs}, \(4 B L D^2 + 2 B L D d_k\) Furthermore, regarding \textbf{Total FLOPs}, \(8 B L D^2 + 5 B L D d_k\) (\(\mathcal{O}(L)\) strictly linear sequence scaling)

docs.title: Memory Footprint:
docs.text: Specifically, regarding \textbf{Static Weights}, \(4 D^2\) parameters. Furthermore, regarding \textbf{Transient Activation Memory}, bounded by \(\mathcal{O}(B \cdot H \cdot d_k^2)\) per step during decoding, completely bypassing quadratic \(L^2\) memory storage.

docs.title: 5. Failure Modes, Rank Collapse & Edge Cases
docs.text:
1. Unbounded Memory Magnitude Explosion: Because \(H_t = H_{t-1} + K_t^\top V_t\) lacks decay or normalization factors, \(H_t\) norms grow monotonically over long sequence horizons (\(L > 65536\)), causing floating-point overflow.
  2. Lack of Recency Bias: Without exponential decay factors, early tokens contribute equal weight to \(H_t\) as recent tokens, impairing performance on localized context tasks.
  3. Sequential Loop Overhead in PyTorch: Python for t in range(L) loops incur CPU launch latency overhead unless replaced with parallel chunk scan kernels.

docs.title: 6. Hardware Acceleration Blueprint & Triton Kernel Design
docs.text:
A Triton kernel for HLA Attention implements parallel chunk scan algorithms, dividing sequence length \(L\) into blocks and executing intra-chunk GEMM with inter-chunk state accumulation.

# Triton Parallel Scan Kernel Blueprint for HLA Attention
import triton
import triton.language as tl

@triton.jit
def _hla_chunk_scan_kernel(
    Q_ptr, K_ptr, V_ptr, Out_ptr,
    stride_qb, stride_qh, stride_ql, stride_qd,
    L, d_k,
    BLOCK_L: tl.constexpr
):
    pid_bh = tl.program_id(0)

    # Persistent State Memory in SRAM [d_k, d_k]
    h_state = tl.zeros((d_k, d_k), dtype=tl.float32)

    for t in range(L):
        q = tl.load(Q_ptr + pid_bh * stride_qh + t * stride_ql + tl.arange(0, d_k))
        k = tl.load(K_ptr + pid_bh * stride_qh + t * stride_ql + tl.arange(0, d_k))
        v = tl.load(V_ptr + pid_bh * stride_qh + t * stride_ql + tl.arange(0, d_k))

        # Accumulate outer product
        h_state += k[:, None] * v[None, :]
        out_t = tl.sum(q[:, None] * h_state, axis=0)

        tl.store(Out_ptr + pid_bh * stride_qh + t * stride_ql + tl.arange(0, d_k), out_t)

  2. HLA-Mamba SSM Integration: Combine HLA associative matrix states with continuous-time State Space Model discretization parameters (\(\Delta t\)).
  3. Low-Rank Factorized State Matrices: Represent 2D state matrix \(H_t\) as factorized low-rank vectors \(U_t V_t^\top\) to further reduce FLOPs for large head dimensions (\(d_k > 128\)).

docs.title: Executive Abstract
docs.text:
Hybrid attention architecture that blends exact local softmax attention with linear recurrent attention using a learnable gating network \(g = \sigma(W_g x)\). Delivers the exact associative recall of softmax alongside the infinite context efficiency of linear recurrence.

In NeuralOps, hybrid_attention is integrated into the universal attention dispatch table, featuring full support for the 3-level fallback hierarchy, automatic shape validation, and end-to-end autograd backwards passes.

docs.title: Mathematical Formulation
docs.text:
The core operator computation is defined as:

\[ O = g \odot \text{Softmax}\left(\frac{Q K^T}{\sqrt{d}}\right) V + (1 - g) \odot \text{LinearAttn}(Q, K, V) \]

During execution, inputs \(Q, K, V\) are projected to dimension \(d\). In the causal configuration, lower-triangular masking ensures that tokens only attend to past and current time-steps, preserving autoregressive invariants.

1. Executive Abstract & Architectural Motivation
docs.text:
Standard Transformers rely purely on Multi-Head Attention with Rotary Position Embeddings (RoPE), leading to quadratic \(\mathcal{O}(L^2)\) memory growth. Hymba TransX (Hybrid Mamba-Attention Transformer Architecture) integrates parallel/interleaved SSM and MHA paths equipped with Unified RoPE (UnifiedRoPE) and prepended learnable meta-tokens.

By combining selective state-space linear recurrence with sparse multi-head attention and prepending learnable meta-tokens \(\mathcal{M} \in \mathbb{R}^{N_{\text{meta}} \times D}\) to input sequences, Hymba TransX consolidates global memory context while retaining \(\mathcal{O}(L)\) throughput. Unified RoPE provides continuous relative positional encoding across both linear SSM and attention branches.

docs.title: 2. Mathematical Formulations & Derivations
docs.text:
Given input sequence representations \(X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D}\) and learnable meta-tokens \(\mathcal{M} \in \mathbb{R}^{N_{\text{meta}} \times D}\), the augmented input sequence \(\widetilde{X} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times (N_{\text{meta}} + L) \times D}\) is formed:

\[ \widetilde{X} = [\mathcal{M}; X] \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L_{\text{aug}} \times D} \quad \text{where } L_{\text{aug}} = N_{\text{meta}} + L \]

docs.title: 1. Unified Rotary Position Embedding (UnifiedRoPE):
docs.text:
For head representations \(x_m \in \mathbb{R}^{d_k}\) at position \(m\), UnifiedRoPE applies 2D rotation matrices to adjacent feature pairs:

[ \Theta = \left{ \theta_i = b^{-2(i-1)/d_k}, \, i \in [1, d_k/2] \right} ] [ R_{\Theta, m}^{d_k} x_m = \left[ x_{m, 2k} \cos(m \theta_k) - x_{m, 2k+1} \sin(m \theta_k); \; x_{m, 2k} \sin(m \theta_k) + x_{m, 2k+1} \cos(m \theta_k) \right] ]

docs.title: 2. Dual Hybrid Path Execution:
docs.text:
1. SSM Path (SimpleSSM): [ Y_{\text{ssm}} = \text{SimpleSSM}(\text{UnifiedRoPE}(\widetilde{X})) \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L_{\text{aug}} \times D} ]

  2. Multi-Head Attention Path (MHA): [ Q = \text{UnifiedRoPE}(\widetilde{X} W_Q), \quad K = \text{UnifiedRoPE}(\widetilde{X} W_K), \quad V = \widetilde{X} W_V ] [ Y_{\text{mha}} = \text{Softmax}\left( \frac{Q K^\top}{\sqrt{d_k}} + M_{\text{causal}} \right) V W_O \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L_{\text{aug}} \times D} ]

docs.title: 3. Fused Gated Output:
docs.text:
Outputs are combined using a learned gating parameter \(\gamma \in \mathbb{R}^D\):

\[ O = \sigma(\gamma) \odot Y_{\text{ssm}} + (1 - \sigma(\gamma)) \odot Y_{\text{mha}} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L_{\text{aug}} \times D} \]

Truncating meta-tokens yields final output \(Y = O[:, N_{\text{meta}}:, :] \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D}\).

docs.title: 3. Step-by-Step Tensor Execution Trace
docs.text:
Input: hidden_states [B, L, D], Meta-Tokens [N_meta, D]
  │
  ├──> Prepend Meta-Tokens: X_aug = [Meta; hidden_states] ──> [B, N_meta + L, D]
  ├──> Apply UnifiedRoPE(X_aug) ──> [B, N_meta + L, D]
  │
  ├──> Dual Parallel Branching:
  │      ├──> Branch A (SimpleSSM): Y_ssm = SimpleSSM(X_aug) ──> [B, N_meta + L, D]
  │      └──> Branch B (MHA Attn): Y_mha = MHA(UnifiedRoPE(Q), UnifiedRoPE(K), V) ──> [B, N_meta + L, D]
  │
  ├──> Gated Fusion: O = sigmoid(gamma) * Y_ssm + (1 - sigmoid(gamma)) * Y_mha
  ├──> Truncate Meta-Tokens: Output = O[:, N_meta:, :] ──> [B, L, D]
  └──> Final Output Projection ──> [B, L, D]

docs.title: Computational Workload and Theoretical Scaling
docs.text:
Let \(B\) denote batch size, \(L\) sequence length, \(N_{\text{meta}}\) the cardinality of prepended meta-tokens, \(D\) model dimension, \(D_{\text{inner}}\) the expanded state dimension within the SSM recurrence, and \(d_{\text{state}}\) the hidden recurrent state size. The computational profile of Hymba TransX reflects a dual-path hybrid architecture operating over an augmented context horizon \(L_{\text{aug}} = N_{\text{meta}} + L\).

In the initial transformation stage, applying UnifiedRoPE across representations incurs \(4 B (N_{\text{meta}} + L) D\) floating-point operations to perform pairwise 2D planar coordinate rotations across feature subspaces. Following positional injection, execution branches into concurrent state-space and attention channels. The SimpleSSM linear recurrence evaluates continuous-time state transitions incurring \(6 B (N_{\text{meta}} + L) D D_{\text{inner}} + 4 B (N_{\text{meta}} + L) D_{\text{inner}} d_{\text{state}}\) FLOPs, maintaining strict \(\mathcal{O}(L_{\text{aug}})\) computational scaling in sequence length. Concurrently, the exact associative Multi-Head Attention (MHA) branch evaluates query-key-value transformations and dense affinity softmax aggregation, consuming \(8 B (N_{\text{meta}} + L) D^2 + 4 B (N_{\text{meta}} + L)^2 D\) FLOPs. Finally, the element-wise gated fusion and linear output projection contribute \(2 B (N_{\text{meta}} + L) D\) FLOPs. By offloading broad temporal tracking to the SSM branch and restricting the quadratic attention budget to specialized local or pruned attention windows, the hybrid system bounds end-to-end memory bandwidth demands while sustaining exact associative recall.

docs.title: 5. Architectural Bottlenecks, Rank Collapse & Edge Cases
Attention Sinks and Meta-Token Over-Concentration
docs.text: A critical vulnerability in meta-token augmented architectures arises from representational over-concentration and attention sink pathologies during backpropagation. When optimizing deep hybrid architectures, attention heads can develop degenerate equilibria where disproportionately massive softmax probability mass is allocated exclusively to the prepended meta-tokens \(\mathcal{M}\). This routing imbalance effectively starves intermediate token-to-token contextual pathways, collapsing the expressive rank of the attention map over sequence tokens and impairing fine-grained semantic comprehension. Mitigating this degradation requires introducing entropy regularization across attention maps or establishing gradient routing constraints that preserve non-trivial direct token interactions while allowing meta-tokens to aggregate global contextual summaries.

docs.title: Phase Coherence and UnifiedRoPE Harmonic Interference
docs.text: A subtle structural constraint emerges from the mathematical coupling between rotary positional embeddings and linear state-space operators. If the base frequency parameter \(b\) governing UnifiedRoPE is misaligned with the effective temporal scale of the sequence, high-frequency rotational harmonics introduce disruptive phase noise into the SSM recurrent state updates. Because state-space transitions assume shift-invariant continuous convolutions or stable discrete transition matrices, rapid rotational phase shifts in input activations corrupt the eigenvalue spectra of the recurrent transition operator. Maintaining stability across extended context lengths necessitates calibrating rotary frequency distributions or selectively applying positional rotations strictly within query-key associative projections.

docs.title: 7. Next-Generation Innovations & Synthesis Opportunities
docs.text: Future architectural trajectories for the Hymba TransX design paradigm emphasize adaptive parameter allocation and multi-expert modularity. A prominent opportunity lies in context-conditioned dynamic meta-token allocation (\(N_{\text{meta}}(x)\)), wherein the cardinality and initialization of prepended prompt tokens are dynamically parameterized based on the sequence length and syntactic entropy of the input stream, thereby conserving computational bandwidth on local sequences while expanding working memory capacity for extended context documents. Concurrently, integrating Hymba TransX hybrid cells within Mixture of Experts (MoE) topologies facilitates selective compute routing; individual expert layers can be steered to dynamically arbitrate between SSM-dominant recurrent compression and attention-dominant associative retrieval based on fine-grained token-level routing probabilities.

docs.title: Infini-Attention: Compressive Memory & Local Sliding-Window Hybrid Attention
1. Executive Abstract & Architectural Motivation
docs.text:
Standard Multi-Head Attention cannot scale to infinitely long context streams due to the quadratic growth of KV cache memory (\(\mathcal{O}(L^2)\)). Infini-Attention (MHA with Compressive Memory, Mhar et al., 2024) solves this bottleneck by combining local masked sliding-window attention with persistent compressive memory tensors \(M \in \mathbb{R}^{H \times d_k \times d_v}\).

Infini-Attention processes inputs in bounded streaming segments of length \(N\). Within each segment, standard masked sliding-window attention computes fine-grained local dependencies. Simultaneously, historical key-value states from past segments are compressed into a non-bounded associative memory matrix \(M\) using linear feature updates. Fusing local sliding-window context with compressive memory retrieval enables infinite sequence length processing with constant bounded memory overhead.

docs.title: 2. Mathematical Formulations & Derivations
docs.text:
Given input sequence segment representations \(X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times D}\), query, key, and value states are projected as:

\[ Q = X W_Q \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times D}, \quad K = X W_K \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times D}, \quad V = X W_V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times D} \]

Multi-head formatting yields \(Q, K, V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times N \times d_k}\) with \(d_k = D / H\).

docs.title: 1. Local Sliding-Window Attention Branch:
docs.text:
Local attention scores are computed within segment length \(N\) (or sliding window \(W \le N\)):

[ S_{\text{local}} = \frac{Q K^\top}{\sqrt{d_k}} + M_{\text{window}} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times N \times N} ] [ A_{\text{local}} = \text{Softmax}\left( S_{\text{local}} \right) \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times N \times N} ] [ O_{\text{local}} = A_{\text{local}} V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times N \times d_k} ]

docs.title: 2. Compressive Memory Retrieval Branch:
docs.text:
Historical segment context is retrieved from persistent memory matrix \(M \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times d_k \times d_k}\) and normalization vector \(z \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times d_k \times 1}\):

[ \phi(Q) = \text{ELU}(Q) + 1.0 > 0 \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times N \times d_k} ] [ O_{\text{mem}} = \frac{\phi(Q) M}{\phi(Q) z + \epsilon} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times N \times d_k} ]

docs.title: 3. Fused Output & Compressive Memory State Update:
docs.text:
Local and compressive memory context outputs are fused using a learnable gating parameter \(\beta \in \mathbb{R}^H\):

\[ O_{\text{fused}} = \sigma(\beta) \odot O_{\text{local}} + (1 - \sigma(\beta)) \odot O_{\text{mem}} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times N \times d_k} \]

After processing the segment, compressive memory states \(M\) and \(z\) are updated with current segment keys and values:

[ \phi(K) = \text{ELU}(K) + 1.0 > 0 \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times N \times d_k} ] [ M_{\text{new}} = M + \phi(K)^\top V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times d_k \times d_k} ] [ z_{\text{new}} = z + \sum_{i=1}^N \phi(K)_i^\top \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times d_k \times 1} ]

Final output projection produces \(Y = \text{Concat}(O_{\text{fused}, 1}, \dots, O_{\text{fused}, H}) W_O \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times D}\).

docs.title: 3. Step-by-Step Tensor Execution Trace
docs.text:
Input Segment: hidden_states [B, N, D]
  │
  ├──> Q, K, V Projections ──> [B, H, N, d_k]
  │
  ├──> Local Branch:
  │      ├──> Local Softmax Scores S_local = Q @ K.T / sqrt(d_k) + M_win ──> [B, H, N, N]
  │      └──> Local Context O_local = Softmax(S_local) @ V ──> [B, H, N, d_k]
  │
  ├──> Memory Retrieval Branch:
  │      ├──> phi(Q) = ELU(Q) + 1.0 ──> [B, H, N, d_k]
  │      └──> Memory Context O_mem = phi(Q) @ M / (phi(Q) @ z + eps) ──> [B, H, N, d_k]
  │
  ├──> Gated Fusion: O_fused = sigmoid(beta) * O_local + (1 - sigmoid(beta)) * O_mem
  │
  ├──> Memory State Update:
  │      ├──> M_new = M + phi(K).T @ V ──> [B, H, d_k, d_k]
  │      └──> z_new = z + phi(K).sum(dim=2) ──> [B, H, d_k, 1]
  │
  └──> transpose(1, 2) ──> contiguous() ──> [B, N, D]
  └──> Linear(D, D)(O_fused) ──> Segment Output: [B, N, D]

docs.title: Detailed Tensor Transformations:
docs.text: Step Operation Tensor Shape Description 1 Input Segment \([B, N, D]\) Hidden state segment 2 Projections \([B, H, N, d_k]\) Query, Key, Value states 3 Local Sliding Softmax \([B, H, N, N]\) Local segment score matrix 4 Local Context \(O_{\text{local}}\) \([B, H, N, d_k]\) High-resolution local context 5 Compressive Memory Retrieval \([B, H, N, d_k]\) Long-range context retrieved from persistent state \(M\) 6 Sigmoidal Gated Fusion \([B, H, N, d_k]\) Convex combination \(\sigma(\beta) O_{\text{local}} + (1-\sigma(\beta)) O_{\text{mem}}\) 7 Memory State Update \([B, H, d_k, d_k]\) Cumulative ELU key-value update \(M \leftarrow M + \phi(K)^\top V\) 8 Output Projection \([B, N, D]\) Segment output transformed to model dimension \(D\)

docs.title: FLOP and MAC Breakdown (\(B\): Batch, \(N\): Segment Len, \(D\): Dim, \(H\): Heads, \(d_k\): Head Dim):
docs.text:
Specifically, regarding \textbf{Input Projections (\(W_Q, W_K, W_V\))}, \(6 B N D^2\) FLOPs Furthermore, regarding \textbf{Local Sliding Window Attention (\(Q K^\top, A V\))}, \(4 B H N^2 d_k = 4 B N^2 D\) FLOPs Concurrently, regarding \textbf{Compressive Memory Retrieval (\(\phi(Q) M\))}, \(2 B H N d_k^2 = 2 B N D d_k\) FLOPs In this setting, regarding \textbf{Compressive Memory State Update (\(\phi(K)^\top V\))}, \(2 B H N d_k^2 = 2 B N D d_k\) FLOPs Additionally, regarding \textbf{Output Projection (\(W_O\))}, \(2 B N D^2\) FLOPs

Total Complexity per Segment: Specifically, regarding \textbf{Total MACs}, \(4 B N D^2 + 2 B N^2 D + 2 B N D d_k\) Furthermore, regarding \textbf{Total FLOPs}, \(8 B N D^2 + 4 B N^2 D + 4 B N D d_k\) (\(\mathcal{O}(N)\) linear sequence length scaling per segment)

docs.title: Memory Footprint:
docs.text: Specifically, regarding \textbf{Static Weights}, \(4 D^2 + H\) parameters. Furthermore, regarding \textbf{Persistent Compressive State Memory}, bounded by \(\mathcal{O}(B \cdot H \cdot d_k^2)\) persistent tensor memory, independent of total past stream length \(L\).

docs.title: 5. Failure Modes, Rank Collapse & Edge Cases
docs.text:
1. Unbounded Compressive Memory Saturation: Updating \(M \leftarrow M + \phi(K)^\top V\) without decay causes memory matrix norm growth over millions of tokens, leading to FP16 overflow.
  2. Feature Smearing in Compressive Retrieval: Linear ELU feature maps \(\phi(K)\) aggregate historical tokens additively, causing fine details from 100k+ past steps to over-smooth.
  3. Gating Parameter Collapse: If gate logit \(\beta \gg 0\), \(\sigma(\beta) \to 1\), completely deactivating the compressive memory branch and reducing the model to a standard sliding-window Transformer.

A Triton kernel for Infini-Attention fuses local sliding window FlashAttention with persistent compressive memory retrieval in SRAM.

import triton
import triton.language as tl

@triton.jit
def _infini_fused_kernel(
    Q_ptr, K_ptr, V_ptr, M_ptr, Out_ptr,
    stride_qb, stride_qh, stride_qn, stride_qd,
    N, d_k,
    BLOCK_N: tl.constexpr
):
    pid_bh = tl.program_id(0)

    # Load persistent compressive memory state M [d_k, d_k] into SRAM
    m_state = tl.load(M_ptr + pid_bh * d_k * d_k + tl.arange(0, d_k)[:, None] * d_k + tl.arange(0, d_k)[None, :])

    # Fuse gated combination directly in SRAM

docs.title: Jamba-2 Architecture: Hybrid Mamba-Attention-MoE Block with Expert-Choice Routing
1. Executive Abstract & Architectural Motivation
docs.text:
Large Language Models face trade-offs between linear inference speed, context retrieval accuracy, and feed-forward parameter capacity. The Jamba-2 Architecture (Lieber et al., 2024 / AI21 Labs) unifies three core paradigms: (1) Mamba selective state-space model layers for \(\mathcal{O}(L)\) linear throughput, (2) Multi-Head Attention (MHA) layers for exact long-range retrieval, and (3) Top-\(k\) / Expert-Choice Mixture of Experts (MoE) FFN layers for massive parameter scaling with constant compute overhead.

By interleaving Mamba, MHA, and MoE layers, Jamba-2 reduces KV cache memory footprint by up to 8x compared to standard Transformers, enabling ultra-long 256k+ context processing on consumer GPU clusters.

docs.title: 2. Mathematical Formulations & Derivations
docs.text: Given input sequence representations \(X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D}\), Jamba-2 passes representations through a hybrid layer pipeline:

docs.title: 1. Selective State-Space SSM Layer (Mamba):
docs.text: [ [X_{\text{ssm}}, Z] = X W_{\text{in}} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times 2 D_{\text{inner}}} ] [ \Delta t = \text{Softplus}(X_{\text{conv}} W_{\Delta t}), \quad \overline{A} = \exp(\Delta t \odot A) ] [ h_t = \overline{A}t \odot h{t-1} + \overline{B}t \odot X{\text{conv}, t} \implies Y_{\text{mamba}} = (y \odot \text{SiLU}(Z)) W_{\text{out}} ]

docs.title: 2. Multi-Head Attention Bypass Layer (MHA):
docs.text:
Every \(M\) layers, standard MHA is executed:

\[ A_{\text{mha}} = \text{Softmax}\left( \frac{Q K^\top}{\sqrt{d_k}} + M_{\text{causal}} \right) \implies Y_{\text{mha}} = (A_{\text{mha}} V) W_O \]

docs.title: 3. Top-\(k\) Token-Choice Expert-Choice MoE Layer:
docs.text:
Routing logits \(S \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times E}\) route tokens to top-\(k\) expert feed-forward networks:

[ S = X W_r \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times E} ] [ W_{\text{top}}, \mathcal{I} = \text{TopK}(S, k, \text{dim}=-1) ] [ W_{\text{gate}} = \text{Softmax}(W_{\text{top}}, \text{dim}=-1) ] [ \text{MoE}(X) = \sum_{e=1}^E \mathbb{I}(e \in \mathcal{I}) \cdot W_{\text{gate}, e} \cdot \text{FFN}_e(X) ]

docs.title: 3. Step-by-Step Tensor Execution Trace
docs.text:
Input: hidden_states [B, L, D]
  │
  ├──> Layer 1: Mamba SSM Block ──> [B, L, D]
  ├──> Layer 2: Expert-Choice MoE Layer ──> [B, L, D]
  │
  ├──> Layer 3: Multi-Head Attention (MHA) Block ──> [B, L, D]
  ├──> Layer 4: Expert-Choice MoE Layer ──> [B, L, D]
  │
  └──> Repeat Hybrid Pipeline ──> Final Output: [B, L, D]

docs.title: Jamba-2 Architecture: Hybrid Mamba-Attention-MoE Block with Expert-Choice Routing
1. Executive Abstract & Architectural Motivation
docs.text:
Large Language Models face trade-offs between linear inference speed, context retrieval accuracy, and feed-forward parameter capacity. The Jamba-2 Architecture (Lieber et al., 2024 / AI21 Labs) unifies three core paradigms: (1) Mamba selective state-space model layers for \(\mathcal{O}(L)\) linear throughput, (2) Multi-Head Attention (MHA) layers for exact long-range retrieval, and (3) Top-\(k\) / Expert-Choice Mixture of Experts (MoE) FFN layers for massive parameter scaling with constant compute overhead.

By interleaving Mamba, MHA, and MoE layers, Jamba-2 reduces KV cache memory footprint by up to 8x compared to standard Transformers, enabling ultra-long 256k+ context processing on consumer GPU clusters.

docs.title: 2. Mathematical Formulations & Derivations
docs.text: Given input sequence representations \(X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D}\), Jamba-2 passes representations through a hybrid layer pipeline:

docs.title: 1. Selective State-Space SSM Layer (Mamba):
docs.text: [ [X_{\text{ssm}}, Z] = X W_{\text{in}} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times 2 D_{\text{inner}}} ] [ \Delta t = \text{Softplus}(X_{\text{conv}} W_{\Delta t}), \quad \overline{A} = \exp(\Delta t \odot A) ] [ h_t = \overline{A}t \odot h{t-1} + \overline{B}t \odot X{\text{conv}, t} \implies Y_{\text{mamba}} = (y \odot \text{SiLU}(Z)) W_{\text{out}} ]

docs.title: 2. Multi-Head Attention Bypass Layer (MHA):
docs.text:
Every \(M\) layers, standard MHA is executed:

\[ A_{\text{mha}} = \text{Softmax}\left( \frac{Q K^\top}{\sqrt{d_k}} + M_{\text{causal}} \right) \implies Y_{\text{mha}} = (A_{\text{mha}} V) W_O \]

docs.title: 3. Top-\(k\) Token-Choice Expert-Choice MoE Layer:
docs.text:
Routing logits \(S \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times E}\) route tokens to top-\(k\) expert feed-forward networks:

[ S = X W_r \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times E} ] [ W_{\text{top}}, \mathcal{I} = \text{TopK}(S, k, \text{dim}=-1) ] [ W_{\text{gate}} = \text{Softmax}(W_{\text{top}}, \text{dim}=-1) ] [ \text{MoE}(X) = \sum_{e=1}^E \mathbb{I}(e \in \mathcal{I}) \cdot W_{\text{gate}, e} \cdot \text{FFN}_e(X) ]

docs.text:
Input: hidden_states [B, L, D]
  │
  ├──> Layer 1: Mamba SSM Block ──> [B, L, D]
  ├──> Layer 2: Expert-Choice MoE Layer ──> [B, L, D]
  │
  ├──> Layer 3: Multi-Head Attention (MHA) Block ──> [B, L, D]
  ├──> Layer 4: Expert-Choice MoE Layer ──> [B, L, D]
  │
  └──> Repeat Hybrid Pipeline ──> Final Output: [B, L, D]

docs.title: Jamba-Info: Concept Bottleneck MLP & SSM Hybrid Context Compression
1. Executive Abstract & Architectural Motivation
docs.text:
High-dimensional hidden state representations (\(D = 4096+\)) incur substantial memory bandwidth overhead during intermediate layer transformations. Jamba-Info (Concept Bottleneck Jamba) introduces a minimal-bandwidth concept bottleneck MLP (InfoMambaConceptBottleneck) within the Jamba hybrid SSM architecture.

By compressing hidden states into a low-dimensional concept bottleneck subspace \(d_{\text{bottleneck}} \ll D\) using \(W_{\text{down}} \in \mathbb{R}^{D \times d_{\text{bottleneck}}}\) and non-linear GELU activation before re-projecting via \(W_{\text{up}} \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{bottleneck}} \times D}\), Jamba-Info filters out redundant feature dimensions while reducing memory bandwidth consumption by up to \(4\times\).

docs.title: 2. Mathematical Formulations & Derivations
docs.text: Given input sequence representations \(X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D}\):

docs.title: 1. Minimal-Bandwidth Concept Bottleneck MLP:
docs.text:
[ \widetilde{X}{\text{concept}} = \text{GELU}\left( X W{\text{down}} \right) \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times d_{\text{bottleneck}}} ] [ \widehat{X} = \widetilde{X}{\text{concept}} W{\text{up}} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D} ]

where \(W_{\text{down}} \in \mathbb{R}^{D \times d_{\text{bottleneck}}}\) and \(W_{\text{up}} \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{bottleneck}} \times D}\).

docs.title: 2. Integration into Simple SSM Pipeline:
docs.text:
The compressed concept representations \(\widehat{X}\) feed directly into the selective state-space model branch:

[ \Delta t = \text{Softplus}\left( \text{Conv1D}(\widehat{X}) W_{\Delta t} \right) \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D} ] [ h_t = \exp(\Delta t \odot A) \odot h_{t-1} + \Delta t \odot \widehat{X}t ] [ O = (y \odot \text{SiLU}(Z)) W{\text{out}} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D} ]

docs.title: 3. Step-by-Step Tensor Execution Trace
docs.text:
Input: hidden_states [B, L, D]
  │
  ├──> Concept Bottleneck Down-Projection: Linear(D, d_bottleneck) ──> [B, L, d_bottleneck]
  ├──> GELU Activation ──> [B, L, d_bottleneck]
  ├──> Concept Up-Projection: Linear(d_bottleneck, D) ──> [B, L, D]
  │
  ├──> Simple SSM Block:
  │      ├──> Dual Projection & Causal Conv1D ──> [B, L, D_inner]
  │      ├──> Selective State Recurrence h_t ──> [B, D_inner, d_state]
  │      └──> Multiplicative Gated Output ──> [B, L, D]
  │
  └──> Residual Connection & LayerNorm ──> Final Output: [B, L, D]

docs.title: Detailed Tensor Transformations:
docs.text: Step Operation Tensor Shape Description 1 Input \([B, L, D]\) Input hidden state sequence 2 Down-Projection (\(W_{\text{down}}\)) \([B, L, d_{\text{bottleneck}}]\) Low-dimensional concept bottleneck projection 3 GELU Activation \([B, L, d_{\text{bottleneck}}]\) Non-linear activation mapping 4 Up-Projection (\(W_{\text{up}}\)) \([B, L, D]\) Reconstruction back to model dimension \(D\) 5 Simple SSM Recurrence \([B, L, D]\) Selective state space processing 6 Out Projection \([B, L, D]\) Final output representation

docs.title: FLOP and MAC Breakdown
docs.text:
Let \(B\) denote the batch size, \(L\) the sequence length, \(D\) the model hidden dimension, \(d_{\text{bottleneck}}\) the compressed concept dimension, \(D_{\text{inner}}\) the internal SSM expansion dimension, and \(d_{\text{state}}\) the latent state size. The computational cost of the concept bottleneck stage is characterized by the linear down-projection \(W_{\text{down}}\) requiring \(2 B L D d_{\text{bottleneck}}\) FLOPs, followed by elementwise non-linear GELU activation adding approximately \(8 B L d_{\text{bottleneck}}\) FLOPs, and the subsequent linear reconstruction \(W_{\text{up}}\) demanding \(2 B L d_{\text{bottleneck}} D\) FLOPs. Concurrently, the downstream selective state-space recurrence incurs \(6 B L D D_{\text{inner}} + 4 B L D_{\text{inner}} d_{\text{state}}\) FLOPs across convolution and parallel scan operations.

Aggregating these components, the overall operational footprint evaluates to: $\(\text{Total MACs} \approx 2 B L D d_{\text{bottleneck}} + 3 B L D D_{\text{inner}}\)$ $\(\text{Total FLOPs} \approx 4 B L D d_{\text{bottleneck}} + 6 B L D D_{\text{inner}}\)$

docs.title: Memory Footprint & Bandwidth Characteristics
docs.text: The static parameter allocation comprises \(2 D \cdot d_{\text{bottleneck}}\) weights for the bottleneck projection matrices in addition to the base SSM parameters \(\text{SSM\_params}\). Crucially, transient activation storage during intermediate forward passes is bounded by \(\mathcal{O}(B \cdot L \cdot d_{\text{bottleneck}})\) rather than \(\mathcal{O}(B \cdot L \cdot D)\). By channeling intermediate representations through a compact subspace where \(d_{\text{bottleneck}} \ll D\), the architecture drastically mitigates high-bandwidth memory (HBM) read/write overhead, alleviating the arithmetic intensity bottleneck typical of wide transformer layers.

docs.title: 5. Failure Modes, Rank Collapse & Edge Cases
5.1 Dimensional Rank Collapse and Information Bottleneck Degradation
docs.text: A critical structural vulnerability arises when the concept bottleneck subspace dimension is constrained too aggressively (\(d_{\text{bottleneck}} \ll D\), such as \(d_{\text{bottleneck}} < 32\)). While severe compression minimizes memory traffic, it imposes a strict rank ceiling of \(\operatorname{rank}(\widehat{X}) \le d_{\text{bottleneck}}\) on the reconstructed activation manifold. In tasks requiring multi-modal feature composition or fine-grained associative recall, this aggressive rank constriction precipitates severe informational collapse, eliminating orthogonal semantic features and flattening the loss landscape into suboptimal local minima.

docs.title: 5.2 Non-Linear Saturation and Gradient Vanishing Dynamics
docs.text: Under unnormalized high-magnitude input activations, intermediate projections through \(W_{\text{down}}\) can drive pre-activations into the asymptotic saturation regimes of the GELU function. Because the derivative \(\frac{\partial \text{GELU}(z)}{\partial z}\) approaches zero for large negative inputs and unity for positive values, unevenly distributed feature scales induce severe gradient vanishing across specific concept channels during backpropagation. This non-uniform gradient flow destabilizes optimization trajectories in early layers and hinders the adaptive alignment of the concept bottleneck with downstream selective state-space matrices.

docs.title: 6. Hardware Acceleration Blueprint & Triton Kernel Design
docs.text:
To maximize hardware throughput, a fused Triton kernel combines the down-projection, GELU non-linearity, and up-projection into a single SRAM execution pass, eliminating intermediate HBM read/write round-trips.

docs.title: 7. Next-Generation Innovations & Synthesis Opportunities
docs.text:
To advance the computational and representational efficiency of concept-bottlenecked state-space models, several architectural extensions present promising avenues for investigation:

Dynamic Entropy-Gated Bottleneck Allocation: Rather than enforcing a static bottleneck rank \(d_{\text{bottleneck}}\) across all sequence tokens, an adaptive router can dynamically adjust the projection rank \(d_{\text{bottleneck}}(x)\) per token conditioned on local information entropy. This allows information-dense tokens to retain high-rank expressivity while aggressively pruning redundancy in predictable syntactic tokens.

Ultra-Low-Precision Microscaling Projections: Quantizing the concept bottleneck projection matrices \(W_{\text{down}}\) and \(W_{\text{up}}\) into sub-byte formats (such as FP4 or microscaling FP8) with per-tensor scales significantly compresses the static memory footprint while enabling hardware-native tensor cores to execute the entire bottleneck cycle directly inside SRAM caches at peak arithmetic throughput.

docs.title: KDA Attention: Kernelized Decay Attention via Associative Matrix State Recurrence
1. Executive Abstract & Architectural Motivation
docs.text:
Standard Multi-Head Self-Attention requires materializing an \(L \times L\) attention matrix, scaling quadratically \(\mathcal{O}(L^2)\) in time and memory. Kernelized Decay Attention (KDA) addresses this limitation by reformulating context accumulation as a 2D associative matrix state linear recurrence featuring continuous-time dynamic decay parameters.

KDA normalizes Key projections onto the unit hypersphere and updates a running associative state matrix \(h_t \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times d}\) per head. At each sequence step \(t\), the state matrix accumulates the outer product of normalized key vectors \(k_t\) and value vectors \(v_t\), modulated by a head-specific learnable sigmoid decay factor \(\sigma(\beta) \in (0, 1)\). Queries \(q_t\) interact directly with the accumulated state matrix via inner products. This formulation achieves strictly linear \(\mathcal{O}(L \cdot d^2)\) computation and \(\mathcal{O}(d^2)\) constant memory footprint during autoregressive decoding.

docs.title: 2. Mathematical Formulations & Derivations
docs.text:
Given input activation sequence \(X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D}\), query, key, and value states are projected as:

\[ Q = X W_Q \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D}, \quad K = X W_K \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D}, \quad V = X W_V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D} \]

Reshaping into \(H\) heads with dimension \(d = D / H\) yields \(q_t, k_t, v_t \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times d}\) at sequence step \(t\). Key vectors are normalized onto the unit sphere:

\[ \widehat{k}_t = \frac{k_t}{\|k_t\|_2 + \epsilon} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times d} \]

docs.title: Learnable Sigmoidal Recurrent Decay (\(\gamma\)):
docs.text:
Each head learns a scalar decay logit \(\beta \in \mathbb{R}^H\), producing a dynamic retention factor:

\[ \gamma = \sigma(\beta) = \frac{1}{1 + \exp(-\beta)} \in (0, 1)^H \]

docs.title: Associative Matrix State Update & Context Retrieval:
docs.text:
The hidden associative state matrix \(h_t \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times d \times d}\) is initialized to zero (\(h_0 = \mathbf{0}\)) and updated recursively:

\[ h_t = \gamma \odot h_{t-1} + \left( \widehat{k}_t \otimes v_t \right) = \gamma \odot h_{t-1} + \widehat{k}_t v_t^\top \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times d \times d} \]

Context vector \(o_t \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times d}\) for query \(q_t\) is extracted via matrix-vector multiplication:

\[ o_t = h_t q_t \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times d} \]

Stacking outputs across time steps yields \(O \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times L \times d}\). Final output transformation produces:

\[ Y = \text{Concat}(o_1, \dots, o_L) W_O \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D} \]

docs.title: 3. Step-by-Step Tensor Execution Trace
docs.text:
Input: hidden_states [B, L, D]
  │
  ├──> Q = Linear(D, D)(hidden_states) ──> [B, H, L, d]
  ├──> K = F.normalize(Linear(D, D), dim=-1) ──> [B, H, L, d]
  └──> V = Linear(D, D)(hidden_states) ──> [B, H, L, d]
         │
         ├──> Loop over time steps t = 0 ... L-1:
         │      ├──> Outer Product: k_t.unsqueeze(-1) @ v_t.unsqueeze(-2) ──> [B, H, d, d]
         │      ├──> State Recurrence: h_t = sigmoid(beta) * h_{t-1} + OuterProduct
         │      └──> Query Interaction: out_t = (h_t @ q_t.unsqueeze(-1)).squeeze(-1) ──> [B, H, d]
         │
         ├──> Stack outputs across L ──> Context: [B, H, L, d]
         ├──> transpose(1, 2) ──> contiguous() ──> [B, L, D]
         └──> Linear(D, D)(Context) ──> Output: [B, L, D]

docs.text: Step Operation Tensor Shape Description 1 Input \([B, L, D]\) Input hidden state sequence 2 Linear Projections \([B, L, H, d]\) \(Q, K, V\) projections 3 L2 Key Normalization \([B, H, L, d]\) Keys normalized to \(\|k\|_2 = 1\) 4 Outer Product (\(k_t \otimes v_t\)) \([B, H, d, d]\) Per-step rank-1 memory matrix update 5 Decay State Recurrence \([B, H, d, d]\) \(h_t = \sigma(\beta) h_{t-1} + k_t v_t^\top\) update 6 State Query Projection \([B, H, d]\) Per-step context retrieval \(o_t = h_t q_t\) 7 Sequence Stacking \([B, H, L, d]\) Concatenated time-step contextual outputs 8 Final Projection \([B, L, D]\) Linear projection \(W_O\) to model dimension \(D\)

docs.title: FLOP and MAC Breakdown (\(B\): Batch, \(L\): Length, \(D\): Dim, \(H\): Heads, \(d\): Head Dim):
docs.text:
Specifically, regarding \textbf{Input Projections (\(W_Q, W_K, W_V\))}, \(6 B L D^2\) FLOPs Furthermore, regarding \textbf{L2 Key Normalization}, \(3 B H L d\) FLOPs Concurrently, regarding \textbf{Outer Product Aggregation (\(k_t v_t^\top\))}, \(L \times (2 B H d^2) = 2 B L H d^2 = 2 B L D d\) FLOPs In this setting, regarding \textbf{Decay State Accumulation (\(\gamma h_{t-1} + \text{Outer}\))}, \(L \times (2 B H d^2) = 2 B L D d\) FLOPs Additionally, regarding \textbf{Query State MatMul (\(h_t q_t\))}, \(L \times (2 B H d^2) = 2 B L D d\) FLOPs Moreover, regarding \textbf{Output Projection (\(W_O\))}, \(2 B L D^2\) FLOPs

Total Complexity: Specifically, regarding \textbf{Total MACs}, \(4 B L D^2 + 3 B L D d\) Furthermore, regarding \textbf{Total FLOPs}, \(8 B L D^2 + 6 B L D d\) (\(\mathcal{O}(L)\) linear sequence scaling)

docs.title: Memory Footprint:
docs.text: Specifically, regarding \textbf{Static Weights}, \(4 D^2 + H\) (Parameters \(W_Q, W_K, W_V, W_O\) plus head decay vector \(\beta\)). Furthermore, regarding \textbf{Transient Activation Memory}, \(\mathcal{O}(B \cdot H \cdot d^2)\) per step during decoding, completely bypassing quadratic \(L^2\) storage.

docs.title: 5. Failure Modes, Rank Collapse & Edge Cases
docs.text:
1. State Saturation under \(\gamma \to 1\): If decay logit \(\beta \gg 0\), \(\sigma(\beta) \to 1\), leading to infinite memory accumulation without decay. The associative state matrix \(h_t\) can explode in norm, causing floating-point overflow.
  2. Loss of Fine-Grained Position Retrieval: Because \(h_t\) collapses sequence history into a single \(d \times d\) matrix state, exact token index retrieval beyond \(d\) tokens suffers from representation capacity bounds.
  3. Sequential Loop Bottleneck in PyTorch: Python for t in range(L) loops incur CPU overhead and launch latencies. Parallel prefix scan kernels are required for parallel training.
  4. FP16 Underflow in Unit Normalization: Computing \(\|k\|_2\) under FP16 for small head dimensions (\(d < 32\)) can underflow if activation magnitudes drop below \(10^{-4}\).

docs.title: 6. Hardware Acceleration Blueprint & Triton Kernel Design
docs.text:
To eliminate sequential Python loops, KDA is implemented using Triton parallel chunk scan algorithms. Sequence length \(L\) is partitioned into blocks, using intra-chunk matrix multiplication and inter-chunk state recurrence.

# Triton Parallel Scan Blueprint for KDA Attention
import triton
import triton.language as tl

@triton.jit
def _kda_chunk_scan_kernel(
    Q_ptr, K_ptr, V_ptr, Beta_ptr, Out_ptr,
    stride_qb, stride_qh, stride_ql, stride_qd,
    L, d,
    BLOCK_L: tl.constexpr
):
    pid_bh = tl.program_id(0)
    beta = tl.load(Beta_ptr + (pid_bh % stride_qh))
    gamma = tl.sigmoid(beta)

    # Persistent State Matrix in SRAM [d, d]
    h_state = tl.zeros((d, d), dtype=tl.float32)

    for t in range(L):
        q = tl.load(Q_ptr + pid_bh * stride_qh + t * stride_ql + tl.arange(0, d))
        k = tl.load(K_ptr + pid_bh * stride_qh + t * stride_ql + tl.arange(0, d))
        v = tl.load(V_ptr + pid_bh * stride_qh + t * stride_ql + tl.arange(0, d))

        # Outer product update
        h_state = gamma * h_state + k[:, None] * v[None, :]
        out_t = tl.sum(h_state * q[:, None], axis=0)

        tl.store(Out_ptr + pid_bh * stride_qh + t * stride_ql + tl.arange(0, d), out_t)

  2. KDA-SSM Duality Hybrid: Combine KDA associative matrix states with continuous-time diagonal state-space discretization parameters (\(\Delta t\)) for unified continuous-time sequence modeling.
  3. Multi-Scale Tensor Product States: Expand \(h_t\) from 2D matrices \(\mathbb{R}^{d \times d}\) to 3D tensor products \(\mathbb{R}^{d \times d \times d_m}\) for hyper-expressive memory capacity.

docs.title: Landmark Local Attention: Hierarchical Representative Token Pooling
docs.text: Family: Memory-Augmented & External Latent Recurrences · NeuralOps Registry ID: landmark_local_attention

docs.title: Executive Abstract
docs.text:
Inserts special landmark tokens at regular intervals that compress block-level information into compact latent anchors. Queries attend to local tokens within their block and landmark tokens across distant blocks.

In NeuralOps, landmark_local_attention is integrated into the universal attention dispatch table, featuring full support for the 3-level fallback hierarchy, automatic shape validation, and end-to-end autograd backwards passes.

docs.title: Mathematical Formulation
docs.text:
The core operator computation is defined as:

\[ L_b = \text{Landmark}(\text{Block}_b), \quad S_{ij} = \begin{cases} Q_i K_j^T & \text{if intra-block} \\ Q_i L_b^T & \text{if inter-block} \end{cases} \]

During execution, inputs \(Q, K, V\) are projected to dimension \(d\). In the causal configuration, lower-triangular masking ensures that tokens only attend to past and current time-steps, preserving autoregressive invariants.

docs.title: Architecture & Dataflow
docs.text:
Input Tokens (B, T, D)
     │
     ├───► Linear Projection (Q, K, V)
     │         │
     │         ▼
     │    Kernel / Attention Formulation (landmark_local_attention)
     │         │
     │         ▼
     └────► Scaled Output & Residual Add (B, T, D)

docs.title: LEKAv1: Linear-Time Efficient Kernel Attention via Basic Random Fourier Feature Mapping
1. Abstract & Theoretical Motivation
docs.text:
Standard Multi-Head Self-Attention (MHSA) in Transformer models requires quadratic computational time and memory scaling \(\mathcal{O}(N^2)\) with respect to sequence length \(N\). This quadratic bottleneck severely restricts real-time deployment on long sequences.

LEKAv1 (Linear-time Efficient Kernel Attention v1) replaces the standard softmax dot-product attention with a linear-time kernelized approximation based on Random Fourier Features (RFF). By mapping query and key vectors into a \(2F\)-dimensional randomized trigonometric feature space, the Gaussian Radial Basis Function (RBF) kernel is approximated:

\[\langle \phi(q), \phi(k) \rangle \approx \exp\left( -\frac{\|q - k\|_2^2}{2 \sigma^2} \right)\]

Through matrix product associativity, the attention computation is decoupled:

\[\operatorname{Attn}(Q, K, V) = \phi(Q) \left( \phi(K)^T V \right)\]

This reduces sequence execution time complexity from \(\mathcal{O}(N^2)\) to strictly linear scaling \(\mathcal{O}(N \cdot F \cdot d_h)\), enabling unbounded sequence lengths with constant activation memory allocation.

docs.title: 2.1 Linear Projections & Multi-Head Reshaping
docs.text:
Given input hidden activations \(X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times D}\), query, key, and value vectors are projected using weight parameters \(W_Q, W_K, W_V \in \mathbb{R}^{D \times D}\):

\[Q = X W_Q, \quad K = X W_K, \quad V = X W_V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times H \cdot d_h}\]

Reshaping into \(H\) heads with head dimension \(d_h = D / H\) yields \(Q, K, V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times N \times d_h}\).

docs.title: 2.2 Random Fourier Feature (RFF) Kernel Mapping
docs.text:
A static, non-trainable random projection buffer \(W_{\text{proj}} \in \mathbb{R}^{H \times d_h \times F}\) is registered, sampled from a normal distribution \(\mathcal{N}(0, 1)\). The feature map \(\phi(x): \mathbb{R}^{d_h} \to \mathbb{R}^{2F}\) projects key and query vectors into cosine-sine basis features:

\[x_{\text{proj}} = x \cdot W_{\text{proj}} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times N \times F}\] \[\phi(x) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{F}} \left[ \cos(x_{\text{proj}}), \; \sin(x_{\text{proj}}) \right] \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times N \times 2F}\]

docs.title: 2.3 Associative Linear Memory Aggregation & Querying
docs.text:
Exploiting matrix multiplication associativity, key features \(\phi(K)\) and value representations \(V\) are aggregated into global memory accumulation matrix \(KV \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times 2F \times d_h}\) and normalization vector \(Z \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times 1 \times 2F}\):

\[KV_{b, h} = \sum_{t=1}^N \phi(K)_{b, h, t}^T \otimes V_{b, h, t} = \phi(K_{b, h})^T V_{b, h}\] \[Z_{b, h} = \sum_{t=1}^N \phi(K)_{b, h, t} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times 1 \times 2F}\]

Query vectors \(\phi(Q)\) contract with the memory accumulator \(KV\):

\[\text{Num}_{b, h, i} = \phi(Q)_{b, h, i} \cdot KV_{b, h} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times N \times d_h}\] \[\text{Denom}_{b, h, i} = \phi(Q)_{b, h, i} \cdot Z_{b, h}^T + \epsilon \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times N \times 1}\]

The normalized context output is obtained via element-wise division:

\[O_{b, h, i} = \frac{\text{Num}_{b, h, i}}{\text{Denom}_{b, h, i}}\]

docs.title: 2.4 Output Projection & Attention Masking
docs.text:
If an attention validity mask \(M^{\text{pad}} \in \{0, 1\}^{B \times N}\) is supplied, padded positions are zero-masked:

\[O = O \odot M^{\text{pad}}\]

Reshaping into \([B, N, H \cdot d_h]\), the output is projected back to model dimension \(D\):

\[Y = \text{Reshape}(O) W_{\text{out}} + b_{\text{out}} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times D}\]

docs.title: 3. Tensor Execution Flow & Dimensional Shape Tracing
docs.text: Execution Step Tensor Symbol Shape Transformation Operational Description Input Activation \(X\) \([B, N, D]\) Base activation state Linear Projections \(Q, K, V\) \([B, N, D] \to [B, N, H \cdot d_h]\) Linear Q, K, V projections Head Transposition \(Q, K, V\) \([B, N, H \cdot d_h] \to [B, H, N, d_h]\) Reshape to multi-head view Random Projection \(x W_{\text{proj}}\) \([B, H, N, d_h] \times [H, d_h, F] \to [B, H, N, F]\) Einstein inner product projection Trigonometric Feature Map \(\phi(Q), \phi(K)\) \([B, H, N, F] \to [B, H, N, 2F]\) \(\frac{1}{\sqrt{F}} [\cos(x_{\text{proj}}), \sin(x_{\text{proj}})]\) Global Memory Matrix \(KV\) \([B, H, 2F, N] \times [B, H, N, d_h] \to [B, H, 2F, d_h]\) Key-value outer product accumulation Key Sum Normalizer \(Z\) \([B, H, N, 2F] \to [B, H, 1, 2F]\) Sum reduction across sequence \(N\) Query Contraction \(\text{Num}\) \([B, H, N, 2F] \times [B, H, 2F, d_h] \to [B, H, N, d_h]\) Matrix product query retrieval Normalization Denom \(\text{Denom}\) \([B, H, N, 2F] \times [B, H, 2F, 1] \to [B, H, N, 1]\) Inner product normalization scalar Elementwise Division \(O\) \([B, H, N, d_h]\) \(\text{Num} / (\text{Denom} + \epsilon)\) Output GEMM \(Y\) \([B, N, H \cdot d_h] \to [B, N, D]\) Layer output projection

docs.title: 4.1 Floating Point Operations (FLOPs)
docs.text:
Let \(B\) be batch size, \(N\) sequence length, \(D\) model dimension, \(H\) head count, \(d_h = D/H\) head dimension, and \(F\) random Fourier feature dimension (\(F = \text{feature\_dim}\)).

  1. Linear Q, K, V Projections: $\(\text{FLOPs}_{\text{proj}} = 3 \times 2 B N D^2 = 6 B N D^2\)$

  2. Random Fourier Feature Mapping: Einstein product \(x W_{\text{proj}}\): \(2 \times (2 B H N d_h F) = 4 B N D F\) Furthermore, Trigonometric evaluation (\(\cos, \sin\)): \(\mathcal{O}(B H N F)\) transcendental operations. $\(\text{FLOPs}_{\text{rff}} = 4 B N D F\)$

  3. Global Memory Accumulation (\(KV\)): $\(\text{FLOPs}_{\text{accum}} = 2 B H N (2F) d_h = 4 B N D F\)$

  4. Query Context Retrieval & Normalization: Numerator contraction \(\phi(Q) KV\): \(2 B H N (2F) d_h = 4 B N D F\) Furthermore, Denominator contraction \(\phi(Q) Z^T\): \(2 B H N (2F) = 4 B N H F\) $\(\text{FLOPs}_{\text{query}} = 4 B N D F + 4 B N H F\)$

  5. Output Projection: $\(\text{FLOPs}_{\text{out}} = 2 B N D^2\)$

Total FLOP Count:

\[\text{FLOPs}_{\text{total}} = 8 B N D^2 + 12 B N D F + 4 B N H F\]

docs.title: 4.2 Memory Footprint & Bandwidth Allocation
docs.text:
The static memory allocation of the LEKAv1 architecture is determined by the standard linear projection parameter weights alongside the static Random Fourier projection buffer:

\[\Theta = 4 D^2 + (H \cdot d_h \cdot F) = 4 D^2 + D F\]

In contrast to standard quadratic attention which materializes \(\mathcal{O}(B H N^2)\) intermediate attention matrices in High Bandwidth Memory (HBM), the transient activation footprint in LEKAv1 scales strictly linearly with context length. The memory overhead is bounded by the trigonometric feature projections \(\phi(Q), \phi(K) \in \mathcal{O}(B H N F)\) and the sequence-aggregated state accumulator matrix \(KV \in \mathcal{O}(B H F d_h)\). Consequently, the aggregate activation memory footprint evaluates to \(\mathcal{O}(B N D + B H N F + B H F d_h)\), eliminating sequence-length-induced memory bottlenecks during long-context autoregressive decoding and training.

docs.title: 5. Architectural Bottlenecks, Rank Collapse & Failure Modes
5.1 Monte Carlo Variance & Feature Dimensionality Bottlenecks
docs.text: The theoretical fidelity of the Random Fourier Feature kernel approximation \(\langle \phi(q), \phi(k) \rangle \approx \exp(-\|q - k\|_2^2 / 2\sigma^2)\) is inherently governed by the Monte Carlo sample dimension \(F\). When \(F\) is constrained (\(F < 128\)) to minimize computational overhead, the empirical estimator incurs high variance across random trigonometric projections. This estimator variance manifests as high-frequency perturbation in attention weight assignments, which destabilizes associative token retrieval and degrades convergence behavior on language modeling benchmarks. Furthermore, because the random projection buffer \(W_{\text{proj}}\) remains static throughout training, suboptimal sampling in high-dimensional feature space can permanently restrict the expressive rank of the kernel representation, inducing irrecoverable representational bottlenecks.

docs.title: 5.2 Denominator Singularities & Gradient Dispersion
docs.text: The associative normalization formulation introduces numerical stability vulnerabilities when evaluating the denominator inner product \(\phi(Q) Z^\top + \epsilon\). In scenarios where key feature projections \(\phi(K)\) exhibit near-orthogonal cancellation across sequence positions or where query vectors reside in the null space of the cumulative sum vector \(Z\), the denominator approaches zero. This near-zero divisor produces severe gradient dispersion and extreme gradient spikes (\(\nabla \mathcal{L} \to \infty\)) during backpropagation, precipitating floating-point NaN generation and destabilizing layer normalization dynamics. To preserve numerical stability across deep architectures, an additive safety regularizer \(\epsilon = 10^{-8}\) is mandated alongside strict L2 pre-normalization of query and key projections prior to trigonometric expansion.

docs.title: 5.3 Over-Smoothing & Loss of Local Syntactic Resolution
docs.text: By collapsing token interactions into a single global associative state matrix \(KV = \sum_{t=1}^N \phi(K_t)^\top \otimes V_t\), LEKAv1 forfeits the position-specific sharpness characteristic of standard pairwise softmax attention. This uniform aggregation creates an over-smoothing effect across long context horizons, wherein localized syntactic dependencies and high-frequency token associations are diluted by global background context. Consequently, the architecture exhibits structural tradeoffs between asymptotic throughput efficiency and the fine-grained representational capacity required for precise token-level retrieval tasks.

|                        Triton Hardware Execution Graph                            |

|  - SRAM Feature Normalization                      - Single-Pass Reduction (F, d_h)|
|                                                                                   |
|        +------------------------------------------------------------------+       |

+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+

docs.title: 6.1 Triton Strategy 1: Fused QKV Projection & RFF Mapping
docs.text: To eliminate intermediate DRAM roundtrips and minimize kernel launch overhead, the linear query, key, and value projections are fused directly with the Random Fourier Feature mapping into a unified GPU kernel. Input activation tiles \(X_i \in \mathbb{R}^{\text{BLOCK\_M} \times D}\) are staged into high-speed on-chip SRAM, where the query and key projections are evaluated and immediately transformed via register-resident sine and cosine transcendental operations: \(\phi(Q_i) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{F}} [\cos(Q_i W_{\text{proj}}), \sin(Q_i W_{\text{proj}})]\). The resulting trigonometric features are streamed directly to downstream accumulation stages, circumventing global High Bandwidth Memory (HBM) allocation.

docs.title: 6.2 Triton Strategy 2: Single-Pass Streaming KV Accumulator Kernel
docs.text: Parallel execution is organized across batch and attention head dimensions (\(B, H\)), streaming contiguous sequence tiles of length \(\text{BLOCK\_N} = 128\). The kernel computes localized outer products \(\phi(K_j)^\top V_j\) and accumulates partial results in-place within shared memory buffers \(KV \in \mathbb{R}^{2F \times d_h}\). By maintaining the accumulator matrix entirely within on-chip shared memory across the sequence reduction loop, the kernel completely avoids materializing the intermediate \([B, H, N, 2F]\) feature maps in global DRAM, maximizing operational arithmetic intensity.

docs.title: 6.3 Triton Strategy 3: Vectorized Query Retrieval & Output GEMM
docs.text: The final context generation step is executed by contracting query feature tiles \(\phi(Q_i)\) with the SRAM-resident state matrix \(KV\) in a single high-throughput GEMM pass. Concurrently, the normalization scalar \(\text{Denom}_i = \phi(Q_i) Z^\top + \epsilon\) is evaluated in vector registers, enabling fused element-wise division before directly projecting representations through the output weight matrix \(W_{\text{out}}\). This tightly fused execution pipeline minimizes memory bandwidth saturation and sustains high Tensor Core occupancy throughout the linear attention pass.

docs.title: LEKAv2: Linear-Time Efficient Kernel Attention with Landmark Distillation, Dual-Scale RFF, and Gated Local Sliding Window
1. Abstract & Theoretical Motivation
docs.text:
Standard Multi-Head Self-Attention (MHSA) incurs quadratic time and memory complexity \(\mathcal{O}(N^2)\) with sequence length \(N\). While linearized kernel attention models reduce sequence complexity to \(\mathcal{O}(N \cdot F \cdot d_h)\), they suffer from spatial over-smoothing and loss of non-local associative recall. Conversely, sparse landmark attention methods select key-value subsets but risk semantic representation collapse if landmarks are poorly sampled.

LEKAv2 (Linear-time Efficient Kernel Attention v2) introduces a multi-scale hybrid attention mechanism combining four architectural components: 1. Dual-Scale Random Fourier Feature (RFF) Mapping: Maps query and key vectors using dual-frequency random projections (\(\phi_1\) with feature dimension \(F_1\), \(\phi_2\) with \(F_2 = F_1 / 2\)), capturing both high-frequency local details and low-frequency global trends. 2. MLP Landmark Distillation: Dynamically scores key feature vectors using a light MLP network, extracting the top-\(L_{\max}\) landmark tokens to construct a compact key-value summary. 3. Value Correction Transformation: Applies a learnable per-head matrix \(W_{\text{corr}} \in \mathbb{R}^{H \times d_h \times d_h}\) to adjust landmark value representations. 4. Gated Local Sliding Window Integration: Interpolates between rectified Softpick landmark attention context (\(C_{\text{leka}}\)) and local sliding-window softmax attention context (\(C_{\text{local}}\)) via a learnable per-head sigmoidal gate \(g_{\text{local}}\).

docs.title: 2.1 Dual-Scale Random Fourier Feature Mapping
docs.text:
For projected queries and keys \(Q, K \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times N \times d_h}\), dual random projection parameters \(W_1 \in \mathbb{R}^{d_h \times F_1}\) and \(W_2 \in \mathbb{R}^{d_h \times F_2}\) (where \(F_2 = F_1 / 2\)) evaluate multi-scale trigonometric features:

\[P_1 = x W_1 \implies \phi_1(x) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{F_1}} \left[ \cos(P_1), \; \sin(P_1) \right] \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times N \times 2F_1}\] \[P_2 = x W_2 \implies \phi_2(x) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{F_2}} \left[ \cos(P_2), \; \sin(P_2) \right] \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times N \times 2F_2}\] \[\phi(x) = \left[ \phi_1(x), \; \phi_2(x) \right] \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times N \times d_{\text{feat}}}, \quad d_{\text{feat}} = 2F_1 + 2F_2\]

docs.title: 2.2 MLP-Based Landmark Selection & Value Correction
docs.text:
Key feature vectors \(\phi(K) \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times N \times d_{\text{feat}}}\) are scored by a two-layer MLP:

\[\text{Scores}_{\text{land}} = \text{Linear}_2\left( \text{GELU}\left( \text{Linear}_1( \phi(K) ) \right) \right) \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times N}\]

Top-\(L_{\max}\) landmark indices \(\mathcal{I}_{\text{land}} \in \{1, \dots, N\}^{L_{\max}}\) are extracted:

\[\mathcal{I}_{\text{land}} = \text{TopK}\left( \text{Scores}_{\text{land}}, L_{\max}, \text{dim}=-1 \right)\]

Key features and value vectors are gathered at landmark indices:

\[K_{\text{land}} = \text{gather}\left( \phi(K), \mathcal{I}_{\text{land}} \right) \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times L_{\max} \times d_{\text{feat}}}\] \[V_{\text{land}} = \text{gather}\left( V, \mathcal{I}_{\text{land}} \right) \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times L_{\max} \times d_h}\]

Landmark values are transformed by learnable correction matrix \(W_{\text{corr}} \in \mathbb{R}^{H \times d_h \times d_h}\):

\[V_{\text{adj}} = V_{\text{land}} W_{\text{corr}} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times L_{\max} \times d_h}\]

docs.title: 2.3 Rectified Softpick Landmark Attention
docs.text:
Landmark score logits are computed by multiplying query features with landmark key features:

\[S_{\text{land}} = \phi(Q) K_{\text{land}}^T \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times N \times L_{\max}}\]

Softpick rectified activation with temperature scaling \(T\) yields sparse landmark attention weights:

\[m_i = \max_l S_{\text{land}, i, l}, \quad e_{i, l} = \exp\left( \frac{S_{\text{land}, i, l} - m_i}{T} \right)\] \[p_{i, l} = \frac{\max\left(0, e_{i, l} - \exp(-m_i / T)\right)}{\sum_k \max\left(0, e_{i, k} - \exp(-m_i / T)\right) + \epsilon}\] \[C_{\text{leka}} = p \cdot V_{\text{adj}} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times N \times d_h}\]

docs.title: 2.4 Gated Local Sliding Window Integration
docs.text:
Local sliding window attention computes scaled dot-product attention within local radius \(W_{\text{local}}\):

\[S_{\text{local}, i, j} = \frac{Q_i K_j^T}{\sqrt{d_h}} + M^{\text{window}}_{i, j}, \quad M^{\text{window}}_{i, j} = \begin{cases} 0 & |i - j| \le \lfloor W_{\text{local}} / 2 \rfloor \\ -\infty & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}\] \[C_{\text{local}} = \text{Softmax}\left( S_{\text{local}} \right) V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times N \times d_h}\]

Landmark and local contexts are interpolated via a learnable per-head gating parameter \(g_{\text{local}} \in \mathbb{R}^H\):

\[\alpha = \sigma(g_{\text{local}}) \in [0, 1]^H\] \[C = \alpha \odot C_{\text{leka}} + (1 - \alpha) \odot C_{\text{local}} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times N \times d_h}\]

The fused tensor is reshaped and projected through output linear layer \(W_O\):

\[Y = \text{Reshape}(C) W_O + b_O \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times D}\]

docs.title: 3. Tensor Execution Flow & Dimensional Shape Tracing
docs.text: Execution Step Tensor Symbol Shape Transformation Operational Description Input State \(X\) \([B, N, D]\) Base activation state Linear Projections Q/K/V \(Q, K, V\) \([B, N, D] \to [B, H, N, d_h]\) Multi-head view split Dual-Scale RFF Mapping \(\phi(Q), \phi(K)\) \([B, H, N, d_h] \to [B, H, N, d_{\text{feat}}]\) Dual projection \(\cos/\sin\) concatenation Landmark MLP Scoring \(\text{Scores}_{\text{land}}\) \([B, H, N, d_{\text{feat}}] \to [B, H, N]\) Two-layer MLP scoring network Top-L Landmark Gather \(K_{\text{land}}, V_{\text{land}}\) \([B, H, N, \dots] \to [B, H, L_{\max}, \dots]\) Top-\(L_{\max}\) token index gather Value Correction Matrix \(V_{\text{adj}}\) \([B, H, L_{\max}, d_h] \times [H, d_h, d_h] \to [B, H, L_{\max}, d_h]\) Tensor contraction \(V_{\text{land}} W_{\text{corr}}\) Landmark Softpick Attn \(C_{\text{leka}}\) \([B, H, N, d_{\text{feat}}] \times [B, H, L_{\max}, d_{\text{feat}}]^T \to [B, H, N, d_h]\) Rectified Softpick value contraction Local Sliding Window \(C_{\text{local}}\) \([B, H, N, d_h] \times [B, H, N, d_h]^T \to [B, H, N, d_h]\) Band-masked softmax attention Sigmoidal Gate Fusion \(C\) \([B, H, N, d_h]\) \(\sigma(g) C_{\text{leka}} + (1 - \sigma(g)) C_{\text{local}}\) Output GEMM \(Y\) \([B, N, H \cdot d_h] \to [B, N, D]\) Layer output projection

docs.title: 4.1 Floating Point Operations (FLOPs)
docs.text:
Let \(B\) be batch size, \(N\) sequence length, \(D\) model dimension, \(H\) head count, \(d_h = D/H\) head dimension, \(F_1, F_2\) RFF feature dimensions (\(d_{\text{feat}} = 2F_1 + 2F_2\)), \(L_{\max}\) landmark count, and \(W_{\text{local}}\) local window width.

  1. Linear Q, K, V Projections: $\(\text{FLOPs}_{\text{proj}} = 3 \times 2 B N D^2 = 6 B N D^2\)$

  2. Dual-Scale RFF Mapping: Dual projections (\(x W_1, x W_2\)): \(2 B H N d_h (F_1 + F_2) = 2 B N D (F_1 + F_2)\) $\(\text{FLOPs}_{\text{rff}} = 2 B N D (F_1 + F_2)\)$

  3. Landmark MLP Scoring & Gathering: MLP scorer: \(2 B H N d_{\text{feat}} (F_1) + 2 B H N (F_1) (1) = 2 B H N d_{\text{feat}} F_1\) $\(\text{FLOPs}_{\text{score}} = 2 B H N d_{\text{feat}} F_1\)$

  4. Value Correction & Landmark Softpick Attention: Value correction matrix product \(V_{\text{land}} W_{\text{corr}}\): \(2 B H L_{\max} d_h^2 = 2 B L_{\max} D d_h\) Furthermore, Landmark score product \(\phi(Q) K_{\text{land}}^T\): \(2 B H N L_{\max} d_{\text{feat}}\) Concurrently, Softpick & Value contraction \(p V_{\text{adj}}\): \(2 B H N L_{\max} d_h = 2 B N L_{\max} D\) $\(\text{FLOPs}_{\text{land}} = 2 B L_{\max} D d_h + 2 B H N L_{\max} d_{\text{feat}} + 2 B N L_{\max} D\)$

  5. Local Sliding Window Attention: $\(\text{FLOPs}_{\text{local}} = 4 B N D W_{\text{local}}\)$

Total FLOP Count:

\[\text{FLOPs}_{\text{total}} \approx 6 B N D^2 + 2 B H N L_{\max} d_{\text{feat}} + 2 B N L_{\max} D + 4 B N D W_{\text{local}}\]

docs.title: 4.2 Memory Footprint & Bandwidth
docs.text:
Specifically, regarding \textbf{Parameter Footprint},

$\(\Theta = 4 D^2 + (d_h F_1 + d_h F_2) + \Theta_{\text{scorer}} + H d_h^2 = 4 D^2 + d_h (F_1 + F_2) + d_{\text{feat}} F_1 + H d_h^2\)$ Specifically, regarding \textbf{Activation Footprint}, Furthermore, Landmark feature buffers: \(\mathcal{O}(B H L_{\max} d_{\text{feat}})\) Concurrently, Landmark attention matrix: \(\mathcal{O}(B H N L_{\max})\) In this setting, Local window logits: \(\mathcal{O}(B H N W_{\text{local}})\) Additionally, Total Memory: \(\mathcal{O}\left(B N D + B H N L_{\max} + B H N W_{\text{local}}\right)\)

docs.title: 5. Architectural Bottlenecks, Rank Collapse & Failure Modes
5.1 Landmark Collapse in Uniform Sequences
docs.text: At the architectural level, the underlying operational mechanism reveals that the landmark MLP scorer evaluates \(\text{MLP}(\phi(K))\). If key features exhibit low variance across the sequence (e.g., repeating tokens or uniform padding), the Top-k operator selects redundant landmark indices. Consequently, this dynamic induces structural implications wherein the landmark summary loses diversity, degrading global attention to a localized repeating context.

docs.title: 5.2 Value Correction Matrix Ill-Conditioning
docs.text: At the architectural level, the underlying operational mechanism reveals that the value correction tensor \(W_{\text{corr}} \in \mathbb{R}^{H \times d_h \times d_h}\) is initialized to the identity matrix. Unconstrained optimization can cause singular values of \(W_{\text{corr}}\) to collapse to zero, corrupting value representations. To systematically mitigate this constraint, the framework enforces an optimization protocol such that add an orthogonal regularization penalty \(\mathcal{L}_{\text{ortho}} = \|W_{\text{corr}}^T W_{\text{corr}} - I\|_F^2\).

docs.title: 5.3 Softpick Temperature Gradient Lock
docs.text: At the architectural level, the underlying operational mechanism reveals that setting Softpick temperature \(T < 0.2\) causes aggressive tail subtraction, zeroing off-diagonal landmark probabilities and locking backpropagation gradients.

docs.title: LEKAv3: Linear-Time Efficient Kernel Attention with Value-Scored Semantic Landmarks and Multi-Scale RFF
1. Abstract & Theoretical Motivation
docs.text:
Standard Multi-Head Self-Attention (MHSA) scales quadratically \(\mathcal{O}(N^2)\) with sequence length \(N\), posing prohibitive computational and memory bottlenecks. While random feature kernel attention linearizes attention to \(\mathcal{O}(N \cdot F \cdot d_h)\), it struggles with spatial over-smoothing and loss of associative memory. Furthermore, key-based landmark selection heuristics frequently select redundant tokens that carry minimal semantic value.

LEKAv3 (Linear-time Efficient Kernel Attention v3) presents an advanced hybrid attention mechanism incorporating four core innovations: 1. Value-State Semantic Landmark Selection: Unlike traditional landmark models that evaluate keys or queries, LEKAv3 dynamically scores tokens via an MLP operating directly on Value representations \(V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times N \times d_h}\), ensuring landmarks are selected based on semantic output information content. 2. Multi-Scale Random Fourier Feature (RFF) Mapping: Query and key vectors are projected into a multi-scale trigonometric space using dual random projection matrices (\(F_1\) and \(F_2 = F_1 / 2\)), capturing both broad sequence context and fine-grained feature correlations. 3. Value Correction Tensor Transformation: Employs a learnable per-head transformation tensor \(W_{\text{corr}} \in \mathbb{R}^{H \times d_h \times d_h}\) to adapt gathered landmark values prior to context contraction. 4. Gated Softpick Landmark & Local Window Fusion: Blends Softpick rectified landmark attention (\(C_{\text{land}}\)) with local sliding-window softmax attention (\(C_{\text{local}}\)) via a learnable per-head sigmoidal gating parameter \(g\).

docs.title: 2.1 Multi-Scale Random Fourier Feature Mapping
docs.text:
For projected queries and keys \(Q, K \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times N \times d_h}\), multi-scale random projections \(W_1 \in \mathbb{R}^{d_h \times F_1}\) and \(W_2 \in \mathbb{R}^{d_h \times F_2}\) (where \(F_2 = F_1 / 2\)) generate trigonometric feature maps:

\[P_1 = x W_1 \implies \phi_1(x) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{F_1}} \left[ \cos(P_1), \; \sin(P_1) \right] \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times N \times 2F_1}\] \[P_2 = x W_2 \implies \phi_2(x) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{F_2}} \left[ \cos(P_2), \; \sin(P_2) \right] \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times N \times 2F_2}\] \[\phi(x) = \left[ \phi_1(x), \; \phi_2(x) \right] \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times N \times d_{\text{feat}}}, \quad d_{\text{feat}} = 2F_1 + 2F_2\]

docs.title: 2.2 Value-State Semantic Landmark Selection (select_landmarks)
docs.text:
Token importance scores are predicted directly from Value states \(V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times N \times d_h}\) using a two-layer bottleneck network:

\[\text{Scores}_{\text{land}} = \text{Linear}_2\left( \text{GELU}\left( \text{Linear}_1( V ) \right) \right) \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times N}\]

The top-\(L_{\max}\) landmark token indices \(\mathcal{I}_{\text{land}} \in \{1, \dots, N\}^{L_{\max}}\) are extracted:

\[\mathcal{I}_{\text{land}} = \text{TopK}\left( \text{Scores}_{\text{land}}, L_{\max}, \text{dim}=-1 \right)\]

Key features \(\phi(K)\) and Value representations \(V\) are gathered at landmark indices:

\[K_{\text{land}} = \text{gather}\left( \phi(K), \mathcal{I}_{\text{land}} \right) \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times L_{\max} \times d_{\text{feat}}}\] \[V_{\text{land}} = \text{gather}\left( V, \mathcal{I}_{\text{land}} \right) \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times L_{\max} \times d_h}\]

Gathered landmark values are adjusted by learnable correction tensor \(W_{\text{corr}} \in \mathbb{R}^{H \times d_h \times d_h}\):

\[V_{\text{adj}} = V_{\text{land}} W_{\text{corr}} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times L_{\max} \times d_h}\]

docs.title: 2.3 Rectified Softpick Landmark Attention
docs.text:
Landmark score logits evaluate inner products between query features \(\phi(Q)\) and landmark key features \(K_{\text{land}}\):

\[S_{\text{land}} = \phi(Q) K_{\text{land}}^T \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times N \times L_{\max}}\]

Softpick rectified activation with temperature scaling \(T\) normalizes probabilities:

\[m_i = \max_l S_{\text{land}, i, l}, \quad e_{i, l} = \exp\left( \frac{S_{\text{land}, i, l} - m_i}{T} \right)\] \[p_{i, l} = \frac{\max\left(0, e_{i, l} - \exp(-m_i / T)\right)}{\sum_k \max\left(0, e_{i, k} - \exp(-m_i / T)\right) + \epsilon}\] \[C_{\text{land}} = p \cdot V_{\text{adj}} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times N \times d_h}\]

docs.title: 2.4 Local Window Attention & Sigmoidal Gate Fusion
docs.text:
Local sliding window attention evaluates scaled dot-product attention within local radius \(W_{\text{local}}\):

\[S_{\text{local}, i, j} = \frac{Q_i K_j^T}{\sqrt{d_h}} + M^{\text{window}}_{i, j}, \quad M^{\text{window}}_{i, j} = \begin{cases} 0 & |i - j| \le \lfloor W_{\text{local}} / 2 \rfloor \\ -\infty & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}\] \[C_{\text{local}} = \text{Softmax}\left( S_{\text{local}} \right) V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times N \times d_h}\]

Landmark context \(C_{\text{land}}\) and local context \(C_{\text{local}}\) are interpolated via learnable per-head gate parameter \(g \in \mathbb{R}^H\):

\[\alpha = \sigma(g) \in [0, 1]^H\] \[C = \alpha \odot C_{\text{land}} + (1 - \alpha) \odot C_{\text{local}} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times N \times d_h}\]

Reshaping into \([B, N, H \cdot d_h]\), the output is projected back to model dimension \(D\):

\[Y = \text{Reshape}(C) W_O + b_O \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times D}\]

docs.title: 4.1 Floating Point Operations (FLOPs)
docs.text:
Let \(B\) be batch size, \(N\) sequence length, \(D\) model dimension, \(H\) head count, \(d_h = D/H\) head dimension, \(F_1, F_2\) RFF feature dimensions (\(d_{\text{feat}} = 2F_1 + 2F_2\)), \(L_{\max}\) landmark count, and \(W_{\text{local}}\) local window width.

  1. Linear Q, K, V Projections: $\(\text{FLOPs}_{\text{proj}} = 3 \times 2 B N D^2 = 6 B N D^2\)$
  2. Multi-Scale RFF Feature Mapping: $\(\text{FLOPs}_{\text{rff}} = 2 B N D (F_1 + F_2)\)$

  3. Value Semantic Landmark Scoring: Bottleneck MLP operating on \(V\): \(2 B H N d_h (32) + 2 B H N (32) (1) = 64 B N D + 64 B H N\) $\(\text{FLOPs}_{\text{score}} \approx 64 B N D\)$

  4. Value Correction & Landmark Softpick Attention: Value correction tensor product \(V_{\text{land}} W_{\text{corr}}\): \(2 B H L_{\max} d_h^2 = 2 B L_{\max} D d_h\) Furthermore, Landmark score product \(\phi(Q) K_{\text{land}}^T\): \(2 B H N L_{\max} d_{\text{feat}}\) Concurrently, Softpick & Value contraction \(p V_{\text{adj}}\): \(2 B H N L_{\max} d_h = 2 B N L_{\max} D\) $\(\text{FLOPs}_{\text{land}} = 2 B L_{\max} D d_h + 2 B H N L_{\max} d_{\text{feat}} + 2 B N L_{\max} D\)$

  5. Local Sliding Window Attention: $\(\text{FLOPs}_{\text{local}} = 4 B N D W_{\text{local}}\)$

Total FLOP Count:

\[\text{FLOPs}_{\text{total}} \approx 6 B N D^2 + 2 B H N L_{\max} d_{\text{feat}} + 2 B N L_{\max} D + 4 B N D W_{\text{local}}\]

docs.title: 4.2 Memory Footprint & Bandwidth
docs.text:
Specifically, regarding \textbf{Parameter Footprint},

$\(\Theta = 4 D^2 + (d_h F_1 + d_h F_2) + \Theta_{\text{v\_scorer}} + H d_h^2 = 4 D^2 + d_h (F_1 + F_2) + 33 d_h + H d_h^2\)$ Specifically, regarding \textbf{Activation Footprint}, Furthermore, Landmark feature buffers: \(\mathcal{O}(B H L_{\max} d_{\text{feat}})\) Concurrently, Landmark attention matrix: \(\mathcal{O}(B H N L_{\max})\) In this setting, Local window logits: \(\mathcal{O}(B H N W_{\text{local}})\) Additionally, Total Memory: \(\mathcal{O}\left(B N D + B H N L_{\max} + B H N W_{\text{local}}\right)\)

docs.title: 5. Architectural Bottlenecks, Rank Collapse & Failure Modes
5.1 Value-State Landmark Score Saturation
docs.text: At the architectural level, the underlying operational mechanism reveals that the landmark MLP scorer evaluates \(\text{MLP}(V)\). If value states \(V\) saturate due to large norm values in deep network layers, the MLP output logits flatten, leading to random Top-k landmark selection. To systematically mitigate this constraint, the framework enforces an optimization protocol such that apply RMSNorm to Value states \(V\) before feeding into landmark_scorer.

docs.title: 5.2 Value Correction Matrix Identity Collapse
docs.text: At the architectural level, the underlying operational mechanism reveals that \(W_{\text{corr}}\) is initialized to identity matrices \(I_{d_h}\). If learning rates are too high, \(W_{\text{corr}}\) weights can drift towards zero, truncating landmark value output.

docs.title: 5.3 Softpick Temperature Gradient Lock
docs.text: At the architectural level, the underlying operational mechanism reveals that setting Softpick temperature \(T < 0.2\) causes aggressive tail subtraction, zeroing off-diagonal landmark probabilities and locking backpropagation gradients.

docs.title: Linformer Attention: Linear-Complexity Sequence Projection via Low-Rank Matrix Factorization
1. Executive Abstract & Architectural Motivation
docs.text:
Standard Multi-Head Self-Attention (Vaswani et al., 2017) computes pairwise token interactions across length \(L\), incurring an \(\mathcal{O}(L^2)\) computational and memory complexity wall. Linformer (Wang et al., 2020) mitigates this bottleneck by proving empirically and theoretically that the normalized attention matrix \(A \in \mathbb{R}^{L imes L}\) is low-rank.

The core architectural motivation of Linformer is to decompose the key and value sequence length projections down to a fixed, compact parameter \(k \ll L\). By applying linear projection matrices \(E, F \in \mathbb{R}^{k imes L}\) along the sequence length dimension, Linformer compresses the key and value representations from \(\mathbb{R}^{L imes d}\) to \(\mathbb{R}^{k imes d}\). This enables scaled dot-product attention to be computed in \(\mathcal{O}(L \cdot k)\) time and memory, maintaining linear scaling with respect to sequence length \(L\). Linformer is particularly effective for long-document processing where \(L \gg k\).

docs.title: 2. Mathematical Formulations & Derivations
docs.text:
Given input sequence representations \(X \in \mathbb{R}^{B imes L imes D}\), Linformer projects \(X\) into query, key, and value subspaces:

\[ Q = X W_Q \in \mathbb{R}^{B imes L imes D}, \quad K = X W_K \in \mathbb{R}^{B imes L imes D}, \quad V = X W_V \in \mathbb{R}^{B imes L imes D} \]

Partitioning into \(H\) heads with head dimension \(d_k = D / H\) yields \(Q_h, K_h, V_h \in \mathbb{R}^{B imes H imes L imes d_k}\).

To compress sequence length, head-specific or parameter-shared linear projection matrices \(E_h, F_h \in \mathbb{R}^{k imes L}\) project sequence dimensions of \(K_h\) and \(V_h\):

\[ \widetilde{K}_h = E_h K_h \in \mathbb{R}^{B imes H imes k imes d_k}, \quad \widetilde{V}_h = F_h V_h \in \mathbb{R}^{B imes H imes k imes d_k} \]

The scaled dot-product score matrix \(S_h \in \mathbb{R}^{B imes H imes L imes k}\) is computed as:

\[ S_h = rac{Q_h \widetilde{K}_h^ op}{\sqrt{d_k}} \in \mathbb{R}^{B imes H imes L imes k} \]

Applying row-wise Softmax along the compressed dimension \(k\):

\[ A_h = ext{Softmax}_k (S_h) \in \mathbb{R}^{B imes H imes L imes k} \]

Context aggregation yields head representation \(O_h \in \mathbb{R}^{B imes H imes L imes d_k}\):

\[ O_h = A_h \widetilde{V}_h = ext{Softmax}\left( rac{Q_h (E_h K_h)^ op}{\sqrt{d_k}} ight) (F_h V_h) \]

Finally, head outputs are concatenated and projected to model dimension \(D\):

\[ ext{Context} = ext{Concat}(O_1, \dots, O_H) \in \mathbb{R}^{B imes L imes D}, \quad Y = ext{Context} \cdot W_O \in \mathbb{R}^{B imes L imes D} \]

docs.title: 3. Step-by-Step Tensor Execution Trace
docs.text:
Input: hidden_states [B, L, D]
  │
  ├──> Q = Linear(D, D)(hidden_states) ──> [B, L, H, d_k] ──> transpose(1, 2) ──> [B, H, L, d_k]
  ├──> K = Linear(D, D)(hidden_states) ──> [B, L, H, d_k] ──> transpose(1, 2) ──> [B, H, L, d_k]
  └──> V = Linear(D, D)(hidden_states) ──> [B, L, H, d_k] ──> transpose(1, 2) ──> [B, H, L, d_k]
         │
         ├──> Compressed K: E @ K ──> [B, H, k, d_k]
         ├──> Compressed V: F @ V ──> [B, H, k, d_k]
         │
         ├──> MatMul: Q @ Compressed_K.T / sqrt(d_k) ──> Scores: [B, H, L, k]
         ├──> Softmax(dim=-1) ──> Attn Map: [B, H, L, k]
         ├──> MatMul: Attn @ Compressed_V ──> Context: [B, H, L, d_k]
