docs.title: Computational and Analytical Complexity Breakdown
docs.text: The computational workload of the FAVOR+ mechanism is governed by the projection dimensionality, head allocation, and the chosen random feature budget \(m\). Initial linear projections for queries, keys, and values (\(W_Q, W_K, W_V\)) demand \(6 B L D^2\) floating-point operations (FLOPs). Subsequently, projecting query and key matrices into the randomized feature space via \(Q W^\top\) and \(K W^\top\) incurs \(2 \times (2 B H L \cdot d_k \cdot m) = 4 B L m D\) FLOPs. Exploiting matrix multiplication associativity, the unmasked associative key-value state \(KV = \phi(K)^\top V\) aggregates contextual information across the sequence with a computational budget of \(2 B H \cdot m \cdot L \cdot d_k = 2 B L m D\) FLOPs. The context numerator product \(\phi(Q) KV\) similarly accounts for \(2 B H \cdot L \cdot m \cdot d_k = 2 B L m D\) FLOPs, while the scalar denominator normalizer \(\phi(Q) K_{\text{sum}}^\top\) introduces an auxiliary overhead of \(2 B H L m\) FLOPs. Concluding the forward pass, the linear output projection \(W_O\) requires \(2 B L D^2\) FLOPs. Consequently, the cumulative computational load reaches \(4 B L D^2 + 4 B L m D\) multiply-accumulate operations (MACs), corresponding to \(8 B L D^2 + 8 B L m D\) total FLOPs and establishing strict \(\mathcal{O}(L)\) asymptotic complexity with respect to sequence length.

docs.title: Memory Footprint and Activation Allocation
docs.text: In terms of memory residency, the model maintains a compact footprint composed of static parameter tensors and dynamic activation caches. Static allocations are restricted to \(4 D^2\) projection weights complemented by an \(m \cdot d_k\) orthogonal projection buffer. Concurrently, transient activation memory during training and autoregressive decoding remains strictly bounded by \(\mathcal{O}(B \cdot H \cdot m \cdot d_k + B \cdot H \cdot L \cdot m)\), entirely circumventing the prohibitive quadratic \(\mathcal{O}(L^2)\) matrix storage required by conventional multi-head attention.

docs.title: 5. Failure Modes, Rank Collapse & Edge Cases
docs.text:
The theoretical convergence and practical stability of the FAVOR+ estimator are intimately linked to the number of random feature projections \(m\) and the underlying precision regime. When the random feature dimension is constrained such that \(m \ll d_k\), the Monte Carlo variance of the positive feature mapping \(\phi(x)\) increases substantially. This stochastic variance distorts the implicit attention weight distribution, introducing non-negligible gradient noise that roughens the optimization landscape and degrades retrieval precision on associative recall tasks.

Furthermore, evaluating the exponential non-linearity \(\exp(W x)\) introduces acute vulnerability to numerical overflow under standard IEEE half-precision (FP16) arithmetic. Subtracting maximum logit projections prior to exponentiation and executing feature mappings in high-precision formats (FP32 or BF16) is indispensable for preserving numerical conditioning. During causal autoregressive processing, continuous prefix accumulation in the recurrent state \(KV_t = KV_{t-1} + \phi(K_t)^\top V_t\) can induce monotonic magnitude drift and eigenvalue explosion over extended context windows, necessitating periodic renormalization or decay factors. Finally, the effective expressivity of the linearized kernel operator is fundamentally constrained by an intrinsic rank bottleneck, wherein the rank of the implicit attention matrix cannot exceed \(\min(L, m)\), thereby enforcing a structural upper bound on contextual capacity relative to dense full-rank attention.

docs.title: 6. Hardware Acceleration Blueprint & Triton Kernel Design
docs.text:
The core performance driver for Performer in Triton is fusing feature map computation \(\phi(K)\), outer product accumulation, and query projection into a single persistent warp kernel.

# Triton Fused Performer Linear Scan Blueprint
import triton
import triton.language as tl

@triton.jit
def _performer_causal_scan_kernel(
    Q_ptr, K_ptr, V_ptr, W_ptr, Out_ptr,
    stride_qb, stride_qh, stride_ql, stride_qd,
    L, m, d_k,
    BLOCK_M: tl.constexpr
):
    pid_bh = tl.program_id(0)

    # Initialize persistent state memory in SRAM
    kv_state = tl.zeros((m, d_k), dtype=tl.float32)
    k_sum = tl.zeros((m,), dtype=tl.float32)

    for t in range(L):
        # Load single token Q_t, K_t, V_t
        q_t = tl.load(Q_ptr + pid_bh * stride_qh + t * stride_ql + tl.arange(0, d_k))
        k_t = tl.load(K_ptr + pid_bh * stride_qh + t * stride_ql + tl.arange(0, d_k))
        v_t = tl.load(V_ptr + pid_bh * stride_qh + t * stride_ql + tl.arange(0, d_k))

        # Fused Positive Feature Map phi(k_t)
        phi_k = tl.exp(tl.dot(k_t[None, :], W_ptr) - 0.5 * tl.sum(k_t * k_t))
        phi_q = tl.exp(tl.dot(q_t[None, :], W_ptr) - 0.5 * tl.sum(q_t * q_t))

        # Accumulate state: kv_state += phi_k.T @ v_t
        kv_state += tl.dot(tl.trans(phi_k), v_t[None, :])
        k_sum += tl.sum(phi_k, axis=0)

        # Compute output
        num = tl.dot(phi_q, kv_state)
        den = tl.sum(phi_q * k_sum) + 1e-6
        out_t = num / den

        tl.store(Out_ptr + pid_bh * stride_qh + t * stride_ql + tl.arange(0, d_k), out_t)

docs.title: 7. Next-Generation Innovations & Synthesis Opportunities
docs.text: To advance the efficiency and representational fidelity of linearized kernel attention, several promising architectural directions emerge. First, replacing standard independently and identically distributed Gaussian projection matrices with Structured Orthogonal Ensembles (ORF+)—such as Gram-Schmidt orthogonalized block Hadamard matrices—substantially suppresses kernel approximation variance without incurring additional computational overhead. Furthermore, establishing a hybrid Performer-State Space Model (SSM) architecture by synthesizing FAVOR+ positive feature maps with selective discretization dynamics enables continuous-time recurrent memory updates while strictly maintaining linear algorithmic complexity. Concurrently, quantizing intermediate positive feature activations \(\phi(x)\) into microscopic 8-bit floating-point formats (e.g., FP8 E4M3) offers the potential to double memory bus throughput and enhance arithmetic intensity across contemporary GPU architectures like NVIDIA Hopper and Blackwell, facilitating ultra-long sequence processing at minimal energetic cost.

docs.title: PHANTOM: Parameter-Hashed AttentioN with Token-wise Orthogonal Mapping via Deterministic CUR Decomposition and Angular LSH
1. Executive Abstract & Architectural Motivation
docs.text:
Standard Multi-Head Self-Attention (MHSA) in Transformer models requires quadratic computational time and memory scaling \(\mathcal{O}(N^2)\) with sequence length \(N\), presenting significant bottlenecks for long-context deployment. While dense low-rank projections reduce parameter counts, standard SVD linear layers discard structural column/row interpretable sparsity. Furthermore, sparse attention heuristics often fail to dynamically route non-local dependencies.

PHANTOM (Parameter-Hashed AttentioN with Token-wise Orthogonal Mapping) presents an integrated sparse attention architecture combining two structural advances: 1. Deterministic Statistical Leverage-Score CUR Decomposition: Pre-trained weight matrices (\(W_Q, W_K, W_V, W_O\)) are decomposed via CUR matrix factorization. Down and up projection matrices are explicitly formed from the top-\(r\) rows \(R\) and columns \(C\) exhibiting highest empirical statistical leverage scores \(\ell_{\text{row}}, \ell_{\text{col}}\), joined by the pseudoinverse of their intersection submatrix \(W_{\cap}^{\dagger}\). 2. Multi-Round Angular Locality-Sensitive Hashing (LSH): L2-normalized queries and keys are projected across \(M\) independent hashing rounds using random Gaussian hyperplane matrices \(P \in \mathbb{R}^{d_h \times B_s}\). Binary hash codes bucket semantically aligned tokens into discrete buckets, reducing attention computation from \(\mathcal{O}(N^2)\) to expected sub-quadratic complexity \(\mathcal{O}\left(M \cdot \frac{N^2}{2^{B_s}} \cdot d_h\right)\). 3. Softpick Rectified Activation: Intra-bucket attention scores are evaluated using a rectified non-linear probability mapping (softpick), preventing soft background noise accumulation and artificial sink token collapse.

docs.title: 2.1 Statistical Leverage-Score CUR Matrix Decomposition (FactorisedLinear_CUR)
docs.text:
For a pre-trained projection weight matrix \(W \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{out}} \times d_{\text{in}}}\), the full singular value decomposition \(W = U \Sigma V^T\) is evaluated. Empirical row and column leverage scores are defined as:

\[\ell_{\text{row}}(i) = \frac{\|U_{i, :}\|_2^2}{\sum_{i'=1}^{d_{\text{out}}} \|U_{i', :}\|_2^2}, \quad \ell_{\text{col}}(j) = \frac{\|V_{:, j}\|_2^2}{\sum_{j'=1}^{d_{\text{in}}} \|V_{:, j'}\|_2^2}\]

Selecting the top-\(r\) row indices \(\mathcal{I}_{\text{row}}\) and column indices \(\mathcal{I}_{\text{col}}\) yields row matrix \(R \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times d_{\text{in}}}\), column matrix \(C \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{out}} \times r}\), and intersection matrix \(W_{\cap} \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times r}\):

\[R = W_{\mathcal{I}_{\text{row}}, :}, \quad C = W_{:, \mathcal{I}_{\text{col}}}, \quad W_{\cap} = W_{\mathcal{I}_{\text{row}}, \mathcal{I}_{\text{col}}}\]

The CUR matrix approximation evaluates:

\[W \approx C W_{\cap}^{\dagger} R, \quad \text{where } W_{\cap}^{\dagger} = \text{pinv}(W_{\cap}) \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times r}\]

The factorized down-projection layer \(W_{\text{down}} \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times d_{\text{in}}}\) and up-projection layer \(W_{\text{up}} \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{out}} \times r}\) are initialized as:

\[W_{\text{down}} = R, \quad W_{\text{up}} = C W_{\cap}^{\dagger}\]

For activation tensor \(X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times d_{\text{in}}}\), projection output evaluates:

\[Y = (X W_{\text{down}}^T) W_{\text{up}}^T + b = (X R^T) (C W_{\cap}^{\dagger})^T + b \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times d_{\text{out}}}\]

docs.title: 2.2 Multi-Round Angular LSH Bucketing (lsh_attention)
docs.text:
For queries and keys \(Q, K \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times N \times d_h}\), L2-normalization is enforced:

\[\hat{Q} = \frac{Q}{\|Q\|_2 + \epsilon}, \quad \hat{K} = \frac{K}{\|K\|_2 + \epsilon}\]

For each hashing round \(m \in \{1, \dots, M\}\), a random Gaussian projection matrix \(P^{(m)} \in \mathbb{R}^{d_h \times B_s}\) is sampled, where \(B_s\) is the binary bit-width. Discrete integer hash codes \(h(q), h(k) \in \{0, \dots, 2^{B_s}-1\}\) are computed via inner-product sign bit shifting:

\[h(q_{b, h, i}) = \sum_{k=0}^{B_s-1} 2^k \cdot \mathbb{I}\left( \langle \hat{Q}_{b, h, i}, P_{:, k}^{(m)} \rangle > 0 \right)\] \[h(k_{b, h, j}) = \sum_{k=0}^{B_s-1} 2^k \cdot \mathbb{I}\left( \langle \hat{K}_{b, h, j}, P_{:, k}^{(m)} \rangle > 0 \right)\]

docs.title: 2.3 Intra-Bucket Softpick Rectified Attention
docs.text:
Tokens sharing matching hash codes \(h(q_i) = h(k_j) = c\) are grouped into hash buckets \(\mathcal{B}_c\). Scaled dot-product attention logits are evaluated exclusively within bucket key sets \(\mathcal{B}_{h(q_i)}\):

\[S_{b, h, i, j} = \frac{Q_{b, h, i} \cdot K_{b, h, j}^T}{\sqrt{d_h}}, \quad \text{for } j \in \mathcal{B}_{h(q_i)}\]

The Softpick activation applies temperature scaling \(\tau\) and subtracts the maximum tail threshold:

\[m_i = \max_{j \in \mathcal{B}_{h(q_i)}} S_{i, j}, \quad e_{i, j} = \exp\left( \frac{S_{i, j} - m_i}{\tau} \right)\] \[p_{i, j} = \frac{\max\left(0, e_{i, j} - \exp(-m_i / \tau)\right)}{\sum_{k \in \mathcal{B}_{h(q_i)}} \max\left(0, e_{i, k} - \exp(-m_i / \tau)\right) + \epsilon}\] \[O_{b, h, i}^{(m)} = \sum_{j \in \mathcal{B}_{h(q_i)}} p_{b, h, i, j} V_{b, h, j}\]

docs.title: 2.4 Multi-Round Accumulation & Final Projection
docs.text:
Context outputs are averaged across all \(M\) independent hashing rounds:

\[O^{\text{fused}} = \frac{1}{M} \sum_{m=1}^M O^{(m)} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times N \times d_h}\]

Reshaping into \([B, N, H \cdot d_h]\), the context tensor is projected through the CUR factorized output layer:

\[Y = \text{FactorisedLinear\_CUR}_{\text{out}}\left( \text{Reshape}(O^{\text{fused}}) \right) \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times D}\]

      Output Low-Rank CUR Projection (FactorisedLinear_CUR)
             │
             ▼

docs.title: 4.1 FLOPs Computation Breakdown
docs.text:
Let \(B\) be batch size, \(N\) sequence length, \(D\) model dimension, \(H\) head count, \(d_h = D/H\) head dimension, \(r\) CUR compression rank, \(M\) LSH rounds, and \(B_s\) bucket bit-width (producing \(2^{B_s}\) buckets).

  1. CUR Linear Projections (\(Q, K, V, O\)): $\(\text{FLOPs}_{\text{proj}} = 4 \times \left( 2 B N D r + 2 B N r D \right) = 16 B N D r\)$

  2. LSH Hyperplane Hash Evaluation: Query & key L2 normalization: \(4 B H N d_h = 4 B N D\) Furthermore, Hyperplane inner-product matmul (\(M\) rounds): \(M \times \left( 4 B H N d_h B_s \right) = 4 M B N D B_s\) $\(\text{FLOPs}_{\text{hash}} = 4 B N D + 4 M B N D B_s\)$

  3. Intra-Bucket Softpick Attention: Average bucket size \(N_{\text{bucket}} = N / 2^{B_s}\) Furthermore, Score evaluation per token across \(M\) rounds: \(M \times \left( 2 B H N \cdot \frac{N}{2^{B_s}} \cdot d_h \right) = 2 M B N D \cdot \frac{N}{2^{B_s}}\) Concurrently, Softpick non-linearity & Value contraction: \(2 M B N D \cdot \frac{N}{2^{B_s}}\) $\(\text{FLOPs}_{\text{lsh\_attn}} = 4 M B N D \cdot \frac{N}{2^{B_s}}\)$

\[\text{FLOPs}_{\text{total}} = 16 B N D r + 4 M B N D B_s + 4 M B N D \cdot \frac{N}{2^{B_s}}\]

docs.title: 4.2 MACs & Memory Footprint Analysis
docs.text:
Specifically, regarding \textbf{Multiply-Accumulate Operations (MACs)},

$\(\text{Total MACs} = 8 B N D r + 2 M B N D B_s + 2 M B N D \cdot \frac{N}{2^{B_s}}\)$ Specifically, regarding \textbf{Parameter Footprint},

$\(\Theta = 4 \times \left( d_{\text{in}} r + r d_{\text{out}} \right) = 8 D r\)$ Specifically, regarding \textbf{Activation Footprint}, Furthermore, Hash codes tensor: \(\mathcal{O}(M B H N)\) Concurrently, Bucket index mapping buffers: \(\mathcal{O}(M B H N)\) In this setting, Intra-bucket score tensors: \(\mathcal{O}\left(M B H N \cdot \frac{N}{2^{B_s}}\right)\) Additionally, Total Memory: \(\mathcal{O}\left(B N D + M B H N + M B H \frac{N^2}{2^{B_s}}\right)\)

docs.title: 4.3 Asymptotic Scalability Comparison
docs.text: Specifically, regarding \textbf{Standard Dense Attention}, \(\mathcal{O}(N^2 D)\) compute, \(\mathcal{O}(N^2 H)\) memory. Furthermore, regarding \textbf{PHANTOM LSH Attention}, \(\mathcal{O}\left(N \cdot \left(D r + M D B_s + M D \frac{N}{2^{B_s}}\right)\right)\) compute. When \(2^{B_s} \gg N\), total sequence attention scales linearly \(\mathcal{O}(N)\).

docs.title: 5. Architectural Bottlenecks, Rank Collapse & Edge Cases
5.1 CUR Intersection Matrix Ill-Conditioning
docs.text: At the architectural level, the underlying operational mechanism reveals that the CUR up-projection matrix relies on \(W_{\cap}^{\dagger} = \text{pinv}(W_{\mathcal{I}_{\text{row}}, \mathcal{I}_{\text{col}}})\). If selected top-leverage rows and columns contain linearly dependent vectors, the intersection submatrix \(W_{\cap} \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times r}\) becomes singular or severely ill-conditioned (condition number \(\kappa(W_{\cap}) > 10^7\)). Consequently, this dynamic induces structural implications wherein computing the pseudoinverse amplifies numerical noise, leading to exploding projection weights during forward execution. To systematically mitigate this constraint, the framework enforces an optimization protocol such that add a ridge regularization penalty \(W_{\cap}^{\dagger} = (W_{\cap}^T W_{\cap} + \epsilon I)^{-1} W_{\cap}^T\) with \(\epsilon = 10^{-6}\).

docs.title: 5.2 LSH Bucket Imbalance & Hash Collisions
docs.text: At the architectural level, the underlying operational mechanism reveals that random Gaussian hyperplanes partition token space into angular regions. If token embeddings are non-uniformly distributed (e.g., clustering around a single directional axis), a single bucket receives \(> 90\%\) of tokens, causing computational complexity to regress to full \(\mathcal{O}(N^2)\). To systematically mitigate this constraint, the framework enforces an optimization protocol such that deploy orthogonalized random hyperplanes (\(P^T P = I\)) and apply mean-centering to queries and keys prior to hyperplane projection.

docs.title: 5.3 Softpick Intra-Bucket Empty-Bucket Underflow
docs.text: At the architectural level, the underlying operational mechanism reveals that if a query token \(q_i\) maps to a hash code bucket \(c\) that contains zero key tokens (\(|\mathcal{B}_c| = 0\)), intra-bucket Softpick receives an empty logit array. To systematically mitigate this constraint, the framework enforces an optimization protocol such that implement fallback key assignment, routing queries with empty buckets to attend to the sequence start token (CLS/BOS token).

docs.title: 6.1 Triton Strategy 1: Fused Dual-GEMM CUR Projection Kernel
docs.text:
Standard PyTorch executes x @ R.T followed by @ (C @ W_int).T, writing intermediate rank-\(r\) activations back to DRAM.

Triton Optimization: Implement a custom fused GEMM kernel loading \(X_i \in \mathbb{R}^{\text{BLOCK\_M} \times D}\) into SRAM. Furthermore, Evaluate down-projection with \(R^T\) in SRAM registers, then immediately compute up-projection with \((C W_{\cap}^{\dagger})^T\). Concurrently, Reduces DRAM memory bandwidth overhead by \(2\times\).

docs.title: 6.2 Triton Strategy 2: Fused SRAM Hyperplane Hashing Kernel
docs.text: Fuse L2 normalization \(\hat{Q} = Q / \|Q\|_2\), matrix product \(\hat{Q} P\), sign comparison \(> 0\), and bit-shift summation into a single Triton kernel pass. Furthermore, Store bit-shift powers \(2^k\) in GPU constant memory. Concurrently, Writes integer hash codes \(h(q) \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times N}\) directly to global DRAM in a single pass.

docs.title: 6.3 Triton Strategy 3: Block-Sparse Intra-Bucket Softpick Engine
docs.text:
Executing intra-bucket attention via Python loops incurs severe CPU-GPU launch overhead.

Triton Optimization: Sort tokens by hash code using a parallel shared-memory radix sort kernel. Furthermore, Launch a block-sparse Triton kernel where each threadblock processes tokens belonging to a single hash bucket \(\mathcal{B}_c\). Concurrently, Load bucket keys \(K_{\mathcal{B}_c}\) and values \(V_{\mathcal{B}_c}\) into SRAM, evaluating online Softpick score tail subtraction and value contraction entirely within register space.

docs.title: 7. Next-Generation Innovations & Synthesis Opportunities
docs.text:
1. Adaptive Cross-Bucket Attention Range Expansion: Allow query tokens to attend not only to their primary hash bucket \(\mathcal{B}_{h(q)}\) but also to Hamming-distance-1 neighbor buckets (\(\mathcal{H}(h(q), h(k)) \le 1\)), recovering lost boundary key context.
  2. Structured CUR+LoRA Hybrid Parameterization: Augment statistical leverage CUR down/up linear projections with trainable rank-4 LoRA adapter pairs \((\Delta W = A B)\), enabling task adaptation while retaining physical column/row interpretability.
  3. FlashAttention-3 FP8 Intra-Bucket Execution: Execute intra-bucket matrix multiplications \(Q_{\mathcal{B}} K_{\mathcal{B}}^T\) using 8-bit floating point precision (E4M3) on NVIDIA Hopper GPUs, quadrupling intra-bucket throughput.
  4. Hierarchical 2-Level Multi-Resolution LSH: Implement macro-hashing (\(B_{s, \text{macro}} = 16\)) followed by micro-hashing (\(B_{s, \text{micro}} = 64\)) for logarithmic candidate bucket pruning on million-token contexts.

docs.title: Positive Kernel Linear Attention: Bounded Non-Negative Feature Mapping
docs.text: Family: Kernelized & Feature-Map Linear Attentions · NeuralOps Registry ID: positive_kernel_linear_attention

docs.title: Executive Abstract
docs.text:
Positive Kernel Linear Attention enforces strict non-negativity across the attention kernel using \(\phi(x) = \text{ELU}(x) + 1\) or \(\text{softplus}(x)\). This guarantees that the denominator normalizer is strictly positive and non-vanishing, eliminating numerical instability and catastrophic cancellation during long-context autoregressive scans.

In NeuralOps, positive_kernel_linear_attention is integrated into the universal attention dispatch table, featuring full support for the 3-level fallback hierarchy, automatic shape validation, and end-to-end autograd backwards passes.

docs.title: Mathematical Formulation
docs.text:
The core operator computation is defined as:

\[ \phi(x) = \text{ELU}(x) + 1, \quad O_i = \frac{\phi(Q_i) \sum_{j \le i} \phi(K_j)^T V_j}{\phi(Q_i) \sum_{j \le i} \phi(K_j)^T \mathbf{1}} \]

During execution, inputs \(Q, K, V\) are projected to dimension \(d\). In the causal configuration, lower-triangular masking ensures that tokens only attend to past and current time-steps, preserving autoregressive invariants.

docs.title: Primal Attention: Asymmetric Kernel SVD via Segment-Pooled Landmark Decomposition
1. Executive Abstract & Architectural Motivation
docs.text:
Standard Multi-Head Attention requires materializing the full pairwise attention score matrix \(A \in \mathbb{R}^{L \times L}\), incurring an \(\mathcal{O}(L^2)\) memory wall. Primal Attention formulates self-attention through asymmetric kernel SVD approximation in the primal representation space.

By extracting \(r \ll L\) landmark queries \(\widetilde{Q}\) and keys \(\widetilde{K}\) via uniform segment average pooling across the sequence length, Primal Attention factorizes the unmaterialized attention matrix into three core sub-matrices: \(F_1 \in \mathbb{R}^{L \times r}\), \(F_2 \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times r}\), and \(F_3 \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times L}\). Computing the Moore-Penrose pseudo-inverse \(F_2^+\) using iterative Newton-Schulz matrix updates guarantees stable low-rank kernel inversion. This enables associative right-to-left context aggregation in \(\mathcal{O}(L \cdot r \cdot d + r^3)\) time, establishing linear sequence scaling.

docs.title: 2. Mathematical Formulations & Derivations
docs.text:
Given input sequence representations \(X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D}\), query, key, and value states are projected as:

\[ Q = X W_Q \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D}, \quad K = X W_K \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D}, \quad V = X W_V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D} \]

Partitioning into \(H\) heads with dimension \(d = D / H\) yields \(Q, K, V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times L \times d}\).

docs.title: Uniform Segment-Pooling Landmark Selection:
docs.text:
Landmark queries \(\widetilde{Q} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times r \times d}\) and keys \(\widetilde{K} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times r \times d}\) are computed by pooling sequence length \(L\) into \(r\) uniform segments:

\[ \widetilde{Q} = \text{AdaptiveAvgPool1D}(Q, r), \quad \widetilde{K} = \text{AdaptiveAvgPool1D}(K, r) \]

docs.title: Asymmetric Kernel Sub-Matrices:
docs.text:
To construct the low-rank kernelized approximation of the attention operator, the architecture factorizes the unmaterialized attention matrix into three cross-affinity sub-matrices. First, full sequence queries are projected against the landmark keys to yield the query-landmark affinity kernel \(F_1\):

\[ F_1 = \frac{Q \widetilde{K}^\top}{\sqrt{d}} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times L \times r} \]

Concurrently, the interaction among the pooled query and key landmarks defines the core landmark kernel matrix \(F_2 \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times r \times r}\), capturing the intrinsic geometric skeleton of the sequence:

\[ F_2 = \frac{\widetilde{Q} \widetilde{K}^\top}{\sqrt{d}} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times r \times r} \]

Finally, the projection of landmark queries onto the full key representations produces the landmark-to-sequence kernel \(F_3\), augmented with the structural masking matrix \(M_{\text{mask}}\):

\[ F_3 = \frac{\widetilde{Q} K^\top}{\sqrt{d}} + M_{\text{mask}} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times r \times L} \]

docs.title: Iterative Newton-Schulz Pseudoinverse (\(F_2^+\)):
docs.text:
The pseudoinverse \(F_2^+ \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times r \times r}\) is computed via \(T\) iterative Schulz updates initialized with \(\alpha = 1 / (\|F_2\|_1 \|F_2\|_\infty)\):

[ V_0 = \alpha F_2^\top ] [ V_{k+1} = V_k (2 I_r - F_2 V_k), \quad k = 0, \dots, T-1 \implies F_2^+ = V_T ]

docs.title: Associative Primal Context Aggregation:
docs.text:
Context output \(O \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times L \times d}\) is evaluated via associative right-to-left matrix products:

[ P_1 = F_3 V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times r \times d} ] [ P_2 = F_2^+ P_1 = F_2^+ (F_3 V) \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times r \times d} ] [ O = F_1 P_2 = F_1 \left( F_2^+ \left( F_3 V \right) \right) \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times L \times d} ]

Final projection yields \(Y = \text{Concat}(O_1, \dots, O_H) W_O \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D}\).

docs.title: 3. Step-by-Step Tensor Execution Trace
docs.text:
Input: hidden_states [B, L, D]
  │
  ├──> Q, K, V Projections ──> [B, H, L, d]
  │
  ├──> Segment Landmark Selection:
  │      ├──> Q_landmarks = AdaptiveAvgPool1D(Q, r) ──> [B, H, r, d]
  │      └──> K_landmarks = AdaptiveAvgPool1D(K, r) ──> [B, H, r, d]
  │
  ├──> Kernel Matrices:
  │      ├──> F1 = Q @ K_landmarks.T / sqrt(d) ──────> [B, H, L, r]
  │      ├──> F2 = Q_landmarks @ K_landmarks.T / sqrt(d) ─> [B, H, r, r]
  │      └──> F3 = Q_landmarks @ K.T / sqrt(d) + M ──> [B, H, r, L]
  │
  ├──> F2_pinv = NewtonSchulz(F2, iters=6) ─────────────> [B, H, r, r]
  │
  ├──> Associative MatMul 1: P1 = F3 @ V ───────────────> [B, H, r, d]
  ├──> Associative MatMul 2: P2 = F2_pinv @ P1 ─────────> [B, H, r, d]
  ├──> Associative MatMul 3: Context = F1 @ P2 ─────────> [B, H, L, d]
  │
  └──> transpose(1, 2) ──> contiguous() ──> [B, L, D]
  └──> Linear(D, D)(Context) ──> Output: [B, L, D]

docs.title: Computational Workload and Asymptotic Complexity
docs.text:
The computational profile of Primal Attention reflects a structural transition from standard quadratic pairwise attention to linear sequence complexity. For an input tensor parameterized by batch size \(B\), sequence length \(L\), model dimension \(D\), head count \(H\), and landmark rank \(r\) (with per-head dimension \(d = D/H\)):

The initial linear projections of input activations into query, key, and value manifolds require \(6 B L D^2\) FLOPs. In contrast, the subsequent 1D adaptive segment pooling incurs an asymptotic overhead of \(\mathcal{O}(B H L d)\) operations, which is computationally negligible relative to dense GEMM kernels. Evaluating the asymmetric kernel sub-matrices demands \(2 B H L r d = 2 B L r D\) FLOPs for the query-landmark affinity \(F_1\), \(2 B H r^2 d\) FLOPs for the landmark-landmark kernel \(F_2\), and an additional \(2 B L r D\) FLOPs for the landmark-to-sequence kernel \(F_3\). The iterative Newton-Schulz matrix inversion across \(T=6\) iterations accounts for \(24 B H r^3\) FLOPs. Finally, the associative right-to-left context aggregation sequence \(F_1(F_2^+(F_3 V))\) expends \(2 B L r D + 2 B H r^2 d + 2 B L r D\) operations, complemented by \(2 B L D^2\) FLOPs for the final output projection \(W_O\).

Aggregating these individual operational components yields the total computational budget: [ \text{Total FLOPs} = 8 B L D^2 + 6 B L r D + 24 B H r^3 + 4 B H r^2 d ] which maps to \(4 B L D^2 + 3 B L r D + 12 B H r^3 + 2 B H r^2 d\) Multiply-Accumulate (MAC) operations. When \(r \ll L\), the asymptotic execution scales strictly as \(\mathcal{O}(L \cdot D \cdot r + r^3)\), entirely bypassing the canonical \(\mathcal{O}(L^2 D)\) memory and compute bottleneck.

docs.title: Memory Footprint & Scaling Behavior
docs.text: The model architecture maintains a static parameter allocation of \(4 D^2\) weights for the projection operators. Peak transient activation memory is rigorously bounded by \(\mathcal{O}(B \cdot H \cdot L \cdot r + B \cdot H \cdot r^2)\), completely avoiding the quadratic \(\mathcal{O}(B \cdot H \cdot L^2)\) memory wall. This sub-quadratic memory footprint enables extended context window scaling on accelerator architectures with constrained High-Bandwidth Memory (HBM).

docs.title: 5. Failure Modes, Rank Collapse & Edge Cases
Ill-Conditioned Landmark Inversion and Spectral Instability
docs.text: A primary vulnerability in the Primal Attention formulation arises from the numerical conditioning of the landmark kernel matrix \(F_2 = \frac{\widetilde{Q} \widetilde{K}^\top}{\sqrt{d}}\). When token representations within adjacent segments exhibit high mutual coherence or collapse into a lower-dimensional manifold, the resulting landmark queries and keys become near-colinear. This induces severe spectral degradation, driving the condition number \(\text{cond}(F_2) \gg 10^4\). Under such ill-conditioned regimes, the iterative Newton-Schulz polynomial fails to converge within a fixed iteration budget \(T\), leading to catastrophic numerical divergence in \(F_2^+\) and gradient explosion during backpropagation. To guarantee stable convergence, the initial spectral scaling factor \(\alpha_0 = 1 / (\|F_2\|_1 \|F_2\|_\infty)\) must remain strictly bounded, or regularized via adaptive diagonal damping.

docs.title: Segment Pooling Resolution Loss and Retrieval Degradation
docs.text: The reliance on uniform 1D segment average pooling introduces an intrinsic structural tradeoff between computational compression and local representational fidelity. By averaging token activations across temporal spans of length \(L/r\), high-frequency attention spikes corresponding to exact keyword matching or sparse syntactic dependencies are effectively low-pass filtered. This over-blurring phenomenon flattens the sharp peaks of the underlying attention distribution, impairing model performance on needle-in-a-haystack associative recall and fine-grained token retrieval tasks where specific positional indexing is imperative.

docs.title: Causal Masking Asymmetries and Rank Distortion
docs.text: Enforcing autoregressive causality introduces an algebraic asymmetry into the factorized operator. Whereas standard multi-head attention applies a strict lower-triangular mask directly to the full \(L \times L\) affinity matrix, Primal Attention must impose causal constraints indirectly onto the rectangular landmark affinity \(F_3 \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times r \times L}\). Because landmark representations pool future tokens within their segment windows, standard causal masking must either mask full blocks or discard unaligned segment boundaries. This structural constraint induces rank distortion in the reconstructed attention map, requiring explicit causal compensation mechanisms to avoid subtle information leakage across segment boundaries.

docs.title: 6. Hardware Acceleration Blueprint & Triton Kernel Design
docs.text:
A Triton implementation fuses landmark segment reduction and kernel matrix multiplication directly into SRAM.

# Triton Fused Primal Landmark Kernel Blueprint
import triton
import triton.language as tl

@triton.jit
def _primal_fused_kernel(
    Q_ptr, K_landmarks_ptr, Out_ptr,
    stride_qb, stride_qh, stride_ql, stride_qd,
    L, r, d,
    BLOCK_M: tl.constexpr, BLOCK_R: tl.constexpr
):
    pid_m = tl.program_id(0)
    pid_bh = tl.program_id(1)

    offs_m = pid_m * BLOCK_M + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_M)
    offs_d = tl.arange(0, d)
    offs_r = tl.arange(0, BLOCK_R)

    q = tl.load(Q_ptr + pid_bh * stride_qh + offs_m[:, None] * stride_ql + offs_d[None, :])

    f1_tile = tl.zeros((BLOCK_M, BLOCK_R), dtype=tl.float32)
    for r_idx in range(0, r, BLOCK_R):
        k_land = tl.load(K_landmarks_ptr + pid_bh * r * d + (r_idx + offs_r)[None, :] * d + offs_d[:, None])
        f1_tile += tl.dot(q, k_land) / tl.sqrt(d.to(tl.float32))

    tl.store(Out_ptr + pid_bh * L * r + offs_m[:, None] * r + offs_r[None, :], f1_tile)

docs.title: Adaptive Density-Aware Landmark Centroid Clustering
docs.text: While static segment pooling offers deterministic computational schedules, future iterations of Primal Attention can integrate content-adaptive landmark selection mechanisms. By replacing uniform 1D pooling with differentiable k-means clustering or token-importance routing, the landmark budget \(r\) can be dynamically concentrated in high-entropy sequence regions. This structural enhancement preserves sharp attention heads and critical associative tokens while aggressively compressing repetitive background context, thereby resolving the resolution degradation inherent in fixed pooling.

docs.title: Tikhonov-Regularized Spectral Inversion in Reduced Precision
docs.text: To fortify numerical stability under half-precision (FP16) and eight-bit (FP8) quantization regimes, iterative Newton-Schulz updates can incorporate dynamic Tikhonov regularization. Injecting a learnable or condition-dependent damping term \((F_2 + \lambda I_r)\) ensures that the singular spectrum of \(F_2\) remains strictly bounded away from zero. This guarantees quadratic convergence of the matrix polynomial even in the presence of degenerate token subspaces, smoothing the optimization loss landscape and preventing backpropagation gradient anomalies.

docs.title: Primal-State Hybridization with Continuous Recurrence
docs.text: A promising architectural synergy lies in the hybridization of Primal Attention with continuous state-space models, such as Mamba or Gated Delta Networks. By interleaving linear Primal Attention layers for global landmark-guided associative retrieval with selective recurrent scan blocks for dense, high-frequency local recurrence, hybrid architectures can achieve near-optimal efficiency-accuracy Pareto frontiers across multi-million token context lengths.

docs.title: 8. Empirical Benchmark Results & Comparative Profiling

docs.title: Progressive Token Pruning: Learnable Saliency Scoring and Monotonic Sequence Compaction
1. Abstract & Theoretical Motivation
docs.text:
Dense Multi-Head Self-Attention (MHSA) in Transformer architectures scales quadratically \(\mathcal{O}(L^2 d)\) with sequence length \(L\). In deep models, sequence representations contain substantial spatial redundancy, as background tokens, stop-words, and repetitive punctuation contribute minimal utility to final task predictions. Processing these non-essential tokens across all layers consumes massive memory bandwidth and FLOPs.

Progressive Token Pruning (ProgressiveTokenPruning) provides an adaptive, data-driven sequence compaction module that dynamically prunes uninformative token vectors along sequence length \(L\). The layer applies a lightweight, learnable scoring projection \(W_s \in \mathbb{R}^{D \times 1}\) to map token embeddings to continuous saliency scores \(s \in (0, 1)\). Given a retention ratio \(\rho \in (0, 1]\), the top-\(k\) (\(k = \lfloor \rho \cdot L \rfloor\)) most salient tokens are extracted. Crucially, the extracted token indices are sorted monotonically prior to gathering, preserving original relative sequence ordering and relative positional embedding alignment.

By reducing sequence length from \(L\) to \(k \le L\) with minimal parameter overhead (\(\mathcal{O}(D)\) parameters), Progressive Token Pruning compounds exponential compute and memory savings down Transformer hierarchies.

docs.title: 2.1 Learnable Token Saliency Scoring
docs.text:
Given hidden sequence representation \(\mathbf{X} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D}\), a linear scoring layer parameterizes token-level salience weights \(\mathbf{W}_s \in \mathbb{R}^{D \times 1}\) and bias \(b_s \in \mathbb{R}\): $\(\mathbf{z} = \mathbf{X} \mathbf{W}_s + b_s \quad \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times 1}\)$

Sigmoid activation maps logit activations to normalized saliency probabilities \(\mathbf{s} \in (0, 1)^{B \times L}\): $\(\mathbf{s}_{b, i} = \sigma\left( \mathbf{z}_{b, i, 1} \right) = \frac{1}{1 + \exp\left( -\mathbf{z}_{b, i, 1} \right)}, \quad \forall i \in \{1, \dots, L\}\)$

docs.title: 2.2 Top-\(k\) Selection & Monotonic Order Preservation
docs.text:
Given retention ratio \(\rho \in (0, 1]\), the number of tokens retained per sequence is: $\(k = \max\left( 1, \lfloor \rho \cdot L \rfloor \right)\)$

  1. Top-\(k\) Extraction: For each batch sequence \(b \in \{1, \dots, B\}\), the indices \(\mathcal{U}_b\) corresponding to the \(k\) highest saliency scores are extracted: $\(\mathcal{U}_b = \operatorname{TopK}\left( \mathbf{s}_{b, :}, k \right) \quad \in \{1, \dots, L\}^k\)$

  2. Monotonic Index Sorting: Because top-\(k\) selection re-orders index entries by descending score magnitude, direct gathering would corrupt sequential relative positions. Monotonic ascending sorting resolves this: $\(\mathcal{I}_b = \operatorname{Sort}_{\text{ascending}}\left( \mathcal{U}_b \right) \quad \in \{1, \dots, L\}^k\)$ such that \(\mathcal{I}_{b, 1} < \mathcal{I}_{b, 2} < \dots < \mathcal{I}_{b, k}\).

docs.title: 2.3 Index Gathering & Sequence Compaction
docs.text:
The hidden activation tensor \(\mathbf{X}\) is gathered along the sequence axis using the sorted index matrix \(\mathcal{I} \in \mathbb{N}^{B \times k}\): $\(\mathbf{X}_{\text{pruned}, b, j, :} = \mathbf{X}_{b, \mathcal{I}_{b, j}, :} \quad \forall j \in \{1, \dots, k\}\)$ $\(\mathbf{X}_{\text{pruned}} = \operatorname{Gather}\left( \mathbf{X}, \text{dim}=1, \text{index}=\mathcal{I} \right) \quad \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times k \times D}\)$

The module outputs the compacted tensor \(\mathbf{X}_{\text{pruned}} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times k \times D}\) and the monotonically sorted index map \(\mathcal{I} \in \mathbb{N}^{B \times k}\).

docs.title: 4.1 FLOPs Computation Breakdown
docs.text:
Let \(B\) be batch size, \(L\) input sequence length, \(D\) hidden dimension, \(\rho\) retention ratio, and \(k = \lfloor \rho \cdot L \rfloor\).

  1. Saliency Score Projection: $\(\operatorname{FLOPs}_{\text{score}} = 2 B L D\)$

  2. Top-\(k\) Extraction & Sorting: Top-\(k\) heap search: \(B \cdot L \log k\) FLOPs. Furthermore, Bitonic monotonic sort: \(B \cdot k \log k\) FLOPs. $\(\operatorname{FLOPs}_{\text{topk\_sort}} = B L \log k + B k \log k\)$

  3. Tensor Gathering Operation: $\(\operatorname{FLOPs}_{\text{gather}} = B k D \quad (\text{Memory copy operation})\)$

\[\text{Total FLOPs} = 2 B L D + B k D + B L \log k + B k \log k\]

docs.title: 4.2 MACs & Memory Footprint Analysis
docs.text:
Specifically, regarding \textbf{Multiply-Accumulate Operations (MACs)},

$\(\text{Total MACs} \approx B L D\)$ Specifically, regarding \textbf{Peak Activation Memory}, Furthermore, Score Tensor: \(B \cdot L \times 4 \text{ bytes}\) Concurrently, Kept Index Tensor: \(B \cdot k \times 8 \text{ bytes}\) In this setting, Compacted Output Activation Buffer: \(B \cdot k \cdot D \times 2 \text{ bytes}\) (FP16/BF16). Additionally, Memory Footprint drops from \(2 B L D\) to \(2 B k D\) bytes.

docs.title: 4.3 Asymptotic Scalability Comparison
docs.text: Specifically, regarding \textbf{Standard Sequence Layer}, \(\mathcal{O}(L D)\) compute, \(\mathcal{O}(L D)\) memory footprint. Furthermore, regarding \textbf{Progressive Token Pruning}, \(\mathcal{O}(L D + k D)\) compute, \(\mathcal{O}(k D)\) downstream memory footprint. Concurrently, Downstream layer attention FLOPs drop by \(\left(\frac{k}{L}\right)^2 = \rho^2 \times\).

docs.title: 5. Architectural Bottlenecks, Rank Collapse & Failure Modes
5.1 Straight-Through Non-Differentiability & Gradient Disconnect
docs.text: The index extraction \(\mathcal{U} = \operatorname{TopK}(\mathbf{s}, k)\) and sorting operations are discrete step functions. Specifically, regarding \textbf{Zero Gradient Derivative}, \(\frac{\partial \mathcal{I}}{\partial \mathbf{s}} = 0\) everywhere. Furthermore, regarding \textbf{Pruning Scorer Disconnect}, gradients flowing from task loss \(\mathcal{L}\) pass through gathered features \(\mathbf{X}_{\text{pruned}}\), but do not backpropagate through \(\operatorname{TopK}\) to optimize the scoring weights \(\mathbf{W}_s\). Concurrently, Without soft relaxation (e.g., Gumbel-Softmax or straight-through estimator scaling \(\mathbf{X} \cdot \mathbf{s}\)), scoring weights \(\mathbf{W}_s\) remain un-optimized or rely purely on heuristic initialization.

docs.title: 5.2 Dynamic Length Ragged Tensor Stalls in Multi-GPU Training
docs.text: If batch size \(B > 1\) and token pruning evaluates dynamic scores: In variable sequence contexts, sorting indices \(\mathcal{I}_b\) for sample 1 might pick different semantic boundaries than sample 2. Furthermore, If \(k\) varies per sample (\(k_1 \neq k_2\)), rectangular tensor format [B, k, D] collapses, producing ragged arrays that force costly CPU host fallback and re-padding overhead.

docs.title: 5.3 Eviction Cascades & Premature Feature Destruction
docs.text: If \(\rho = 0.5\) across 6 consecutive pruning layers: Layer 1: \(L \to 0.5 L\) Furthermore, Layer 2: \(0.5 L \to 0.25 L\) Concurrently, Layer 6: \(L \to 0.015 L\) (\(1.5\%\) of tokens remaining!). In this setting, regarding \textbf{Severe Context Starvation}, exponential compounding reduces sequence length to a tiny fragment, destroying essential multi-token syntactic structures before deep layers can process them.

docs.title: 6. Hardware Acceleration Blueprint & Triton Optimization Strategies
docs.text: To achieve full hardware acceleration and prevent dynamic memory fragmentation, Progressive Token Pruning requires a custom Triton GPU kernel executing fused scoring, warp bitonic top-\(k\) sorting, and contiguous SRAM token gathering.

docs.title: 6.1 Triton Hardware Acceleration Pipeline Layout
docs.text:
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                        TRITON FUSED PTP PIPELINE                                  |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|  1. FUSED SALIENCY SCORE & BITONIC TOP-K KERNEL                                   |
|     - Loads X [B, L, D] into SRAM.                                                |
|     - Computes s_i = sigmoid(X @ W_s + b_s) in register files.                    |
|     - Executes Bitonic Top-k sort across L elements in warp registers.            |
|     - Sorts top-k indices monotonically ascending: I_sorted = sort(topk_idx).      |
|                                                                                   |
|  2. CONTIGUOUS SRAM GATHER & RE-PACKING KERNEL                                    |
|     - Indirect reads X[b, I_sorted[b, j], :] using hardware pointers.             |
|     - Writes packed, aligned tensor X_pruned [B, k, D] directly to device memory.   |
|     - Eliminates intermediate PyTorch torch.gather memory allocations.            |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+

docs.title: 6.2 Implementation Code Blueprint (Triton Fused Prune & Pack Kernel)
docs.text:
import triton
import triton.language as tl

@triton.jit
def _ptp_fused_score_sort_pack_kernel(
    X_ptr, W_score_ptr, Out_ptr, Indices_ptr,
    stride_xb, stride_xl, stride_xd,
    stride_ob, stride_ok, stride_od,
    stride_ib, stride_ik,
    L_ORIG: tl.constexpr,
    K_KEEP: tl.constexpr,
    D: tl.constexpr
):
    batch_id = tl.program_id(axis=0)
    offs_d = tl.arange(0, D)

    # Base pointers for batch
    x_batch = X_ptr + batch_id * stride_xb
    out_batch = Out_ptr + batch_id * stride_ob
    idx_batch = Indices_ptr + batch_id * stride_ib

    # Load scoring weight vector into SRAM
    w_score = tl.load(W_score_ptr + offs_d)

    # Note: In Triton, we compute saliency scores s_i for i in 0..L_ORIG,
    # perform bitonic top-k sort to extract K_KEEP indices,
    # and sort indices monotonically. Below illustrates the indirect gather step:

    for k_idx in range(K_KEEP):
        # Fetch monotonically sorted token index
        source_idx = tl.load(idx_batch + k_idx * stride_ik)

        # Indirect load token representation [D]
        x_ptrs = x_batch + source_idx * stride_xl + offs_d * stride_xd
        token_vec = tl.load(x_ptrs)

        # Store into contiguous packed output buffer
        out_ptrs = out_base + k_idx * stride_ok + offs_d * stride_od
        tl.store(out_ptrs, token_vec)

docs.title: 6.3 Hardware Acceleration Summary
docs.text:
1. Fused In-Register Sorting: Bitonic sorting in warp registers eliminates global DRAM reads and writes for intermediate score matrices.
  2. SIMD Alignment Preservation: Packing gathered vectors into contiguous FP16 memory blocks [B, k, D] maximizes memory bus utilization for all downstream Transformer layers.

docs.title: Projection Factorized SVD Linear Attention: Production-Hardened Operator
docs.text: Family: Multi-Head Latent & Key-Value Compressed Attentions · NeuralOps Registry ID: projection_factorized_attn

docs.title: Executive Abstract
docs.text:
Production-hardened factorized linear attention operator. Decouples inner rank projections across attention heads, allowing fine-grained rank allocation based on head importance metrics.

In NeuralOps, projection_factorized_attn is integrated into the universal attention dispatch table, featuring full support for the 3-level fallback hierarchy, automatic shape validation, and end-to-end autograd backwards passes.

docs.title: Mathematical Formulation
docs.text:
The core operator computation is defined as:

\[ Q = x W_{Q, 1} W_{Q, 2}, \quad K = x W_{K, 1} W_{K, 2}, \quad V = x W_{V, 1} W_{V, 2} \]

During execution, inputs \(Q, K, V\) are projected to dimension \(d\). In the causal configuration, lower-triangular masking ensures that tokens only attend to past and current time-steps, preserving autoregressive invariants.

docs.title: Quality and Capacity-Aware Grouped Query Attention (QCQA): Dynamic Soft-Routing Mixture over Compressed KV Subspaces
1. Executive Abstract & Architectural Motivation
docs.text:
Quality and Capacity-Aware Grouped Query Attention (QCQA) resolves a fundamental limitation of static Grouped-Query Attention (GQA): rigid, deterministic assignment of query heads to key-value heads. In GQA, a fixed group of query heads shares a static key-value head pair, regardless of input token content or contextual semantics. This rigid partition can restrict expressive capacity when queries require information outside their pre-assigned KV head group.

QCQA replaces static assignment with continuous, token-level soft routing. For every token position and query head \(h \in \{1, \dots, H_q\}\), a routing layer computes a dynamic Softmax probability distribution over all compressed key-value heads \(j \in \{1, \dots, H_{kv}\}\). Key and Value representations are synthesized dynamically per query head via differentiable linear combinations (torch.bmm). This gives each query head dynamic access to the entire compressed KV memory pool while retaining the KV cache compression benefits of GQA during inference.

docs.title: 2. Mathematical Formulations & Derivations
docs.text: Let \(X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times D}\) denote input activations. Let \(H_q\) be the number of query heads, \(H_{kv}\) the compressed key-value heads (\(H_{kv} \le H_q\)), \(d_k = D / H_q\), and \(\tau > 0\) the router temperature scaling factor.

docs.title: Subspace Projections:
docs.text:
Query, key, and value linear transformations map hidden activations into head subspaces:

[ Q = X W_Q \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times (H_q \cdot d_k)}, \quad W_Q \in \mathbb{R}^{D \times (H_q \cdot d_k)} ] [ K = X W_K \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times (H_{kv} \cdot d_k)}, \quad W_K \in \mathbb{R}^{D \times (H_{kv} \cdot d_k)} ] [ V = X W_V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times (H_{kv} \cdot d_k)}, \quad W_V \in \mathbb{R}^{D \times (H_{kv} \cdot d_k)} ]

Reshaping yields \(Q \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times H_q \times d_k}\) and \(K, V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times H_{kv} \times d_k}\).

docs.title: Dynamic Soft Routing Distribution:
docs.text:
A routing linear projection \(W_{\text{router}} \in \mathbb{R}^{d_k \times H_{kv}}\) processes query states \(Q\) to compute router logits, scaled by temperature \(\tau\):

\[ R_{b, n, h, j} = \frac{1}{\tau} \sum_{m=1}^{d_k} Q_{b, n, h, m} \cdot (W_{\text{router}})_{m, j}, \quad \forall j \in \{1, \dots, H_{kv}\} \]

Routing probabilities \(\pi \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times H_q \times H_{kv}}\) are derived via Softmax normalization across \(H_{kv}\):

\[ \pi_{b, n, h, j} = \frac{\exp(R_{b, n, h, j})}{\sum_{j'=1}^{H_{kv}} \exp(R_{b, n, h, j'})} \]

docs.title: Head Mixture Synthesis via Batched Matrix Multiplication:
docs.text:
For each batch token index \((b, n)\), dynamic head representations \(\widetilde{K}_h, \widetilde{V}_h \in \mathbb{R}^{d_k}\) are synthesized as convex combinations of the \(H_{kv}\) compressed heads using torch.bmm:

[ \widetilde{K}{b, n, h, m} = \sum{j=1}^{H_{kv}} \pi_{b, n, h, j} \cdot K_{b, n, j, m} ] [ \widetilde{V}{b, n, h, m} = \sum{j=1}^{H_{kv}} \pi_{b, n, h, j} \cdot V_{b, n, j, m} ]

Yielding synthesized multi-head tensors \(\widetilde{K}, \widetilde{V} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H_q \times N \times d_k}\) after transposing sequence and head dimensions.

docs.title: Scaled Attention & Output Projection:
docs.text:
Query heads execute scaled dot-product attention against their synthesized Key-Value representations:

[ S_{b, h, i, j} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{d_k}} \sum_{m=1}^{d_k} Q_{b, h, i, m} \cdot \widetilde{K}{b, h, j, m} ] [ A{b, h, i, j} = \text{Softmax}j (S{b, h, i, j} + M_{b, 1, i, j}) ] [ O_{b, h, i, m} = \sum_{j=1}^N \text{Dropout}(A){b, h, i, j} \cdot \widetilde{V}{b, h, j, m} ] [ Y = \text{Concat}(O_1, \dots, O_{H_q}) W_O \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times D} ]

docs.text: Execution Stage Input Tensor Shape Transformation / Operation Output Tensor Shape Input [B, N, D] Input activation batch [B, N, D] Projections [B, N, D] self.q_proj, self.k_proj, self.v_proj Q: [B, N, H_q, d_k], K, V: [B, N, H_kv, d_k] Router Logits Q: [B, N, H_q, d_k] self.router(Q) / router_temp [B, N, H_q, H_kv] Softmax Routing route_logits F.softmax(dim=-1) route_weights: [B, N, H_q, H_kv] Flattens for BMM route_weights, K, V .reshape(B*N, H_q, H_kv) & .reshape(B*N, H_kv, d_k) W_flat: [B*N, H_q, H_kv], K_flat, V_flat: [B*N, H_kv, d_k] Synthesize KV Mixture W_flat, K_flat, V_flat torch.bmm(W_flat, K_flat), torch.bmm(W_flat, V_flat) K_mixed, V_mixed: [B, N, H_q, d_k] Multi-Head Transpose Q, K_mixed, V_mixed .transpose(1, 2) [B, H_q, N, d_k] each Score Matrix MatMul Q, K_mixed torch.matmul(q, k_mixed.transpose(-2, -1)) / sqrt(d_k) [B, H_q, N, N] Softmax & Value Agg scores, V_mixed apply_mask + softmax + matmul(attn, v_mixed) [B, H_q, N, d_k] Out Projection context .transpose(1, 2).view(B, N, D) + self.out_proj [B, N, D]

docs.title: Computational Workload (FLOPs & MACs)
docs.text:
Let \(B\) be batch size, \(N\) sequence length, \(D\) model dimension, \(H_q\) query heads, \(H_{kv}\) compressed KV heads, and ratio \(R = H_q / H_{kv}\).

  1. Linear Projections: \(W_Q, W_O\): \(4 B N D^2\) FLOPs. Furthermore, \(W_K, W_V\): \(\frac{4}{R} B N D^2\) FLOPs. Concurrently, Router Projection \(W_{\text{router}}\): \(2 B N H_q d_k H_{kv} = 2 B N D H_{kv}\) FLOPs.

  2. Head Mixture Synthesis (torch.bmm): \(W_{\text{flat}} K_{\text{flat}}\): \(2 (B N) H_q H_{kv} d_k = 2 B N D H_{kv}\) FLOPs. Furthermore, \(W_{\text{flat}} V_{\text{flat}}\): \(2 B N D H_{kv}\) FLOPs. Concurrently, Total Routing & Mixture Cost: \(6 B N D H_{kv}\) FLOPs (\(3 B N D H_{kv}\) MACs).

  3. Core Scaled Dot-Product Attention: \(Q \widetilde{K}^\top\) & \(A \widetilde{V}\): \(4 B N^2 D\) FLOPs. Furthermore, Softmax & Masking: \(7 B H_q N^2\) FLOPs.

  4. Total Complexity Summary: Specifically, regarding \textbf{Total MACs}, \(2 \left(1 + \frac{1}{R}\right) B N D^2 + 3 B N D H_{kv} + 2 B N^2 D\) Furthermore, regarding \textbf{Total FLOPs}, \(4 \left(1 + \frac{1}{R}\right) B N D^2 + 6 B N D H_{kv} + 4 B N^2 D + 7 B H_q N^2\)

docs.title: Memory Footprint & KV Cache Analysis
docs.text:
Specifically, regarding \textbf{Parameter Count}, \(D^2 \left(2 + \frac{2}{R}\right) + d_k H_{kv} + D + H_q d_k\) floats. Furthermore, regarding \textbf{Autoregressive Decoding KV Cache Size}, only compressed \(H_{kv}\) heads are cached:

[ \text{KV Cache Size}{\text{QCQA}} = 2 \cdot B \cdot H{kv} \cdot N \cdot d_k \cdot b = \frac{2 B N D \cdot b}{R} \text{ bytes} ]

docs.title: 5. Architectural Bottlenecks, Rank Collapse & Edge Cases
Softmax Routing Entropy Collapse
docs.text: When router temperature \(\tau \to 0\), the routing Softmax converges to a single-hot argmax selection (\(\pi_{b,n,h,j} \to \delta_{j, j^*}\)). This degenerates QCQA back into hard static GQA assignment, losing dynamic mixture capacity. Conversely, if \(\tau \to \infty\), routing probabilities become uniform (\(\pi \to 1/H_{kv}\)), averaging all KV heads into a single uninformative mean state.

docs.title: Materialization of Intermediate Mixture Tensors
docs.text: In PyTorch, materializing \(\widetilde{K}\) and \(\widetilde{V}\) of shape \([B, N, H_q, d_k]\) prior to attention matrix multiplication expands memory allocation from \(H_{kv}\) to \(H_q\), temporarily negating activation memory footprint savings during forward propagation unless fused into custom CUDA/Triton kernels.

docs.title: 6. Hardware Acceleration Blueprint & Triton Kernel Design
docs.text:
A Triton kernel for QCQA fuses the routing linear transformation, routing Softmax, KV mixture matrix multiplication, and online attention Softmax in SRAM.

                    Global Memory (HBM)
   ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
   │ Q: [B, N, H_q, d_k], K, V: [B, N, H_kv, d_k]                │
   │ W_router: [d_k, H_kv]                                       │
   └──────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────┘
                                  │ Load Tiles into SRAM Scratchpad
                                  ▼
 ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 │                     Triton SRAM Scratchpad                     │
 │ 1. Load Q_tile [BLOCK_M, d_k] for query head q_h               │
 │ 2. Compute Router Logits: r_j = Q_tile @ W_router / tau        │
 │ 3. Compute Softmax Routing Probabilities pi_j over H_kv        │
 │ 4. Load K_j, V_j [BLOCK_N, d_k] for all j in 1..H_kv           │
 │ 5. Compute Fused Mixed K_tile = sum_j (pi_j * K_j)             │
 │ 6. Compute Fused Mixed V_tile = sum_j (pi_j * V_j)             │
 │ 7. Compute Online Scaled Attention: S_ij = Q_tile @ K_tile.T   │
 └────────────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────┘
                                  │ Stream Context Output
                                  ▼
   ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
   │ Context Output: O [B, N, H_q, d_k]                          │
   └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

docs.title: 7. Next-Generation Innovations & Synthesis Opportunities
docs.text:
1. Top-\(k\) Sparse Routing: Instead of dense Softmax over all \(H_{kv}\) heads, route each query head to only the top-\(k\) (\(k \ll H_{kv}\)) relevant KV heads to reduce mixture compute.
  2. Spectral Subspace Router Regularization: Enforce orthogonality constraints on \(W_{\text{router}}\) to guarantee maximum diversity among synthesized KV mixtures.
  3. MoE-QCQA Hybrids: Integrate Mixture-of-Experts routing for attention key-values alongside MoE feed-forward layers for unified sparse expert scaling.

docs.title: Rank-Augmented Linear Attention (RALA): Low-Rank Parametric Head Interaction Augmentation
1. Executive Abstract & Architectural Motivation
docs.text:
Rank-Augmented Linear Attention (RALA, ICLR 2024) addresses the expressivity bottlenecks of standard kernel-based linear attention mechanisms. While standard linear attention reduces the quadratic sequence complexity (\(\mathcal{O}(N^2)\)) of Multi-Head Attention to linear complexity (\(\mathcal{O}(N)\)) via positive kernel feature maps (\(\phi(x) = \text{ELU}(x) + 1.0\)), low-rank associative memory approximations suffer from capacity saturation when modeling complex multi-head token interactions.

RALA overcomes this limitation by augmenting kernel-based linear attention with a low-rank parametric state memory matrix \(M_{\text{rank}} = U V^\top \in \mathbb{R}^{H \times d_k \times d_k}\) (rank \(r \ll d_k\), default \(r = 8\)). The rank-augmented projection path (\(O_{\text{aug}}\)) operates in parallel with the kernel linear path (\(O_{\text{lin}}\)) and is scaled by learnable mixing parameter \(\alpha\). This provides additional parametric rank capacity to capture token interactions while strictly maintaining linear computational complexity (\(\mathcal{O}(N)\)) in sequence length.

docs.title: 2. Mathematical Formulations & Derivations
docs.text: Let \(X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times D}\) denote input activations. Let \(H\) be query heads, \(d_k = D / H\) head dimension, \(r\) augmentation rank (\(r \ll d_k\)), and \(\alpha \in \mathbb{R}\) learnable scalar mixing weight initialized to \(0.1\).

docs.title: Subspace Projections & Positive ELU Feature Mapping:
docs.text:
Input activations are mapped into Query, Key, and Value states:

\[ Q = X W_Q \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times N \times d_k}, \quad K = X W_K \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times N \times d_k}, \quad V = X W_V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times N \times d_k} \]

Non-linear positive feature maps \(\phi(x) = \text{ELU}(x) + 1.0 > 0\) transform Query and Key representations:

\[ \Phi_Q = \text{ELU}(Q) + 1.0 \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times N \times d_k}, \quad \Phi_K = \text{apply\_linear\_mask}(\text{ELU}(K) + 1.0, M) \]

docs.title: Linear Associative Memory Path (\(O_{\text{lin}}\)):
docs.text:
Key-Value associative memory \(S_{\text{KV}} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times d_k \times d_k}\) and un-weighted sum vector \(z \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times d_k}\) are aggregated across sequence length \(N\) using torch.einsum:

[ (S_{\text{KV}}){b, h, d_1, d_2} = \sum{j=1}^N (\Phi_K){b, h, j, d_1} \cdot V{b, h, j, d_2} ] [ z_{b, h, d_1} = \sum_{j=1}^N (\Phi_K)_{b, h, j, d_1} ]

The linear attention context vector \(O_{\text{lin}}\) is evaluated with denominator normalizer:

[ \text{Denom}{b, h, i} = \sum{m=1}^{d_k} (\Phi_Q){b, h, i, m} \cdot z{b, h, m} + \epsilon ] [ (O_{\text{lin}}){b, h, i, e} = \frac{1}{\text{Denom}{b, h, i}} \sum_{m=1}^{d_k} (\Phi_Q){b, h, i, m} \cdot (S{\text{KV}})_{b, h, m, e} ]

docs.title: Low-Rank Parametric Augmentation Path (\(O_{\text{aug}}\)):
docs.text:
Learnable parameter tensors \(U, V \in \mathbb{R}^{H \times d_k \times r}\) synthesize low-rank head interaction matrices \(M_{\text{rank}} \in \mathbb{R}^{H \times d_k \times d_k}\):

\[ (M_{\text{rank}})_{h, d_1, d_2} = \sum_{k=1}^r U_{h, d_1, k} \cdot V_{h, d_2, k} \]

The augmented context representation \(O_{\text{aug}}\) is projected through \(M_{\text{rank}}\):

\[ (O_{\text{aug}})_{b, h, i, e} = \frac{1}{\text{Denom}_{b, h, i}} \sum_{m=1}^{d_k} (\Phi_Q)_{b, h, i, m} \cdot (M_{\text{rank}})_{h, m, e} \]

docs.title: Fused Output Synthesis & Projection:
docs.text:
Linear and augmented paths are combined using learnable scalar \(\alpha\):

[ O_{\text{fused}} = O_{\text{lin}} + \alpha \cdot O_{\text{aug}} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times N \times d_k} ] [ Y = \text{Concat}(O_{\text{fused}, 1}, \dots, O_{\text{fused}, H}) W_O + b_O \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times D} ]

docs.title: Tensor Shape Transformation Table
docs.text: Execution Stage Input Shape Transformation / Operation Output Shape Input [B, N, D] Input activation batch [B, N, D] Projections [B, N, D] self.q_proj, self.k_proj, self.v_proj [B, N, D] each Multi-Head View [B, N, D] .view(B, N, H, d_k).transpose(1, 2) [B, H, N, d_k] each Feature Mapping Q, K F.elu(q) + 1.0, apply_linear_mask(F.elu(k) + 1.0) q_prime, k_prime: [B, H, N, d_k] Associative Memory Einsum k_prime, V torch.einsum("bhnd,bhne->bhde", k_prime, V) kv: [B, H, d_k, d_k] Normalizer Sum k_prime k_prime.sum(dim=2) z: [B, H, d_k] Denominator Vector q_prime, z torch.einsum("bhnd,bhd->bhn", q_prime, z) denom: [B, H, N, 1] Linear Path Output q_prime, kv, denom torch.einsum("bhnd,bhde->bhne", q_prime, kv) / denom lin_out: [B, H, N, d_k] Low-Rank Matrix Einsum U: [H, d_k, r], V: [H, d_k, r] torch.einsum("hdr,her->hde", U, V) rank_mat: [H, d_k, d_k] Augmented Path Output q_prime, rank_mat torch.einsum("bhnd,hde->bhne", q_prime, rank_mat) / denom aug_out: [B, H, N, d_k] Fused Output lin_out, aug_out lin_out + alpha * aug_out [B, H, N, d_k] Out Projection output .transpose(1, 2).view(B, N, D) + out_proj Output: [B, N, D]

docs.text:

          ┌─────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────┐
          ▼                             ▼                             ▼

docs.title: Computational Workload & Scaling Dynamics
docs.text:
Let \(B\) represent the batch size, \(N\) sequence length, \(D\) model dimension, \(H\) the number of attention heads, \(d_k = D/H\) the head dimension, and \(r\) the rank of the parametric augmentation subspace where \(r \ll d_k\).

The arithmetic operational profile of Rank-Augmented Linear Attention demonstrates strict \(\mathcal{O}(N)\) computational scalability across all sequence lengths. The initial input projection stage spanning transformations \(W_Q, W_K, W_V,\) and \(W_O\) requires \(8 B N D^2\) floating-point operations (\(4 B N D^2\) multiply-accumulate operations). Subsequently, associative state construction proceeds by contracting positive feature mappings into the Key-Value memory tensor \(S_{\text{KV}}\), which consumes \(2 B H N d_k^2 = 2 B N D d_k\) FLOPs alongside \(2 B N D\) FLOPs dedicated to computing the normalization denominator sum.

Evaluation of the dual-path context representation executes with minimal asymptotic overhead. The primary kernel linear attention path \(O_{\text{lin}}\) requires \(2 B H N d_k^2 = 2 B N D d_k\) FLOPs to query the aggregated associative memory. In parallel, the parametric low-rank interaction matrix \(M_{\text{rank}} = U V^\top\) is pre-computed once per head requiring \(2 H d_k^2 r\) FLOPs, after which the query projections compute \(O_{\text{aug}}\) in \(2 B H N d_k^2 = 2 B N D d_k\) FLOPs. Aggregating these operations yields a cumulative workload of \(4 B N D^2 + 3 B N D d_k + H d_k^2 r\) MACs (or \(8 B N D^2 + 6 B N D d_k + 2 H d_k^2 r + 2 B N D\) FLOPs). Crucially, because no intermediate \(N \times N\) token affinity matrices are materialized in memory, memory consumption and arithmetic complexity remain strictly linear with respect to sequence length.

docs.title: Parameter Footprint and Subspace Capacity
docs.text: Compared to standard linear attention frameworks that parameterize \(4 D^2 + 4 D\) weights for basic input-output projections, RALA incorporates low-rank factorization matrices \(U, V \in \mathbb{R}^{H \times d_k \times r}\) and the learnable blending scalar \(\alpha\): [ \text{Params}_{\text{RALA}} = 4 D^2 + 4 D + 2 \cdot H \cdot d_k \cdot r + 1 = 4 D^2 + 4 D + 2 D r + 1 \text{ parameters} ] Under representative large-scale model dimensions (\(D = 4096, H = 32, d_k = 128, r = 8\)), the additional parametric allocation amounts to \(2 \times 4096 \times 8 + 1 = 65,537\) parameters. This represents an overhead of less than \(0.1\%\) relative to the baseline architecture, achieving significant expressivity enhancements across complex associative retrieval tasks without measurable parametric expansion.

docs.title: 5. Architectural Bottlenecks, Rank Collapse & Edge Cases
Normalization Stability and Denominator Vanishing
docs.text: A central stability consideration in kernelized linear attention mechanisms is the vulnerability to denominator collapse. In scenarios where extensive causal or sequence padding masks suppress large contiguous blocks of key tokens, the accumulated normalizer \(\text{Denom}_{b, h, i} = \sum_{m=1}^{d_k} (\Phi_Q)_{b, h, i, m} \cdot z_{b, h, m}\) can vanish towards zero. This denominator degeneracy induces numerical singularity, generating exploding gradients and NaN activations in backpropagation. To guarantee gradient stability across degenerate sequence distributions, an additive damping constant \(\epsilon = 10^{-8}\) is enforced within the normalization denominator, establishing a strictly positive lower bound on the loss landscape denominator manifold.

docs.title: Ill-Conditioning and Optimization Dynamics of Low-Rank Memory
docs.text: A potential optimization impediment arises from the unconstrained magnitude scaling of the parametric low-rank matrices \(U\) and \(V\). If \(U\) and \(V\) are initialized with large variance, the resulting parametric output \(O_{\text{aug}}\) can drastically overpower the associative kernel output \(O_{\text{lin}}\), effectively uncoupling the attention block from the dynamic input sequence context and collapsing it into an invariant static transformation. To preserve well-conditioned gradient flow across both paths, factor matrices \(U\) and \(V\) are initialized with Gaussian perturbations scaled to small standard deviations (\(\sigma = 0.02\)), while the scalar mixing coefficient is initialized conservatively to \(\alpha = 0.1\). This ensures that initial training dynamics remain anchored to the associative memory path while the low-rank subspace progressively learns complementary high-order feature correlations.

docs.title: 6. Hardware Acceleration Blueprint & Triton Kernel Design
docs.text:
A Triton kernel for RALA fuses the associative memory reduction \(S_{\text{KV}}\), low-rank parametric projection \(M_{\text{rank}}\), and query multiplication into SIMD thread blocks.

                    Global Memory (HBM)
   ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
   │ Q, K, V: [B, H, N, d_k]                                     │
   │ Low-Rank Parametric Weights: U [H, d_k, r], V [H, d_k, r]   │
   │ Mixing Coefficient: alpha                                   │
   └──────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────┘
                                  │ Vectorized Block Load
                                  ▼
 ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 │                     Triton SRAM Scratchpad                     │
 │ 1. Load Activation Tiles Q_i, K_j, V_j [BLOCK_M, d_k]          │
 │ 2. Compute ELU Maps: phi(Q_i), phi(K_j)                        │
 │ 3. Accumulate KV State: S_KV += phi(K_j).T @ V_j              │
 │ 4. Compute On-Chip Rank Matrix: M_rank = U @ V.T              │
 │ 5. Evaluate Fused Output: O_i = (phi(Q_i) @ (S_KV + alpha*M)) / z│
 └────────────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────┘
                                  │ Write Context Output
                                  ▼
   ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
   │ Context Output: O [B, N, D]                                 │
   └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

docs.title: 7. Next-Generation Innovations & Synthesis Opportunities
docs.text: The integration of parametric rank augmentation into linear attention architectures unlocks multiple avenues for structural innovation and hardware efficiency. One compelling direction involves unifying RALA with continuous-time State-Space Models (SSMs), establishing Mamba-RALA hybrid layers wherein selective recurrent state transitions track non-stationary temporal dynamics while low-rank parametric matrices maintain cross-channel associative capacity under strict linear-time complexity. Furthermore, memory footprint during high-throughput autoregressive decoding can be minimized by quantizing the static parametric memory tensors \(U\) and \(V\) into low-bit representations (such as INT4 or FP4 formats), thereby mitigating SRAM register pressure during fused kernel execution. Concurrently, parameterizing head-specific adaptive mixing coefficients \(\alpha_h\) enables individual attention heads to autonomously determine their optimal reliance on static parametric rank memory versus dynamic associative state aggregation.

docs.title: RALA Compressor: Rank-Augmented Linear Attention Layer Architecture & Masking Specifications
1. Executive Abstract & Architectural Motivation
docs.text:
Rank-Augmented Linear Attention Compressor (RALALinearAttention in rala_compressor.py) provides an expressive linear-complexity attention mechanism (\(\mathcal{O}(N)\)). Standard linear attention models approximate Softmax attention using kernel feature maps (\(\phi(x) = \text{ELU}(x) + 1.0\)), reducing quadratic sequence scaling (\(\mathcal{O}(N^2)\)) to linear scaling. However, fixed feature maps introduce capacity bottlenecks that degrade long-range retrieval performance.

RALA resolves this capacity limit by augmenting the linear associative memory path (\(O_{\text{lin}}\)) with a low-rank parametric memory matrix (\(M_{\text{rank}} = U V^\top \in \mathbb{R}^{H \times d_k \times d_k}\), rank \(r \ll d_k\)). The augmented memory branch (\(O_{\text{aug}}\)) provides trainable head interaction capacity without breaking linear sequence complexity. The compressor incorporates multi-dimensional mask handling for 2D, 3D, and 4D mask tensors.

docs.title: 2. Mathematical Formulations & Derivations
docs.text: Let \(X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times D}\) denote input activations. Let \(H\) be query heads, \(d_k = D / H\) head dimension, \(r\) augmentation rank, and \(\alpha\) mixing weight.

docs.title: Positive ELU Feature Mapping & Mask Normalization:
docs.text:
Input activations are mapped into multi-head projections \(Q, K, V \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times N \times d_k}\). Positive feature maps transform Query and Key states:

\[ \Phi_Q = \text{ELU}(Q) + 1.0 \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times N \times d_k}, \quad \Phi_K = (\text{ELU}(K) + 1.0) \odot M_{\text{valid}} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times N \times d_k} \]

Where valid token mask \(M_{\text{valid}}\) parses 2D, 3D, or 4D attention masks:

\[ M_{\text{valid}} = \begin{cases} M \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times 1 \times N \times 1} & \text{if } \text{dim} = 2 \\ M \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times 1 \times N \times 1} & \text{if } \text{dim} = 3 \\ (M > -10^4) \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times 1 \times N \times 1} & \text{if } \text{dim} = 4 \end{cases} \]

docs.title: Linear Associative Memory & Normalization:
docs.text:
Key-Value associative state memory \(S_{\text{KV}} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times d_k \times d_k}\) and normalizer vector \(z \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times d_k}\) are constructed via sequence summation:

[ S_{\text{KV}} = \sum_{j=1}^N \Phi_{K, j} V_j^\top = \text{einsum}("b h n d, b h n e \to b h d e", \Phi_K, V) ] [ z = \sum_{j=1}^N \Phi_{K, j} = \text{sum}(\Phi_K, \text{dim}=2) \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times d_k} ]

Linear attention output \(O_{\text{lin}}\) and scalar denominator vector are computed:

[ \text{Denom} = \Phi_Q \cdot z^\top + \epsilon = \text{einsum}("b h n d, b h d \to b h n", \Phi_Q, z) \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times N \times 1} ] [ O_{\text{lin}} = \frac{\Phi_Q S_{\text{KV}}}{\text{Denom}} = \frac{\text{einsum}("b h n d, b h d e \to b h n e", \Phi_Q, S_{\text{KV}})}{\text{Denom}} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times N \times d_k} ]

docs.title: Low-Rank Parametric Memory Augmentation:
docs.text:
Learnable factor matrices \(U, V \in \mathbb{R}^{H \times d_k \times r}\) compute dynamic head memory matrix \(M_{\text{rank}} \in \mathbb{R}^{H \times d_k \times d_k}\):

[ M_{\text{rank}} = U V^\top = \text{einsum}("h d r, h e r \to h d e", U, V) ] [ O_{\text{aug}} = \frac{\Phi_Q M_{\text{rank}}}{\text{Denom}} = \frac{\text{einsum}("b h n d, h d e \to b h n e", \Phi_Q, M_{\text{rank}})}{\text{Denom}} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times N \times d_k} ]

docs.title: Fused Residual Output & Projection:
docs.text:
Linear and augmented paths are combined via learnable scalar \(\alpha\):

[ O_{\text{fused}} = O_{\text{lin}} + \alpha \cdot O_{\text{aug}} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times N \times d_k} ] [ Y = \text{Concat}(O_{\text{fused}, 1}, \dots, O_{\text{fused}, H}) W_O + b_O \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times D} ]

docs.title: Computational Workload (FLOPs & MACs)
docs.text:
A rigorous examination of the computational workload demonstrates how RALA maintains strict linear asymptotic complexity with minimal arithmetic overhead. For a batch size \(B\), sequence length \(N\), hidden model dimension \(D\), head count \(H\), head dimension \(d_k = D/H\), and augmentation rank \(r\), the operational pipeline decomposes into distinct computational stages.

The initial linear projection phase maps input representations across projection matrices \(W_Q, W_K, W_V,\) and \(W_O\), incurring \(8 B N D^2\) FLOPs (corresponding to \(4 B N D^2\) Multiply-Accumulate operations). Subsequently, the construction of the associative memory state via sequence contraction \(S_{\text{KV}} = \sum_{j=1}^N \Phi_{K, j} V_j^\top\) demands \(2 B H N d_k^2 = 2 B N D d_k\) FLOPs, alongside \(2 B N D\) FLOPs allocated to the reduction of the normalizer vector \(z\). The linear retrieval branch evaluates the tensor contraction \(\Phi_Q S_{\text{KV}}\) with an arithmetic complexity of \(2 B N D d_k\) FLOPs. Concurrently, the parametric memory augmentation path constructs the dynamic head matrix \(M_{\text{rank}} = U V^\top\) at a sequence-independent cost of \(2 H d_k^2 r\) FLOPs, followed by the projection \(\Phi_Q M_{\text{rank}}\) requiring \(2 B N D d_k\) FLOPs.

Summing these individual components yields an aggregate arithmetic workload of \(4 B N D^2 + 3 B N D d_k + H d_k^2 r\) MACs, or equivalently \(8 B N D^2 + 6 B N D d_k + 2 H d_k^2 r + 2 B N D\) FLOPs. Crucially, the total computational complexity scales as \(\mathcal{O}(N)\) with respect to sequence length, fundamentally circumventing the quadratic \(\mathcal{O}(N^2)\) memory and compute bottleneck characteristic of standard Softmax attention.

docs.title: Parameter Overhead Profile
docs.text:
The parameter footprint of standard linear attention comprises \(4 D^2 + 4 D\) floating-point parameters across all projection heads. In contrast, the RALA architecture augments this foundation with low-rank factorization matrices and the scalar mixing parameter:

\[ \text{Params}_{\text{RALA}} = 4 D^2 + 4 D + 2 H d_k r + 1 = 4 D^2 + 4 D + 2 D r + 1 \text{ floats} \]

Under a canonical transformer configuration (\(D = 768, H = 12, d_k = 64, r = 8\)), standard linear attention entails \(2,362,368\) parameters. RALA incorporates an additional \(12,289\) parameters to reach \(2,374,657\) floats, introducing an exceptionally modest parameter overhead of approximately \(0.5\%\). This minimal footprint delivers substantial expressive capacity gains without straining parameter budgets or saturating memory bandwidth during weight transfers.

docs.title: 5. Architectural Bottlenecks, Rank Collapse & Optimization Dynamics
docs.text:
The dual-path formulation of RALA introduces critical considerations regarding optimization stability, numerical conditioning, and spectrum degeneracy across varying sequence topologies. A primary operational challenge arises from input tensor formatting and broadcasting inconsistencies. Passing unnormalized boolean or multi-dimensional masks without rigorous dimension alignment triggers structural shape mismatches during the element-wise Hadamard product \(\Phi_K \odot M_{\text{valid}}\). To guarantee invariant execution across heterogeneous architectures, the internal dispatch mechanism evaluates tensor dimensionality across 2D padding masks, 3D broadcast tensors, and additive 4D causal masks, projecting all inputs into a canonical shape \([B, 1, N, 1]\) before feature mapping.

Furthermore, extreme sparsity patterns—such as batches dominated by padding tokens—induce severe numerical vulnerabilities. When an entire sequence segment comprises non-informative padding tokens, the sequence reduction over \(\Phi_K\) collapses toward zero, forcing the denominator scalar \(\Phi_Q z^\top \to 0\). To prevent gradient singularities and catastrophic floating-point underflow (producing NaN or Inf representations during backpropagation), a stabilizing offset \(\epsilon = 10^{-8}\) is strictly enforced within the normalization denominator.

From an optimization perspective, augmenting the linear associative memory with a parametric matrix \(M_{\text{rank}} = U V^\top\) alters the loss landscape geometry. While standard linear attention is susceptible to associative capacity saturation and low-rank state decay in long sequences, unconstrained optimization of \(U\) and \(V\) can induce spectral rank collapse if the singular values of \(M_{\text{rank}}\) concentrate excessively along dominant eigenspaces. This phenomenon can over-index on static head interactions at the expense of dynamic context aggregation. The learnable scalar multiplier \(\alpha\) acts as an adaptive regularizer, dynamically balancing the loss landscape gradients between the sequence-dependent associative memory \(O_{\text{lin}}\) and the static parametric manifold \(O_{\text{aug}}\), thereby preserving stable gradient flow throughout deep layer stacks.

docs.title: 7. Next-Generation Innovations & Synthesis Opportunities
docs.text:
The architectural modularity of RALA enables several compelling avenues for future research and engineering synthesis. First, automated model-wide injection pipelines—instantiated via high-level replacement interfaces such as replace_attention(model, "rala")—allow seamless, zero-shot substitution of dense attention kernels across arbitrary autoregressive large language models, democratizing linear-complexity fine-tuning.

Second, the parametric memory footprint can be further compressed through aggressive low-bit quantization. By casting the static factorization tensors \(U\) and \(V\) into microscopic FP8 or INT4 formats, the runtime kernel drastically reduces SRAM register pressure and memory-bus traffic during speculative decoding and long-context inference phases.

Finally, a promising structural convergence lies in the synthesis of hybrid RALA-Mamba state-space architectures. Interleaving RALA rank-augmented linear layers with selective state-space model (SSM) blocks establishes a complementary dynamic: while SSMs capture continuous temporal decays and selective token filtering, RALA supplies global associative retrieval and cross-head static capacity, providing an expressive and fully linear \(\mathcal{O}(N)\) foundation for next-generation sequence modeling.

docs.title: REAP-MoE: Robust Expert Allocation and Pruning
docs.text: Family: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) & Sparsely-Gated Attentions · NeuralOps Registry ID: reap_moe

docs.title: Executive Abstract
docs.text:
REAP-MoE dynamically profiles expert utility during post-surgery calibration, identifying redundant experts and pruning up to 50% of expert capacity while rerouting token traffic to high-capacity experts.

In NeuralOps, reap_moe is integrated into the universal attention dispatch table, featuring full support for the 3-level fallback hierarchy, automatic shape validation, and end-to-end autograd backwards passes.

docs.title: Mathematical Formulation
docs.text:
The core operator computation is defined as:

\[ \text{Score}(e) = \sum_{t} \alpha_{t, e} \cdot \|\nabla_{\theta_e} \mathcal{L}\|, \quad e \in \text{Pruned if Score}(e) < \tau \]

During execution, inputs \(Q, K, V\) are projected to dimension \(d\). In the causal configuration, lower-triangular masking ensures that tokens only attend to past and current time-steps, preserving autoregressive invariants.
