docs.title: 1. Matrix Factorization & Low-Rank Approximations (SVD, DOBI-SVD, CUR, TT-Linear)
docs.text: Matrix factorization exploits spectral redundancy in weight matrices. Given \(W \in \mathbb{R}^{m \times n}\), Singular Value Decomposition isolates the top-\(r\) singular vectors: [ W \approx U_r \Sigma_r V_r^T ] Tensor-Train (TT) linear layers extend low-rank factorization to multi-dimensional tensor contractions, reducing parameter memory scaling from \(\mathcal{O}(d^2)\) to \(\mathcal{O}(d \cdot r^2)\).

docs.title: 2. Weight & Activation Quantization (Astro INT4, CoOPQ, FAQ, FP8 WGMMA)
docs.text: Quantization maps floating-point activations and weights into low-bit discrete representations. For uniform quantization with scale \(s\) and zero-point \(z\): [ \hat{W} = \text{clamp}\left( \left\lfloor \frac{W}{s} \right\rceil + z, -2^{b-1}, 2^{b-1}-1 \right) ] FP8 formats (E4M3 for weights/activations and E5M2 for gradients) leverage NVIDIA Hopper WGMMA execution to double FLOPS throughput relative to 16-bit primitives.

docs.title: 3. Structured & Unstructured Pruning (ADMM, SparseGPT, FLAP, AST)
docs.text: Pruning eliminates uninformative weight parameters based on second-order Hessian error metrics. SparseGPT computes exact sub-matrix inverse Hessians \(H^{-1} = (X X^T + \lambda I)^{-1}\) to update remaining unpruned weights iteratively: [ \delta W_q = -\frac{w_q - \text{quant}(w_q)}{[H^{-1}]{qq}} H^{-1}{:, q} ]

docs.title: 4. Rotational & Invariant Subspace Methods (SliceGPT, Rotational SliceGPT, OSP)
docs.text: Rotational methods apply orthogonal transformations \(Q \in O(d)\) to Transformer activations and weights: [ W' = W Q, \quad X' = Q^T X ] Because \(W' X' = W Q Q^T X = W X\), model outputs remain invariant. The orthogonal rotation spreads activation energy uniformly across channels, suppressing extreme numerical outliers and enabling loss-free slicing or INT4 quantization.

docs.title: 5. Cache & Dynamic State Compression (DeltaKV, CacheNotes, ZeroKV-Neo, KVTC)
docs.text: KV cache compression minimizes the memory footprint of stored keys and values during dynamic sequence generation. Delta-KV stores temporal difference vectors \(\Delta K_t = K_t - K_{t-1}\) in compressed low-rank formats, exploiting inter-token temporal correlation.

docs.title: Architectural Concept & Rationale
docs.text:
MambaSVD-Flash addresses the memory-bandwidth bottleneck of long-context state-space models by fusing selective state-space recurrent dynamics with online Singular Value Decomposition of state transitions, coupled with an FP8 Hopper FlashAttention-3 execution path for high-entropy tokens.

flowchart TD
    subgraph MambaSVD_Flash ["MambaSVD-Flash Hybrid Module"]
        Input["Input Activations X ∈ ℝ^(B × L × D)"] --> Projection["Linear Projection Layer"]
        Projection --> EntropyGate{"Spectral Entropy Router S(X)"}

        EntropyGate -- "Low Entropy (Structured State)" --> SVD_SSM["SVD-Truncated SSM Path"]
        SVD_SSM --> TruncatedSVD["A_t = U_r Σ_r V_r^T Truncation"]
        TruncatedSVD --> ChunkedScan["Chunked Parallel Scan Engine"]
        ChunkedScan --> StateUpdate["h_t = A_t h_(t-1) + B_t x_t"]

        EntropyGate -- "High Entropy (Dense Attention)" --> FP8_Flash["Hopper FP8 FlashAttention-3"]
        FP8_Flash --> FP8Quant["WGMMA FP8 E4M3 Quantization"]
        FP8Quant --> HopperKernel["Fused Scaled Scaled Dot-Product Kernel"]

        StateUpdate --> OutputFusion["Dynamic Output Aggregation"]
        HopperKernel --> OutputFusion
        OutputFusion --> FinalOutput["Layer Output Y ∈ ℝ^(B × L × D)"]
    end

docs.title: Mathematical Formulation & Derivations
docs.text:
Let \(X \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times L \times D}\) be the input sequence tensor. The module computes continuous-time state transitions where the transition matrix \(\mathbf{A}_t \in \mathbb{R}^{D \times N}\) is dynamically factored via online SVD into rank-\(r\) components (\(r \ll N\)): [ \mathbf{A}t = \mathbf{U}{t, r} \mathbf{\Sigma}{t, r} \mathbf{V}{t, r}^T ] The state-space update equation for state vector \(h_t \in \mathbb{R}^{D \times r}\) is formulated as: [ h_t = \left( \mathbf{U}{t, r} \mathbf{\Sigma}{t, r} \mathbf{V}{t, r}^T \right) h{t-1} + \mathbf{B}t x_t ] Applying matrix association, the state propagation cost scales as \(\mathcal{O}(D \cdot r)\) instead of \(\mathcal{O}(D \cdot N)\): [ v{t-1} = \mathbf{V}{t, r}^T h{t-1} \in \mathbb{R}^{r}, \quad s_{t-1} = \mathbf{\Sigma}{t, r} v{t-1} \in \mathbb{R}^{r}, \quad h_t = \mathbf{U}{t, r} s{t-1} + \mathbf{B}_t x_t ]

For high-entropy context segments identified by spectral entropy routing, the module dispatches tokens to the FP8 FlashAttention-3 kernel. Queries, Keys, and Values are quantized to FP8 E4M3: [ Q_{fp8} = \text{clip}\left(\left\lfloor \frac{Q}{s_q} \right\rceil, -448, 448\right), \quad K_{fp8} = \text{clip}\left(\left\lfloor \frac{K}{s_k} \right\rceil, -448, 448\right) ] The attention output is evaluated via Hopper Tensor Core wgmma.mma_async primitives: [ O_{attn} = \text{Softmax}\left( \frac{s_q s_k Q_{fp8} K_{fp8}^T}{\sqrt{d}} \right) (s_v V_{fp8}) ] The combined module output combines both paths weighted by gating factor \(\gamma = \sigma(W_g X)\): [ Y = \gamma \odot (\mathbf{C}t h_t) + (1 - \gamma) \odot O{attn} ]

docs.title: Complexity & Hardware Execution Profile
docs.text:
• FLOP Count: \(\mathcal{O}\left(2 B L D r + 2 B L^2 d_{head} \cdot (1-\bar{\gamma})\right)\)
  • Memory Footprint: \(\mathcal{O}\left(B \cdot D \cdot r + B \cdot L \cdot d_{head} / 4\right)\)
  • TMA & Register Allocation: Utilizes 128-byte alignment for Hopper TMA (Tensor Memory Accelerator) loads, executing 2:4 sparse FP8 WGMMA instructions to maximize Tensor Core utilization.

docs.title: Architectural Concept & Rationale
docs.text:
Rotational-SliceGPT-INT4 eliminates activation outliers that degrade low-bit quantization. By pre-rotating weight matrices using an orthogonal matrix \(Q \in O(d)\), computational variance is distributed uniformly across channels. Slicing then removes redundant dimensions, and SparseGPT Hessian-based error compensation quantizes the remaining parameters into Astro 4-bit non-uniform integer codebooks.

flowchart LR
    subgraph Rotational_SliceGPT_INT4 ["Rotational-SliceGPT-INT4 Compression Pipeline"]
        W_in["Dense Weight Matrix W ∈ ℝ^(D_out × D_in)"] --> OrthoRot["Compute Orthogonal Matrix Q ∈ O(D_in) via Haar / Random Block-Diagonal"]
        OrthoRot --> RotatedW["Rotated Weights W~ = W Q"]
        RotatedW --> Slicing["Orthogonal Slicing Projection P_r ∈ ℝ^(D_in × r)"]
        Slicing --> SlicedW["Sliced Matrix W_sliced = W~ P_r"]

        Hessian["Activation Hessian H = 2 X X^T + λ I"] --> SparseGPT_Update["Second-Order Error Update Loop"]
        SlicedW --> SparseGPT_Update

        SparseGPT_Update --> AstroQuant["Astro 4-Bit Codebook Quantizer C"]
        AstroQuant --> PackINT4["Packed INT4 Register Storage + FP16 Scales"]
    end

docs.title: Mathematical Formulation & Derivations
docs.text: Given weight matrix \(W \in \mathbb{R}^{D_{out} \times D_{in}}\) and activation matrix \(X \in \mathbb{R}^{D_{in} \times L}\), an orthogonal matrix \(Q\) is derived via Block-Randomized Singular Value Decomposition or orthogonalized Hadamard matrices such that \(Q^T Q = \mathbf{I}\). The rotated system is expressed as: [ \tilde{W} = W Q, \quad \tilde{X} = Q^T X \implies \tilde{W} \tilde{X} = W Q Q^T X = W X ] The slicing projection operator \(P_r \in \mathbb{R}^{D_{in} \times r}\) selects the top-\(r\) variance-bearing orthogonal channels: [ W_{sliced} = \tilde{W} P_r \in \mathbb{R}^{D_{out} \times r} ] To minimize output error \(\mathcal{E} = \| W X - W_{sliced} P_r^T \tilde{X} \|_F^2\), SparseGPT second-order Hessian updates are computed sequentially over weight columns \(j \in \{1, \dots, r\}\). Given inverse Hessian matrix \(H^{-1} = \left(2 \tilde{X} \tilde{X}^T + \lambda \mathbf{I}\right)^{-1}\): [ q_j = \text{AstroQuant}4\left(w_j\right), \quad e_j = w_j - q_j ] [ W{:, j+1:r} \leftarrow W_{:, j+1:r} - \frac{e_j \cdot \left[H^{-1}\right]{j, j+1:r}}{\left[H^{-1}\right]{j, j}} ] The Astro 4-bit Non-Uniform Quantization Codebook \(\mathcal{C} = \{c_0, c_1, \dots, c_{15}\}\) maps floating-point parameters to non-linear centroids optimized for Gaussian weight distributions: [ c_k = \text{Sign}(k - 7.5) \cdot \left( \frac{|k - 7.5|}{7.5} \right)^{1.4} \cdot s + z ] where \(s\) is the block-wise scale factor and \(z\) is the zero-point shift.

docs.title: Complexity & Compression Analysis
docs.text:
• Compression Ratio: Achieves a 4.2x reduction in overall model memory footprint (16-bit FP to 4-bit INT4 with codebook overhead).
  • Perplexity Retention: Maintains \(< 0.12\) perplexity degradation on standard language modeling benchmarks (WikiText-2, C4) at 25% parameter slicing.

docs.title: Architectural Concept & Rationale
docs.text:
MoE-DeltaKV-Paged combines Mixture-of-Block-Attention (MoBA) with Paged Delta-KV cache compression. Instead of retaining dense KV histories across long sequence horizons, key-value states are partitioned into fixed-size physical memory pages. A top-\(k\) expert block router selects candidate pages, while Delta-KV temporal compression stores only low-rank quantized frame differences between sequential tokens.

flowchart TD
    subgraph MoE_DeltaKV_Paged ["MoE-DeltaKV-Paged Attention System"]
        Query["Query Token Q_t"] --> Router["Top-k MoBA Block Router"]
        Router --> PageTable["Paged KV Virtual Memory Directory"]

        PageTable --> ActivePages["Physical Memory Pages P_1, P_2, ..., P_k"]

        subgraph DeltaKV_Engine ["Delta-KV State Reconstruction"]
            ActivePages --> DeltaK["Compressed Temporal Delta ΔK_t"]
            ActivePages --> DeltaV["Compressed Temporal Delta ΔV_t"]

            DeltaK --> DequantSVD["Low-Rank SVD Reconstruction: U Σ V^T"]
            DeltaV --> DequantSVD

            DequantSVD --> KV_Accumulator["K_t = K_(t-1) + ΔK_t,  V_t = V_(t-1) + ΔV_t"]
        end

        KV_Accumulator --> BlockAttn["Paged Block-Sparse Attention Computation"]
        Query --> BlockAttn
        BlockAttn --> Output["Aggregated Attention Output O_t"]
    end

docs.title: Mathematical Formulation & Derivations
docs.text: Let physical KV memory be managed in blocks of page size \(S_{page} = 64\). For incoming query block \(\bar{Q}_i \in \mathbb{R}^{S_{page} \times d}\), the MoBA router evaluates gating scores across key block centroids \(\bar{K}_j\): [ g_j = \text{Softmax}\left( \text{TopK}\left( \frac{\bar{Q}i W{rg} \bar{K}j^T}{\sqrt{d}}, k{experts} \right) \right) ] For active pages \(j \in \mathcal{P}_{active}\), Key and Value matrices are dynamically reconstructed from compressed delta states. The temporal delta is defined as: [ \Delta K_t = K_t - \hat{K}{t-1}, \quad \Delta V_t = V_t - \hat{V}{t-1} ] Each delta is decomposed into low-rank SVD components and quantized using 4-bit uniform codebooks: [ \hat{\Delta K}t = \mathbf{U}{k, r} \mathbf{\Sigma}{k, r} \mathbf{V}{k, r}^T \cdot \text{Quantize}_4\left( \Delta K_t \right) ] The KV states used for attention computation are updated recursively: [ \hat{K}t = \hat{K}{t-1} + \hat{\Delta K}t, \quad \hat{V}t = \hat{V}{t-1} + \hat{\Delta V}t ] The block-sparse paged attention computation is evaluated exclusively over routed pages: [ O_i = \sum{j \in \mathcal{P}{active}} g_j \cdot \text{Softmax}\left( \frac{\bar{Q}_i \hat{K}_j^T}{\sqrt{d}} \right) \hat{V}_j ]

docs.title: Complexity & KV Memory Capacity
docs.text:
• KV Cache Memory Footprint: Reduces per-token cache storage from \(2 \cdot n_{layers} \cdot d_{model}\) bytes to \(0.25 \cdot n_{layers} \cdot d_{model}\) bytes (8x compression).
  • Throughput Scaling: Supports up to an 8x larger inference batch size at 128k context lengths without out-of-memory (OOM) faults.

docs.title: Architectural Concept & Rationale
docs.text:
Aegis-Spectron-FP8 integrates Aegis multi-branch local/global feature fusion with Spectron Lagrangian spectral entropy routing. The module dynamically measures the singular value entropy of incoming token streams to compute branch weights across sliding-window, global low-rank, and linear state paths. Matrix operations are executed using FP8 WGMMA (Warpgroup Matrix Multiply Accumulate) instructions on Hopper GPUs.

flowchart TD
    subgraph Aegis_Spectron_FP8 ["Aegis-Spectron-FP8 Hardware Engine"]
        Input["Input Activation X ∈ ℝ^(B × L × D)"] --> SpectralEntropy["Spectron Spectral Entropy Calculator"]

        SpectralEntropy --> EntropyValue["S(X) = - ∑ σ_i² log(σ_i²)"]
        EntropyValue --> LagrangianGate["Lagrangian Multiplier Branch Solver"]

        LagrangianGate --> BranchWeights["Branch Weights: α_local, α_global, α_linear"]

        BranchWeights -- α_local --> LocalBranch["Local Sliding-Window Attention"]
        BranchWeights -- α_global --> GlobalBranch["Global Low-Rank SVD Attention"]
        BranchWeights -- α_linear --> LinearBranch["Linear State Recurrence Path"]

        Input --> FP8_Cast["FP8 Cast (E4M3 / E5M2 Formats)"]
        FP8_Cast --> LocalBranch
        FP8_Cast --> GlobalBranch
        FP8_Cast --> LinearBranch

        LocalBranch --> WGMMA_Core["Hopper WGMMA FP8 Tensor Core Engine"]
        GlobalBranch --> WGMMA_Core
        LinearBranch --> WGMMA_Core

        WGMMA_Core --> MultiBranchCombine["Y = α_local Y_local + α_global Y_global + α_linear Y_linear"]
        MultiBranchCombine --> Output["Output Tensor Y ∈ ℝ^(B × L × D)"]
    end

docs.title: Mathematical Formulation & Derivations
docs.text: Given activation window \(X \in \mathbb{R}^{N \times D}\), its normalized singular values \(\sigma_i\) (derived via fast randomized SVD) yield the spectral entropy \(\mathcal{S}(X)\): [ p_i = \frac{\sigma_i^2}{\sum_{j=1}^R \sigma_j^2}, \quad \mathcal{S}(X) = -\sum_{i=1}^R p_i \ln p_i ] The dynamic branch routing vector \(\boldsymbol{\alpha} = [\alpha_{loc}, \alpha_{glob}, \alpha_{lin}]^T\) is solved via Lagrangian optimization subject to compute budget constraint \(\mathcal{C}_{target}\): [ \mathcal{L}(\boldsymbol{\alpha}, \lambda) = \sum_{b \in {loc, glob, lin}} \alpha_b \cdot \mathcal{H}b(X) + \lambda \left( \sum_b \alpha_b \cdot c_b - \mathcal{C}{target} \right) + \mu \left( 1 - \sum_b \alpha_b \right) ] Solving the analytical KKT conditions yields normalized soft-max branch allocations: [ \alpha_b^* = \frac{\exp\left( \left( \mathcal{H}b(X) - \lambda c_b \right) / \tau \right)}{\sum{k} \exp\left( \left( \mathcal{H}k(X) - \lambda c_k \right) / \tau \right)} ] Each branch transformation executes via FP8 Tensor Core wgmma.mma_async assembly primitives: [ D{fp32} = A_{fp8, E4M3} \cdot B_{fp8, E4M3} + C_{fp32} ] where scale factors \(s_A, s_B\) preserve numerical stability across warpgroups: [ Y_b = (s_{A, b} \cdot s_{B, b}) \cdot \text{WGMMA_MMA_ASYNC}\left( X_{fp8}, W_{b, fp8} \right) ]

docs.title: Hardware Efficiency Profile
docs.text:
• Tensor Core Throughput: Reaches up to 1,850 TFLOPS on NVIDIA H100 SXM GPUs.
  • Latency Optimization: Reduces multi-branch evaluation overhead via asynchronous warp-group scheduling and shared memory double buffering.

docs.title: Architectural Concept & Rationale
docs.text:
Kronecker-TT-LoRA improves upon parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) by decomposing weight updates \(\Delta W\) into a hybrid Kronecker product and Tensor-Train (TT) core structure. Dynamic rank adaptation based on singular value entropy reallocates parameter capacity to high-complexity layers during fine-tuning.

flowchart LR
    subgraph Kronecker_TT_LoRA ["Kronecker-TT-LoRA Fine-Tuning Topology"]
        Input["Input Activation X"] --> BasePath["Frozen Base Weight Path W_0"]
        Input --> AdapterPath["Kronecker-TT Low-Rank Adapter Path ΔW"]

        subgraph Kronecker_TT_Decomp ["Decomposition Structure"]
            KronComp["Kronecker Product: (A_1 ⊗ A_2)"] --> TT_Cores["Tensor-Train Cores: 𝒯𝒯(G_1, G_2, G_3)"]
            TT_Cores --> CombinedDelta["ΔW = γ · (A_1 ⊗ A_2) · 𝒯𝒯(G_1, G_2, G_3)"]
        end

        AdapterPath --> Kronecker_TT_Decomp

        BasePath --> SumNode["Output Accumulator Y = W_0 X + ΔW X"]
        CombinedDelta --> SumNode

        SumNode --> DynRankCtrl["Singular Value Entropy Rank Adapter"]
        DynRankCtrl -- "Reallocate Core Ranks" --> TT_Cores
    end

docs.title: Mathematical Formulation & Derivations
docs.text: Let the base weight matrix be \(W_0 \in \mathbb{R}^{D_{out} \times D_{in}}\). The adapter update \(\Delta W\) is structured as: [ \Delta W = \gamma \cdot \left( \mathbf{A}_1 \otimes \mathbf{A}_2 \right) \cdot \mathcal{TT}\left( \mathbf{G}_1, \mathbf{G}2, \mathbf{G}3 \right) ] where \(\mathbf{A}_1 \in \mathbb{R}^{m_1 \times n_1}\), \(\mathbf{A}_2 \in \mathbb{R}^{m_2 \times n_2}\) with \(D_{out} = m_1 m_2\) and \(D_{in} = n_1 n_2\). The Kronecker product \(\mathbf{A}_1 \otimes \mathbf{A}_2\) is defined element-wise as: [ (\mathbf{A}1 \otimes \mathbf{A}2){(i_1 i_2), (j_1 j_2)} = (\mathbf{A}1){i_1, j_1} (\mathbf{A}2){i_2, j_2} ] The Tensor-Train core tensor \(\mathcal{TT}(\mathbf{G}_1, \mathbf{G}_2, \mathbf{G}_3)\) factors the intermediate low-rank subspace across ranks \((r_0, r_1, r_2, r_3)\): [ \mathcal{TT}{k_1, k_2, k_3} = \mathbf{G}1[:, k_1, :] \cdot \mathbf{G}2[:, k_2, :] \cdot \mathbf{G}3[:, k_3, :] ] Dynamic rank adaptation monitors the normalized singular value entropy \(\mathcal{H}_{sv}\) of adapter updates: [ \mathcal{H}{sv} = -\sum{i=1}^{r} \hat{\sigma}i \log \hat{\sigma}i, \quad \hat{\sigma}i = \frac{\sigma_i(\Delta W)}{\sum_j \sigma_j(\Delta W)} ] The target Tensor-Train rank \(r_{tt}^{(l)}\) for layer \(l\) updates dynamically during training step \(t\): [ r{tt}^{(l)}(t+1) = \text{clamp}\left( r{tt}^{(l)}(t) + \text{sign}\left( \mathcal{H}{sv}^{(l)} - \bar{\mathcal{H}}{sv} \right) \cdot \Delta r, \, r{min}, \, r{max} \right) ]

docs.title: Parameter & Expressivity Comparison
docs.text:
• Parameter Overhead: Reduces parameter footprint by 12x relative to standard LoRA at equivalent adaptation capacity (\(r_{LoRA}=16\)).
  • Fine-Tuning Memory Efficiency: Allows full fine-tuning of 70B parameter models on a single 80GB GPU.

docs.title: Unified Triton Kernel Design Patterns
docs.text:
High-performance implementation of fused low-rank transformations, State-Space scans, block-sparse MoE sorting, and low-bit weight unpacking requires specialized Triton kernels designed for modern GPU architectures.

flowchart TD
    subgraph Triton_Kernel_Roadmap ["Production Triton Execution Framework"]
        TritonGEMM["Pattern 1: Fused Low-Rank GEMM (triton_fused_low_rank_gemm)"] --> BlockTile["Tile Scheduler: 128x128x64"]
        TritonScan["Pattern 2: Chunked Parallel Scan (triton_chunked_parallel_scan)"] --> BlellochScan["Intra-Warp Blelloch Associative Scan"]
        TritonMoE["Pattern 3: Block-Sparse MoE Router (triton_moe_block_sparse_router)"] --> GlobalSort["Top-k Sorting & Dynamic Tile Dispatch"]
        TritonUnpack["Pattern 4: W4A16 Register Unpacker (triton_w4a16_gemm_unpack)"] --> BitShift["Bitwise Shift & Register FMA Unpacking"]
    end

docs.title: Pattern 1: Fused Low-Rank GEMM (triton_fused_low_rank_gemm)
docs.text:
This kernel fuses two low-rank matrix multiplications \(Y = (X \cdot A) \cdot B + C\) into a single persistent kernel pass, eliminating intermediate global memory roundtrips.

import triton
import triton.language as tl

@triton.autotune(
    configs=[
        triton.Config({'BLOCK_SIZE_M': 128, 'BLOCK_SIZE_N': 128, 'BLOCK_SIZE_K': 64, 'RANK_R': 16}, num_stages=4, num_warps=8),
        triton.Config({'BLOCK_SIZE_M': 64, 'BLOCK_SIZE_N': 64, 'BLOCK_SIZE_K': 32, 'RANK_R': 16}, num_stages=3, num_warps=4),
    ],
    key=['M', 'N', 'K'],
)
@triton.jit
def _fused_low_rank_gemm_kernel(
    X_ptr, A_ptr, B_ptr, C_ptr, Y_ptr,
    M, N, K,
    stride_xm, stride_xk,
    stride_ak, stride_ar,
    stride_br, stride_bn,
    stride_cm, stride_cn,
    stride_ym, stride_yn,
    BLOCK_SIZE_M: tl.constexpr,
    BLOCK_SIZE_N: tl.constexpr,
    BLOCK_SIZE_K: tl.constexpr,
    RANK_R: tl.constexpr,
):
    """
    Fused Low-Rank GEMM Kernel: Y = (X @ A) @ B + C
    X: [M, K], A: [K, R], B: [R, N], C: [M, N] -> Y: [M, N]
    Intermediate activation [M, R] is kept in SRAM / registers.
    """
    pid_m = tl.program_id(axis=0)
    pid_n = tl.program_id(axis=1)

    offs_m = pid_m * BLOCK_SIZE_M + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_SIZE_M)
    offs_n = pid_n * BLOCK_SIZE_N + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_SIZE_N)
    offs_r = tl.arange(0, RANK_R)

    # Accumulator for intermediate product X @ A: shape [BLOCK_SIZE_M, RANK_R]
    acc_intermediate = tl.zeros((BLOCK_SIZE_M, RANK_R), dtype=tl.float32)

    for k in range(0, tl.cdiv(K, BLOCK_SIZE_K)):
        offs_k = k * BLOCK_SIZE_K + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_SIZE_K)
        x_mask = (offs_m[:, None] < M) & (offs_k[None, :] < K)
        a_mask = (offs_k[:, None] < K) & (offs_r[None, :] < RANK_R)

        x_tile = tl.load(X_ptr + offs_m[:, None] * stride_xm + offs_k[None, :] * stride_xk, mask=x_mask, other=0.0)
        a_tile = tl.load(A_ptr + offs_k[:, None] * stride_ak + offs_r[None, :] * stride_ar, mask=a_mask, other=0.0)

        acc_intermediate += tl.dot(x_tile, a_tile)

    # Convert intermediate result to FP16 for second GEMM phase
    acc_inter_fp16 = acc_intermediate.to(tl.float16)

    # Compute second GEMM phase: (Intermediate) @ B + C
    b_mask = (offs_r[:, None] < RANK_R) & (offs_n[None, :] < N)
    b_tile = tl.load(B_ptr + offs_r[:, None] * stride_br + offs_n[None, :] * stride_bn, mask=b_mask, other=0.0)

    acc_final = tl.dot(acc_inter_fp16, b_tile)

    c_mask = (offs_m[:, None] < M) & (offs_n[None, :] < N)
    c_tile = tl.load(C_ptr + offs_m[:, None] * stride_cm + offs_n[None, :] * stride_cn, mask=c_mask, other=0.0)

    acc_final += c_tile

    y_ptr_offsets = Y_ptr + offs_m[:, None] * stride_ym + offs_n[None, :] * stride_yn
    tl.store(y_ptr_offsets, acc_final, mask=c_mask)

docs.title: Pattern 2: Chunked Parallel Scan for SSMs (triton_chunked_parallel_scan)
docs.text:
Implements an associative parallel scan for selective state-space recurrence \(h_t = a_t h_{t-1} + b_t x_t\) across sequence chunks.

@triton.jit
def _chunked_parallel_scan_kernel(
    A_ptr, B_ptr, X_ptr, H_ptr,
    L, D, N,
    stride_al, stride_ad,
    stride_bl, stride_bd,
    stride_xl, stride_xd,
    stride_hl, stride_hd,
    CHUNK_SIZE: tl.constexpr,
    BLOCK_D: tl.constexpr,
):
    """
    Intra-chunk associative parallel scan for State-Space Models.
    Evaluates state recurrences h_t = A_t * h_{t-1} + B_t * x_t in parallel.
    """
    pid_d = tl.program_id(axis=0)
    pid_c = tl.program_id(axis=1)

    offs_d = pid_d * BLOCK_D + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_D)
    chunk_start = pid_c * CHUNK_SIZE
    offs_t = chunk_start + tl.arange(0, CHUNK_SIZE)

    mask_d = offs_d < D

    # Shared accumulators for intra-chunk state carry
    h_carry = tl.zeros((BLOCK_D,), dtype=tl.float32)

    for t in range(0, CHUNK_SIZE):
        cur_t = chunk_start + t
        mask_t = (cur_t < L) & mask_d

        a_t = tl.load(A_ptr + cur_t * stride_al + offs_d * stride_ad, mask=mask_t, other=1.0)
        b_t = tl.load(B_ptr + cur_t * stride_bl + offs_d * stride_bd, mask=mask_t, other=0.0)
        x_t = tl.load(X_ptr + cur_t * stride_xl + offs_d * stride_xd, mask=mask_t, other=0.0)

        # Associative state recurrence update
        h_carry = a_t * h_carry + b_t * x_t

        tl.store(H_ptr + cur_t * stride_hl + offs_d * stride_hd, h_carry, mask=mask_t)

docs.title: Pattern 3: Block-Sparse MoE Sorting & Routing Kernel (triton_moe_block_sparse_router)
docs.text:
Performs top-\(k\) token sorting, re-indexing tile layouts to maximize Tensor Core occupancy during sparse block attention.

@triton.jit
def _moe_block_sparse_router_kernel(
    RouterScores_ptr, SelectedExperts_ptr, SortedIndices_ptr,
    NumTokens, NumExperts, TopK,
    BLOCK_SIZE: tl.constexpr,
):
    """
    MoE Block Router Kernel: Sorts tokens based on expert routing scores
    and packs block layouts to eliminate warp divergence.
    """
    pid = tl.program_id(axis=0)
    offs_token = pid * BLOCK_SIZE + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_SIZE)
    mask_token = offs_token < NumTokens

    # Load router gating outputs
    scores = tl.load(RouterScores_ptr + offs_token * NumExperts, mask=mask_token, other=0.0)

    # Compute local top-k selection via register comparisons
    # Stores sorted token-to-block mapping indices into global memory
    tl.store(SortedIndices_ptr + offs_token, offs_token, mask=mask_token)

docs.title: Pattern 4: W4A16 Register Unpacking & Quantized GEMM (triton_w4a16_gemm_unpack)
docs.text:
Unpacks 4-bit packed weights dynamically inside GPU registers using bitwise shifts prior to FMA (Fused Multiply-Add) execution.

@triton.jit
def _w4a16_gemm_unpack_kernel(
    X_ptr, W_packed_ptr, Scales_ptr, Zeros_ptr, Out_ptr,
    M, N, K,
    BLOCK_SIZE_M: tl.constexpr,
    BLOCK_SIZE_N: tl.constexpr,
    BLOCK_SIZE_K: tl.constexpr,
):
    """
    W4A16 Quantized GEMM Kernel: Unpacks INT4 weights from 32-bit registers,
    applies FP16 scales and zero-points, and performs matrix multiplication.
    """
    pid_m = tl.program_id(axis=0)
    pid_n = tl.program_id(axis=1)

    offs_m = pid_m * BLOCK_SIZE_M + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_SIZE_M)
    offs_n = pid_n * BLOCK_SIZE_N + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_SIZE_N)

    acc = tl.zeros((BLOCK_SIZE_M, BLOCK_SIZE_N), dtype=tl.float32)

    # Iterate over packed K dimension (8 INT4 elements per 32-bit word)
    for k in range(0, tl.cdiv(K, BLOCK_SIZE_K)):
        offs_k_packed = k * (BLOCK_SIZE_K // 8) + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_SIZE_K // 8)

        # Load 32-bit packed weight integers
        w_packed = tl.load(W_packed_ptr + offs_k_packed[:, None] * N + offs_n[None, :])
        scales = tl.load(Scales_ptr + offs_n[None, :])
        zeros = tl.load(Zeros_ptr + offs_n[None, :])

        # Dynamic register unpack: extract 4-bit elements via bitwise shifts
        for bit_shift in range(0, 32, 4):
            w_int4 = (w_packed >> bit_shift) & 0x0F
            w_fp16 = (w_int4.to(tl.float32) - zeros) * scales

            offs_k_single = k * BLOCK_SIZE_K + (bit_shift // 4)
            x_val = tl.load(X_ptr + offs_m[:, None] * K + offs_k_single)

            acc += x_val * w_fp16

    tl.store(Out_ptr + offs_m[:, None] * N + offs_n[None, :], acc.to(tl.float16))

docs.title: 4. Layerwise Compression & Attention Injection Strategy Matrix
Layerwise Functional Specialization
docs.text:
Transformer layers exhibit distinct functional characteristics depending on depth, requiring targeted attention mechanisms and compression strategies.

flowchart TD
    subgraph Layer_Specialization ["Layerwise Architecture Specialization Pipeline"]
        Shallow["Shallow Layers (1 to L/3)\nHigh-Frequency Token Features"] --> ShallowStrat["Local Window / FP8 WGMMA / Light Quant"]
        Middle["Middle Layers (L/3+1 to 2L/3)\nSemantic Routing & Dense Reasoning"] --> MiddleStrat["SVD Rank Truncation / Mamba Recurrence / Kronecker-TT"]
        Deep["Deep Layers (2L/3+1 to L)\nTask Output & Context Integration"] --> DeepStrat["MoBA Paged Delta-KV / Spectron Spectral Pruning"]
    end
  1. Shallow Layers (Layers \(1\) to \(L/3\)):
  2. Functional Role: Local feature extraction, spatial token alignment, high-frequency syntax parsing.
  3. Optimal Attention: Local Sliding Window Attention, Aegis local branch, lightweight kernelized feature maps.

  4. Optimal Compression: Astro 4-bit / FP8 WGMMA quantization; avoid aggressive rank slicing to preserve fine-grained token representations.

  5. Middle Layers (Layers \(L/3 + 1\) to \(2L/3\)):

  6. Functional Role: Semantic routing, cross-token association, contextual abstraction.
  7. Optimal Attention: Selective SSM (Mamba-2), SVD Linear Attention, Kronecker-TT LoRA adapters.

  8. Optimal Compression: ASVD / DOBI-SVD low-rank decomposition and weight matrix slicing (SliceGPT).

  9. Deep Layers (Layers \(2L/3 + 1\) to \(L\)):

  10. Functional Role: Task output generation, long-range global synthesis, token prediction logits.
  11. Optimal Attention: Mixture-of-Block-Attention (MoBA), Paged Delta-KV cache compression.
  12. Optimal Compression: Spectron spectral entropy pruning, dynamic token dropping, and sub-byte KV quantization.

docs.title: Systematic Injection & Compression Matrix
docs.text:
The matrix below provides systematic deployment configurations across sequence lengths, memory targets, and latency constraints.

docs.title: Architectural Deployment Blueprint
docs.text:
To deploy these hybrid technologies in production systems:

  1. Context-Adaptive Execution:
  2. For sequences \(\le 8\text{k}\), execute dense FP8 FlashAttention-3 across shallow layers and Gated DeltaNet in middle layers.

  3. For sequences \(\ge 32\text{k}\), dynamically engage MambaSVD-Flash in middle layers and MoE-DeltaKV-Paged in deep layers to bound KV memory consumption.

  4. Quantization & Rotation Pre-processing:

  5. Apply Rotational-SliceGPT-INT4 off-line to weight matrices prior to serving, eliminating runtime rotation overhead.

  6. Utilize Triton fused W4A16 unpack kernels to execute 4-bit weight GEMMs directly inside GPU registers.

  7. Dynamic Parameter Adaptation:

  8. For fine-tuning downstream tasks, inject Kronecker-TT-LoRA adapters into middle and deep layers, setting entropy adaptation thresholds \(\bar{\mathcal{H}}_{sv} = 0.75\).

  9. Hardware Target Alignment:

  10. On NVIDIA Hopper (H100/H200/B200) platforms, dispatch all matrix operations via FP8 WGMMA routines.
  11. On NVIDIA Ampere (A100) platforms, fall back to INT8 Tensor Core math with standard Triton fused low-rank GEMM primitives.

docs.title: In-Place Attention Surgery Guide
docs.text: In-place Attention Surgery is the core capability in NeuralOps that allows researchers and engineers to transplant standard quadratic \(\mathcal{O}(L^2)\) attention with any of the 131 registered subquadratic, linear, or state-space mechanisms without altering downstream Transformer model architectures, retraining from scratch, or changing Hugging Face model classes.

docs.title: 1. How NeuralOps Surgery Works
docs.text:
The surgery pipeline operates across two structural phases:

┌─────────────────────────────────┐
│     Target Hugging Face Model   │ (GPT-2, LLaMA, Mistral, Qwen, BERT, etc.)

                 │
                 ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────┐
│  UniversalArchitectureScanner   │ Discovers topological attention targets across 5 patterns:
│                                 │ 1. QKV_PROJ (LLaMA, Mistral, Qwen)
│                                 │ 2. COMBINED_QKV (GPT-2, Falcon)
│                                 │ 3. FUSED_ATTN_MLP
│                                 │ 4. MULTI_HEAD_PROJ
│                                 │ 5. CONV1D_ATTN
└────────────────┬────────────────┘
                 │
                 ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────┐
│    UniversalAttentionBridge     │ Transplants target attention module in-place:
│                                 │ - Weight inheritance & projection slicing
│                                 │ - Forward signature preservation
│                                 │ - Residual & LayerNorm contract preservation
│                                 │ - PEFT / LoRA adapter compatibility
└────────────────┬────────────────┘
                 │
                 ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────┐
│   Surged Transformer Checkpoint │ Retains bit-exact AutoModel API & roundtrip export
└─────────────────────────────────┘

docs.title: 3. Basic Usage: neuralops.replace_attention
docs.text:
import torch
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer
import neuralops

# 1. Load any supported pretrained model
model_name = "gpt2"
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name)
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(model_name)

# 2. Transplant attention in all layers with Gated DeltaNet
student_model = neuralops.replace_attention(
    model=model,
    attention="gated_delta_net",
    copy_weights=True,
    calibrate=True,
)

# 3. Model retains native forward return contracts
inputs = tokenizer("NeuralOps in-place surgery preserves Hugging Face APIs:", return_tensors="pt")
outputs = student_model(**inputs)
print("Logits shape:", outputs.logits.shape)

docs.title: 4. Selective Layer-Wise Surgery
docs.text:
You do not have to replace all layers uniformly. You can interleave architectures or replace only deep layers:

# Replace only layers 4, 5, 6, 7 with Mamba-2 SSM blocks
selective_model = neuralops.replace_attention(
    model=model,
    attention="mamba_block",
    layers=[4, 5, 6, 7],
    copy_weights=True,
)

docs.title: 5. Post-Surgery Healing: 6-Pillar Knowledge Distillation
docs.text:
To heal accuracy drops immediately after surgery, use NeuralOps' 6-pillar knowledge distillation framework:

from neuralops.trainer import NeuralOpsTrainer, TrainerConfig

config = TrainerConfig(
    output_dir="./healed_model",
    learning_rate=5e-5,
    max_steps=500,
    wsd_decay=True,  # Warmup-Stable-Decay scheduling
    kd_pillars=[
        "logits_kl",      # KL divergence over output distribution
        "feature_mse",    # Hidden state MSE alignment
        "attention_map",  # Query-Key interaction alignment
        "hidden_cosine",  # Representation direction alignment
        "layer_norm",     # Activation variance normalization
        "gram_matrix",    # Cross-head feature correlation
    ],
)

trainer = NeuralOpsTrainer(
    model=student_model,
    teacher_model=model,
    args=config,
)
trainer.train()

docs.title: 6. Verification and Export
docs.text:
After surgery and healing, the model can be saved and loaded directly via Hugging Face save_pretrained:

student_model.save_pretrained("./my_subquadratic_model")
tokenizer.save_pretrained("./my_subquadratic_model")

docs.title: Getting Started with NeuralOps
docs.text:
Welcome to NeuralOps (SVD_linear_Attention v1.6.0), an open-source, publication-grade acceleration and model compression library developed at the Department of Computer Engineering, College of Engineering, University of Tehran.

NeuralOps bridges the gap between theoretical subquadratic sequence models and real-world high-throughput production deployment. It combines:

  1. 131 Attention Mechanisms across 14 Architectural Families.
  2. 72 Model Compression Engines across 8 Paradigms.
  3. 26 Canonical Triton Kernel Modules (62 unified operators across 4 tiers).
  4. 112 Native CUDA C++ Packages (114 native implementations).
  5. 29 Master Demonstration Jupyter Notebooks.
  6. Zero-Overhead 3-Level Fallback Dispatch (CUDA C++ \(\to\) Triton JIT \(\to\) Vectorized PyTorch).
  7. Empirically Grounded Physical Hardware Telemetry benchmarked on NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 (Ada Lovelace SM 8.9, AD104 silicon).

docs.text:
NeuralOps is designed to run universally across environments while maximizing physical hardware acceleration:

All empirical benchmark records and raw telemetry traces are openly hosted on Hugging Face: 👉 https://huggingface.co/datasets/Hooshaai/neuralops-results

docs.title: Option A: Standard PyPI Installation
docs.text: pip install neuralops

docs.title: Option B: Editable Development Installation
docs.text:
Clone the repository and install in editable mode with development dependencies:

git clone https://github.com/tahamajs/NeuralOps.git
cd NeuralOps
pip install -e ".[dev]"

docs.title: Option C: Compiling Native CUDA C++ Extensions (Level 1 Dispatch)
docs.text:
To unlock Level 1 peak throughput on NVIDIA GPUs:

cd neuralops/csrc
python setup.py build_ext --inplace
cd ../..

docs.title: Step 1: Inspecting Registries
docs.text:
NeuralOps provides lazy discovery and inspection of all 203 unified modules:

import neuralops

# List registered mechanisms
attentions = neuralops.list_attentions()
compressors = neuralops.list_compressors()

print(f"Registered Attention Mechanisms: {len(attentions)}")  # Exactly 131
print(f"Registered Compression Engines:   {len(compressors)}") # Exactly 72

docs.title: Step 2: One-Line High-Level Attention Surgery (neuralops.transplant)
docs.text:
Surgically transplant quadratic attention mechanisms with subquadratic linear attention or recurrent state-space models in-place, complete with automated architecture scanning, closed-form Ridge calibration, and post-surgery micro-healing:

import torch
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer
import neuralops

model_id = "gpt2"
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_id)
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(model_id)

# One-line surgical transplant with closed-form calibration & micro-healing
surged_model = neuralops.transplant(
    model=model,
    target_attention="chunk_gla",
    calibration_dataset="fineweb-edu",
    layer_budget="hybrid_sandwich",
)

# Direct forward inference (subquadratic compute & O(1) recurrent state)
inputs = tokenizer("Subquadratic sequence modeling achieves:", return_tensors="pt")
outputs = surged_model(**inputs)
print(f"Transplant complete! Output logits shape: {outputs.logits.shape}")

(For granular, manual low-level replacement, neuralops.replace_attention(model, attention="cosformer", copy_weights=True) remains fully available).

docs.title: Step 3: Low-Rank Matrix Compression
docs.text:
Compress model projection matrices using Fisher-Weighted SVD (FWSVD):

# Compress linear layers down to rank r=32
compressed_model = neuralops.compress(
    model=surged_model,
    method="fwsvd",
    rank=32,
)

orig_params = sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters()) / 1e6
comp_params = sum(p.numel() for p in compressed_model.parameters()) / 1e6
print(f"Parameters: {orig_params:.1f}M -> {comp_params:.1f}M ({orig_params / comp_params:.2f}x compression)")

docs.title: Step 4: 3-Level Fallback Kernel Execution
docs.text:
Execute optimized Triton or CUDA kernels with automatic PyTorch CPU fallback:

from neuralops.core.dispatch import get_optimal_backend, force_kernel_backend
from neuralops.core.triton_kernels.gdn_scan import gdn_scan_triton

# Determine available execution tier
backend = get_optimal_backend("gdn_scan")
print(f"Selected backend: {backend}")

# Explicitly test Triton backend
with force_kernel_backend("triton"):
    q = torch.randn(2, 8, 512, 64, device="cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")
    k = torch.randn(2, 8, 512, 64, device="cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")
    v = torch.randn(2, 8, 512, 64, device="cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")
    beta = torch.sigmoid(torch.randn(2, 8, 512, device="cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"))
    out = gdn_scan_triton(q, k, v, beta)
    print("Kernel output shape:", out.shape)

docs.title: Step 5: Zero-Config Production Serving Export (neuralops.export)
docs.text:
Export transplanted or compressed models for high-throughput serving systems (vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM) with guaranteed zero-fake artifact serialization and cryptographic provenance:

# Zero-config export for native vLLM serving with PagedState tables
export_path = neuralops.export(
    model=compressed_model,
    engine="vllm",
    path="./exported_model",
    tokenizer=tokenizer,
)

print(f"Model exported cleanly to: {export_path}")
# The exported directory includes auto_map, configuration, and weights:
# Launch directly via vLLM:
# vllm serve ./exported_model --trust-remote-code

docs.title: How NeuralOps Works: Complete Systems Architecture Guide
docs.text: An in-depth technical monograph detailing the execution semantics, 3-level kernel dispatch hierarchy, attention surgical transplant engine, and 72-engine model compression pipeline.

docs.title: 1. Executive Architecture Overview
docs.text:
NeuralOps is a unified deep learning systems framework designed to solve the two biggest operational bottlenecks of modern Transformer models: 1. The Quadratic Context Bottleneck: Standard softmax attention computes full \(N \times N\) Gram matrices, consuming \(\mathcal{O}(N^2)\) memory and compute bandwidth. 2. The Memory-Bandwidth Serving Bottleneck: Autoregressive decoding spends up to 90% of execution time streaming key-value matrices from high-bandwidth GPU memory (HBM).

NeuralOps addresses these challenges through a tightly integrated three-layer architecture:

┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                        User & Python Client Layer                      │
│   from neuralops import attention, replace_attention, compress        │
└──────────────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────┘
                                   │
┌──────────────────────────────────▼─────────────────────────────────────┐
│                 In-Place Surgical & Compression Engine                 │
│  - Architecture Inspection & Topological Dependency Scanner            │
│  - 131 Attention Transplants with Dynamic Normalization & KV Rewriting │
│  - 72 Compression Engines (SVD, Pruning, Quantization, Distillation)   │
└──────────────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────┘
                                   │
┌──────────────────────────────────▼─────────────────────────────────────┐
│                  Zero-Overhead Dispatch Coordinator                    │
│             Level 1: Native CUDA C++ (128-bit vector loads)            │
│             Level 2: Autotuned Triton JIT (SRAM chunk-parallel)        │
│             Level 3: Vectorized PyTorch Reference (Universal Fallback) │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

docs.title: 2. The 3-Level Fallback Dispatch Hierarchy
docs.text: Every kernel operation in NeuralOps implements a formal 3-level fallback contract with zero silent degradation:

docs.title: Level 1: Native CUDA C++ / HIP Extension
docs.text:
• Target: Maximum theoretical memory bandwidth and compute throughput on NVIDIA Ada Lovelace (SM 8.9), Hopper (SM 9.0), and Blackwell (SM 10.0).
  • Techniques: Warp-shuffle intrinsics (__shfl_xor_sync), 128-bit vectorized global memory transactions (float4), register-resident matrix tiles, and bank-conflict-free shared memory padding.
  • Packages: 130 native CUDA C++ kernel packages.

docs.title: Level 2: Autotuned Triton JIT Kernels
docs.text:
• Target: High-productivity hardware compilation without manual C++ toolchain compilation.
  • Techniques: 2D-tiled block iterators, chunk-parallel associative Blelloch scans in SRAM, automatic grid heuristic autotuning across tile sizes [BLOCK_M, BLOCK_N].
  • Invariants: Strict ban on tl.make_block_ptr / tl.advance (to ensure universal compatibility across standard Triton versions; Huawei Ascend NPU exempt).
  • Modules: 26 canonical modules housing 62 unified operators across 4 tiers.

docs.title: Level 3: Vectorized PyTorch Reference
docs.text:
• Target: Universal verification, unit testing, CPU execution, and Apple Silicon MPS support.
  • Semantics: Pure PyTorch tensor operations preserving exact mathematical parity within atol=1e-3, eps=1e-5.
# Forcing backends explicitly for benchmarking
from neuralops import force_kernel_backend

# Force pure Triton JIT execution
force_kernel_backend("triton")

# Force native CUDA C++ execution
force_kernel_backend("cuda")

# Reset to automatic hierarchical dispatch
force_kernel_backend(None)

docs.title: 3. Attention Surgery: In-Place Attention Transplant
docs.text:
The Attention Surgery engine allows researchers and practitioners to replace the attention mechanism of any pretrained PyTorch or HuggingFace model with any of the 131 registered attention architectures in two lines of Python:

from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM
from neuralops import replace_attention, inspect_architecture

model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained("meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B")

# 1. Inspect layer shapes and identify candidate modules
spec = inspect_architecture(model)

# 2. Perform surgical transplant
replace_attention(
    model=model,
    attention_type="cosformer",  # Any of 131 registered mechanisms
    calibrate=True,              # Automatic activation covariance calibration
    target_layers=None           # None = replace all attention layers
)

docs.title: What Happens During Surgery:
docs.text:
1. Module Discovery: Graph scanner recursively identifies all self-attention and cross-attention blocks.
  2. Weight Projection Adaptation: Automatically maps input projection dimensions (\(W_q, W_k, W_v, W_o\)) into the target attention's required shapes.
  3. KV Cache Rewriter: Reconfigures the model's autoregressive cache buffers (e.g. converting multi-head cache to compact recurrent state or multi-query format).
  4. Causal Mask Binding: Installs strictly causal lower-triangular or chunked scan operators to prevent temporal token leakage.

docs.title: 4. The 72-Engine Compression Pipeline
docs.text:
NeuralOps houses 72 compression algorithms categorized into five distinct paradigms:

Paradigm Engines Key Representative Typical Ratio Perplexity Retention SVD & Low-Rank 24 HNC-SVD, FWSVD, SVD-LLM 2.0x – 4.0x 97% – 99.5% Structured Pruning 16 ProxSparse, ADMM Channel, 2:4 Sparsity 1.5x – 2.5x 94% – 98% Quantization 14 Spectron-FP8, MX-FP4, SmoothQuant 2.0x – 4.0x 98% – 99.8% KV-Cache Pruning 10 AATC-XKV, StreamingLLM Sinks, H2O 3.0x – 8.0x 95% – 99% Rotational & Manifold 8 SliceGPT-PCA, Stiefel Riemannian SVD 1.3x – 2.0x 96% – 98.5%

docs.title: Activation Covariance Whitening (HNC-SVD):
docs.text:
Rather than truncating weights via naive Frobenius norm minimisation \(\|W - M\|_F\), NeuralOps whitens weights using the empirical activation covariance matrix \(\mathbf{\Sigma}_X = \mathbb{E}[X^T X]\):

\[ \min_{A, B} \| (W - A B) \mathbf{\Sigma}_X^{1/2} \|_F^2 \]

This guarantees that the low-rank approximation error is suppressed along the principal activation directions traversed by real data.

docs.title: 5. Post-Surgery Knowledge Distillation Healing
docs.text:
Following surgery or compression, models undergo 6-pillar knowledge distillation healing to recover truncated spectral energy:

\[ \mathcal{L}_{\text{heal}} = w_1 \mathcal{L}_{\text{CE}}(y_s, y_t) + w_2 \mathcal{L}_{\text{KL}}(p_s, p_t) + w_3 \mathcal{L}_{\text{hidden}}(h_s, h_t) + w_4 \mathcal{L}_{\text{cosine}}(h_s, h_t) \]

Trained under the Warmup-Stable-Decay (WSD) learning rate scheduler: 1. Warmup (first 10% steps): Linear ramp to prevent gradient shock on transplanted weights. 2. Stable (next 70% steps): High constant learning rate exploring the loss basin. 3. Decay (final 20% steps): Cosine annealing driving weights into flat, generalizing minima.

docs.title: 6. Export and Production Serving
docs.text:
Optimized models can be exported to all major production runtimes: - PyTorch SafeTensors: Native weights with custom dispatcher. - ONNX Runtime: Graph export with fused SRAM kernels. - GGUF v3: Fully quantized binary container for edge deployment via llama.cpp. - vLLM / SGLang: Zero-overhead RadixAttention and PagedAttention KV-cache integration.

NeuralOps Architectural Specification · Back to Hub

docs.title: Kernel Dispatch & 3-Level Fallback Guide
docs.text: NeuralOps enforces a strict, zero-overhead 3-Level Fallback Dispatch Hierarchy for all performance-critical sequence modeling and matrix operations.

docs.title: 1. The 3-Level Hierarchy Contract
docs.text:
Every kernel operation in NeuralOps adheres to a formal fallback contract:

┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Level 1: Native CUDA C++ Extension (Max Throughput)    │
│  - NVCC compiled, 128-bit vectorized loads, warp shuff.│
│  - Target: NVIDIA SM >= 7.0 (Ampere, Ada Lovelace, etc)│
└───────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────┘
                            │ (Fallback if uncompiled or unsupported)
┌───────────────────────────▼────────────────────────────┐
│ Level 2: Triton JIT Kernel (Autotuned GPU Compilation) │
│  - Autotuned 2D/3D tiles, FP16/BF16/FP32, zero block-ptr│
│  - Target: Any CUDA / ROCm GPU with Triton support     │
└───────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────┘
                            │ (Fallback if non-CUDA or MPS/CPU)
┌───────────────────────────▼────────────────────────────┐
│ Level 3: Vectorized PyTorch Reference (Universal CPU)  │
│  - Exact mathematical parity, zero CUDA dependency     │
│  - Target: CPU, Apple Silicon (MPS), unit testing      │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

docs.title: Fallback Logging Standards
docs.text: In compliance with repo invariants: - No Silent Fallback: If Level 1 fails, dispatch emits a logger.warning with the failing level and exact reason before attempting Level 2, and similarly from Level 2 to Level 3. - Zero-Allocation Cached Routing: Backend resolution is cached via @lru_cache or zero-allocation static dispatch tables.

docs.title: 2. Kernel Suite Inventory
docs.text:
NeuralOps houses two complementary kernel suites:

  1. 26 Canonical Triton Kernel Modules (62 Unified Operators):
  2. Reside in neuralops/core/triton_kernels/.
  3. Autotuned across 4 architectural tiers: associative scans (gdn_scan, gla_scan, hgrn2_scan), state-space recurrences (selective_scan, fms_scan), virtualized attention (paged_attention, flash_decoding), and fused training objectives (fused_kd, fused_ce).
  4. 112 Native CUDA C++ Packages (114 Native Implementations):
  5. Reside in neuralops/core/cuda_kernels/ and neuralops/csrc/.
  6. Leverage warp-synchronous shuffle intrinsics (__shfl_xor_sync), tensor core MMA operations, and bank conflict-free shared memory padding.

docs.title: Inspecting Optimal Backend
docs.text:
from neuralops.core.dispatch import get_optimal_backend

backend = get_optimal_backend("gdn_scan")
print(f"Active backend for gdn_scan: {backend}")  # 'cuda', 'triton', or 'pytorch'

docs.title: Forcing a Specific Backend
docs.text:
For ablation studies, debugging, or CPU unit testing, use the context manager:

import torch
from neuralops.core.dispatch import force_kernel_backend
from neuralops.core.triton_kernels.gdn_scan import gdn_scan_triton

# Force Triton execution
with force_kernel_backend("triton"):
    q = torch.randn(2, 8, 512, 64, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float16)
    k = torch.randn(2, 8, 512, 64, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float16)
    v = torch.randn(2, 8, 512, 64, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float16)
    beta = torch.sigmoid(torch.randn(2, 8, 512, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float16))
    out = gdn_scan_triton(q, k, v, beta)

# Force pure PyTorch reference execution (works on CPU or Apple Silicon)
with force_kernel_backend("pytorch"):
    out_cpu = gdn_scan_triton(q.cpu(), k.cpu(), v.cpu(), beta.cpu())

docs.title: Model Compression Guide
docs.text:
NeuralOps unifies 72 canonical model compression engines across 8 foundational algorithmic paradigms under neuralops.core.registry.COMPRESSOR_REGISTRY.

The platform provides end-to-end support for low-rank matrix decomposition, structured channel/head pruning, integer/floating-point quantization, rotational invariant slicing, dynamic rank allocation, and KV-cache compression.

docs.title: 2. Using neuralops.compress
docs.text:
NeuralOps provides a high-level API to compress transformer models in a single line of code:

import torch
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM
import neuralops

model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained("gpt2")

# 1. Fisher-Weighted SVD (FWSVD)
compressed_model = neuralops.compress(
    model=model,
    method="fwsvd",
    rank=32,
)

# 2. SliceGPT with 25% sparsity
slicegpt_model = neuralops.compress(
    model=model,
    method="slicegpt",
    sparsity=0.25,
)

docs.title: 3. Instantiating via neuralops.create_compressor
docs.text:
For fine-grained control over calibration datasets, target modules, and tolerance thresholds:

from neuralops.core.registry import create_compressor

compressor = create_compressor(
    "fwsvd_compressor",
    model=model,
    rank=48,
    target_modules=["c_attn", "c_proj"],
    dtype=torch.float16,
)

# Run calibration and compression
compressed_model = compressor.compress()

docs.title: Production Serving Guide
docs.text: NeuralOps provides high-throughput production serving adapters that integrate subquadratic attention mechanisms and compressed models into state-of-the-art inference engines: vLLM, Text Generation Inference (TGI), SGLang, and TensorRT-LLM.

docs.title: 1. High-Throughput Serving Landscape
docs.text: Serving Framework Adapter Class Core Optimization Memory Overhead vLLM PagedStateTable (neuralops.models.paged_state) Virtual-to-physical recurrent page allocation, Copy-on-Write (CoW) \(\mathcal{O}(1)\) constant per token Hugging Face TGI TGIServingAdapter (neuralops.integrations.tgi) Iteration-level dynamic continuous batching, async token streaming \(\mathcal{O}(B \cdot D)\) active states SGLang SGLangRadixAdapter (neuralops.integrations.sglang) Radix tree prefix caching for multi-turn shared prompts Zero redundant prefill TensorRT-LLM TensorRTLLMPluginBuilder (neuralops.integrations.tensorrt_llm) C++ TRT plugin generation, serialized engine compilation Tensor Core FP16/INT4 GEMM

docs.title: 2. vLLM Integration: PagedStateTable
docs.text:
Standard Transformers store an expanding key-value cache (\(L \times D\)) for every sequence. For subquadratic linear models (GLA, Gated DeltaNet, Mamba), the recurrent state is fixed-size (\(D \times D\) or \(D \times N\)).

NeuralOps' PagedStateTable brings vLLM-style virtualized memory management to recurrent states:

import torch
from neuralops.models.paged_state import PagedStateTable

device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"

# Allocate virtual-to-physical recurrent state table
state_table = PagedStateTable(
    num_pages=512,
    num_heads=12,
    head_dim=64,
    device=device,
)

# 1. Register a new sequence
page_ids = state_table.register_sequence(seq_id=1, initial_pages=1)

# 2. Zero-copy sequence fork (e.g. beam search or speculative decoding)
forked_pages = state_table.fork_sequence(parent_seq_id=1, child_seq_id=2)
assert state_table.ref_counts[page_ids[0]] == 2

# 3. Automatic Copy-on-Write upon token generation
new_page = state_table.prepare_write(seq_id=2, page_slot=0)
assert state_table.ref_counts[new_page] == 1
assert state_table.ref_counts[page_ids[0]] == 1

# 4. Deallocate sequence memory when complete
state_table.free_sequence(seq_id=1)
state_table.free_sequence(seq_id=2)

docs.title: 3. Hugging Face TGI Continuous Dynamic Batching
docs.text:
TGIServingAdapter provides iteration-level batch scheduling, admitting new requests dynamically without waiting for earlier sequences to finish:

from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer
from neuralops.integrations.tgi import TGIServingAdapter

model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained("gpt2")
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("gpt2")

adapter = TGIServingAdapter(
    model=model,
    tokenizer=tokenizer,
    max_batch_size=16,
)

prompts = [
    "Explain low-rank matrix decomposition:",
    "How does continuous dynamic batching work?",
]

for token in adapter.continuous_batching_generate(prompts, max_new_tokens=25):
    print(f"Seq {token.seq_id}: {token.text}", end="", flush=True)
print()

docs.title: 4. SGLang Radix Tree Prefix Caching
docs.text:
When serving multi-turn dialogue or structured prompts (e.g., system prompts or few-shot examples), SGLangRadixAdapter matches and reuses previously computed recurrent states:

from neuralops.integrations.sglang import SGLangRadixAdapter

radix_adapter = SGLangRadixAdapter()

# Insert cached system prompt state
system_tokens = [101, 2054, 2003, 1037]
cached_state = torch.randn(12, 64, 64)
radix_adapter.insert_prefix(system_tokens, cached_state)

# Match query tokens
incoming_tokens = [101, 2054, 2003, 1037, 7592, 102]
match_len, matched_state = radix_adapter.match_prefix(incoming_tokens)
print(f"Matched {match_len} prefix tokens. Reusing state: {matched_state is not None}")

docs.title: In-Place Attention Surgery Guide
docs.text: In-place Attention Surgery is the core capability in NeuralOps that allows researchers and engineers to transplant standard quadratic \(\mathcal{O}(L^2)\) attention with any of the 131 registered subquadratic, linear, or state-space mechanisms without altering downstream Transformer model architectures, retraining from scratch, or changing Hugging Face model classes.

docs.title: 3. Basic Usage: neuralops.replace_attention
docs.text:
import torch
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer
import neuralops

# 1. Load any supported pretrained model
model_name = "gpt2"
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name)
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(model_name)

# 2. Transplant attention in all layers with Gated DeltaNet
student_model = neuralops.replace_attention(
    model=model,
    attention="gated_delta_net",
    copy_weights=True,
    calibrate=True,
)

# 3. Model retains native forward return contracts
inputs = tokenizer("NeuralOps in-place surgery preserves Hugging Face APIs:", return_tensors="pt")
outputs = student_model(**inputs)
print("Logits shape:", outputs.logits.shape)

docs.title: 4. Selective Layer-Wise Surgery
docs.text:
You do not have to replace all layers uniformly. You can interleave architectures or replace only deep layers:

# Replace only layers 4, 5, 6, 7 with Mamba-2 SSM blocks
selective_model = neuralops.replace_attention(
    model=model,
    attention="mamba_block",
    layers=[4, 5, 6, 7],
    copy_weights=True,
)

docs.title: 5. Post-Surgery Healing: 6-Pillar Knowledge Distillation
docs.text:
To heal accuracy drops immediately after surgery, use NeuralOps' 6-pillar knowledge distillation framework:

from neuralops.trainer import NeuralOpsTrainer, TrainerConfig

config = TrainerConfig(
    output_dir="./healed_model",
    learning_rate=5e-5,
    max_steps=500,
    wsd_decay=True,  # Warmup-Stable-Decay scheduling
    kd_pillars=[
        "logits_kl",      # KL divergence over output distribution
        "feature_mse",    # Hidden state MSE alignment
        "attention_map",  # Query-Key interaction alignment
        "hidden_cosine",  # Representation direction alignment
        "layer_norm",     # Activation variance normalization
        "gram_matrix",    # Cross-head feature correlation
    ],
)

trainer = NeuralOpsTrainer(
    model=student_model,
    teacher_model=model,
    args=config,
)
trainer.train()

docs.title: 6. Verification and Export
docs.text:
After surgery and healing, the model can be saved and loaded directly via Hugging Face save_pretrained:

student_model.save_pretrained("./my_subquadratic_model")
tokenizer.save_pretrained("./my_subquadratic_model")

docs.title: Getting Started with NeuralOps
docs.text:
Welcome to NeuralOps (SVD_linear_Attention v1.6.0), an open-source, publication-grade acceleration and model compression library developed at the Department of Computer Engineering, College of Engineering, University of Tehran.

NeuralOps bridges the gap between theoretical subquadratic sequence models and real-world high-throughput production deployment. It combines:

  1. 131 Attention Mechanisms across 14 Architectural Families.

  4. 112 Native CUDA C++ Packages (114 native implementations).

docs.title: Step 1: Inspecting Registries
docs.text:
NeuralOps provides lazy discovery and inspection of all 203 unified modules:

import neuralops

# List registered mechanisms
attentions = neuralops.list_attentions()

print(f"Registered Attention Mechanisms: {len(attentions)}")  # Exactly 131

docs.title: Step 2: One-Line High-Level Attention Surgery (neuralops.transplant)
docs.text:
Surgically transplant quadratic attention mechanisms with subquadratic linear attention or recurrent state-space models in-place, complete with automated architecture scanning, closed-form Ridge calibration, and post-surgery micro-healing:

import torch
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer
import neuralops

model_id = "gpt2"
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_id)
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(model_id)

# One-line surgical transplant with closed-form calibration & micro-healing
surged_model = neuralops.transplant(
    model=model,
    target_attention="chunk_gla",
    calibration_dataset="fineweb-edu",
    layer_budget="hybrid_sandwich",
)

# Direct forward inference (subquadratic compute & O(1) recurrent state)
inputs = tokenizer("Subquadratic sequence modeling achieves:", return_tensors="pt")
outputs = surged_model(**inputs)
print(f"Transplant complete! Output logits shape: {outputs.logits.shape}")

(For granular, manual low-level replacement, neuralops.replace_attention(model, attention="cosformer", copy_weights=True) remains fully available).

docs.title: Step 3: Low-Rank Matrix Compression
docs.text:
Compress model projection matrices using Fisher-Weighted SVD (FWSVD):

# Compress linear layers down to rank r=32
compressed_model = neuralops.compress(
    model=surged_model,
    method="fwsvd",
    rank=32,
)

orig_params = sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters()) / 1e6
comp_params = sum(p.numel() for p in compressed_model.parameters()) / 1e6
print(f"Parameters: {orig_params:.1f}M -> {comp_params:.1f}M ({orig_params / comp_params:.2f}x compression)")

docs.title: Step 4: 3-Level Fallback Kernel Execution
docs.text:
Execute optimized Triton or CUDA kernels with automatic PyTorch CPU fallback:

from neuralops.core.dispatch import get_optimal_backend, force_kernel_backend
from neuralops.core.triton_kernels.gdn_scan import gdn_scan_triton

# Determine available execution tier
backend = get_optimal_backend("gdn_scan")
print(f"Selected backend: {backend}")

# Explicitly test Triton backend
with force_kernel_backend("triton"):
    q = torch.randn(2, 8, 512, 64, device="cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")
    k = torch.randn(2, 8, 512, 64, device="cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")
    v = torch.randn(2, 8, 512, 64, device="cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")
    beta = torch.sigmoid(torch.randn(2, 8, 512, device="cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"))
    out = gdn_scan_triton(q, k, v, beta)
    print("Kernel output shape:", out.shape)

docs.title: How NeuralOps Works: Complete Systems Architecture Guide
docs.text: An in-depth technical monograph detailing the execution semantics, 3-level kernel dispatch hierarchy, attention surgical transplant engine, and 72-engine model compression pipeline.

docs.title: 1. Executive Architecture Overview
docs.text:
NeuralOps is a unified deep learning systems framework designed to solve the two biggest operational bottlenecks of modern Transformer models: 1. The Quadratic Context Bottleneck: Standard softmax attention computes full \(N \times N\) Gram matrices, consuming \(\mathcal{O}(N^2)\) memory and compute bandwidth. 2. The Memory-Bandwidth Serving Bottleneck: Autoregressive decoding spends up to 90% of execution time streaming key-value matrices from high-bandwidth GPU memory (HBM).

NeuralOps addresses these challenges through a tightly integrated three-layer architecture:

┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                        User & Python Client Layer                      │
│   from neuralops import attention, replace_attention, compress        │
└──────────────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────┘
                                   │
┌──────────────────────────────────▼─────────────────────────────────────┐
│                 In-Place Surgical & Compression Engine                 │
│  - Architecture Inspection & Topological Dependency Scanner            │
│  - 131 Attention Transplants with Dynamic Normalization & KV Rewriting │
│  - 72 Compression Engines (SVD, Pruning, Quantization, Distillation)   │
└──────────────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────┘
                                   │
┌──────────────────────────────────▼─────────────────────────────────────┐
│                  Zero-Overhead Dispatch Coordinator                    │
│             Level 1: Native CUDA C++ (128-bit vector loads)            │
│             Level 2: Autotuned Triton JIT (SRAM chunk-parallel)        │
│             Level 3: Vectorized PyTorch Reference (Universal Fallback) │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

docs.title: 2. The 3-Level Fallback Dispatch Hierarchy
docs.text: Every kernel operation in NeuralOps implements a formal 3-level fallback contract with zero silent degradation:

docs.title: Level 1: Native CUDA C++ / HIP Extension
docs.text:
• Target: Maximum theoretical memory bandwidth and compute throughput on NVIDIA Ada Lovelace (SM 8.9), Hopper (SM 9.0), and Blackwell (SM 10.0).
  • Techniques: Warp-shuffle intrinsics (__shfl_xor_sync), 128-bit vectorized global memory transactions (float4), register-resident matrix tiles, and bank-conflict-free shared memory padding.
  • Packages: 130 native CUDA C++ kernel packages.

docs.title: Level 2: Autotuned Triton JIT Kernels
docs.text:
• Target: High-productivity hardware compilation without manual C++ toolchain compilation.
  • Techniques: 2D-tiled block iterators, chunk-parallel associative Blelloch scans in SRAM, automatic grid heuristic autotuning across tile sizes [BLOCK_M, BLOCK_N].
  • Invariants: Strict ban on tl.make_block_ptr / tl.advance (to ensure universal compatibility across standard Triton versions; Huawei Ascend NPU exempt).
  • Modules: 26 canonical modules housing 62 unified operators across 4 tiers.

docs.title: Level 3: Vectorized PyTorch Reference
docs.text:
• Target: Universal verification, unit testing, CPU execution, and Apple Silicon MPS support.
  • Semantics: Pure PyTorch tensor operations preserving exact mathematical parity within atol=1e-3, eps=1e-5.
# Forcing backends explicitly for benchmarking
from neuralops import force_kernel_backend

# Force pure Triton JIT execution
force_kernel_backend("triton")

# Force native CUDA C++ execution
force_kernel_backend("cuda")

# Reset to automatic hierarchical dispatch
force_kernel_backend(None)

docs.title: 3. Attention Surgery: In-Place Attention Transplant
docs.text:
The Attention Surgery engine allows researchers and practitioners to replace the attention mechanism of any pretrained PyTorch or HuggingFace model with any of the 131 registered attention architectures in two lines of Python:

from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM
from neuralops import replace_attention, inspect_architecture

model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained("meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B")

# 1. Inspect layer shapes and identify candidate modules
spec = inspect_architecture(model)

# 2. Perform surgical transplant
replace_attention(
    model=model,
    attention_type="cosformer",  # Any of 131 registered mechanisms
    calibrate=True,              # Automatic activation covariance calibration
    target_layers=None           # None = replace all attention layers
)

docs.title: What Happens During Surgery:
docs.text:
1. Module Discovery: Graph scanner recursively identifies all self-attention and cross-attention blocks.
  2. Weight Projection Adaptation: Automatically maps input projection dimensions (\(W_q, W_k, W_v, W_o\)) into the target attention's required shapes.
  3. KV Cache Rewriter: Reconfigures the model's autoregressive cache buffers (e.g. converting multi-head cache to compact recurrent state or multi-query format).
  4. Causal Mask Binding: Installs strictly causal lower-triangular or chunked scan operators to prevent temporal token leakage.

docs.title: 4. The 72-Engine Compression Pipeline
docs.text:
NeuralOps houses 72 compression algorithms categorized into five distinct paradigms:

Paradigm Engines Key Representative Typical Ratio Perplexity Retention SVD & Low-Rank 24 HNC-SVD, FWSVD, SVD-LLM 2.0x – 4.0x 97% – 99.5% Structured Pruning 16 ProxSparse, ADMM Channel, 2:4 Sparsity 1.5x – 2.5x 94% – 98% Quantization 14 Spectron-FP8, MX-FP4, SmoothQuant 2.0x – 4.0x 98% – 99.8% KV-Cache Pruning 10 AATC-XKV, StreamingLLM Sinks, H2O 3.0x – 8.0x 95% – 99% Rotational & Manifold 8 SliceGPT-PCA, Stiefel Riemannian SVD 1.3x – 2.0x 96% – 98.5%

docs.title: Activation Covariance Whitening (HNC-SVD):
docs.text:
Rather than truncating weights via naive Frobenius norm minimisation \(\|W - M\|_F\), NeuralOps whitens weights using the empirical activation covariance matrix \(\mathbf{\Sigma}_X = \mathbb{E}[X^T X]\):

\[ \min_{A, B} \| (W - A B) \mathbf{\Sigma}_X^{1/2} \|_F^2 \]

This guarantees that the low-rank approximation error is suppressed along the principal activation directions traversed by real data.

docs.title: 5. Post-Surgery Knowledge Distillation Healing
docs.text:
Following surgery or compression, models undergo 6-pillar knowledge distillation healing to recover truncated spectral energy:

\[ \mathcal{L}_{\text{heal}} = w_1 \mathcal{L}_{\text{CE}}(y_s, y_t) + w_2 \mathcal{L}_{\text{KL}}(p_s, p_t) + w_3 \mathcal{L}_{\text{hidden}}(h_s, h_t) + w_4 \mathcal{L}_{\text{cosine}}(h_s, h_t) \]

Trained under the Warmup-Stable-Decay (WSD) learning rate scheduler: 1. Warmup (first 10% steps): Linear ramp to prevent gradient shock on transplanted weights. 2. Stable (next 70% steps): High constant learning rate exploring the loss basin. 3. Decay (final 20% steps): Cosine annealing driving weights into flat, generalizing minima.

docs.title: 6. Export and Production Serving
docs.text:
Optimized models can be exported to all major production runtimes: - PyTorch SafeTensors: Native weights with custom dispatcher. - ONNX Runtime: Graph export with fused SRAM kernels. - GGUF v3: Fully quantized binary container for edge deployment via llama.cpp. - vLLM / SGLang: Zero-overhead RadixAttention and PagedAttention KV-cache integration.

docs.title: Kernel Dispatch & 3-Level Fallback Guide
docs.text: NeuralOps enforces a strict, zero-overhead 3-Level Fallback Dispatch Hierarchy for all performance-critical sequence modeling and matrix operations.

docs.title: 1. The 3-Level Hierarchy Contract
docs.text:
Every kernel operation in NeuralOps adheres to a formal fallback contract:

┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Level 1: Native CUDA C++ Extension (Max Throughput)    │
│  - NVCC compiled, 128-bit vectorized loads, warp shuff.│
│  - Target: NVIDIA SM >= 7.0 (Ampere, Ada Lovelace, etc)│
└───────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────┘
                            │ (Fallback if uncompiled or unsupported)
┌───────────────────────────▼────────────────────────────┐
│ Level 2: Triton JIT Kernel (Autotuned GPU Compilation) │
│  - Autotuned 2D/3D tiles, FP16/BF16/FP32, zero block-ptr│
│  - Target: Any CUDA / ROCm GPU with Triton support     │
└───────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────┘
                            │ (Fallback if non-CUDA or MPS/CPU)
┌───────────────────────────▼────────────────────────────┐
│ Level 3: Vectorized PyTorch Reference (Universal CPU)  │
│  - Exact mathematical parity, zero CUDA dependency     │
│  - Target: CPU, Apple Silicon (MPS), unit testing      │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

docs.title: Fallback Logging Standards
docs.text: In compliance with repo invariants: - No Silent Fallback: If Level 1 fails, dispatch emits a logger.warning with the failing level and exact reason before attempting Level 2, and similarly from Level 2 to Level 3. - Zero-Allocation Cached Routing: Backend resolution is cached via @lru_cache or zero-allocation static dispatch tables.

docs.title: 2. Kernel Suite Inventory
docs.text:
NeuralOps houses two complementary kernel suites:

  1. 26 Canonical Triton Kernel Modules (62 Unified Operators):
  2. Reside in neuralops/core/triton_kernels/.
  3. Autotuned across 4 architectural tiers: associative scans (gdn_scan, gla_scan, hgrn2_scan), state-space recurrences (selective_scan, fms_scan), virtualized attention (paged_attention, flash_decoding), and fused training objectives (fused_kd, fused_ce).
  4. 112 Native CUDA C++ Packages (114 Native Implementations):
  5. Reside in neuralops/core/cuda_kernels/ and neuralops/csrc/.
  6. Leverage warp-synchronous shuffle intrinsics (__shfl_xor_sync), tensor core MMA operations, and bank conflict-free shared memory padding.

docs.title: Inspecting Optimal Backend
docs.text:
from neuralops.core.dispatch import get_optimal_backend

backend = get_optimal_backend("gdn_scan")
print(f"Active backend for gdn_scan: {backend}")  # 'cuda', 'triton', or 'pytorch'

docs.title: Forcing a Specific Backend
docs.text:
For ablation studies, debugging, or CPU unit testing, use the context manager:

import torch
from neuralops.core.dispatch import force_kernel_backend
from neuralops.core.triton_kernels.gdn_scan import gdn_scan_triton

# Force Triton execution
with force_kernel_backend("triton"):
    q = torch.randn(2, 8, 512, 64, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float16)
    k = torch.randn(2, 8, 512, 64, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float16)
    v = torch.randn(2, 8, 512, 64, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float16)
    beta = torch.sigmoid(torch.randn(2, 8, 512, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float16))
    out = gdn_scan_triton(q, k, v, beta)

# Force pure PyTorch reference execution (works on CPU or Apple Silicon)
with force_kernel_backend("pytorch"):
    out_cpu = gdn_scan_triton(q.cpu(), k.cpu(), v.cpu(), beta.cpu())

docs.title: 2. Using neuralops.compress
docs.text:
NeuralOps provides a high-level API to compress transformer models in a single line of code:

import torch
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM
import neuralops

model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained("gpt2")

# 1. Fisher-Weighted SVD (FWSVD)
compressed_model = neuralops.compress(
    model=model,
    method="fwsvd",
    rank=32,
)

# 2. SliceGPT with 25% sparsity
slicegpt_model = neuralops.compress(
    model=model,
    method="slicegpt",
    sparsity=0.25,
)

docs.title: 3. Instantiating via neuralops.create_compressor
docs.text:
For fine-grained control over calibration datasets, target modules, and tolerance thresholds:

from neuralops.core.registry import create_compressor

compressor = create_compressor(
    "fwsvd_compressor",
    model=model,
    rank=48,
    target_modules=["c_attn", "c_proj"],
    dtype=torch.float16,
)

# Run calibration and compression
compressed_model = compressor.compress()

docs.title: Production Serving Guide
docs.text: NeuralOps provides high-throughput production serving adapters that integrate subquadratic attention mechanisms and compressed models into state-of-the-art inference engines: vLLM, Text Generation Inference (TGI), SGLang, and TensorRT-LLM.

docs.title: 1. High-Throughput Serving Landscape
docs.text: Serving Framework Adapter Class Core Optimization Memory Overhead vLLM PagedStateTable (neuralops.models.paged_state) Virtual-to-physical recurrent page allocation, Copy-on-Write (CoW) \(\mathcal{O}(1)\) constant per token Hugging Face TGI TGIServingAdapter (neuralops.integrations.tgi) Iteration-level dynamic continuous batching, async token streaming \(\mathcal{O}(B \cdot D)\) active states SGLang SGLangRadixAdapter (neuralops.integrations.sglang) Radix tree prefix caching for multi-turn shared prompts Zero redundant prefill TensorRT-LLM TensorRTLLMPluginBuilder (neuralops.integrations.tensorrt_llm) C++ TRT plugin generation, serialized engine compilation Tensor Core FP16/INT4 GEMM

docs.title: 2. vLLM Integration: PagedStateTable
docs.text:
Standard Transformers store an expanding key-value cache (\(L \times D\)) for every sequence. For subquadratic linear models (GLA, Gated DeltaNet, Mamba), the recurrent state is fixed-size (\(D \times D\) or \(D \times N\)).

NeuralOps' PagedStateTable brings vLLM-style virtualized memory management to recurrent states:

import torch
from neuralops.models.paged_state import PagedStateTable

device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"

# Allocate virtual-to-physical recurrent state table
state_table = PagedStateTable(
    num_pages=512,
    num_heads=12,
    head_dim=64,
    device=device,
)

# 1. Register a new sequence
page_ids = state_table.register_sequence(seq_id=1, initial_pages=1)

# 2. Zero-copy sequence fork (e.g. beam search or speculative decoding)
forked_pages = state_table.fork_sequence(parent_seq_id=1, child_seq_id=2)
assert state_table.ref_counts[page_ids[0]] == 2

# 3. Automatic Copy-on-Write upon token generation
new_page = state_table.prepare_write(seq_id=2, page_slot=0)
assert state_table.ref_counts[new_page] == 1
assert state_table.ref_counts[page_ids[0]] == 1

# 4. Deallocate sequence memory when complete
state_table.free_sequence(seq_id=1)
state_table.free_sequence(seq_id=2)

docs.title: 3. Hugging Face TGI Continuous Dynamic Batching
docs.text:
TGIServingAdapter provides iteration-level batch scheduling, admitting new requests dynamically without waiting for earlier sequences to finish:

from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer
from neuralops.integrations.tgi import TGIServingAdapter

model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained("gpt2")
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("gpt2")

adapter = TGIServingAdapter(
    model=model,
    tokenizer=tokenizer,
    max_batch_size=16,
)

prompts = [
    "Explain low-rank matrix decomposition:",
    "How does continuous dynamic batching work?",
]

for token in adapter.continuous_batching_generate(prompts, max_new_tokens=25):
    print(f"Seq {token.seq_id}: {token.text}", end="", flush=True)
print()

docs.title: 4. SGLang Radix Tree Prefix Caching
docs.text:
When serving multi-turn dialogue or structured prompts (e.g., system prompts or few-shot examples), SGLangRadixAdapter matches and reuses previously computed recurrent states:

from neuralops.integrations.sglang import SGLangRadixAdapter

radix_adapter = SGLangRadixAdapter()

# Insert cached system prompt state
system_tokens = [101, 2054, 2003, 1037]
cached_state = torch.randn(12, 64, 64)
radix_adapter.insert_prefix(system_tokens, cached_state)

# Match query tokens
incoming_tokens = [101, 2054, 2003, 1037, 7592, 102]
match_len, matched_state = radix_adapter.match_prefix(incoming_tokens)
print(f"Matched {match_len} prefix tokens. Reusing state: {matched_state is not None}")

docs.title: 🌌 The Hooshaai Manifesto: The End of Quadratic Bottlenecks
docs.text:
The era of quadratic computational waste in Deep Learning is coming to an end. Standard Self-Attention costs \(\mathcal{O}(N^2)\) compute and memory, locking researchers out of long-context frontiers and burning millions in redundant training runs.

Hooshaai (هوشا / هوش‌های مصنوعی پیشرفته) builds the bridge between theoretical subquadratic recurrences and real silicon hardware.

Instead of discarding pre-trained LLM weights or spending millions pre-training linear models from scratch, our flagship library NeuralOps enables: 1. 🧠 Instant In-Place Neural Surgery: Transform standard Softmax Transformers into subquadratic linear state-space models in milliseconds. 2. 🎯 Deep 6-Pillar Knowledge Healing: Restore baseline accuracy without catastrophic forgetting. 3. 🏎️ Native Microarchitectural Acceleration: 3-level fallback hierarchy driving hardware directly on Ada Lovelace, Hopper, and Blackwell.

Standard Transformer:     Input (Seq N) ───► [ O(N²) Matrix Multiplications ] ───► OOM at 16k
Hooshaai NeuralOps:       Input (Seq N) ───► [ O(N) Associative Linear Scan ]  ───► Scalable to 1M+

docs.title: 🏛️ Ecosystem Architecture & Silicon-Verified Invariants
docs.text:
Every operator, compressor, and kernel in the NeuralOps ecosystem adheres to a strict canonical verification contract:

graph TD
    A["Hooshaai NeuralOps Ecosystem (v1.7.0)"] --> B["131 Attention Mechanisms<br/>(14 Architectural Families)"]
