import pyarrow.ipc as ipc
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F
from torch.utils.data import DataLoader, Dataset
from transformers import PreTrainedTokenizerFast
from safetensors.torch import load_file

logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(asctime)s [%(levelname)s] %(message)s")
logger = logging.getLogger("qwen_wiki_kd")


class RMSNorm(nn.Module):
    """Root Mean Square Layer Normalization with FP32 Variance Protection."""
    def __init__(self, dim: int, eps: float = 1e-6) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.eps = eps
        self.weight = nn.Parameter(torch.ones(dim))

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        input_dtype = x.dtype
        variance = x.to(torch.float32).pow(2).mean(-1, keepdim=True)
        x = x * torch.rsqrt(variance + self.eps)
        return self.weight * x.to(input_dtype)


class RoPEEmbedding(nn.Module):
    """Rotary Position Embedding for Qwen2 causal attention."""
    def __init__(self, dim: int, max_position_embeddings: int = 32768, base: float = 1000000.0) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.dim = dim
        inv_freq = 1.0 / (base ** (torch.arange(0, dim, 2).float() / dim))
        self.register_buffer("inv_freq", inv_freq, persistent=False)
        t = torch.arange(max_position_embeddings, dtype=torch.float32)
        freqs = torch.outer(t, inv_freq)
        emb = torch.cat((freqs, freqs), dim=-1)
        self.register_buffer("cos_cached", emb.cos(), persistent=False)
        self.register_buffer("sin_cached", emb.sin(), persistent=False)

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor, seq_len: int) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
        return self.cos_cached[:seq_len, :], self.sin_cached[:seq_len, :]


def rotate_half(x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    x1 = x[..., : x.shape[-1] // 2]
    x2 = x[..., x.shape[-1] // 2 :]
    return torch.cat((-x2, x1), dim=-1)


def apply_rotary_pos_emb(
    q: torch.Tensor, k: torch.Tensor, cos: torch.Tensor, sin: torch.Tensor
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    cos = cos.unsqueeze(0).unsqueeze(1)
    sin = sin.unsqueeze(0).unsqueeze(1)
    q_embed = (q * cos) + (rotate_half(q) * sin)
    k_embed = (k * cos) + (rotate_half(k) * sin)
    return q_embed, k_embed


class Qwen2MLP(nn.Module):
    """SwiGLU Multi-Layer Perceptron."""
    def __init__(self, hidden_size: int, intermediate_size: int) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.gate_proj = nn.Linear(hidden_size, intermediate_size, bias=False)
        self.up_proj = nn.Linear(hidden_size, intermediate_size, bias=False)
        self.down_proj = nn.Linear(intermediate_size, hidden_size, bias=False)

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        return self.down_proj(F.silu(self.gate_proj(x)) * self.up_proj(x))


class Qwen2Attention(nn.Module):
    """Standard Grouped-Query Causal Attention with RoPE."""
    def __init__(self, hidden_size: int, num_heads: int, num_kv_heads: int) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.hidden_size = hidden_size
        self.num_heads = num_heads
        self.num_kv_heads = num_kv_heads
        self.head_dim = hidden_size // num_heads
        self.num_key_value_groups = num_heads // num_kv_heads

        self.q_proj = nn.Linear(hidden_size, num_heads * self.head_dim, bias=True)
        self.k_proj = nn.Linear(hidden_size, num_kv_heads * self.head_dim, bias=True)
        self.v_proj = nn.Linear(hidden_size, num_kv_heads * self.head_dim, bias=True)
        self.o_proj = nn.Linear(num_heads * self.head_dim, hidden_size, bias=False)

    def forward(
        self,
        x: torch.Tensor,
        cos: torch.Tensor,
        sin: torch.Tensor,
        mask: torch.Tensor | None = None,
    ) -> torch.Tensor:
        bsz, q_len, _ = x.size()
        q = self.q_proj(x).view(bsz, q_len, self.num_heads, self.head_dim).transpose(1, 2)
        k = self.k_proj(x).view(bsz, q_len, self.num_kv_heads, self.head_dim).transpose(1, 2)
        v = self.v_proj(x).view(bsz, q_len, self.num_kv_heads, self.head_dim).transpose(1, 2)

        q, k = apply_rotary_pos_emb(q, k, cos, sin)

        if self.num_key_value_groups > 1:
            k = k.repeat_interleave(self.num_key_value_groups, dim=1)
            v = v.repeat_interleave(self.num_key_value_groups, dim=1)

        scores = torch.matmul(q, k.transpose(-1, -2)) / math.sqrt(self.head_dim)
        if mask is not None:
            scores = scores + mask
        probs = F.softmax(scores, dim=-1).to(v.dtype)
        out = torch.matmul(probs, v)
        out = out.transpose(1, 2).contiguous().view(bsz, q_len, self.hidden_size)
        return self.o_proj(out)


class CausalAttentionSurgeonAdapter(nn.Module):
    """Universal Adapter reconciling Grouped-Query Attention & RoPE with Registry modules."""
    def __init__(self, core_attn: nn.Module, hidden_size: int) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.core_attn = core_attn

    def forward(
        self,
        x: torch.Tensor,
        cos: torch.Tensor,
        sin: torch.Tensor,
        mask: torch.Tensor | None = None,
    ) -> torch.Tensor:
        out = self.core_attn(x, mask=mask)
        out_tensor = out[0] if isinstance(out, tuple) else out
        return out_tensor


class Qwen2DecoderLayer(nn.Module):
    """Single transformer decoder block."""
    def __init__(
        self,
        hidden_size: int,
        intermediate_size: int,
        num_heads: int,
        num_kv_heads: int,
        rms_eps: float,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.input_layernorm = RMSNorm(hidden_size, eps=rms_eps)
        self.self_attn = Qwen2Attention(hidden_size, num_heads, num_kv_heads)
        self.post_attention_layernorm = RMSNorm(hidden_size, eps=rms_eps)
        self.mlp = Qwen2MLP(hidden_size, intermediate_size)

    def forward(
        self,
        x: torch.Tensor,
        cos: torch.Tensor,
        sin: torch.Tensor,
        mask: torch.Tensor | None = None,
    ) -> torch.Tensor:
        h = x + self.self_attn(self.input_layernorm(x), cos, sin, mask)
        out = h + self.mlp(self.post_attention_layernorm(h))
        return out


class StandaloneQwen2ForCausalLM(nn.Module):
    """Clean PyTorch 1.12+ compatible implementation of Qwen2/2.5 Causal LM."""
    def __init__(self, config: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.config = config
        hidden_size = config["hidden_size"]
        intermediate_size = config["intermediate_size"]
        num_layers = config["num_hidden_layers"]
        num_heads = config["num_attention_heads"]
        num_kv_heads = config["num_key_value_heads"]
        rms_eps = config.get("rms_norm_eps", 1e-6)
        vocab_size = config["vocab_size"]

        self.embed_tokens = nn.Embedding(vocab_size, hidden_size)
        self.rotary_emb = RoPEEmbedding(hidden_size // num_heads, base=config.get("rope_theta", 1000000.0))
        self.layers = nn.ModuleList([
            Qwen2DecoderLayer(hidden_size, intermediate_size, num_heads, num_kv_heads, rms_eps)
            for _ in range(num_layers)
        ])
        self.norm = RMSNorm(hidden_size, eps=rms_eps)
        self.lm_head = nn.Linear(hidden_size, vocab_size, bias=False)
        if config.get("tie_word_embeddings", False):
            self.lm_head.weight = self.embed_tokens.weight

    def forward(
        self,
        input_ids: torch.Tensor,
        labels: torch.Tensor | None = None,
        return_hidden_only: bool = False,
    ) -> Any:
        bsz, seq_len = input_ids.shape
        x = self.embed_tokens(input_ids)
        cos, sin = self.rotary_emb(x, seq_len)
        cos = cos.to(dtype=x.dtype, device=x.device)
        sin = sin.to(dtype=x.dtype, device=x.device)

        mask = torch.triu(torch.full((seq_len, seq_len), float("-inf"), device=x.device), diagonal=1)
        mask = mask.unsqueeze(0).unsqueeze(1)

        for layer in self.layers:
            x = layer(x, cos, sin, mask)
        x = self.norm(x)

        if return_hidden_only:
            return x

        loss = None
        if labels is not None:
            shift_x = x[:, :-1, :]
            shift_labels = labels[:, 1:]
            total_loss_sum = 0.0
            chunk_size = 64
            vocab_sz = self.config["vocab_size"]
            for i in range(0, shift_x.size(1), chunk_size):
                h_c = shift_x[:, i:i + chunk_size, :]
                l_c = shift_labels[:, i:i + chunk_size]
                logits_c = self.lm_head(h_c).float()  # Compute in FP32
                loss_c = F.cross_entropy(logits_c.view(-1, vocab_sz), l_c.reshape(-1), reduction="sum")
                total_loss_sum = total_loss_sum + loss_c
            loss = total_loss_sum / shift_labels.numel()
            return type("CausalLMOutput", (), {"logits": None, "hidden_states": x, "loss": loss})()

        logits = self.lm_head(x)
        return type("CausalLMOutput", (), {"logits": logits, "hidden_states": x, "loss": None})()


class ArrowWikiTextDataset(Dataset):
    """Direct streaming of tokenized WikiText-2 blocks for Causal LM evaluation."""
    def __init__(self, arrow_path: str, tokenizer: Any, seq_len: int = 512) -> None:
        with open(arrow_path, "rb") as f:
            reader = ipc.open_stream(f)
            self.table = reader.read_all()
        raw_texts = self.table["text"].to_pylist()
        concatenated = "\n\n".join([t for t in raw_texts if t.strip()])
        tokens = tokenizer.encode(concatenated)
        self.num_samples = len(tokens) // seq_len
        self.tokens = torch.tensor(tokens[:self.num_samples * seq_len], dtype=torch.long)
        self.seq_len = seq_len

    def __len__(self) -> int:
        return self.num_samples

    def __getitem__(self, idx: int) -> dict[str, torch.Tensor]:
        start = idx * self.seq_len
        chunk = self.tokens[start:start + self.seq_len]
        return {
            "input_ids": chunk,
            "labels": chunk.clone()
        }


def evaluate_ppl(model: nn.Module, dataloader: DataLoader, device: torch.device, max_batches: int = 40) -> float:
    """Calculates official Perplexity on WikiText-2 with causal cross-entropy."""
    model.eval()
    total_loss = 0.0
    total_tokens = 0

    with torch.no_grad():
        for b_idx, batch in enumerate(dataloader):
            if b_idx >= max_batches:
                break
            input_ids = batch["input_ids"].to(device, non_blocking=True)
            labels = batch["labels"].to(device, non_blocking=True)

            outputs = model(input_ids=input_ids, labels=labels)
            loss = outputs.loss
            tokens_count = (labels.size(1) - 1) * labels.size(0)

            total_loss += loss.item() * tokens_count
            total_tokens += tokens_count

    if total_tokens == 0:
        return 999.9
    avg_loss = total_loss / total_tokens
    ppl = math.exp(min(avg_loss, 20.0))
    return round(ppl, 2)


def run_qwen_surgery_pipeline(
    module_name: str,
    teacher_model: StandaloneQwen2ForCausalLM,
    train_loader: DataLoader,
    test_loader: DataLoader,
    device: torch.device,
    isolated_steps: int = 40,
    polish_steps: int = 15,
    iso_lr: float = 2e-5,
    polish_lr: float = 1e-6,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    from neuralops.core.registry import create_attention

    logger.info(f"\n{'='*80}\n[QWEN SURGERY] Testing Attention Module: {module_name}\n{'='*80}")
    t0 = time.time()

    student_model = copy.deepcopy(teacher_model)
    hidden_size = student_model.config["hidden_size"]
    num_heads = student_model.config["num_attention_heads"]

    # Replace Qwen attention layers with adapted registry module
    for layer in student_model.layers:
        try:
            core_attn = create_attention(module_name, embed_dim=hidden_size, num_heads=num_heads)
        except Exception:
            core_attn = create_attention(module_name, dim=hidden_size, num_heads=num_heads)
        layer.self_attn = CausalAttentionSurgeonAdapter(core_attn, hidden_size).to(device, dtype=torch.float16)

    student_model.to(device)
    zero_shot_ppl = evaluate_ppl(student_model, test_loader, device)
    logger.info(f"[{module_name}] Stage 0 (Zero-Shot Surgery): PPL={zero_shot_ppl:.2f}")

    # Stage 1: Isolated Attention Mimicry (Backbone Frozen)
    t_iso_start = time.time()
    for name, param in student_model.named_parameters():
        param.requires_grad = "self_attn" in name

    trainable_params = [p for p in student_model.parameters() if p.requires_grad]
    optimizer_iso = torch.optim.AdamW(trainable_params, lr=iso_lr, weight_decay=1e-4)
    student_model.train()

    for step, batch in enumerate(train_loader):
        if step >= isolated_steps:
            break
        in_ids = batch["input_ids"].to(device, non_blocking=True)
        lbls = batch["labels"].to(device, non_blocking=True)

        optimizer_iso.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
        with torch.no_grad():
            t_hidden = teacher_model(input_ids=in_ids, return_hidden_only=True)
        s_hidden = student_model(input_ids=in_ids, return_hidden_only=True)

        kd_loss = F.mse_loss(s_hidden.float(), t_hidden.float())
        s_out = student_model(input_ids=in_ids, labels=lbls)
        lm_loss = s_out.loss
        loss = kd_loss + lm_loss

        loss.backward()
        torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(trainable_params, 0.5)
        optimizer_iso.step()

    t_iso_dur = time.time() - t_iso_start
    isolated_ppl = evaluate_ppl(student_model, test_loader, device)
    logger.info(f"[{module_name}] Stage 1 (Isolated Attn): PPL={isolated_ppl:.2f} | Time={t_iso_dur:.1f}s")

    # Stage 2: Quick E2E Distillation Polish
    t_pol_start = time.time()
    for name, param in student_model.named_parameters():
        param.requires_grad = "self_attn" in name

    trainable_params_pol = [p for p in student_model.parameters() if p.requires_grad]
    optimizer_pol = torch.optim.AdamW(trainable_params_pol, lr=polish_lr, weight_decay=1e-4)
    student_model.train()

    for step, batch in enumerate(train_loader):
        if step >= polish_steps:
            break
        in_ids = batch["input_ids"].to(device, non_blocking=True)
        lbls = batch["labels"].to(device, non_blocking=True)

        optimizer_pol.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
        with torch.no_grad():
            t_hidden = teacher_model(input_ids=in_ids, return_hidden_only=True)
        s_hidden = student_model(input_ids=in_ids, return_hidden_only=True)

        kd_loss = F.mse_loss(s_hidden.float(), t_hidden.float())
        s_out = student_model(input_ids=in_ids, labels=lbls)
        lm_loss = s_out.loss
        total_l = kd_loss + lm_loss

        total_l.backward()
        torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(trainable_params_pol, 0.5)
        optimizer_pol.step()

    t_pol_dur = time.time() - t_pol_start
    final_ppl = evaluate_ppl(student_model, test_loader, device)
    total_dur = time.time() - t0
    logger.info(f"[{module_name}] Stage 2 (Quick Polish): PPL={final_ppl:.2f} | TotalTime={total_dur:.1f}s")

    del student_model
    gc.collect()
    torch.cuda.empty_cache()

    return {
        "module": module_name,
        "zero_shot_ppl": zero_shot_ppl,
        "isolated_ppl": isolated_ppl,
        "polished_ppl": final_ppl,
        "isolated_time_s": round(t_iso_dur, 1),
        "polish_time_s": round(t_pol_dur, 1),
        "total_time_s": round(total_dur, 1),
        "status": "PASSED"
    }


def persist_qwen_sqlite(results: list[dict[str, Any]], base_ppl: float, sqlite_path: str = "results/master_ledger.sqlite") -> None:
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(sqlite_path), exist_ok=True)
    conn = sqlite3.connect(sqlite_path)
    cur = conn.cursor()
    cur.execute("""
        CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS qwen_wikitext_kd_ablation (
            id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
            timestamp TEXT,
            model_name TEXT,
            dataset TEXT,
            module TEXT,
            teacher_baseline_ppl REAL,
            zero_shot_ppl REAL,
            isolated_ppl REAL,
            polished_ppl REAL,
            ppl_delta REAL,
            total_time_s REAL,
            status TEXT
        )
    """)
    ts = datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).isoformat()
    for r in results:
        pol_ppl = r.get("polished_ppl", 0.0)
        delta = round(pol_ppl - base_ppl, 2)
        cur.execute("""
            INSERT INTO qwen_wikitext_kd_ablation (
                timestamp, model_name, dataset, module, teacher_baseline_ppl,
                zero_shot_ppl, isolated_ppl, polished_ppl, ppl_delta,
                total_time_s, status
            ) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
        """, (
            ts,
            "Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B",
            "WikiText-2",
            r.get("module"),
            base_ppl,
            r.get("zero_shot_ppl", 0.0),
            r.get("isolated_ppl", 0.0),
            pol_ppl,
            delta,
            r.get("total_time_s", 0.0),
            r.get("status", "UNKNOWN")
        ))
    conn.commit()
    conn.close()


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Qwen WikiText-2 Causal KD Ablation")
    parser.add_argument("--model-path", type=str, default="/home/tahamajlesi.ut/.cache/huggingface/hub/models--Qwen--Qwen2.5-0.5B/snapshots/060db6499f32faf8b98477b0a26969ef7d8b9987")
    parser.add_argument("--module", type=str, default=None)
    parser.add_argument("--all-modules", action="store_true")
    parser.add_argument("--batch-size", type=int, default=2)
    parser.add_argument("--seq-len", type=int, default=512)
    parser.add_argument("--isolated-steps", type=int, default=60)
    parser.add_argument("--polish-steps", type=int, default=25)
    parser.add_argument("--iso-lr", type=float, default=1e-4)
    parser.add_argument("--polish-lr", type=float, default=1e-5)
    parser.add_argument("--out-csv", type=str, default="results/qwen_wikitext_kd_ablation.csv")
    parser.add_argument("--out-json", type=str, default="results/qwen_wikitext_kd_ablation.json")
    parser.add_argument("--ledger-db", type=str, default="results/master_ledger.sqlite")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    device = torch.device("cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")
    logger.info(f"=== Launching Qwen Causal LM KD on: {torch.cuda.get_device_name(0)} ===")

    tokenizer_path = os.path.join(args.model_path, "tokenizer.json")
    tokenizer = PreTrainedTokenizerFast(tokenizer_file=tokenizer_path)

    train_path = os.path.expanduser("~/.cache/huggingface/datasets/wikitext/wikitext-2-raw-v1/0.0.0/b08601e04326c79dfdd32d625aee71d232d685c3/wikitext-train.arrow")
    test_path = os.path.expanduser("~/.cache/huggingface/datasets/wikitext/wikitext-2-raw-v1/0.0.0/b08601e04326c79dfdd32d625aee71d232d685c3/wikitext-test.arrow")

    train_dataset = ArrowWikiTextDataset(train_path, tokenizer, seq_len=args.seq_len)
    test_dataset = ArrowWikiTextDataset(test_path, tokenizer, seq_len=args.seq_len)

    train_loader = DataLoader(train_dataset, batch_size=args.batch_size, shuffle=True, pin_memory=True)
    test_loader = DataLoader(test_dataset, batch_size=args.batch_size, shuffle=False, pin_memory=True)

    logger.info(f"Loading Standalone Qwen Teacher from {args.model_path} in float16...")
    with open(os.path.join(args.model_path, "config.json")) as f:
        cfg = json.load(f)
    teacher_model = StandaloneQwen2ForCausalLM(cfg)
    weights = load_file(os.path.join(args.model_path, "model.safetensors"))
    cleaned_sd = {k[6:] if k.startswith("model.") else k: v for k, v in weights.items()}
    teacher_model.load_state_dict(cleaned_sd, strict=False)
    teacher_model = teacher_model.to(device=device, dtype=torch.float16)
    teacher_model.eval()
    for p in teacher_model.parameters():
        p.requires_grad = False

    teacher_ppl = evaluate_ppl(teacher_model, test_loader, device)
    logger.info(f"Verified Teacher Baseline PPL on WikiText-2: {teacher_ppl:.2f}")

    if args.module:
        target_modules = [args.module]
    elif args.all_modules:
        from neuralops.core.registry import ATTENTION_REGISTRY
        target_modules = list(ATTENTION_REGISTRY.keys())
    else:
        target_modules = [
            "cosformer",
            "linear_attention",
            "gla_attention",
            "svd_linear_attention",
            "decay_linear_attention",
        ]

    results = []
    for mod_name in target_modules:
        try:
            res = run_qwen_surgery_pipeline(
                module_name=mod_name,
                teacher_model=teacher_model,
                train_loader=train_loader,
                test_loader=test_loader,
                device=device,
                isolated_steps=args.isolated_steps,
                polish_steps=args.polish_steps,
                iso_lr=args.iso_lr,
                polish_lr=args.polish_lr,
            )
            res["teacher_ppl"] = teacher_ppl
            results.append(res)
        except Exception as exc:
            logger.error(f"Error evaluating {mod_name} on Qwen: {exc}")
            results.append({
                "module": mod_name,
                "zero_shot_ppl": 999.9,
                "isolated_ppl": 999.9,
                "polished_ppl": 999.9,
                "teacher_ppl": teacher_ppl,
                "total_time_s": 0.0,
                "status": f"FAILED: {exc}"
            })

        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(args.out_json), exist_ok=True)
        with open(args.out_json, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            json.dump(results, f, indent=2)

    import pandas as pd
    df = pd.DataFrame(results)
    df.to_csv(args.out_csv, index=False)
    persist_qwen_sqlite(results, base_ppl=teacher_ppl, sqlite_path=args.ledger_db)

    print("\n" + "=" * 105)
    print(f"QWEN WIKITEXT-2 PERPLEXITY ABLATION SUMMARY (Teacher Baseline PPL: {teacher_ppl:.2f})")
    print("=" * 105)
    print(f"{'Module':<25} | {'Zero-Shot PPL':<15} | {'Isolated PPL':<15} | {'Polished PPL':<15} | {'Total Time':<12} | {'Status'}")
    print("-" * 105)
    for r in results:
        mod = r.get("module", "")[:24]
        zs = f"{r.get('zero_shot_ppl', 0.0):.2f}"
        iso = f"{r.get('isolated_ppl', 0.0):.2f}"
        pol = f"{r.get('polished_ppl', 0.0):.2f}"
        tt = f"{r.get('total_time_s', 0.0):.1f}s"
        st = r.get("status", "")
        print(f"{mod:<25} | {zs:<15} | {iso:<15} | {pol:<15} | {tt:<12} | {st}")
    print("=" * 105)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

docs.title: Comprehensive Engineering Blueprint & Architectural Specification: Unified Benchmark Execution, Config Management, Experiment Tracking, and Per-Run Artifact Isolation
docs.text: Author / Lead Systems Architect: Taha Majlesi (tahamaj4@gmail.com) Project: NeuralOps Architecture & Optimization Framework (v1.5.0 / Branch: main) Document Classification: Core Architectural Redesign & Systems Engineering Specification Scope: neuralops/cli/, neuralops/config/, neuralops/tracking/, neuralops/results_saver/, benchmarks/ Date: November 4, 2026 Status: Canonical Engineering Roadmap & Specification Document (1,000+ Lines)

docs.title: Executive Summary & Design Philosophy
docs.text:
The objective of this engineering specification is to resolve structural fragmentation across the NeuralOps benchmarking ecosystem. Currently, benchmarking tasks, command-line interfaces, configuration parsers, experiment tracking, and results persistence operate through partially decoupled pathways.

To achieve an enterprise-grade, reproducible, and verifiable deep learning systems architecture, we establish a Single Source of Truth Unified Pipeline. Under this paradigm:

  1. Zero External Wrappers: The root-level benchmarks/ directory (which contains redundant standalone wrapper scripts) is completely eliminated. All benchmarking capabilities are exposed strictly through the native CLI (neuralops benchmark) backed by internal package modules in neuralops/benchmarks/.
  2. Unified Declarative Configuration Engine (neuralops/config/): Every benchmark run is defined via declarative, versioned YAML/JSON configuration files validated against structured Pydantic schemas. Hardcoded hyperparameters and scattered CLI flags are eradicated.
  3. Deep Lifecycle Experiment Tracking (neuralops/tracking/): Every run instantiates an isolated ExperimentTracker instance logging real-time step-by-step loss trajectories, hardware telemetry (VRAM, temperature, latency), and intermediate evaluations into offline-first JSONL and TensorBoard events.
  4. Per-Run Directory Encapsulation (results/benchmarks/<benchmark_name>/runs/<run_id>/): Flat directory clutter in results/ is replaced by an isolated, hermetic folder per execution containing the full configuration snapshot, Git commit hash, environment metadata, raw telemetry, step-level metric logs, console streams, and serialized artifacts.
  5. Atomic Ledger Synchronization: Each isolated execution commits a summarized forensic record to the central SQLite ledger (results/master_ledger.sqlite) and updates the benchmark's rolling summary.csv, maintaining cross-session empirical provenance.

docs.title: 1. Forensic Audit of Current State (As-Is Architecture)
1.1 The Root-Level benchmarks/ Directory Redundancy
docs.text: A rigorous inspection of the repository root reveals a standalone folder named benchmarks/ containing 32 files and subdirectories: - Standalone execution scripts: benchmark_all_26_comprehensive.py, benchmark_all_26_kernels.py, benchmark_torch_compile_131_attentions.py, bench_llm_bandwidth.py, measure_multiprecision.py, multi_seed_stress_test_131_72.py, etc. - Legacy configuration presets: benchmarks/configs/quick_cuda.json, exhaustive_cuda.json, long_context_cuda.json. - Competitor benchmarks: benchmarks/competitors/. - Shell runners: benchmarks/run_suite.sh.

docs.title: Architectural Vulnerabilities:
docs.text:
1. Code Duplication & Maintenance Drift: Every script in benchmarks/ is essentially a thin wrapper importing or re-implementing functionality that already exists within neuralops/benchmarks/. When bugs are patched in neuralops/benchmarks/, the root scripts are frequently neglected, creating severe version drift.
  2. Ambiguous User Experience: Users and automated pipelines face conflicting entrypoints:
  3. Should they run python benchmarks/benchmark_all_26_comprehensive.py?
  4. Or should they run python -m neuralops.benchmarks.cli run ...?
  5. Or neuralops eval ...?
  6. Violations of Package Isolation: A Python framework package (neuralops) should be self-contained and distributable via pip install neuralops. Having critical operational logic residing in a root-level benchmarks/ folder breaks packaging invariants and prevents wheel installations from accessing full benchmarking features.

docs.title: 1.2 The Flat results/ Storage Anti-Pattern
docs.text:
Inspection of the results/ directory shows over 167 distinct files and subdirectories dumped in a flat namespace: 

results/
├── master_ledger.sqlite               # Central database
├── qwen_wikitext_kd_ablation.csv      # CSV output from Qwen ablation
├── qwen_wikitext_kd_ablation.json     # JSON output from Qwen ablation
├── sst2_layerwise_kd_ablation.json    # JSON output from SST-2 ablation
├── sst2_cached_layerwise_kd.csv       # CSV output from SST-2 cache run
├── triton_26_kernels_comprehensive_benchmark.csv
├── triton_26_kernels_rtx3090_baseline.csv
├── benchmark_3level_cuda_triton_pytorch.csv
├── direct_sst2_kd.log                 # Loose log file
├── exhaustive_no_hla.log              # Loose log file
├── teacher_layerwise_cache_sst2.pt    # 4.99 GB binary cache
└── ... (over 150 more scattered files)

docs.title: Critical Failure Modes of the Flat Schema:
docs.text:
• Zero Run Isolation: If a user runs the Qwen WikiText ablation multiple times with different learning rates or sequence lengths, the files qwen_wikitext_kd_ablation.csv and .json are blindly overwritten unless manually renamed by the user.
  • Lost Context and Provenance: When viewing results/triton_26_kernels_comprehensive_benchmark.csv, it is impossible to determine after the fact which Git commit produced it, what the exact GPU clock rate or temperature was, or what specific CLI arguments were passed.
  • File System Clutter: Automated sweeps producing hundreds of logs and checkpoints create an unmanageable root directory where identifying experimental baselines requires manual grep operations.

docs.title: 1.3 Decoupling Between neuralops/tracking/ and Benchmarking Workflows
docs.text: NeuralOps contains a dedicated tracking package at neuralops/tracking/ with high-quality abstractions: - ExperimentTracker (neuralops/tracking/tracker.py) - LocalTracker, TensorBoardTracker, WandBTracker, MLflowTracker (neuralops/tracking/backends.py) - TrackerCallback (neuralops/tracking/callbacks.py)

docs.title: The Architectural Disconnect:
docs.text: Despite the existence of this infrastructure, none of the benchmark scripts currently instantiate ExperimentTracker: - In scripts/benchmarks/run_qwen_wikitext_kd_ablation.py, metrics are accumulated into standard Python lists and dumped to disk at the end of the script using pandas.DataFrame.to_csv() and raw SQLite SQL queries. - Step-by-step training loss during Stage 1 and Stage 2 distillation is computed in memory but never logged to a time-series or step-series tracker. - As a consequence, researchers cannot visualize learning dynamics in TensorBoard or inspect step-level loss curves if an experiment crashes mid-run.

docs.title: 1.4 State of the Configuration Subsystem (neuralops/config/)
docs.text: The neuralops/config/ package provides Pydantic-based configuration schemas: - config.py (NeuralOpsConfig) - experiment_config.py (ExperimentConfig) - training_config.py (TrainingConfig) - model_config.py (ModelConfig) - data_config.py (DataConfig) - loader.py (load_config, parse_args_to_config)

docs.title: Existing Limitations:
docs.text:
• The configuration loader is primarily wired to neuralops train and neuralops compress.
  • Benchmark workflows lack a dedicated BenchmarkConfig schema supporting specialized benchmarking fields:
  • Micro-batch sizes vs. evaluation batch sizes.
  • Context extrapolation steps (\(512 o 32,768\)).
  • Fallback tier verification contracts (CUDA $ o$ Triton $ o$ PyTorch).
  • Target metrics selection (PPL, accuracy, latency, memory bandwidth, arithmetic intensity).
  • Tracking backend selection and destination path schemas.

docs.title: 1.5 The Existing SQLite Database Schema (results/master_ledger.sqlite)
docs.text:
The central database currently manages four tables: 1. results: 2,635 rows of general benchmark measurements across 27 columns. 2. qwen_wikitext_kd_ablation: 13 rows tracking Qwen2.5 WikiText-2 causal language model ablation runs across 12 columns. 3. layerwise_kd_ablation: 2 rows tracking RoBERTa SST-2 distillation runs across 9 columns. 4. sqlite_sequence: Internal SQLite sequence tracking.

While the SQLite database functions reliably, it represents an aggregate summary sink. It does not capture fine-grained step-level histories or link back to specific run directory manifests.

docs.title: 2.1 The Five Pillars of Unified Execution
Pillar 1: Total Elimination of Root benchmarks/ Wrappers
docs.text:
All scripts in the root benchmarks/ folder will be safely archived or deleted. The sole authoritative entrypoint for benchmarking will be: 

neuralops benchmark <subcommand>
Backed by neuralops/cli/bench_cmd.py and modular kernels in neuralops/benchmarks/.

docs.title: Pillar 2: Schema-Enforced Declarative Configuration
docs.text: Every benchmark must be completely expressible as a clean YAML or JSON document. The CLI will accept --config <path> alongside standard key-value overrides (--override batch_size=8).

docs.title: Pillar 3: Granular Real-Time Experiment Tracking
docs.text:
By integrating ExperimentTracker into all benchmark loops, every step of micro-training, distillation, or kernel timing is captured. Researchers can open TensorBoard at any time to monitor progress: 

tensorboard --logdir results/benchmarks/

docs.title: Pillar 4: Per-Run Directory Hermeticity
docs.text: Every execution produces a uniquely timestamped folder under results/benchmarks/<benchmark_name>/runs/<run_id>/. This folder contains everything required to forensically audit the experiment without inspecting external databases.

docs.title: Pillar 5: Atomic Double-Entry Ledger Synchronization
docs.text: High-level summary metrics are atomically inserted into results/master_ledger.sqlite and appended to results/benchmarks/<benchmark_name>/summary.csv, maintaining historical analytics while guaranteeing individual run isolation.

docs.title: 3. Deep Dive: The Experiment Tracking Engine (neuralops/tracking/)
3.1 Architectural Decomposition of ExperimentTracker
docs.text:
The neuralops/tracking/ package is structured around a centralized Facade design pattern:

neuralops/tracking/
├── __init__.py        # Re-exports ExperimentTracker, TrackingBackend, TrackerCallback
├── backends.py        # Abstract BaseTracker + Local, TensorBoard, WandB, MLflow adapters
├── callbacks.py       # PyTorch Lightning & Transformers Trainer Callback implementations
└── tracker.py         # ExperimentTracker facade class

docs.title: Core Class Signature (ExperimentTracker):
docs.text:
class ExperimentTracker:
    def __init__(
        self,
        backend: str = "local",
        experiment_name: str = "experiment",
        log_dir: str = "./results/logs",
        project: str | None = None,
        config_dict: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
        tracking_uri: str | None = None,
    ) -> None: ...

    def log_metric(self, name: str, value: float, step: int | None = None) -> None: ...
    def log_metrics(self, metrics: dict[str, float], step: int | None = None) -> None: ...
    def log_param(self, key: str, value: Any) -> None: ...
    def log_params(self, params: dict[str, Any]) -> None: ...
    def log_artifact(self, local_path: str) -> None: ...
    def finalize(self, result: dict[str, Any] | None = None) -> None: ...
    def close(self) -> None: ...

docs.title: 3.2 Offline-First Design for Air-Gapped Supercomputers (Sharif HPC)
docs.text: A critical requirement of NeuralOps is the ability to run on air-gapped academic HPC clusters (such as Sharif University HPC compute node GPU-3090-1), where all outbound network access is blocked by campus firewalls.

docs.title: Why LocalTracker & TensorBoardTracker Excel in Air-Gapped Environments:
docs.text:
1. Zero Network Calls: LocalTracker appends JSON objects directly to local disk storage using standard POSIX file append calls (open(mode="a")). No socket initialization, DNS lookups, or SSL handshakes occur.
  2. Crash-Resilience: Because metrics.jsonl is written with immediate flushing (flush() on each step), if a cluster job terminates due to wall-time limits (PBS walltime exceeded) or out-of-memory errors, all metrics up to the exact crash step are preserved.
  3. Zero External Dependencies: LocalTracker uses standard library modules (json, os, shutil, datetime). It requires no third-party packages.
  4. Binary Visualization with TensorBoard: TensorBoardTracker utilizes PyTorch's native torch.utils.tensorboard.SummaryWriter, creating local protobuf event streams (events.out.tfevents.*) that can be inspected without internet connectivity.

docs.title: 3.4 Integration of Real-Time Step-Level Telemetry
docs.text:
To achieve comprehensive tracking during benchmarking and distillation, the tracking engine must log multiple metric channels concurrently:

# Real-Time Telemetry Logging Protocol
for step, batch in enumerate(train_loader):
    loss, aux_losses = model_step(batch)

    # 1. Algorithmic Losses
    tracker.log_metric("train/total_loss", loss.item(), step=step)
    tracker.log_metric("train/kd_feature_loss", aux_losses["kd"].item(), step=step)
    tracker.log_metric("train/causal_lm_loss", aux_losses["lm"].item(), step=step)

    # 2. Optimization Dynamics
    tracker.log_metric("optim/learning_rate", scheduler.get_last_lr()[0], step=step)
    tracker.log_metric("optim/grad_norm", current_grad_norm, step=step)

    # 3. Hardware Telemetry
    if step % 10 == 0 and torch.cuda.is_available():
        allocated_mb = torch.cuda.memory_allocated() / (1024 * 1024)
        reserved_mb = torch.cuda.memory_reserved() / (1024 * 1024)
        tracker.log_metric("hardware/vram_allocated_mb", allocated_mb, step=step)
        tracker.log_metric("hardware/vram_reserved_mb", reserved_mb, step=step)

docs.title: 4.1 Schema Modeling via Pydantic (BenchmarkConfig)
docs.text:
We introduce a formalized schema for benchmark configurations in neuralops/config/benchmark_config.py using Pydantic:

from __future__ import annotations
from typing import Any, List, Optional, Union
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

class BenchmarkTargetConfig(BaseModel):
    name: str = Field(..., description="Unique benchmark identifier, e.g. 'qwen_wikitext_kd'")
    category: str = Field(..., description="Benchmark domain: 'attention', 'kernel', 'compression', 'serving'")
    description: Optional[str] = Field(None, description="Human-readable description of benchmark scope")
    output_root: str = Field("results/benchmarks", description="Root storage directory for benchmark runs")

class ModelTargetConfig(BaseModel):
    name: str = Field(..., description="Hugging Face ID or local path, e.g. 'Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B'")
    type: str = Field("causal_lm", description="'causal_lm', 'masked_lm', or 'custom'")
    torch_dtype: str = Field("float16", description="'float16', 'bfloat16', or 'float32'")
    device: str = Field("cuda", description="'cuda', 'cpu', or 'mps'")

class DatasetTargetConfig(BaseModel):
    name: str = Field(..., description="Dataset identifier, e.g. 'wikitext', 'sst2'")
    subset: Optional[str] = Field("wikitext-2-raw-v1", description="Dataset configuration or split subset")
    seq_len: int = Field(512, description="Evaluation sequence context length")
    batch_size: int = Field(4, description="Micro-batch size per evaluation / training step")
    max_eval_batches: int = Field(40, description="Max batches for perplexity / accuracy evaluation")

class RegimesConfig(BaseModel):
    isolated_steps: int = Field(80, description="Stage 1 isolated mimicry training steps")
    polish_steps: int = Field(30, description="Stage 2 end-to-end polish steps")
    isolated_lr: float = Field(5.0e-4, description="Stage 1 optimizer learning rate")
    polish_lr: float = Field(1.0e-4, description="Stage 2 optimizer learning rate")
    weight_decay: float = Field(1.0e-4, description="AdamW weight decay coefficient")
    grad_clip_norm: float = Field(0.5, description="Maximum gradient norm threshold")

class TrackingSetupConfig(BaseModel):
    backend: str = Field("local", description="'local', 'tensorboard', 'wandb', or 'mlflow'")
    project: str = Field("neuralops_benchmarks", description="Project namespace for tracking dashboard")
    log_step_interval: int = Field(1, description="Interval for step metric recording")
    enable_tensorboard: bool = Field(True, description="Enable simultaneous TensorBoard event export")

class LedgerSetupConfig(BaseModel):
    sqlite_path: str = Field("results/master_ledger.sqlite", description="Path to canonical SQLite ledger")
    update_rolling_summary: bool = Field(True, description="Update summary.csv in benchmark folder")

class BenchmarkConfig(BaseModel):
    benchmark: BenchmarkTargetConfig
    model: ModelTargetConfig
    dataset: DatasetTargetConfig
    modules: List[str] = Field(..., description="List of attention or compressor modules to evaluate")
    regimes: Optional[RegimesConfig] = Field(default_factory=RegimesConfig)
    tracking: TrackingSetupConfig = Field(default_factory=TrackingSetupConfig)
    ledger: LedgerSetupConfig = Field(default_factory=LedgerSetupConfig)

docs.title: 4.3 CLI Dynamic Override Protocol
docs.text:
To maintain flexibility without modifying YAML files on disk, the CLI supports dynamic dot-notation overrides: 

neuralops benchmark run     --config neuralops/config/benchmarks/qwen_wikitext_kd.yaml     --override dataset.batch_size=8     --override regimes.isolated_steps=120     --override tracking.backend=tensorboard

docs.title: 5. Deep Dive: Hermetic Per-Run Directory Isolation & Results Saver
5.1 Encapsulated Folder Structure for Execution Runs
docs.text:

docs.title: 5.5 Dual-Commit to master_ledger.sqlite
docs.text:
While individual run folders preserve granular file artifacts, the centralized SQLite database remains the master index for cross-benchmark SQL querying and global dashboard visualization:

def commit_to_master_ledger(
    manifest: dict[str, Any],
    results: list[dict[str, Any]],
    sqlite_path: str = "results/master_ledger.sqlite",
) -> None:
    conn = sqlite3.connect(sqlite_path)
    cur = conn.cursor()

    # Ensure foreign-linkable benchmark runs table exists
    cur.execute('''
        CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS benchmark_runs (
            run_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
            benchmark_name TEXT,
            timestamp_utc TEXT,
            commit_sha TEXT,
            hostname TEXT,
            device_name TEXT,
            run_dir TEXT,
            duration_s REAL,
            status TEXT
        )
    ''')

    cur.execute('''
        INSERT OR REPLACE INTO benchmark_runs (
            run_id, benchmark_name, timestamp_utc, commit_sha,
            hostname, device_name, run_dir, duration_s, status
        ) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
    ''', (
        manifest["run_id"],
        manifest["benchmark_name"],
        manifest["timestamp_start_utc"],
        manifest["git_provenance"]["commit_sha"],
        manifest["host_environment"]["hostname"],
        manifest["host_environment"]["gpu_devices"][0]["name"],
        f"results/benchmarks/{manifest['benchmark_name']}/runs/{manifest['run_id']}",
        manifest["duration_seconds"],
        manifest["execution_outcome"]["status"],
    ))

    conn.commit()
    conn.close()

docs.title: 6.1 Design Principles & Subcommand Taxonomy
docs.text:
The central entry point for all benchmark operations is neuralops benchmark registered in neuralops/cli/bench_cmd.py. The legacy habit of calling loose, non-packaged python scripts in the repository root (e.g., python benchmarks/benchmark_attention.py) introduces version skew, environment mismatches, non-standardized argument parsing, and untracked outputs.

Under the unified architecture, neuralops benchmark exposes a strict, intuitive hierarchical taxonomy:

neuralops benchmark
├── run                 Execute an active benchmark suite
│   ├── --suite, -s     Suite identifier (attention, compressor, e2e, niah, roofline)
│   ├── --config, -c    Path to declarative YAML/JSON configuration
│   ├── --backend       Hardware backend selection (cuda, triton, torch, auto)
│   ├── --output-dir    Optional custom root override (default: results/benchmarks/)
│   ├── --device        Compute device target (cuda:0, cpu, mps)
│   ├── --tag           User-defined categorization tag
│   └── --dry-run       Validate schema and print execution plan without compute
├── list                Inspect available benchmark suites and registered components
│   ├── --suites        List registered benchmark classes
│   ├── --attentions    List the 131 canonical registered attention mechanisms
│   └── --compressors   List the 72 canonical registered model compressors
├── show                Display details or results of a past run
│   ├── <run_id>        Forensic inspection of a specific execution run
│   ├── --metrics       Print tabular metric summary
│   ├── --manifest      Display full JSON provenance manifest
│   └── --log           Stream execution stderr/stdout log
├── compare             Side-by-side performance comparison of multiple runs
│   ├── <run_id_1> <run_id_2> ... Compare execution metrics across runs
│   ├── --metric        Target metric to compare (latency_ms, peak_vram_mb, tflops)
│   └── --format        Output format (table, json, markdown, latex)
└── export              Export run telemetry to external reporting formats
    ├── <run_id>        Target run identifier
    └── --format        Target serialization format (parquet, latex, csv, wandb)

docs.title: 6.2 Full Argument Parsing Specification
docs.text:
The CLI is implemented using Python's argparse standard library module, maintaining zero external dependencies while providing rich formatting, type casting, validation, and auto-generated help.

# File: neuralops/cli/bench_cmd.py (Target Architecture)

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from typing import List, Optional

from neuralops.config.benchmark_schema import BenchmarkRunConfig
from neuralops.benchmarks.core.runner import BenchmarkRunner
from neuralops.benchmarks.core.registry import BENCHMARK_REGISTRY


def add_benchmark_parser(subparsers: argparse._SubParsersAction) -> None:
    """Register 'benchmark' command and subcommands into NeuralOps central CLI."""
    bench_parser = subparsers.add_parser(
        "benchmark",
        help="Unified benchmarking, profiling, and telemetry system",
        description="Execute, monitor, track, and analyze benchmark suites across hardware."
    )

    bench_subparsers = bench_parser.add_subparsers(dest="bench_command", required=True)

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Subcommand: run
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    run_parser = bench_subparsers.add_parser(
        "run",
        help="Execute an empirical benchmark run",
        description="Run specified benchmark suite with declarative configuration and hermetic tracking."
    )
    run_parser.add_argument(
        "--suite", "-s",
        type=str,
        required=True,
        choices=sorted(BENCHMARK_REGISTRY.keys()),
        help="Benchmark suite identifier to execute"
    )
    run_parser.add_argument(
        "--config", "-c",
        type=str,
        default=None,
        help="Path to YAML or JSON benchmark run configuration file"
    )
    run_parser.add_argument(
        "--backend",
        type=str,
        default="auto",
        choices=["auto", "cuda", "triton", "torch"],
        help="Target execution backend for 3-level fallback hierarchy"
    )
    run_parser.add_argument(
        "--output-dir",
        type=str,
        default="results/benchmarks",
        help="Root destination directory for benchmark run isolates"
    )
    run_parser.add_argument(
        "--device",
        type=str,
        default="cuda:0",
        help="Target compute device string (e.g., 'cuda:0', 'cpu')"
    )
    run_parser.add_argument(
        "--batch-sizes",
        type=int,
        nargs="+",
        default=None,
        help="Override batch sizes (e.g. --batch-sizes 1 4 16)"
    )
    run_parser.add_argument(
        "--seq-lens",
        type=int,
        nargs="+",
        default=None,
        help="Override sequence lengths (e.g. --seq-lens 512 2048 8192)"
    )
    run_parser.add_argument(
        "--tag",
        type=str,
        default=None,
        help="User-defined semantic tag for ledger indexing and filtering"
    )
    run_parser.add_argument(
        "--dry-run",
        action="store_true",
        help="Validate parameters and print execution manifest without invoking kernels"
    )

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Subcommand: list
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    list_parser = bench_subparsers.add_parser(
        "list",
        help="List available benchmark suites and kernel registry entities"
    )
    list_group = list_parser.add_mutually_exclusive_group()
    list_group.add_argument(
        "--suites",
        action="store_true",
        help="List registered benchmark suites"
    )
    list_group.add_argument(
        "--attentions",
        action="store_true",
        help="List all 131 canonical registered attention mechanisms"
    )
    list_group.add_argument(
        "--compressors",
        action="store_true",
        help="List all 72 canonical registered model compressors"
    )

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Subcommand: show
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    show_parser = bench_subparsers.add_parser(
        "show",
        help="Inspect details and metrics of a previous benchmark run"
    )
    show_parser.add_argument(
        "run_id",
        type=str,
        help="UUID or timestamp-based run identifier"
    )
    show_parser.add_argument(
        "--manifest",
        action="store_true",
        help="Output raw JSON provenance manifest"
    )
    show_parser.add_argument(
        "--log",
        action="store_true",
        help="Display raw execution stderr/stdout log"
    )

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Subcommand: compare
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    cmp_parser = bench_subparsers.add_parser(
        "compare",
        help="Compare execution metrics across multiple benchmark runs"
    )
    cmp_parser.add_argument(
        "run_ids",
        type=str,
        nargs="+",
        help="List of run IDs to compare"
    )
    cmp_parser.add_argument(
        "--metric",
        type=str,
        default="latency_ms",
        choices=["latency_ms", "tflops", "peak_vram_mb", "retention"],
        help="Target comparison metric"
    )
    cmp_parser.add_argument(
        "--format",
        type=str,
        default="table",
        choices=["table", "markdown", "latex", "json"],
        help="Comparison presentation format"
    )


def execute_benchmark_cli(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    """Main execution dispatcher for 'neuralops benchmark' CLI command."""
    if args.bench_command == "list":
        return _handle_list(args)
    elif args.bench_command == "run":
        return _handle_run(args)
    elif args.bench_command == "show":
        return _handle_show(args)
    elif args.bench_command == "compare":
        return _handle_compare(args)
    return 1

docs.title: 6.3 End-to-End Command Execution Flow
docs.text:
When a user or automated PBS job submits neuralops benchmark run --suite attention --config configs/benchmarks/attention_sm89.yaml:

  1. CLI Parsing: bench_cmd.py parses CLI arguments into a validated namespace.
  2. Config Composition: If --config is supplied, BenchmarkConfigLoader.load_yaml() parses the file. Any explicit CLI overrides (such as --device or --batch-sizes) override file values.
  3. Pydantic Validation: BenchmarkRunConfig(**merged_dict) rigorously verifies types, constraints, ranges, and existence.
  4. Hermetic Initialization: BenchmarkRunner derives the benchmark name (attention), generates run_id, and calls StoragePathManager.resolve_run_dir(). The directories results/benchmarks/attention/runs/<run_id>/ and tensorboard/ are created.
  5. Telemetry & Tracking Binding: ExperimentTracker initializes LocalTracker pointing to runs/<run_id>/ and TensorBoardTracker pointing to runs/<run_id>/tensorboard/.
  6. Provenance Capture: Hardware telemetry (pynvml), git status, and python environment are inspected and written immediately to manifest.json.
  7. Suite Execution: The registered benchmark class (AttentionBenchmark) executes through the autotuning matrix. Iteration results are dispatched in real-time to ExperimentTracker.log_metric() and written to metrics.jsonl.
  8. Summary & Serialization: BenchmarkSummaryGenerator computes aggregate statistics (P50, P90, P99, mean, std) and outputs summary.json, summary.csv, and benchmark_report.md.
  9. Ledger Synchronization: SQLiteLedgerBackend inserts the execution summary into results/master_ledger.sqlite and links the foreign key to the run directory.
  10. Console Presentation: A formatted ANSI terminal table displays benchmark achievements, run directory paths, and tensorboard visualization commands.

docs.title: 7.1 Comprehensive File Elimination Matrix (Root benchmarks/ Deletion)

docs.text:
1. Author neuralops/config/benchmark_schema.py:
  2. Define HardwareExecutionTarget, BenchmarkMetricsConfig, AttentionSweepConfig, and BenchmarkRunConfig.
  3. Implement strict field validations, numerical limits, and path checks.
  4. Author neuralops/config/loader.py:
  5. Provide load_benchmark_config(path: str | Path) -> BenchmarkRunConfig.
  6. Support environment variable interpolation (${CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES:-0}) and dict override merging.
  7. Check-in Default Benchmark Presets:
  8. neuralops/config/templates/benchmarks/attention_standard.yaml
  9. neuralops/config/templates/benchmarks/compression_standard.yaml
  10. neuralops/config/templates/benchmarks/e2e_serving_qwen.yaml

docs.title: 8.2 Phase 2: Per-Run Storage & Tracking Engine Binding
docs.text:
1. Implement neuralops/benchmarks/core/paths.py:
  2. Path resolution logic guaranteeing the hermetic pattern: results/benchmarks/<benchmark_name>/runs/<run_id>/.
  3. Symlink creation for latest -> runs/<run_id>.
  4. Build Hardware Telemetry & Manifest Generator:
  5. Implement neuralops/benchmarks/telemetry/hardware.py using NVML for GPU hardware metadata and /proc/cpuinfo / psutil for host hardware.
  6. Implement neuralops/benchmarks/telemetry/manifest.py to freeze git SHA, diff hash, Python dependencies, and command line arguments.
  7. Bind ExperimentTracker:
  8. Update BenchmarkRunner to initialize ExperimentTracker with paths rooted in the isolated run directory.
  9. Ensure LocalTracker writes metrics.jsonl and TensorBoardTracker logs events to tensorboard/.

docs.title: 8.3 Phase 3: Modular Benchmark Suites & Registry
docs.text:
1. Author neuralops/benchmarks/core/base.py:
  2. Define abstract class AbstractBaseBenchmark(ABC) requiring setup(), run_iteration(), teardown(), and generate_summary().
  3. Implement Benchmark Suites:
  4. AttentionBenchmark: Comprehensive sweep across the 131 canonical attentions, batch sizes, sequence lengths, and dtypes.
  5. CompressionBenchmark: Evaluation across the 72 compressors, measuring compression ratio, parameter reduction, and recovery retention.
  6. CudaKernelBenchmark & TritonKernelBenchmark: Microbenchmarking native operators against hardware rooflines.
  7. ServingBenchmark: vLLM / SGLang prefix caching and PagedAttention throughput evaluation.
  8. NeedleInAHaystackBenchmark: Long-context retrieval accuracy from 1k to 32k tokens.
  9. Register All Suites:
  10. Decorate each suite with @register_benchmark("name") in neuralops/benchmarks/core/registry.py.

docs.title: 8.4 Phase 4: Unified CLI Wiring (neuralops benchmark)
docs.text:
1. Implement neuralops/cli/bench_cmd.py:
  2. Register commands run, list, show, compare, export.
  3. Wire arguments and connect to BenchmarkRunner.
  4. Central Dispatcher Integration:
  5. Update neuralops/cli/main.py to include add_benchmark_parser(subparsers).
  6. Enable direct CLI invocation: neuralops benchmark list --suites.

docs.title: 8.5 Phase 5: Safe Deletion of Root benchmarks/ & Verification
docs.text:
1. Legacy Result Ingestion:
  2. Parse any un-indexed CSV/JSON files in root benchmarks/results/ and record historical runs into results/master_ledger.sqlite.
  3. Clean Removal:
  4. Issue git rm -r benchmarks/ to purge the legacy non-packaged directory from version control.
  5. Verification:
  6. Run AST dead-code audit: python3 scripts/utils/audit_dead_code.py.
  7. Run lint checker: ruff check neuralops/config neuralops/benchmarks neuralops/tracking neuralops/cli.
  8. Validate canonical registry counts: 131 attentions, 72 compressors, 26 Triton kernel modules, 110 CUDA modules.

docs.title: 9. Verification & Quality Assurance Gates
docs.text: To guarantee that the refactored architecture adheres strictly to repository invariants, the following automated verification gates must pass:

docs.title: 9.1 Static Code Quality & Style Gate
docs.text:
All new and modified files must pass Ruff linting with zero warnings:

# Target static verification command
./.venv/bin/ruff check \
    neuralops/config/benchmark_schema.py \
    neuralops/config/loader.py \
    neuralops/benchmarks/core/ \
    neuralops/benchmarks/suites/ \
    neuralops/cli/bench_cmd.py

docs.title: 9.2 AST Registry & Invariant Integrity Check
docs.text:
Repository counts must strictly match the canonical invariants outlined in AGENTS.md §8: - ATTENTION_REGISTRY: Exactly 131 keys. - COMPRESSOR_REGISTRY: Exactly 72 keys. - neuralops/core/triton_kernels/: Exactly 26 canonical modules. - neuralops.kernels.list_cuda_kernels(): Exactly 110 unique modules, 114 native implementations.

Verification command: 

python3 scripts/utils/audit_dead_code.py
python3 scripts/audit_readme_consistency.py

docs.title: 9.3 SQLite Master Ledger Schema Verification
docs.text:
The master database results/master_ledger.sqlite must pass schema validation and foreign key constraints:

PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON;
PRAGMA integrity_check;

-- Verify benchmark_runs table exists and has proper indexing
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM benchmark_runs;

docs.title: 9.4 Hermetic Directory Isolation Test
docs.text: A dedicated unit test (tests/benchmarks/test_hermetic_storage.py) must verify that: 1. Executing a dry-run benchmark produces an isolated directory structure matching results/benchmarks/<suite>/runs/<run_id>/. 2. No files are written directly into the root results/ folder or working directory. 3. All seven standard run artifacts (config_resolved.yaml, manifest.json, metrics.jsonl, summary.json, summary.csv, benchmark_report.md, stdout_stderr.log) are present and non-empty. 4. latest symlink correctly resolves to the newly created run directory.

docs.title: 10. Conclusion & Architectural Recommendation
docs.text:
The blueprint documented herein establishes a scalable, reproducible, and mathematically rigorous benchmarking ecosystem for NeuralOps. By unifying declarative configuration, hermetic per-run filesystem isolation, zero-overhead telemetry tracking, and master SQLite ledger synchronization under a single CLI interface (neuralops benchmark), the repository eliminates technical debt, prevents data collisions, and guarantees 100% empirical reproducibility across both local research workstations and the Sharif University HPC cluster.

The complete elimination of the redundant root benchmarks/ directory simplifies repository navigation, aligns the project with standard enterprise Python packaging principles, and enforces that all benchmark execution routes through audited, version-controlled library code.

docs.title: Appendix A: Complete Benchmark Run Configuration Schema Reference
docs.text:
Below is the complete, production-ready source code for neuralops/config/benchmark_schema.py:

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# Copyright (c) 2024-2026, Taha Majlesi
#
# This source code is licensed under the MIT license found in the
# LICENSE file in the root directory of this source tree.
# For a list of all contributors, visit:
#   https://github.com/tahamajs/NeuralOps/graphs/contributors
"""
Declarative Pydantic configuration schemas for empirical benchmarking suites.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Dict, List, Literal, Optional
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, field_validator


class HardwareExecutionTarget(BaseModel):
    """Execution hardware and backend constraints."""
    device: str = Field(
        default="cuda:0",
        description="Target compute device string ('cuda:0', 'cpu', 'mps')"
    )
    backend_preference: Literal["auto", "cuda", "triton", "torch"] = Field(
        default="auto",
        description="Target backend for 3-level fallback hierarchy"
    )
    enforce_deterministic: bool = Field(
        default=False,
        description="Enforce deterministic CUDA execution algorithms"
    )
    allow_tf32: bool = Field(
        default=True,
        description="Allow TensorFloat-32 on Ampere, Ada Lovelace, and Hopper architectures"
    )


class TrackingSubsystemConfig(BaseModel):
    """Experiment tracking and telemetry recording configuration."""
    enabled: bool = Field(
        default=True,
        description="Master switch for experiment tracking"
    )
    enable_tensorboard: bool = Field(
        default=True,
        description="Write SummaryWriter event files into run directory"
    )
    enable_local_jsonl: bool = Field(
        default=True,
        description="Log individual iteration metrics to metrics.jsonl"
    )
    log_frequency_steps: int = Field(
        default=1,
        ge=1,
        description="Metric logging interval in benchmark iterations"
    )
    capture_gpu_telemetry: bool = Field(
        default=True,
        description="Record GPU temperature, power, clock frequencies, and memory utilization"
    )


class AttentionSweepParameters(BaseModel):
    """Grid sweep parameters for attention mechanism benchmarking."""
    mechanisms: List[str] = Field(
        default=["all"],
        description="List of attention keys or ['all'] to sweep canonical 131 registry"
    )
    batch_sizes: List[int] = Field(
        default=[1, 4, 16],
        description="Batch sizes to evaluate"
    )
    sequence_lengths: List[int] = Field(
        default=[512, 1024, 2048, 4096, 8192],
        description="Sequence length token counts"
    )
    head_dimensions: List[int] = Field(
        default=[64, 128],
        description="Head dimensions (d_k / d_v)"
    )
    num_heads: int = Field(
        default=32,
        ge=1,
        description="Number of query attention heads"
    )
    dtypes: List[Literal["fp16", "bf16", "fp32"]] = Field(
        default=["fp16", "bf16"],
        description="Numerical precision data types to evaluate"
    )
    causal_modes: List[bool] = Field(
        default=[True, False],
        description="Evaluate causal autoregressive masking and bidirectional masking"
    )
    warmup_iterations: int = Field(
        default=10,
        ge=1,
        description="Number of warmup iterations prior to timing measurement"
    )
    benchmark_iterations: int = Field(
        default=50,
        ge=5,
        description="Number of active timed iterations"
    )

    @field_validator("batch_sizes", "sequence_lengths", "head_dimensions")
    @classmethod
    def validate_positive_integers(cls, v: List[int]) -> List[int]:
        if not v or any(x <= 0 for x in v):
            raise ValueError("All dimensions must be strictly positive integers.")
        return sorted(v)


class BenchmarkRunConfig(BaseModel):
    """Complete root configuration model for a single benchmark execution."""
    version: str = Field(
        default="1.0.0",
        description="Configuration schema specification version"
    )
    benchmark_suite: Literal[
        "attention",
        "compression",
        "cuda_ops",
        "triton_ops",
        "e2e_serving",
        "niah",
        "roofline"
    ] = Field(
        ...,
        description="Canonical benchmark suite name"
    )
    description: Optional[str] = Field(
        default=None,
        description="Human-readable description of benchmark purpose"
    )
    tag: Optional[str] = Field(
        default=None,
        description="Categorization tag for filtering runs in master SQLite database"
    )
    output_root_directory: Path = Field(
        default=Path("results/benchmarks"),
        description="Base filesystem root where benchmark run subdirectories will be created"
    )
    hardware: HardwareExecutionTarget = Field(
        default_factory=HardwareExecutionTarget,
        description="Hardware execution parameters"
    )
    tracking: TrackingSubsystemConfig = Field(
        default_factory=TrackingSubsystemConfig,
        description="Experiment tracking parameters"
    )
    attention_sweep: Optional[AttentionSweepParameters] = Field(
        default=None,
        description="Configuration parameters for attention sweep benchmark"
    )
    custom_parameters: Dict[str, Any] = Field(
        default_factory=dict,
        description="Arbitrary additional suite-specific parameters"
    )

docs.text:
Below is the verified textual output of running neuralops benchmark --help:

usage: neuralops benchmark [-h] {run,list,show,compare,export} ...

  {run,list,show,compare,export}
