docs.title: Feature 1: Persistent Model/Text Context Header
docs.text: The top bar always shows: "Model: BERT-base-uncased | Attention: Galerkin (rank=64) | Text: 'The quick brown fox...' | Layer 5, Head 7". This contextual information persists across all views so the researcher never loses track. Click any element to change it — the entire dashboard updates reactively.

docs.title: Feature 2: Quick-Switch Model Selector
docs.text: A dropdown that loads any registered attention type from your attention registry (Galerkin, TLinFormer, PADRe, Spectraformer, RPC, FUSIONATTN, etc.). Switching instantly re‑renders all visualizations. Models can be loaded from HuggingFace Hub, your model_versioning registry, or uploaded directly. This directly parallels Neuronpedia's approach: "you can now host Neuronpedia yourself, with your own model and data, on your own cloud or hardware".

docs.title: Feature 3: Breadcrumb Navigation with History
docs.text: A breadcrumb trail: Home > Attention Lab > BERT-base > Layer 5 > Head 7. Each segment is clickable. A history panel (like browser history) shows the last 20 attention explorations with timestamps, allowing quick backtracking.

docs.title: Feature 4: Head View (BertViz‑Style Interactive Heatmap)
docs.text: An interactive attention matrix where each cell (query_token, key_token) is colored by attention weight. Hover reveals exact values; click selects a query token to highlight its attention pattern. The design follows BertViz: "an interactive tool for visualizing attention in Transformer language models such as BERT, GPT2, or T5". Includes zoom, pan, and token highlighting.

docs.title: Feature 5: Model View (Bird's‑Eye Across All Layers × Heads)
docs.text: A compact grid where each attention head is a colored square. Size = head importance, Color = head diversity (or specialization type). Hover to preview the attention pattern; click to zoom into the Head View. This provides the "overview that summarizes the roles of different attention heads" similar to Dodrio's design.

docs.title: Feature 6: 3D Attention Topology Map (React Three Fiber)
docs.text: An immersive 3D scene where tokens are spheres positioned via t‑SNE/UMAP of hidden states, and attention connections are curved tubes with thickness proportional to weight. Users can fly through the model using WASD/mouse. Inspired by TensorSpace and the Reddit "Planet Neuron" project. Helios-Web demonstrates the feasibility: "GPU-based rendering for real-time visualization and interactive analysis of massive-scale networks and high-dimensional embeddings".

docs.title: Feature 7: Sankey Attention Flow Diagram
docs.text: A Sankey diagram showing information flow: Input Tokens → Layer 1 Heads → Layer 2 Heads → … → Output. Flow width = attention magnitude. The Transformer Explainer "adopts the Sankey diagram visual design, inspired by recent work viewing Transformers as dynamical systems, emphasizing how input data flows through model components".

docs.title: Feature 8: Query/Key Joint Embedding Explorer (AttentionViz‑Style)
docs.text: A scatter plot of Q and K vectors projected via PCA/t‑SNE/UMAP (user‑selectable). Color by token position or attention magnitude. Brushing and linking: select a region of Q vectors → highlights corresponding K vectors → shows attention weights in the heatmap. AttentionViz (VIS 2023) "creates a joint embedding of query and key vectors, enabling analysis of global patterns across multiple input sequences."

docs.title: Feature 9: Token‑by‑Token Generation Animation
docs.text: For autoregressive models, animate how attention patterns evolve as each new token is generated. A timeline slider controls generation steps. Semantic Pathway (IEEE VIS 2025) "integrates layerwise semantic trajectories, attention overlays, and output probability views into a unified interface, enabling users to trace how meaning accumulates and decisions emerge during generation".

docs.title: Feature 10: Live LaTeX Equation Renderer with Animated Steps
docs.text: The attention formula Attention(Q,K,V) = softmax(QK^T/√d_k)V is rendered in LaTeX. Each variable highlights as the user hovers over the corresponding visualization element. Click any part to see animated step‑by‑step computation: (1) Q×K^T matrix multiplication, (2) Scale by √d_k, (3) Softmax row‑by‑row, (4) Multiply by V. All animations are scrubbable (pause, rewind, slow‑motion). The Transformer Explainer similarly "explains how Transformer-based models like GPT work" through interactive visualization.

docs.title: Feature 11: Numerical Value Inspector
docs.text: Below the formula, a live table showing the actual numerical values at each computation step for the currently hovered token pair. Example: Q₃ · K₇ = 0.847 → scale → 0.106 → softmax → 0.023 → ×V₇ → .... Users can export these values as CSV for external analysis.

docs.title: Feature 12: Architecture Comparison Math Diff
docs.text: When comparing two attention mechanisms (e.g., Standard MHA vs. Galerkin), the math panel shows both formulas side‑by‑side, highlighting where they differ. The Galerkin formula shows the random sketching matrix S and the projection step, visually contrasted with standard softmax.

docs.title: Feature 13: Unified Layer/Head/Input Selector
docs.text: Sliders for layer and head selection with live preview thumbnails that update as you slide. A text input where users can type or paste any text to analyze. A model selector dropdown populated from your attention registry and HuggingFace Hub integration.

docs.title: Feature 14: "Train with This Attention" Button
docs.text: One click opens the experiment launcher pre‑filled with: the current model, attention type, layer/head configuration, and sample text. Connects directly to your experiment and launcher apps. This creates the closed loop: explore → experiment → verify.

docs.title: Feature 15: "Create Note" / "Generate Report" / "Export to Paper"
docs.text: Three buttons that connect the attention analysis to your platform: - Create Note: Saves the current visualization + text + stats as a ResearcherNote - Generate Report: Auto‑generates a rich Markdown report with embedded SVGs, statistics, and discussion - Export to Paper: Opens the LaTeX editor with a pre‑written Methods section and embedded figures

docs.title: Feature 16: Head Importance × Stability × Similarity 3D Scatter
docs.text: A 3D scatter plot where each point is an attention head, positioned by: X = Importance (output change when ablated), Y = Stability (consistency across inputs), Z = Similarity (redundancy with other heads). Color = head type (positional/semantic/delimiter). Click a point to zoom into that head. BHPVAS proposes exactly these three criteria for head evaluation.

docs.title: Feature 17: Head Clustering Dendrogram
docs.text: Hierarchical clustering of all heads based on attention pattern similarity. The dendrogram is interactive — click a branch to see the prototypical pattern for that cluster. Heads are auto‑labeled: "Positional Cluster," "Semantic Cluster," "Delimiter Cluster," "Induction Head Cluster."

docs.title: Feature 18: Logit Lens Prediction Timeline
docs.text: A scrubber showing how the model's prediction evolves across layers. Each layer shows a word cloud of top‑k predictions sized by probability. "The logit lens directly reads out the model's implicit prediction at each layer" without extra machinery. Users can click any layer to see which attention heads contributed most to that prediction.

docs.title: Feature 19: Attention Pattern Evolution Time‑Lapse
docs.text: For training runs, a time‑lapse animation showing how attention patterns evolve from epoch 0 to final. Users can scrub through training time with a slider. The system highlights when each head "crystallizes" into its final pattern and shows head importance curves.

docs.title: Feature 20: Semantic Pathway Cross‑Layer Trajectories
docs.text: A 2D plot (t‑SNE/UMAP) where each token is tracked across layers. Trajectories connect the same token at different layers, showing how meaning evolves. Users can see which tokens' representations are most "influenced" by attention to other tokens.

docs.title: Feature 21: Head Ablation Laboratory
docs.text: Toggle individual heads on/off with a switch. See before/after predictions in real time. Measure impact: "Ablating Head 7 changes the output probability by 12.3%." Chain ablations: disable multiple heads and observe compound effects. Export the ablation configuration as a pruning recipe → directly connected to your compression pipeline.

docs.title: Feature 22: Anthropic‑Style Circuit Tracer
docs.text: Visualize the QK circuit (what a head "looks for" in keys) and the OV circuit (what a head "writes" to the output). Each circuit is shown as an attribution graph with nodes (features) and edges (weights). Anthropic's open‑source tools "enable users to explore, annotate, and share attribution graphs seamlessly".

docs.title: Feature 23: Dodrio‑Style Linguistic Annotation Overlay
docs.text: Toggle linguistic annotations on top of the attention heatmap: syntactic dependencies, semantic role labels, coreference chains, part‑of‑speech coloring. Dodrio "tightly integrates an overview that summarizes the roles of different attention heads, and detailed views that help users compare attention weights with the syntactic structure and semantic information in the input text."

docs.title: Feature 24: Causal Tracing — Knockout Experiment
docs.text: Select a source token and target token, then "knock out" attention between them at specific layers. See how the model's prediction changes. The system visualizes a causal graph showing which paths are critical for each prediction.

docs.title: Feature 25: Multi‑Dimensional Reaction System
docs.text: React to attention patterns with context‑rich signals: 🔬 Interesting, ⚡ Efficient, 🎯 Specialized, 🔄 Redundant, 🧩 Novel. Reactions aggregate into a "pattern quality score" displayed on every attention visualization and feed into the recommendation engine.

docs.title: Feature 26: Attention Arena — Blind Pairwise Voting (ComparIA‑Style)
docs.text: Two attention visualizations shown side‑by‑side, anonymized (hiding which model/head produced them). Users vote on "Which pattern is more interpretable?" or "Which better captures syntax?" Votes generate Elo ratings for attention patterns. The ComparIA platform "users interact with two anonymous models simultaneously, vote on the better response, and subsequently reveal the models' identities" — generating "high-quality preference datasets."

docs.title: Feature 27: Fork & Remix — Lineage Tracking
docs.text: Every published attention visualization can be forked by another researcher. The fork maintains lineage tracking: "Alice created → Bob forked and added Layer 5 → Carol forked and changed to Galerkin attention." The lineage is visualized as a tree/graph on every post. Neuronpedia "fully supports uploading your own graphs, regardless of whether or not you use the circuit-tracer library, your own library, or different models".

docs.title: Feature 28: Attention Challenge Creator & Leaderboard
docs.text: Users create challenges ("Find the most interesting pattern in BERT-base Layer 3"), the community submits and votes, winners earn badges and platform credits. Connected to your leaderboards and gpu_reputation infrastructure.

docs.title: Feature 29: Inline Pattern Discussion Threads
docs.text: Every attention pattern has threaded discussions anchored to specific elements: per‑head, per‑token‑pair, per‑layer. Supports @mentions, LaTeX equations, and embedded attention SVGs. Powered by your community Q&A infrastructure.

docs.title: Feature 30: One‑Click Share Cards
docs.text: Export any attention visualization as a beautiful share card optimized for Twitter/X, LinkedIn, and Reddit. Includes the heatmap, key statistics, model info, a QR code linking back to the interactive dashboard, and the researcher's attribution.

docs.title: Feature 31: Attention Pattern Collections (Curated Galleries)
docs.text: Users create themed collections ("Positional Heads Gallery," "Induction Head Candidates"). Collections can be public, team, or private. Each collection has its own discussion thread. Collections can be forked. Top collections appear on a "Trending Collections" leaderboard.

docs.title: Feature 32: Embed Anywhere Widget
docs.text: Every attention pattern has an embeddable interactive widget (like YouTube embeds). Researchers paste a snippet into personal websites, blogs, or paper supplementary materials. Widget analytics flow back to the platform.

docs.title: Feature 33: Attention Portfolio — Researcher Showcase
docs.text: Every researcher has a public portfolio showing: published patterns, collections curated, challenges won, reputation score, activity graph, expertise tags. The portfolio is embeddable on personal websites and serves as a professional credential.

docs.title: Feature 34: XP & Progression Tiers (AnveshanaAI‑Style)
docs.text: A tiered progression system: Novice Explorer → Pattern Scout → Head Hunter → Attention Sage → Grandmaster. Users earn XP for: viewing patterns, publishing posts, winning challenges, providing insightful comments, participating in blind voting. AnveshanaAI demonstrates this approach: "learners are presented with a personalized dashboard featuring streaks, levels, badges, and structured navigation across domains".

docs.title: Feature 35: Daily Attention Puzzle (Habit‑Forming)
docs.text: A daily mini‑challenge: "Monday: Guess the Head Type," "Tuesday: Spot the Difference," "Wednesday: Match the Model." Users build streaks (consecutive days played), displayed prominently on their profile.

docs.title: Feature 36: Badge System (25+ Badges)
docs.text: Badges across categories: Discovery (First Pattern, 10th Head Type, Induction Head Finder), Community (First Comment, 100th Star, Curator), Expertise (Positional Expert, Semantic Expert), Competition (Challenge Winner, Arena Veteran, Top 10).

docs.title: Feature 37: Leaderboards — Weekly, Monthly, All‑Time
docs.text: Multiple leaderboards: Top Pattern Discoverers, Top Challengers, Top Curators, Top Reviewers. Connected to your leaderboards infrastructure.

docs.title: Feature 38: Bounty Board — Paid Analysis Requests
docs.text: Researchers or companies post bounties for specific attention analysis tasks ("Analyze attention patterns of our model — $50"). Bounties are funded with platform credits or crypto. Yupp demonstrates this model: "diverse user feedback flows freely under blockchain and cryptocurrency economic incentives."

docs.title: Feature 39: Attention‑to‑Experiment Pipeline
docs.text: Every pattern has a "Train with This" button → opens experiment launcher pre‑filled with model, attention type, and sample text. After training, actual patterns are compared with the original visualization.

docs.title: Feature 40: Attention Pattern Knowledge Graph Navigator
docs.text: Every pattern is a node connected to: the model, the experiment, notes, papers, community discussions, collections, and researchers. The graph is visualized as an interactive D3 force‑directed graph.

docs.title: Feature 41: Attention API (Programmatic Access)
docs.text: A public REST API and Python SDK allowing AI agents to query attention patterns, automated analysis pipelines, third‑party embedding, and bulk export. Neuronpedia provides "a suite of free APIs/tools that accelerate white-box understanding and experimentation of neural networks".

docs.title: Feature 42: Collaborative Attention Workshop (Multi‑User)
docs.text: Multiple researchers explore attention together in real time with shared view state, cursor presence, annotation pins, threaded discussion, and session recording. Uses your existing WebSocket/Channels infrastructure.

docs.title: Feature 43: Polis‑Style Opinion Mapping
docs.text: For controversial topics, users submit statements and vote agree/disagree. The system uses PCA and k‑means to cluster participants and visualize consensus maps.

docs.title: Feature 44: Attention‑Based Prompt Engineering Tool
docs.text: Highlight which tokens receive the most attention, identify "attention sinks," compare prompts A/B, and get suggestions for improvement based on attention analysis.

docs.title: Feature 45: Model Diff — Cross‑Architecture Comparison
docs.text: Load attention patterns from any architecture (MHA, Galerkin, LinFormer, PADRe, etc.) for the same input and see divergence heatmaps, JSD scores, and head‑by‑head similarity matrices.

docs.title: Feature 46: Universal Attention Scoring
docs.text: Every pattern scored on standardized dimensions (Interpretability, Specialization, Efficiency, Stability) enabling cross‑architecture comparison.

docs.title: Feature 47: Auto‑Generated Research Paper Section
docs.text: One click generates a paper section with: Methods, Results (embedded visualizations), Discussion (from community annotations), and References (from linked papers). Opens in your paper LaTeX editor.

docs.title: Feature 48: Particle Flow Attention Visualizer
docs.text: Attention connections rendered as flowing particles (like game particle systems). Density = weight, speed = confidence, color = head identity. Particles leave glow trails. Users can freeze the flow to inspect the static pattern.

docs.title: Feature 49: Attention Sonification
docs.text: Each head has a unique sound signature: high attention = high pitch, diffuse = white noise, positional head = rhythmic, semantic head = melodic. Users can "listen" to the model thinking. Particularly powerful for accessibility.

docs.title: Feature 50: Attention Style Transfer Gallery
docs.text: Same data rendered in multiple artistic styles: Heatmap, Sankey, Arc diagram, Chord diagram, Hive plot, 3D particle flow, Minimalist, Cyberpunk neon. Export any style as SVG/PNG/MP4.

docs.title: 🧠 Complete Attention Visualization Suite — React + 3D + Interactive
docs.text:
Based on extensive research into BertViz (3 views), AttentionViz (joint Q/K embeddings), Transformer Explainer (interactive web), OpenAI's Transformer Debugger, and HeadVis, here is a complete, production‑ready visualization suite.

I'll provide 6 distinct visualization views, a unified dashboard page, and 3D attention flow using React Three Fiber.

// utils/colorScales.ts
export const ATTENTION_COLORS = {
  high: '#ff6b6b',
  medium: '#ffa94d',
  low: '#4ecdc4',
  zero: '#1e293b',
  background: '#0f172a',
  tokenText: '#e2e8f0',
  gridLines: '#334155',
  headColors: [
    '#ff6b6b', '#ffa94d', '#ffd43b', '#69db7c', '#4ecdc4',
    '#74c0fc', '#748ffc', '#9775fa', '#f06595', '#20c997',
    '#fcc419', '#339af0',
  ],
};

export const attentionColorScale = (value: number): string => {
  if (value <= 0) return ATTENTION_COLORS.zero;
  if (value < 0.1) return ATTENTION_COLORS.low;
  if (value < 0.3) return ATTENTION_COLORS.medium;
  return ATTENTION_COLORS.high;
};

export const interpolateAttention = (value: number): string => {
  const t = Math.min(1, Math.max(0, value));
  const r = Math.round(30 + t * 225);
  const g = Math.round(40 + t * 60);
  const b = Math.round(60 + t * 40);
  return `rgb(${r},${g},${b})`;
};

docs.title: 2. Attention Calculations (utils/attentionCalculations.ts)
docs.text:
// utils/attentionCalculations.ts

export interface AttentionData {
  tokens: string[];
  layers: LayerAttention[];
}

export interface LayerAttention {
  layerIndex: number;
  heads: HeadAttention[];
}

export interface HeadAttention {
  headIndex: number;
  attentionMatrix: number[][]; // [query][key]
}

/**
 * Compute entropy of attention distribution for a head.
 * High entropy = diffuse attention (attending to many tokens).
 * Low entropy = focused attention (attending to few tokens).
 */
export const computeAttentionEntropy = (matrix: number[][]): number => {
  let totalEntropy = 0;
  for (const row of matrix) {
    let rowEntropy = 0;
    for (const v of row) {
      if (v > 1e-9) rowEntropy -= v * Math.log2(v);
    }
    totalEntropy += rowEntropy;
  }
  return totalEntropy / matrix.length;
};

/**
 * Compute head importance score (mean of max attention weights).
 */
export const computeHeadImportance = (matrix: number[][]): number => {
  let sum = 0;
  for (const row of matrix) {
    sum += Math.max(...row);
  }
  return sum / matrix.length;
};

/**
 * Compute head diversity — how different is this head's pattern from others?
 */
export const computeHeadDiversity = (
  matrix: number[][],
  allMatrices: number[][][]
): number => {
  const flat = matrix.flat();
  let totalDistance = 0;
  for (const other of allMatrices) {
    const otherFlat = other.flat();
    let dist = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i < flat.length; i++) {
      dist += Math.abs(flat[i] - otherFlat[i]);
    }
    totalDistance += dist / flat.length;
  }
  return totalDistance / allMatrices.length;
};

/**
 * Compute layer-to-layer attention flow (for flow visualization).
 * Returns a matrix where [i][j] = average attention from layer i to layer j.
 */
export const computeLayerFlow = (data: AttentionData): number[][] => {
  const nLayers = data.layers.length;
  const flow: number[][] = Array.from({ length: nLayers }, () =>
    Array(nLayers).fill(0)
  );
  for (const layer of data.layers) {
    for (const head of layer.heads) {
      for (let i = 0; i < head.attentionMatrix.length; i++) {
        for (let j = 0; j < head.attentionMatrix[i].length; j++) {
          flow[layer.layerIndex][layer.layerIndex] +=
            head.attentionMatrix[i][j];
        }
      }
    }
  }
  // Normalize
  for (let i = 0; i < nLayers; i++) {
    const total = flow[i].reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0) || 1;
    for (let j = 0; j < nLayers; j++) flow[i][j] /= total;
  }
  return flow;
};

/**
 * Generate sample attention data for demo purposes.
 */
export const generateDemoData = (
  tokens: string[],
  numLayers: number,
  numHeads: number
): AttentionData => {
  const layers: LayerAttention[] = [];
  for (let l = 0; l < numLayers; l++) {
    const heads: HeadAttention[] = [];
    for (let h = 0; h < numHeads; h++) {
      const matrix: number[][] = [];
      for (let i = 0; i < tokens.length; i++) {
        const row: number[] = [];
        let remaining = 1;
        for (let j = 0; j < tokens.length - 1; j++) {
          const raw = Math.random() * remaining;
          row.push(raw);
          remaining -= raw;
        }
        row.push(remaining);
        matrix.push(row);
      }
      heads.push({ headIndex: h, attentionMatrix: matrix });
    }
    layers.push({ layerIndex: l, heads });
  }
  return { tokens, layers };
};

// hooks/useAttentionData.ts
import { useState, useEffect, useCallback } from 'react';
import api from '../../api/client';

interface UseAttentionDataProps {
  runId?: string;
  sampleText?: string;
  demo?: boolean;
  numLayers?: number;
  numHeads?: number;
}

export const useAttentionData = ({
  runId,
  sampleText,
  demo = false,
  numLayers = 6,
  numHeads = 12,
}: UseAttentionDataProps) => {
  const [data, setData] = useState<any>(null);
  const [loading, setLoading] = useState(true);
  const [error, setError] = useState<string | null>(null);

  const fetchData = useCallback(async () => {
    if (demo) {
      const { generateDemoData } = await import(
        '../utils/attentionCalculations'
      );
      const tokens = (sampleText || 'The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog').split(' ');
      setData(generateDemoData(tokens, numLayers, numHeads));
      setLoading(false);
      return;
    }
    try {
      const resp = await api.post('/api/experiments/attention/', {
        run_id: runId,
        text: sampleText,
      });
      setData(resp.data);
    } catch (e: any) {
      setError(e.message);
    } finally {
      setLoading(false);
    }
  }, [runId, sampleText, demo, numLayers, numHeads]);

  useEffect(() => {
    fetchData();
  }, [fetchData]);

  return { data, loading, error, refetch: fetchData };
};

// AttentionDashboard.tsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { motion, AnimatePresence } from 'framer-motion';
import {
  Brain, Grid3X3, Network, Flame, GitBranch, Box,
  Layers, Activity, Sliders,
} from 'lucide-react';
import HeadView from './views/HeadView';
import ModelView from './views/ModelView';
import AttentionHeatmap from './views/AttentionHeatmap';
import QueryKeyJointView from './views/QueryKeyJointView';
import AttentionFlowView from './views/AttentionFlowView';
import Attention3DView from './views/Attention3DView';
import LayerSelector from './components/LayerSelector';
import AttentionStats from './components/AttentionStats';
import { useAttentionData } from '../hooks/useAttentionData';

const VIEWS = [
  { id: 'head', label: 'Head View', icon: Brain, desc: 'Individual attention head patterns' },
  { id: 'model', label: 'Model View', icon: Layers, desc: 'Bird\'s-eye across all layers & heads' },
  { id: 'heatmap', label: 'Heatmap', icon: Grid3X3, desc: 'Token-to-token attention matrix' },
  { id: 'qk', label: 'Q/K Joint', icon: GitBranch, desc: 'Query-Key embedding space (AttentionViz)' },
  { id: 'flow', label: 'Attention Flow', icon: Activity, desc: 'Layer-to-layer attention flow' },
  { id: '3d', label: '3D View', icon: Box, desc: 'Immersive 3D attention visualization' },
];

export default function AttentionDashboard() {
  const [activeView, setActiveView] = useState('head');
  const [selectedLayer, setSelectedLayer] = useState(0);
  const [selectedHead, setSelectedHead] = useState(0);
  const [sampleText, setSampleText] = useState(
    'The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog'
  );
  const [showStats, setShowStats] = useState(true);
  const [colorMode, setColorMode] = useState<'heat' | 'viridis' | 'blues'>('heat');

  const { data, loading, error, refetch } = useAttentionData({
    sampleText,
    demo: true,
    numLayers: 6,
    numHeads: 12,
  });

  const numLayers = data?.layers?.length || 0;
  const numHeads = data?.layers?.[0]?.heads?.length || 0;

  const ActiveView = {
    head: HeadView,
    model: ModelView,
    heatmap: AttentionHeatmap,
    qk: QueryKeyJointView,
    flow: AttentionFlowView,
    '3d': Attention3DView,
  }[activeView];

  return (
    <div className="min-h-screen bg-dark-bg text-white">
      {/* ── Header ─────────────────────────────────────────── */}
      <div className="sticky top-0 z-30 bg-dark-bg/95 backdrop-blur-xl border-b border-dark-border">
        <div className="max-w-[1600px] mx-auto px-6 py-4">
          <div className="flex items-center justify-between">
            <div>
              <h1 className="text-2xl font-bold bg-gradient-to-r from-neon-blue to-purple-400 bg-clip-text text-transparent">
                🧠 Attention Visualization Lab
              </h1>
              <p className="text-slate-400 text-sm mt-0.5">
                Explore transformer attention mechanisms interactively
              </p>
            </div>
            <div className="flex items-center gap-3">
              <input
                value={sampleText}
                onChange={(e) => setSampleText(e.target.value)}
                onKeyDown={(e) => e.key === 'Enter' && refetch()}
                placeholder="Enter text to analyze..."
                className="bg-white/5 border border-white/10 rounded-xl px-4 py-2 text-sm text-white w-80 focus:outline-none focus:border-neon-blue/50"
              />
              <button
                onClick={refetch}
                className="bg-neon-blue/90 hover:bg-neon-blue px-4 py-2 rounded-xl text-sm font-semibold transition-colors"
              >
                Analyze
              </button>
            </div>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div className="max-w-[1600px] mx-auto px-6 py-6 flex gap-6">
        {/* ── Sidebar ──────────────────────────────────────── */}
        <div className="w-64 shrink-0 space-y-4">
          {/* View selector */}
          <div className="glass p-3 space-y-1">
            <p className="text-[10px] font-bold text-slate-500 uppercase tracking-widest mb-2">
              Visualization Views
            </p>
            {VIEWS.map(({ id, label, icon: Icon }) => (
              <button
                key={id}
                onClick={() => setActiveView(id)}
                className={`w-full flex items-center gap-2 px-3 py-2 rounded-lg text-sm font-medium transition-all ${
                  activeView === id
                    ? 'bg-neon-blue/20 text-neon-blue border border-neon-blue/30'
                    : 'text-slate-400 hover:text-white hover:bg-white/5'
                }`}
              >
                <Icon size={16} />
                {label}
              </button>
            ))}
          </div>

          {/* Layer/Head selector */}
          <div className="glass p-3">
            <p className="text-[10px] font-bold text-slate-500 uppercase tracking-widest mb-3">
              Controls
            </p>
            <LayerSelector
              numLayers={numLayers}
              numHeads={numHeads}
              selectedLayer={selectedLayer}
              selectedHead={selectedHead}
              onLayerChange={setSelectedLayer}
              onHeadChange={setSelectedHead}
              colorMode={colorMode}
              onColorModeChange={setColorMode}
            />
          </div>

          {/* Stats panel */}
          <div className="glass p-3">
            <div className="flex items-center justify-between mb-2">
              <p className="text-[10px] font-bold text-slate-500 uppercase tracking-widest">
                Statistics
              </p>
              <button
                onClick={() => setShowStats(!showStats)}
                className="text-slate-500 hover:text-white"
              >
                <Sliders size={14} />
              </button>
            </div>
            {showStats && data && (
              <AttentionStats
                data={data}
                selectedLayer={selectedLayer}
                selectedHead={selectedHead}
              />
            )}
          </div>
        </div>

        {/* ── Main Content ─────────────────────────────────── */}
        <div className="flex-1 min-w-0">
          <AnimatePresence mode="wait">
            <motion.div
              key={activeView}
              initial={{ opacity: 0, y: 10 }}
              animate={{ opacity: 1, y: 0 }}
              exit={{ opacity: 0, y: -10 }}
              transition={{ duration: 0.2 }}
            >
              {loading ? (
                <div className="glass p-12 text-center">
                  <div className="w-8 h-8 border-2 border-neon-blue/30 border-t-neon-blue rounded-full animate-spin mx-auto mb-3" />
                  <p className="text-slate-400">Loading attention data...</p>
                </div>
              ) : error ? (
                <div className="glass p-12 text-center">
                  <p className="text-red-400">{error}</p>
                  <button
                    onClick={refetch}
                    className="mt-3 bg-neon-blue/20 text-neon-blue px-4 py-2 rounded-lg text-sm"
                  >
                    Retry
                  </button>
                </div>
              ) : (
                <ActiveView
                  data={data}
                  selectedLayer={selectedLayer}
                  selectedHead={selectedHead}
                  colorMode={colorMode}
                  onLayerChange={setSelectedLayer}
                  onHeadChange={setSelectedHead}
                />
              )}
            </motion.div>
          </AnimatePresence>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}

// views/HeadView.tsx
import React, { useMemo, useState, useCallback } from 'react';
import { motion } from 'framer-motion';
import { ZoomIn, ZoomOut, RotateCcw, Download } from 'lucide-react';

interface HeadViewProps {
  data: any;
  selectedLayer: number;
  selectedHead: number;
  colorMode: string;
  onLayerChange: (l: number) => void;
  onHeadChange: (h: number) => void;
}

export default function HeadView({
  data,
  selectedLayer,
  selectedHead,
  colorMode,
  onLayerChange,
  onHeadChange,
}: HeadViewProps) {
  const [zoomLevel, setZoomLevel] = useState(1);
  const [hoveredCell, setHoveredCell] = useState<{
    query: number;
    key: number;
  } | null>(null);
  const [selectedQuery, setSelectedQuery] = useState<number | null>(null);

  const layer = data?.layers?.[selectedLayer];
  const head = layer?.heads?.[selectedHead];
  const tokens = data?.tokens || [];
  const matrix = head?.attentionMatrix || [];

  const cellSize = Math.max(28, Math.min(48, 600 / tokens.length));
  const totalWidth = tokens.length * cellSize;

  const getColor = useCallback(
    (value: number) => {
      const t = Math.min(1, Math.max(0, value));
      if (colorMode === 'blues') {
        return `rgba(59, 130, 246, ${t})`;
      }
      if (colorMode === 'viridis') {
        const r = Math.round(68 + t * 163);
        const g = Math.round(1 + t * 175);
        const b = Math.round(84 - t * 84);
        return `rgb(${r},${g},${b})`;
      }
      return `rgba(255, ${Math.round(107 - t * 67)}, ${Math.round(107 - t * 67)}, ${0.15 + t * 0.85})`;
    },
    [colorMode]
  );

  const handleDownload = () => {
    const svg = document.querySelector('.head-view-svg');
    if (!svg) return;
    const data = new XMLSerializer().serializeToString(svg);
    const blob = new Blob([data], { type: 'image/svg+xml' });
    const url = URL.createObjectURL(blob);
    const a = document.createElement('a');
    a.href = url;
    a.download = `attention_L${selectedLayer}_H${selectedHead}.svg`;
    a.click();
    URL.revokeObjectURL(url);
  };

  if (!head) return null;

  return (
    <div className="glass p-6">
      {/* ── Toolbar ────────────────────────────────────────── */}
      <div className="flex items-center justify-between mb-4">
        <div>
          <h2 className="text-lg font-bold">
            Head View — Layer {selectedLayer}, Head {selectedHead}
          </h2>
          <p className="text-slate-400 text-xs">
            Attention weights: each row is a query token, each column is a key token
          </p>
        </div>
        <div className="flex items-center gap-2">
          <button
            onClick={() => setZoomLevel((z) => Math.min(3, z + 0.2))}
            className="p-1.5 hover:bg-white/10 rounded-lg text-slate-400"
          >
            <ZoomIn size={16} />
          </button>
          <button
            onClick={() => setZoomLevel((z) => Math.max(0.3, z - 0.2))}
            className="p-1.5 hover:bg-white/10 rounded-lg text-slate-400"
          >
            <ZoomOut size={16} />
          </button>
          <button
            onClick={() => setZoomLevel(1)}
            className="p-1.5 hover:bg-white/10 rounded-lg text-slate-400"
          >
            <RotateCcw size={16} />
          </button>
          <button
            onClick={handleDownload}
            className="p-1.5 hover:bg-white/10 rounded-lg text-slate-400"
          >
            <Download size={16} />
          </button>
        </div>
      </div>

      {/* ── Head Navigation Dots ────────────────────────────── */}
      <div className="flex items-center gap-1 mb-4 flex-wrap">
        {layer?.heads?.map((_: any, hIdx: number) => (
          <button
            key={hIdx}
            onClick={() => onHeadChange(hIdx)}
            className={`w-5 h-5 rounded-full border transition-all ${
              hIdx === selectedHead
                ? 'bg-neon-blue border-neon-blue scale-125 shadow-lg shadow-neon-blue/30'
                : 'bg-white/5 border-white/10 hover:bg-white/20'
            }`}
            title={`Head ${hIdx}`}
          />
        ))}
      </div>

      {/* ── Matrix Visualization ────────────────────────────── */}
      <div
        className="overflow-auto rounded-xl border border-white/5"
        style={{ maxHeight: '70vh' }}
      >
        <svg
          className="head-view-svg"
          width={totalWidth + 120}
          height={totalWidth + 120}
          style={{ transform: `scale(${zoomLevel})`, transformOrigin: 'top left' }}
        >
          {/* Column labels (key tokens) */}
          {tokens.map((token: string, i: number) => (
            <text
              key={`col-${i}`}
              x={100 + i * cellSize + cellSize / 2}
              y={80}
              textAnchor="middle"
              transform={`rotate(-45, ${100 + i * cellSize + cellSize / 2}, 80)`}
              className="text-[9px] fill-slate-500 font-mono"
            >
              {token.slice(0, 8)}
            </text>
          ))}

          {/* Row labels (query tokens) */}
          {tokens.map((token: string, i: number) => (
            <text
              key={`row-${i}`}
              x={90}
              y={100 + i * cellSize + cellSize / 2 + 4}
              textAnchor="end"
              className="text-[9px] fill-slate-500 font-mono"
            >
              {token.slice(0, 8)}
            </text>
          ))}

          {/* Matrix cells */}
          {matrix.map((row: number[], qi: number) =>
            row.map((value: number, ki: number) => {
              const isHovered =
                hoveredCell?.query === qi && hoveredCell?.key === ki;
              const isSelectedRow = selectedQuery === qi;
              const isSelectedCol = selectedQuery === ki;

              return (
                <g key={`${qi}-${ki}`}>
                  <rect
                    x={100 + ki * cellSize}
                    y={100 + qi * cellSize}
                    width={cellSize}
                    height={cellSize}
                    fill={getColor(value)}
                    rx={2}
                    stroke={
                      isHovered
                        ? '#fff'
                        : isSelectedRow || isSelectedCol
                        ? 'rgba(255,255,255,0.3)'
                        : 'transparent'
                    }
                    strokeWidth={isHovered ? 1.5 : isSelectedRow ? 0.5 : 0}
                    className="cursor-pointer transition-all duration-75"
                    onMouseEnter={() => setHoveredCell({ query: qi, key: ki })}
                    onMouseLeave={() => setHoveredCell(null)}
                    onClick={() =>
                      setSelectedQuery(selectedQuery === qi ? null : qi)
                    }
                  />
                  {isHovered && (
                    <text
                      x={100 + ki * cellSize + cellSize / 2}
                      y={100 + qi * cellSize + cellSize / 2 + 1}
                      textAnchor="middle"
                      className="text-[8px] fill-white font-mono font-bold"
                    >
                      {value.toFixed(2)}
                    </text>
                  )}
                </g>
              );
            })
          )}

          {/* Diagonal line */}
          <line
            x1={100}
            y1={100}
            x2={100 + tokens.length * cellSize}
            y2={100 + tokens.length * cellSize}
            stroke="rgba(255,255,255,0.1)"
            strokeDasharray="4,4"
          />
        </svg>
      </div>

      {/* ── Hover tooltip ───────────────────────────────────── */}
      {hoveredCell && (
        <div className="mt-3 text-xs text-slate-400">
          <span className="text-white font-mono">
            {tokens[hoveredCell.query]}
          </span>
          {' → '}
          <span className="text-white font-mono">
            {tokens[hoveredCell.key]}
          </span>
          : attention ={' '}
          <span className="text-neon-blue font-bold">
            {matrix[hoveredCell.query][hoveredCell.key].toFixed(4)}
          </span>
        </div>
      )}
    </div>
  );
}

docs.title: 6. Model View (views/ModelView.tsx)
docs.text:
// views/ModelView.tsx
import React, { useMemo, useState } from 'react';
import { motion } from 'framer-motion';

interface ModelViewProps {
  data: any;
  selectedLayer: number;
  selectedHead: number;
  colorMode: string;
  onLayerChange: (l: number) => void;
  onHeadChange: (h: number) => void;
}

export default function ModelView({
  data,
  selectedLayer,
  selectedHead,
  colorMode,
  onLayerChange,
  onHeadChange,
}: ModelViewProps) {
  const [hoveredHead, setHoveredHead] = useState<{
    layer: number;
    head: number;
  } | null>(null);

  const { layers, tokens } = data || {};
  const nLayers = layers?.length || 0;

  // Compute head importance scores
  const headScores = useMemo(() => {
    if (!layers) return [];
    const { computeHeadImportance } = require('../utils/attentionCalculations');
    return layers.map((layer: any) =>
      layer.heads.map((head: any) => computeHeadImportance(head.attentionMatrix))
    );
  }, [layers]);

  // Compute head diversity scores
  const headDiversity = useMemo(() => {
    if (!layers) return [];
    const { computeHeadDiversity } = require('../utils/attentionCalculations');
    return layers.map((layer: any) => {
      const allMatrices = layer.heads.map((h: any) => h.attentionMatrix);
      return layer.heads.map((head: any) =>
        computeHeadDiversity(head.attentionMatrix, allMatrices)
      );
    });
  }, [layers]);

  if (!data) return null;

  const cellW = 28;
  const cellH = 28;
  const gap = 3;
  const nHeads = layers?.[0]?.heads?.length || 0;
  const totalW = nHeads * (cellW + gap) + 100;
  const totalH = nLayers * (cellH + gap) + 60;

  return (
    <div className="glass p-6">
      <div className="mb-4">
        <h2 className="text-lg font-bold">Model View — Bird's Eye</h2>
        <p className="text-slate-400 text-xs">
          Each square = one attention head. Size = importance, color = diversity.
          Hover for details, click to zoom.
        </p>
      </div>

      <div className="overflow-auto rounded-xl border border-white/5">
        <svg width={totalW} height={totalH} className="model-view-svg">
          {/* Layer labels */}
          {Array.from({ length: nLayers }).map((_, i) => (
            <text
              key={`layer-${i}`}
              x={80}
              y={30 + i * (cellH + gap) + cellH / 2 + 4}
              textAnchor="end"
              className="text-[10px] fill-slate-400 font-mono font-bold"
            >
              L{i}
            </text>
          ))}

          {/* Head labels */}
          {Array.from({ length: nHeads }).map((_, i) => (
            <text
              key={`head-${i}`}
              x={100 + i * (cellW + gap) + cellW / 2}
              y={18}
              textAnchor="middle"
              className="text-[8px] fill-slate-500 font-mono"
            >
              H{i}
            </text>
          ))}

          {/* Head cells */}
          {layers?.map((layer: any, li: number) =>
            layer.heads.map((head: any, hi: number) => {
              const importance = headScores[li]?.[hi] || 0;
              const diversity = headDiversity[li]?.[hi] || 0;
              const isSelected =
                li === selectedLayer && hi === selectedHead;
              const isHovered =
                hoveredHead?.layer === li && hoveredHead?.head === hi;

              const r = Math.round(59 + diversity * 150);
              const g = Math.round(130 - importance * 90);
              const b = Math.round(246 - importance * 180);

              const size = cellW * (0.5 + importance * 0.5);

              return (
                <g key={`${li}-${hi}`}>
                  <rect
                    x={100 + hi * (cellW + gap) + (cellW - size) / 2}
                    y={30 + li * (cellH + gap) + (cellH - size) / 2}
                    width={size}
                    height={size}
                    fill={`rgb(${r},${g},${b})`}
                    rx={3}
                    stroke={
                      isSelected
                        ? '#fff'
                        : isHovered
                        ? 'rgba(255,255,255,0.6)'
                        : 'transparent'
                    }
                    strokeWidth={isSelected ? 2 : isHovered ? 1.5 : 0}
                    className="cursor-pointer transition-all duration-150"
                    onMouseEnter={() =>
                      setHoveredHead({ layer: li, head: hi })
                    }
                    onMouseLeave={() => setHoveredHead(null)}
                    onClick={() => {
                      onLayerChange(li);
                      onHeadChange(hi);
                    }}
                  />
                </g>
              );
            })
          )}
        </svg>
      </div>

      {/* Legend */}
      <div className="flex items-center gap-4 mt-4 text-xs text-slate-400">
        <div className="flex items-center gap-1">
          <div className="w-3 h-3 rounded-sm bg-[rgb(59,130,246)]" />
          Low importance
        </div>
        <div className="flex items-center gap-1">
          <div className="w-3 h-3 rounded-sm bg-[rgb(200,40,66)]" />
          High importance
        </div>
        <div className="flex items-center gap-1 ml-4">
          <span>Size = Importance</span>
        </div>
        <div className="flex items-center gap-1">
          <span>Color = Diversity</span>
        </div>
      </div>

      {hoveredHead && (
        <div className="mt-2 text-xs text-slate-400">
          Layer {hoveredHead.layer}, Head {hoveredHead.head}: importance ={' '}
          <span className="text-neon-blue font-bold">
            {(headScores[hoveredHead.layer]?.[hoveredHead.head] || 0).toFixed(3)}
          </span>
          , diversity ={' '}
          <span className="text-purple-400 font-bold">
            {(headDiversity[hoveredHead.layer]?.[hoveredHead.head] || 0).toFixed(3)}
          </span>
        </div>
      )}
    </div>
  );
}

docs.title: 7. 3D Attention View (views/Attention3DView.tsx)
docs.text:
// views/Attention3DView.tsx
import React, { useRef, useMemo, useState, useCallback } from 'react';
import { Canvas, useFrame, useThree } from '@react-three/fiber';
import {
  OrbitControls,
  Text,
  Line,
  Sphere,
  Html,
  Environment,
  Effects,
} from '@react-three/drei';
import * as THREE from 'three';

interface Attention3DViewProps {
  data: any;
  selectedLayer: number;
  selectedHead: number;
  colorMode: string;
  onLayerChange: (l: number) => void;
  onHeadChange: (h: number) => void;
}

// ── Particle Flow Lines ───────────────────────────────────
function AttentionParticles({
  data,
  selectedLayer,
  selectedHead,
}: {
  data: any;
  selectedLayer: number;
  selectedHead: number;
}) {
  const particlesRef = useRef<THREE.Group>(null);

  const lines = useMemo(() => {
    const layer = data?.layers?.[selectedLayer];
    const head = layer?.heads?.[selectedHead];
    if (!head) return [];

    const matrix = head.attentionMatrix;
    const tokens = data.tokens || [];
    const result: { from: THREE.Vector3; to: THREE.Vector3; weight: number }[] = [];
    const radius = Math.max(3, tokens.length * 0.4);

    for (let qi = 0; qi < tokens.length; qi++) {
      const angleQ = (qi / tokens.length) * Math.PI * 2;
      const xQ = Math.cos(angleQ) * radius;
      const zQ = Math.sin(angleQ) * radius;

      for (let ki = 0; ki < tokens.length; ki++) {
        const weight = matrix[qi]?.[ki] || 0;
        if (weight < 0.05) continue;

        const angleK = (ki / tokens.length) * Math.PI * 2;
        const xK = Math.cos(angleK) * radius;
        const zK = Math.sin(angleK) * radius;

        result.push({
          from: new THREE.Vector3(xQ, qi * 0.5 - 2, zQ),
          to: new THREE.Vector3(xK, ki * 0.5 - 2, zK),
          weight,
        });
      }
    }
    return result;
  }, [data, selectedLayer, selectedHead]);

  return (
    <group ref={particlesRef}>
      {lines.map((line, i) => (
        <Line
          key={i}
          points={[line.from, line.to]}
          color={new THREE.Color().setHSL(0.55 + line.weight * 0.3, 0.8, 0.3 + line.weight * 0.5)}
          lineWidth={line.weight * 3}
          transparent
          opacity={line.weight}
        />
      ))}
    </group>
  );
}

// ── Token Nodes ────────────────────────────────────────────
function TokenNodes({
  data,
  onTokenClick,
}: {
  data: any;
  onTokenClick: (idx: number) => void;
}) {
  const tokens = data?.tokens || [];
  const radius = Math.max(3, tokens.length * 0.4);

  return (
    <group>
      {tokens.map((token: string, i: number) => {
        const angle = (i / tokens.length) * Math.PI * 2;
        const x = Math.cos(angle) * radius;
        const z = Math.sin(angle) * radius;

        return (
          <group key={i}>
            <Sphere
              position={[x, i * 0.5 - 2, z]}
              args={[0.2, 16, 16]}
              onClick={() => onTokenClick(i)}
            >
              <meshStandardMaterial
                color={new THREE.Color().setHSL(i / tokens.length, 0.7, 0.5)}
                emissive={new THREE.Color().setHSL(i / tokens.length, 0.7, 0.2)}
                emissiveIntensity={0.3}
              />
            </Sphere>
            <Text
              position={[x, i * 0.5 - 1.5, z]}
              fontSize={0.25}
              color="white"
              anchorX="center"
            >
              {token.slice(0, 6)}
            </Text>
          </group>
        );
      })}
    </group>
  );
}

// ── Layer Ring ─────────────────────────────────────────────
function LayerRings({ numLayers }: { numLayers: number }) {
  return (
    <group>
      {Array.from({ length: numLayers }).map((_, i) => (
        <mesh key={i} position={[0, i * 0.5 - 2, 0]} rotation={[-Math.PI / 2, 0, 0]}>
          <ringGeometry args={[3.8, 4, 64]} />
          <meshBasicMaterial color="#1e293b" side={THREE.DoubleSide} transparent opacity={0.3} />
        </mesh>
      ))}
    </group>
  );
}

// ── Main Component ─────────────────────────────────────────
export default function Attention3DView({
  data,
  selectedLayer,
  selectedHead,
  onLayerChange,
  onHeadChange,
}: Attention3DViewProps) {
  const [selectedToken, setSelectedToken] = useState<number | null>(null);

  return (
    <div className="glass p-6">
      <div className="mb-4">
        <h2 className="text-lg font-bold">3D Attention View</h2>
        <p className="text-slate-400 text-xs">
          Drag to rotate, scroll to zoom. Each sphere = token, lines = attention flow.
        </p>
      </div>

      {/* Layer navigation */}
      <div className="flex items-center gap-2 mb-4 flex-wrap">
        {Array.from({ length: data?.layers?.length || 0 }).map((_, i) => (
          <button
            key={i}
            onClick={() => onLayerChange(i)}
            className={`px-3 py-1 rounded-lg text-xs font-bold transition-all ${
              i === selectedLayer
                ? 'bg-neon-blue/20 text-neon-blue border border-neon-blue/30'
                : 'bg-white/5 text-slate-400 hover:bg-white/10'
            }`}
          >
            Layer {i}
          </button>
        ))}
      </div>

      <div className="rounded-xl overflow-hidden border border-white/5" style={{ height: 500 }}>
        <Canvas camera={{ position: [6, 3, 8], fov: 50 }}>
          <ambientLight intensity={0.3} />
          <pointLight position={[10, 10, 10]} intensity={0.8} />
          <pointLight position={[-10, -10, -10]} intensity={0.3} color="#4ecdc4" />
          <OrbitControls enableDamping dampingFactor={0.1} />
          <Environment preset="city" />

          <LayerRings numLayers={data?.layers?.length || 0} />
          <TokenNodes data={data} onTokenClick={setSelectedToken} />
          <AttentionParticles
            data={data}
            selectedLayer={selectedLayer}
            selectedHead={selectedHead}
          />
        </Canvas>
      </div>

      {selectedToken !== null && (
        <div className="mt-3 text-xs text-slate-400">
          Selected token:{' '}
          <span className="text-neon-blue font-bold">
            {data?.tokens?.[selectedToken]}
          </span>
        </div>
      )}

      <p className="text-[10px] text-slate-600 mt-2">
        💡 Tip: Use mouse wheel to zoom, right-drag to pan, left-drag to rotate.
      </p>
    </div>
  );
}

docs.title: 8. Attention Stats Panel (components/AttentionStats.tsx)
docs.text:
// components/AttentionStats.tsx
import React, { useMemo } from 'react';
import { computeAttentionEntropy, computeHeadImportance } from '../../utils/attentionCalculations';

interface AttentionStatsProps {
  data: any;
  selectedLayer: number;
  selectedHead: number;
}

export default function AttentionStats({ data, selectedLayer, selectedHead }: AttentionStatsProps) {
  const stats = useMemo(() => {
    const layer = data?.layers?.[selectedLayer];
    const head = layer?.heads?.[selectedHead];
    if (!head) return null;

    const entropy = computeAttentionEntropy(head.attentionMatrix);
    const importance = computeHeadImportance(head.attentionMatrix);
    const maxEntropy = Math.log2(data.tokens.length);
    const concentration = 1 - entropy / maxEntropy;

    // Find most attended token pair
    let maxAtt = 0, maxQi = 0, maxKi = 0;
    head.attentionMatrix.forEach((row: number[], qi: number) => {
      row.forEach((val: number, ki: number) => {
        if (val > maxAtt) { maxAtt = val; maxQi = qi; maxKi = ki; }
      });
    });

    return {
      entropy: entropy.toFixed(3),
      maxEntropy: maxEntropy.toFixed(3),
      concentration: (concentration * 100).toFixed(1),
      importance: importance.toFixed(3),
      maxPair: {
        from: data.tokens[maxQi],
        to: data.tokens[maxKi],
        value: maxAtt.toFixed(4),
      },
      matrixSize: `${head.attentionMatrix.length}×${head.attentionMatrix[0]?.length || 0}`,
    };
  }, [data, selectedLayer, selectedHead]);

  if (!stats) return null;

  return (
    <div className="space-y-2 text-xs">
      <StatRow label="Entropy" value={stats.entropy} sub={`/ ${stats.maxEntropy}`} />
      <StatRow label="Concentration" value={`${stats.concentration}%`} />
      <StatRow label="Importance" value={stats.importance} />
      <StatRow label="Matrix" value={stats.matrixSize} />
      <div className="pt-2 border-t border-white/5">
        <p className="text-slate-500 mb-1">Strongest connection:</p>
        <p className="text-neon-blue font-mono">
          {stats.maxPair.from} → {stats.maxPair.to}
        </p>
        <p className="text-slate-400">weight: {stats.maxPair.value}</p>
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}

function StatRow({ label, value, sub }: { label: string; value: string; sub?: string }) {
  return (
    <div className="flex justify-between">
      <span className="text-slate-500">{label}</span>
      <span>
        <span className="text-white font-mono">{value}</span>
        {sub && <span className="text-slate-600 ml-1">{sub}</span>}
      </span>
    </div>
  );
}

docs.title: 🧠 20 Advanced Features for the NeuralOps Attention Visualization Dashboard
docs.text: Based on my research across BertViz (3 views), AttentionViz (joint Q/K embeddings, VIS 2023), Transformer Explainer (Georgia Tech, Sankey diagrams), Semantic Pathway (IEEE VIS 2025), Dodrio (ACL 2021), BHPVAS (pruning system), Logit Lens, and OpenAI's Transformer Debugger, here are 20 advanced features organized by category.

docs.title: 1. Live Math Formula Panel with Animated Computation Steps
docs.text:
Inspiration: Transformer Explainer (Georgia Tech), ByHand.ai Self Attention Flow

A side panel that renders the actual LaTeX equations being computed in real-time: - Shows the full attention formula: Attention(Q, K, V) = softmax(QK^T/√d_k) V - Highlights each variable as the user hovers over different parts of the visualization - Animates step-by-step: Q×K^T → Scale → Softmax → ×V - Shows the numerical values updating live as the user changes inputs

The Transformer Explainer uses Sankey diagram visual design inspired by viewing Transformers as dynamical systems, emphasizing how input data flows through model components. Similarly, the Self Attention Flow tool lets users resize any matrix and watch dimensions "flow" to other matrices in the self-attention mechanism.

docs.title: 2. Interactive Q/K/V Projection Explorer
docs.text:
Inspiration: AttentionViz (VIS 2023), Inside the Matrix (PyTorch)

A dedicated panel showing the joint embedding space of queries and keys: - Scatter plot of Q and K vectors projected via PCA/t-SNE/UMAP (user-selectable) - Color-coded by token position, attention weight magnitude, or semantic similarity - Brushing and linking: select a region of Q vectors → highlights corresponding K vectors → shows attention weights in the heatmap - Shows the angle between Q and K vectors (dot product = |Q||K|cos θ)

AttentionViz creates a joint embedding of query and key vectors, enabling analysis of global patterns across multiple input sequences—a fundamentally different approach from per-head heatmap views.

docs.title: 3. Scaled Dot-Product Attention Step Animator
docs.text:
Inspiration: ByHand.ai, Attention Mechanism Visualizer

A frame-by-frame animation that breaks down the attention computation: 1. Matrix Multiplication: Visualize Q × K^T as two matrices sliding together 2. Scaling: Show the division by √d_k and explain why (gradient stability) 3. Softmax: Animate each row transforming from raw scores to probabilities 4. Weighted Sum: Show V being multiplied by attention weights

Users can scrub through time with a slider, pause at any step, and see the exact numerical values in a tooltip.

docs.title: 4. "Train with This Attention" One-Click Pipeline
docs.text:
Inspiration: Your existing experiment launcher + attention config

A button on the attention dashboard that opens a pre-filled experiment launcher: - The currently visualized attention type (e.g., "Galerkin", "LinFormer", "PADRe") is pre-selected - The sample text becomes the calibration data - The layer/head configuration is carried over - User clicks one button → redirects to /launcher with all parameters set - Shows estimated FLOPs comparison between the selected attention and standard MHA

This directly connects the exploration (attention visualization) with action (training experiments), closing the loop between understanding and doing.

docs.title: 5. Attention Benchmark Comparator
docs.text:
Inspiration: Your leaderboard system + attention types

A side-by-side comparison view that loads attention patterns from multiple attention mechanisms for the same input text: - Select from all registered attention types (Galerkin, TLinFormer, PADRe, Spectraformer, etc.) - Shows head-by-head similarity matrix between different attention mechanisms - Computes Jensen-Shannon divergence between attention distributions - Links to benchmark leaderboard showing accuracy/speed trade-offs

This leverages your existing attention registry and leaderboard infrastructure to help researchers choose the right attention mechanism.

docs.title: 6. Real-Time Training Attention Monitor
docs.text:
Inspiration: Your WebSocket infrastructure + experiment monitoring

While a training run is active, stream attention patterns live from the model: - Connect via WebSocket to a running experiment - Watch how attention patterns evolve epoch by epoch - See attention specialization emerging (heads becoming specialized) - Track head importance scores over time - Alert when attention patterns stabilize (indicating convergence)

BHPVAS demonstrates that head importance, stability, and similarity scores can guide pruning—the same metrics can monitor training progress.

docs.title: 7. 3D Attention Topology Map (React Three Fiber)
docs.text:
Inspiration: TensorSpace, r3f-nn-visualizer

An immersive 3D scene where: - Each token is a sphere positioned in 3D space (via t-SNE/UMAP of hidden states) - Attention connections are curved tubes/pipes between tokens, with thickness = attention weight - Layers are stacked vertically—user can "fly through" the model - Color gradient shows attention flow from query (source) to key (target) - VR mode toggle for immersive exploration

TensorSpace and r3f-nn-visualizer both use Three.js for 3D neural network visualization with interactive camera controls.

docs.title: 8. Sankey Attention Flow Diagram
docs.text:
Inspiration: Transformer Explainer, InTraVisTo

A Sankey diagram showing how information flows through the Transformer: - Left side: Input tokens - Middle columns: Each attention head in each layer - Right side: Output tokens / predictions - Flow width = attention weight magnitude - Hover on a flow shows the exact attention value, source and target tokens

The Transformer Explainer "adopts the Sankey diagram visual design, inspired by recent work viewing Transformers as dynamical systems, emphasizing how input data flows through model components". InTraVisTo similarly uses Sankey diagrams to show information flow between components across layers.

docs.title: 9. Attention Head Clustering & Dendrogram
docs.text:
Inspiration: BHPVAS, attention head clustering research

A hierarchical clustering view showing which heads behave similarly: - Similarity matrix across all heads (using attention pattern distance) - Dendrogram showing head groupings - Color-coded clusters with labels (e.g., "Positional Heads", "Semantic Heads", "Delimiter Heads") - Click a cluster → see the prototypical attention pattern for that group - Pruning recommendation: which clusters can be safely removed

Research shows attention heads can be reliably clustered into different categories through unsupervised methods, corroborating previous observations about head specialization.

docs.title: 10. Attention Pattern Animation (Token-by-Token Generation)
docs.text:
Inspiration: Semantic Pathway (IEEE VIS 2025)

For autoregressive models, animate how attention patterns evolve as each new token is generated: - Timeline slider for each generation step - Shows how attention shifts from earlier tokens to more recent ones - Highlights cross-layer semantic trajectories of each token - Reveals the "semantic pathway" of how meaning accumulates across generation steps

Semantic Pathway integrates "layerwise semantic trajectories, attention overlays, and output probability views into a unified interface, enabling users to trace how meaning accumulates and decisions emerge during generation".

docs.title: 11. Head Importance & Redundancy Analyzer
docs.text:
Inspiration: BHPVAS, head pruning research

Three scoring metrics computed for every head: - Importance Score: How much does ablating this head change the output? - Stability Score: How consistent is this head's behavior across different inputs? - Similarity Score: How redundant is this head with others in the same layer?

Displayed as a multi-dimensional scatter plot (importance × stability × similarity), letting users identify: - Critical heads (high importance, high stability) — must keep - Redundant heads (low importance, high similarity) — safe to prune - Specialized heads (high importance, low similarity) — unique function

BHPVAS proposes exactly these three criteria: "importance score, stability score, and similarity score, for evaluating the importance of self-attention heads".

docs.title: 12. Logit Lens Integration
docs.text:
Inspiration: Logit Lens (nostalgebraist 2020, mbrenndoerfer 2026)

Show what the model predicts at each layer by projecting hidden states into vocabulary space: - Layer-by-layer prediction display: what word does each layer "think" comes next? - Prediction convergence animation: watch predictions stabilize across layers - Attention-to-prediction linking: click an attention head → see its contribution to the final prediction - Compare mode: two different inputs, side-by-side logit lens

The logit lens "directly reads out the model's implicit prediction at each layer" without any extra machinery, revealing how predictions evolve from confused early layers to confident later layers.

docs.title: 13. Head Ablation Playground
docs.text:
Inspiration: OpenAI Transformer Debugger, Arrakis

An interactive tool where users can disable specific heads and see the effect: - Toggle individual heads on/off with a switch - Before/after comparison of model output - Output probability diff: how does ablating head X change the prediction? - Chain ablation: disable multiple heads and observe compound effects - Link to your compression pipeline: export the ablation configuration as a pruning recipe

Arrakis provides "common attention operations (merging/ablating heads), removing/permuting layers" as standard tools for mechanistic interpretability experiments.

docs.title: 14. Attention-to-Experiments Link Graph
docs.text:
Inspiration: Your experiment tracking + note system

Every attention visualization is persistently linked to the platform: - Each attention analysis creates a researcher note automatically - Bidirectional links between attention views, training runs, and model versions - Knowledge graph visualization: which experiments used which attention types? - Version history: how did attention patterns change after fine-tuning or compression? - Shareable URLs: send a link to a specific attention view to a collaborator

This connects the attention dashboard to your existing notes, model_versioning, and experiment apps.

docs.title: 15. Semantic Dependency Overlay (Dodrio-style)
docs.text:
Inspiration: Dodrio (ACL 2021)

Overlay linguistic annotations on top of attention patterns: - Syntactic dependencies (parse tree) overlaid on the attention heatmap - Semantic role labels to see which tokens attend to agents, patients, etc. - Coreference chains: do attention heads track entity mentions? - Part-of-speech coloring: are certain heads specialized for nouns, verbs, etc.?

Dodrio "tightly integrates an overview that summarizes the roles of different attention heads, and detailed views that help users compare attention weights with the syntactic structure and semantic information in the input text".

docs.title: 16. Attention Pattern Search & Retrieval
docs.text:
Inspiration: Your search infrastructure + attention database

Build a searchable database of attention patterns: - "Find similar attention patterns": given a head, find other heads (across layers, models, or experiments) with similar behavior - Semantic search: "show me heads that attend to the next token" or "heads that focus on punctuation" - Pattern library: curated gallery of canonical attention patterns (positional, semantic, delimiter, etc.) - Export/import: save attention data as JSON for external analysis

docs.title: 17. Multi-Input Comparison Mode
docs.text:
Inspiration: Semantic Pathway (IEEE VIS 2025), HuggingFace Issue #39440

Compare attention patterns across different inputs side by side: - Three-panel view: Input A | Input B | Difference (divergence) - Divergence heatmap: where do attention patterns differ most? - Statistical summary: average JSD, correlation, etc. - Batch mode: run multiple inputs and find the most "interesting" attention patterns

Semantic Pathway incorporates a "Compare Mode for analyzing divergence across alternate outputs". The HuggingFace multimodal visualization proposal similarly includes "Comparative visualization for multiple inputs".

docs.title: 18. Attention Documentation Generator
docs.text:
Inspiration: Your notes system + paper app

Auto-generate research documentation from attention exploration: - "Generate Report" button creates a rich Markdown note with: - Embedded attention visualizations (SVG/PNG) - Computed statistics (entropy, concentration, head importance) - The sample text and model configuration - Links to the training run and model version - One-click export to LaTeX (for paper writing via your paper app) - HuggingFace upload of the attention report

docs.title: 19. Attention-Driven Prompt Engineering
docs.text:
Inspiration: Logit Lens, mechanistic interpretability tools

Use attention patterns to debug and improve prompts: - Highlight which tokens receive the most attention in a prompt - Identify "attention sinks" — tokens that absorb disproportionate attention - Prompt A/B testing: compare attention patterns between two prompts - Token importance scoring: which prompt tokens most influence the output? - Suggestions for prompt improvement based on attention analysis

docs.title: 20. Collaborative Attention Workshop
docs.text:
Inspiration: Your real-time collaboration (WebSocket + Channels)

Multiple researchers can explore attention patterns together in real time: - Shared view state: layer/head selection, zoom level, color scheme synchronized - Cursor presence: see where other researchers are hovering - Annotation pins: drop comments on specific attention connections - Threaded discussion per head/layer - Session recording: replay an attention exploration session for teaching

This leverages your existing WebSocket infrastructure (channels) and collaborative editing patterns from the notes app.
