docs.title: Summary of Key Technical Decisions
docs.text:
Decision Choice Rationale Rendering engine React Three Fiber + Three.js Largest ecosystem, best WebXR support, declarative API GPU compute WebGPU (WGSL) with WebGL2 fallback 3-5x faster than WebGL; "10万粒子系统可达300FPS" VR provider @react-three/xr Official Poimandres library, hand tracking support Multi-user sync Yjs CRDT + WebRTC DataChannel Proven in collaborative 3D tools; P2P for low latency Spatial audio Three.js PositionalAudio + Web Audio API Built-in HRTF, mature API, R3F integration Session recording Custom delta-encoded pose stream Lightweight, replayable in the same scene Platform backend Django Channels (existing) Reuses existing WebSocket infrastructure Desktop fallback OrbitControls + WASD Same scene, no code duplication

This specification provides a complete, implementable blueprint for the VR Immersion Room. Every component has been selected based on proven technology with strong community support and performance characteristics suitable for both desktop and standalone VR headsets. The phased implementation roadmap delivers incremental value, with each phase producing a usable feature set while building toward the full collaborative VR experience.

docs.title: 🧮 Weight Matrix Decomposer — Complete Implementation Specification
docs.text: "The SVD decomposition of transformer weight matrices is highly interpretable — the primary directions used by the network can be inferred from the SVD." — SVDInterpretTransformer (ICML 2026)

docs.title: 0. Architecture Overview
docs.text: The Weight Matrix Decomposer is a client‑side computational visualization engine that performs real‑time matrix decomposition directly in the browser, then renders the results across four coordinated views. This eliminates server round‑trips for computation while leveraging GPU acceleration for rendering.

docs.title: Technology Stack
docs.text: Layer Technology Purpose Computation Engine Pyodide (CPython → WebAssembly) + NumPy + SciPy Run full SVD, CUR, Kronecker, Tensor Train decompositions in‑browser with near‑native performance. Pyodide "brings Python runtime and scientific computing libraries—including NumPy, Pandas, Matplotlib, and SciPy—directly in the browser" 3D Rendering React Three Fiber (R3F) + Three.js + Drei Declarative React components for 3D matrix visualization, singular value spectrum, and direction space. R3F "lets you write 3D using React components instead of raw Three.js API" GPU Acceleration Deck.gl (WebGL2/WebGPU) Render massive weight matrices (768×768 to 4096×4096) with GPU‑powered layers. "deck.gl is a GPU‑powered framework for visual exploratory data analysis of large datasets" 2D Charts Plotly.js + Recharts Interactive heatmaps, bar charts for singular value spectrum, cumulative energy curves. Plotly provides "hover, zoom, 3D surface plots, and export to standalone interactive HTML" WebGL Math gl‑matrix "Hand‑tuned functions for maximum JavaScript performance" for matrix operations, "designed for WebGL applications with Float32Array storage" Animation Engine Manim Community Edition (server‑side) 3Blue1Brown‑style mathematical animations rendered on‑demand. "Manim is an engine for precise programmatic animations, designed for creating explanatory math videos" Linear Algebra (JS) Loshu.js "Capable of matrix decompositions, eigenvalue and vectors, solution and approximation to linear systems" in pure JavaScript, as lightweight fallback State Management Zustand + React Query Manage decomposition state, caching of SVD results, and synchronization across the 4 coordinated views Web Workers Comlink + Pyodide WebWorker Offload heavy SVD computation to a background thread so the UI remains responsive at 60fps Data Transfer SharedArrayBuffer Zero‑copy data transfer between the computation worker and the rendering thread for large matrices

docs.title: Implementation Architecture
docs.text: This view displays the singular value spectrum of a selected weight matrix as an interactive visualization. The design follows the SVDInterpretTransformer approach: "the projection matrices of MLP sublayers admit a natural decomposition into orthogonal, interpretable rank‑1 subspaces".

docs.title: Sub‑Component Tree
docs.text:
<SingularValueSpectrum>
  ├── <MatrixSelector>           // Dropdown: Q, K, V, O, FFN1, FFN2 per layer
  ├── <SpectrumChart>            // Plotly.js bar + line chart
  │   ├── <SingularValueBar>     // One bar per σᵢ, color by cumulative energy
  │   ├── <CumulativeEnergyLine> // Overlaid line: Σσ² / Σσ²_total
  │   └── <HoverTooltip>         // Shows σᵢ value, individual %, cumulative %
  ├── <RankSlider>               // Interactive k slider: 1 … max_rank
  │   ├── <EnergyThresholdMark>  // Dashed line at 95% energy
  │   └── <RankPreviewBadge>     // "Rank 64 → 98.3% energy retained"
  ├── <SingularVectorTable>      // Top-5 singular vectors with word cloud
  └── <DecompositionMetadata>    // Computation time, matrix dimensions, norm

docs.title: Technology Choices
docs.text: Component Technology Rationale Spectrum Chart Plotly.js Bar + Scatter overlay GPU‑accelerated WebGL rendering, built‑in hover/zoom/export, handles 1000+ bars smoothly Bar Colors D3‑interpolate interpolateRdBu Color gradient from blue (σ₁) to red (σₙ) showing importance decay Rank Slider Radix UI Slider + Framer Motion Accessible, animated, with spring physics for smooth value transitions Word Cloud React‑Wordcloud (D3‑based) Visualize top tokens aligned with each singular vector direction

docs.title: Data Flow
docs.text:
1. User selects weight matrix (e.g., "Layer 3 — Query Projection W_Q")
  2. React component calls decompositionWorker.computeSVD(matrixId) via Comlink
  3. Pyodide Web Worker loads the matrix from a SharedArrayBuffer, runs np.linalg.svd(W, full_matrices=False)
  4. Returns {U_shape, S_array, Vt_shape, compute_time_ms} via Comlink proxy
  5. Zustand store updates → all 4 canvases re‑render reactively
  6. Spectrum chart renders σ₁…σₙ as descending bars with cumulative energy overlay

docs.title: Key Interaction: Energy‑Threshold Rank Selection
docs.text:
Research shows "small singular values matter" — "our findings highlight the overlooked importance of the low end of the spectrum and provide theoretical and practical guidance for SVD‑based pruning and compression". The user drags the rank slider; the chart updates:

  • Bars to keep (σ₁…σ_k): full color opacity
  • Bars to discard (σ_{k+1}…σ_n): grayed out, 30% opacity
  • Cumulative energy line: vertical dashed line at k, showing "95.3% energy retained"
  • Reconstruction error: Frobenius norm ‖W − W_k‖_F displayed live

docs.title: Implementation Architecture
docs.text: This view visualizes the semantic meaning of each singular vector direction. Based on the SVDInterpretTransformer finding: "each unique term in a corpus is assigned to a row… you take the SVD" revealing interpretable directions.

docs.title: Sub‑Component Tree
docs.text:
<SVDirectionInterpreter>
  ├── <DirectionSelector>        // Which singular vector (1…k) to explore
  ├── <Direction3DScatter>       // R3F 3D scatter: all tokens projected onto U_i
  │   ├── <TokenSphere>          // One sphere per vocabulary token
  │   ├── <DirectionArrow>       // Arrow showing the singular vector direction
  │   └── <OrbitControls>        // R3F‑Drei camera controls
  ├── <TokenRankingTable>        // Top-20 tokens most aligned with this direction
  ├── <DirectionWordCloud>       // Word cloud visualization
  └── <SemanticLabel>            // Auto‑generated label: "This direction captures verb tense"

docs.title: Technology Choices
docs.text: Component Technology Rationale 3D Scatter React Three Fiber + @react-three/drei Sphere, Line, Text "R3F lets you write 3D using React components" with GPU‑accelerated rendering via Three.js Scatter Layout UMAP (via Pyodide) or t‑SNE Dimensionality reduction for token embedding visualization in 3D space Word Cloud D3‑cloud layout Classic word cloud with font size proportional to alignment score Semantic Label LLM‑generated (server‑side) Feed top‑20 tokens to GPT‑4o mini for interpretable label generation

docs.title: Data Flow
docs.text:
1. User selects singular vector index i (1 ≤ i ≤ k)
  2. Worker computes the projection: scores_j = |U_i · E_j| for each token embedding E_j
  3. Top‑50 tokens returned to main thread
  4. 3D scatter: each token is a sphere; position = (scores_j, x_j, y_j) where x,y are UMAP projections
  5. Direction arrow: shows the orientation of the singular vector in embedding space

docs.title: Implementation Architecture
docs.text: This is the most powerful and novel view — it lets researchers interactively explore the compression landscape by adjusting decomposition parameters and seeing real‑time reconstruction quality. Directly connected to your 60+ compression methods (A3, ERC‑SVD, AdaSVD, CUR, Kronecker, TT, etc.).

docs.title: Sub‑Component Tree
docs.text:
<CompressionPreview>
  ├── <CompressorSelector>       // Dropdown: All registered compressors
  ├── <ParameterPanel>           // Dynamic params based on selected compressor
  │   ├── <RankSlider>           // For SVD‑based: k = 1…min(m,n)
  │   ├── <EnergyThreshold>      // For ERC‑SVD: 0.90 … 0.999
  │   ├── <LeverageSampling>     // For CUR: uniform vs. leverage score
  │   ├── <FactorDims>           // For Kronecker: m₁,m₂, n₁,n₂
  │   └── <TTRanks>              // For Tensor Train: r₁, r₂, …
  ├── <ReconstructionGrid>       // Side‑by‑side: Original vs. Reconstructed
  │   ├── <OriginalMatrix>       // Deck.gl BitmapLayer — original W
  │   ├── <ReconstructedMatrix>  // Deck.gl BitmapLayer — W_approx

docs.title: Technology Choices
docs.text: Component Technology Rationale Matrix Visualization Deck.gl BitmapLayer or custom R3F instanced mesh "deck.gl is a GPU‑powered framework… WebGL2/WebGPU‑based visualization of large data sets" — can render 768×768 matrices as pixel‑perfect grids at 60fps Difference Matrix R3F shader material with custom GLSL GPU‑accelerated element‑wise difference computation and color mapping Stats Panel Recharts RadialBar + Framer Motion animated numbers Already in your stack; spring‑animated number transitions Accuracy Prediction Pyodide + small ONNX model Run a lightweight regression model that predicts accuracy impact from (rank_ratio, layer_type, original_norm) Apply Button Your existing launcher API Pre‑fills experiment config with compression parameters

docs.title: Data Flow for "What If?" Interaction
docs.text:
1. User selects "CUR decomposition" from the compressor dropdown
  2. Worker computes CUR: column selection via leverage scores → C, row selection → R, pseudo‑inverse → U
  3. W_approx = C @ U @ R computed in Pyodide
  4. Original W, W_approx, and element‑wise difference sent to main thread via SharedArrayBuffer
  5. Deck.gl renders all three matrices as tiled heatmaps with synchronized zoom/pan
  6. Stats panel updates reactively from the store

docs.title: Key Interaction: Real‑Time Reconstruction
docs.text:
As the user drags the rank slider, the reconstruction updates at 30fps using a debounced Pyodide call. The implementation uses:

  • Throttled SVD: If the user is sliding, compute only for the final value after a 200ms debounce
  • Cached intermediate results: For CUR, cache the column/row indices; only recompute U
  • Web Worker isolation: Heavy computation never blocks the main thread

docs.title: 4. MATH PANEL: Live LaTeX + Numerical Computation

  │   └── <TruncationIndicator>  // Highlights which parts are kept/discarded
  ├── <StepByStepComputation>    // Animated computation walkthrough
  │   ├── <Step1_MatrixMult>     // Q^T K step
  │   ├── <Step2_Scale>          // ÷ √d_k
  │   ├── <Step3_Softmax>        // Row‑wise softmax

docs.title: Implementation Notes for Math Panel
docs.text:
LaTeX Live Rendering: KaTeX renders the formula W = U Σ V^T with color‑coded dimensions. When the user hovers over a singular value bar in Canvas 1, the corresponding σᵢ highlights in the LaTeX. When they change the rank k, the truncation indicator updates to show W_k = U_k Σ_k V_k^T.

Step‑by‑Step Animation: Uses SVG <rect> elements animated with Framer Motion's layoutId for seamless transitions. Each step highlights the current operation and shows intermediate numerical results.

Manim Animation: When the user clicks "Watch Explanation," a request is sent to a server endpoint that runs Manim CE with a pre‑written SVD explanation scene. The rendered MP4 is streamed back. "Manim is an engine for precise programmatic animations, designed for creating explanatory math videos".

Implementation Architecture

docs.text: The control panel provides unified access to all 60+ compressors in your library, with dynamic parameter forms that adapt to each method.

docs.title: Implementation Notes
docs.text:
The DynamicParameterForm uses a registry pattern: each compressor exports a CompressorConfigSchema that describes its parameters (name, type, min, max, default). The form renders appropriate inputs for each parameter type.

// Conceptual type definition
interface CompressorConfigSchema {
  method: string;
  parameters: {
    name: string;
    type: 'slider' | 'dropdown' | 'number' | 'toggle';
    min?: number;
    max?: number;
    step?: number;
    options?: { label: string; value: string }[];
    default: any;
  }[];
}

docs.title: Implementation Architecture
docs.text: The most powerful feature: directly connecting the visualization to your compression infrastructure. When a user finds a promising compression configuration, they can apply it to the actual model with one click.

docs.title: Integration Points
docs.text: Integration Endpoint / Module Data Flow Compressor Registry framework.core.registry.COMPRESSOR_REGISTRY Read available compressors and their parameter schemas Apply Compression POST /api/runs/start-compress/ Send compression config, model ID, layer selection Experiment Monitor ws/experiments/{run_id}/ WebSocket stream for real‑time progress Model Versioning model_versioning app Auto‑create version with compressed model Benchmark gpu_benchmark app Run MLPerf‑style benchmark on compressed model Leaderboard leaderboards app Submit compressed model performance to leaderboard

docs.title: Data Flow for One‑Click Compression
docs.text:
1. User configures compression parameters in the dashboard (e.g., ERC‑SVD, rank=64, energy_threshold=0.95)
  2. Clicks "Apply This Compression to the Model"
  3. Frontend calls POST /api/runs/start-compress/ with: 
    {
  "model_name": "bert-base-uncased",
  "compressor": "erc",
  "compressor_config": { "erc_allowed_error": 0.05 },
  "target_layers": ["encoder.layer.3.attention.self.query"],
  "experiment_name": "Compress BERT Layer 3 Query — ERC‑SVD rank 64"
}
  4. Backend creates a TrainingRun with job_type='compression'
  5. WebSocket streams progress: "Computing SVD…", "Reconstructing weights…", "Benchmarking…"
  6. On completion: before/after comparison appears in the dashboard automatically

docs.title: Matrix Size Tiers
docs.text: Matrix Size Computation Strategy Rendering Strategy ≤ 512×512 Pyodide SVD in Web Worker (~50ms) Deck.gl BitmapLayer, 60fps 512×512 – 2048×2048 Pyodide SVD in Web Worker (~500ms), show progress bar Deck.gl with Level‑of‑Detail, 30fps > 2048×2048 Server‑side SVD via API, stream results Deck.gl with tiled rendering, progressive loading

docs.title: Caching Strategy
docs.text:
• LRU Cache (Zustand middleware): cache the last 20 SVD results with key = (matrix_hash, rank)
  • Pre‑computation: when a model is loaded, pre‑compute SVD for all linear layers in a Web Worker pool
  • Incremental loading: load singular values first (fast), then singular vectors on‑demand

docs.title: Memory Management
docs.text:
• SharedArrayBuffer: transfer weight matrices between threads without copying
  • Float32Array: all matrix data stored as Float32 (not Float64) to halve memory usage
  • Garbage Collection: explicitly nullify large arrays when switching views

docs.title: 3D Neural Architecture Visualizer & Attention Lab: 5-Minute Demo Script
docs.text: Live Deployment: Hugging Face Spaces - 3D Neural Architecture Visualizer Source Repository: Hooshaai/3d-neural-architecture-visualizer Target Audience: AI researchers, ML engineers, systems architects, and students.

docs.title: Executive Overview
docs.text:
The Attention Lab / 3D Neural Architecture Visualizer is an interactive, GPU-accelerated spatial laboratory built in Three.js and vanilla Web standards. It renders exact token physics and tensor projections for modern transformer models, including DistilBERT, RoBERTa, GPT-2, Qwen 2.5 (GQA), ToMoE, and SliceGPT.

The visualizer provides real-time architectural telemetry across 13 attention mechanisms, a deep 10-section telemetry inspector, a 6-model comparison matrix, an educational atlas, complete 3D dataflow wiring & residual highways, and a cinematic Present Mode designed for high-impact 5-minute conference demonstrations.

docs.title: Timing Breakdown
docs.text:
• 0:00 - 0:30 (Step 1): Welcome & The Transformer Anatomy
  • 0:30 - 1:00 (Step 2): Standard Multi-Head Attention (MHA)
  • 1:00 - 1:35 (Step 3): Grouped-Query Attention (GQA) & KV Cache Efficiency
  • 1:35 - 2:05 (Step 4): Fused QKV Projections (c_attn)
  • 2:05 - 2:45 (Step 5): SVD Low-Rank Attention Factorization
  • 2:45 - 3:20 (Step 6): Multi-Head Latent Attention (MLA)
  • 3:20 - 3:55 (Step 7): Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) Dynamic Routing
  • 3:55 - 4:25 (Step 8): Structured Dimensional Slicing (SliceGPT)
  • 4:25 - 4:45 (Step 9): Residual Highways & Normalization
  • 4:45 - 5:00 (Step 10): Cross-Model Matrix & Summary

docs.title: Step 1: Welcome & The Transformer Anatomy (0:00 - 0:30)
docs.text:
• Visual Action: Start in standard view with DistilBERT loaded. Click ▶ Present Mode (or press P). The camera flies to an overview of the 6 transformer layers.
  • Presenter Narration:

    "Welcome to the Attention Lab and 3D Neural Architecture Visualizer. What you are seeing is a real-time, mathematically accurate 3D representation of a Transformer. Tokens enter through the embedding layer at the bottom and stream upward through repeating blocks of Multi-Head Attention, Feed-Forward Networks, and lateral Residual Highways. Every geometry you see corresponds directly to exact weight matrix dimensions, tensor ranks, and memory footprints."

docs.title: Step 2: Multi-Head Self-Attention (MHA) (0:30 - 1:00)
docs.text:
• Visual Action: Advance to Step 2 (click Next ▶ or press ]). The camera swoops into Layer 0's Attention block. The inspector drawer updates with head telemetry and projection dimensions.
  • Presenter Narration:

    "Here we enter Layer 0: standard Multi-Head Attention. The hidden dimension of 768 is split across 12 independent query heads, each of dimension 64. In the inspector drawer on the right, observe the exact projection operators: \(W_Q, W_K, W_V, W_O\), the scaling factor \(1/\sqrt{d_k} = 0.125\), and the live attention probability heatmap. Notice how each head projects tokens into a distinct subspace, allowing the network to simultaneously track syntactic dependencies and long-range semantics."

docs.title: Step 3: Grouped-Query Attention (GQA) & KV Cache Efficiency (1:00 - 1:35)
docs.text:
• Visual Action: Switch model to Qwen 2.5 (GQA). Observe the 3D projection streams: Query tokens fan out into 14 wide heads, while Key and Value tokens compress into just 2 shared head groups.
  • Presenter Narration:

    "Now we switch to Qwen 2.5, featuring Grouped-Query Attention (GQA). In standard MHA, every query head requires its own Key and Value cache, which causes massive memory bandwidth bottlenecks during autoregressive generation. GQA shares 1 Key and 1 Value head across every 7 Query heads. As shown in the KV Cache Footprint bar chart, this slashes KV memory by 85.7%—reducing cache consumption from 1,536 bytes per token down to just 256 bytes per token—enabling 8× larger batch sizes on GPU hardware."

docs.title: Step 4: Fused QKV Projections (GPT-2 c_attn) (1:35 - 2:05)
docs.text:
• Visual Action: Switch model to GPT-2. The separate Q, K, V slabs coalesce into a single unified green projection slab.
  • Presenter Narration:

    "Looking at GPT-2, we see another engineering optimization: Fused QKV Attention. Rather than executing three separate matrix multiplications for \(W_Q\), \(W_K\), and \(W_V\), GPT-2 packs them into a single \([768 \times 2304]\) fused linear operator (c_attn). This maximizes GPU compute kernel occupancy and memory bandwidth utilization before slicing the result in SRAM."

docs.title: Step 5: SVD Low-Rank Attention Factorization (2:05 - 2:45)
docs.text:
• Visual Action: Open the Module Catalog (Library (241)), search for svd, and apply SVDLinearAttention. The attention projection nodes morph into dual-cone hourglass bottleneck twins.
  • Presenter Narration:

    "Here is our core research contribution: Singular Value Decomposition applied to linear attention. By computing the truncated Eckart-Young-Mirsky approximation \(W \approx U_r \Sigma_r V_r^\top\), we replace full \([768 \times 768]\) dense matrices with factorized rank-\(r\) bottleneck twins: Factor \(V\) down-projects \(768 \to 64\), and Factor \(U\) up-projects \(64 \to 768\). Look at the telemetry: this achieves an 83.3% parameter reduction with 92.4% retained SST-2 accuracy, running fully uncompressed on standard PyTorch runtimes."

docs.title: Step 6: Multi-Head Latent Attention (MLA) (2:45 - 3:20)
docs.text:
• Visual Action: Advance tour to Step 6 (MLA). The 3D token stream compresses into a narrow golden latent bottleneck conduit.
  • Presenter Narration:

    "Pioneered in DeepSeek-V2 and V3, Multi-Head Latent Attention takes compression one step further. Instead of caching high-dimensional Key-Value heads, MLA compresses the entire KV representation into a single 512-dimensional latent vector \(c_t^{KV}\). During autoregressive decoding, only this compact vector is stored in VRAM. The decompression matrix can even be absorbed directly into the queries, completely eliminating key decompression during attention calculation."

docs.title: Step 7: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) Dynamic Routing (3:20 - 3:55)
docs.text:
• Visual Action: Switch model to ToMoE (MoE). Camera moves to the FFN layer. The single dense slab expands into 4 parallel expert subnetworks with a gating router at the front.
  • Presenter Narration:

    "Moving to the Feed-Forward sublayer, we observe Mixture-of-Experts. Instead of passing every token through a uniform dense FFN, a learned Top-2 gating router scores each token and dynamically routes it to only 2 of the 4 specialized expert subnetworks. This provides 4× the parameter capacity with the FLOP budget and execution latency of a standard dense layer."

docs.title: Step 8: Structured Pruning & Dimensional Reduction (SliceGPT) (3:55 - 4:25)
docs.text:
• Visual Action: Switch model to SliceGPT. The transformer layers visibly shrink in width; inactive channels turn dim gray.
  • Presenter Narration:

    "Unlike traditional unstructured pruning which creates irregular sparse masks that run slowly on GPUs, SliceGPT performs structured coordinate slicing. Using orthogonal transformation matrices \(Q\) computed from activation covariances, signal energy is concentrated into principal coordinates, physically excising 25% of the hidden dimensions. The result is a physically smaller, denser model that runs instantly faster on standard Tensor Cores."

docs.title: Step 9: Residual Highways & Normalization (4:25 - 4:45)
docs.text:
• Visual Action: Camera tilts to display the lateral green emerald conduit running alongside the main layer stack.
  • Presenter Narration:

    "Notice the lateral emerald green particle stream running parallel to the transformer blocks. This is the Residual Highway. Rather than forcing information to pass exclusively through parameterized transformations, tokens bypass the sublayers and are recombined via additive residual junctions (\(+\)). Paired with pre-layer normalization (RMSNorm / LayerNorm), this ensures gradients propagate without vanishing across deep networks."

docs.title: Step 10: Cross-Model Matrix & Summary (4:45 - 5:00)
docs.text:
• Visual Action: Press M to open the Cross-Model Comparison Matrix Dashboard.
  • Presenter Narration:

    "To conclude, we open the Cross-Model Matrix Dashboard. Here we compare all 6 architectures across parameter count, hidden dimension, KV cache footprint, and SST-2 accuracy. Every metric is exportable as publication-ready CSV data. The visualizer is live on Hugging Face Spaces for interactive research. Thank you!"

docs.title: 1. Dual-Viewport Comparison
docs.text: The scene renders two vertical computational columns side-by-side: * Baseline Column (Left, \(X = -4.5\)): The uncompressed dense monolithic architecture (\(O(N^2)\) quadratic attention, dense MLP projections). * Compressed Column (Right, \(X = +4.5\)): The active compression paradigm (SVD rank bottleneck, Mixture-of-Experts routing, DeepSeek MLA latent KV caching, or SliceGPT channel slicing).

docs.title: 2. Semantic Zoom & Continuous Level-of-Detail (LOD)
docs.text: Visual density dynamically adapts to camera proximity: * Far View (LOD 0, Distance > 40): Layers collapse into consolidated enclosing macro bounding boxes. * Transition Zone (Distance 25–40): Macro boxes smoothly fade as internal matrix tensors materialize. * Near View (LOD 1, Distance < 25): Full granular tensor boxes, attention head partitions, SVD necks, and floating dimension badges ([768 × 768], 12H, r=64).

docs.title: 3. Code-Accurate Token Dynamics
docs.text: Particles are not decorative; their 3D paths evaluate real transformer dataflow equations: * Qwen 2.5/3.5: Multi-query fan-out with 14 Query heads, 2 shared Key/Value head bundles, and SwiGLU gate_proj/up_proj bifurcations. * GPT-2: Unified travel through fused \(c\_attn\) Conv1D wide tensor projections. * DistilBERT / RoBERTa: Physical constriction into the rank-64 SVD Factor \(V\) eigenspace, expanding through Factor \(U\). * Residual Highways: 25% of tokens bypass sublayers to visualize the identity skip addition: \(X_{\text{out}} = X_{\text{in}} + \text{Sublayer}(\text{Norm}(X_{\text{in}}))\).

docs.title: 1. Conduits Overview
docs.text:
Modern transformer architectures are not isolated blocks; they are deeply connected networks of attention operators, multi-query head splits, gating mechanisms, and residual highways.

The visualizer computes code-accurate 3D cubic Bezier curves (src/builders/conduit_builder.js) that physically route token signals between operations.

       Layer Input Bus Port Ring (◎)
                 │
      ┌──────────┴──────────┐
      ▼                     ▼
[Query Projection]   [Key/Value Split]
      │                     │
      └──────────┬──────────┘
                 ▼
          [Attention Core]
                 │
                 ▼
          [Output Dense]
                 │
                 ▼
       Residual Addition Node (+)  ◀──── [Bypass Highway Conduit]

docs.title: 2. Color-Coded Signal Bus Standards
docs.text: Signal Type Color Hex Visual Role Input Stream Emerald Green #10b981 Sequence entry from embedding lookup Baseline Feed Sky Blue #38bdf8 Dense baseline forward connections Compressed Feed Mint Cyan #2dd4bf Low-rank / compressed forward connections GQA KV Bundle Amber Orange #f59e0b Shared Key/Value projections (Qwen) SwiGLU Branch Violet Purple #a855f7 Bifurcated gate/up projection cables Residual Attn Deep Azure #0284c7 Attention identity skip highway (\(+X_{\text{in}}\)) Residual FFN Royal Indigo #7c3aed Feed-forward identity skip highway (\(+X_{\text{mid}}\)) Output Head Crimson Rose #f43f5e LM Unembedding Softmax distribution

docs.title: 3. Port Rings
docs.text: At every layer entrance and exit, the engine instantiates a high-tech circular ingress/egress port ring (THREE.RingGeometry) indicating active tensor flow. When a user clicks on any sublayer in the Deep Inspector or Component Pipeline, the associated conduits illuminate in bright emissive white to trace the signal pathway.

docs.title: Data Schema Documentation · 3D Neural Architecture Visualizer
docs.text:
This document formally specifies all data schemas used by the 3D Neural Architecture Visualizer (Docs/visualizer). The visualizer consumes three primary data files and a directory of modular JSON component topologies:

  1. spatial-data.json (~3.1 MB)
  2. modules-catalog.json (~543 KB)
  3. modules_components.json (~1.4 MB)
  4. components/<module_id>.json (240 files)

docs.title: 1. spatial-data.json Schema
docs.text:
spatial-data.json provides the spatial scene graph, node bounding boxes, 3D coordinates, and structural conduits across all 4 supported model families.

{
  "title": "3D Neural Architecture Spatial Layout",
  "generated_at": "ISO-8601 string",
  "models": {
    "distilbert": ModelSpatialData,
    "roberta": ModelSpatialData,
    "gpt2": ModelSpatialData,
    "qwen": ModelSpatialData
  }
}

docs.title: ModelSpatialData Object
docs.text: Field Type Description true_num_layers number Physical number of transformer layers in model (e.g. 6, 12, 24) capped_num_layers number Rendered layers in the 3D canvas (capped for 60fps WebGL rendering) baseline_nodes Node3D[] Array of dense uncompressed nodes (left column, \(X = -4.5\)) baseline_macro_nodes MacroNode[] Consolidated macro blocks for far-distance LOD 0 compressed_nodes Node3D[] Array of default SVD-compressed nodes (right column, \(X = +4.5\)) macro_nodes MacroNode[] Compressed macro blocks for LOD 0 edges Edge3D[] Structural connecting curves and conduits between tensor nodes max_y number Maximum vertical scene height in Three.js world units num_baseline number Count of baseline nodes num_compressed number Count of compressed nodes total_baseline_params number Exact baseline parameter integer total_baseline_params_formatted string Formatted parameter string (e.g. "66.36M") total_compressed_params number Exact compressed parameter integer total_compressed_params_formatted string Formatted compressed parameter string (e.g. "29.20M") overall_compression_ratio number Reduction factor (e.g. 2.27) storage_saved_bytes number Storage delta in bytes storage_saved_formatted string Formatted storage savings (e.g. "148.6 MB") modules Record<string, ModuleSpatialData> Embedded spatial layouts for default paradigms (svd, moe, mla, slicegpt)

docs.title: Node3D Schema
docs.text: Field Type Required Description id string YES Unique identifier (e.g. "layer.0.attention.q_lin") type string YES Functional category ("dense", "svd", "moe", "mla", "embedding", "output_head", "residual_add") sub_type string NO Sublayer specialization ("v_factor", "u_factor", "router", "expert", "gate_proj") parent_layer_index number YES Zero-indexed transformer layer index parent_layer_name string YES Human-readable parent name (e.g. "Layer 0") sequence_index number YES Execution sequence order within the layer x number YES Three.js X world position y number YES Three.js Y world position (vertical height) z number YES Three.js Z world position (depth plane) width number YES Tensor mesh box width (X-dimension) height number YES Tensor mesh box height (Y-dimension) depth number YES Tensor mesh box depth (Z-dimension) label string YES Display title rendered on billboard sprite badges metadata NodeMetadata YES Detailed shape, parameter counts, and theoretical storage

docs.title: NodeMetadata Schema
docs.text:
interface NodeMetadata {
  shape: [number, number] | [number]; // Matrix dimensions [d_out, d_in]
  params: string;                     // e.g. "590.6K" or "23.44M"
  params_raw: number;                 // Integer parameter count (e.g. 590592)
  storage: string;                    // Estimated FP32/FP16 footprint (e.g. "2.36 MB")
  storage_bytes: number;              // Raw storage footprint in bytes
  dense_equivalent_params?: number;   // Baseline parameters before compression
  dense_equivalent_params_formatted?: string;
  compression_ratio?: number;         // Ratio relative to dense baseline (1.0 = baseline)
  compression?: string;               // Formatted string (e.g. "2.27x (-56.0%)")
  type?: string;                      // Human description (e.g. "Dense Linear Projection")
  rank?: number;                      // Low-rank bottleneck rank r (for SVD layers)
  heads?: number;                     // Attention head count (for MHA/GQA projections)
  num_experts?: number;               // Expert count (for MoE layers)
}

docs.title: 2. modules-catalog.json Schema
docs.text:
modules-catalog.json catalogs all 240+ research attention modules and compression engines in the repository, indexed for fast filtering, search, and preview in the Library Modal.

{
  "total_count": 240,
  "generated_at": "ISO-8601 string",
  "modules": [ModuleCatalogEntry]
}

docs.title: ModuleCatalogEntry Schema
docs.text: Field Type Description id string Canonical module identifier matching codebase filename (e.g. "SOAFusedAttention", "a3_compressor") name string Formatted display title file string Relative path to implementation in Codes/framework/ type string "Attention Module" or "Compression Engine" category string One of 7 primary research categories (see PARADIGMS in constants.js) paradigm string Primary algorithmic paradigm ("svd", "moe", "ssm", "mla", "slicegpt", "quant") icon string UI emoji indicator (e.g. "⚡", "🔀", "🐍", "💎") description string Extracted module docstring / architectural summary math string Symbolic mathematical formulation (LaTeX / plain-text) markdown_preview string Markdown excerpt from canonical documentation in Docs/content/ verified_benchmark BenchmarkResults Benchmark scores harvested from results/

docs.title: 3. modules_components.json Schema
docs.text:
modules_components.json provides the complete deep-inspection specification for every module, including its sublayer decomposition, before-and-after structural transformation rules, and cross-model parameter projections across all 4 architectures.

{
  "total": 240,
  "modules": [ModuleComponentDefinition]
}

docs.title: ModuleComponentDefinition Schema
docs.text: Field Type Description id string Canonical module identifier name string Human-readable module name file string Source file path in Codes/framework/ type string Component type category string Architectural category paradigm string Algorithmic paradigm key icon string Visual indicator icon description string Detailed technical description classes string[] Python class names defined in the module methods_count number Number of methods in the main module class math_latex string Complete LaTeX equation for KaTeX rendering components SublayerComponent[] Breakdown of internal operator sublayers (e.g. Factor V, Factor U) model_projections Record<ModelKey, ModelProjection> Model-specific projections across DistilBERT, RoBERTa, GPT-2, and Qwen3.5 verified_benchmark BenchmarkResults Verified empirical accuracy, throughput, and memory stats

docs.title: SublayerComponent Schema
docs.text:
interface SublayerComponent {
  id: string;              // e.g. "v_factor", "u_factor", "router", "expert"
  name: string;            // e.g. "Factor V (Low-Rank Subspace Projection, r=64)"
  role: string;            // e.g. "Projection to Rank-r Eigenspace"
  shape_transform: string; // e.g. "[64 × d_in]", "[d_out × 64]"
  color: string;           // Hex color code (e.g. "#3acbb8")
}

docs.title: ModelProjection Schema
docs.text:
interface ModelProjection {
  model_name: string;               // e.g. "DistilBERT-Base", "Qwen2.5-0.5B"
  family: string;                   // "Encoder", "Causal Decoder", "GQA Decoder (SLM)"
  hidden_size: number;              // Hidden dimension d_model (768 or 896)
  intermediate_size: number;        // MLP intermediate dimension (3072 or 4864)
  num_layers: number;               // Number of layers (6, 12, or 24)
  baseline_layer_params: number;    // Params in one uncompressed baseline layer
  compressed_layer_p: number;       // Params in one compressed layer
  total_baseline_params: number;    // Full uncompressed model param count
  total_compressed_params: number;  // Full compressed model param count
  savings_ratio: number;            // Savings ratio (e.g. 2.27, 8.0)
  storage_saved_bytes: number;      // Storage reduction in bytes

docs.title: BenchmarkResults Schema
docs.text:
interface BenchmarkResults {
  status: "PASS" | "PASS_LOW" | "FAIL" | "SKIP" | "PENDING";
  accuracy_pct?: number;           // Downstream GLUE accuracy (e.g. 81.31%)
  f1_score?: number;               // F1 score
  peak_vram_mb?: number;           // Peak GPU memory in MB
  throughput_tokens_sec?: number;  // Inference throughput in tokens/sec
  source_file?: string;            // Path to CSV log in results/
}

docs.title: 4. components/<module_id>.json Schema
docs.text: Each of the 240 standalone files inside Docs/visualizer/components/ is an exact single-module export of the ModuleComponentDefinition schema above. This allows modular on-demand fetching when selecting any research module without parsing the full consolidated catalog upfront.

docs.title: Extending the 3D Neural Architecture Visualizer
docs.text: This guide explains how to add new attention modules, compression algorithms, or foundation models.

docs.title: 1. Adding a New Compression or Attention Module
Step 1: Place Module in Framework
docs.text: Save your PyTorch implementation in either: * Codes/framework/attentions/<my_module>.py * Codes/framework/compression_engine/<my_module>.py

docs.title: Step 2: Define Component Topology in components/<my_module>.json
docs.text:
Create Docs/visualizer/components/<my_module>.json:

{
  "id": "my_module",
  "name": "My Efficient Attention",
  "file": "Codes/framework/attentions/my_module.py",
  "type": "Attention Module",
  "category": "Low-Rank SVD & Factorization",
  "paradigm": "svd",
  "icon": "⚡",
  "description": "Factorizes QKV with custom rank bottleneck.",
  "math_latex": "W_{proj} = U \\cdot V, \\quad r=32",
  "components": [
    {
      "id": "v_factor",
      "name": "Factor V (Subspace Proj, r=32)",
      "role": "Rank-32 Compression",
      "shape_transform": "[32 × d_in]",
      "color": "#3acbb8"
    },
    {
      "id": "u_factor",
      "name": "Factor U (Expansion, r=32)",
      "role": "Reconstruction",
      "shape_transform": "[d_out × 32]",
      "color": "#2dd4bf"
    }
  ],
  "model_projections": {
    "distilbert": {
      "model_name": "DistilBERT-Base",
      "savings_ratio": 4.5,
      "storage_saved_formatted": "45.2 MB",
      "benchmark": { "status": "PASS", "accuracy_pct": 82.5 }
    }
  }
}

docs.title: Step 3: Re-index Catalog
docs.text:
Run the catalog generator: 

python3 Docs/visualizer/export_module_catalog.py
Your module will immediately appear in the Library Modal and Quick Pick dropdown!

docs.title: 2. Adding a New Model Architecture
docs.text:
1. Add Specs to src/constants.js: 
    MODEL_SPECS.my_model = {
    name: 'MyModel-7B',
    family: 'Decoder',
    num_layers: 32,
    hidden_size: 4096,
    intermediate_size: 11008,
    base_layer_params: 200000000,
    base_total: 6700000000,
    descr: '32 Layers · 4096d · 32 Heads',
    vocab_size: 32000
};
  2. Add Branch to src/physics/token_trajectory.js: Add custom particle routing for any non-standard tensor splits (e.g. cross-attention, recurrent states).
  3. Run python3 Docs/visualizer/generate_module_components.py to recalculate projections across all 240+ modules.

docs.title: 1. Three Visual Tiers
docs.text:
The visualizer implements a continuous Level-of-Detail (LOD) manager that automatically balances visual clarity with 60 FPS WebGL rendering performance based on camera distance:

Camera Distance from Model Center:
Distance > 40 units  ───▶  LOD 0: Macro Bounding Blocks
Distance 25 - 40     ───▶  Transition Zone (Smooth Fade)
Distance < 25 units  ───▶  LOD 1: Granular Matrices & Badges
Level Camera Distance Visible Subsystems Educational Purpose Macro (LOD 0) \(> 40\) units Consolidated layer boundary blocks, layer indices Architecture-wide structure, depth comparison Transition \(25 - 40\) units Macro blocks fade; internal tensors appear Connects layer macro volume to internal sublayers Granular (LOD 1) \(< 25\) units Matrix boxes, head partition lines, floating shape badges Exact dimensional transformations, rank bottlenecks

docs.title: 2. Mathematical Switching Logic
docs.text:
In src/index.js, the distance is computed every frame:

const camDist = camera.position.distanceTo(controls.target);

if (camDist > VISUAL_CONFIG.ZOOM.macroThreshold) {
    // LOD 0: Only Macro blocks
    macroGroup.visible = true;
    granularGroup.visible = false;
    dimensionBadgesGroup.visible = false;
} else if (camDist > VISUAL_CONFIG.ZOOM.transitionStart) {
    // Transition: Both Macro and Granular visible
    macroGroup.visible = true;
    granularGroup.visible = true;
    dimensionBadgesGroup.visible = false;
} else {
    // LOD 1: Detailed Granular + Floating Dimension Badges
    macroGroup.visible = false;
    granularGroup.visible = true;
    dimensionBadgesGroup.visible = true;
}

docs.title: 3. Dimension Badges Staggering & Overlap Prevention
docs.text: Floating dimension badges ([768 × 768], r=64, 12H, 2H GQA) are rendered on 2D billboard sprites positioned on the front face of each 3D box (\(Z = \text{node.z} + \frac{\text{node.depth}}{2} + 0.05\)). For adjacent narrow projections (such as Key and Value projections in GQA), vertical offsets are automatically staggered (\(\pm 0.06\)) to ensure text never overlaps.

docs.title: 1. Conceptual Model
docs.text:
In the 3D Neural Architecture Visualizer, token particles do not move randomly. Their trajectories directly reflect the underlying mathematical transformations computed by each transformer layer.

Vertical Progression (Y Axis):
y = 0.0          ← Input Sequence Ingestion & Token Embeddings
y = 1.0 + 0·3.2  ← Layer 0 (Input Norm → Attn QKV → Add #1 → FFN → Add #2)
y = 1.0 + 1·3.2  ← Layer 1
y = 1.0 + 2·3.2  ← Layer 2
...
y = max_y        ← Layer L Exit → Final Norm → Output Softmax Unembedding

Within each layer (\(STRIDE = 3.2\) units), normalized progress \(\tau \in [0.0, 1.0)\) determines intra-layer operations:

Phase \(\tau\) Range Operation Mathematical Formula A 0.00 – 0.12 Pre-Attention Norm \(\bar{X} = \text{RMSNorm}(X) = \frac{X}{\sqrt{\frac{1}{d} \sum x_i^2 + \epsilon}} \odot \gamma\) B 0.12 – 0.46 Self-Attention / Projections \(Q = \bar{X} W_Q, \; K = \bar{X} W_K, \; V = \bar{X} W_V, \; A = \text{Softmax}(Q K^\top / \sqrt{d}) V\) C 0.46 – 0.52 Attention Residual Add (+) \(X_{\text{mid}} = X_{\text{in}} + \text{Dropout}(A W_O)\) D 0.52 – 0.88 Feed-Forward Network / MoE \(\text{FFN}(X) = \text{GELU}(X W_1 + b_1) W_2 + b_2\) or \(\text{SwiGLU}(X)\) E 0.88 – 1.00 Layer Residual Add (+) \(X_{\text{out}} = X_{\text{mid}} + \text{Dropout}(\text{FFN}(\bar{X}_{\text{mid}}))\)

docs.title: 1. DistilBERT & RoBERTa (Standard SVD Rank Bottleneck)
docs.text:
• Tokens pass into Factor \(V \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times d_{\text{in}}}\), physically squeezing into rank bottleneck \(r=64\) (\(\text{width} = 0.45\)).
  • Tokens expand through Factor \(U \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{out}} \times r}\), reconstructing back into full hidden dimension \(d=768\).

docs.title: 2. GPT-2 (Fused \(c\_attn\) Conv1D)
docs.text:
• In GPT-2, \(Q, K, V\) projections are packed into a single wide contiguous tensor: $\(W_{\text{fused}} \in \mathbb{R}^{768 \times 2304}\)$
  • Tokens pass through this unified wide block together before branching into contextual attention.

docs.title: 3. Qwen 2.5 / 3.5 (Grouped Query Attention & SwiGLU)
docs.text:
• GQA Attention: 14 Query heads query only 2 shared Key/Value head bundles, visualized as 14 wide Query branches and two compact Key/Value streams.
  • SwiGLU FFN: Tokens bifurcate into parallel gate_proj (\(\text{SiLU}\)) and up_proj branches before being recombined in down_proj: $\(\text{SwiGLU}(x) = (x W_{\text{gate}}) \otimes \text{SiLU}(x W_{\text{up}}) W_{\text{down}}\)$

docs.title: 4. Mixture of Experts (MoE Routing)
docs.text:
• Tokens hit the MoE Gating Router at \(\tau \approx 0.55\).
  • The router evaluates gating logits \(G(x) = \text{Softmax}(\text{TopK}(x \cdot W_g))\).
  • Each token branches laterally to its routed expert (one of 4 parallel blocks, colored Cyan, Purple, Amber, or Rose).

docs.title: 3. Residual Skip Connection Highways
docs.text: To illustrate identity propagation: $\(X_{l+1} = X_l + \mathcal{F}(X_l)\)$ 25% of all active tokens (t.isResidual = true) travel along the outer lateral bypass conduit (\(X = \pm 6.35\)). They do not enter the internal matrix blocks; instead, they carry the unmodified identity state forward and execute smooth Bezier dips into: 1. Addition Operator 1 at \(\tau \in [0.40, 0.48]\) 2. Addition Operator 2 at \(\tau \in [0.88, 0.98]\)

docs.title: 3. Code-Verified Attention & Compression Modules
docs.text: The modular refactoring incorporates physical and dimensional insights directly harvested from PyTorch module implementations in Codes/framework/: 1. SOAFusedAttention.py: Factorized SVD low-rank bottleneck pairs (\(V\) and \(U\)) initialized from truncated singular value decomposition with LoRA adapters. 2. gated_linear_attention.py: Linear attention recurrence with data-dependent decay gating, SiLU output projection (\(Z\)), and denominator normalization. 3. mla_attention.py: DeepSeek-V2 Multi-Head Latent Attention with unified down-projection into low-rank latent vector \(c_t^{KV} \in \mathbb{R}^{r}\) and dual up-projections (\(k_t^C, v_t^C\)). 4. a3_compressor.py: Activation-aware Fisher-weighted SVD factorized linear replacement (\(y = (x V^\top) U^\top + b\)) with LayerNorm recalibration. 5. slicegpt.py: Orthogonal rotation coordinate invariance (\(W Q\)) and variance-informed channel slicing (\(P_r\)).

docs.title: 1. Prerequisites
docs.text:
The visualizer is built on pure standard web technologies with no compilation steps or node_modules dependencies needed to run in the browser.

  • Any modern web browser with WebGL enabled (Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge)
  • Python 3.8+ (for local HTTP serving)

docs.title: 2. Launching Locally
docs.text:
From the root of the project, run: 

python3 Docs/visualizer/serve.py
This starts an HTTP server at http://localhost:8080 with proper CORS headers and automatically opens your browser to http://localhost:8080/Docs/visualizer/index.html.

docs.title: 3. Running Unit Tests
docs.text:
Run the Node.js built-in automated test runner: 

node --test Docs/visualizer/tests/*.test.js
All 19 tests validating constants, model specs, token physics trajectories, and JSON schemas will execute.

if (modelKey === 'llama3') {

docs.title: Tutorial 04: Custom PBR Materials & Shaders
docs.text: Learn how to create custom shaders and glowing materials for specific tensor components.

docs.title: 1. Material Cache in src/core/materials.js
docs.text:
The engine automatically manages PBR materials via getOrCreateCustomMaterial(hexColor):

import * as THREE from 'three';

export function createHolographicMaterial(hexColor) {
    const c = new THREE.Color(hexColor);
    return new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({
        color: c,
        roughness: 0.15,
        metalness: 0.85,
        transparent: true,
        opacity: 0.88,
        emissive: c.clone().multiplyScalar(0.4),
        emissiveIntensity: 0.5
    });
}

docs.title: 2. Using Custom Shaders via THREE.ShaderMaterial
docs.text:
If you want custom animated vertex displacement (e.g. quantum probability clouds or activation ripples), instantiate a ShaderMaterial:

const rippleShaderMaterial = new THREE.ShaderMaterial({
    uniforms: {
        time: { value: 0 },
        baseColor: { value: new THREE.Color(0x53ecd9) }
    },
    vertexShader: `
        uniform float time;
        varying vec3 vNormal;
        void main() {
            vNormal = normal;
            vec3 pos = position;
            pos += normal * sin(pos.y * 10.0 + time * 4.0) * 0.05;
            gl_Position = projectionMatrix * modelViewMatrix * vec4(pos, 1.0);
        }
    `,
    fragmentShader: `
        uniform vec3 baseColor;
        varying vec3 vNormal;
        void main() {
            float intensity = pow(0.7 - dot(vNormal, vec3(0.0, 0.0, 1.0)), 2.0);
            gl_FragColor = vec4(baseColor + vec3(intensity), 0.9);
        }
    `,
    transparent: true
});
Update rippleShaderMaterial.uniforms.time.value = timestamp * 0.001; inside the animation loop in src/index.js.
